author: linuxdynasty
body:
Refs #10354.

**Phase 5 5.2 builds the CVE List mirror lane: midnight-baseline store, deltaLog tail with fetchTime cursor, and full-shard proof.**

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Broken | Criterion 1 had no projection proof at full-shard volume, only in-memory 5.1 numbers. |
| Fix | Baseline store, delta tail, cursor continuity, lag metric, and committable benches plus a live writer test. |
| Proof | RED-first unit tests, three benches, and a disposable-Postgres live test at 334-CVE volume all green. |
| Risk | Mostly new files, plus additive gate-filter widening with ledger and inventory enrollment; no production behavior changes. |

## Problem

#10354 criterion 1 requires a projection measurement at full-shard volume
(1,000 records) before 5.3 promotion. 5.1 produced in-memory T1-T4 numbers
with no baseline store, no cursor, and no deployed-cadence observation, so
the criterion stayed unproven. The arbiter DEFER ruling (see evidence note)
scoped 5.2 as the lane that builds exactly that substrate, and corrected the
criterion-1 wording from a Neo4j PROFILE to a reducer-side Postgres
projection — no vulnerability Cypher exists in the repo to profile.

## What changed

- `go/internal/vulnsource/cvelist_delta_tail.go`: stream-parse of
  `cves/deltaLog.json`, stop at the fetchTime cursor, count invariant,
  non-empty error fails the batch, gap reports re-seed.
- `go/internal/vulnsource/cvelist_baseline.go`: midnight-zip store with
  stream sha256 verify, latest-plus-previous retention, cursor file, and
  inner-zip extraction for the double-zip wrapper layout.
- Lag metric from cursor fetchTime for the deployed-cadence observation.
- Committable benches: delta replay (~170µs), shard selection (~690µs),
  full-shard build (~27ms).
- Live writer test enrolled as `dedicated_ci` under the `reducer-contention`
  runner: idempotent replay, retraction, and upsert EXPLAIN at 334-CVE
  volume on disposable Postgres.
- Evidence note `docs/internal/evidence/10354-cve-baseline-delta-tail.md`
  with real census (420,477 baseline members, 910-record shard), re-scope
  correction, and the 5.3 verdict; ruling copy with identifiers redacted.

## Proof

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `go test ./internal/vulnsource/ -count=1` | no baseline/delta code | ok, 15 RED-first tests green |
| Shard build bench (`-benchtime=10x`) | no committed bench | ~27ms over the 1,000-fact shard |
| Live writer test (disposable PG) | unproven at volume | PASS: 334 rows, retraction 34, EXPLAIN 14.3ms |
| `bash scripts/verify-live-tests-ledger.sh` | row missing | PASS with `dedicated_ci` row |

<details>
<summary>Rebased head, review verdict, and pre-push result</summary>

HEAD `0e83177c03` on `origin/main` `c1cb309c1d`. Preliminary
verdict on the pre-rebase head: P0=0, P1=0, P2-blocking=0 (one P3, fixed).
Added commit (enrollment + gosec/citation fixes): scoped re-review P0=0,
P1=0, P2-blocking=0 (one prose P3, Risk line fixed in this body). `make
pre-push` exit 0 on this head (8/8 PASS, merge tree `a647479d`).
`ci-gates review-attest verify` matched on these exact claims.

</details>

**NOT_CHECKED:** Full `make pre-pr` was not run; the change adds new files and
touches no queue, lease, schema, hot-path Cypher, or reducer projection path.
Deployed-cadence observation (mirror count equals baseline, lag within
cadence) needs 5.2 deployed on schedule and lands with the 5.3 verdict.

body:
# Description With `minY > maxY` (or `minX > maxX`), the titles of that axis collapsed into one or two overlapping labels on its edge, and its grid lines disappeared. The data itself was already drawn correctly flipped, since `getPixelY` / `getPixelX` are linear. Three places in the shared axis code assumed `min <= max`: - `AxisChartHelper.iterateThroughAxis` stepped from `min` towards `max`, so with `min > max` it stopped right away and only yielded the end values. - `Utils.getEfficientInterval` returned a negative, unrounded interval for a negative range (e.g. `-0.857…` instead of `1.0`). - `SideTitlesWidget` only computed a title's position when `max - min > 0`, so every title of an inverted axis landed on the same edge. `iterateThroughAxis` now walks from the smaller end, swapping `minIncluded` and `maxIncluded` together with `min` and `max`, and always steps by `interval.abs()`. Without the `abs()`, the swap would turn an inverted axis with a negative `interval` into an endless loop (a normal axis with a negative interval already looped forever before this change; it now yields the same values as the positive interval). `getEfficientInterval` uses the absolute range, and the title position is computed for any non-zero range. The fix lives in the shared code, so it covers the X axis and the titles and grid lines of `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `ScatterChart` and `CandlestickChart`. Normal axes are unchanged value by value. Out of scope (different root causes, left untouched): the bar rods of an inverted `BarChart`, the touch indicator clamping of `LineChart`, and the touch hit test of `CandlestickChart`. Whether `min > max` should be documented as supported is left to the maintainers; this PR changes no dartdoc. ## TestResult Regression tests: 20 new tests in 8 existing test files (`iterateThroughAxis`, `getEfficientInterval`, `SideTitlesWidget` for all four axis charts, `drawGrid` for all four painters, and a widget test with the reporter's config). 17 of them fail on `main` (e60b4c13) and all pass with this PR; the other 3 lock the `min == max` output to what `main` produces. `make sure` passes (726 tests). Screenshots: a temporary harness app (not part of this PR), chart height 400. S1, S2, S3 and S5 use the config from #1769 (same spots, `FlBorderData(show: false)`, touch disabled, top titles on), but the left titles use `meta.formattedValue` instead of the issue's `(-3 - value)`, so the values are readable. Each image: **left = `main` (before), right = this PR (after)**. | # | Scenario | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | S1 | LineChart `minX: 1, maxX: 18, minY: 3, maxY: -3`, auto interval (#1769) | Two `3` labels stacked at the bottom-left, no horizontal grid lines | `-3` (top) … `3` (bottom), 13 titles, horizontal grid lines back | | S2 | S1 with left `SideTitles.interval: 1` | One `-3` label at the bottom | `-3, -2 … 3`, 7 titles, `-3` at the top | | S3 | LineChart `minX: 18, maxX: 1, minY: -3, maxY: 3` (top titles) | `1` and `18` stacked on the left edge, no vertical grid lines | `18` (left) … `1` (right), vertical grid lines back | | S4 | ScatterChart `minX: 0, maxX: 10, minY: 10, maxY: 0` | One `0` label | `0` (top) … `10` (bottom), 11 titles, horizontal grid lines back | | S5 | S1 with `minY: -3, maxY: 3` (regression check) | Normal | Identical (chart area pixel-identical on all three platforms) | ### Android
S1 – #1769 config, inverted Y axis
S2 – left interval 1
S3 – inverted X axis
S4 – ScatterChart, inverted Y axis
S5 – normal axis (unchanged)
### iOS
S1 – #1769 config, inverted Y axis
S2 – left interval 1
S3 – inverted X axis
S4 – ScatterChart, inverted Y axis
S5 – normal axis (unchanged)
### Chrome
S1 – #1769 config, inverted Y axis
S2 – left interval 1
S3 – inverted X axis
S4 – ScatterChart, inverted Y axis
S5 – normal axis (unchanged)
## Checklist - [x] I have followed the [Contributor Guide] when preparing my PR. - [x] I have updated/added tests for ALL new/updated/fixed functionality. - [ ] I have updated/added relevant documentation and added dartdoc comments with `///`. - [ ] I have updated/added relevant examples in `example`. ## Breaking Change? - [ ] Yes, this PR is a breaking change. - [x] No, this PR is not a breaking change. `min > max` was never documented, and normal axes are unchanged. One note for apps that worked around this bug: if you set `minY > maxY` and reversed the label text yourself in `getTitlesWidget` (for example `(-3 - value)`, as suggested in #809), the `value` you receive is now already correct, so your own reversal shows wrong text (`3` becomes `-6.00`)

author: ykuwai
body:
## What changes

#362 keeps each COM type information it reads, so later objects of the same interface skip a `GetTypeAttr`. It kept every one that passed through pywin32's wrapper, and that wrapper is patched for the whole process. So Excel's type informations were kept too: a chart's workbook, its sheets and ranges, on every chart data edit through Excel.

`utils/held_refs.py` (#299) explains why that matters. Letting go of the last reference into an Excel that is shutting down takes 2 to 12 s, sometimes a full minute. That outlasts the worker's 45 s budget, so those references are kept away from the worker until their Excel has ended. The cache let go of them in two places:

- when it reached 256 entries, inline in some later call, which could happen after a few dozen chart data edits while the last chart's Excel was still ending;
- at worker exit, through `forget_type_infos()`.

Now a type information is kept only if it comes from PowerPoint's or Office's type library. Its library is read once, when it is first read. Any other one, Excel's among them, is asked each time, as before #362.

Found in review of #362.

## Tested

- [x] `uv run --frozen pytest -q` on macOS: 3512 passed, 231 skipped.
- [x] New tests `test_excels_are_not_kept` and `test_one_whose_library_cannot_be_read_is_not_kept` fail without the change.
- [ ] Windows: tests and the layout check timing to be run there.

## Why
Across conpost-aotori, 48 of 51 cancelled runs (2026-10-08 to 2026-11-07) died in the "Install Japanese fonts" step: `apt-get install fonts-noto-cjk` (61.2 MB) sometimes crawls from azure.archive.ubuntu.com (e.g. "Fetched 61.2 MB in 6min 17s (162 kB/s)") and the job hits `timeout-minutes` before posting.

Replace only the CJK apt install with a direct download of the same files from the pinned upstream release:

Workflows: etf-daily.yml
Pillow loads /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-{Regular,Bold}.ttc by path (the NotoSansCJKjp-*.otf entries are later fallbacks apt never provided). etf-alert.yml installs no fonts and is unchanged.

author: realcopacetic
body:
Kodi profiles share the skin's generated files (`special://skin`), but each profile has its own settings (`special://profile/addon_data`). After a profile switch the helper kept the files the last profile built, so profile B showed A's menus.

**What changes**
- The resolver cache now records a digest of each output it built (`HashManager.compute_hash`). The start check rebuilds if an output on disk isn't one it built: another profile, a reinstall or a hand edit.
- A missing output is still built on its own.
- The first start after this update rebuilds once. The bytes match, so nothing is written and there's no reload. The cache schema is unchanged; an older helper ignores the new key.
- C2's generated XML is unchanged; only `resolver_cache.json` gains `"outputs"`. No library writes.

**Merge order:** rebase after #70 (one comment conflict in `tests/README.md`; the code merges cleanly, and all 29 service tests pass on the merged tree).

**What to try**
1. With two profiles, change the Home menu in profile B, then switch to profile A. A shows its own menu after one reload.
2. Switch back to B. B's change is there.

Reviewed by both lanes (correctness, adversarial runtime); their findings are fixed and the delta was reviewed again, clean.

author: dredodin
body:
## Summary

New `npm run sandcastle -- clean`: removes worktrees and local branches of finished takes.

```
clean(repo):
  workspace = workspaceHere()            # .env GH_TOKEN exported, no full setup
  plan = planClean(porcelain, branches, closedRoots)   # shared/worktrees.mts, pure
  for take whose root issue is closed:
    remove linked worktrees (incl. detached, matched by folder name)
    delete local integration + item branches
  main tree = first porcelain block: never removed;
  closed branch checked out there: kept, logged with what to do
```

- Open roots, remote branches and the main working tree are untouched; take/resume never run clean.
- `takePrefix` is the single branch-scheme builder; `rootsOfBranches`/`branchesOfRoots` replace `rootOfBranch`; `isRootClosed` is shared by `checkRoot` and `clean`.
- `shared/worktrees.mts` (one porcelain parser, also used by `worktreeOf`) is under stryker at 100%.
- README, run-factory skill (human-only) and glossary updated; v0.6.2.

## Evidence

- **Before:** closed takes leave worktrees and branches behind; no command removes them.
  **After:** `clean` removes them; `shared/worktrees.test.mts` covers `planClean` (main tree kept, detached worktrees removed, checked-out closed branch kept). `verify.sh` green before each commit.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

`clean` force-removes worktrees and deletes local branches, but only when run by a human, only for closed roots; unpushed work on such branches would be lost.

**Blast Radius:** local-checkouts

<!-- sandcastle-run -->
Models: PLAN `opus` (claudeCode, medium), IMPLEMENT `sonnet` (claudeCode, medium), REVIEW `opus` (claudeCode, medium), MERGE `opus` (claudeCode, medium), PR `sonnet` (claudeCode, medium).

## Review

### Pass 1

<details><summary>Report</summary>

## Code review — Standards

1. **`shared/branches.mts` (`rootOfBranch`)**: Standards. The function returns `number | undefined`. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` › Rules says "no `undefined` in owned contracts". **Fix:** return a value the type spells out, for example `number | null`, or a tagged result. Better still, have it return only the matching roots from a list of branches (see finding 3), so there is no "nothing" case at all.

2. **`workflow/clean.mts` (`linkedWorktrees`)**: Standards (Duplicated Code). It splits `git worktree list --porcelain` into blocks, then strips the `worktree ` and `branch refs/heads/` prefixes. `worktreeOf` in `shared/repo.mts` already does the same parsing. **Fix:** write one porcelain parser, used by both `worktreeOf` and `clean`. It is pure logic, so it belongs in `shared/` (see finding 3).

3. **`workflow/clean.mts`**: Standards. Pure decision logic sits in the workflow, tangled with git and gh calls, and has no tests. The rule broken is `CODING_STANDARDS.md` › "Pure logic in `shared/` (data in → answer out); `git`/`gh`/file calls stay thin one-liners beside it", plus ADR-0001's "extract the decision as a pure function". The tangled decisions are:
   - parsing the worktree porcelain;
   - excluding the main working tree;
   - picking which branches and worktrees belong to closed roots.

   **Fix:** add a tested pure function in `shared/`, for example `(porcelain, branches, closedRoots) → { worktrees, branches }`. `clean.mts` then keeps only the `gh`, `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D` one-liners.

4. **`workflow/clean.mts` (`isClosed`)**: Standards (Duplicated Code, judgement call). `checkRoot` in `shared/repo.mts` already makes the same `gh issue view <root> --repo <home> --json state` call and has its own zod schema. **Fix:** add one `rootState(workspace, root)` beside `checkRoot` in `shared/repo.mts`, and use it from `checkRoot` and `clean`.

## Code review — Spec

5. **`workflow/clean.mts` (main working tree)**: Spec (c). The spec says: "`clean` removes every worktree and local branch of every take of a closed root issue". Two weaknesses:
   - The main working tree is skipped only by comparing strings (`path === repo.path`). It is safer to skip the first porcelain block, which git always lists as the main tree. If the two path spellings differ (symlinks, or Windows/Git Bash slashes), `git worktree remove --force` runs on the main tree, git refuses, and `clean` throws.
   - If a repo's main tree has a branch of a closed root checked out, `git branch -D` fails ("cannot delete branch … used by worktree"). Since nothing catches it, `clean` stops and the remaining branches and repos are left as they were.

   **Fix:** drop the first porcelain block instead of comparing paths. Skip any branch that is checked out in the main tree, with a log line, in the same way `checkNotCheckedOut` treats that case.

6. **`main.mts` (`clean` runs the full `setup`)**: Spec (b), judgement call. The spec asks only that `clean` be "run by hand" and go "over every repo of the workspace". This branch runs the whole `setup` first, which:
   - requires every `.env` key and opens the wizard when one is missing;
   - starts the Podman machine;
   - creates repo labels on GitHub;
   - exports the secrets.

   So `clean` fails without model and API keys, and it writes to GitHub. The header comment was also changed to "Every mode runs setup first". **Fix:** resolve only the workspace for `clean` (`readLayout` + `sourcePaths` + `resolveWorkspace`), and leave `setup`'s full path to `setup`, `take` and `resume`.

## Doc review — Convention

7. **`GLOSSARY.md` (Run)**, `README.md`, `skills/run-factory/SKILL.md**: Convention (judgement call: each fact lives in one file). All three files repeat what `clean` does ("removes worktrees and local branches of takes whose root issue is closed"). The glossary entry also puts command behaviour into a term definition, when the spec asked only that "a Run is still only a take or a resume". **Fix:** in the glossary, say only that `setup` and `clean` are human commands, not runs. Keep the behaviour in README's command list, and have the skill table say "human-only, like `setup`" without restating it.

8. **`main.mts` header comment**: Convention. "Every mode runs setup first; only take and resume run." is ambiguous: "run" is the glossary term, but the sentence reads like the verb. **Fix:** "take and resume are Runs; every mode runs setup first", or drop the second clause. If finding 6 is fixed, update this comment to match.

</details>

Fixed:
- Fix the branch review findings for `clean` in sandcastle-factory (verbatim from the review report):
  
  1. **`shared/branches.mts` (`rootOfBranch`)**: Standards. The function returns `number | undefined`. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` › Rules says "no `undefined` in owned contracts". **Fix:** return a value the type spells out, for example `number | null`, or a tagged result. Better still, have it return only the matching roots from a list of branches (see finding 3), so there is no "nothing" case at all.
  
  2. **`workflow/clean.mts` (`linkedWorktrees`)**: Standards (Duplicated Code). It splits `git worktree list --porcelain` into blocks, then strips the `worktree ` and `branch refs/heads/` prefixes. `worktreeOf` in `shared/repo.mts` already does the same parsing. **Fix:** write one porcelain parser, used by both `worktreeOf` and `clean`. It is pure logic, so it belongs in `shared/` (see finding 3).
  
  3. **`workflow/clean.mts`**: Standards. Pure decision logic sits in the workflow, tangled with git and gh calls, and has no tests. The rule broken is `CODING_STANDARDS.md` › "Pure logic in `shared/` (data in → answer out); `git`/`gh`/file calls stay thin one-liners beside it", plus ADR-0001's "extract the decision as a pure function". The tangled decisions are: parsing the worktree porcelain; excluding the main working tree; picking which branches and worktrees belong to closed roots. **Fix:** add a tested pure function in `shared/`, for example `(porcelain, branches, closedRoots) → { worktrees, branches }`. `clean.mts` then keeps only the `gh`, `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D` one-liners.

author: dev-vinicius-andrade
body:
BYO T12 (docs/design/47 section 10 and T12): the privacy and legal texts for keeping a baby's care records in the owner's own PostgreSQL. Texts only; no feature code.

## What changes
- **Privacy policy 13 (2026-11-07)**, en and pt-BR: a new section "Your own database (optional)" plus a data row (sealed connection details), a recipient row (the database provider the user chooses), and lines in legal bases, consent, rights, retention, security and transfers. It says plainly: the app and account stay the same, only where the baby's care records are stored changes; records pass through the Lotties servers, which can read them; connection details are AES-256-GCM sealed, but the operator holds the key and can open them; not end-to-end encryption; the provider is the user's choice, with its own terms, region, pausing and backups; no reminders, members or doctor access for such a baby in this first version; move back or disconnect any time.
- `legal/dataFlows.ts`: `OWN_DATABASE_FLOW` (the facts the section is held to) and a `chosenBy: 'lotties' | 'user'` field on every recipient; the new recipient `ownDatabaseProvider` is the only `user` one.
- `legal/byoDatabaseConsent.ts`: the legal text of the optional consent `byo_database` (en, pt-BR, `{provider}` filled in by `byoDatabaseConsentText`), included in the consent `textDigest`. T9 renders it.
- `legal/forbiddenClaims.ts` + test: `findForbiddenClaims(text, locale)` for claims no privacy text may make ("end-to-end", "only you can read", "Lotties cannot see", "zero-knowledge", "never touches our servers", "we do not store your data", pt-BR equivalents), allowing the honest "this is not end-to-end encryption". The test scans the policy, the terms and the consent; T9's string tests can reuse it.
- Consent entry `2026-11-07.1` (terms 1, privacy 13, **minor**) in `consentVersions.json` and `Lotties.Domain.Consents.ConsentVersions`, with the new digest.
- Audit 33 (inventory row 25, a section 3 row, section 17), lawyer brief item 19 (questions only), design 47 status, filemap.

## Why minor
Nobody who does not opt in has anything collected, sent or changed, and the one person whose data goes to the new recipient gives the separate `byo_database` consent naming the provider first. Design 47 section 10 recommends minor. The literal material rule lists "a new recipient", so the lawyer is asked (brief item 19) and the owner may promote it with a later entry.

## Tests
- `npm --prefix code/web run lint`: clean.
- `npm --prefix code/web run test`: 4661 passed, 2 failed in `SettingsPage.test.tsx` under full-suite load; that file passes on its own (31/31) and is untouched here.
- `dotnet test code/api/Lotties.sln --filter Consent`: Domain 8, Infrastructure 3, Api 96 passed; `Lotties.Domain.Tests` all 2838 passed.

Not legal advice.

## Statements that depend on PRs not yet on main
Everything is behind `Stores:Enabled` (off by default) and the per-account allowlist, so none of this is offered before those rules land:
- "a short undo period whose date the app shows" and moving records in and out: **#66 (T7)**, the 7-day undo window and the `store_moving` write block.
- "no reminders, no invited members and no doctor access" for a baby on an external store: **#65 (T11)**, `store_owner_only` 409 on invites and reminders skipped.
- "Deleting your Lotties account deletes the connection details": the `data_stores` erasure rule is on main; wiping the user's own database on deletion (T10) is not built, and the policy does not claim it.

author: r-xue
body:
This pull request introduces comprehensive support for regression test discovery, parallel batch execution, automated result synthesis, and coverage reporting in `calibpipe`. It adds new subcommands (`collect`, `report`, `coverage`), extends the configuration and documentation to support test arrays, and provides native Slurm concurrency throttling and automated wrap-up job scheduling. The documentation is significantly expanded to guide users through these new workflows.

**Key features and changes:**

### Regression Test Discovery & Batch Execution

* Added the `calibpipe collect` subcommand for automated discovery of pytest test nodes using CASA Python, with support for marker/keyword filtering and runfile export. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7c95078171e33908b6b5efaeba91957dc5ab60a18ae622a1fcfb351847a412b1R1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R13-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R27-R34) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aR1315-R1470) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b4d68dc855d0f9476d3f2ee343853bd21bf82ea9960d0cf06661baa244439dd6L18-R21)
* Extended batch submission to support test arrays: each test is run as an independent job in its own subdirectory, with support for on-the-fly collection (`--collect`), runfile submission, and concurrency throttling (`--max-concurrent`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aL965-R1065) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aL592-R599) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a3de6acaaaa3b6a4a52ede7d1f71503ff6c08008276e7254bf3bef49620cfec8R321-R333)

### Automated Reporting & Coverage Synthesis

* Added the `calibpipe report` subcommand to aggregate JUnit XML results, combine distributed `.coverage.*` files, and generate both terminal and HTML coverage reports, with support for CASA Python fallback and cross-environment source path remapping. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-77f023b99d3d58008351d3e82fc06e6d06ba1bc2da9e41be6329b7fa4f419f05R25-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-85fbf7cbf1602eb6ce923589115313a14dd458fa0c32b4b038c0d0a5eaeaa104R1-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aR1315-R1470)
* Added the `calibpipe coverage` subcommand for standalone coverage combination and reporting, including recursive discovery and path remapping. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-33e809139eafc061d4f2ad3f71dbb0344afeb664419812b57b9ec9c7d89e964bR1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R13-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aR1315-R1470)

### Configuration & Documentation

* Expanded `[profiles.<name>]` configuration with fields for test collection and batch array execution (`test_target`, `test_marker`, `test_filter`, `test_opts`, `with_report`, `max_concurrent`), and provided detailed documentation and examples for all new workflows. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3de6acaaaa3b6a4a52ede7d1f71503ff6c08008276e7254bf3bef49620cfec8R321-R333) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aL592-R599) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-07fdd026b11c494c3b62c97f764f6939803c453389ebefd6b05e6f187d44859aL965-R1065) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R13-R15) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R27-R34) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b4d68dc855d0f9476d3f2ee343853bd21bf82ea9960d0cf06661baa244439dd6L18-R21)

### API Documentation

* Added API documentation stubs for the new modules: `calibpipe.collect`, `calibpipe.coverage`, and `calibpipe.report`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7c95078171e33908b6b5efaeba91957dc5ab60a18ae622a1fcfb351847a412b1R1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-33e809139eafc061d4f2ad3f71dbb0344afeb664419812b57b9ec9c7d89e964bR1-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-85fbf7cbf1602eb6ce923589115313a14dd458fa0c32b4b038c0d0a5eaeaa104R1-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-363e82493e2e04f41b234969fa9b7e9fe40d2a09b746ff381162a71206632657R13-R15)

These changes provide a robust, end-to-end workflow for regression test management, batch scheduling, and result synthesis in `calibpipe`.

body:
Vendor wire formats live in `hellas-adaptors`; the gateway keeps HTTP routing and model wiring.

Changes:
- **`hellas_adaptors::openai::audio_transcriptions`** parses the `/v1/audio/transcriptions` form: model, file, language and `response_format` json|text. Gateway routing and the handler share one model-field check:
  - a missing model is 400 "model field is required";
  - a model that isn't served is 404 "unknown model".
- **`hellas_adaptors::openai::images`** parses and renders `/v1/images/generations`. An explicit `null` in an optional field means its default.
- **Error shapes:** `WireAdaptor::render_error(status, message)` renders refusals in each format's error shape. `/v1/messages` errors now use the Anthropic shape (`{"type":"error","error":{...}}`); OpenAI routes keep `{"error":{"message":...}}`. Status codes are unchanged.
- **One handler:** a single generic `dispatch::serve` serves every text and Fetch Responses route, with one `WorkExecutionBackend` call site.
- **Deleted:**
  - the uncalled loose Responses ingress decoder (`WireIngress` and its helpers);
  - `hellas_gateway::run`;
  - the unused `hellas-adaptors` dependencies in cli and client.

body:
## Ligne 440 : le singulier des pluriels en -eaux

**Ce qui change pour le scripteur** : « Ils rangent leur bateaux au port » et « Elles ouvrent leur cadeaux » reçoivent maintenant « leurs » en rouge (exemples inventés). Avant, elles passaient sans marque, alors que « leur chevaux » était déjà corrigé.

**Cause** : pour s'assurer qu'un nom en -x ou -s est un vrai pluriel, quatre règles cherchaient son singulier. Pour -aux, elles ne tentaient que -al (chevaux → cheval). Gâteaux, bateaux, cadeaux (-eau + x) passaient donc pour des non-pluriels, et la règle se taisait.

**Réparation** (`extension/dys-core.js` ≡ `app/omega-pendu.html`) : une fonction commune `_sgPl440` tente -al, puis le mot sans sa dernière lettre. Elle sert à :
- leur / leurs (`rLeur`, l'adjectif sauté et le palier) ;
- c'est / ces (`cestCesVig`) ;
- le nombre du déterminant (`rDetNumber`).

**Mesure** (produit entier, 43 094 passages : 3 corpus dys, leurs versions corrigées, UD ; contre la ligne 416) : aucune marque ne change. La tournure n'est pas dans les corpus ; la preuve est dans les tests.

**Tests**
- `dictee/recall_comportements.json` : 2 corrections (non détectées par l'ancien moteur) et 1 phrase sans fausse marque.
- Texte neuf T69 (bilan d'un atelier pâtisserie avec des enfants), avec « leur gâteaux » : 7 fautes trouvées sur 7, aucune fausse marque.

Trouvé par le texte neuf T59 (ligne 426).

dev.sh : 146/147. Le contrôle rouge est la sonde d'accessibilité dans un vrai Chrome : « Espace sur une correction n'ouvre pas la carte ». Relancée seule deux fois : verte deux fois. C'est un raté passager de l'ouverture de la carte, qu'on avait déjà vu une fois sur une autre sonde Chrome ; la ligne ne touche pas au clavier. Puis un vieux commentaire reformulé sur une ligne modifiée (sans effet) : reconstruction et contrôles ciblés relancés, verts. Empilée sur la ligne 416, rebasée sur main après sa fusion #1235.

## The picture | First phone screen | "More on this story" opened | |---|---| | | | _Caption — `/app/` at 390, from `npm run shoot:landing` over the checked-in Nov 6 edition, dates cut as of Sun Nov 8. Desktop frame: `docs/shots/landing/landing-desktop.jpg`._ ## Summary - Sign-in opens the day's market news at `/app/`: key facts and coming reports first, the rest on tap. - News takes the first tab; the Leaderboard keeps its route, via Profile's league card. #7089 aligns to §5.9. - Part of #7077 (slice 1 of 3); the edition is hand-written until #6949 slice 5. Review live: `/app/`
Why, acceptance & the weeds ### Why Eric, #7018 round 0: "I don't care for the leaderboard as the landing page." Round 1 picked the news with a mission narrator, and asked for progressive disclosure: "flag the key elements of this event … withold the bulk of the information until a user expresses interest." ### Acceptance criteria (EARS), this slice - WHEN a member with an account signs in, the app SHALL open the landing page at `/app/`; the Leaderboard keeps its route (c1). Verified by `e2e/landing.spec.ts` › gives News the first tab…, and `e2e/leaderboard.spec.ts` › an old /?by= bookmark still opens the leaderboard. - Each story SHALL show key facts first (what moved, by how much, its dated reports on its own tile) and open the rest only on a tap (c3). Verified by `e2e/landing.spec.ts` › holds the rest of a story until the member taps for more. - Each story SHALL carry its headline in the news voice and at most one narrator line, with no franchise phrase (c4). Verified by `tests/domain/edition.spec.ts` › holds the narrator to one original line. - The copy SHALL never frame a time as good to buy; every base rate SHALL show its sample size; modeled says "modeled"; reported causes are marked unconfirmed (c7). Verified by `tests/domain/edition.spec.ts` › refuses a base rate with no sample size, › refuses copy that frames a time as good to buy, › marks every line. - At 390 the first screen SHALL show the lead story's key facts (c8's news half). Verified by `e2e/landing.spec.ts` › opens on the news…. - Not in this slice: the ask box and the per-story ask (c2, c5: slice 2), quest slots (c6: slice 3). ### What changed - `src/domain/edition.ts` + `src/domain/editions/2026-11-06.json`: the edition record and its loader. The loader enforces the honesty rules above, and it reads nothing at import (the study worlds run the server graph in an older corpus where these directories don't exist). - `GET /api/edition` (`content-api-routes.ts`): the latest edition on or before today in New York, with past dates dropped from each story and from What's next. Behind the existing auth gate; market data only. - `app/src/routes/index.tsx`: the landing page. `app/src/shell/edition-story.tsx`: one story tile. `app/src/styles/edition.css`. - `__root.tsx`: the first tab is now **News** (`/`); the Leaderboard tab is gone. - `docs/members/triage.json` + `coverage.md`: `/` is a living screen now, not a redirect. Architecture source and page updated for the browser container. - `scripts/shoot/landing.mjs` (`npm run shoot:landing`): the surface's shoot script. ### Design notes & trade-offs - **As merged, this PR predates `docs/IA.md` §5.9 (#7081).** It shipped the tab as "News" with facts before reports. The follow-up #7089 renames the tab to "Chronicles" and puts reports first, with a ▲ ▼ ∿ shape on each move. - **The edition is a server record, not copy in the app.** When #6949 slice 5 writes editions, it writes this same file shape and the page doesn't change. - **An edition's age is always on the page.** The masthead says whose close the news describes ("As of the Fri, Nov 6 close"). Once the edition is more than a weekend old, a plain line adds how many days old it is. The kicker never claims "today's". - **A story is written as of its close.** A report whose day has passed stays on the tile, struck through and worded "passed", so "three reports are inbound" still counts three. What's next looks forward, so a passed item leaves it. - **The lead story pairs the fall with the coming reports, and never calls it a buy.** The +5% take-profit base rate is shown with n=65, along with the fact that the rule made money 52% of the time against 53% from any day. - **A side effect on `/u/:id`:** its way back to the Leaderboard was the tab. Browser back and Profile's league card remain, which is the door #7077 named. ### Verification - [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:app` - [x] `npm run lint` - [x] `npm test` (15,638 passed), `npm run test:app` (2,238 passed) - [x] `npx playwright test`: 219 passed. Two page baselines were re-cut on purpose: `e2e/feedback.spec.ts-snapshots/feedback-page-chromium-linux.png` and `e2e/settings.spec.ts-snapshots/settings-page-chromium-linux.png`. The first tab now reads News, which leaves the status line room for its full widget, and the Feedback baseline also predated #6325's copy. - [x] Screenshots: `npm run shoot:landing`, phone first - [x] `/code-review medium` before opening. Fixed: passed reports, the age line, franchise false positives (Enterprise, Vulcan), non-object entries named, duplicate rows refused, `market-day.ts` and `book-events` `dayLabel` reused, a plain error line. The writer in #6949 slice 5 owns skipping bad output. (b) "a same-day item whose time has passed stays in What's next until midnight": its time is printed beside it, and cutting by time of day waits on the writer's timestamps. ### Risk & rollback - Reversible in one revert: the Leaderboard route is untouched, and `/` going back to a redirect restores the old landing. - No member data is read or written, and no order path is touched. ### Follow-ups - Slice 2: the ask box (your question first, two quick questions as fallbacks) and the per-story ask "Is this a chance to buy?", wiring #7041. - Slice 3: quest slots by source, filled by #7028. author: wishborn
body:
Tynn #445: ADF A1, the first story of #392. Spec: `.ai/plans/specs/adf-sdk.md`, story A1, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07 (q_f0804e19).

## What changed
New `src/core/catalog.ts` (pure, no Node imports) and `test/catalog.test.ts`. Nothing else in the app reads the catalog yet; that is A2 onward.

- **One envelope** for every element a builtin, plugin or GApp contributes: `id`, `kind`, `version`, `packageId`, `source` (`builtin` / `plugin` / `gapp`), `aliases`, `docs`, `reach` (scopes, host or client side, requiresWindow, remote policy), `permissions` (capabilities plus a network allow-list) and a kind `payload`.
- **One validator**, `validateDefinition`. It is strict: an unknown key is refused by name. Payloads are checked per kind:
  - a tool needs a handler id and an object input schema;
  - an editor needs the extensions it claims and a vetted Fancy editor;
  - a panel needs a vetted Fancy component;
  - a flow node needs an executor;
  - a recipe needs its steps.

  Only plain JSON is accepted (no functions), and what gets registered is frozen.
- **Atomic registration with revisions** (`Catalog.register`):
  - The whole package is validated first, and every contribution must belong to it.
  - Ids and aliases are checked against every other package.
  - Then the package is replaced whole and the revision moves by one. On any failure nothing is registered and the revision stays.
  - `unregister` removes a package at the next revision.
- **Decisions encoded:**
  - (1) the kinds are what a plugin or GApp can contribute: tool, panel, editor, recipe, flow-node, page, overlay, provider, service-engine.
  - (3) Genie 1's never-run families (flyout, modal, wizard, workstation-page, workspace-settings-page) are accepted as reserved.
  - (4) network egress is an allow-list that defaults to none.
  - (2) aliases resolve to their definition, so today's `ai.genie.*` names can sit beside a restored namespace.

## Red first (CI)
- `b62f946d`, the test alone, before `catalog.ts` existed (push run 42436424131, PR run 42436429725). `typecheck + unit` failed with `test/catalog.test.ts(2,93): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../src/core/catalog.js'`. That is the failure the acceptance criteria call for.
- `0d9055ef`: the implementation.

## Not proven / left for later stories
- Nothing reads the catalog yet. Builtins registering through it is A2, the move into genie-host is A3, the protocol is A4, projections are A5, lifecycle is A6.
- Payload checks for page, overlay, provider, service-engine and the reserved kinds are "an object" only, until the story that makes each one run.
- Genie 1's `contributes` manifest shape is normalized in B, not here.

author: elrey72011
body:
## Why
The NCAAB Pinnacle plan (D19 B market-skill, `model: pinnacle`) is the next step toward validated picks. Its calibration reached 36/40 decided spread games on 2026-11-07. As built, a frozen plan would have been slow and could have failed on sample size:
- **Entry quote.** Bound predictions used each game's first canonical US quote (`_reference_quotes`). Pinnacle had the same line there for only 30 of 139 recent NCAAB games, and that price rarely cleared the bet rule (EV ≥ 2% against Pinnacle). On the 2026-11-07 slate, NCAAB candidates beating Pinnacle by 2% numbered 0–2 per export (about 48 games). At that rate 50 bets take roughly 25–50 days per window, for two windows.
- **Window size.** `games_per_day` counted every game over a fixed 14 days. That undercounts a new season (NCAAB capture started about 2026-11-04) and includes games a Pinnacle plan cannot predict.
- **Scoring (found while tracing settlement).** `prospective_result` holds one result per (event, market, side), settled at whichever quote is settled first, and `_cohort` grades every prediction against that row. A prediction at another line was graded at the wrong line.

## Changes
- **`pinnacle_model.plan_quotes`** picks a Pinnacle plan's entry quote per game with a fixed, price-only rule:
  - the canonical side (home team or Over), so each game is settled once per side;
  - the **earliest capture** in which Pinnacle and a US book post the same line;
  - the book whose better side has the highest EV against Pinnacle's no-vig price (ties: price, then book), with both of its sides posted, since the market-skill gate uses them;
  - pregame, verified, half or whole lines only, never Pinnacle itself.
  
  `predict` uses it by default. Decision capture still passes its own `select`.
- **`pinnacle_model.plan_games_per_day`** counts plan-predictable games per day over the days actually observed. `draft_bound_plan` sizes a Pinnacle plan's windows with it; research-model plans are unchanged.
- **`prospective_evidence._outcome_at_quote_line`**: when a game's score settlement was made at a different line than the prediction's quote, the prediction is scored from the same verified final score at its own line. Other result sources are unchanged.

It affects only predictions of a plan bound to the Pinnacle model, none of which exist yet; decision capture is unchanged. No pick, gate, stake or app change. `prospective_research_models.py` is not edited.

## Testing
- New `tests/test_pinnacle_plan_selection.py` (5):
  - earliest capture with a shared line and the best-EV book;
  - away-side value still enters at the canonical quote, and one-sided books are skipped;
  - no entry after the start or before `now`;
  - window rate over the observed days (6 plan games in 3 days = 2/day, not 6/14);
  - line-aware scoring: win, loss and push at other lines; unchanged at the same line and for non-score results.
- 179 tests pass across the Pinnacle, calibration, evidence, bound-plan, decision-capture, market-skill, research loop, scheduler, research picks and readiness modules.
- `protected_change_guard.py`: PASS, no existing-test changes. NCAAF runtime binding: OK.

**Owner note:** draft and freeze the NCAAB Pinnacle plan only after this merges. A draft made before it uses the old entry rule and window size.

author: trissim
body:
The actual Termux startup rejected its registry's ancestors: `/data` and `/data/data` are Android system UID/GID 1000 with mode 0771, and the app's `files` directory is mode 0771 under its isolated app UID/GID. The POSIX root-or-current-owner check rejected that native layout.

Platform now owns trusted ancestor principals and untrusted directory write bits. Android declares its system identity and isolated primary group. The filesystem role and registry guard derive those facts from the selected platform; their separate sticky-directory policies and owner-only registry-root check remain intact. Permission checks receive the observed stat record so they can distinguish group identities, not just mode bits.

Evidence:

- Actual phone traceback: `Private registry guard has an untrusted directory ancestor` during native root preparation.
- Regression before: 1 failed / 6 passed. It reproduces the phone's observed ancestor UID/GID/modes through both the registry and path owners.
- After: 59 passed / 1 skipped across Android platform, ancestor policy, private path and declaration suites.
- Other app owners, foreign writable groups, world writes, symlinks and non-private registry roots remain rejected. Linux does not inherit Android's system/group authority.

Android's declarations: [AID_SYSTEM](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/refs/heads/main/libcutils/include/private/android_filesystem_config.h), [app sandbox](https://source.android.com/docs/security/app-sandbox).

author: robertscholey98
body:
Pressing Cmd+R in Brainstorm's window left it on "This page needs Brainstorm's window. Open Brainstorm from its app, or run a brainstorm command to start it." until the app restarted.

The window gets its UI token in the URL's hash. The page keeps the token in memory and wipes it from the URL, so any second load of the page (a reload, or a renderer coming back after a crash) has no token.

- `src/electron/main.ts`: when the main frame loads the app's origin without `#ui=`, or its renderer dies, main loads the URL that carries the token again.
- `src/renderer/main.tsx`: that URL differs from the reloaded one only by its hash, so Chromium treats the load as a hash change, not a new page. With no token at start, the page waits for the token to arrive as a hash change and then renders the app.

## Verification

- `npm run verify:7` adds two checks. One reloads the window and one crashes its renderer, and each expects the top bar back within 10 s. Before the fix both failed; with it, verify:7 prints `VERIFIED`.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `npx vitest run`: 336 pass, and `test/design.test.ts` fails on Windows. Git's `core.autocrlf` turns `src/renderer/design.css` into CRLF on checkout, and the test compares it with LF output. This PR touches neither file.

author: jvictormaynard
body:
## What changed

Opening Settings now reuses an Electron window. The same Electron process renders the compact React pill. Python/Qt continues to own recording, providers, storage, text insertion and global hotkeys; a bounded, private JSON-lines bridge connects the two processes.

The pill restores compact recording/cancel states, waveform and transition animations. It fixes dragging at fractional DPI and restores ALT+T, native picker focus, arrow navigation, Enter selection and Escape cancellation. The native QML fallback, file-import panel and explicit legacy Tauri build remain available.

CI selects checks from affected modules and their dependencies. UI-only changes run Settings unit/browser checks and the Windows Electron lane. Engine changes also select Python/Qt checks. Planner/workflow changes, unknown paths and failed diff discovery select the full plan. Main retains the full backstop and the strict `CI required` aggregate.

## Why

The desktop shell migration must preserve the existing engine and portable updater while reducing repeated UI startup. CI must validate each affected module without rebuilding unrelated products on every small change.

The selection model follows the inspected T3 Code ownership/dependency approach. The Windows Electron lane caches the pinned runtime download, packages the shell and runs a native smoke test. The portable EXE embeds the complete runtime, license inventory and per-file manifest so the existing atomic updater can replace it safely.

## Validation

- Shared local Python, Qt, Windows, Settings unit/browser, policy, workflow and static checks passed. Settings: 81 unit tests and 133 browser tests passed.
- Electron bridge/lifecycle tests, packaged Windows smoke, frozen startup, embedded payload/license verification and four updater recovery cases passed. npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities.
- After integrating current main: Settings types/unit checks, a fresh production build and all five production boot tests passed.
- Independent requirements and engineering reviews completed. Fixed their runtime-cache and `-SkipGitHooks` forwarding findings.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/jvictormaynard/clarify/actions/runs/42438765801): all 27 checks passed on `7abb9a7`, including `CI required`, Windows installer lifecycle and native iOS validation. This workflow/planner change selected the full plan; later small changes can use selective checks.
- Native Windows captures and motion evidence are retained locally outside Git. No GitHub attachment upload is available through the connected tools, so before/after images and the recording are not attached.
- Native smoke covers UI lifecycle and keyboard/drag behavior with isolated profiles and fake providers. Real-provider dictation and final release acceptance remain separate gates.

## Safety and privacy

- [x] No API keys, private transcripts, selected text, personal paths, or config files are included
- [x] Retained tests add necessary coverage; affected redundant tests were removed or consolidated
- [x] Documentation changes have a lasting user, operational, or design purpose
- [x] PR-only evidence, scratch files, runtime state, and local reports are outside the diff
- [x] New third-party code or assets have compatible licenses and are documented

## Notes for reviewers

- The full Electron runtime increases portable package size. The complete embedded tree preserves the existing single-EXE update contract; every embedded file is checked against its manifest.
- The local Apple-flag experiment is excluded. This PR uses the existing project SVG flags.
- No public release is created by opening this PR.

author: kentarokamiyajp
body:
## What

`updateTaskFromTable` (the table / board inline edit) now loads the full task with the **row's own `updatedAt` as the freshness baseline**, the same guard the preview's loaders already pass.

## Why

The full copy it loads is the base of a full PUT, which re-sends the milestone, parent, body, links and more of whatever it holds. Without a baseline, a cached copy older than a move or an edit made elsewhere was accepted and its old values were written back. This is one of the paths by which MIP-1168 (a stale copy putting MIP-598's tree back into the wrong milestone) can happen. The real fix is on the server (genos-api #661: a milestone that contradicts the parent is ignored). This is the second line of defence for every other field.

## Verified

- New test: the loader is asked for a copy at least as new as the row. Mutation-checked: without the baseline it fails. The existing start-date and save-refusal tests pass (20 in the three files). `tsc` and prettier clean.
- Not looked at in a browser: no visible change. The cost is one extra GET when the cached copy really is older than the row.

## Limits

I could not prove this was the path that broke MIP-598 (it was a description edit in the preview). The other loaders without a baseline (Recents/activity rows, notes preview, thread task meta, task modal) are read paths for display; whether a save can start from them needs its own look.

Does not close MIP-1168 (branch carries no id).

body:
## Qué fallaba

Seis de las once emisoras no sonaban: **Chill, Beats suaves, Voces suaves, Atmósfera, Espacio profundo y Meditación** (las de SomaFM). Usaban la dirección corta `https://ice.somafm.com/<canal>`, que SomaFM ya no sirve: responde **404**.

## Qué cambia

- **Catálogo** (`data/Station.kt`): las seis pasan a la dirección completa `https://ice2.somafm.com/<canal>-128-mp3`. Las otras cinco ya funcionaban y no cambian. Quien ya tenga la app recibe las direcciones nuevas al actualizar, sin perder su orden ni sus favoritas (`StationRepository.mergeWithCatalog`).
- **Flujo nuevo "Emisoras"** (`.github/workflows/streams.yml`), que se lanza al cambiar el catálogo y a mano:
  1. *Sonda de red* (`tools/streams/check_streams.py`): conecta a cada emisora en 3 rondas, igual que el móvil (solo HTTPS, sin seguir redirecciones a http), y analiza el audio con ffprobe.
  2. *Reproducción en Android* (`StationPlaybackTest`): reproduce cada emisora en un emulador (API 34) con el mismo reproductor y los mismos reintentos que `RadioPlayerService`. Tiene que empezar a sonar en 20 s como máximo y seguir sonando 8 s.
- `tools/streams/candidates.txt`: emisoras de reserva comprobadas, para reponer una que deje de funcionar.
- README: sección "Comprobar las emisoras".

## Resultado de la primera comprobación (catálogo anterior)

| Emisora | Red (3 rondas) | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Lo-Fi | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ suena en 1,3 s |
| Clásica (NPO Radio 4) | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ 1,3 s |
| Ambiental (Frisky Chill) | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ 1,0 s |
| Jazz (Jazz24) | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ 1,3 s |
| Dormir (Ambient Sleeping Pill) | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ 1,5 s |
| Las 6 de SomaFM con `ice.somafm.com/<canal>` | ❌ 404 | ❌ 404 |
| Las mismas 6 con `ice2.somafm.com/<canal>-128-mp3` | ✅ 3/3 | ✅ entre 0,5 y 1,0 s |

Ejecución: https://github.com/Tolstoy789/Mi-Zenradio/actions/runs/42434501830

Este pull request vuelve a lanzar la comprobación con el catálogo corregido.

## Otro hallazgo, sin cambiar aquí

La prueba en Android también muestra que la app no llega a enseñar el título de la canción, aunque las emisoras sí lo envían (metadatos ICY): `liveTrackTitle()` devuelve null porque el título del `MediaItem` (el nombre de la emisora) tiene prioridad sobre el de ICY en `player.mediaMetadata`. Queda para otro cambio.

author: willishoke
body:
Phase 6 of the faces-and-fields plan. D7, as decided: a parametric surface's bundle stores **the request that builds it**, not samples of it.

## What

- **Schema.** A manifest's geometry is a choice, told apart by key (`BundleManifest`): a landscape (`Manifest`, keys unchanged), or, when it has a `surface` key, a parametric surface (`SurfaceManifest`). The second holds the `SurfaceRequest`, its layers, presets and provenance, with no arrays and no axes. A polyhedron can come in later as a third geometry the same way (phase 7, not built here).
- **`SurfaceRequest`** moves into Core and gets its JSON plus `check()`. `check()` refuses malformed requests and names the bad number. What only building can find (an unknown system, an expression that doesn't parse) is refused when the bundle is read.
- **Layers on the surface face.** The `surface` face, refused in a landscape manifest, is allowed in parametric manifests only:
  - contours of u, v and height on any surface;
  - contours of |f| and arg f where a function is painted (sn, periodic, relief), with `belowTruncation` allowed only in relief;
  - coordinate curves, linear curves, fold curves, and a trajectory on a forced torus.
  
  Hatching, walls, edges and dumped layers are refused. The layers restyle the drawing (`SurfaceDrawing.restyled`). An edit reuses only what its request drew, so a drawing still depends on its request alone.
- **sn in relief** becomes a request shape (`relief`), so `surface sn --relief` builds through `SurfaceDrawing` and can be saved. Its slider in the app is still 11d.
- **CLI:**
  - `surface … --save PATH` writes the bundle, with the camera and resolution it bakes at.
  - `bake`, `depth` and `inspect` read either kind of bundle.
  - `contract` round-trips either kind.
- **App:** `Document.State.surface` folds into `.ready(Opened)`, which holds a landscape's or a surface's bundle.
  - `SurfaceSection` edits the bundle's request.
  - A surface's contour families get the level slider (restyle).
  - ⌘S writes either kind, with contours at the levels on screen.
  - Headless: `--surface NAME --save`, plus `--set` / `--levels` / `--save` / `--bake` on a bundle.

## Schema: stays 3

The addition is additive. No key of a landscape's manifest changed, every existing bundle reads and writes byte for byte as before, and nothing outside the repo writes schema 3. A bump would have rewritten every fixture's version number and bought nothing. A reader from before this PR refuses the new manifest (`json: Manifest has no key 'axes'`) rather than misreading it.

## Gates

- `scripts/check.sh --clean`: all green, 1630 checks.
- 27 reference bakes byte-identical to a clean release build of 69bb98b, including `sn`, `sn-relief`, `torus`, `forced` and `periodic`. `sn --relief` now goes through the request.
- Goldens: unchanged except the new `contract/surface.kurven`. Gallery: byte-identical.
- For each of sn, torus, forced, periodic and sn --relief: `kurven-cli surface K --save` then `kurven-cli bake` gives 69bb98b's `surface K` SVG byte for byte. The same holds with non-default flags: camera, resolution, linear curves, coordinate curves, and relief repeat/turn/floor/soft.
- App: the sn torus opened, saved by the app, reopened and baked with `Kurven --bake` matches `kurven-cli surface sn`'s SVG byte for byte, and the app's saved manifest matches the CLI's byte for byte.
- New tests, each shown to fail on a deliberate break:
  - every shape, saved, reopened and baked, matches the request's bake;
  - open, restyle, save, reopen;
  - a request edit after a restyle builds the same drawing as from scratch;
  - refusals of malformed requests and layers;
  - the contract bundle decodes and draws.

## How the app's save path was exercised

`--surface NAME` opens a SwiftUI window; I measured one on screen with `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`. A bundle passed as a bare path opens none. So the windowless chain is:
1. `kurven-cli surface sn --save a.kurven` (same `SurfaceBundle`/`SurfaceManifest` writer the app uses);
2. `KurvenApp a.kurven --save b.kurven`: the app's own `Document.load`, then `saveBundle` (the ⌘S path);
3. `KurvenApp b.kurven --bake c.svg`.

Zero app windows appeared during steps 2 and 3. `--surface sn --save` (with its window) writes the same bundle byte for byte. The app restyle path was run the same way: `--levels mag_major=5 --levels ang_minor=4 --save`, reopen, `--bake`. The result matches `kurven-cli bake` of the saved bundle. kurven-test can't import the app target, so the test suite holds the same transitions on `SurfaceBundle` values.

## After review (71ad43d, c526f47, b478fa4, b0cfb94)

- **Bounds.** Layers are checked against their request. Coordinate curves must be counts. A linear curve needs a finite slope and at least one turn of one strand, and may take at most 2^24 vertices.
  - Every count that drives work is capped: 2^25 surface samples, reckoned from the grid and the radii; a function grid of 4096; relief repeats of 16 each way; a fit of 100000 time units at 64 harmonics; trajectory and coordinate-curve vertices.
  - JSON integers outside `Int` (such as 1e30) are refused instead of trapping.
  - Duplicate layer names are refused.
  - A bundle with no presets is refused when it is read, by both the app and the CLI.
  - Refusals name the manifest key (`surface.shape.modulus`); the CLI names the flag (`--samples`, `--grid`).
  - Every case in the reviewer's `probe/bad/` is a refusal test. Run through `kurven-cli bake`, none traps.
- **Request edits keep the file's layers** (`SurfaceDrawing.keeping`). The request's own curves (coordinate curves, linear curve, trajectory, folds) follow the edit. Level counts are keyed by layer name.
- **Restyle from samples taken once.** `PeriodicTorus.Drawing.contours` keeps the sampled function and its refiner, and carries them through repeat, re-placement and relief.

  Timings from the reviewer's `perf.sh`, under the guard (app headless: open, set levels, save):

  | Bundle | Action | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | relief 1×1 | open + save | 0.67 s | 0.68 s |
  | relief 1×1 | one family's levels | 0.90 s | 0.67 s |
  | relief 1×1 | four families' levels | 1.80 s | 0.95 s |
  | relief 8×2 | open + save | 5.38 s | 5.40 s |
  | relief 8×2 | one family's levels | 9.85 s | 5.38 s |
  | relief 8×2 | four families' levels | 24.27 s | 6.42 s |
  | relief 8×2 | open with its own levels | 9.90 s | 5.47 s |

  Every saved bundle is byte-identical before and after.
- **Level slider.** It now has a minimum of 2 and resamples over the family's own range (`KurvenBundle.levels(of:count:)`), so a family saved at the slider's minimum keeps its range. This applies to landscapes too.
- **Smaller fixes.**
  - `load()` drops queued edits.
  - sn, periodic and relief now draw the coordinate curves their request asks for. The app toggle used to do nothing; no reference drawing asks for them.
- **Contract fixtures** now cover torus, periodic, forced (with its trajectory) and relief, in a fixtures-only commit.
- **`check.sh` app step:** the windowless app chain compared with `cmp` against the CLI's output; a `--levels` count set before a `--set` edit stays on its family; the contract surface, edited, keeps its levels and extra contours. It runs in about 2 s.
- **Re-gated:**
  - `check.sh --clean`: all green, 1669 checks, including the app step.
  - 27 bakes identical to 69bb98b; gallery unchanged; all 10 contract bundles round-trip.
  - The reviewer's 17 round-trip flag sets: all identical to base.
  - App gate: ok.
  - Each new check fails on a deliberate break.

## Found, not fixed

- `facing` is not a `ContourField`. Fold curves remain its level 0.
- `kurven-cli surface sn --relief` now prints the generic surface summary instead of its old relief summary.
- `preview`, `bench` and `flicker` still read landscapes only.
- A relief's amplitude has no control in the app (11d).

author: umege
body:
Fixes #3833

## Problem

On the v1.x line, closing a stateful streamable-HTTP session the normal way (the client's
`streamablehttp_client` context exits and sends `DELETE`) logs an `ERROR` with a full traceback:

```
ERROR mcp.server.streamable_http: Error in standalone SSE writer
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ... standalone_sse_writer
    async for event_message in standalone_stream_reader:
anyio.ClosedResourceError
```

`StreamableHTTPServerTransport.terminate()` closes every request stream, including the standalone
GET stream (`GET_STREAM_KEY`), while `standalone_sse_writer` is still iterating it. The resulting
`anyio.ClosedResourceError` is caught by the writer's generic `except Exception: logger.exception(...)`,
so every successfully-closed session leaves an ERROR traceback in the server log and buries real
errors. Nothing actually fails — the calls succeed and the server keeps serving.

## Fix

Catch `anyio.ClosedResourceError` separately in `standalone_sse_writer` and log it at `DEBUG`: a
stream closed under the writer during a client-initiated termination is a normal end of the stream.
All other exceptions keep the existing `logger.exception("Error in standalone SSE writer")`.

## Tests

New in-process regression test in `tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py`:
`test_termination_does_not_log_an_error_in_the_standalone_sse_writer`

It drives a GET request straight into a `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` (no server process needed),
waits for the standalone GET stream to register, calls `terminate()` (exactly what a `DELETE` does)
and asserts that `mcp.server.streamable_http` emitted no record at `ERROR` or above.

On the unpatched v1.x source the test reproduces the issue and fails with the traceback above; with
the fix it passes. Validation on this machine (Windows, Python 3.12):

```
pytest tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py -q -k "does_not_log_an_error_in_the_standalone" -n0
# 1 passed  (1 failed on unpatched source)

pytest tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py -q -k "streamable_http_transport or termination or idle" -n0
# 13 passed

ruff check src/mcp/server/streamable_http.py tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py   # All checks passed!
ruff format --check src/mcp/server/streamable_http.py tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py  # clean
```

## AI assistance

Tool(s) used: DeepSeek Harness (coding agent). The agent reproduced the exact traceback through the
transport's public ASGI path, added the regression test first (red on unpatched source), split the
`ClosedResourceError` handling out of the generic branch and ran the focused suite plus ruff. I
reviewed the diff, the log-level choice and the red/green output, and take responsibility for the
change.

Every catalog run since 2026-11-05 failed at **Yu-Gi-Oh fingerprints** with `ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined`. The run then skipped the Pokémon and One Piece fingerprints, the photo small copies, the problem and parity checks, and saving the base snapshot.

**Checked:** I loaded the built `cv-*.mjs` under `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 electron`. Without the fix it throws the same ReferenceError; with it, cv initialises and makes a Mat. I'll also run the catalog workflow from this branch.

author: elroynbenjamins
body:
## Veldryn class-stat rebalancing — implementation and refinement

**Role identity without gear resets**: Shared `effectiveStats` now applies budget-conserving, monotone class weighting to the flat equipment Attack and Defense pool. Attack share for evenly balanced gear: Ironwarden 45%, Bastion 40%, Dreadguard 50%, Wayfinder 60%, Ravager 65%, Hexweaver 60%, Knife Dancer 65%, Dawnkeeper 45%, Stonecaller 55%. These are not final stat caps; player build choices, class base stats, buffs, gems and sets remain significant. Saves, items, levels, equipment ownership and progression are untouched.

**Correct actual combat and comparisons**: Preserve fractional Attack/Defense bonuses through the final effective stat calculation, avoiding per-stage ceilings that hid small enhancements. Character view, equipment inspector/preview, solo PvE, and server-verified co-op/Echo/regional snapshots consume the same source. Co-op engine and frozen-snapshot validations are not weakened.

**Class / regional sustain polish**:
- Ravager Bloodrush converts up to **1% of Attack** into actual after-kill HP recovery, but only against damage exceeding the area's minimum hourly attrition; cannot negate lethal blows or trivialize ordinary food.
- Knife Dancer Blade Rhythm emphasizes agility with **12% incoming damage avoidance**, distinct from tank armor. Its Attack/Defense equipment target remains 65/35.
- Regional missing-tier attrition increased minimally **0.60 → 0.62**, retaining hard requirements to make undergeared hunting less efficient. Nine-class equipment/boss sustain tests retained intact.

**App-wide build maintenance during validation**: repaired duplicate gameplay translation entry and missing localized Guild Projects, Quest, Muster, Bank and Party/Dungeon text; corrected stale baseline test strings for Guild Raid’s live clock, Companion verified completion, equipment sets and startup stats; made Roadmap ScrollView indicator settings consistent; updated online Sunscar Alchemy test setup to current recipe costs. All additions have translations and safe interpolation; player-entered text remains unchanged.

**Validation and release**: Focused nine-class Chapter 1, regional food/sustain, legal equipment and co-op/dungeon verification have passed on previous candidate heads. Generated gameplay and co-op Edge bundles synchronized via the trusted backend build, and the temporary workflow was deleted. Full final-head CI remains the release gate; no migrations needed. Do not deploy client/server independently or rewrite frozen runs.

- Phong cách có 8 thẻ ảnh, chip đã chọn trong khung nhập, tự đóng sau lựa chọn. Khung hình có 6 thẻ tỷ lệ (3 cột × 2 hàng).
- Vùng chọn nằm trên input, tự căn dưới topbar và giới hạn chiều cao theo viewport để chừa ô nhập/CTA; danh sách cuộn riêng, keyboard/focus/Escape và reduced-motion.
- Ảnh có pan/zoom nhẹ và hover zoom. Tám PNG mới copy nguyên bản từ ảnh đính kèm của chủ dự án, có manifest và nhãn minh họa; không đổi token.
- Backend whitelist `oil-painting`, `3d`, `comic`, thêm chỉ dẫn chất liệu toàn cảnh sau dịch; giữ prompt gốc, chủ thể/hành động/bố cục và chữ/thoại được yêu cầu. Loại ràng buộc cấm chữ/bong bóng thoại trong preset comic.
- Giữ validation độ dài cuối 2048 UTF-16 trước quota, ownership/CSRF, payload fingerprint và replay; lưu/khôi phục settings; saving retry dùng checkpoint mà không thêm inference.

## Kiểm tra local
- FE/BE build đạt; diff check đạt.
- Unit: 54 đạt, 1 skip vì thiếu MONGODB_TEST_URI riêng.
- Full isolated integration chạy tuần tự: 20 đạt / 0 skip; có HTTP/API thật, MongoDB memory replica set riêng, provider/storage giả lập.
- Strict typecheck hai file test preset đạt. Ba preset đều kiểm tra validation/auth/ownership, replay/conflict, quota, translated/submitted prompt, history/detail, private download và phục hồi lỗi saving qua worker mới.

- Luồng browser riêng với API thật + DB tạm xác nhận 3D + 16:9 lưu/khôi phục/khóa khi queued, một POST chủ động và 0 provider calls. Các ảnh minh chứng dùng dữ liệu QA có nhãn.

Chưa nghiệm thu chất lượng ảnh FLUX/Cloudinary live cho ba preset; không gọi cloud thật hoặc bật billing trong test. Full browser E2E tổng quát chưa đạt trọn bộ (timeout ở phần tài khoản/điều hướng; các luồng thay đổi được kiểm tra riêng). Không coi PR này là hoàn tất checklist nghiệm thu chung #17.

author: adriyansyah-mf
body:
## Summary
Stage B2 of Web Protection: endpoint agents (Linux **and** Windows) enforce the B1 blocklist. Stacked on #125 (B1). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-08-web-protection-b2.md`; operations: `docs/operations/web-protection.md`.

New Go package `agent/internal/webblock`:
- **Sync** (`store.go`): delta pages from `/api/ingest/web-blocklist`, echoing the `rules` marker; reset on group change; saved in the state dir and enforced offline.
- **Hosts sinkhole** (`hosts*.go`): managed `# BEGIN/END ADSIEM WEBBLOCK` block in `/etc/hosts` or `drivers\etc\hosts`.
  - Lines outside the block are never touched.
  - Domains are validated, so server data cannot inject lines.
  - Symlinks are followed; on a bind mount (EBUSY) the file is written in place.
  - On Windows the file is written in place, which keeps its ACL and read-only attribute.
  - Orphan markers are repaired, and the DNS cache is flushed after a change.
- **Per-endpoint CA** (`ca.go`, `cafs*`, `trust*`): generated automatically (ECDSA P-256, 10 years, path length 0, **ServerAuth-only EKU**).
  - The key is created with a protected ACL from the first byte: SYSTEM+Administrators on Windows, 0700/0600 on Linux, in `<state>/webblock`.
  - The CA is installed in the system trust store (`LocalMachine\Root`, `update-ca-certificates`, `update-ca-trust`); trust tools run with a process-group timeout.
  - Leaf certificates are minted only for blocked domains, with strict SNI checks.
- **Block page server** (`server.go`, `page.go`): listens on `127.84.0.1` and `[::1]`, ports 80/443.
  - Every request gets a 403 with the group's page, rendered byte-identically to the server preview.
  - Responses carry a strict CSP and bounded timeouts.
- **Events** (`event.go`): `web_block` events with a best-effort client process (`/proc` or `GetExtendedTcpTable`), rate-limited per domain/pid with a global cap of 120 lines per minute. New decoder `decoders/web_block.yaml`.
- **Controller** (`controller.go`): idempotent apply; repairs a tampered hosts file and a removed CA every 5 minutes; health is sent in the heartbeat.
- **Removal**: `siem-agent -webblock-cleanup` runs from the deb prerm and rpm `%preun` (after stopping the service) and from an MSI deferred SYSTEM action.

Server/dashboard: `web_block_health` stored per agent; `GET /api/web-blocks/agents`; Agents tab on the Web Protection page.

## Review notes
Every task went through spec and quality review; the CA and sanitising pieces were reviewed on the most capable model. Notable fixes from review:
- Windows CA key ACL race (critical, fixed).
- Hosts writes that broke symlinks and bind mounts.
- Trust-tool hangs.
- Uninstall ordering.
- Event floods.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./internal/webblock/... -race`; vet and builds for linux, windows and darwin
- [x] `tests/server-api` + `tests/evidence` (CI pytest pin): 431 passed; dashboard `tsc` + `vite build`
- [ ] CI Linux: `WEBBLOCK_E2E=1` end to end as root (hosts, CA in the system store, HTTP/HTTPS 403 page, event, clean removal)
- [ ] CI Windows: webblock unit tests + end to end elevated (first run of the Windows-only code)
- [ ] Manual: a Windows desktop with Chrome/Edge shows the custom page for a blocked HTTPS site

author: frenb
body:
Adds the last three steps `Install.ps1` did that `install.md` didn't:

- **13 `clients`** starts one supervised Unity client (`Start-ClientAtLogon.ps1 -N 1`) and waits up to 3 minutes for its ROS handshake. A client started before the current ros-server is restarted too. Failures show the end of `Player.log` to the `unity-client` catalog phase.
- **14 `autostart`** creates the same Startup-folder shortcut `Install.ps1` makes. It has an `uninstall` block that deletes the shortcut.
- **15 `firstjob`** queues the installer's 2,000-iteration TRAIN job (new `scripts/install/first-job.js`, the same document `Install.ps1` inserts) and waits for the trainer to pick it up and finish two iterations. Verify checks that TensorBoard shows scalars. Uses `phase=trainer timeout=50m`. Leave it out with `installzero install --skip firstjob` (needs installzero after 4446915).

How installzero ranks them: `clients` and `autostart` are machine-wide and ask for approval, because they stop and start processes and create a COM-made shortcut. `firstjob` only touches this project's containers and database, so it's project-tier.

This file runs one client; `Install.ps1 -Clients N` remains the way to run up to four.

Tested: `installzero install --plan` parses all 15 steps. On a dev PC with the stack running, the three detect blocks correctly reported "not done" (no client running, no shortcut, no installer job). Not yet run end to end; that's the clean-account test.

author: stephenstirling
body:
## Opening multi-part archives
Opened from **any** part, the whole set is read:
- RAR volumes: `name.part1.rar`, `name.part2.rar` … and the older `name.rar`, `name.r00`, `name.r01` …
- Split archives: `name.7z.001`, `.002` … (also split ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ …), read as one file
- Spanned ZIP: `name.z01`, `name.z02` … `name.zip`

A missing part is named ("film.part2.rar needs to be in the same folder"). The status bar and Archive info show how many parts there are, and the size and zip-bomb checks use all the parts together.

## Creating 7z and password-protected archives
- **7Z** is a new format in the New archive dialog.
- **Password (typed twice)** for ZIP and 7Z: AES-256. A 7z also hides its file names; a ZIP can't, and the dialog says Windows' built-in zip folders can't open an AES ZIP.
- Opening a 7z whose names are hidden now asks for the password (and says when it's wrong) instead of failing.

SharpCompress can't write either, so these go through 7-Zip's own **7za.exe** (7-Zip Extra 26.05, LGPL, official build from github.com/ip7z/7zip; hashes in `third-party/7-Zip/README.md`). It ships in a `7-Zip` folder beside Arca.exe with its licence, and the release signs it with Arca's certificate, which its licence allows. The password goes to 7za through its input, never on a command line other programs can see. Reading never uses 7za.

## Tests
Part finding (every naming style, missing parts), split ZIP and TAR.GZ read from any piece, 7z round trip, split 7z, password 7z (no password / wrong / right, with a non-ASCII password containing quotes), AES ZIP, and that TAR refuses a password.
