author: jykwon91
body:
## What

A talent calculator for WoW Forever: `/wow-forever/talents` (class picker) and `/wow-forever/talents/:class`.

- All 9 Classic classes, 3 trees each in the in-game 7 × 4 grid, with talent icons, rank counters (`r/max`) and prerequisite arrows (green once met).
- Click / tap adds a point. Right-click, a long press (touch / pen), or the details panel's − removes one. Each grid is a single Tab stop: arrow keys move, Enter adds, Shift+Enter removes.
- Classic rules (`lib/talents/talentRules.ts`):
  - a row opens at 5 points per row above it in that tree;
  - prerequisites need their ranks;
  - a point can't come out while a dependent talent or a lower row needs it;
  - the level stepper runs 10–60, with points = level − 9.
- Hover or keyboard focus shows a tooltip with the current and next rank. The picked talent's details panel shows the same, says why a change is blocked, and has 44 px − / + buttons.
- **Share:** the build is the URL, `?b=1-<tree1>-<tree2>-<tree3>&lvl=N`. Each talent is one digit, trailing zeros are dropped, `lvl` is omitted at 60, and every change replaces the history entry. "Copy link" uses `shareOrigin()`, so links made inside the Discord Activity point at the real site; there's also Reset. Decoding is strict: a link with a build this class can't have opens an empty build and says so.
- **Mobile (375 px):** one tree at a time behind tabs that show each tree's points; three columns from `lg`. Targets are at least 44 px, with no sideways scroll.
- Each class's data is its own lazy chunk (about 10 KB + 5 KB per class). The page has a skeleton loader, the left-nav item "Talents" (Sparkles icon), a What's new entry, and the provenance guide / trademark notice through `withSuggestFooter`.

## Design pass — every data point on the page

| Data point | Why it's here | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Class picker (9 links) | Choose the class; links so Back returns to the last class | `data/classes.ts` |
| Level (− / input / +) | Caps the points; floor = what's spent | URL `lvl` |
| Points spent / available, points left | Shows what's left to spend | derived |
| Build split (a / b / c) | The usual way players describe a build | derived |
| Copy link, Reset | Share the build / start over | URL |
| Tree name, icon, points | Which tree, and how far into it | Forever `TalentTab` |
| Talent icon, rank `r/max`, ring state | The calculator itself | Forever `Talent`, `SpellMisc` |
| Prerequisite arrows (met / unmet) | Why a talent is locked | Forever `Talent.PrereqTalent` |
| Tooltip: name, rank, current + next rank text, block reason | What a point does, before spending it | Forever spell text (Game files) |
| Details: same, plus − / +, "Changed in Forever. Classic: …" | Touch / keyboard way to edit; what Forever changed | Forever text (Game files badge), cmangos (Classic data badge) |
| Classic text in place of a rank Forever lacks, plus a note on a talent Forever changed | Most ranks would be blank otherwise | Classic Era wording + cmangos numbers (Classic data badge) |
| Classic Era name badge on 13 talents | Their name isn't in the Forever client | Classic Era `SpellName` |
| Footnote | Where each part comes from and what's missing | — |

Left out on purpose: talent "build guides" and recommended specs (nothing published for Forever), and any Wowhead or foreverchanges.pro data or links.

## Data

`python -m scripts.wow_talents.build --hotfix-cache <DBCache.bin>`, run from `backend/`, is also added to `wow_refresh` before the icons build.

- **Sources:** wago.tools `wowf 1.60.1.70790` (Talent, TalentTab, Spell, SpellName, SpellEffect, SpellMisc, SpellAuraOptions, SpellDuration, SpellRadius), layered client file → wago hotfixes → the operator's `DBCache.bin`, the same as the item build.
- **Token substitution:** `$s1`, `$o`, `$t`, `$d`, `$a`, `$x`, `$h`, `$n`, `$u`, `$l` plurals, `${expr}.N`, `$S` and conditionals are filled through the shared `scripts/wow_food/tooltip.py`, now extended and tested in `tests/test_wow_spell_tooltip.py`.
- **Classic text (comparison and fallback):** the Classic Era client's own tooltip wording (wago.tools `wow_classic_era 1.15.9.70576`: Spell, SpellName, SpellDuration, SpellRadius), filled with the 1.12 numbers from **[cmangos classic-db](https://github.com/cmangos/classic-db) `spell_template` at commit `ec4f596146be6467ea93c57397858e329e2db852`, licensed GPL-3.0**. `LICENSE` and `README.md` sit next to the data in `frontend/src/games/wow-forever/data/talents/classic/`. No cmangos code is copied. Each class file holds `talents` (ranks Forever changed) and `fallback` (ranks Forever doesn't have yet).
- **Dbd fix:** `dbd.py` now reads `$noninline,relation$` fields, which SpellEffect needs for the hotfix-cache decode.

### Does Forever differ from Classic? **Yes**

313 talents and 316 ranks have Forever text that differs from Classic's. A rank counts as changed only when Forever's text is complete and Classic's resolves fully. Examples:

- Arcane Focus: hit +2% (Classic: resist −2%)
- Blood Craze: 3% (Classic: 1%)
- Clever Traps: 30% (Classic: 15%)
- Initiative: 100% (Classic: 25%)

These ranks carry the "Changed in Forever" note.

### Data gaps

- **839 of 1,357 ranks aren't in the Forever client yet.** 834 of them now show Classic's text in their place, tagged with the "Classic data" badge (the hover tooltip, which has no badges, prefixes it with "Classic:"). This is the same pattern the dungeon quests use.
  - On talents where Forever changed other ranks, the fallback rank also says: "Forever changed other ranks of this talent; this rank's Forever value isn't known yet."
  - Nothing is extrapolated from neighbouring ranks.
  - **5 ranks have no text in either client** and still read "This rank isn't in the game files yet.": Feral Swiftness rank 2 and Lethal Attacks ranks 2–5 (their rank spells aren't Classic spells).
- **13 talents have no rank in the client at all.** They use their Classic Era name with a Classic data badge, and every one of their ranks shows Classic text (badged):
  - Polearm Specialization (no icon either)
  - Improved Backstab
  - Improved Prayer of Healing
  - Blood Frenzy
  - Dark Pact
  - Improved Drain Soul
  - Improved Drain Mana
  - Faerie Fire (Feral)
  - Fel Stamina
  - Wyvern Sting
  - Improved Scorpid Sting
  - Blessing of Sanctuary
  - Improved Lay on Hands
- **6 rank texts lost one sentence** because it holds a token the client can't fill: spells 11426, 12323, 14251, 15237, 20150 and 20177 (`$proccooldown`, `$a1`, `$a2`, `${431+$SPFR…}`, `$19718d`).
- **Martyrdom reads "0% chance".** That is the client's own `$m1`.

## ⚠️ R2 icon publish needed

There are 259 new talent and tree icons: the icon map grew from 1,843 to 2,102 files. They show as placeholders until published. Run this from `apps/mygamingassistant/backend` (it needs `scripts/.env.r2`; add `--dry-run` to see the count first):

```
python -m scripts.wow_icons.publish --to r2
```

## Tests (targeted)

- **Backend pytest:** talents generator (36 tests, incl. the fallback: only missing ranks are filled, the 13 no-rank talents are filled for every rank, unfillable sentences dropped), spell tooltip (20), icons, items hotfix cache, food, professions, engineering and refresh. All passed.
- **Vitest:**
  - `wowTalentRules` (Classic fallback only on missing ranks, the changed-elsewhere note, tier gating, prerequisites, removal blocked by a dependent or a lower row, level cap, legality, cell states, keys);
  - `wowTalentBuildCode` (codec round trip and rejections; every class's real trees: a full 51-point build round-trips);
  - nav, What's new, game icon and landing tests.

  All passed.
- **Playwright:** `wow-forever-talents.spec.ts` has 9 tests: pick a class, spend points, Arcane Focus rank 4 shows the Classic fallback + badge + changed-elsewhere note, gating, prerequisite and dependent, level cap, keyboard, Copy-link round trip in a

body:
## What

The Claude Code section of `plugin/README.md` now explains how to install the plugin from GitHub:

- One step: `claude plugin install statute --marketplace 50lo/statute` (Claude Code 2.1.292 or later).
- Fallback for older versions: `claude plugin marketplace add 50lo/statute`, then `claude plugin install statute@statute`.

Before this change, the section said to "install this directory as a plugin" without giving a command. The marketplace manifest (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) is already on `main`, so the commands work as written.

author: nkskater
body:
Adds `postbox git` (connect, status, diff, commit, branch list/create/switch, push, pull, continue, abort) for directories written by `collection pull`.

- Git is spawned without a shell, with a fixed env, fixed subcommand set, hooks directed to an empty dir, no global/system config, no external diff/merge/filter/credential programs
- A repository whose own .git/config can run programs or redirect traffic is refused, naming the setting
- Only https/ssh remotes (local paths need --allow-local); no credentials in URLs; branch names validated
- Remote host checked against HostPolicy at connect and before every push/pull
- Conflicts: pull leaves the merge in progress, exits 5 and lists files; continue refuses leftover markers; abort restores
- Tokens come from an env var (--token-env) via a throw-away askpass helper and are scrubbed from output. The vault API is write-only, so the CLI cannot read vault values; noted in docs/git-adapter.md
- Tests: 15 core scenarios (clean pull, divergent branches, conflict round trip with the repository format, hooks never run, evil config refused, policy) plus CLI exit-code tests
- Not included: in-app UI for git (CLI only)

author: jasagiri
body:
refs #25059

As asked in https://github.com/nim-lang/Nim/issues/25059#issuecomment-6704740258, this fixes only the tutorial. `doc/tut1.md` said that the shift operators "always treat their arguments as *unsigned*" and pointed to multiplication or division for arithmetic shifts. Since `shr` became sign preserving, that is the opposite of what the code does for signed integers.

The paragraph now says that `shl` fills with zeros, `shr` is an arithmetic shift for signed integers (example `-8 shr 1` is `-4`) and a logical shift for unsigned integers, and that a signed value can be shifted logically by converting it to the unsigned type of the same size. This matches the doc comment of `shr` in `lib/system/arithmetics.nim`.

Checked on devel 05d45b6f (macOS arm64), C with `--mm:orc` and `--mm:refc`, and JS: `int8(-2) shr 1` is `-1`, `uint8(254) shr 1` is `127`, `uint8(-2'i8) shr 1` is `127`, `-8 shr 1` is `-4`. `nim md2html doc/tut1.md` builds with no new warnings.

author: vscarpenter
body:
**PR id:** AND-RESURRECT-2 (the Lead, 2026-11-08), from my re-cut review of web #701 (`sprint/reviews/WEB-RESURRECT-recut-by-S-AND.md`, A1 and A2). The iOS half is #97, and the test names match it. SPEC-3's rule 3 wording is web #705. Tip `d349cb6` on `main` `bd00dad`. Four commits: A1, A2, A2's identity guard, and a test that pins the 403 half of the auth-failure stop.

## What and why

### A1: a queued delete keeps a remembered task in Trash (`4d9fce6`)

**The failure:**
1. A run fails before forgetting, for example on a dead session or an incomplete listing, so an id stays remembered.
2. The user restores that task and trashes it again while signed in. That leaves a Trash row and a queued delete.
3. The next run's step brought the task back active.
4. The push sent the delete, so the server copy went.
5. Reconciliation then removed the active copy with no Trash entry.

So the user's latest delete lost its Trash copy.

**The fix:** the step now keeps the id and the Trash row when the task has a queued delete (`hasQueuedDelete`). A failed delete counts as well as a pending one, because Android re-arms failed rows on launch and manual sync (§9.5). Web counts pending rows only, since it never re-arms one. That's the same split as the hold-off (`HOLDOFF-FAILED-ROWS`). Sign-in drops every queued delete, so one here was made since the id was remembered. The id is forgotten at the next listing, once the delete has landed.

### A2: a failed step doesn't skip the push (`96852b8`, `98010b5`)

A run is pull, then the step, then push, in one `try`, so a step that threw ended the run before the push. A transient listing failure cost one run's upload. A permanent one, such as an account over 10,000 records, blocked every push while any id was remembered, and the ids were never forgotten.

**The fix:** the step's failure now goes to `SyncEngine`'s new `onResurrectFailed`, forgets nothing, and the run goes on to push, as web does. The engine has no logger, so `AppContainer` logs it under `GsdSync`, with the class name only.

**Three things still end the run:**
- **A stale session** (`StaleSyncSession`).
- **An identity mismatch** (`IdentityMismatch`): a token the identity check confirmed for another account. Only reconciliation checks identity again, after the push and only when something is missing, so a caught mismatch let the push write to the wrong account. The Lead caught this in iOS #97's review, and `98010b5` adds the guard.
- **An auth failure** (`PocketBaseApi.Unauthorized`): a dead token. The pull can't see one, because a guest listing is empty. The push would spend a retry on every queued item.

`onResurrectFailed` sits before `ownerId`, so a trailing lambda at a call site still binds to the owner. Several tests rely on that.

**Spec:** `docs/gsd-android-spec.md` §9.4.

## Tests

All in `SyncEngineTest`, except the last row, which is in `PocketBaseApiTest`.

| Test | Red first? |
|---|---|
| `a remembered id with a pending delete stays in Trash and is kept` (SPEC-3 §6, web #705) | yes: the Trash row was gone (expected the tombstone, was null) |
| `a remembered id with a failed delete stays in Trash and is kept` | no; a mutation that counts pending rows only fails it |
| `a step that fails forgets nothing and leaves the sync successful` | yes: status was `error` |
| `a step whose identity check fails stops the run before the push` (iOS #97's name) | yes: status was `success`, and the edit pushed |
| `a dead session found by the step pushes nothing` (iOS #97's name) | no; a mutation that swallows `Unauthorized` fails it |
| `a session that ends during the step stops the run` | no; a mutation that swallows `StaleSyncSession` fails it |
| `confirmIdentity is unauthorized when the server forbids the session` | no; it pins today's 403 mapping, which matches iOS #97's 401-or-403 stop, and a mutation that maps 403 to `HttpError` fails it |

The test fake gains two knobs: `incompleteEpochListings`, a listing that claims one more record than it sends, and `otherAccount`, an identity check that throws `IdentityMismatch` as `PocketBaseApi.confirmIdentity` does.

## Verification

Run on 2026-11-08, 01:44Z to 01:56Z, on the `gsd-e2e` AVD (`ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554`, `android-emu` lock), at `d349cb6` on `main` `bd00dad`, from a clean install (app uninstalled first).

- `./gradlew :core:model:test`: 275 tests, 0 failures.
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`: `:core:sync` 209 tests (`main` has 202; this adds 7) and `:app` 111, 0 failures. `:core:store` has no JVM unit tests.
- `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`: green.
- `./gradlew connectedAndroidTest`: `:core:store` 90 tests and `:app` 329 tests, 0 failures.
- **One earlier run doesn't count.** The gate at `98010b5` failed once in `ReminderNoneSyncTest > pickingTheDefaultForALegacyNullKeepsASentReminder` ("the connection pool has been closed"). That's a teardown race in the test: it closes the database in `@After`, inside the Compose rule, while the editor sheet is still composed. The test never calls the sync engine, so this change can't reach it.
  - Its rate so far: 1 failure in 3 full-suite runs (#88's gate, `98010b5`, `d349cb6`), and 0 in 5 runs of the class alone.
  - The fix is its own test-only PR, AND-TEARDOWN-RACE.
- **Not run:** a real-server run (item 24).

## Follow-ups

- **iOS #97** matches all three of A2's stops as of `c94e4fd`, including a 401 or 403 from the step (F1 in `sprint/reviews/ios-97-by-S-AND.md`). Android maps both statuses to `Unauthorized`.

author: fairchild
body:
## What each file is for

- `skills/repo-steward/references/chat-channels.md`: how to run workers through one `#task-<slug>` channel per task on an IRC-style chat service. Each worker posts status once, to its own channel. The steward steers with @mentions, which the worker hears through a bounded wait at its checkpoints. Text a worker writes to a channel is data, not instructions. Invites and credentials reach a worker as a mode-600 file, never in a prompt or transcript. When the task closes, the channel closes and the invite is revoked.
- `skills/repo-steward/references/cloud-sessions.md`: how to dispatch a worker as a cloud session.
  - One task per session, with the brief in the first message, the branch named up front, and the model chosen per task.
  - The steward watches by reads: session status, session events, the PR, and the report. It schedules its own check-ins, because a session that finishes cleanly sends nothing back.
  - Limits: one branch per session; Linux containers only, so for macOS-only toolchains CI is the only check; a refused permission goes to the operator.
  - At most three workers at once. When the PR is ready, the worker is told to stand down, so one hand stays on the branch.
- `skills/repo-steward/SKILL.md`: links both references from "Your workspace tooling".
- `skills/consequential-check/` (new, experimental): decides whether a PR needs the owner to merge it.
  - `scripts/consequential.py`: a uv single-file script using the Anthropic SDK.
    - A cheap decision model gives a probability for each of five typed questions: `hard_to_undo`, `weakens_security`, `costs_money`, `product_decision`, `exposes_private_data`.
    - Each question has its own line above which it raises: 0.3 for security and private data, 0.5–0.6 for the rest.
    - Any answer with `max(p, 1-p) < 0.75` sends the whole question set to a stronger model. With no decision-model key, the stronger model answers alone.
    - The PR is routed to the owner when there is no key at all, when the diff is empty, unreadable or over 400k chars, or when a model call fails.
    - The prompt tells the model that the title, body and diff are data, and that instructions written there are not to be followed.
    - `--self-test` covers the thresholds, the escalation paths and the no-key route. It makes no model calls.
  - `assets/rubric.md`: concrete yes/no situations for each question, rather than low/medium/high.
  - `assets/consequential-check.yml`: the workflow template.
    - It runs the script and rubric from the **base** commit, so a PR can't edit its own judge, and reads the diff through the API as data.
    - It fails closed. `Route` runs under `shell: bash` (pipefail). `Label` runs unless the step was cancelled or the router said exactly `false`. `Post the verdict` runs after a failure too, and posts "router failed; routed to the owner" when there is no readable verdict.
    - It keeps one verdict comment current. It never merges, approves, or removes the label. PRs from forks are skipped.
  - `SKILL.md`: how to install it, and how tuning works.
    - The owner confirms or corrects a verdict with a one-line reply: `consequential: right` or `consequential: wrong <question-id> <why>`. A `gh api` query collects those replies.
    - It notes that the PR text reaches the judge untrusted, and that the decision model is pinned once it is tuned.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: one new line in the `config` job runs `consequential.py --self-test`. This is a net-new check: offline, under a second.
- `README.md`: the catalog row, regenerated.

## Commands run

- `python .github/scripts/validate-config.py`: `59/59 files valid`
- `python .github/scripts/test-workflows.py`: `OK`
- `python scripts/catalog.py readme --check`: `OK: README catalog matches frontmatter`
- `python scripts/portability.py --check`: `44 skills: 0 failing, 44 clean`
- `python scripts/test_portability.py`: `OK`
- `python scripts/test_public_text_guard.py`: `OK`
- `python skills/consequential-check/scripts/consequential.py --self-test`: `self-test: ok`
- Template checks, from a scratch script:
  - parsed the YAML, and every `run:` block passes `bash -n`.
  - ran the verdict-comment block against a good verdict, a missing `verdict.json`, and a garbage one. The good verdict rendered the table. The other two rendered "Consequential: yes … router failed; routed to the owner".
- `bash -e -c 'false | tee /dev/null; …'` continues past the failure, and `bash -eo pipefail` stops. That is the bug this PR's review found, and the reason `Route` now has `shell: bash`.
- Manual script runs with no keys, an empty diff, and a rubric missing its sections: each was routed to the owner or gave a usage error.

## Not run

- **actionlint** on the template: it isn't installed in this session, and the `go run` fetch was blocked. CI's actionlint only covers `.github/workflows/`, not `assets/`.
- **`public-text-guard.py check`**: it could not run here (`CANNOT RUN`, no private-repo list). I grepped the diff by hand for names, hosts, emails and banned vocabulary instead.
- No live model calls. The template has not been installed on any repo, so nothing has been run end to end.
- `webui/` was not touched, so Playwright wasn't run.

author: rafalopez15
body:
The 95% coverage gate fails a PR, but the number only appeared in the job log. You couldn't see whether a PR lowered coverage or which new lines it left untested.

## What changed

- **`.github/scripts/summarize_coverage.py`** writes a **Coverage** section for the CI comment, between Tests and Pylint:
  - The total, ✅ or ❌ against the gate. The gate is read from `pytest.ini`, so they can't drift apart.
  - The change against `main`: ▲, ▼ or no change.
  - Each changed file under `src/` or `main.py` with untested lines, with the line numbers as ranges. Fully covered files are collapsed underneath, and the table collapses when it passes 10 files.
  - If pytest never wrote a report, the section shows a ⚠️ line instead.
- **Tests job in `ci.yml`:**
  - pytest also writes `coverage.xml`, in CI only.
  - On PRs, the job downloads the `coverage.xml` saved by `main`'s latest successful run and lists the changed files with `gh pr diff`, printing them in the log. That needs `pull-requests: read` on this job.
  - Pushes to `main` save their report as the `coverage-main` artifact for 90 days. Downloading it needs `actions: read` on this job.
- **`tests/test_summarize_coverage.py`** tests the new script.
- **README and CLAUDE.md** describe the section.

- **Branch coverage:** `pytest.ini` adds `--cov-branch`, so the gate also counts both sides of every `if`. The code is already at 100% with it (110 branches), so nothing fails. The summary counts branches the same way and lists untested ones as `8→10`.

The threshold is unchanged: CI still fails under 95%.

## What to expect

`main` has no saved report until this merges, so this PR's comment says "No coverage report from `main` to compare against". The first PR after the merge shows the comparison.

This is also the first PR under the new `main` ruleset. The merge button should stay disabled until Tests, Pylint, Format and Smoke test all pass.

Closes FPL-65

author: voces
body:
## What

- **The shadow carries each node's write history.** `scripts/box-dst-shadow/probe.sh` now also patches the probe's checker. Every box-record write is logged in order, per program and per instance capture, and tagged with the recorder that made it (`ctx` contextual stamp, `join` from `recordBoxTy`, `exit` from `boxExitsStamp`). A row whose node holds more than one union gets `| hist first= last= join= any= : <trail>`, graded against the site union. The VL half is `hist.vl.in`. Probe only: the tree's compiler is unchanged by it.
- **Variant fields read the record.** `emitVariantFieldValueUnder` and `emitVariantFieldStoreVal` share `emitVariantFieldBox`. It calls `emitDelivered` where `boxOwedAt` holds. Otherwise it boxes into the field's own union: a nullable-literal field (`v: 1 | null`) is recorded as a nullable niche but stored as a box. A first cut without that floor lost `D4268` and `unions/shared-nullable-literal-field-read`.

Note: `docs/internals/refactor-notes/2026-11-08-unionbox-write-order-variant-fields.md`.

## Measured

Write order, over 111,367 deliveries in 23,615 programs:
- 513 top-level deliveries in 166 files read a node written with more than one union.
- The **last** write matches the site union at 469 of them. First-write fails about 300 and a join about 280. The later writes are refinements, e.g. `i32|string` → `i64|string`.
- 470 of the 513 are the same recorder twice, so a per-role record would not separate them.
- The 43 last-write misses:
  - 27: a later write names an open type parameter after a closed union.
  - 7: values already a box, so never boxed.
  - 9 disagree: 8 are a literal-alias spelling or a closed union after an empty write, and 1 is a real conflict, `f64|null` → `i32|null`.
- No position in this lane with 0 history rows depends on the policy: variant fields, assignIdent, struct-field store, map default, fn-tag dispatch, const-cell init.

Variant fields: 1,096 deliveries are boxed by the table and 4 (in 2 files) by the floor. Union-box call sites deleted: 0, two become one floor call.

- Fixpoint seed 6,499,782 bytes, +38 against the base fixpoint (6,499,744); refreshed twice, byte-identical. After the master merge: 6,504,387, also a fixpoint.
- Sweep, base fixpoint against candidate fixpoint: 23,615 same, 0 bytes-only, 0 `runs → not-runs`, 0 new traps.

author: clay-good
body:
## Status

Not a review — this is the change. Advisory only: no new gate, no rule-table or verdict change. Ready to review once CI is green.

## What was wrong

Four ways a schema could be graded wrongly, or vanish, with nothing said:

1. **A generated or vendored copy was graded as this repository's own contract, silently.** `src/__generated__/schema.graphql`, a `# @generated`-headed SDL, or a vendored copy of someone else's schema produced a breaking verdict that reads as "you broke your API". The walker already computed `isGenerated` per file; the contract candidate test never consulted it, and certify had no notion of provenance at all.
2. **The directory exclusion deleted tracked, hand-written schemas.** `SKIP_DIR` matched a `build/`, `dist/`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/` or `.git/` segment **anywhere** in a path, for tracked and untracked files alike, with no `boundaries` line and no `notAssessed`. On `googleapis/googleapis` that silently dropped four hand-written Google API protos (`google/devtools/build/v1/build_events.proto`, `build_status.proto`, `publish_build_event.proto`, `google/devtools/containeranalysis/v1beta1/build/build.proto`).
3. **Only Relay configs were read.** `apollo.config.*`, `graphql.config.*`, `.graphqlrc*` and `codegen.*` were read by nothing, so a schema a frontend vendors for one of those tools was graded as this repository's with no disclosure. The Relay disclosure itself only looked at root-level configs, so in a monorepo (`relay-examples`) it fired for none of the four Relay projects.
4. **Three lists were cut at a cap with no omitted count** — `surface`, and the ambiguous-type and conflict entries of `notAssessed` — so operations past the cap were simply absent.

A fifth, found while reviewing this change: **the YAML/JSON window had no unexamined-candidate sweep** (protobuf and GraphQL have had one all along). A cap that displaced the repository's only OpenAPI document returned `suggestedBump: "patch"` for a removed operation — an affirmative compatibility claim about a document nothing read. That is the gate-bypass class that bit #688, and narrowing the directory rule made it easier to reach, so it is fixed here.

## How it was fixed

**One provenance predicate, dependency-free** (`src/core/analyzer/contract/types.ts`), used by both the analyze and the certify path: a generator header in a **bounded head** of the file (`certainty: "declared"`), else a path pattern (`certainty: "path-pattern"`). The marker ids are `generated-file-guard.ts`'s own (`at-generated`, `go-code-generated`, …) and the path names are its vocabulary too, plus one documented addition, `third_party/`; a test compares the two implementations' verdicts so they cannot drift apart silently. The analyzer may not import the service layer, so the implementation is narrow and local, exactly as `generated-client.ts` already does.

- **Certify**: each graded schema's `specs` entry carries `provenance` (`{ kind, matched, certainty }`), carried through `ScanScope`/`SpecSide`. The schema is graded exactly as before — **disclosed, not dropped**. The CLI prints it on the schema's own line.
- **Analyze**: the contract projection discloses `schemaProvenance` (an optional `Disclosed<…>` beside `skippedCandidates`), for files that are schemas by their own format test. Nothing is dropped, and the Relay drop is unchanged.
- **The directory rule is narrowed on a principle**: it applies to **untracked** files only, because a tracked file is part of the repository by definition. `node_modules/` stays excluded for tracked files too, as one named exception with its reason (a committed dependency tree is genuinely another project's contract). The same rule now runs on the working tree and on the base revision, so an exclusion can never read as an addition or a removal, and every excluded path is named in one `boundaries` line with the count and the first few paths.
- **Client configs widened** to Apollo, graphql-config, `.graphqlrc*` and GraphQL Code Generator, reusing Relay's escape rule verbatim — a path that climbs out of the config's own directory is never claimed, because a config must not let OpenLore speak for someone else's schema, or stop it speaking about this repository's own. Each config that was read is named in its own boundary line. **A config can never make certify drop a schema**, and `relaySchemaPaths` (the only set that drops, on the analyze side) still contains Relay configs alone. Values are read one line at a time, so a `#`-commented-out line, a `my_schema:` key, a `$schema` URL, an empty value and a list form are not misread.
- **Every cap now carries its count**: `surfaceOmitted`, the further-ambiguous/conflict lines, the further-config-disclosure line, and the configs past the read cap. The client-document disclosure is no longer gated on a schema being found.
- **The YAML/JSON unexamined-candidate sweep** withholds `suggestedBump` when a displaced candidate changed, and the parity reason no longer asserts "no document was found" when the cap stopped the scan before one.

## Replication / proof

Failing-first: with only the source changes stashed, the 20 new cases fail; with them, all pass.

New tests:

- `src/core/analyzer/contract/schema-provenance.test.ts` — `reads a declared generator header as 'declared', by the guard's marker ids` · `reads a path pattern as 'path-pattern', never as 'declared'` · `a declared header wins over a path pattern, and neither ever drops a schema` · `stays in step with the generated-file guard it borrows its vocabulary from` · `reads only a bounded head, whatever the file size, and stays linear` (a 10 MB SDL, a 128 KB path, constant-cost head).
- `src/core/analyzer/contract/graphql.test.ts` — `reads the single literal schema path out of each config kind it knows` · `never claims a schema outside the config's own directory, or one that is not a literal path` · `reads the config's own value, not a commented-out line, another key, or the next line` · `keeps relaySchemaPaths to Relay configs alone: only Relay may make a schema drop`.
- `src/core/analyzer/contract/project-graphql.test.ts` — `discloses a generated or vendored schema copy as provenance, and projects it all the same` · `says nothing about a hand-written schema, and discloses provenance even when it is the only thing to say`.
- `src/core/analyzer/contract/graphql-integration.test.ts` — `discloses a generated schema copy end to end, and still projects its operations`.
- `src/core/services/mcp-handlers/service-contract.test.ts` — `grades a generated schema copy and names what said it is generated` · `reads a '@generated' header as 'declared', and says nothing about a hand-written schema` · `a vendored copy under node_modules is excluded WITH a boundary naming it, never silently` · `a tracked file under build/ is read and graded; an untracked one under dist/ is disclosed` (the googleapis case) · `names the client config that named a schema, and grades the schema all the same` (the invariant, over all five config kinds: a config never drops a schema) · `does not claim a schema a config names outside the config's own directory` · `counts the surface entries past the cap instead of cutting them silently` · `withholds the bump when the scan cap displaced a specification, instead of reporting patch` · `does not claim no document was found when the cap stopped the scan before one` · `does not compare a schema the working-tree scan excluded but the base revision has` · `counts the config disclosures past the cap` · `discloses client documents in a repository that has no schema at all`.

### Real repositories, before and after (local build, pinned clones)

**`googleapis/googleapis` @ `bf54c1031efd` — four tracked protos restored, and the arithmetic closes.**

```
git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard | grep -c '\.proto$'   → 7553

before:  specs 477 · boundary "Past the protobuf cap (500 files), 7049 .proto file(s) were not read."
         500 + 7049 = 754

author: cdoughty08
body:
## Change

A query that created `#work` can now estimate a selected `SELECT ... FROM #work` through **Display Estimated Plan in Query Session**. The existing Estimated Plan button, Ctrl+L and callers that omit `mode` still compile on a fresh isolated connection. The pane labels the acquisition context and can switch modes explicitly.

The opt-in `plans.estimate` mode borrows the tab's persistent physical connection under its existing ownership checks/session gate. It uses the same one-time session opener as ordinary execution, preserves result handles and statistics, and keeps the existing 30-second / two-acquisition / XML bounds and cancel lifecycle. Viewer sources and statement/operator identities are unchanged; this PR does not modify the parser, model, canvas or caching.

## SQL Server strategy and effects

Proved against localhost SQL Server 2025 Developer 17.0.1000.7 with Windows integrated authentication before implementing session capture. The same physical session is needed to see local temporary objects, existing SET options, impersonation and uncommitted data/schema. A dynamic `EXEC('SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON')` probe demonstrated that SHOWPLAN does not survive the nested scope, so a fresh connection or nested wrapper cannot provide the original session's compilation context.

Submitted SQL is never executed. Existing GO/selection handling and capture-toggle guards apply; runtime SET, EXECUTE AS and transaction changes in the submitted selection are not executed. Table/local variables from earlier batches and temp objects created only by estimated SQL remain unavailable. Standalone USE batches temporarily change compilation context and the original database is restored. Existing compile-only/capture settings are refused without taking ownership or changing them; OFFSETS/FIPS_FLAGGER tokens are conservatively refused in session mode.

Live adversarial validation found two material SQL Server behaviors:

- A low session TEXTSIZE silently truncates SHOWPLAN XML. Capture now temporarily raises TEXTSIZE, then restores it and QUOTED_IDENTIFIER/database context during bounded cleanup.
- Capture/preflight/cleanup overwrite @@ROWCOUNT and @@ERROR (both 0 after successful cleanup on this server). These registers cannot be restored. Cancelling blocked compilation with XACT_ABORT ON rolled back the pre-existing transaction despite executing none of the submitted SQL. Errors/deadlocks/cancellation follow SQL Server transaction rules; users must check transaction state before continuing.

Compilation can also acquire schema locks/update optimizer statistics. The pane, cancellation errors and docs explain these effects. Live coverage here is SQL Server 2025; other supported SQL Server versions/Azure SQL were not available for this run.

## Failure and cleanup

The session gate remains held until SHOWPLAN OFF, an executing sentinel and context restoration finish with a fresh two-second cleanup token. An ordinary compile/permission/size error or cancellation leaves the session open when cleanup succeeds, subject to SQL Server transaction effects above. Cleanup or transport failure removes and closes the physical session before releasing the gate, returns SESSION_LOST, clears stale UI session identity and explains loss of temporary objects/SET options and rollback of any remaining transaction. Existing unknown-outcome commit warnings are preserved. No SQL retry or execution fallback is added.

Already-running work fails fast. Closing during session capture uses the existing running-query/rollback prompt; isolated capture retains its idle-session transaction prompt. Disconnect, early Stop, session close and backend loss use the existing lifecycle, including generation tracking for sessions opened by estimation.

## Validation

- `npm run check`: typecheck, 1,679 offline .NET checks, 3,550 Vitest tests and production build.
- `VARIA_TEST_SQL_SERVER=localhost dotnet run --project backend/Varia.Backend.Tests --configuration Release -- --live-suite EstimatedPlans`: 67 live checks across both modes, including opening failure without a surviving session.
- `VARIA_TEST_SQL_SERVER=localhost node scripts/estimated-plans-smoke.mjs`: fake-backend and real-SQL Electron passes with isolated profiles, selection through the visible pane and Query menu, preserved transaction/temp data, subsequent ordinary execution, existing actual plans/statistics and saved .sqlplan workflow. Inspected the 1024x700 session-mode screenshot.
- Full `npm run test:smoke`: passed (all configured Electron suites; SQL-only Live Plan is validated separately below).
- Live Plan SQL smoke against localhost: passed, including changing operator rows, actual capture, cancellation, GO repetitions and estimation followed by ordinary Live/Actual execution. The final real-SQL estimated-plan smoke also passed on the committed head.
- Adversarial review covered capture escape attempts, existing SHOWPLAN/NOEXEC/PARSEONLY/FMTONLY, busy-gate overlap, size limits, blocked cancellation/timeout, XACT_ABORT rollback, cleanup/transport failure, disconnect, session close and backend-generation ownership. Regression tests exercise the discovered TEXTSIZE and transaction effects.

Leave merge approval to the user. The branch is based on origin/main including foundation commit 142858b0.

author: skye967
body:
Pushing a `holster-catalog/vX.Y.Z` tag now publishes the library as a wheel and sdist on a GitHub Release. The library README gains the version policy and install instructions.

**The release job, in order:**
1. It fails if the tagged commit isn't on main.
2. It fails if the tag's version isn't `pyproject.toml`'s.
3. It runs the library's test suite.
4. It builds with `uv build --package holster-catalog --no-sources` and runs `gh release create --generate-notes`.

Steps 1 and 3 are there because main isn't protected and `ci.yml` only runs on pull requests. Without them, a commit that never passed CI could be released.

**Tag the first release on this PR's merge commit, not #73's.** A tag push runs the workflows that exist at the tagged commit. #73's merge commit has no release workflow, so a tag there would quietly do nothing. The version is still 0.2.0, so `holster-catalog/v0.2.0` goes on this merge commit.

**Choices that might look wrong:**
- **`persist-credentials: false`:** after the checkout, nothing needs git credentials. `gh` authenticates with `GH_TOKEN`.
- **No job-level `UV_LOCKED`:** `uv version` and `uv build` don't read the lock. The test step passes `--locked` itself.
- **Generated notes cover the whole repo:** they list every merged PR in the repository, not just library PRs. The README says the CHANGELOG is the library's record.

**Deliberately left out:** PyPI, trusted publishing and signing. Also not handled: re-running a half-finished release, pre-release tags, and the "Latest" badge. There is only one release series so far.

**Tested locally, not in Actions:**
- The built wheel installs into a fresh venv, imports `holster_catalog` 0.2.0 and runs a scripted turn.
- Both checks pass and fail as intended.
- The test step passes in a clean export.

The workflow itself first runs on the tag.

**Open, outside this PR:**
- The root README says MIT, but there's no `LICENSE` file and no `license` field, so the released artifacts carry no licence notice.
- Branch protection with required checks on main would close the CI gap at its source.

author: degenhard
body:
Implements #256 - the Registered users list of the Server administration window, from the protocol through the engine to the UI.

## What changes and why

- **Protocol** (`crates/protocol/src/registered.rs`): one message type both ways. An empty `UserList` asks the server for its accounts; one entry with a new name renames an account, the same entry **without** a name removes the registration. Answers arrive as the new `Event::UserList`. Nothing outside the standard Mumble protocol is used.
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/registered.rs`): the accounts a connection read live in memory only, dropped when the tab closes or the connection ends (FR-10.63). The **Register** right of the root channel rides along in `ChannelPermissions`, so the UI can hide an entry instead of offering one that can only be refused (FR-10.1, FR-10.20).
- **Commands**: `registered_users_open`, `registered_user_rename`, `registered_user_unregister`, `registered_user_groups`, `registered_users_close` and `person_register`.
- **Registering a connected person** uses the standard path - `UserState` with `userId 0` - so the server binds the account to the certificate and the name that person uses right now. Without a client certificate the command is refused, because a standard server would only refuse it later for a reason the user cannot act on.
- **UI**: Server administration is now tabbed (**Bans**, **Registered users**). The tab has search, the filters *All / Online / Inactive 90+ days* with their counts, and sortable columns for name, account id, last seen and last channel; the two columns a server does not report drop away instead of showing dashes. Only the rows on screen are drawn, so a server with thousands of accounts scrolls smoothly (FR-10.53).
- A selected row opens its panel: the name to set, last seen, the **groups that name that account** (read from the channel the server last saw them in, root channel as fallback), **Ban certificate…** when a certificate and the Ban right are there (hands the fingerprint and the name to the ban form), and **Unregister…** with a confirmation that says what the person loses.
- Entry points: server menu → Admin ▸ **Registered users…**, and **Register on server…** in an online guest's menu. Both only appear with the Register right (FR-10.20).
- Changes queue per account and go out one at a time on save; the footer counts them. Keyboard operable (arrow keys walk the list, Enter opens the name field) with screen-reader announcements for every action. Strings in all 24 languages.

## Server behaviour that shaped this

Measured against the local `mumble-server` (testenv v15): a server **does not push** its list after a change, so every save reads the list back and reports from what the server says. A rename onto a name another account already holds is dropped without any message, which is why a save can come back as `kept` - the UI then shows the account as it stands and says the server did not take the name, rather than showing the typed name as saved.

## Notes and small deviations

- The footer's unsaved hint is a count badge with a noun-free label ("**1** · not saved yet"). With a plain `{{count}}` string it read "1 changes not saved yet" in English and needed per-language plural forms in 24 locales; this stays correct in every one of them.
- Rebased onto main and kept the new **Admin ▸ sub-menu** (#249): the registered users entry sits in it next to the ban list, each gated by its own right. The moderation and move entries of the person menu (#257, #255) are unchanged; "Register on server…" joins that group ahead of the red entries.
- Group names a server builds itself (`~…`, `#…`, `$…`) stand for a condition rather than a group an admin made, so they are left out of the panel.
- Admin text is treated as untrusted: control characters are stripped before rendering, and names, fingerprints and reasons are never logged.

## Tests

- `crates/protocol/tests/live_registered_users.rs` (ignored, `MUMCORD_LIVE=1`): register a connected guest, rename, unregister, reconnect as a guest, and the permission refusal - against the local test server.
- Protocol and engine unit tests for the message shapes, the read-back decision (`saved` vs `kept`), the memory-only lifetime and the root-channel right.
- `ui/src/features/admin/registeredFormat.test.ts` and `RegisteredUsersTab.test.tsx`: columns and hidden columns, search, filters, sorting, the detail panel, save, a rename the server did not take, the unregister flow, the discard guard, the certificate-ban handover, the tab staying away without the right, and keyboard navigation. `PersonMenu.test.tsx` covers "Register on server…".
- `ui/src/api/mock.ts` now behaves like the test server, including keeping a held name, so the whole flow can be walked without a server.
- Full suites: 294 UI files / 3203 tests, `eslint` + `prettier`, `tsc -b`, `cargo test` (protocol 88, engine 1011, app 400), `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt` clean.

## Screenshots

Mock engine (`VITE_MUMCORD_MOCK=1 VITE_MUMCORD_MOCK_SEED=demo`) in headless Chromium at 1440x900, dark and light.

![Registered users, dark](docs/images/screenshots/registered-users-dark.png)
![Registered users, light](docs/images/screenshots/registered-users-light.png)

## Review round 1

- `last_channel()` in the engine searched every connection's list for an account id, and Mumble ids are server-local, so a group read could use a channel of another server. It now takes the `server_id` and reads only that connection's slot; the test holds the same id on two servers to keep it that way.
- A save announced "Changes sent to the server" whatever happened, because `saveChanges()` swallowed its errors. It now returns what it did (`idle | closed | error | saved | kept`) and the tab says that back: the error in the same words the banner shows, a kept change in the banner's sentence, nothing when the queue was empty or the window closed mid-save. The tests listen to the announcements now.
- The kept-change sentence no longer names a *name*, because an unregister the server did not take gets the same notice. Reworded in all 24 languages.
- Rebased onto `milestone/0.8.0` and the changelog entry sits under Unreleased there.

author: qontinui-dev[bot]
body:
## What

`Backend E2E Tests (3.12)` in `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` intermittently hit its 20-minute job cap on the self-hosted light pool. Every self-hosted run installed **with no pip cache at all**: `PIP_CACHE_DIR` lived under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, which is wiped after each job, and `actions/cache` runs on hosted runners only. When the install was slow but healthy, the job was cancelled with no failed step. That turns the required `Test Summary` red on PRs and on `main` (coord finding `930cd70a`).

Measured, re-read over REST:
- job 128549290971 (PR #2136, nawa-org-8): install 22:33:06→22:48:02 (14m56s), tests passed, job cancelled at 20m04s.
- job 128311913910 (nawa-org-13): cancelled mid-install after 17m07s.
- Over GraphQL, 17 recent self-hosted jobs installed in 1.2–9.2 min, and PR #2136 had an 11.1 min install. Tests take at most 2.9 min.

## Change

1. **A shared pip cache for the whole self-hosted pool**, at `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/qontinui-web-ci/pip`.
   - It is namespaced to this repo and survives across jobs.
   - pip writes its cache atomically (`network/cache.py` replace, `wheel_builder.py` os.replace), so concurrent jobs can share it.
   - Each install holds a **shared** flock for its whole step.
   - The only delete is a prune under a **non-blocking exclusive** flock. It runs when the cache is over 8 GiB, or when free space is under 60 GiB and the cache is over 1 GiB. Each prune emits a `::warning`.
   - If a size or free-space read fails, the prune is skipped; the step never fails because of it.
   - If `flock`/`du`/`df` is missing, the cache dir is unwritable, or the 5-minute lock wait times out, the job uses a job-scoped cache instead.
   - Why one dir rather than one per `$RUNNER_NAME`: per-runner dirs on a pool of ~56 registrations grow without bound (plan `2026-11-04-devops-ci-persistent-target-caches-keyed-per-registration-grow-without-bound-on-the-org-pool`).
   - Hosted runners still use `actions/cache` as before.
2. **Job cap raised from 20 to 35 min**, sized for a cold cache: install >17.1 min (censored) + 2.9 tests + 2.5 other = 22.5 min, × 1.5 = 33.75, rounded up to 35. `Install dependencies` gets its own 28-min cap, so a hung install fails and names that step instead of cancelling the job.
3. Comments and the cancelled-job notice now give the new numbers. The `--no-cache-dir -e ../../qontinui-schemas` install is unchanged.

## Trust

- Fork PRs never reach the pool: the `runs-on` fork guard sends them to `ubuntu-latest`.
- Same-repo jobs on the pool already share one unix user, its `$HOME`, and the tool cache's interpreter. The shared pip cache therefore adds no new trust boundary.

## Verification

- actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.30.1 (the versions workflow-lint pins) pass on the edited file.
- `backend/tests/test_ci_timeout_marker.py` and `test_workflow_lint_drift.py`: 59 passed, 11 skipped (the skipped tests need bash 4+ and git; CI runs them).
- The two edited `run:` blocks were extracted and run under `bash -e` in `python:3.12-slim`:
  - normal run: no prune;
  - bound 0: pruned (size condition);
  - floor met by a small cache: not pruned;
  - floor met with a 0 MB minimum: pruned;
  - a backgrounded `flock -s` holder: `prune skipped`;
  - unwritable cache dir (non-root user): falls back with rc 0;
  - hosted: exits early.
- Independent review by a fresh-context code-reviewer subagent, 3 rounds, ending clean.
- **Still owed on this PR's own runs:** the self-hosted Backend E2E log should show `pip cache: …/qontinui-web-ci/pip <n>MB before install`, and a warm re-run should have a shorter `Install dependencies`.

No ci-integrity workflow exists in qontinui-web, so no `ci:gate-change=*` label applies.

Plan: 2026-11-08-web-backend-e2e-job-cap-cancels-a-slow-uncached-pip-install-on-the-light-pool phases: 1
Review-Arm: spawned_code_reviewer (degrade) ~/.qontinui/review-arm/41fee684-52b2-41fc-9dee-2ea0d48322d8.json

Coord-Arming-None: workflow-only change (.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml): no production code symbol changes; observed through the Backend E2E job log lines pip cache: ... before/after install on self-hosted runs

Coord-Handoff-Load-Bearing: the free-space prune arm requires the cache to be over PIP_CACHE_FLOOR_MIN_SIZE_MB, so a disk filled by others cannot empty a small warm cache every run

author: ligf-ai
body:
## What changed

Documentation only — XML remarks in seven files; no behavior changes, no public API changes. Each addition states behavior the implementation already has (closing the documentation-grade items of the 2026-11-07 full-repo audit):

- `INavigationService` (interface remarks): the Recognition section now names the two type notions — stack recognition compares ViewModel runtime types; the cache lookup, self-target shortcut, `GoBackTo` and `Remove` address pages by the static type each page was navigated to (with the base-registration/derived-implementation consequence spelled out).
- `INavigationService.Remove`: new Serialization paragraph (the removal is serialized with navigation state transitions, but a navigation still in its departure phase does not hold the navigation lock, so covered pages can be removed mid-departure and the in-flight navigation commits against the stack as it then stands); the Reentrancy paragraph now states the disposed check runs first.
- `INavigationService` cache methods (`ClearCache` / `ClearAllCache` / `ClearCacheAsync` / `ClearAllCacheAsync`): the silent-no-op paragraph now states the same precedence — a call from within a lifecycle callback after disposal has begun is a silent no-op instead of throwing.
- `NavigationService.DisposeAsync` remarks: the Concurrency paragraph now states that callers arriving after completion return immediately also when the operation completed with collected errors; the errors are observed only by callers that awaited the operation while it ran and are not presented again.
- `JournalNavigationService` remarks: new "Calls registered from lifecycle callbacks" paragraph — such calls are recorded at registration; if the registered navigation is then superseded or vetoed by a leave guard, the page never lands but the entry remains, and a snapshot restore will navigate to that page. This discloses the known phantom-entry gap (audit item P1-2) in the package's public documentation.
- `JsonFileNavigationJournalStore` remarks: new paragraph warning that two stores can collide through the derived snapshot path (`a.json` vs `a.snapshot.json`) without sharing an entries path.
- `RouteMatch.Query`: a pair beginning with `=` yields an entry under the empty key (as in `URLSearchParams`).
- `NavigationHost` (WPF and Avalonia): the `NavigationService` property now states that setting it to null keeps the last presented content, and that attaching a service whose region currently has no page clears the host.

## Verification

Every added sentence was verified against the implementation in an adversarial review pass (check order in all four cache implementations, the DisposeAsync starter's completed-task branch, the controller's refresh behavior on both hosts incl. Avalonia's deferred-while-detached path, the Router's query parsing, the store's path derivation, the pump's callback-registration semantics and Journal's restore replay). Full suite: 665 tests green; consumer `verify.sh` PASS (docs are compiled into the packages; packaging and AOT consumer unaffected).

Companion note outside this repo diff: the Journal design document gained a "记录保真补遗" addendum recording the phantom-entry form and clarifying that serializer error reports are recording-side health reports not anchored to entries.

author: sims1253
body:
Fixes #466.

## Problem

Once any weak reference touched a host proxy, `extptr.rs:new_weak_ref` set `HOST_WEAK_REFS` for the rest of the session. From then on every collection of the core heap (`collect_needing` → `mark_api_roots` → `mark_proxies`) built a fresh `ObjectGraph` over everything reachable from every proxy and every escaped environment, and `trace_proxy` followed it.

## Cost on current main (2a5ff0b3, with #436 and #442)

Harnesses (callgrind, release build). Both load testthat and tibble first.

| harness | total | core-only collections |
|---|---|---|
| vctrs `vec_slice` + rlang `expr_deparse`, 150 iterations | 15.82 G | 9 collections, 1.89 G (**11.96%**), 210 M each |
| 60 `test_that` blocks of tibble/vctrs/rlang expectations | 37.28 G | 11 collections, 3.01 G (**8.07%**) |

**Option 1 doesn't fit.** cli's `.onLoad` runs `reg.finalizer(asNamespace("cli"), function(x) x$unload(), TRUE)`, an onexit finalizer whose key lives for the whole session. In a testthat + tibble session it is the only weak reference with a proxy, so a count of live proxy weak references never reaches zero.

## What this does

Every proxy is **pinned** (a core hold) from its creation until `sweep_stored` finds only the bridge holding its object. Holds are roots in every core collection; only `gc()` turns `held_roots` off. In a core collection, then:

- a pinned weak key is marked whatever the graph says;
- an unpinned key that only the bridge holds (count 1) is marked by neither pass, and core marking decides it;
- a key that is a C object is held (also a root) wherever the runtime refers to it;
- weak values and finalizers are marked from their keys.

The graph decides differently only for an **unpinned proxy key that something else holds again** (count > 1), for example a key back from C that was put into a dead cycle. So `graph_marking(c)` is now true in `gc()`/autogc (as before) or while such a key is registered: one scan of the weak list per collection. This is exact relative to main, since every key gets the same decision in every core collection. `HOST_WEAK_REFS`, `enable_host_weak_refs` and the unused `NativeBridge::finalizers_active` are removed.

Of the issue's options, this is option 2 in its cheapest form: the graph is used only for the weak keys it can change. I rejected two others:

- **Refcount marking in every core collection** (relying on gc()/autogc for cycles). Same speed, but not exact: the unpinned key in a dead cycle is finalized late. The new fixture catches that.
- **Skipping only keys that are registered namespaces.** Exact, but it still graph-marks for every other pinned key.

## Metric before → after

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| vctrs/rlang harness | 15.82 G | 13.63 G (**−13.8%**) |
| ... its core-only collections | 1.89 G | 0.23 G (**−87.6%**, 210 M → 26 M each) |
| same harness with its own live `reg.finalizer` env and `new_weakref` | 15.82 G | 13.64 G |
| testthat harness | 37.28 G | 34.86 G (−6.5%) |
| ... its core-only collections | 3.01 G | 0.34 G (−88.7%) |
| testthat harness, wall (best of 3, busy machine) | 10.80 s | 9.96 s |
| `scripts/perf.py` instr, 86 comparable programs | | all within ±0.013%, none slower |

`perf.py` has 3 programs that fail on base and candidate alike (`volcano`, `flexclust*`, a local environment issue).

## Verification

- `cargo test -p robigo-core -p robigo-capi`, also under `ROBIGO_GCTORTURE=1`: pass. `cargo test -p robigo-runtime`: pass, apart from the two known host-glibc `c_library*` oracle tests, which were skipped.
- Conformance, all three tiers (`conformance`, `compiled_matches_interpreted`): every ratcheted script passes except `graphics/cairo-devices.R`. It fails because grDevices/graphics natives aren't built locally; base and candidate give the same output for it.
- capi corpus, whole: 65/67, 0 regressions.
- New fixture `tests/r/capi/weak-keys-collections.R`, recorded with GNU R 4.5.0 and ratcheted. It covers:
  - a namespace key held for the whole session;
  - C keys at collections that C's allocations trigger;
  - a key-value cycle;
  - a self-cycle held from a global;
  - a key that only a C-preserved closure reaches;
  - an unpinned key back from C in a dead cycle. This passes on main and with this change, and fails with refcount-only marking.
- `cargo fmt`, `scripts/lint.sh`: clean.
- Ledger: `docs/ledger/core.md`.

Not changed, but found along the way: a finalizer closure created in the frame that holds its key is itself a pinned proxy, so core collections keep the key until `gc()`/autogc. Main does the same, and it is not observable at `gc()`.

author: levenst24
body:
When single-line voice regeneration succeeds in the ADV backlog (`createBacklog` in `frontend/src/adv/backlog.js`), `bindRegenerateControl` stores the completion prompt (`"语音已生成，点语音播放。"`) in `regenerationFeedback`. Clicking the replay button (`replayBtn.onclick` in `renderAssistantLineEntry` and `renderAssistantLegacyEntry`) hides `.adv-log-audio-status` upfront via `updateReplayButtonState`, but after `deps.audio.playLine` settles, `regenerationFeedback.delete(lineKey)` was only called on `'failed'` or `loadRetryText[result]` (`'timeout'` / `'network'`). When playback completed normally (`'ended'`) or was stopped by starting another replay (`'interrupted'`, which also increments `replaySequence`), the stale entry stayed in `regenerationFeedback` and reappeared on already-played lines whenever `renderAll()` or `_refreshAudioState()` ran while LOG remained open; conversely, when browser autoplay policy blocked playback (`'blocked'`), the temporarily hidden prompt was not restored.

## What changes

- Delete `lineKey` from `regenerationFeedback` after playback settles with `'ended'` or `'interrupted'` (outside `if (replaySequence === thisReplay)` and guarded by `activeRegeneration?.key !== lineKey`) in both `renderAssistantLineEntry` and `renderAssistantLegacyEntry` in `frontend/src/adv/backlog.js`.
- Call `refreshAudioState()` inside the active `replaySequence === thisReplay` branch when playback returns `'blocked'` so unplayed regeneration feedback remains visible.
- Add regression tests in `tests/test_adv_backlog.mjs` covering `'ended'`, `'interrupted'`, `'blocked'`, and concurrent in-flight regeneration for both split-line and legacy backlog entries.
- Document the fix under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- `node --test --test-timeout=60000 tests/test_adv_backlog.mjs` (failed 2 new tests before the fix because `.adv-log-audio-status` resurrected `"语音已生成，点语音播放。"` after `'ended'`/`'interrupted'` replay and did not restore it on `'blocked'`; passed all 48 tests after the fix).
- `npm --prefix frontend test` (passed all 60 frontend test suites; Python `.venv` tests were not run in this environment because no backend files changed).

## Resumen

Sustituye el frontend de Create React App por la plantilla oficial de Vite con React Compiler, integrada con Laravel siguiendo la configuración de blulablel. El código anterior del frontend sigue disponible en la rama `master`.

## Frontend

- Plantilla limpia `create-vite --template react-compiler` (JavaScript): Vite 8, React 19 y `babel-plugin-react-compiler` 1.0. Linter: oxlint.
- **Integración con Laravel:**
  - El build se genera en `backend/public`.
  - El plugin `laravel-output` mueve `index.html` a `resources/views/app.blade.php` de forma síncrona, sin la condición de carrera del `mv` asíncrono de blulablel.
  - `emptyOutDir: false` para que un build local no borre `index.php`; el plugin limpia solo `public/assets` y `public/index.html`.
- **HTTPS en desarrollo** con `vite-plugin-mkcert` (https://localhost:5173). Solo se carga con `vite`, no en el build ni en los tests. Los certificados quedan fuera de git y de la imagen.
- **Tests** con vitest y Testing Library (jsdom, jest-dom, user-event), con un test de ejemplo. `npm test` hace una pasada y `npm run test:watch` se queda en watch.
- `.env.example` con las variables `VITE_REVERB_*`.

## Backend y Docker

- Catch-all del SPA en `routes/web.php`. Excluye `api`, `up`, `app`, `broadcasting` y `assets/`, así que un chunk inexistente sigue dando 404.
- `Dockerfile.prod`: la etapa Node pasa a Vite (sin `--legacy-peer-deps` ni la copia de `build/` de CRA) y mueve `index.html` de forma determinista, con verificación.
- Los ignorados de CRA se sustituyen por los de Vite. `app.blade.php` sale del índice, porque estaba versionado por error.
- README con el flujo nuevo del frontend.

## CI

- Workflow `check_test_frontend.yml`: `npm ci`, `npm run lint` y `npm test` con Node 22 en los PR a `next` que toquen `frontend/`.

## Verificación

- [x] `npm run lint`: 0 errores y 0 avisos.
- [x] `npm test`: 2 tests pasan.
- [x] `npm run build`: los artefactos quedan en `backend/public` y están ignorados por git.
- [x] El React Compiler está activo en el bundle (`react.memo_cache_sentinel`).
- [x] Imagen de producción con MariaDB 11.4: `/`, los assets, las rutas profundas y `/up` responden 200; `/api/user` da 401; un asset inexistente da 404.
- [x] El build no ejecuta mkcert ni necesita red para ello.
- [x] `npm run dev` sirve por HTTPS en `:5173`.

author: blaze0089
body:
Fixes #751.

`LiveCapture._get_tshark_process()` creates a pipe with `os.pipe()` and passes the write end to dumpcap and the read end to tshark, but never closes either end in the parent. Both descriptors stay open for the life of the capture, and if spawning tshark fails the read end is leaked as well.

Close `write` right after dumpcap starts, close `read` after tshark starts, and close whichever ends are still open in a `finally` block. The child processes keep their inherited copies, so data flow is unchanged.

Added two tests in `tests/capture/test_live_capture.py` with a fake pipe: one for the success path and one where the tshark spawn raises, asserting both descriptors are closed. The existing `test_get_dumpcap_interface_parameter` tests still require a local tshark install and fail here for that pre-existing reason.

What the log does show on WebKit just before it: console errors for the staged bank-logo lookups (api.faviconkit.com and its redirect target), which the test's filter excludes only by the console message's location address; WebKit may report a different address. 1. **Layer image export preview wait.** On main, the core shard fails `LayerImageExportScreenshotTests.CaptureTheRealExportWindowsInBothThemesAsync` and `LayerPreviewBitmapConverterTests.RebindingReusesTheBitmapAndNewBytesReplaceItAsync` since 7e7b00c (reported by PC-Commander). I could not reproduce this locally. The fix is in `LayerImageExportViewTestSession.CompletePreviewAsync`. It repeats the clock advance and the wait until the newest preview has finished, with a 5-round failure guard. No sleep.
2. **Outcome test cannot find the Advanced fields.** After #383 the Advanced block of the Export layer image window starts collapsed. `DxfLayerImageExportWindowOutcomeTests.ExportButtonsWriteOnlyTheChosenLayerAsBmpWithRequestedPixelsAndPaddingAsync` sets Padding and Line width before it opens, so it fails with "Pixels X" not found. The fix expands Advanced first (2 lines, commit by NFH).

Each fix keeps its own commit. The two commits touch different files.

## Metric

Failing tests in the core shard on main: from 3 (or 1 on a run where the preview tests pass) to 0.

## Verification

- Local queue on main 83c7787, tests filtered to `LayerImageExport` and `LayerPreviewBitmapConverter`: the preview fix alone passed 67 of 68. The one failure was the Outcome test (cause 2).
- CI on #423 (preview fix only): all checks passed except the Outcome test.
- CI on this PR must be fully green before B accept.

body:
For v2.0.9. mini-m5 gets PostgreSQL through a fleet play, never from CI (replaces the rejected #6254).

**Play.** `nova-fleet runner-packages` (`fleet/runner-packages.yml`, `fleet/roles/runner-packages`) on the `runner` group installs `nova_runner_packages[<os>]` from `group_vars/all.yml`: `{darwin: ["postgresql@18"], debian: []}`, so Linux benches change nothing.
- darwin: finds brew the way the tailscale role does, reads `brew list --formula -1`, installs only the missing formulae (`HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`, no upgrade or reinstall). mini-m5's existing postgresql@18 is adopted, so the run should report `changed=0`.
- debian: `package_facts`, then apt for the missing only. Another OS with a non-empty list is refused.
- Packages only: no server start, no `brew services`, no unit. The tests run their own initdb/pg_ctl.
- One line per host: `RUNNER-PACKAGES host=<h> wanted=<n> present=<n> installed=<n>`. `--check` prints `WOULD-INSTALL brew install --formula <name>` per missing formula, like tailscale.
- Play list and help come from the embedded play's purpose line (`nova-fleet plays`, `nova-fleet help runner-packages`). Docs: one table row plus a `## runner-packages` section in fleet/README.md, and the CI line in docs/TESTING.md.
- `fleet/roles/nova-tools-install` is untouched (#6249).

**CI.** New `functional-macos` job on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64, mini-m5]`, the unit job's macOS labels, added to `ci-ok`. Its first step puts `/opt/homebrew/bin` and the postgresql@N keg's bin on PATH. If `initdb` is missing, it fails with `run: nova-fleet runner-packages -- -l mini-m5` and installs nothing. Then it runs `env -u LANG -u LC_ALL go test -count=1 -p 4 -tags functional,slow ./...` with `NOVA_CONTRACT_STRICT=1`.

**Tests (written first, red before the role existed).** `fleet/runner_packages_play_test.go`:
- the play targets `runner` without play-level become
- the vars are exact
- no service/launchd/systemd/template module, and no `services`, `pg_ctl`, `initdb`, `launchctl` or `systemctl` in any task
- every install task comes after the `rp_present` check, loops or names `rp_missing`, is skipped under `--check`, and never upgrades or reinstalls
- there is exactly one receipt line

A deliberate mutation (`brew services start`, a blind `brew install`) turns them red. `hosts_play_test.go` gains the play's row. `TestUnitTestsArePure` passes.

**Not run:** no play was run and no machine was touched. The play runs after merge, and the macOS leg is expected to stay red until then if initdb is not yet on the runner's PATH.

body:
## What

The actions group, after Button and IconButton.

- **ButtonGroup**, standard and connected, selecting none, one or several. `bind selected: List<Int>` covers both single and multi select, and `icon_only` and `on_tap(i)` cover the rest. Connected items share their outer corners, and the selected one rounds fully. The items are toggle buttons in a group: Tab moves between them and Space toggles.
- **SplitButton**, xs to xl, filled, tonal, elevated and outlined. The trailing half turns its chevron and rounds when `open`, and says so with `a11y_expanded`. The menu itself comes in wave 2. For now there's `on_menu`.
- **Fab** in three sizes, the six colour sets, and lowered.
- **ExtendedFab** in three sizes, and `expanded`.
- **FabMenu**: the FAB turns into a close button, and its items sit in an Overlay anchored above it. Escape, a tap outside, or picking an item closes it.

## What's still missing

Several things snap where Material moves:
- the connected items' corners;
- the split button's shape when it opens;
- a pressed item in a group widening;
- an ExtendedFab collapsing.

Byard can't animate `width`, padding, or a radius given per corner. These go in the engine work wave 1 turned up. The widening also uses `pointer_down`/`pointer_up`, so Space doesn't trigger it until it can go in `on pressed`.

A raised FAB doesn't lift on hover. The shadow presets stop at `"lg"`, and the FAB rests there.

## How to check

```bash
cd gallery
byard get
byard test
byard shot . --view ButtonGroupPage --size 900x1300 -o groups.png
byard shot . --view FabPage --size 900x2600 -o fabs.png
```

Values I'm not sure of, all in the notes: the group's gaps and inner corners, the split button's trailing width and inner corners, the extended FAB measurements, how much a pressed item widens (my own guess), and the FAB menu's colours and spacing.

## Summary

Closes javedh-dev/tracktor#242.

Compliance PUT called .partial() on a Zod object containing refinements, causing HTTP 500 before updates could be validated. Earlier localized-date fixes alone did not address this server-side failure.

Load the existing record, merge the submitted changes, force route-owned identifiers, and validate the complete result with the original refined schema. This preserves omitted attachments and recurrence fields while retaining the other-type label invariant.

```diff
- complianceSchema.partial()
+ complianceSchema.parse({ ...existing, ...changes, id: routeId, vehicleId: routeVehicleId })
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Compliance PUT called .partial() on a Zod object containing refinements, causing HTTP 500 before updates could be validated. Earlier localized-date fixes alone did not address this server-side failure.
- **After:** Both route tests failed before the fix and passed afterward. Tests execute the actual PUT handler with mocked persistence, verify omitted-field preservation, and reject removal of a required other-type label. The existing service retains vehicle ownership checks.
- `pnpm test`: 36 passed (36).
- `pnpm check`: passed, with zero errors and warnings.
- `pnpm lint`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Environment: Node.js 26.13.0 and pnpm 10.33.0. Validation was local; remote PR CI has not run for this branch.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. The code can be reverted. No destructive schema change is introduced.

**Blast Radius:** Compliance.

Partial updates now validate the complete merged record, preserving omitted fields and enforcing existing refinements. Route tests mock persistence; the service retains its existing vehicle ownership checks.

Everything built since #3: SEC-based analysis (statements, ratios, valuation, insiders, filings), a rebuilt Fundamentals tab for long-term investors, and a UI/UX and performance redesign of the whole app.

## Before merging

- **Merging deploys to production, and the build runs database migrations.** `npm run build` runs `scripts/db-setup.ts`, which applies pending migrations `0001`–`0004` (sector metrics, insiders, metric reloads) to the production database, then loads SEC sector data within a time budget. If previews and production share the Neon database, preview builds have already applied them; otherwise the first production build will.
- The preview has only been checked from outside the beta gate: the build, health check and gate redirect work. Please look at it logged in, ideally with **AAPL** (covered by the free FMP plan) and **KO** (not covered: it should show the plan messages), on phone and desktop.

## What's included

**SEC data (public, outside the beta gate)**
- Financial statements parser with per-cell citations; Financials tab with TTM, number checks, links to each SEC document, and projections from editable assumptions.
- Ratios with sector percentiles (SEC frames) and 10-year history; banks, insurers and REITs get their own metrics.
- Filings tab (all EDGAR filings, filters, direct links); Insiders tab from Form 4.
- Fundamentals: Buffett-style quality tests on 10 years of 10-Ks (split-adjusted per-share data), 3/5/10-year growth, 10-year trends.

**Valuation (FMP prices, behind the gate)**
- Interactive comps, a fillable DCF checked against an independent reference, and a 5-year multiples history with median ±1σ.
- Analyst consensus (estimates, price target, ratings), where the free plan allows it.
- Plan restrictions are cached for a day so they don't spend the daily quota.

**Redesign (last 4 commits)**
- Shell: skip link, header that works at 320 px, mobile search panel, SVG icons, shared UI primitives.
- Home: search shown first, each quote section streams on its own, ETFs labelled as ETFs, recently viewed.
- Stock page: the 404 for unknown tickers is kept. Sections stream independently, and each summary sentence shows its number, period and source. Tab and chart settings live in the URL.
- Chart: one chart instance per mount, a crosshair legend and a data table.
- Search: race-safe, with explicit loading, empty and error states.
- Watchlist: paged quotes (no more silent 30-symbol cut-off), stale/expired/rate-limit states, sorting, undo.

## Measurements (local production builds, demo data, 300 ms simulated provider latency)

| | Before | After |

| Stock, mobile: first price on screen | 2,373 ms | 669 ms |

Mobile = 390 px, 4× CPU, Slow 4G; cold cache; median of runs. Provider calls per journey are unchanged (home 12 quote calls, stock page 6). Method and scripts: `e2e/README.md`.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` passes; `npm test` passes 244 unit tests.
- Browser journeys: 21 passing. Accessibility and responsive audit: 9 screens at 7 viewports, both languages and themes, with no horizontal overflow and 0 axe violations. Both run against a local demo build (`npm run start:demo`, then `npm run e2e` / `npm run e2e:audit`).

body:
# Phase 4.5-D Boundary Hardening — Database Identity, Audit Authenticity & Activation Boundary Hardening

Stacked on: #55 (`enterprise/phase-4.5d-final-boundary-remediation`)
Base Commit: `397edde4cd5f26e36028ffbf220c9885edf33c21`
Head Commit: `a9b02fb816cf2daf76f108a661b134108463e3da`

## Scope & Architectural Invariants Preserved
- Single Organization: Canonical ID `000000000000000000000001` (Bharat Properties). Multi-tenant development remains strictly on HOLD.
- Truthful Authority State: `permissionStatus: GRANTED`, `evidenceBasis: OWNER_ATTESTED_AUTHORITY_PERMISSION`.
- Maker-Checker Separation: Distinct submitter, approver, and reviewer authenticated users required. External contracts/permits strictly separated from internal owner attestation.
- Human Review Guard: `requiresHumanReview: true`, `isApplied: false`, zero automated inventory writes.
- Strict PII Prohibition: No allottee names, personal phone numbers, emails, PAN/Aadhaar stored.
- Fail-Closed Runtime: Live HTTP transport blocked while reviewStatus is UNDER_REVIEW.

## Key Changes
1. **P0 Database Connection Identity Verification (`backend/services/authority/databaseEnvironmentSafety.js`):**
   - Implemented exact port equality, host loopback alias constraints, replica-set seeds verification, and SRV verification in `compareConnectionIdentities`.
   - Post-connection identity re-verification in runner before any default setup or writes.
2. **P1 Production Environment Classification:**
   - Robust normalization of `NODE_ENV`, `APP_ENV`, `APPLICATION_ENV`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `STAGE`.
   - Explicit `UNSET` handling for `'undefined'` string coercions.
