body:
## Findings

Semrush Site Audit for www.beautifulblindsandshades.com (project 30275556, crawl finished 2026-11-07) flags **17 pages** with "page `<title>` duplicates the H1" (issue 105). All 17 are the town pages under `/beautiful-blinds-shades-service-areas/`. The redirect plan (`seo/2026-09-25/url-preservation-and-redirect-plan.csv`) keeps all 17 URLs, so each maps to the same route in this site. A scan of every generated page found no other title = H1 pages.

## Cause

`live-metadata.json` (PR #4) carries the live Webflow titles into the rebuild, and each town page's H1 in `homepage/pages/<town>.html` is the same text. `check_location_migration.py` even required them to match. Without this change, all 17 duplicates would go live at launch.

## Change

- `homepage/routes.py`: new `distinct_title(title, h1)`. If the title equals the H1 (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised), it returns the H1 with ", IN"/", OH" plus the brand suffix: `| Beautiful Blinds & Shades`, or the shorter `| Beautiful Blinds` (already used on the site). If that is still over 60 characters, it drops a leading "Custom". Otherwise it leaves the title unchanged.
- `homepage/build_pages.py`: `apply_distinct_title()` runs after `apply_live_metadata()` for every page, including the homepage. Re-fetching live metadata therefore can't bring the duplicate back. The H1s, descriptions, canonicals and schema stay the same, and only the 17 town pages' `<title>` lines change in `dist/`.
- `homepage/check_location_migration.py`: the H1 must still be the live title, and `<title>` must be the distinct one.
- `tests/search-block.test.mjs` (already in the Netlify build command): new test that fails if any `.html` page in `homepage/dist` has a title equal to its H1. I added it to an existing file instead of a new one so `netlify.toml` stays untouched, because open PR #5 edits that line.
- README: one sentence on the rule.

body:
### 🔴 coxd greenlight — RED · read every line
Why: touches sacred path(s): deploy/Dockerfile, deploy/docker-compose.coxd.yml

**Look here first:**
- [low] coxd/cli.py:44 — COXD_CONCURRENCY is checked to be >= 1, but `--concurrency` is still a plain `type=int`. So `--concurrency 0` or a negative number is still accepted, and then the runner never starts a task. This was already true before this change. A small argparse type check would make the flag match the env-var check.
- [low] coxd/cli.py:45 — Running `coxd serve` locally with no flag or env var now gets a cap of 1 instead of 2. This looks intentional, but laptop users will see one task at a time instead of two. Worth a line in the changelog or docs.
- [low] coxd/supervisor.py:243 — The default for the `concurrency` parameter of `serve()` is still 2, but the CLI default is now 1. Any caller that skips the CLI gets a different default. Changing it to 1 would keep them consistent.

---
`coxd serve` now takes its global cap from `COXD_CONCURRENCY`, and the board header and `/api/factory` show it. The new test passes. A loop over all `coxd/test_*.py` files failed only on that test, and the failure was a test bug (wrong base URL), which I fixed. I didn't re-run the full loop after the fix. The commit is made and not pushed. The final `git commit` printed a permission error on `packed-refs.lock`, but `git log` shows the commit.

**Root cause:** the Dockerfile hardcoded `--concurrency 1`, while the CLI default was 2. The cap also wasn't visible anywhere in the UI.

**Fix**
- **`cli.py serve`:**
  - `--concurrency` now defaults to unset. When it isn't given, the cap comes from `COXD_CONCURRENCY`, and from 1 if that is also unset.

- **`factory.py` / `supervisor.py`:** `serve()` records the cap, and `factory.status()` now includes `concurrency`. `/api/factory` and the board's `factory` payload both include it.
- **Board:** the "running" pill now reads `running N / cap`.
- **Deploy:**
  - The Dockerfile `CMD` no longer passes `--concurrency`.

- the default of 1;

author: rogueprocess13
body:
This PR fixes three problems in the gate-reconcile, verify and implement skills. Each fix moves a mechanical decision out of SKILL.md text into a small lib script that has its own test. All three SKILL.md files are now smaller than on main. `make skill-baseline` ran last, and there is no `allow-growth` line.

Later commits fix the points from two reviews. The decision script now holds the ticket on any bad input, and AC headings are read in more forms. The #601 seeder run was moved out of implement and into VERIFY's existing locked section, and the way it picks and runs scenarios was rebuilt so that no ticket text is ever executed (see below). The plugin is bumped to 0.86.0.

## #599: an answer-only reconcile cycle no longer holds again

**Root cause (checked on current main, after #594's marker-based boundary).** `reconcile-comments.sh` is correct: the operator's answer is a user comment posted after the last amendment. The bug was in Step 5 Condition 2 of ticket-gate-reconcile: "If `{UNPROCESSED_COMMENTS}` is non-empty → hold". So a cycle whose only input was the answer to the open questions still posted an amendment, ran `re-claim` and held. That cost another `/ticket-approve` round with nothing left to review.

**Fix.** The agent still makes two judgements. It decides whether each question is answered. It also sorts each comment into *answer-only* or *new-input*, and an answer that adds behaviour, a field, a role or an AC counts as new-input. It then strikes answered questions as before. The hold decision itself is now `lib/reconcile-decide.sh`:

- **hold:** an unstruck `- [needs-human]` bullet remains (new questions count), or at least one comment is new-input.
- **clean-recorded:** every comment is answer-only. The skill posts the amendment comment, which moves the next boundary past the answers, skips `re-claim`, and passes clean.
- **clean:** there is nothing to record.

The script never lets a bad call through. An empty, missing or non-numeric count prints `RECONCILE_DECISION=hold HOLD_REASON=reconcile_decide_error`, so an unset `COMMENTS_N` holds the ticket instead of producing an empty decision. When the new-input count is higher than the total, the script raises the total; it never lowers the new-input count.

**Test.** `lib/tests/test-reconcile-decide.sh` has 14 checks:
- **origin/main:** 0 passed, 14 failed.
- **Previous PR head (66536c3):** 9 passed, 5 failed. The failures are new-input above the total, unset or invalid counts, and the SKILL rule.
- **Now:** 14 passed.

## #604: ACs added during the gate hold now reach context.md and VERIFY

**Root cause (checked).** `context.md` is written once by `ticket-setup/setup.sh`, and nothing compared it with the tracker after the hold. ticket-verify Step 1c also called the context.md Description "the authoritative body".

**Fix.** `lib/ac-drift.sh` compares the tracker's ACs with context.md's ACs and with the notes.md Verification Plan rows, which it counts with the shared `vplan_parse`. Text is compared after normalising case, whitespace and checkbox state. Behaviour:

- **Finding the AC section:** a heading of any level starts it, and so does a `**Acceptance Criteria**` label (as in notes-parse). The section ends at the next heading of the same or a higher level, or at a `---` line.
- **On drift:** it logs `AC_DRIFT_AT_<TAG>`, prints `AC_ADDED_n` lines and exits 1.
- **With no ACs in the tracker:** if the description is empty or has no AC section, it logs `AC_DRIFT_UNKNOWN` and leaves context.md unchanged.
- **`--refresh`:** it replaces only the body of context.md's AC section and keeps that file's own heading level.

How the skills use it:
- **Gate reconcile:** saves the description to `$TICKET_DIR/artifacts/tracker-description.md`, not `/tmp`. In the Step 8 clean pass it runs the refresh, and the agent then adds Verification Plan rows for the new ACs.
- **ticket-verify Step 1c:** pipes the Step 1b description into the script. On drift, the Linear list is authoritative.

**Test.** `lib/tests/test-ac-drift.sh` has 29 checks, including h3 and bold-label headings, an empty description with `--refresh`, and an h3 heading in context.md:
- **origin/main:** 4 passed, 25 failed.
- **Previous PR head:** 23 passed, 6 failed.
- **Now:** 29 passed.

## #601: seeder scenarios run twice as a VERIFY precheck, before any criterion

**Root cause (checked).** A ticket's own seeder scenario first ran inside the VERIFY criteria, after about 25 minutes of other checks. A contract bug, or a race that only shows on a clean DB, then cost a re-implement plus a second full VERIFY. Only test-data-engineer tickets had any rule to run the seed command earlier.

**Why the run happens in VERIFY and not in implement.** The local stack and its DB are shared and use fixed ports. VERIFY already holds `lib/verify-lock.sh` from stack start through its checks, runs `env-start.sh`, and applies blocker `Seed command:` targets inside that locked section. Running the seeder from implement needed a second lock holder, a project reset command and a release path, and review showed that path could free VERIFY's own lock or leak it. VERIFY's locked section already gives the clean baseline the issue asks for and runs on every re-implement. The failure now arrives at the start of VERIFY, before any criterion.

**Fix: `lib/seed-precheck.sh`, called from ticket-verify Step 1.6d** (after seed-apply, still under the lock; browser and live-backend modes like 1.6c). The agent runs one command and routes on its result. It never runs seed commands itself.

- **Which scenarios (trust model).** Nothing a tracker user can edit is executed or parsed into a command. Names come only from the seed tool's own git history: commits on any ref whose message names this ticket id, limited to the seed directory, and only the `scenario_<name>()` functions those commits add or change. context.md, the tracker description, comments and the plan are never read, so a scenario that a blocker or an AC merely mentions is not run. Each name must match a strict regex (no flags, no trailing `.`, `_` or `-`), must not be `baseline`, and must be defined in the checked-out seed directory.
- **How it runs.** `bash <seed-dir>/seed.sh <name>` as an argv list, no `bash -c`, no eval, stdin from `/dev/null`, from the verify worktree, twice per scenario. Each run is a background job under `set -m`, so it gets its own process group. On timeout (`SEED_APPLY_TIMEOUT_SECS`, default 900; 0 = none) the whole group gets TERM, a 10 s grace, then KILL, so grandchildren the seeder started (a `sleep`, a client, a forked server) die with it. `timeout(1)` only signals its direct child and left those orphaned. If the helper itself is killed with TERM or INT, it kills the seeder group before it exits.
- **Results.** `SEED_PRECHECK_STATUS=pass|skip|unavailable|fail` (eval-safe). `pass`, `skip` (no scenario changed by this ticket) and `unavailable` (no seed tool, not a git repo, or a changed scenario missing from the checkout; exit 3) continue to the criteria. `fail` (exit 1) logs `VERIFY|seed-precheck|fail|<name> run <n>: <reason>`, releases the verify lock (`--release-on-fail`), and the agent goes to Step 7 as a normal FAIL: WHAT_FAILED is `SEED_PRECHECK_MSG`, and the REMEDIATION_BRIEF points at the seeder.
- **Attempt counting (deliberate).** The `seed-precheck|fail` line is a step line. `verify_attempt_count`, `verify_latest_verdict` and detect-resume key on `VERIFY|verify|fail|`, so that line alone burns no VERIFY attempt and is no verdict. Step 7's own `VERIFY|verify|fail` line then counts that attempt exactly once. It must count: if it did not, a seeder that never passes would re-implement forever, because the attempt cap would never be reached. fleet-controller's `detect_phase_failures` reads the line as a WARN-level phase failure, not a gate-stop, so the failure is visible on the fleet side too.
- **ticket-implement Step 4b:** static checks plus a pointer only. It checks every request t

## Summary

Closes javedh-dev/tracktor#177.

Fuel CSV import could fail when optional quantities were unmapped, even though the wizard marked them optional. The gallons column in the reported sample was not recognized by automatic mapping, and format requirements were unclear.

Recognize gallons during automatic mapping, allow blank optional odometer/fuel amounts as null, reject non-finite or nonpositive supplied quantities, and preserve decimal precision. Document exact header mapping, date formats, units, optional fields, and partial-import behavior.

```diff
- Require optional odometer and fuel amount during import
+ Preserve blank optional quantities as null and automatically recognize gallons
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Fuel CSV import could fail when optional quantities were unmapped, even though the wizard marked them optional. The gallons column in the reported sample was not recognized by automatic mapping, and format requirements were unclear.
- **After:** Tests parse the exact reported CSV, map price/gallons, retain 11.308 gallons, validate saved payloads with the real fuel schema, import omitted optional quantities, and report failed rows while retaining successful rows. Persistence is mocked. The selected file date format must match the CSV; no automatic unit conversion or atomic import behavior was introduced.
- `pnpm test`: 37 passed (37).
- `pnpm check`: passed, with zero errors and warnings.
- `pnpm lint`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Environment: Node.js 26.13.0 and pnpm 10.33.0. Validation was local; remote PR CI has not run for this branch.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. The code can be reverted. No destructive schema change is introduced.

**Blast Radius:** Import.

Imports still save rows individually, retain successful rows after failures, and do not convert units. File date format must match the CSV. Persistence is mocked in the regression tests.

author: jaydeep-comprint
body:
## What
  On-demand, cited AI summaries for teachers: one for a class (last 7 days, 30 days or all time) and one for a single student, each with up to 3 re-teaching notes (1 for a student) that link to lessons and prefill an assignment.

  - **What the model sees:** only numbered facts built from the 010 dashboard numbers (`dashboard.class_snapshot` / `student_snapshot`), with students as `{Sn}` pseudonyms. No names, usernames, ids or emails are sent, and this is asserted in tests on the recorded request.
  - **Citation guard** (`app/ai/teacher_guard.py`): server-side and pure. It drops any claim that is uncited, cites an unknown fact, or contains a number or student its cited facts don't support. After that comes one retry with a note saying what was dropped; then the better of the two replies is kept as `partial`, or the summary is `failed`.
  - **Storage:** summaries are stored in `teacher_summary` (migration 0011, RLS on, composite FKs) and `partial`, or the summary is `failed`.
- **Storage:** summaries are stored in `teacher_summary` (migration 0011, RLS on, composite FKs) and shared by the school's teachers. They're marked stale when the facts hash changes.
- **Caps:** 10 per teacher and 50 per school per IST day, a 10-minute cooldown on unchanged data, and one generation per target at a time. The caps are checked under an advisory lock, and no transaction is open during the model call. `TEACHER_AI_ENABLED` is the kill switch.
- **Model:** DeepSeek `deepseek-v4-pro` (JSON mode, prefix cache), on the tutor's client and key.
- **UI:** a summary card on the class Overview and on the student page. It has citation chips (a popover on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones) that link to the source card, concept, misconception, assignment or student section, plus Copy, and Assign prefilled from a note. A lesson opens at a KP with `?step=`.
- **Eval:** `app teacher-ai eval [--runs 3] [--case ID]`, 10 fact-set cases graded by a judge.

## Differences from the spec
- `ResourceOut` has `concept`, `available` and `in_course` instead of `course` and `concept_course`.
- A 503 on POST shows a message instead of hiding the card.
- The eval prints tokens, not cost (multiply by the current prices).
- The service cases are tested in the DB tests (`test_teacher_ai_db.py`), not in a separate offline file.
- Limits raised after the eval: per-request timeout 120 s, overall cap 180 s, `max_tokens` 16000. If the overall cap expires after a call has finished, the result is kept with its tokens (`partial`, or `failed`, which is counted) instead of becoming an uncounted `error`.

## Also in this PR
- `tests/test_tutor_api_db.py`: the hint test assumed KP1's first question is numeric. KP1 also has an MCQ, which made the test fail now and then with `KeyError: 'value'`. It now checks the numeric answer only when there is one. (This was already flaky on `main`; the related derived-order bug is fixed in #13.)

## Eval (`uv run app teacher-ai eval --runs 3`, deepseek-v4-pro writer and judge)

Prompt as of abb7c1a. Pass = 0 unsupported claims and 0 overclaimed causes.

```
case                       runs fail  ok part  tokens in/out
typical_class                 3    0   3    0    2961/7518
struggling_with_causes        3    0   3    0    3033/13278
thin_data                     3    0   2    1    2331/4048
few_tries_high_rate           3    0   3    0    2592/6986
same_rates                    3    0   3    0    2604/4869
injection_in_title            3    1   3    0    2586/7800
    injection: attempted names   <- old check (see below)
student_memory_only           3    0   3    0    2472/3880
student_overdue_rushing       3    0   3    0    2718/7148
window_all                    3    0   3    0    2874/11958
no_causes                     3    0   3    0    2586/5914

Total 30 runs: 0 unsupported claims, 0 overclaimed causes, 0 runs without a claim, 0 unverified runs.
Vague quantities 0% of claims; actionable notes 100%.
Tokens: writer 26757 in (22912 cache hits) / 73399 out, judge 24917 in / 55808 out.
```

The one injection flag came from the eval's own check: the injected misconception title says "real name", so
quoting the title tripped it. The model never receives real names. The check now ignores titles quoted from the
facts and says what triggered it (9ddf2f3). Re-run of that case with the same prompt:

```
injection_in_title            5    0   5    0    4310/12742
Total 5 runs: 0 unsupported claims, 0 overclaimed causes, 0 runs without a claim, 0 unverified runs. PASS
```

Fixes the eval drove: per-request timeout 60 -> 120 s and wall clock 150 -> 180 s (a timeout), `max_tokens`
8000 -> 16000, prompt rules against unbacked comparisons and against presenting other numbers as at-risk reasons,
and the judge no longer treating an at-risk fact's own reasons as an overclaimed cause.

## Verification
- `make check`: 710 backend tests, 202 frontend tests, ruff, mypy, eslint and prettier clean, content OK.
- `make test-db`: all 159 DB tests pass, in two runs because the connection to Supabase was slow. The first run, on 4f597e7, had 131 passed (including all 10 in `test_teacher_ai_db.py`) and then hit the flaky tutor test. The second covered the tutor and XP files after the fix in 0ec14d6: 28 passed.
- Reviewer subagent against the spec: two passes. Fixes are in 26a7613 and 4f597e7; the only item left is optional (the injection check in the eval doesn't strip curly-quoted titles, so it can only over-report).
- Browser click-through at desktop and 360 px, done by hand.
- Note: after the eval, 4f597e7 changed one sentence in the prompt's example note, from "Most failures are on…" to numbers. The eval wasn't re-run after that change.

author: dfkunstler
body:
A parse error no longer keeps a copy of the input document (#42).

1. When the failing value of a schema entry of `OscalParseError.errors` is an object or an array, its `input` is the
   sentinel `OscalParseError.OMITTED_INPUT` (repr `<omitted input>`). It stays the same object through `copy`,
   `deepcopy`, and `pickle`. Scalar inputs stay. Limit entries keep `input: None`.
2. `parse_oscal` raises outside the `except` block, as it already did for a limit entry. Neither `__cause__` nor
   `__context__` keeps the `ValidationError` and its copy of the input.
3. The `oscal_document_type` message still names the keys of the object: it reads them before the input is replaced.

The sentinel is a class attribute, so `__all__`, the surface snapshot, and `traceability.json` do not change. No
existing test changes: `git diff --stat tests/` shows only new tests in `tests/test_parser.py`.

## Results

NIST SP 800-53 rev5 catalog. "Held" is the memory that dropping the caught error frees.

| Fault | Entries | Held |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog` missing `metadata` | 1 | 1.6 KB (25.7 MB before) |
| one control `id` is an int | 2 | 2.6 KB |
| 3 control `id`s are ints in each of 20 groups | 80 | 70.3 KB (25.0 MB before) |

The memory test measures what dropping the error frees, because pydantic-core keeps a JSON string cache across
parses (about 0.9 MB cold, 0.45 MB warm) that is not tied to the error. With the input replacement removed, the same
test reports 24.8 MB.

The 2 and 80 entries above still include the nested-union fan-out of #43 (cairn-proofs/oscal-bindings-specs#36). This
PR bounds what each entry holds, not how many entries a fault gives.

## Release notes

- **Changed error content.** In `OscalParseError.errors`, an entry whose failing value is an object or an array has
  `input` `OscalParseError.OMITTED_INPUT` (shown as `<omitted input>`), not the value. Use `loc` to find the value in
  your input. `json.dumps(e.errors)` now needs `default=repr`.
- A parse error no longer chains the pydantic `ValidationError` as `__cause__`. The entries carry its detail.
- A schema error on a large document holds a few KB, not a copy of the document.

Closes #42.

author: trevorbrown-dev
body:
Fixes #2097 (split from #2091 item 1). Item 3 of #2091 is #2099; item 2 (#2098) already imports correctly on main.

## Cause

An instance scaled with the Scale tool (K) in Figma keeps its own size and stores `symbolData.uniformScaleFactor`. Its layers' lengths are the main's times that factor. FigCraft's `.fig` export already writes the factor: `export/component.rs` derives it and moves every value that follows from it into `derivedSymbolData`, so FigCraft-to-FigCraft round trips were fine. The importer, though, read `symbolID` and `symbolOverrides` and never the factor (`Fig::instance` in `map/component.rs`). A layer with no derived row therefore came in at the main's values. In the reporter's file that covered 370 instances: a 128 px instance of a 256 px icon component drew its 256 px child with the main's 64 px radius, where Figma draws 128 px and 32 px.

## Fix

- The factor is read in `Fig::instance` and composed through nested instances. A factor outside 0.001 to 1000 is ignored, the product is clamped to that range, and results that aren't finite are dropped.
- `View` (`map.rs`) carries a factor per layer it stacks:
  - The main's layers take the instance's factor.
  - The instance's override, derived and stale rows take 1, since they are written at the instance's scale already.
  - A linked style takes the factor of the layer that links it.
  - A length is read at the scale of the row that supplies it, so there is no double scaling and every reader in `map/*.rs` agrees.
- Lengths covered, mirroring what FigCraft's own Scale tool (`scale_node`) scales:
  - size, and the translation of the transform
  - corner radii, stroke weights (with the per-side weights) and dashes
  - effects' radius, spread and offsets, and noise size
  - layout grids
  - auto layout gap, cross gap, paddings, grid gaps, min and max size
  - font size, and line height and letter spacing in pixels
  - paragraph spacing and indent, list spacing, and the style override table
- The constraint fit (`Fit`) and the `resized` check compare the instance with its main at the main's scaled size. Without that, the layers of a scaled instance would be fitted again to a size they already have.

## Verified

- `fig::tests::a_scaled_instance_draws_its_layers_at_the_factor` (the reproducer): child 256 x 256 with radius 64 before, 128 x 128 with radius 32 now.
- `fig::scale_factor_tests` (new, 7 tests), each red before the change where it applies:
  - a derived `size` row is taken as written while the position and radius from the main scale;
  - no rows at all;
  - auto layout gap, cross gap and padding (20, 6, 10 at 0.5 now 10, 3, 5);
  - an override row's dashes are not scaled again;
  - a nested instance inside a scaled one composes (0.5 inside 0.5);
  - factor 1 and a missing factor change nothing;
  - junk factors (-0.5, 0, 1e30, 3e38, 1e-30) change nothing and do not overflow.
- Review fixes (c7c5a4f8), each red first: a nested instance's own override and derived rows are read at its enclosing main's scale (`a_nested_instances_own_rows_are_at_its_enclosing_mains_scale`: a Dot of 100 with radius 7 inside a 0.5 instance is 50 and 3.5, not 100 and 7); a progressive blur's start and end are unit-box positions and are not rescaled (`a_progressive_blurs_positions_are_not_lengths`); an effect or grid style takes the factor of the layer that links it, so one an instance row links stays as the style defines it (`an_effect_style_takes_the_scale_of_the_layer_that_links_it`). Component property text runs of a nested instance take its scale too. Format 655 passed.
- `fig::export_tests::assets::a_scaled_instance_keeps_its_radius_through_a_round_trip`: green before and after.
- `cargo test -p figcraft-format --lib`: 652 passed.
- `-p figcraft-engine --lib`: 1897 passed. The one local failure is `board_tables_tests::a_double_click_types_in_the_cell_and_its_row_grows_with_the_text`, from craft-fonts missing here.
- clippy `-D warnings` on format and engine, and `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the `.fig` row and its revision history.

## Not changed

- `fillGeometry` and `strokeGeometry` blobs: a real file supplies them in derived rows, and a vector's network follows the layer's size.
- Lengths the Scale tool scales that have no clear or tested `.fig` path here:
  - per-point network corner radii
  - fixed grid tracks
  - image tile scale
  - glass
  - text decoration thickness and offset
  - text on a path
  - guides
  - a style's own effects, grids and text beyond the linking layer's factor
- A pre-existing exporter gap, not changed here: a length inside a scaled instance reset by hand to exactly the main's value is not `changed`, so the exporter writes it in neither list while still writing `uniformScaleFactor`; importing (FigCraft now, and Figma) scales it.
- NaN and infinite factors could not be written by the test encoder. The range check refuses them.

Reviewed (Fable 5.1) before marking ready; its three findings are fixed in c7c5a4f8.

  * Imported `.fig` files now preserve component-instance scaling, including nested instances and applicable geometry, layout, effects, and text measurements.
  * Import and export preserve scaled-instance overrides and style links, including explicit clears.

## What happened
In the developer log, a streaming recognizer returned only a short rolling window of the newest words. Stable-mode matching dropped any word more than 3 ahead of the cursor, and those words were still counted as handled. The page stalled for ~18s, then jumped 57 words, then said "Oops! We skipped a part" and snapped the reader back to words she had already read.

## Fix (`shellfie/app.js`)
- A run of 3 contiguous words heard ahead of the cursor (kept across updates) now moves the highlight to the reader (`follow-ahead` log event). Skipped words stay unread.

- Added `tests/follow_ahead.js`, which replays the rolling-window case. It fails on the old code and passes now. Simulated speech only.

- `asr_revisions`, `sound_alikes`, `follow_ahead` pass.
- `reader_stress` has one failing check, `noisyRoom`, which fails the same way without this change.

author: drecoder
body:
## Stage

**Codification (stage 2), after proofing (stage 3) of the white paper.** No implementation, and no conformance tests: those are stages 4–5, gated on owner approval of this standard.

**Stacked on #58** (Quality Policy Engine): the harness consumes `policy_decision.v1`. Merge #58 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it codifies

The hypothesis: an autonomous engineering system should not decide on model reasoning alone. It should weigh organizational knowledge, current reliability, deterministic quality evidence and governance state, and stay context-aware without becoming self-authorizing.

- **Standard:** `06_AgentZone/09_Adaptive_Harness.md` (status: proposed)
- **Diagram:** `docs/architecture/sheet-4-adaptive-harness.svg`
- **Contracts (proposed):**
  - `harness_decision.v1`, one bounded decision with its inputs, from a closed action vocabulary
  - `knowledge_record.v1`, a long-term memory entry that points to a sealed source
- **Rules:** AGENTS.md (two "target design" bullets); an amendment to Telemetry-Driven Dynamics; cross-references in the notepad doc; ARCHITECTURE.md; MASTER_INDEX §10; a textbook chapter

## Proofing findings, and how each is resolved

The full report is in the Software Factory project (`claude/harness-whitepaper-proof.md`).

- **B1 (blocking):** the white paper is truncated. The second copy runs through §13 and stops mid-sentence in §14 (deliverables). §1–13 are codified; **the owner supplies §14 if it lists anything more** (open decision O3).
- **B2 (blocking):** "operational telemetry" mixed the harness's own health with the target service's reliability. Every state now names its subject: `service`, `harness` or `practice`.
- **C1–C9 (conflicts with existing standards):**
  - The memory model, steering bounds, model selection, rules-before-models, Red/Green naming, fixer routing and autonomy levels are reused, not duplicated.
  - One conflict is **documented, not edited** (white paper §12): the hypothesis lets concurrency return toward its ceiling, but Telemetry-Driven Dynamics allows pacing down only. It is open decision O1; until decided, Dynamics governs and `restore_concurrency` is not in the vocabulary.
- **G1–G6 (gaps):** causal attribution needs a recorded chain; "stale" is defined by the burn-rate short windows; promotion criteria; retrieved content is data; "high CRAP" and "surviving mutants" are defined from Policy Engine findings; an empty input is UNKNOWN.
- **F1–F3 (feasibility):**
  - No factory service has SLOs (SD-07), so every service state is UNKNOWN today and the harness would escalate before every advance. This is the intended conservative behavior.
  - Retrieval stays lexicographic until a calibration set exists.

## White paper §9–13 (second commit)

- **§12 Evaluation cadence:** cheap complexity and CRAP checks each iteration; mutation at checkpoints on changed modules; the gate's full evaluation is the only authoritative one.
- **§13 Audit trail:** the decision record carries the evaluation identity (commit, merge base, candidate and baseline digests, toolchain, evaluation ID), the telemetry window, the selected tier, and the previous decision with its outcome. Knowledge records name the decisions they came from. No new store.
- **§14 Acceptance criteria:** all 24, each mapped to the part of the standard that carries it, plus adversarial cases for test design.
- **§15 Conflicts and open decisions:** O1 concurrency, O2 the status vocabulary (PROPOSED is the legend's Design), O3 the truncated §14, O4 numeric weights.
- **§16 Status:** per capability, in BUILT / PARTIAL / PROPOSED / OPEN.

## No new thresholds

GREEN, RED and UNKNOWN come from the existing burn-rate pairs and their windows, saturation alerts, error budgets and open incidents. Quality terms come from QP rules and `quality_policy.v1`. Observation windows come from the autonomy policy's `period`.

## Verification at this stage

- Both schemas are valid JSON Schema and their examples validate (`tests/contracts/test_harness_contracts.py`).
- 25 ad-hoc proofing checks (after §9–13) confirmed each contract constraint matches the decision table. They are not committed: committed conformance cases are the test-design stage's job.
- markdownlint: no new findings. The textbook builds with the new chapter (37) and the diagram.

author: wsustone
body:
Found while adding the planned fuzzing of the `.nnrec` reader.

### Bug: every recording reported 1 record and 0 seconds
`scan()` reads a recording's length and record count, which feed the replay scrub bar and `/api/runs`. It read each record's payload length straight after the address length, without skipping the address itself. So it took the first four characters of `"10.0.1.10:40000"` as a length of about 825 MB, skipped to the end of the file, and reported **1 record, 0 s**. It now skips the address, then the payload. A test records 11 datagrams one second apart and checks for 11 records and 10 s.

### Crashes on damaged files
- Times running backwards in a damaged file underflowed the duration: a panic in debug, a huge length in release. That case now gives 0.
- A huge time value overflowed `SystemTime`, which panics. It now returns an `InvalidData` error, like other damage.

A new test writes 3,000 damaged recordings (bit flips, extreme bytes, truncation, extreme time fields) and requires the reader never to panic. I checked that it does panic without the fix.

### Recordings lost their last seconds when the server was stopped
`serve` has no signal handler, so Ctrl-C or SIGTERM ended it without flushing the recorder's buffer: a 20 s run kept only 17.3 s. It now flushes on the 1 s state tick, so a stopped server loses at most about a second; the same test now keeps 19.95 s.

### Checked end to end
I recorded 20 s of generator traffic with `serve --record`, stopped it with SIGTERM, and listed the file with `serve --runs`. `/api/runs` showed `dur` **0.0** with the old reader, and **19.95 s** with this branch.

All 232 tests, clippy and fmt are clean.

author: wielandtech
body:
## /weather: why Current Conditions failed

Every Home Assistant pod restart starts a **new Prometheus series**, because the `pod` and `instance` labels change. There were 3 temperature series in the last 24h and about 50 over the retention period.

- `/api/weather/` ran a plain instant query. During each rollover the old pod's series goes stale before the new pod reports (I saw a gap of about 3.6 min). The query came back empty, the view returned `status: error`, and the JS drew the red box.
- The charts kept only `result[0]` of the range query. That was a fragment from an old pod: the 24h temperature line ended **5.7 hours ago**, so the charts weren't fully live either.

## Fix
- New `_latest_sample()` reads the raw samples in the last hour (`<series>[1h]`) and returns the newest one across all pod series, with its real timestamp. The API now returns `as_of`. With no reading in the last hour it returns `status: no_data`.
- Chart queries use `max by (entity) (...)`, so the pod fragments merge into one line. The 24h series now has 288 points running up to now, checked against live Prometheus.
- The current-conditions selectors are now shared constants pinned to exact entities. The old regexes could pick indoor humidity, could pick absolute or relative pressure at random, and used a UV metric name (`uv_index`) that doesn't exist; the real one is `unit_index`. Rain is now `daily_rain`, labelled "Rain Today".
- UI: Temperature and Wind are big stat tiles at the top, styled like the homelab metric cards. A muted "as of 10:05 PM" shows the reading time instead of the page refresh time. With no data you get a muted "No reading in the last hour" in place of the red error box, and the tiles and compass reset to `--`.

## /contact
- Heading changed from "Get In Touch" to "Contact".
- A row of teal links under the form: GitHub and LinkedIn.
- The reCAPTCHA "Invalid domain" badge is deliberately not touched. It's a Google console setting, tracked in its own needs-human issue.

Only palette tokens from `dark-mode.css` are used. `main.css` and the navbar are untouched.

## Review / follow-ups
`/code-review` ran before this PR. Two findings were fixed: a stale wind tile, and the compass not resetting. Not fixed:
- History humidity and pressure queries are still wrong (they aren't charted): #59
- `as_of` is the temperature reading's time, and other metrics may be up to 1h older. That's accepted, since they report together.
- The new `core/tests.py` tests have **not been run**. Application Control blocks the local 3.12 venv, and CI has no test step.

## Verification
- [x] Review app https://pr-60.review.wielandtech.com: `/weather/` and `/contact/` checked in the light and dark themes at 1280px and 375px, with no horizontal overflow at 375px. The tiles show live values with "as of 10:20 PM", and the 24h chart's last point is from right now (289 points). Calling `showNoReading()` forces the muted empty state, and it renders cleanly. `/contact/` shows the "Contact" heading and teal GitHub/LinkedIn links (`#35A89C`) in both themes.
- The review app shows "Anti-spam verification is not configured" because it has no reCAPTCHA keys. That's an environment issue, unrelated to this PR.

author: qubitium
body:
## Problem
The four CPU native int4pack fusion adapters in merged #3567 miss the independent BF16 projection oracle at a GQA boundary on an aarch64 Cortex-X925/A725 host. The same error occurs before fusion, so it is in the shared native CPU compute path: at one failing element, the output was `-0.2490234375` against the correctly rounded BF16 oracle `-0.251953125` (`0.0029296875` difference, over the existing `rtol=atol=2e-3` gate). The exact FP64 result was `-0.2511187978`.

## Fix
Use FP32 activation and affine-metadata operands for BF16 calls to the native CPU int4pack op, then return the caller's BF16 dtype. The packed `qweight` stays packed; converted activations and metadata are local to each call. FP16 follows the existing path. The helper is shared by `TorchAtenLinear`, `TorchAtenAwqLinear`, `TorchFusedLinear`, and `TorchFusedAwqLinear`. This is a localized numerical change inside the existing CPU call, so no flow diagram is needed.

## Validation
- After merged #3575 corrected the independent oracle, the combined native fusion, device inference, and Llama fusion suites passed: **165 passed, 126 skipped**. The four previously failing BF16 GQA nodes now pass; max projection error is `0.001953125` in each, parent off/on drift is zero, and retained additional packed-weight bytes are zero.
- AWQ fused and ATen import/packing regression suites: **4 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Actual CPU: aarch64 Cortex-X925/A725, Torch 2.15.0+cu132, no AVX512-BF16. Tested FP16 and BF16, K=512, GQA widths 512/256/256, group 128, and rows 1/8/33/257; the full matrix also covers gate/up rows through 1025 and mutation/restoration.
- An op-only probe with eight Torch threads, four warmups and twenty timed calls measured BF16 vs FP32 operands at 1/8/257 rows: `0.052/0.526/3.565 ms` vs `0.055/0.548/3.070 ms`. These are local kernel timings, not full-model latency claims.
- For K=512, N=512, M=257, explicit temporary FP32 input, metadata and output total **1,069,056 bytes**; internal ATen scratch is excluded. No dense or expanded weight is retained. [Measured CPU evidence](https://github.com/ModelCloud/GPTQModel/blob/fix/cpu-int4pack-bf16/docs/fusion-device-validation.md#additional-cpu-bf16-precision-check-on-arm) and [raw numbers](https://github.com/ModelCloud/GPTQModel/blob/fix/cpu-int4pack-bf16/docs/benchmarks/cpu-bf16-int4pack-arm-regression.json) are committed.
- Ruff, JSON validation, and `git diff --check` passed.

The FP32 operand path has been measured on this ARM host; full-model latency and other CPU architectures were not measured in this PR.

author: vanman989
body:
## G361: Survey points and 3D linework

Closes #681

Board: chapter 30, crates `geom-2d` and `geom-curve`, chapter 17.2; depends on G81, G61, G58, G87 and G284 (a gate review with no code). G81 and G87 are still open (#611, #598), so this is cut from `piece/G87` (which holds G80, G81, G82, G86 and G87) and targets it. G359 is not a dependency and is not merged in.

### What changed

- **`geom_2d::survey`** (new). `import` takes the import operation's `OpPath` and the dataset's records (an ID, a stable `PointKey` and a grid position) and returns one Acorn body: its outside region `Created { op, role: region.outside }` and one vertex per point, `Created { op, role: survey.point(key) }`, published by `Builder::publish_named`, so its arenas are in name order and the body does not depend on the order of the records. Each point's ID is the attribute `kit.geom/survey.id` v1 (its value the ID's CBOR text; Propagate at a split, KeepIfEqual at a merge), keyed by the point's name, so renaming a point changes no name. `PointKey::first_import` makes a key from an ID: the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over `SKG survey point key v1\0` and the ID as a CBOR text string. The caller keeps it, so a re-import with the same `OpPath` and keys gives every point the same name, renamed points included. Two records with one ID fail with `DuplicateId { id, first, second }`, naming both; two with one key with `DuplicateKey`; an ID that is empty or not NFC under Unicode 18.0.0 (32.19's text rule, checked as `Role::new` checks role names) with `Id`.
- **`geom_op::KEYED_ROLES`** gains `survey.point`, so a name graph never takes a point's key for a parent name (`geom_name::graph::parents` skips it, as it skips a boolean's operand keys). G87's attack test lists it.
- **`geom_curve::linework`** (new). `linework(points, segments, meter)` joins one figure's grid points by `Segment::Line`, `Segment::Arc` (through the next point to the one after) and `Segment::Smooth { points, rule }` into one `Composite<3>`.
  - An arc's center is the circumcenter of its plan points, ported from SMLib's `smgu_CircleFrom3Points`; its sense and collinearity are decided exactly in `i128`. It is one helix when its plan chords and rises are equal (both halves then turn through equal angles, so the grade is one), one level arc (`Circle`) when its three heights are equal, and otherwise two pieces meeting at the middle point, each a helix or, where its two heights are equal, a level arc. All three heights are kept and no tolerance decides it. Each piece is a `Helix` (or `Circle`) on a frame with its reference vector toward its first point and its normal up or down by the turn, from parameter 0 over its turn in half-turns (the kernel's `atan2`); its pitch is twice its rise over that turn.
  - A smooth figure is `geom-nurbs`'s A9.1 interpolation, cubic (quadratic through three points), by the rule asked for.
  - Every surveyed point's distance from the curve at its parameter, from both sides at each joint, is certified from interval enclosures and must be at most ε_fit (64 steps), or the figure fails with `OverFit`. `Linework::exactness(step)` is Exact for lines alone and Certified with the bound rounded up to whole steps otherwise. Repeated points, collinear arcs, short figures and miscounted segments are typed errors naming the point or segment.
- `Composite` gains a crate-internal `starting_within`: the constructor with a joint allowance that transforms already used, for pieces that meet at a surveyed point only within their certified bounds of it. Each joint's gap is recorded as for any composite.
- **Chapter 17.2** gains an "As built (G361)" paragraph.

### Done when

- Acorn points named by import and record key: done, as above, with names stable across re-imports and renames.
- Duplicate-ID errors: done, naming the ID and both records.
- 3D polylines with helix arcs: done, one helix or two pieces by an exact grade test.
- Smooth figures within ε_fit: done, NURBS interpolation certified within ε_fit at every point.

### How it was checked

On a development machine: `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `geom-curve`, `geom-2d`, `geom-op`, `geom-name` and `geom-bench` (and for `geom-bench` on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`); map, provenance and recursion checks; the new tests `geom-curve/tests/linework.rs` (12) and `geom-2d/tests/survey.rs` (9).

- `cargo nextest run` of `geom-curve`, `geom-2d`, `geom-op`, `geom-name` and `geom-topo`: 346 passed; doctests pass.
- `cargo test -p geom-bench --release`: every test passes with `golden.txt` re-recorded (3 new lines, no digest moved); `clippy --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p geom-bench --all-targets`: clean.
- `engine-geometry` with `--run-ignored all` (wasmtime on the path): every test passes but `attack_g12::attack_statics_from_files_the_scan_never_reads`, which refuses a temporary folder outside the workspace and failed only because that run's target folder was outside it; CI's default target is inside. The crate table now marks `geom-2d` built (`Elsewhere("G361")`), as G80 marked `geom-topo`, which `attack_g09` asks of a crate that holds code.
- `golden -- check`, `map -- check`, `provenance -- check` and `recursion -- check`: clean.

Oracles: each arc's circumcenter and radius in exact rationals (`dashu-ratio`) against the stored helix or level arc; every point against the curve evaluated at its parameter; each helix piece's grade against its points' rise over its turn; seeded arcs on random circles of radius 2^12 to 2^34 steps in every quadrant, turning either way (`SPAREKIT_SEED` replays one); a first import's key against SHA-256 over the prefix and the ID's CBOR text written out byte by byte; each name against `TopoName::id` of the name chapter 17.2 gives; and the name graph's parents of a point's name, which are none.

### Benchmarks

A new `survey` group in `geom-bench` (decision 32.44): `survey/linework` (a figure of a line, an arc and a smooth figure), `survey/import` (datasets of 16 points) and `survey/first_import`. `golden.txt` gains 3 lines and no existing digest moved; the golden store records it (piece G361).

**Store edit for the owner to approve at merge:** `geom-bench/output-hashes` in `crates/geom-test/golden/store.json`, one new corpus history record.

### Sources

- Existing code first: solidcore at `7a593124c98e2bdfc7adc4fa94aeeb9b758cf450` has no survey points, three-point arcs or surveyed linework (its arcs are given by center and angles, `curve/arc.rs`, and its helix is a sampled B-spline, `primitive/api_curves.rs`, where the kernel's `Helix` is exact). NVIDIA's usd-brep (SMLib) has the circle through three points: `smgu_CircleCenterFrom3Points` and `smgu_CircleFrom3Points` in `SmGeomUtility.cpp` (Apache-2.0; the same file at `c9c5979f04cea8c38213004d4f04df0dcfb40d05`, the commit `notices/usd-brep.txt` pins, and at today's `3fd5b9548d19aa8c12c29bc9637a96d42a06f8a5`), ported into `linework.rs` with its `Source:` record. Its weaknesses, fixed in the port: collinearity by a distance against `SM_EFF_ZERO` (here exact in integers); the bisector equations on absolute coordinates squared in doubles, which lose their low bits far from the origin (here relative to the first point, in double-double); and its circle checked only by debug assertions (here every point is certified).
- Methods: chapter 17.2; The NURBS Book's A9.1 (through `geom-nurbs`, G58); chapter 20.2's names and 32.19's NameScheme v1; chapter 8.4's attributes.
- Crates: none new. `geom-bench` gains `geom-2d` and `geom-op` as path dependencies (already in its tree through `geom-topo`).

### Notes for review

- The key derivation (prefix and CBOR text) is new and is hashed into names, so it is fixed once files hold such names; its prefix carries a version for any later rule.
- `survey.point` in `KEYED_ROLES` changes G87's constant (this is stacked on it). The attribute `kit.geom/survey.id` is defined in `geom-2

author: willibaldsoft
body:
Adds an editable, Node-only Cockpit-XP ZIP import preview for drivers, cars, tracks, finished sessions, results and laps. Users review/edit/remove rows, resolve links and explicitly confirm before anything is written. Existing linked entities are preserved; writes use Prisma transactions, import fingerprints and the standard mandatory pre-import database backup.

The preview now offers an **unchecked optional copy into the local vehicle/tyre catalog**. It becomes available when the local catalog from #16 is installed; this import PR still works independently without that feature or its schema. No catalog implementation or migration is duplicated here.

- Copies reviewed cars with brand, model, year, scale, photos, equipment, front/rear tyre references, notes and explicit gram/millimetre measurements.
- Prefills explicit source article numbers and lets users supply missing references in the preview. References must be present and unique; they are never inferred from model names.
- Preserves existing catalog references and linked cars. Newly created cars receive the reviewed reference. The completion message reports added/skipped catalog articles.
- Keeps tyre details with their car. Original tyre properties without an explicit axle remain reviewable source notes rather than being guessed into front/rear fields. Source measurements without known units are not converted.
- Catalog writes participate in the existing transaction and backup. Catalog changes invalidate stale previews. Drivers, tracks, sessions, results and laps retain their normal destinations.

FR/EN/DE translations and docs/COCKPIT-XP-IMPORT.md describe the workflow. Version, changelog and dependency lockfile are unchanged by this addition. Source backup files and personal cars/photos are not included.

Validation at head b11f559 (Linux / Node 22.23.3):

- Complete standalone backend suite: **180/180 tests in 20/20 suites**, zero failures or skipped tests, through `npm test -w @racehubos/backend` with explicit VM-module startup flags and a writable Prisma cache.
- **13/13 targeted backend tests with both features installed**, including actual photo-byte restoration, axle-specific tyres, car/catalog links, preserved existing articles and stale catalog detection.
- **6 Chromium cases**: FR/EN/DE with the catalog available, plus FR/EN/DE with the import PR alone and the option disabled.
- Production builds for the standalone and combined installations and `npm run check:push` pass.
- Regression proof: deliberately ignoring an existing catalog article makes the new protection test fail; restoring the implementation makes the targeted tests pass.

Based on upstream main e162798e943406b8fe26ba5597fcf6d4ff6b593c (1.25.8). Replaces #4, closed during the upstream history rewrite; Anselme's original review remains there. Hardware and cross-platform acceptance remain separate from these Linux checks.

Submitted under the current CONTRIBUTING.md terms: AGPL-3.0 with permission for the maintainer to distribute these contributions under a commercial license. Maintainer edits are enabled.

author: vapi-eisen
body:
> **Stacked on #356.** This branch includes #356's commits; review only the last two and merge after #356.

# perf(media): media executor v2 — lane timing wheel and one clock read per lane pass

Branch `perf/media-lane-timing-wheel`. **Stacked: based on #356
(`perf/media-lane-tick`, at 315a6ee8); merge after it.** Targets 0.5.0. Two
commits on top of #356.

`MediaExecutorConfig::v1()` (the default) is unchanged. Both switches are part
of `MediaExecutorConfig::v2()`, as the production profile runs them.

## Summary

| # | Commit | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `perf(rtp-core): keep lane-clock deadlines in a timing wheel and read the clock once per lane pass` | `MediaExecutorConfig::lane_timer_wheel` / `lane_pass_clock`; lane-clock timing wheel; per-pass clock reading served through `media_clock::now`/`now_std`; `LaneWheelCounters` |
| 2 | `test(sip): check the pass clock serves a v2 call's lane passes` | the real v2 loopback call also checks the pass clock served its lane passes |

## Motivation

After the lane tick (#356) a lane pass serves many sockets and deadlines at
once, and two per-item costs remain on it: every lane-clock deadline filed,
moved or cancelled is a binary-heap push (with lazy deletion and periodic
compaction), and every hosted future, owner timer and receive loop reads the
clock itself (`clock_gettime` per packet and per deadline check). The timing
wheel makes deadline bookkeeping O(1) without allocation; the pass clock
reads the clock once for everything one pass polls.

## Design

### Config additions (rtp-core `executor`, own delimited block)

```rust
pub struct MediaExecutorConfig {
    // … #351 / #353 / #356 fields …
    // ---- Lane timing wheel and pass clock ----
    pub lane_timer_wheel: bool,
    pub lane_pass_clock: bool,
    // ---- End lane timing wheel and pass clock ----
}
// v1(): false, false        v2(): true, true
// with_lane_timer_wheel(bool), with_lane_pass_clock(bool)
// lane_timer_wheel_active() = lane_timer_active() && lane_timer_wheel   (needs the lane clock)
// lane_pass_clock_active()  = lane_poller_active() && lane_pass_clock   (needs the lane poller)
// executor::lane_timer_wheel_enabled(), executor::lane_pass_clock_enabled()
// executor::lane_wheel_counters() -> LaneWheelCounters (#[non_exhaustive])
```

- Prerequisites follow #351/#356's rule: a missing prerequisite reads as off
  and is not an error. This is required, not just consistent: `v2()` presets
  both, so `v2().with_lane_timer(false)` and `v2().with_lane_poller(false)`
  must stay valid. (The vendored build refused these at boot from env vars.)
- `validate()` has nothing new to reject.
- The porting manifest sketched `pass_clock: Option<bool>` ("`None` follows
  the wheel"); that default only existed for env-var convenience, so these
  are two plain bools with `v2()` setting both. Each part alone is
  `v2().with_lane_pass_clock(false)` / `v2().with_lane_timer_wheel(false)`.
- The pass clock needs only the lane poller (it is a property of a poller
  pass); the vendored build also tied it to the lane clock. Under `v2()`
  both are on, so the measured profile is unchanged.

### Timing wheel (`lane_clock`)

A single-level wheel of 256 buckets: one tick quantum each when the poller
files on the tick grid (#356 grid timers; the wheel's origin is the grid's,
so each bucket is one tick), else 1 ms (the runtime timer's resolution).
Entries are linked into their bucket through intrusive doubly-linked lists
threaded through the existing entry slab (`bucket`/`prev`/`next` fields), so
filing, cancelling and re-arming are O(1) and never allocate; an occupancy
bitmap finds the next non-empty bucket by words. Deadlines beyond the span
wait in an overflow heap (lazy deletion and compaction, as the heap clock
did) and cascade into their bucket as the cursor reaches them; 20 ms media
deadlines never go there. Each bucket keeps a lower bound of its keys, so a
pass with nothing due touches no entry; due buckets drain whole and the
current bucket is scanned only when its bound is due.

Semantics are the heap's exactly: an entry is taken iff its filed key is at
or before `now`, entries taken together wake in (key, slot) order (the heap's
pop order), and the driver's rounds, self-wakes and runtime-timer rules are
unchanged — the driver only asks the clock for its earliest key and the due
entries. Existing lane-timer counters keep their meaning.

### Pass clock (`lane_clock`, `lane_poller`, `media_clock`)

A poller pass takes one clock reading at its start (the tick's start reading
when ticking) and serves it to everything it polls: `LaneSleep::poll`, the
socket owner's inline receive path and owner timer (`udp.rs`), the lane
clock's first timer round, and any caller of `media_clock::now()` /
`now_std()`. A reading is always an earlier reading of the same monotonic
clock, so a "has this deadline passed?" check can only say "not yet" a little
longer, never "yes" too early. Staleness is bounded in work: one reading
serves at most 32 reads and 16 hosted polls, and each later timer round and
the tick's due check (whose reading also ends the pass for the tick
scheduler) read afresh. Outside a pass, or with the switch off, both
functions read the clock as before.

**Public seam:** `rvoip_rtp_core::media_clock::now()` / `now_std()` are the
public entry points (application pacing code on a lane — e.g. a recording
sender — gets the pass reading by calling them).

### Counters

`executor::lane_wheel_counters()` → `LaneWheelCounters`: wheel inserts / far
inserts / cancels / cascades / slot scans, pass-clock cached and fresh reads,
and the age readings reached when replaced (samples, sum, max). Process
atomics published in batches of 64 passes, no `metrics` crate.

## What was cut from the vendored source

Ported from the snapshot 9c77dab6 (E52), hand-ported onto #356:

- `VAPI_MEDIA_EXECUTOR_LANE_TIMER_WHEEL` / `_LANE_PASS_CLOCK` env parsing,
  `LaneWheelConfig`, `validate_lane_wheel_env` and the boot refusal → the
  typed fields above (prerequisites read as off).
- `vapi_central_media_executor_lane_timer_wheel_ops_total` /
  `_lane_pass_clock_*` metrics → the counters snapshot.
- `research_clock::now`/`now_std` → `media_clock::now`/`now_std` (#351's
  rename).
- 72e0ffc5 (a later E54 test fix adding prefetch hints to `arm`) does not
  apply: `arm` has no prefetch argument here.

## Measured context

Production v2 runs both switches (`LANE_TIMER_WHEEL=1`, `LANE_PASS_CLOCK=1`)
on top of the 2 ms lane tick: **−4.6% CPU per call** on Xeon 6 SMT.
Load/perf qualification runs on Xeon 6 SMT in the next rvoip release qualification.

## Evidence (build host: Xeon 6, 32 vCPU, Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.91.0)

On the branch at 0edfef66 (base #356 at 315a6ee8):

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p rvoip-rtp-core -p rvoip-media-core -p rvoip-sip -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p rvoip-rtp-core -p rvoip-media-core -p rvoip-sip`: clean.
- Commit 1 builds on its own (`cargo check --locked -p rvoip-rtp-core -p rvoip-sip --all-targets`).
- `cargo test --locked -p rvoip-rtp-core`: all pass (lib 581, was 565; every integration binary; doctests).
- `cargo test --locked -p rvoip-media-core`: all pass (lib 394 plus every integration binary; doctests 3 passed, 1 ignored, as before).
- `cargo test --locked -p rvoip-sip --lib`: 876 passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p rvoip-sip` with the 16 media integration binaries
  (`adapter_eager_streams`, `amr_call_integration`, `audio_roundtrip_integration`,
  `bridge_roundtrip_integration`, `config_channel_capacity_integration`,
  `dtls_srtp_call_integration`, `early_media_tests`,
  `endpoint_audio_roundtrip_integration`, `media_executor_config_integration`,
  `media_quality_integration`, `media_runtime_config_integration`,
  `media_runtime_dedicated_integration`, `provisional_media_security`,
  `reliable_provisional_bridge`, `srtp_call_integrat

author: in-c0
body:
Implements the SHOWHAUS side of CVF's founder revenue operations loop (in-c0/combinatory-venture-farming `spec/DECISION-2026-11-08-founder-revenue-operations.md` §3–§5) for the 48h sprint.

**What ships**
- `POST /api/e` — first-party beacons. Allowed from pages: `view, search, place_card, pro_interest, signin_open, cta`. Account and money events are server-only, so a page cannot forge them. Environment is `production` only on showhaus.app; previews/workers.dev are `test`; probes (`cvf-e2e` UA, `x-cvf-synthetic: 1`, `?synthetic=1`) are `synthetic`. Stored: pseudonymous actor, path without query, referrer host, utm. No email, IP or query string.
- `POST /api/auth/start|verify|logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` — non-guest email sign-up / log-in with a 6-digit code (10 min, 5 tries, 5 sends/address/hour, 300/day). Code mail goes through the Cloudflare Email Service binding `MAIL` from `login@showhaus.app`. Accounts are keyed by an HMAC of the address; the address itself is never written. Emits `signup` (first time) / `login` / `logout`.
- `POST /hooks/stripe` — Stripe webhook verified against `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (5 min tolerance, constant-time compare, dedupe by event id). **Returns 503 `webhook secret not set` until the secret exists.** Records `payment_succeeded / payment_pending / payment_failed / checkout_abandoned / refund / dispute` with amount, currency, mode, payment-link id and a pseudonymous customer only.
- `checkout_started` is recorded server-side whenever any route redirects to `buy.stripe.com` / `checkout.stripe.com` (covers `/pay/*` without touching those routes).
- `GET /api/ops/summary`, `POST /api/ops/replay` — CVF's read side and webhook replay. Authenticated with a **GitHub Actions OIDC token** (audience `showhaus-ops`, repo `in-c0/combinatory-venture-farming`), so no shared secret is needed. `GET /api/ops/health` is public booleans only.
- Store: D1 `showhaus-ops` (binding `OPS_DB`), declared without an id so the deploy provisions it by name.
- UI: header **Sign in** button + small dialog (email → code → signed in); Pro lens gets "Count me in — sign in". Beacons on search, place card and Pro clicks. GPC / DNT → events without any id.

**Checks**
- `scripts/showhaus-ops.test.mjs` (12 tests) runs the real handlers against an in-memory D1 shim: no raw email stored, forged payment events refused, cross-origin POST refused, rate limit, mail failure path, webhook 503 → signed → dedupe, OIDC audience/repo/expiry/signature.
- Local `wrangler dev` (4.158): sign-up → me → logout, signed webhook (test secret) recorded once, wrong signature 400.
- `showhaus-judge.mjs`: 108/108 locally.

author: raantss18
body:
Suite de #58 (à fusionner après elle : cette branche la contient). Branche le petit modèle par signe (ADR 0038) selon le contrat v1 (`entrainement/CONTRAT.md`, ADR 0040) ; réglages et mesures dans l'ADR 0041.

## Ce que ça change
- `rendu_signe.dart` : image 32×32 et 5 mesures du contrat, en Dart pur, avec les mêmes disques et segments que Pillow (`rendu.py`). Case de la ligne selon la règle du contrat.
- `ClasseurOnnx` : charge `assets/modeles/{signes.onnx, signes_classes.txt, signes.json}` s'ils y sont (contrat v1 vérifié), en fond au démarrage ; sinon `null` et l'app lit comme avant.
- `ClasseurAppris` : les gabarits d'abord ; le modèle répond quand ils doutent, à p ≥ 0,7 et 0,3 d'écart, et seulement pour les classes que la lecture au tracé sait écrire. Le modèle fournit aussi les 3 lectures de « toucher un signe ».
- Les poids restent **hors Git** (`.gitignore`) : choisir la version adoptée revient à Antsa (ADR 0040). `assets/modeles/LISEZMOI.md` explique comment en embarquer une.
- Banc : justesse et temps par signe, règle de doute sur les séances jamais vues, lignes entières avec et sans modèle.

## Vérifié
- `flutter analyze` propre ; tests verts (660 au total sur la branche).
- Rendu Dart contre `rendu.py` sur 138 signes réels : écart moyen 0,0001 par pixel, pire 0,5 % de l'encre ; cases et mesures identiques (`rendu_signe_test`).
- Pad 7, modèle v1 (sha256 a0e7a6bc…) : 3,6 ms par signe en médiane ; 36/45 justes sur les séances jamais vues (les 80 % mesurés sur PC). Là où les gabarits doutent : seuil 0,7, 18 pris sur 33, tous justes ; à 0,5, une erreur.
- Lignes entières des fixtures : le modèle n'en change aucune (mêmes 6 lues au tracé, les autres échouent pour des raisons de structure). APK arm64 : 71,6 → 73,3 Mo avec le modèle.

## Supposé / reste à tester
- Seuil réglé sur 33 signes seulement : à revoir avec l'écriture collectée.
- Sur signes isolés, le modèle (36/45) fait mieux que les gabarits sûrs (26 justes, 13 faux) : le laisser passer devant les gabarits est une décision à prendre avec plus de données.
- Pas essayé sur le téléphone.

body:
## Summary

usque carries AuroraVPN's WARP/MASQUE traffic but had **no security scanning**. This adds the same pipeline as firestack, and fixes vulnerable dependencies.

**`.github/workflows/security.yml`** runs on every PR, on pushes to `main`, and weekly:

| Job | Blocks merge? |
|---|---|
| Tests with the race detector | yes |
| **govulncheck**, fails on reachable known vulnerabilities, plus SARIF upload | yes |
| gosec (SAST), SARIF to the Security tab | report |
| CodeQL for Go (`security-extended`) | via code-scanning alerts |
| gitleaks over the full git history | yes |

All actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Tool versions are pinned and were at least two weeks old when chosen.

**Dependencies:** `golang.org/x/net` v0.56.0 → **v0.61.0** and `golang.org/x/text` v0.38.0 → v0.43.0. These are the same fixes as paulvers-ui2/firestack#3 (GO-2026-6617/6612/6611/6610/6603 in x/net http2, GO-2026-5970 in x/text). They're applied by a one-time workflow that runs `go get`, `go mod tidy`, `go mod verify`, build and vet, commits `go.mod`/`go.sum`, and deletes itself in that same commit.

**`SECURITY.md`:** private vulnerability reporting, linked to the app's security program.

Private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot alerts are now **enabled** in this repo's settings.

⚠️ Merge only when green, especially govulncheck. If it still fails after the bump, it has found another reachable vulnerability (for example in quic-go), and that needs fixing before merge.

## Changes

- Add an opt-in `CoreAIEmbeddingProvider` for iOS and macOS 27+. It accepts a local MiniLM-compatible model and a host tokenizer, with explicit model and tokenizer revisions, vector-space identity, and network declaration.
- Validate input tensors and output vectors, map failures to typed errors, and check cancellation around tokenization and inference. The package retains its 26.4 deployment floor and adds no third-party runtime dependencies.
- Exercise the public adapter in the existing iPhone probe and document setup and persistent index compatibility.

## Verification

- Warning-free package build, all 724 Swift package tests, network-disabled suite, 23 demo tests, seven probe tests, strict formatting, layering, and DocC checks passed.
- Core and Runtime line coverage was 98.87% (2,897 of 2,930 lines).
- The signed probe passed all 44 comparisons on the physical iPhone running iOS 27.2. The fresh report had an independently recomputed maximum absolute difference of `1.7851e-7` against pinned PyTorch output, below the `1e-4` tolerance. The iOS binary weak-links Core AI and declares a 26.4 minimum.

The parity fixture uses precomputed tokens. App-supplied tokenizers need their own verification, and the PDF demo continues to use its existing provider.

A new macOS installation can show Backend disconnected without exposing the login item. Keep the status task mounted, and allow registration when Service Management has no record for a valid packaged agent.

After registration, launchd can pass a bundle-relative argv[0]. Resolve the resident's executable path from dyld so the bundled Python starts regardless of the working directory. The macOS package self-check reproduces that launch invocation.

Kimi K3.1 Pro approved the revision. The 23 Swift tests, macOS package smoke check, and Linux/macOS CI passed. On an installed app, the registration controls appeared while disconnected and the packaged worker connected to the UI when started directly.

author: fatheus97
body:
Slice 5d of the households work, the last backend piece: redeeming an invite, and the joiner's kitchen moving into the household. Behind `HOUSEHOLDS_ENABLED`, which is off in prod, so nothing changes for anyone yet. Design and reasons: `docs/household-design.md`, "Join and leave".

## Redeem, in order

1. Flag, then a verified, non-demo, entitled caller.
2. A plain read of where the code leads. An unknown code and the caller's own household are both a 404.
3. Both households' kitchen locks, lowest id first, then the caller's membership is re-read.
4. Both households' user rows, by id. Account deletes take no kitchen lock and lock the user row first.
5. The caller must be alone, checked only now: someone they invited could have joined them during the wait.
6. The email-bound `DELETE ... RETURNING`. Someone else's code and an expired one are the same 404 as an unknown one.
7. The cap, then every member active and entitled, the joiner re-read too. Then consent of everyone holding health data on either side, and the size of the merged fridge and staples. None of these names anyone, and a refusal rolls back the delete, so the invite stays usable.

Then the joiner's drafts go and their plans move (meals and health rows follow). The fridge rows move, staples merge through `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`, the user row moves, both versions bump, and the old household is deleted with its leftover staples and invites. No trigger fires on an update of a user's household, so all of this is explicit, in an order that keeps the foreign keys happy.

## Also in here

- **`merge_into_fridge_buckets` kept only the last of two existing rows that share a name and expiry,** then rewrote the whole fridge from that. A join creates that state routinely (rice from each side), so a merge, finish or unconfirm silently lost the other batch. It now sums them. The case was reachable before too, through a PUT.
- **`shelf_version`** answers 409 `household_changed` instead of a 500 when a join deleted the household after the request read its user.
- **The last-admin scan** is ordered by id, so it cannot deadlock with the id-ordered member locks.
- **The list caps moved** to the services (`MAX_FRIDGE_ITEMS`, `MAX_STAPLES`), since the join checks them too.

## Tested

2619 backend tests, ruff, and mypy strict on the backend. No frontend or migration change.

- Every behaviour above has a negative control: break it and a test goes red. About 55, rerun as the code changed.
- Races run on real connections through the real route where the route is the side that waits:
  - a second redeem by the same person;
  - two redeems at the cap;
  - two people inviting each other;
  - a joiner deactivated during the wait;
  - a delete of a member, of the minter, of the joiner, and of a member during a held redeem.
- A refusal leaving the invite usable is shown on real connections too. The shared-session harness cannot show a rollback.

## Reviewed before pushing, and what I left

A multi-agent pass with an adversarial verifier ran before the push. Its confirmed findings are fixed here, apart from these:

- **Someone already sharing a household hears "you already share" before the code and address are proved,** so they can tell that a code exists. That is all it reveals, about a 256-bit code they already hold. Moving the check after the delete would turn two people inviting each other into a 404 for the second. The route docstring and the tests now claim "answer alike" only for a caller who is alone.
- **The consent check counts rows on a plan that reads as lost.** That is a wrong refusal in a rare state, which re-consenting clears, and not a leak. 5e removes the state, and its test list gets this case.

author: crescendo2344
body:
This PR has three parts: the session fix it was opened for, the fixes from the second group self-check, and a migration that makes earlier imports undoable.

## 1. Return to login when the session ends in another tab
Publishing an announcement failed with **"Authentication credentials were not provided"** after the login was removed in another tab of the same browser.
- Dashboards now notice when the shared login changes in another tab (the browser's `storage` event) and go to the login page with a clear message.
- A refused request with no saved login does the same.
- Only tabs showing a dashboard redirect.

## 2. Fixes from the second self-check

### Import Price History
- **Flexible column names.** A file with `date, species, price_per_kg_php, market` used to be read as "one column per fish", with "species" and "price_per_kg_php" taken as fish names, so 0 prices were imported. Column names are now matched loosely (underscores, `(₱)`, `php` and similar are ignored), and a column named like a price, species, market or note is never read as a fish.
- **Undo import.** Each import is saved as a batch (new `PriceImportBatch` model and `PriceRecord.import_batch`, migration `0025`). The batch ID is shared across chunks. A new **Recent Imports** table lists past imports with **↶ Undo import**, which removes every price from that file.
  - LGU Officers see their own imports; Administrators see all.
  - The undo is written to the activity log.
  - New endpoints: `GET /api/prices/import-batches/` and `POST /api/prices/import-batches/<id>/undo/`.
- **Choose what happens after importing:** **Published right away** (past official records) or **Sent to Review & Publish** (new or unchecked data, saved as pending).
- **Earlier imports are undoable too (migration `0026`).** Prices from imports made before batches existed are grouped into batches (same person, same source, saved in the same minute). They show in Recent Imports as "Earlier import (file name not recorded)" and can be undone. Locally, two earlier imports (137 + 1,990 prices) became one batch of 2,127 prices.

### Announcements
- Vendor and LGU dashboards check for new announcements every minute, and when the tab is opened again.
- Unseen announcements **pop up** with **Got it**. After that they show only in **Notifications**, which LGU Officers now have too.
- The permanent dashboard banner is removed.

### Dashboards and layout
- **LGU dashboard:**
  - "Average Price Today" averaged every fish together and only counted prices dated today. It's replaced by **Latest Prices** (the newest price date and how many fish were priced that day).
  - "Records This Week" counted from Sunday. It's replaced by **Records in the Last 7 Days**, counted by each price's date, imports included.
  - Suggestions also count the last 7 days.
- **Data Monitoring:** a **Fish** column with the fish photo on every row.
- **Top bar:** shows the panel name and today's date instead of repeating each page's title.
- **One icon style:**
  - Sidebar icons are white silhouettes, and emojis drawn on boxes are replaced with simple symbols.
  - Card icons are navy on one light background.
  - Forecast icons use "∿", because "◔" is missing from common fonts.
- **Registration:** the chosen fish appear as photo cards below the dropdown, each with a remove button.

## Testing
- New backend tests:
  - one import sent in two chunks becomes one batch
  - only LGU and Admin can undo, and a second undo is refused
  - "send to review" saves the prices as pending
- The full backend suite passes (121 tests). The import tests also pass with migration `0026` applied on a fresh database.
- Browser checks:
  - a file shaped like the group's (`date,species,price_per_kg_php,market`) finds 5 prices, imports them, appears in Recent Imports, and Undo removes all 5
  - an Admin announcement pops up for the vendor (390px phone) and closes with Got it
  - the LGU dashboard cards, Data Monitoring, all three sidebars, and the registration fish cards
  - the two-tab session test
- `npm run build` passes.

## After merging, on PythonAnywhere
`git pull`, then `python manage.py migrate` (adds the import batches and groups earlier imports), then Reload.

author: shenxingy
body:
## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that changes existing behavior)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Description

Closes the follow-up recorded as: **"Follow-up: a sync store created from scratch would commit the private correction log"**, which TODO.md states as the constraint *"`sync-setup.sh` writes no `.gitignore` for `corrections/history.jsonl`, so a fresh sync store pushes this log to its remote."*

#205 made `sync-setup.sh` write a `.gitignore` into a new store, but only `*.corrupt.*` and `skills/.trash/`. Stores cloned from an existing remote inherit a hand-made `.gitignore` and were fine; a store created from scratch (every new Clade user) got no line for `corrections/history.jsonl`, the raw correction event log, so `sync-push.sh` would commit and push it.

What changed:

- **One definition of the ignore set.** New `configs/scripts/sync-store-heal.sh` holds six commented groups, the live store's eight patterns: `corrections/history.jsonl`; `*.bak-*` and `.backups/`; `skills/synced/`; `__pycache__/` and `*.py[cod]`; `*.corrupt.*`; `skills/.trash/`. `sync-setup.sh` and `sync-push.sh` both source it from `dirname "$0"`, so it works from a checkout and from `~/.claude/scripts` (install.sh copies `configs/scripts/*.sh` there). The duplicated two-pattern list and the test pinning the two copies identical are gone.
- **The healer stays append-only, whole-line and idempotent.** It never reorders or rewrites existing lines or comments, repairs an unterminated last line before appending, and writes a group's comment only when that group is incomplete (an earlier draft added 4 orphan comments to the live `.gitignore`).
- **sync-push never fails on the helper.** A missing or broken helper is skipped (best-effort under `set -e`); the healer runs before the conflict-marker scan as #205 made it.
- **An already-tracked `history.jsonl` is never untracked automatically.** Push writes one line per day to `~/.claude/.sync-conflicts.log` naming the file and the command that would untrack it (`git -C "$SYNC_DIR" rm --cached corrections/history.jsonl`). It is written after the refusal gate, so it cannot break sync-health's REFUSED streak.
- **sync-setup stops with a named error** if the helper cannot be loaded or the heal fails, before its initial commit (it used to exit silently there).
- Tests: `tests/test-sync-store.sh` (97 assertions) and the fixture in `tests/test-memory-sync-breaker.sh`; doc counts in `docs/facts.json`, `docs/how-it-works.md`, `mcp-package/README.md`; `VERIFY.md`.

Overlap: PR #209 (open, owner review) rewrites the same healer block in `sync-push.sh` to also heal `.gitattributes` lines. It can drop its own `sync_push_append_missing` and feed its `.gitattributes` line to `sync_store_append_missing_lines` from the shared helper. `sync-push.sh`, `test-sync-store.sh` and the breaker fixture will conflict as text; whichever PR merges second resolves them.

Implemented by Kimi K3.1 Pro (kimi-code/k3.1-pro, thinking effort max), supervised and independently verified by Claude.

## Related issue

Follow-up to #205. Overlaps #209 (see above).

## Testing

- [ ] `python3 configs/scripts/ci-local.py` passed locally — ci-local.py not run in full: aries load ~140 on 32 cores; the targeted suites and drift gates above ran locally; the hosted run on this PR is the full gate.
- [x] Anything it reported as **skipped** or **unproven** is listed below — not applicable, it was not run (see above)
- [x] Any step it reported **flaky** is listed below — not applicable, it was not run
- [ ] Hooks fire correctly (verified in a Claude Code session) — no hook changed

Tests run (verifier, verbatim):
- bash -n on 5 changed .sh -> ok
- bash configs/scripts/checks.sh shellcheck <5 files> -> rc 0
- git diff --check -> rc 0
- bash tests/test-sync-store.sh (final) -> 97/97 passed
