- python3 configs/scripts/check-ci-checklist.py (final) -> all 70 gates covered
- python3 configs/scripts/doc-align.py verify (final) -> no drift
- python3 configs/scripts/check-references.py (final) -> pass
- python3 configs/scripts/check-runnable-paths.py (final) -> 456 paths ok
- python3 configs/scripts/check-sibling-facts.py -> no surviving changed fact

Red proof (verifier, verbatim):

```
Each source file was put back to HEAD in place, the suite run, and the copy restored. The diff sha1 was identical after every restore (778df4e…).
Final 97-assertion suite:
- all three at HEAD: 62/35
- HEAD sync-push.sh: 85/12
- HEAD sync-setup.sh: 81/16
- helper moved away: 64/33
Round-0 Kimi files under the round-1 suite (87 assertions):
- helper: 78/9, on the orphan-comment tests
- push: 76/11, on missing helper and REFUSED streak
- setup: 85/2, on the error-message tests
Round-1 files are identical to the final ones (control): 97/97.
```

Mutations (verifier, verbatim; each turned the suite red):
- whole-line match -qxF->-qF -> red

author: svilgelm
body:
MCP clients refuse the OAuth token exchange over plain HTTP to non-localhost hosts (Claude Code: `OAuth token requests MUST use TLS (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 are exempt)`), and Scrypted's self-signed cert on 10443 fails verification, so typical LAN installs couldn't connect at all.

Admins can now create static API tokens in Settings → API Tokens. Clients send them as `Authorization: Bearer smcp_...`, never get a 401, and so never start OAuth. Only the SHA-256 is stored; the plaintext is shown exactly once, alongside a ready-to-paste `claude mcp add` command, and a lost token is simply regenerated. Tokens are revoked by removing them from the multi-select, and "Revoke all tokens" covers them too. README and CLAUDE.md document the HTTP path. Bumps the version to 1.2.0.

Tested against a live Scrypted server over http://<lan-ip>:11080 with Claude Code: token creation, one-time display, connecting, and revocation (revoked token gets 401).

body:
The home now has photographed oak and woven materials, modern licensed cloth seating, detailed wooden toys, coherent kitchen joinery, improved fixed lighting, garden window context and clothed Leo meshes fitted to the existing rig. Actual matched camera renders show the resulting scene and the corrected sofa/denim mapping in [the gallery](https://github.com/ely2ba/pyr-cion-b7da2a69-submission-repo/blob/0219ba4/docs/home-design/README.md).

The new [ephemeral GPU browser launcher](https://github.com/ely2ba/pyr-cion-b7da2a69-submission-repo/blob/0219ba4/experiments/MUJOCO_LIVE.md) runs the full existing MuJoCo/Brain on one L40S, with native Filament RGB, same-world EGL depth/segmentation, BB-main/room-inset view, existing manual controls and optional asynchronous Gemma parent text. Reset replaces the renderer-owner process so terminated EGL state is not reused; the IPC socket, monotonic frame sequence and fixed session deadline survive. No persistent deployment or model launch is required.

Validation:
- 156 tests pass with main PR31/32 integrated.
- Matched actual renders preserve baseline camera/physical state within1e-10;86 contact geometries,6cameras, robot inertias, joints and timestep remain exact. Nine Leo RGB-D compatibility cases preserve detection/occlusion and mocap transforms.
- Actual single-L40S startup verified native Vulkan and NVIDIA EGL,15tangent meshes/no missing cache; live reset recovered frames. Actual browser Check-Leo reached the owner; configured Gemma requests reached ready without blocking controls.
- The retained600-frame live tail published a median5.639fps, RGB-D/Brain sense median65.537ms/p9570.413ms. These are publisher timings, not browser paint FPS or a matched resolution benchmark.

Limits: garden views are static photographic planes with plane depth; Leo retains rigid articulation seams. Camera detection uses simulator segmentation/depth, not independent model recognition. The measured stream needs further smoothness work; manual stair failure/alarm behavior remains possible. Explicit asset licenses, hashes and scales are included. Audio is muted; browser microphone integration is separate ongoing work.

Nie ma pliku `src/i18n/pt.ts`, portugalski zostaje w `PLANNED_LANGUAGE_ENTRIES`, a teksty prawne są nietknięte (D-96/D-136: agent tłumaczy, native speaker poprawia).
  - **Kod języka**: repo już nazywa brazylijski portugalski `pt` (locale i `storeLocale` pt-BR, D-212; urządzenie pt-PT też go dostaje). Dlatego plik to `pt.json`, nie `pt-br.json`. Nazwę z locale sklepu mają tylko pliki sklepu (`docs/store/pt-br.md`, uwagi `docs/store/review/pt-br.md`).
  - **Forma zwracania się**: brazylijskie „você” z trybem rozkazującym jak w opisie sklepu („Construa”, „Conecte”). Pisownia i słownictwo są brazylijskie („tela”, „mouse”, „aparelho”, „salvar”, „excluir”, „compartilhar”), nazwy miast pochodzą z `src/data/city-names.json` („Madri”, „Acra”), a cudzysłowy to “ ”.
  - `gameover.region.*` mają rodzajnik („a América do Norte”, „o Oriente Médio”), bo każde zdanie, które ich używa, brzmi „para {region}”. `region.name.*` zostają bez rodzajnika.
- **Słownik `docs/i18n/README.md`**: kolumna portugalska, zasady rejestru i 8 otwartych terminów dla korektora brazylijskiego.
- **Strażnik `test:i18n-drafts`**: to ten sam mechanizm (D-306/D-308), bez drugiego. Obejmuje teraz 4 pliki. Test liczby form liczby mnogiej (2–3) działa też dla `pt`. Nowy test przypina kod `pt` i locale pt-BR, więc plik `pt-br.json` zostałby odrzucony jako nieznany język. Ten test pilnuje konwencji i na starym kodzie też przechodzi. Reguły nadal siedzą w `validateImport`.
- **`docs/store/review/pt-br.md`**: uwagi do każdego pola `docs/store/pt-br.md`, a sam plik sklepu się nie zmienia. Uwagi obejmują liczniki, słownictwo sklepu porównane ze szkicem gry, nieaktualny akapit „mundo em diorama”, teksty alternatywne o częściach Róży oraz rodzaj nazwy („da Airway” w sklepie, „do Airway” w grze). Ostatecznego tekstu sklepu nie piszę, bo powstanie w U7 z nowego EN (D-296).

### Dostosowanie przestarzałych punktów zlecenia
- Zlecenie opisuje Różę jako skórkę w grze. Wydaną skórką jest Linoryt (D-301), więc teksty alternatywne o Róży (róże wiatrów, tarcza 24 h, menu na łuku) oznaczyłem do przepisania w U7.
- Zlecenie podaje numery D-282 i Q-90. Aktualny jest D-309, a nowych pytań do `OWNER-QUESTIONS.md` nie dodałem.
- Zlecenie zakładało, że `test:i18n-drafts` może jeszcze nie istnieć. Istnieje (D-306), więc go rozszerzyłem zamiast tylko uruchamiać `--check`.
- Gałąź to `night/53a-wave1-ptbr`, nie `gpt/15-pt-br-draft`, zgodnie z poleceniem koordynatora.

### Wymuszone skróty (budżety długości)
`hud.passengers` „Viajantes” (10; „Passageiros” ma 11), `menu.onTime` „Pontual” (8; „No horário” ma 10), `settings.saver` „Modo economia” (14; „Economia de bateria” ma 19), `note.jam` „Congestionado: rede fecha em {seconds} s” (34; z „Congestionamento, a rede…” wychodzi 36), `dock.widebody` „Fus. larga” (10), `dock.speed` „Vel. {speed}×” (10), `menu.logbook` „Diário” (10; „Diário de bordo” w tytule ekranu), `region.short.*` „Am. Norte”, „Am. Sul”, „Eur. Norte”, „Eur. Sul”, „Or. Médio” (10), `logbook.col.weeks` „Sem.” (4).

UI się nie zmienia, więc w PR nie ma zrzutów ekranu. Testy nie zostawiły żadnych wygenerowanych plików do zatwierdzenia.

author: brunux
body:
## Summary
Complete rofi and legacy shell helper retirement as specified in Spec 014 (full framework closure).

All 45+ interactive surfaces and launchers are now native subcommands in `lazyos` (Ratatui in floating foot) or multi-call symlinks in `~/.config/bin/`.

### Changes
- **Rofi removal:** Purged `rofi` from `packages.list`, eliminating X11/Pango legacy dependencies and reducing image footprint.
- **Helper retirement:** Deleted `lib-rofi.sh`, `bar-pick`, and `~/.config/rofi/` (`config.rasi`, `solarized.rasi`).
- **Theme engine update:** Removed `rofi` surface from `lazyos-theme` (templates and golden fixtures), reducing active theme surfaces to 13.
- **Passphrase inputs:** Migrated sensitive password/passphrase prompts in `lazyos menu dev` to native masked inputs via `Question::input`, passing `--passphrase-file` to GPG in `lazyos-profile`.
- **Witnesses:**
  - Added Spec 014 retirement witness in `scripts/check-system.sh` confirming `lib-rofi.sh` is absent.
  - Verified `lazyos --icon-names` resolves 100% against the LazyOS theme.
  - Tested disk menu `/usr/sbin` tool resolution under stripped PATH.
  - Updated documentation in `02-rofi.md`, `06-troubleshooting.md`, `07-agents.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

### Verification
- Pinned compilation on Cortex-A76 power cores (`taskset -c 4-7 -j 4`).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` passed (all 200+ unit and integration tests).
- `check-system.sh` passed all framework, theme, and package checks.

author: rhseung
body: Part of #147 (썸네일 진도) ## 바뀐 것 - **지금 보는 쪽 (2026-11-08 사용자).** 검정 2pt 테두리를 걷고, 미리보기 앱처럼 썸네일과 쪽 번호 뒤에 옅은 둥근 바탕을 깐다. 번호는 `text` semibold로 진하게 쓴다. - 색은 기존 토큰 `Palette.fill`이다(사람 목록, ⌘K 팔레트에서 고른 행의 바탕). 라이트와 다크 값이 이미 있어서 새 토큰은 만들지 않았다. - 바탕은 썸네일과 번호에서 8pt(`Space.s`) 나가고, 모서리는 썸네일 모서리에 그 거리를 더한 12pt(`Radius.small + Space.s`)라 썸네일 모서리와 나란하다. - 옆으로는 열의 여백까지 나가서 썸네일 폭이 줄지 않는다. 위아래 8pt는 썸네일 안쪽 여백이 되어 썸네일 사이가 4pt 넓어졌다. - **고르기와 겹칠 때.** 바탕은 과목 `tint`가 아닌 회색이라, 지금 쪽이 고른 범위 안에 있으면 회색 바탕, 과목 색 테두리, 과목 `ink` 번호가 함께 보인다. 이전에는 고른 테두리가 지금 쪽 테두리를 덮어서 어느 쪽이 지금 쪽인지 보이지 않았다. 저장 칸(`tint` 바탕)과도 섞이지 않는다. - 구획 선과는 2pt 떨어진다. 선이 끝나는 곳과 썸네일이 시작하는 곳 사이의 간격이 원래 10pt라서 열 폭(128, 렉처 208)은 그대로 두었다. - 모든 PDF 쪽 열에 쓴다. 바꾼 곳이 공용 `PageThumbnail`이라 렉처 파일, 다른 PDF, 렉처 나누기 화면의 썸네일 열이 함께 바뀐다. - 디버그 스냅숏(`FOLIO_SNAPSHOT_STRIP`): 창 높이를 화면의 보이는 높이 안으로 줄이고, 범위를 고른 뒤 저장 칸이 자리를 잡은 다음에 그 쪽으로 스크롤한다. 전에는 지금 쪽이 열 아래 끝이나 흐림 밑에 걸려 그림에서 잘렸다. 디버그 빌드에만 있는 코드다. - **주 버튼의 채움색 (2026-11-08 사용자).** 과목 안이면 과목 색, 밖이면 시스템 강조색이다. 처음에는 쪽 띠의 "저장" 버튼만 시스템 파랑으로 바꿨는데, 사용자 결정에 따라 이 규칙으로 바꾸고 앱의 모든 주 버튼에 적용했다. - 원인: 과목 화면은 과목 `ink`로 `.tint`가 걸려 있다. `.borderedProminent`가 그 색으로 채워졌는데, 다크의 `ink`는 옅어서(바이올렛 `#C2BFFF`) 흰 글자가 묻혔다. - 새 버튼 스타일 `.prominent`(`interaction.swift`): `.borderedProminent`에 채움색을 직접 준다. 환경의 `\.accent`가 과목이면 과목 `fill`, `.gray`(과목 없음)이면 `Color.accentColor`다. `.pointing(.borderedProminent)` 23곳을 모두 이 스타일로 바꿨다(오늘 화면 빠른 추가의 `.glassProminent`는 과목 밖이라 그대로 둔다). - 새 값 `CourseAccent.fill`(라이트·다크, 프리셋마다): `color`를 같은 색상으로 어둡게 해서 흰 글자와 4.5:1 이상이 되게 했다. 이미 4.5:1을 넘던 라이트 blue, green, graphite는 `color`와 같다. 글자색 `ink`는 그대로다. `ThemeTests.whiteReadsOnEveryFill`이 모든 프리셋과 `gray`의 대비를 검사한다. - 시트: 과목 화면 안에서 연 시트도 `\.accent`(와 `tint`)를 물려받는 것을 디버그 앱으로 확인했다. 그래서 과목 안 시트의 저장도 과목 색이다. - 앞 커밋에서 넣은 `Theme.Palette.prominent` 토큰은 뺐다. - `DESIGN.md`의 "버튼의 무게"에 규칙을 적고, 과목 색 설명에 `fill`을 더했다. - 디버그 스냅숏 `FOLIO_SNAPSHOT_KEY`: 앱을 앞으로 가져오는 대신 창과 폼에 `controlActiveState = .key`를 준다. Mac을 쓰는 중에는 앞으로 가져오기가 거절되었고, 키 창이 아니면 주 버튼이 회색으로 그려진다. - **다크의 지금 쪽 바탕 (2026-11-08 사용자).** 다크에서 `fill`(`#33312E`)이 열 바탕과 거의 같아서 잘 보이지 않았다. 새 토큰 `Theme.Palette.currentPage`를 두었다. 라이트는 `fill` 그대로이고, 다크는 한 단계 밝은 회색 `#4A4743`이다. 회색이라 과목 색 구획 선이나 고른 테두리와 헷갈리지 않는다. - **과목 색은 한 수식어로 (2026-11-08 사용자).** `.courseAccent(_:)`가 `\.accent`와 고스트 버튼이 읽는 `tint`(과목 `ink`)를 함께 넣는다. 과목 밖(`.gray`)이면 `tint`를 시스템 강조색에 둔다. 전에는 두 값을 따로 넣어서, 수업 정리 시트가 `\.accent`만 받으면 주 버튼은 과목 색인데 고스트 버튼("바꾸기", "+ 시험")은 시스템 파랑이었다. `\.accent`를 넣던 모든 곳(과목 화면, 수업 정리, 복습, Claude 패널, 파일 보기, 시험 계획, 자동 완성 메뉴, 폼 스냅숏)을 이 수식어로 바꿨고, `check-design`이 앱 코드의 `environment(\.accent, …)`를 막는다. app-tests의 노트 벤치는 기준 이미지를 그린 그대로 `\.accent`만 넣으므로 검사에서 뺐다. - `DESIGN.md` 파일 보기 절의 "지금 쪽" 설명을 고쳤고, #147 `정한 것`에 이번 결정을 적었다. ## 화면 busyDay 사본에 진도(10/19 1–5, 10/21 6–8, 10/26 9–12, 10/28 13–15, 11/2 16–18쪽)를 CLI로 넣고, 시계를 11/4(수) 10:00에 고정해 디버그 앱 창을 찍었다. 이전 그림도 같은 사본과 같은 스크롤로 찍었다. **평소.** 지금 쪽(16)이 펼친 11/2 구획 안에 있다. 테두리 대신 옅은 바탕이 깔리고, 번호가 진해졌다. | | 이전 | 이후 | | --- | --- | --- | | 라이트 | | | | 다크 | | | **고르는 중.** 19–21쪽을 골랐고 지금 쪽은 21이다. 이전에는 21이 다른 고른 쪽과 똑같아 보였다. 이후에는 회색 바탕이 지금 쪽을, 과목 색 테두리가 고른 쪽을 따로 보인다. | | 이전 | 이후 | | --- | --- | --- | | 라이트 | | | | 다크 | | | **주 버튼.** 디버그 앱을 키 창 상태로 찍었다. 이전(바이올렛). 쪽 띠의 저장 칸이다. 다크에서 옅은 `ink`에 흰 글자라 흐리다. | 라이트 | 다크 | | --- | --- | | | | 이후, 과목 안: 쪽 띠의 저장 칸, 프리셋 세 개. | | 라이트 | 다크 | | --- | --- | --- | | violet | | | | orange | | | | teal | | | 이후, 과목 안의 시트(수업 정리, 바이올렛). 이전에는 고스트 버튼이 시스템 파랑이었고, 이후에는 과목 `ink`이다. | | 이전 | 이후 | | --- | --- | --- | | 라이트 | | | | 다크 | | | 이후, 과목 밖(학기 추가): 시스템 강조색이다. | 라이트 | 다크 | | --- | --- | | | | **다크의 지금 쪽 바탕.** 16쪽이 지금 쪽이다. | | 이전 | 이후 | | --- | --- | --- | | violet | | | | orange | | | | teal | |

author: rijan-adhikari
body:
## What changed
- Correct weighted-average cost basis and realized P&L so buy fees are capitalized and sell fees reduce proceeds.
- Add API integration tests for registration, refresh, BUY/SELL lifecycle, transaction ledger, readiness and client-IP handling.
- Harden authentication with Argon2id via `argon2-cffi`, PyJWT, HS256-only validation, refresh-token persistence/refresh in the frontend, and scoped logout storage cleanup.
- Add order rate limiting and stop trusting raw, unverified `X-Forwarded-For` headers.
- Remove fabricated dashboard balances/index values and load the five simulated quotes from the backend.
- Pin frontend dependencies, patch audited npm packages, upgrade vulnerable Python dependencies, and replace `python-jose`/`ecdsa` with PyJWT.
- Normalize PostgreSQL URLs, require PostgreSQL and a strong JWT secret in production, and make `/ready` return 503 when the DB is unavailable.
- Configure the app for Neon PostgreSQL with a small SQLAlchemy connection pool, pooled Neon connection-string guidance, and Render environment secret injection.
- Replace the expiring Render Free Postgres resource in the Blueprint with an externally provisioned Neon Free database. The Blueprint creates only the free API web service and static frontend.
- Rewrite deployment instructions for Render + Neon, including database creation, pooled TLS URL setup, migrations, free-tier caveats and manual backup guidance.
- Add CI for backend tests, pip-audit, npm audit, frontend build, PostgreSQL migrations and Alembic schema parity.

## Verification
The previous PR workflow passed:
- 11 backend tests passed.
- Backend `pip-audit` passed.
- Frontend `npm audit --audit-level=high` passed and `npm run build` succeeded.
- PostgreSQL 16 migration and `alembic check` passed.

The new Neon compatibility commits have been pushed and require the newly triggered CI run to complete before merge/deployment.

## Remaining product and hosting limitations — intentionally not hidden
- The market feed is still five hardcoded demo quotes with generated candles; there is no licensed/live NEPSE data provider.
- Only immediate market paper orders are supported. Limit/stop orders, exchange-session enforcement, full symbol directory, user-managed watchlists, alerts and notification delivery are not implemented.
- Refresh tokens are not revoked/rotated server-side; browser tokens remain in localStorage.
- Render Free services sleep after inactivity; Neon Free compute can suspend while idle. Cold starts and provider quotas are accepted for this zero-cost setup.
- Free tiers and quotas can change. Neon data must be exported periodically to a copy kept outside the hosting provider; free hosting is not a backup guarantee.
- No live Render/Neon deployment or browser-based end-to-end test has been performed.

This is a reviewable hardening and free-hosting compatibility pass for the existing educational paper-trading MVP, not a claim that the app is a live-market production platform.

author: upd4ting
body:
Fixes #98

## Why

A translator who empties a key's base (English) text in the key panel is asked "Clear the base text of <key>?". The dialog opened under the panel, so its **Clear** button could not be clicked. The base text could only be kept, never cleared, from the panel. After this change the dialog opens above the panel, and its Clear, Cancel and Escape all work.

## Cause

`useConfirm()` opens its dialog through Nuxt UI's global overlay host. The DMS portals that host into `#dms-overlays`, an `isolate` element placed before the page's other overlays. The DMS drawer that holds the key panel teleports to `<body>`, after `#dms-overlays`. Every dialog the host opens therefore paints under an open drawer. Delete in the same panel was not affected, because the drawer closes before its dialog opens.

## Change

- The key panel renders `<DmsConfirmModal>` itself. The dialog inherits the drawer's portal and mounts after it, so it opens above the panel.
- `useKeySaves` exposes the dialog's texts (`clearBaseDialog`) and `useBaseClearQuestion`, which holds the open question. Each question gets its own dialog (`:key`), and a dialog that finishes leaving clears only its own question. A question asked while the previous dialog is still leaving opens a fresh dialog and is answered.
- Matrix cells keep `confirmClearBase` through `useConfirm`, with the same texts. Their dialog has no drawer to sit under.
- The `matrix/key-panel-stays-open-on-a-failed-save` journey now presses Cancel (the base text comes back), then Clear, and reads the cleared base text back from the API.

The cause sits in the DMS, where the drawer escapes the `#dms-overlays` portal. A fix there would cover every module that confirms from inside a drawer. This PR fixes the panel without waiting on a DMS release.

## Proof

### Before (main) and after

| Before: the dialog sits under the panel | After: the dialog opens above it |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AntelopeJS/dms-lang/5413fcc38875300f32980ad4cdebe90b4e3772e4/pr-127/proof/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AntelopeJS/dms-lang/5413fcc38875300f32980ad4cdebe90b4e3772e4/pr-127/proof/after.png) |

On main, agent-browser refused the click: `Element is covered by <div.fixed.inset-0> at its click point`.

### Video of the flow (agent-browser, fixed build)

The recording empties English, then saves. It presses Cancel, and the text comes back. It empties English and saves again, then presses Escape: only the dialog closes, and the text comes back. Finally it empties English, saves and presses Clear: the base text is cleared and the panel stays open.

![flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AntelopeJS/dms-lang/5413fcc38875300f32980ad4cdebe90b4e3772e4/pr-127/proof/after-flow.gif)

[MP4](https://github.com/AntelopeJS/dms-lang/blob/verify-evidence/pr-127/proof/after-flow.mp4) · [WebM](https://github.com/AntelopeJS/dms-lang/blob/verify-evidence/pr-127/proof/after-flow.webm)

### The failing journey, then passing

On main, with the journey from this PR:

```
FAIL matrix/key-panel-stays-open-on-a-failed-save
    28-admin-click-button-clear-in-dialog-clear-the-base-text-of-sh: click button "Clear" in dialog "Clear the base text of shop.title?" (locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded.)
    critical step 28-admin-click-button-clear-in-dialog-clear-the-base-text-of-sh failed
```

On this branch's head, on a fresh `dms-control up --prepare` run:

```
smoke PASS smoke
matrix PASS key-panel-stays-open-on-a-failed-save
matrix: 47 of 47 journeys PASS
```

`dms-control plan` maps the diff to `smoke` and `matrix`, and both features ran whole.

### Checks

- `pnpm run checks`: `Checks: 8 passed, 0 failed.`
- `pnpm test:frontend`: build and type check pass.
- The docs (`docs/4.usage/2.translation-matrix.md:49`, "except before clearing the base text") still match.

## Review

Two independent reviewers (Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5) both found the same race in the first version. A second question during the first dialog's leave animation reused the closed dialog, never opened, and wedged the panel's save queue. The second commit fixes it with one dialog per question. Opus also noted that the journey read the cleared text only once after Clear, which could flake on a slow runner. It now uses `eventually`.

author: simpleprogrammingau
body:
Closes #20

## Summary

`deal(deck, handCount, handSize, options?)` deals from the top of a deck into hands and returns a frozen `{ hands, remainder }`. The chain gets a `deal` method that ends the pipeline, as `draw` does.

```text
deal(deck, handCount, handSize, { packetSize = 1, runOut = RunOut.THROW })
  check deck, hand count, hand size, options, packetSize, runOut
  if RunOut.THROW and the deck is short: throw InsufficientCardsError, before dealing
  each hand's target = handSize
                     | HandSize.MAXIMIZE → ⌊cards / hands⌋, +1 for the first (cards mod hands) hands
  round after round, until every hand is full or the deck is empty
    each hand in turn takes min(packet, what it still needs, cards left) from the top
  hands, each hand, remainder and result: new and frozen
```

```ts
deal(deck, 4, 13);                                       // round-robin
deal(deck, 4, 5, { packetSize: 3 });                     // 3 then 2, as in Euchre
deal(deck, 4, 13, { packetSize: PacketSize.HAND });      // each hand's cards at once
deal(deck, 3, HandSize.MAXIMIZE);                        // 18, 17, 17
deal(deck, 5, 11, { runOut: RunOut.STOP });              // 11, 11, 10, 10, 10: short hands
chain(deck).shuffle({ random }).deal(4, 5).value();      // ends the chain
```

Decided in the grilling:

- **Packets, not blocks.** One `packetSize` setting covers round-robin (the default, 1), packet deals, and whole hands (`PacketSize.HAND`). A hand's last packet is smaller if it needs fewer cards, and a packet bigger than the hand gives it all its cards at once. A function for packet patterns is #58.
- **The first card dealt to a hand is its top card.** There's no option to reverse it. A new consequence in ADR 0004 records it.
- **Counts are 1 or more.** The hand count can go up to 2³² − 1, the longest an array can be. Every hand is made before the deal starts, so under `RunOut.STOP` a huge hand count can run out of memory; the doc comment says so. With a fixed hand size, `requested` is handCount × handSize as computed, even `Infinity`. With `HandSize.MAXIMIZE`, it's the hand count, so a deck needs a card for each hand.
- **Named values are strings with a constant and a type of the same name:** `HandSize.MAXIMIZE`, `PacketSize.HAND`, `RunOut.STOP` and `RunOut.THROW`. They aren't enums, because `erasableSyntaxOnly` rules those out. New ADR 0010 records the pattern, with `Rank`, `Suit` and `Color` exempt.
- **Reshuffling the discards mid-deal moved to #29.** Only a value that holds the deck and its pile together can check that the pile came from that deck. The design notes are in a comment there.
- **The issue's question: the checks are shared.** Each one in `src/internal/checks.ts` returns the error or `undefined`, and each public function chains them with `??` and throws once, in its own body, where `jsdoc/require-throws` sees it. `invalidStack` and `invalidCount` are gone. `draw`, `peek`, `shuffle` and `chain` keep their messages and check order.

```diff
 src/
+├── deal.ts              # deal, DealOptions, DealResult, HandSize, PacketSize, RunOut
+├── deal.test.ts / deal.test-d.ts / deal.bench.ts
 ├── chain.ts             # + Chain.deal
 ├── draw.ts, shuffle.ts  # checks through internal/checks.ts
 └── internal/
+    ├── checks.ts        # countProblem, optionsProblem, shortfall, sizeProblem, stackProblem
     └── stack.ts         # - invalidStack, invalidCount
 test/helpers.ts          # + deals() and sameValues(), now shared by two test files
```

Domain docs:

- **GLOSSARY.md:** new terms **Packet** and **Short hand**. **Deal** is reworded around packets.
- **ADRs:** new ADR 0010. ADR 0004 gains the hand order. ADR 0009 says "a deal's packet size" instead of "dealing in blocks".
- **CONTRIBUTING.md:** a Code rules bullet for ADR 0010.

## Evidence

```text
                                        main                        this PR
import { deal } from "deckshoes"        no such export              deal, HandSize, PacketSize, RunOut
deal(standard52(), 4, 5, { packetSize: 3 }).hands[0]
                                        –                           AH 2H 3H KH AC
deal(standard52(), 3, HandSize.MAXIMIZE) sizes
                                        –                           18 17 17
deal(standard52(), 3, 18, { packetSize: 3, runOut: RunOut.STOP }) sizes
                                        –                           18 18 16
deal(standard52(), 5, 11)               –                           throws INSUFFICIENT_CARDS
tests                                   551 passed                  683 passed
```

- **The main property:** taking each hand's packets round by round, then the remainder, gives the deck back exactly (`Object.is`, position by position). It holds:
  - for every packet size, with a fixed hand size, `HandSize.MAXIMIZE` and `RunOut.STOP`;
  - on stacks of `fc.anything()`.
- **Other properties:**
  - `PacketSize.HAND` gives the same hands as successive `draw`s.
  - `RunOut.STOP` with enough cards gives the same result as `RunOut.THROW`.
  - Every array subclass gives plain frozen stacks.
  - Each option is read once.
- **Bundle size:** the top-level `Object.freeze` calls for the constants kept them in every bundle, so "shuffle only, no chain" grew from 796 B to 849 B, over its 800 B budget. `/* @__PURE__ */` brings it back to 796 B (`fix:` commit). The budget is unchanged. "Everything" is 2.25 kB of 5 kB.
- **Benchmark:** a 52-card deal takes about 1.5 µs with `PacketSize.HAND` and 1.8 µs round-robin (`pnpm bench src/deal.bench.ts`).
- `pnpm check` exits 0.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way, once released.

`deal`, the three constants and their string values become public API in the next alpha. So do the hand order and how MAXIMIZE splits the deck: changing either later changes every seeded deal. Before the alpha ships, reverting the `feat:` commits removes it all.

**Blast Radius:** additive.

No existing export changes behaviour. `draw`, `peek`, `shuffle` and `chain` go through the new shared checks, with the same messages and order, and their existing tests pass unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes locally
- [x] Tests cover the change (property tests for stack operations; a seeded random source for anything random)
- [x] Public exports have full doc comments, with new ones marked `@since NEXT`
- [x] `@example` blocks show results with `// =>` and pass as doctests
- [x] A changeset is included (`pnpm changeset`), or this PR doesn't change the published package

author: laodouya
body:
Part of #443. Please squash-merge: an intermediate commit does not pass its own tests.

The sanitizer checked the statements that sqlparser found, joined them with `"; "`, and passed the result to SQLite, which splits it by its own rules. Where the two disagree, a statement runs unchecked. On develop, ``create index i on t(a) where a = 'x;select 2 --'; insert into r values(1)`` inserts a row and creates the index. `explain select #p; insert into r values(1)`, with one argument, also inserts a row.

The sanitizer now requires exactly one statement. It passes SQLite the pattern as it is, or the SHOW rewrite; several statements fail with `ErrMultipleStatements`. A trailing semicolon and #445's transaction statements still pass. Several statements must be sent as separate queries, so a script in a single `Exec` now fails.

The PR also bumps go-sqlite3-encrypt to v1.13.0 and turns on its `SingleStatement` mode for both drivers that `xenomint/sqlite` registers. They refuse a string that SQLite reads as more than one statement without stepping the first or preparing the second. That covers reads, writes and replay, plus the BP, KMS and observer storage, which already run one statement at a time. This is defence in depth: with the current sqlparser, no input is known that the sanitizer sees as one statement but SQLite runs as two.

sqlparser skips the rest of a CREATE INDEX or an EXPLAIN up to the first semicolon, even one inside a string. So a single statement such as `EXPLAIN SELECT 'a;select 2 --'`, which develop ran after re-joining, is now rejected as two. The held CovenantSQL/sqlparser `fix/ddl-tail-semicolons` would remove these false rejections. Like every step of #443, this changes which queries miners accept; no network is running.

### Testing

linux/amd64, Docker golang:1.27 with libicu-dev, 4 CPUs, `UNITTESTTAGS` from ci.yml:

- `go test -race -tags "$UNITTESTTAGS" -run '^(TestState|TestConvertQueryAndBuildArgs)$' ./xenomint/` and `-run '^TestStorage$' ./xenomint/sqlite/`: the new cases fail on develop, built with this go.mod so that they compile, and pass here.
  - Through State, both patterns above are refused on reads, writes, request replay and block replay, and leave no row and no index.
  - On the storage connections, `INSERT …; SELECT 2` is refused before the INSERT runs.
- `go test -race ./xenomint/...`, `go vet` and `go mod tidy` are clean.
- `make -j4 all && ./alltest.sh` passes on develop and on this branch.

author: haus-chat[bot]
body:
## What
For **today and the two most recent closed account-local dates**, `performance_daily` target rows now come from whichever source was refreshed most recently: hourly data (Marketing Stream rollup or hourly-grain report) or the daily report. Search and all day and month ranges read one dataset that matches the Ads console. No Amazon API calls are added.

## Design
- **Derivation** (`src/lib/daily-target-freshness/refresh-daily-target-performance.ts`): when hourly data is newer than the daily report, the date is rebuilt from `performance_hourly` in one transaction under a per-account, per-date advisory lock. Only changed rows are upserted; rows that hourly no longer has are deleted. DST days sum 23 or 25 hours. If hourly is newer but has no rows, a date the daily report already filled is left alone.
- **Daily report parsing** (`daily-target.ts`) now replaces its date atomically under the same lock and removes rows the report no longer contains. An empty report deletes nothing, and rows for ads whose report rows failed target lookup are kept.
- **Triggers:** after each successful Stream rollup, after any report is processed, and the existing 15-minute schedule. The job name is unchanged, so health checks, metrics and the dashboard keep working.
- **Events** are written per date only when the chosen source or row counts change.

## Precedence
- **Hourly as-of** = the later of (a) Stream as-of, while the rollup's 24h window reaches into the date, and (b) the request time of the last processed hourly report, counted only when that report is completed and nothing is in flight.
- **Stream as-of** = the earlier of the latest successful rollup start and the latest AMS `received_at` for the advertiser.
  - It is null if no AMS message arrived in the last **90 minutes**. AMS traffic arrives in hourly bursts with 20–40 minute gaps, so 90 minutes allows a normal gap but still catches a stalled Stream.
  - It is also null if the account has no entity id.
- **Daily as-of** = the request time of the daily report. If a newer daily report is in flight, derivation pauses. Ties go to daily.
- **Migration 0065** (additive): `received_at timestamptz default now()` on `ams_sp_traffic` and `ams_sp_conversion`, plus an `(advertiser_id, received_at)` index on each. The traffic index is built on about 1.3M rows during migration, which briefly blocks worker inserts; SQS redelivery covers that.

## Tests
- Unit: 17/17, including precedence cases, stale AMS, no entity id, DST windows, and events only on change.
- Integration (PGlite): 9/9 — hourly newer; daily newer; target only in hourly; Nov 1 fall-back DST day; today; stale AMS; no entity id; empty hourly; atomic daily replacement.
- Local `check:fast`: 224 passed, 1 skipped, 11 suites failed. All 11 failures are the pre-existing `@merchbaseco/access` install issue on the mini. CI is the judge.

## Read-only prod comparison
US account, as of Nov 7 22:07 PT. Format: clicks / spend / purchases / sales.

| Date | Source | Account now → after | Campaign "Christmas - ALL - Standards - Auto" now → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nov 5 | hourly | 719/262.46/27/476.83 → 796/290.61/31/561.78 | 59/22.08/1/18.95 → 68/25.64/2/35.94 |
| Nov 6 | hourly | 711/250.58/21/391.94 → 752/264.56/30/545.89 | 74/28.50/2/33.98 → 79/30.25/5/84.95 |
| Nov 7 | hourly | unchanged | unchanged |

Deck The Palms ad, Nov 5–7: 92 / 1 / $16.99 → 98 / 5 / $84.95. The Ads console shows 97 / 5 / $84.95.

## Risks
- Derived totals come from Amazon's hourly pipeline until the next daily report (T+2/T+3) replaces them, so there can be small variance.
- Right after deploy, existing AMS rows carry the migration time as `received_at`.
- Search coverage flags still read daily report metadata.
- Advisory locks were exercised in PGlite only; they will be verified live after deploy.

## Live check plan
After deploy: watch the per-date events on the dashboard, re-run the comparison above, and spot-check campaigns and ad groups against the Ads console for today, yesterday and 2+ days ago.

author: snehit70
body:
Builds were spending most of their time on the APK. On the PR #72 runs, the release APK step took 7m04s of an 8m01s job. The Flutter CI job took 7m15s, run as analyze, then tests (1m25s), then the debug APK (4m48s).

## Changes

**1. Release builds only arm64.** `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` compiled armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a and x86_64, and only the arm64 APK ships. Adding `--target-platform android-arm64` drops the other two. `--split-per-abi` stays on purpose. In Flutter 3.44.4's Gradle plugin, an ABI split output gets `versionCodeOverride = 2*1000 + versionCode` and the name `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk`. So the version code, the file name and `verify-android-release.sh` all stay the same, and installed phones update in place. Without the split, the version code would drop below what is installed and Android would refuse the update.

**2. Gradle caching.** `~/.gradle/caches` and `~/.gradle/wrapper` are now restored and saved with `actions/cache`, and the Gradle build cache is turned on through `~/.gradle/gradle.properties`.
- The keys hash the Gradle files, the wrapper properties and `pubspec.lock`, so a new entry (a GB or more) is only saved when those inputs change. Saving per commit would fill the repo's 10 GB cache and push out the Flutter and Rust entries.
- Release and debug builds use separate keys. PRs only restore and never save.
- `-Dorg.gradle.caching=false` and `flutter clean` came in with the signing-key pin (6c4b110). `flutter clean` stays. Caching doesn't touch signing: AGP's packaging task isn't cacheable, the Dart AOT task isn't either, and the release verify step still checks the certificate, version code and ABI on every build.

**3. Flutter CI split into two parallel jobs.** "Flutter analyze and test" (no Java needed) and "Flutter debug APK". The debug APK is built for arm64 only. Nothing `needs:` the old job, and `main` has no required checks.

**4. CI concurrency.** A new push to a PR cancels that PR's older run. Each push to `main` gets its own group (`github.sha`). GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a shared group would drop the middle commit's run.

## Review

A review subagent read this against the Flutter 3.44.4 sources. It confirmed the version code and ABI behaviour, and it caught two problems that are fixed here: per-commit cache keys, and a shared concurrency group for `main`.

## Verification

- PR CI covers the split jobs and the debug build.
- `release.yml` only runs on `main`, so the first release after merge is the real test. Its verify step fails the release if the package, version, ABI or certificate is wrong.
- The first run on each key has an empty Gradle cache, so the caching gain shows from the second run on.

author: profnardi
body:
## Description

Fixes #592.

`submit` refused a changeset without a comment when it gave zero IMPs,
taking this as "no change". Some changes give no IMPs, such as a new
order of the sequences of an issue, so the indexer had to add a comment
to submit them.

As suggested in the issue, `submit` now refuses only when no revision
of the changeset is changed, using `compare_changes()` and
`is_changed` as the compare view does (a helper in
`apps/oi/views.py`). The check only runs when the IMPs are zero.

This also lets other changes without IMPs be submitted without a
comment, for example replacing a credit with "?" (#31) or correcting
a sort name to the name (#644).

## Testing

In the dev Docker setup, 2 passed in the new
`apps/oi/tests/test_submit_empty_change.py`. The test reserves an issue
with two sequences, swaps them with the real reorder view and submits
without a comment. Without the change, the submission is refused as an
empty change. A reservation without any change is still refused, with
and without the change.

Full suite: 762 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are the select view
tests fixed by #805; they fail on `beta` as well.

No new native/audio module, and no changes to `app.json` or `packages/*`. - `available === false` (Expo Go / older binary) → "needs the latest Arcade app" screen (`testID="needs-arcade"`). - `permission === "denied"` or `error` → friendly explanation + **Try again** (re-requests) + **Open Settings** (`testID="mic-denied"`). - **Gameplay** lives in pure `src/logic.ts` (no RN imports), so it can be unit-tested: - absolute pitch, C2–C6 (MIDI 36–84) mapped to height; ~14 semitones visible; camera follows the smoothed pitch with its own smoothing. - each wall has a pitch class `pc`; `holesFor(pc)` = one hole per octave in range; `fitsHole` = nearest hole within ±`toleranceCents` (60). - `step(state, dtMs, hz, walls, cfg)`: moves at constant `speedMps`; silence holds the last height; collision is checked on the swept interval, so long frames can't tunnel through a wall; no lives, so one crash ends the run; score = distance in metres. - **Best distance is kept only for the app session**: it lives in a module-level `sessionBest = { distance, walls, seed }` and resets when the app restarts. `@viral/game-kit` has no storage module, and this PR doesn't touch `packages/*` or add native deps. The share sheet invite `{ g, s: bestRun.seed, sc: best }` replays the walls of the best run. - All tunables (speed, tolerance cents, wall spacing/width, visible range, pitch/scroll smoothing, confidence) are in `src/config.ts`. ## Verification - `pnpm typecheck` ✅, `pnpm test` ✅ (12 new tests in `games/pitch-runner/test/logic.test.ts`, run on synthetic Hz samples: holes in every octave, ±60c accept/reject, traversing many walls while switching octaves, crashing on the wrong note, drifting off-note inside a wide wall, silence hold, clamping, no tunneling, camera lag). - Android dev client built with `cd apps/arcade && npx expo run:android` on the `arcade` emulator. The emulator's virtual mic sends noise that starts the run and crashes it quickly, so the flow accepts either the round screen or the result screen. - Real singing input can't be tested on the emulator. ## Why

The `opentelemetry-core` Dependabot group lists six modules by name. Any other `go.opentelemetry.io` module that becomes a direct dependency would get its own PR, outside the group. That includes `otel/log`, `proto/otlp`, `auto/sdk` (all currently indirect) or a new exporter.

`.github/dependabot.yml`: the gomod group now matches `go.opentelemetry.io/*` instead of six exact names, and it's renamed from `opentelemetry-core` to `opentelemetry`. All other Go dependencies still get separate PRs.

- The YAML parses, and the group has the single `go.opentelemetry.io/*` pattern.
- Dependabot validates the config once this is on master. The next OTel release should arrive as one `opentelemetry` group PR.

author: codiearyan
body:
## Why
Installing Island and figuring out how it works took a lot of guessing. The app gave no hint that hovering or ⌥Space opens it, there was no visible way to quit it, and on macOS 15+ right-click → Open no longer gets past Gatekeeper. The Scripts tab also had a real bug: **Choose folder…** opened the dialog *behind* the notch.

## What

**Install**
- `scripts/install.sh`: run `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Arjun-Bhandari/Island/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`. It installs the latest release to `/Applications`, clears the quarantine flag and opens the app. I tested it against the current `v1.0.2` release.
- If Island is started from outside Applications (e.g. Downloads), the welcome tour offers **Move to Applications** and relaunches from there. This matters because launch at login uses the app's current path.
- The README and the site's hero now show the one-liner, and the Gatekeeper steps are updated for macOS 15.

- The release now also ships `Island.dmg`, the usual Mac disk image: open it and drag Island onto the Applications shortcut. The DMG window is styled: background art generated with Codex image gen, a notch motif, a drag arrow, and the first-launch Gatekeeper hint. It's built by `dmgbuild` (installed into a venv under `.build/`, no Finder scripting, so it works on CI). Icons sit on a light card because Finder always draws icon names in black. `scripts/dmg-background.swift` re-renders the background. The site's **Download for macOS** button links to it instead of the zip. `Island.zip` is still published because `install.sh` uses it.

**Onboarding**: a welcome window on first launch with 5 steps:
1. Welcome
2. Features
3. Keyboard shortcuts (you can record new ones right there)
4. Launch at login / Keyboard only
5. "You're all set", which opens the notch

You can skip it at any point, and **Settings → Welcome tour** brings it back.

**Quit**
- **Settings → Quit Island** is in a footer that stays visible while you scroll.
- ⌘Q quits while the notch is focused.

**Scripts**
- Each script has an icon. By default it's guessed from the command (`pnpm dev` → server, `swift test` → test tube, `git …` → branch). You can also pick one from a strip of 16 when adding or editing.
- Redesigned rows: icon tile coloured by status, Running/Done/Failed badge, command · folder on one line, and a clear Run/Stop button. Delete now asks for a quick confirmation.
- The shortcut recorder moved into the add/edit form. Rows just show the key cap when a shortcut is set.
- New empty state with **New script** and **Import .sh file**. The Add button stays disabled until both name and command are filled.
- Older `scripts.json` files still load: `icon` is optional, and a test covers this.

**Fixes**
- File/folder pickers (Scripts and Cleanup) appeared under the notch, because the notch panel sits at `.screenSaver` level. Moving the mouse onto the dialog also collapsed the notch and threw away the form. Pickers now open above the notch, and the notch stays open until the picker is closed.
- A script's global shortcut kept running its pre-edit command, because the closure captured the old item.

## Testing
- `swift build`, plus `swift test` (new `IslandTests` target: legacy decode and icon guessing)
- Ran the dev build and checked screenshots of each onboarding step, the scripts list/form/empty state and the Settings footer
- Not checked by hand: clicking through the folder picker, and Move to Applications from a real translocated download

body: ## 目的 为 **openbmb/MiniCPM3-4B** 补齐 Ascend 使能材料。该模型为 62 层 / 隐藏维度 2560 的稠密模型，采用 MLA 注意力、SwiGLU MLP 和 LongRoPE（4B 参数，理论上下文 32K）。 上游 vLLM 已内置 `MiniCPM3ForCausalLM`（注意力、权重映射、采样集成、LongRoPE 处理），因此**无需任何模型专用 kernel 或建模层补丁**。缺的是将其在 Ascend 上验收合格所需的全部材料：一份 E2E 配置、一份生成用例、一篇教程，以及支持矩阵 / 每日任务（nightly）的条目。 ## 本 PR 做了什么 | 文件 | 改动 | | --- | --- | | `tests/e2e/models/configs/MiniCPM3-4B.yaml` | 新增 E2E 配置：BF16、TP1、`max_model_len=4096`、`gpu_memory_utilization=0.8`、`enforce_eager=true`、GSM8K 参考值、生成矩阵参数 | | `tests/e2e/models/configs/accuracy.txt` | 注册 `MiniCPM3-4B.yaml`，使 nightly 精度任务覆盖该模型 | | `tests/e2e/models/test_minicpm3_generation.py` | 新增可选（opt-in）生成矩阵：离线 vs OpenAI 兼容服务的贪心一致性、种子非贪心可复现性、中英文短提示与约 2K token 长提示、多次运行的 NPU 显存增长上限、TP1/TP2 | | `docs/source/tutorials/models/MiniCPM3-4B.md` | 新增教程：支持特性、权重下载、部署、功能/精度/性能验证、限制与故障排查 | | `docs/source/user_guide/support_matrix/supported_models.md` | 新增 `MiniCPM3-4B` 行（A2，experimental） | | `mkdocs.yml` | 在导航中注册教程 | | `.github/workflows/configs/nightly_config.yaml` | 将该模型加入 nightly 精度矩阵 | | `.agents/skills/minicpm3-4b-ascend-adaptation/SKILL.md` | 新增该模型的适配经验笔记 | | `.agents/README.md` | 注册新技能 | 未改动 `vllm_ascend/` 运行时代码，未新增自定义算子。 ## 为什么配置长这样 - `--trust-remote-code` 是**必需的**：checkpoint 自带 `configuration_minicpm.py` / `modeling_minicpm.py`。 - `--dtype bfloat16`：checkpoint 为 BF16；FP16 与量化社区版 checkpoint 不在已验证路径内。 - `--max-model-len 4096`：保守的合格长度。`max_position_embeddings=32768` 是理论上限；32K 下的长上下文精度与显存峰值尚未验收。 - `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8` + `--enforce-eager`：BF16 权重约 7.6 GiB。在 32 GB 卡上可为激活值留出数 GB 余量，并跳过 aclgraph 捕获（其编译/捕获阶段会同时拉高 NPU 和主机内存，使内存受限的容器不稳定）。 - lm-eval 任务中 `batch_size: 8`：lm-eval 的 `auto` 模式会持续上调 batch 直到显存耗尽，这是 32 GB 卡无法承受的。 ## 自验证报告 ### 环境 | 项目 | 版本 / 数值 | | --- | --- | | NPU | Atlas A2（910B4），单卡，32 GB HBM | | vLLM | `0.33.0rc1.dev370+empty`（源码构建 @ `24420b7a3`） | | vLLM Ascend | `0.19.1rc2.dev3339+g40b3842d3`（@ `40b3842d3`） | | torch / torch_npu | `2.10.0+cpu` / `2.10.0.post7` | | CANN | `9.0.0` | | triton-ascend | `3.6.0` | | transformers | `5.22.2` | | 模型 | `openbmb/MiniCPM3-4B`，8,148,010,378 字节，sha256 已校验 | 验证宿主机自带 CANN 9.0.0，因此 KV cache 走的是连续（contiguous）PagedAttention 布局——见「已知限制 → CANN 9.0.0 上的 block-strided GQA KV cache」。其余软件版本均与 `requirements-ascend.txt` 一致。 ### 1. 静态检查 ```text py_compile: OK yaml model_name: openbmb/MiniCPM3-4B yaml serve: {'tensor_parallel_size': 1, 'dtype': 'bfloat16', 'max_model_len': 4096, 'gpu_memory_utilization': 0.8, 'trust_remote_code': True, 'enforce_eager': True} accuracy.txt contains MiniCPM3-4B.yaml: True ``` ### 2. 服务 + 运行时探针（`vllm serve`，OpenAI 兼容 API） ```text [PASS] server reached /v1/models [PASS] GET /v1/models exposes the served name :: served=['minicpm3-4b'] [PASS] greedy completion: 'Hello, my name is' :: finish_reason=length tokens=32 [PASS] greedy completion: '人工智能的未来是' :: finish_reason=length tokens=32 [PASS] greedy is deterministic across repeated requests :: identical 32-token ids [PASS] seeded non-greedy sampling is reproducible :: 2/2 identical 32-token ids [PASS] chat completions returns non-empty content :: finish_reason=stop chars=90 [PASS] English long prompt (~2048 tokens) is answered :: prompt_tokens=2058 finish_reason=stop [PASS] Chinese long prompt (~2048 tokens) is answered :: prompt_tokens=2058 finish_reason=length [PASS] repeated generation round 1/3 stayed healthy [PASS] repeated generation round 2/3 stayed healthy [PASS] repeated generation round 3/3 stayed healthy ``` `Hello, my name is` 的贪心示例输出（32 tokens，temperature=0）： ```text 9855, 72, 1417, 1891, 1348, 5623, 22480, 1384, 32262, 16434, 59342, 1384, 1417, 1891, 2438, 1385, 6679, 1449, 1450, 1842, 4483, 1508, 10161, 1449, 1982, 1580, 72, 1417, 1580, 1348, 5997, 3138 ``` ### 3. GSM8K 精度（`test_lm_eval_correctness.py`，5-shot，chat template，batch_size=8） ```bash python -m pytest -sv tests/e2e/models \ --config tests/e2e/models/configs/MiniCPM3-4B.yaml --tp-size 1 ``` | 指标 | 配置中的门槛值 | Ascend 实测值 | | --- | --- | --- | | `exact_match,strict-match` | 0.77 | **0.7566** ✅ | | `exact_match,flexible-extract` | 0.78 | **0.7597** ✅ | 官方 model card 的 GSM8K 结果为 81.1。Ascend 实测值按仓库统一的 `test_lm_eval_correctness.py` 中 `RTOL=0.05` 进行判定，均在容差内。 ### 4. pytest 结果 | 用例 | 结果 | | --- | --- | | `test_lm_eval_correctness`（GSM8K，5-shot，chat template） | **PASSED** | | `test_minicpm3_generation.py::test_minicpm3_offline_online`（tp1） | **PASSED** | | 同一生成用例在 `--tp-size 2` 下 | SKIPPED（宿主机只有一张 NPU） | 本 PR **有意不包含**与 `transformers` 的 token 级对拍用例：checkpoint 自带的 `modeling_minicpm.py` 面向 `transformers` 4.x 的缓存/生成契约编写，在 `transformers` 5.x 下直接驱动会返回 NaN logits（`seen_tokens` / `get_max_cache_shape` / `get_usable_length` 被移除，mask 与 rotary 语义变更）。数值正确性因此改由 GSM8K 把关——它以 1319 条样本做端到端度量，远比 8 个 token 的对拍有说服力。 ## 已知限制 - **仅验证 BF16。** W8A8/W4A8、FP16 与量化社区版 checkpoint 未验证。 - **TP2 为实验性。** `num_attention_heads=40` 可被 2 整除，且已附带 TP2 E2E 用例，但尚未实际运行（验证宿主机只有单卡 NPU）。在 CI 覆盖前，支持矩阵保持 experimental。 - **32K 为理论值。** E2E 使用 4096 tokens。 - **LongRoPE 警告无害。** transformers ≥5 在归一化 checkpoint 的 `rope_scaling` 时会打印 `rope_parameters short_factor ... must have length 48, got 16`；仅在加载阶段出现，不影响外推窗口以下的生成（已在 2K 验证）。 - **无 token 级 `transformers` 对拍用例。** checkpoint 自带远程代码假设 `transformers` 4.x 的缓存与生成契约；在 5.x 下会报 `seen_tokens`、`get_max_cache_shape`、`get_usable_length` 缺失，且不带缓存直接前向会返回 NaN logits。精度改由 1319 条样本的 GSM8K 把关。 - **CANN 9.0.0 上的 block-strided GQA KV cache。** 验证使用了连续 PagedAttention KV 布局。当前 `main` 对纯 GQA 模型选择的 block-strided 布局，在此软件栈（`torch_npu==2.10.0.post7`、CANN 9.0.0、910B4）上会在首个解码步骤中于 `aclnnScatterPaKvCache` 处中止，报错 `EZ9999: Op ScatterPaKvCache has 2 uncontiguous input: keyCacheRef, valueCacheRef`——该算子在此栈上拒绝 strided 输入。本版本官方支持的软件栈钉定 CANN 9.2.1，非连续路径预计在那里可以工作；宿主机无法提供该组合，**合并前必须在官方 CANN 上复核**。本 PR 未包含针对此问题的 `vllm_ascend/` 代码改动。 ## 检查清单 - [x] 已新增模型 E2E 配置并注册进 `accuracy.txt` - [x] 已新增生成 / 离线-在线一致性测试 - [x] 已新增教程并链接进 `mkdocs.yml` - [x] 已新增支持矩阵行 - [x] 已更新 nightly 精度配置 - [x] 已在真实硬件上验证：serve + OpenAI API 探针 + GSM8K - [ ] TP2 已在 CI 中验证 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

body:
Currently, "required checks" on PRs are hidden from maintainers, and can get out of sync with the reality of a repo. To fix this, we're adding a `.github/required-checks.yml` file, which lists the checks that must pass before a PR can merge into main. 

When this file is changed, the ruleset that manages branch protection automatically gets synced up. The new `Required checks` workflow checks that all the checks listed in `required-checks.yml` exist.

_(Sidenote: I'm increasingly wary of agents that have access to GitHub mistakenly (or potentially nefariously) doing things that could do us damage or cause us to have unexpected or high costs. That's why I'm using CODEOWNERS on a more frequent basis for files that are always worth just getting a second pair of eyes on. It's not a reflection on trust for maintainers 🙂)_

The file adds the following Required Checks:

- `Suites match their templates`
- `ci`
- `configlet / configlet`
- `i18n / completeness`

author: thehalfmoon
body:
## What this fixes

Only a config's `tasks.<task>` entries counted toward a task's command surface. An edit to settings that apply to every task (`timeouts`, `budgetMs`, `redactEnv`) ran every task normally. Removing a `redactEnv` name let that secret be persisted unredacted. Raising the default timeout allowed a weeks-long hang.

Now:
- When a tracked `ascout.config.json` is modified, deleted, or renamed, every task treats it as a changed authority path, and is refused without `--allow-changed-command-surface`.
- A newly added config, as `ascout init` writes, keeps the per-task rule, so `init` followed by `check` still runs.
- A change of unknown kind is treated as an edit.

## Scope
- `src/check.ts`: the rule in `decideRunAdmissions`.
- `src/discovery.ts`: `ChangedPathView` carries Git's optional change kind, which the comparison already provides.

## Verification
- 6 new tests:
  - edited, deleted, renamed, and unknown-kind configs refuse every task, while an added config keeps the per-task rule;
  - a real `check` where removing `redactEnv` from a committed config refuses the discovered Vitest test task, which the config never names.
  
  Five of them fail without this change.
- The admission, override, nested-config, and CLI suites pass locally.

Exact-head CI evidence follows in a comment.

author: fumiya-kume
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #12773 (`--emit dex/apk`). That PR made Android framework classes resolvable in Sema via lazy `android.jar` import, but a real View-based app still failed to compile because the classpath importer only exposed Java methods — Kotlin callers need properties, constants, and SAM shapes. This change teaches the JVM classpath importer to emit the member shapes Kotlin code expects:

- **Classfile parsing** (`JVMClassReader`): read modern constant-pool tags (int/float/long/double/String/MethodHandle/Module/Package) and `ConstantValue` field attributes so `android.jar` classfiles parse; allow `$` segments in binary names.
- **Member synthesis** (`JVMClasspathIndex`):
  - Pair Java `getX`/`setX` accessors into Kotlin `var`s, including inherited setters and interface contract requirements.
  - Expose `public static final` fields as companion `const val`s.
  - Mark single-abstract-method interfaces as `fun interface` so SAM conversion (`setOnClickListener { ... }`) works.
  - Emit `const val` stubs bound to literal `ConstantValue`s.
- **Owner resolution** (`JVMFunctionBuilder+Members`): resolve imported property/function owners through the nominal parent chain so companion and nested-class members bind to the right classfile binary name, and bind stub methods by binary owner so nested declarations (e.g. `View.OnClickListener.onClick`) reach codegen.
- **Regression test** (`JVMBackendTests+JavaClassMembers`): covers static constants, JavaBean property pairing, `var` setter resolution, `fun interface` SAM conversion, and inherited accessors in both `.jvmJar` and `.jvmClass` modes.

#### Test plan

- [x] `swift_test.sh --filter javaStaticConstantsBeanPropertiesSAMAndInheritedAccessors` — 2 cases pass (`.jvmJar`, `.jvmClass`)
- [x] E2E: two-Activity View-based app (`Activity`, `LinearLayout`, `TextView`, `Button`, `Intent`, `Log`) compiles via `--emit apk` to a signed APK; verified on Android emulator — install, launch, counter increment (`Log.d` output), `Intent` extra to second Activity, back-navigation state preservation
- [x] `swift build --product kswiftc` clean
- [ ] Full `CompilerBackendTests` — **not run to completion**; see note below

**Note on unrelated failures:** a broad `CompilerBackendTests` run surfaced ~15 failing tests (`bundledJVMComparisonHelpers`, `collectionBuilders...`, `m14JavaAndKotlinInlineSuspendConsumers`, `collectionToArray...`, etc.). A/B verification against the base commit (`e94ad64e9e`, in a separate worktree) shows **all of them fail identically without this change** — they are pre-existing at the branch point, not regressions. This branch has since been rebased onto current `origin/master`.

O PDF do certificado de conclusão ganha o visual do site da Átrios e um verso com o conteúdo programático. O desenho foi aprovado pelo usuário a partir de um modelo em HTML; este PR reproduz o modelo no pdfkit.

author: saariuslystoned
body:
Resubmits #195067, which openclaw-barnacle auto-closed under the active-PR limit (the author can't reopen a PR closed by the bot). Same branch; the author is back under the limit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage cost estimates for Grok requests with long prompts (200k tokens or more) show half of what xAI charges.

## User Impact

Cost estimates and usage reports for long-prompt Grok requests now use xAI's long-context rate. Short prompts are unchanged. Existing xAI OAuth configs get the rate after `openclaw doctor --fix`. On the subscription route these numbers remain labeled estimates, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

xAI's [model pricing table](https://docs.x.ai/developers/models) lists a second row "≥ 200k prompt tokens" for every priced Grok model (4.7, 4.6, 4.5, 4.3, both 4.20-0309 variants, grok-build-0.1): input, cached input and output all double, and "requests whose prompt reaches the listed token threshold are billed at the higher rate for all tokens in the request." Core already prices whole requests by prompt-token tier through `cost.tieredPricing` (half-open ranges; the openai and anthropic manifests use it). The xAI manifest had only the flat short-context rate, and `docs/providers/xai.md` described that as a limitation that predates tier support in manifests.

This adds the documented tier to the seven priced rows. `model-definitions.ts` turns the manifest into typed model definitions, and JSON imports widen tier ranges to `number[]`, so a small typed mapper restores the `[start, end]` / `[start]` tuple without casts. The docs paragraph now describes the tiers.

**Existing OAuth configs.** OAuth sign-in saves each catalog row, `cost` included, into `models.providers.xai.models` (`applyXaiOAuthConfig` ← `buildLiveXaiOAuthProvider`, `cost: fallback?.cost`), and saved rows override the catalog at runtime. So configs written before this PR kept flat prices. The xAI Doctor contract (`doctor-contract-api.ts`) now adds the catalog's `tieredPricing` to saved xAI rows that are on an official xAI route (the row's `baseUrl`, else the provider's, is unset, `https://api.x.ai/v1` or the Grok OAuth route), whose flat rates still equal the catalog's, and that carry no tiers. Rows on a custom `baseUrl` own their own billing and are left as written even at catalog rates, as are rows with custom prices, rows that already have tiers (even an empty list), and zero-priced rows.

Why Doctor rather than not persisting `cost` at sign-in: `cost` is a required field of `ModelDefinitionConfig`, so dropping it from the OAuth patch would change the config contract. This plugin's Doctor contract already repairs stale generated xAI rows (`isLegacyXaiBuiltinModel`), and the repo rule sends legacy config shapes to Doctor rather than to runtime readers. If maintainers prefer pricing to stay purely plugin-owned, the switch is: make `cost` optional for provider-config rows, omit it in `applyXaiOAuthConfig`, and have this Doctor rule delete catalog-equal `cost` objects instead of adding tiers.

## Evidence

- **Red on main** (`1166f73e0`): the `api.test.ts` catalog-pricing case expects `grok-4.5` to carry xAI's tiers and fails because `tieredPricing` is missing.
- **Red before the Doctor repair:** the `doctor-contract-api.test.ts` case uses the exact row shape OAuth sign-in saved (`id, name, api, baseUrl, reasoning, input, cost, contextWindow, maxTokens, compat`, flat cost, the OAuth route). Without the repair no Doctor rule matches it. On the previous head (`6fd4932c4`), the custom-route cases fail because the row on `https://proxy.example.test/v1` was tiered. With this head, the OAuth row gains both tiers, a second run changes nothing, and custom-route (model or provider `baseUrl`), custom-price, already-tiered and zero-price rows stay identical. Whole xAI extension suite: 34 files, 408 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt`, the test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Green with the fix:** all xAI extension tests plus the core consumers that read xAI catalog rows or tier prices (`clawrouter-xai-responses`, thinking defaults, effective tool inventory, xAI auto-retirement, startup config corpus, catalog/manifest contracts, `session-cost-usage-pricing`): 43 files, 534 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Every added tier value was checked row by row against xAI's table.
- **Live Gateway turn** (local Gateway built from `main` plus this PR, xAI OAuth, `xai/grok-4.7`, one turn): the usage report gave `promptTokens 179241` (input 178,089 + cached 1,152), output 7,123, `cost.total 0.399492`. That is exactly the short-tier rate ($2 / $0.50 / $6 per M), which is correct below 200k.
- **Shipped calculator at the boundary:** the built `calculateUsageCost` (`packages/llm-core/dist`) run against the built `dist/extensions/xai/openclaw.plugin.json` row for `grok-4.7`, with 50,000 cached prompt tokens in each case:

  | prompt tokens (incl. cached) | this PR | flat catalog on `main` |
  |---|---|---|
  | 179,241 (the live turn above) | $0.399492 | $0.399492 |
  | 199,999 | $0.336998 | $0.336998 |
  | 200,000 | **$0.674000** | $0.337000 |
  | 240,000 | **$0.834000** | $0.417000 |

  Tier selection counts input + cached + cache-write tokens, so cached input moves a request over the boundary, and the whole request doubles, as xAI's table says.
- **Live ≥200k turn, before the Doctor repair** (same Gateway, one turn): `promptTokens 209280` (input 208,128 + cached 1,152), output 29. The Gateway recorded **$0.417006**, which is `main`'s flat figure, because its OAuth rows were saved before this PR.
- **Live ≥200k turn, after the Doctor repair** (Gateway rebuilt from `main` plus this PR at `1914c08b0`; same OAuth config, signed in before the change): `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` reported `Added xAI's long-context price tier to 3 saved xAI model row(s)` and left the zero-priced row untouched. One turn with the same 790 KB prompt: `promptTokens 209280` (input 208,128 + cached 1,152), output 30. The Gateway recorded **$0.834024**, which is exactly the ≥200k rate (208,128 × $4 + 1,152 × $1 + 30 × $12 per M). The flat figure for the same usage is $0.417012.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable (`2026.11.2`):** a state dir whose `models.providers.xai.models` holds the rows exactly as an earlier OAuth sign-in saved them (flat costs on the OAuth route), plus a `grok-4.6` row on a custom `baseUrl` at catalog rates. `openclaw@2026.11.2` `config validate` accepts it and reads all four rows unchanged. This head's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` on the same state reports `Added xAI's long-context price tier to 2 saved xAI model row(s)`: grok-4.7 and grok-4.5 on the OAuth route gain both tiers, while the custom-route grok-4.6 row and the zero-priced row are byte-identical. A second Doctor run reports no xAI repair.
- **Boundary:** unit tests at the Doctor and catalog contracts; the latest-stable upgrade above (config validation on the released package, then this head's Doctor from source, no Gateway); and a live local Gateway on the xAI OAuth route for both ≥200k turns. For each long turn, the local `grok-4.7` `contextWindow` was raised to 320k so the pre-send estimate didn't compact the prompt below 200k, then restored. The live turns ran before the custom-route scoping; that change only narrows which rows Doctor touches, and the official-route row in the live config is one the scoped rule still repairs.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: the 62 added regression lines have their own `config/test-lines-allocations/xai-long-context-pricing.txt` record.
- **Data model:** no schema change. `cost.tieredPricing` is an existing optional field on model rows (the openai and anthropic manifests already use it). The repaired config also passes `openclaw@2026.11.2` `config validate`, so going back to the latest stable a

author: ihid
body:
Currently, "required checks" on PRs are hidden from maintainers, and can get out of sync with the reality of a repo. To fix this, we're adding a `.github/required-checks.yml` file, which lists the checks that must pass before a PR can merge into main. 

When this file is changed, the ruleset that manages branch protection automatically gets synced up. The new `Required checks` workflow checks that all the checks listed in `required-checks.yml` exist.

_(Sidenote: I'm increasingly wary of agents that have access to GitHub mistakenly (or potentially nefariously) doing things that could do us damage or cause us to have unexpected or high costs. That's why I'm using CODEOWNERS on a more frequent basis for files that are always worth just getting a second pair of eyes on. It's not a reflection on trust for maintainers 🙂)_

The file adds the following Required Checks:

- `configlet / configlet`
- `i18n / completeness`
- `Validation`
- `Validate required checks` (rather recursively, I admit!)

For many repos (including Groovy), the build jobs are named with the OS image (e.g. `Build (macos-26)` and `Build (windows-2025)`). Those names change whenever an image is bumped, which is quite unstable, and then the required checks break. I'm going to fix that separately by adding a check with a more standard name (e.g. "tests"), which can rely on the unstably named jobs, and add that to this file. That'll be a separate PR.

author: gabrielgellner
body:
Adds `Tape` (saved as "tape"), a slot effect after Airwindows' ToTape9 (the newest ToTape, MIT, Chris Johnson's notice kept), with wow and flutter from Mutable Instruments' Beads (`fx/wow_and_flutter.h`, MIT).

## What it does
In order, it applies drive, ToTape's "Dubly" encode, Beads' wow and flutter on a short line from the effect pool, bias (9 slew-limit stages), a tiny hysteresis, slew-dependent darkening around ToTape's sine-series saturation, the head bump, Dubly decode, and ToTape's ClipOnly3. The output never goes above 0.94 (about -0.5 dB).

| Setting | Label | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drive | DRIV | -18 to +18 dB (ToTape's Input) | `80`, 0 dB |
| Tone | TONE | ToTape's Tilt, centred | `80`, flat |
| Bias | BIAS | underbias below `80`, overbias above | `80`, none |
| Bump | BUMP | ToTape's HeadBmp | `80`, as ToTape starts |
| Wow | WOW | squared; `80` = Beads' amount, `FF` = 4x | `40` |
| Flutter | FLUT | squared; `80` = Beads' amount, `FF` = 4x | `40` |
| Mix | MIX | | `FF` |
| Gain | GAIN | | `E0` |

## Choices for you to review
- **Settings:** ToTape's `Shape` and `HeadFrq` stay at their defaults (half way, so a 68.75 Hz head bump), which keeps it to 6 settings plus Mix and Gain. ToTape's Output and dry/wet are replaced by our Gain and Mix.
- **Bias:** the top end is capped at 0.75 of ToTape's overbias, because at ToTape's full overbias the slew limits close and the sound goes silent. When it's unbiased, the slew stages keep tracking the signal, so turning bias back on doesn't click.
- **Wow and flutter:** these come from Beads, not ToTape's own flutter, which is left out. They use one line for both sides (one transport) and a cubic read. Beads' low-pass after the line is left out, since `Tone` covers that. The wobble is worked out every 32 frames and moved in a straight line between, as Beads does once a block. The drift randomness uses a fixed-seed xorshift.
- **No noise:** Airwindows' fpd dither, its denormal trick and the noise that moves ClipOnly3's level are all left out, so the output is deterministic.
- **ClipOnly3:** its shift loops leave every intermediate sample equal to the newest, so it's ported as it actually behaves: 1 frame of latency at any rate.
- **Latency:** about 2 frames, more with wow. Nothing compensates for it, so `Mix` below `FF` gives a faint chorus.
- **Loud highs:** these soften with level (about -2 dB at 5 kHz at -12 dBFS), as ToTape's do. Quiet sounds come through within 0.5 dB.
- **Density** is left out. It's another sine shaper next to Drive and would be a 7th setting; it could be a slot of its own.
- **Console** is out of scope. A Console summing choice for the master is left for later, in #175.
- **CPU:** about 0.65% of one core per slot at 48 kHz.

## Tests
- Gentle settings are near-transparent: quiet sounds come through within 0.5 dB and line up with the input, and a louder low or mid sound gets less than 1% third harmonic.
- Drive adds odd harmonics and the peaks stay bounded.
- Tone tilts the highs, Bump lifts the lows, and overbias softens the highs.
- Wow and flutter move the pitch; with both off it stays still.
- Every setting glides with no steps when stepped every 64 frames.
- Output stays finite and bounded at every extreme, at 44.1 and 192 kHz.
- The line is long enough at every rate.
- An engine test is in `tests/fx.rs`.
- The no-allocation and memory-pool tests in `link.rs` cover Tape.

Closes #163

author: savar-g
body:
The CI test step outgrew its 22-minute limit. Main run 42452867626 on 51b16ca8 timed out with no failing test.

## What changes
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` only:
- **`unit`:** a matrix of two vitest shards (`--shard=1/2` and `--shard=2/2`). The step limit is 25 minutes and the job limit is 30. `fail-fast` is off, so one shard's failure doesn't hide the other's result.
- **`checks`:** the family-zones check, the family-window SQL comparison, and `npx eslint src`. This is the only place lint runs.
- **`test`:** the final job, named exactly `test`. It needs `unit` and `checks`, runs even when one fails (`if: always()`), and fails unless both are `success`. Vercel's Deployment Check and the branch rules keep using the name `test`.

Triggers, concurrency and permissions are unchanged. `blog-publish.yml` starts this workflow with `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main` (`workflow_dispatch`), which still exists, so the blog flow keeps starting CI on main.

## Vercel build
`scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh` skips a build when only `.github/` changed, but **only after the branch has an earlier deployment**. This is a new branch, so its first push builds once ("No earlier deployment on this branch: build."). Later pushes to this branch, and the merge to main, skip.

author: ihid
body:
Currently, "required checks" on PRs are hidden from maintainers, and can get out of sync with the reality of a repo. To fix this, we're adding a `.github/required-checks.yml` file, which lists the checks that must pass before a PR can merge into main. 

When this file is changed, the ruleset that manages branch protection automatically gets synced up. The new `Required checks` workflow checks that all the checks listed in `required-checks.yml` exist.

_(Sidenote: I'm increasingly wary of agents that have access to GitHub mistakenly (or potentially nefariously) doing things that could do us damage or cause us to have unexpected or high costs. That's why I'm using CODEOWNERS on a more frequent basis for files that are always worth just getting a second pair of eyes on. It's not a reflection on trust for maintainers 🙂)_

The file adds the following Required Checks:

- `configlet / configlet`
- `i18n / completeness`
- `Validate required checks` (rather recursively, I admit!)

For many repos (including Ballerina), the exercise tests are named with version (e.g. `ci (ubuntu-26.04, 2201.13.3)` and `ci (macos-14, 2201.13.3)`). Those names change whenever a version is bumped, which is quite unstable, and then the required checks break. I'm going to fix that separately by adding a check with a more standard name (e.g. "tests"), which can rely on the unstably named tests, and add that to this file. That'll be a separate PR.

author: familyofs4k-lab
body:
## Summary
- `POST /api/v1/ask` is the only route that spends LLM credits. It now has a sliding-window limit of 10 requests/minute per client IP and a global daily cap on LLM calls (`VEDAGRAPH_ASK_DAILY_CAP`, default 1000; 0 refuses everything).
- Both limits return HTTP 429 in the existing `ErrorBody` format (`RATE_LIMITED` / `DAILY_CAP_REACHED`) with a `Retry-After` header. `ApiError` can now carry response headers.
- Per-IP check runs first. The daily cap is charged only once the provider resolves, so 422s and unconfigured-provider 503s cost nothing.
- Client IP comes from `X-Forwarded-For` at `VEDAGRAPH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` hops from the right (default 1), falling back to the socket address when the header is shorter. A wrong setting therefore shares a bucket and never lets a caller forge one.
- Also configurable: `VEDAGRAPH_ASK_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 10).

## Before relying on this in production
- **Set `VEDAGRAPH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` on Render.** Traffic goes browser → Vercel/Next rewrite → Render proxy → API, so the default of 1 probably puts every visitor in one shared bucket. The real count has not been measured; log the raw `X-Forwarded-For` for one Ask call from the live site and count the entries.
- Counters are in process memory: they reset on restart and are per worker. The provider-side monthly budget is still the real spend ceiling.
- 1000/day is a guess; check it against the model's price per call.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/api/ask/test_ask_rate_limit.py`: both limits, `Retry-After`, window sliding, daily reset at UTC midnight, forged header, trusted-proxy hops, table sweep, env vars
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --strict` clean
- [x] `tests/api`: 929 passed. `test_closure_regressions.py::test_an_empty_choices_response_is_retryable_not_permanent` fails, and also fails on a clean `main`

author: dillonlille
body:
## Summary

Joining or leaving a Slack channel, and switching an integration on or off, show their change at once, with nothing dimmed while they save.

## Symptom

Joining or leaving a channel greyed out every Join and Leave button, showed a spinner, and left the channel under its old heading until Slack answered, then it jumped lists. After confirming an integration switch, its card showed the old state for a moment until the workspace was read again.

## Cause

Caused by: #482

The channels list disabled every button while one channel saved and moved the channel only on Slack's answer, since #482. An integration's card showed only the workspace as last read, so it waited for the reading after its switch.

## Fix

- A channel moves to Joined or Not joined as it is asked. Each channel keeps what Slack last answered apart from the latest it was asked, so an earlier answer never moves it while a later asking waits, and one that fails leaves it as Slack last answered. Requests go one after another in the order asked, saved with `useAction`; no button is disabled and the spinner is gone.
- An integration switches as its question is confirmed. The Slack client keeps, for each integration, the latest asked and what the server last answered: switches of one integration save one after another, so the last asked is the last saved; every reading of the account (the card, and the workspace's sections, so its settings open at once) shows the latest asked while any saves, then what was answered, until a reading asked for after that answer has it, each reading catching up on its own. One refused shows what was last saved, and its error above the cards.

## Risk

Only these two Slack sections change; their requests are the same. Undo by reverting the commit.

## Verification

`dispatchdev check` and the Slack browser test pass. It holds a join open and finds the channel already under Joined with the other buttons enabled; a Leave asked before the join is answered keeps it under Not joined; two refused requests leave it as Slack last had it; an integration's switch held open finds the card already switched as its question closes; switched back and forth with the first held, the last asked is what's saved; one refused shows what was saved last; and a reading answered before a switch's answer but shown after it doesn't undo it, which fails against the previous version of this fix. These fail against the code before this fix, and the refused pair against the first version of it.

```
dispatchdev check
dispatchdev test
```

## Review

Tier standard · 3 passes · gpt-6.1-sol · Important 7 (fixed 7) · Nit 1 (fixed 1) · Pre-existing 0 · the UI changed after its preview: features/slack/frontend/integrations/IntegrationSwitch.tsx, features/slack/frontend/integrations/IntegrationsSection.tsx, features/slack/frontend/workspace/ChannelsSection.tsx
