author: bhargavchintam
body:
## Description

Some users have two accounts because they typed their email with a different case each time (`mike@` and `Mike@`). The issue says it is generally safe to treat emails as case-insensitive, and that the inputs then need normalising in the user forms and in `BookingForm`. This PR does that. It does not add the `UniqueConstraint` the issue mentions, and it does not merge existing accounts.

New emails are stored in lower case: at signup (`RegisterForm` and `PasswordLessRegisterForm`, through a small `NormaliseEmailMixin`), in the change-email request (`sendSecondaryEmailActivation`), and when `BookingForm` creates a new user for a comp or box office booking.

Typed emails are now matched ignoring case: login (`get_user_to_login`), password reset and resend activation (`get_user_by_email`), the `BookingForm` user lookup, and `productionPermissions` (`subject_user`). These go through a new helper, `get_by_email()` in `uobtheatre/utils/utils.py`, which tries an exact match first. Some existing accounts differ only by case, and a plain `iexact` lookup can return the other account, so login with the right password would fail for them. The "email already in use" check (`UserStatus.email_is_free`) now uses `iexact`, so signup and change email refuse `Mike@` when `mike@` exists.

There is no `Lower("email")` unique constraint and no data migration. A unique index on the lower-cased email should fail to build while the existing duplicate accounts are in the table. I have not tried it against a copy of the real data. Django admin login is not changed and still matches emails exactly.

One question from my comment on the issue is still open: this lower-cases the whole address. Would you rather keep the mailbox part as typed? If so, only `normalise_email()` changes, and the lookups stay case-insensitive.

I wrote this with help from Claude Code. I reviewed the change, and the runs below are from my machine.

## Testing

12 new tests: 8 in `users/test/test_schema.py`, 3 in `bookings/test/test_mutations.py` and 1 in `productions/test/test_mutations.py`. The command below selects exactly those 12. With the source files from `dev` (f43bbcc), 10 of them fail. Two examples are shown, and the other 8 FAILED lines are cut: the second signup with `mike@` succeeds after `Mike@`, and a comp for `ABC@Email.com` goes to a new user instead of `abc@email.com`.

```
$ make test-v path="uobtheatre/users/test/test_schema.py uobtheatre/bookings/test/test_mutations.py uobtheatre/productions/test/test_mutations.py" test="email_case or lower_case or differs_by_case or case_variant or exact_email or exact_target"
FAILED uobtheatre/users/test/test_schema.py::test_register_rejects_email_that_only_differs_by_case - assert True is False
FAILED uobtheatre/bookings/test/test_mutations.py::test_create_comp_booking_finds_target_user_whatever_the_email_case - AssertionError: assert 'ABC@Email.com' == 'abc@email.com'
=========== 10 failed, 2 passed, 166 deselected, 3 warnings in 1.22s ===========
```

The 2 that pass on `dev` check that an exact match wins when two accounts differ only by case. With `get_by_email()` changed to a plain `iexact` lookup, the same command gives `2 failed, 10 passed, 166 deselected`, and the 2 failures are those two tests. On this branch:

```
$ make test-v path="uobtheatre/users/test/test_schema.py uobtheatre/bookings/test/test_mutations.py uobtheatre/productions/test/test_mutations.py" test="email_case or lower_case or differs_by_case or case_variant or exact_email or exact_target"
================ 12 passed, 166 deselected, 6 warnings in 1.27s ================
```

`make pr` on this branch, with the container start lines, the isort and black banners and the per-file coverage table cut:

```
$ make pr
Successfully dumped GraphQL schema to schema.graphql
Skipped 1 files
386 files left unchanged.
Your code has been rated at 10.00/10
Success: no issues found in 376 source files
TOTAL                                                                                                  5925      0    890      0   100%
Required test coverage of 100% reached. Total coverage: 100.00%
========= 1278 passed, 2 skipped, 3 deselected, 126 warnings in 45.27s =========
$ git status --short
(no output)
```

An earlier `make pr` run on the same commit failed one other test, `test_create_booking_with_too_many_tickets[True]`, which does not use `userEmail`. I think the cause is its venue: it gets a random `internal_capacity` from `Faker("pyint")` (0 to 9999), and a value of 10 or less leaves no room for the test's 11 tickets. I could not recover the failed run's random data, so this is the likely cause, not a proven one. With the capacity forced to 10 the test fails the same way. On its own it passed 20 runs out of 20, and it passed in the run above.

## PR Links

- Resolves #834
- [uobtheatre-web#637](https://github.com/BristolSTA/uobtheatre-web/issues/637), the web issue that was moved here

author: harahu
body:
Rubric review of `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Haar.lean`.

**Generalize and move**
- `isMulRightInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure` and `isInvInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure` now take `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` instead of `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` and are renamed `..._of_isFiniteMeasure`. This is a real generalization: for example, Mathlib's un-normalized `Measure.haar` on a compact group is now covered.
- Both now follow from a new lemma, `isMulLeftInvariant_eq_of_measure_univ_eq`: a left-invariant measure with the same total mass as a finite Haar measure equals it. It generalizes Mathlib's `isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure` and is proved from `isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace`. The first measure only needs to be left-invariant; its finiteness follows from the equal total mass. The inversion proof also no longer builds `IsHaarMeasure μ.inv` field by field.
- These three lemmas are generic measure theory, so they now live in `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/Unique.lean`, in the `MeasureTheory.Measure` namespace, each with an additive version from `@[to_additive]`. `Compact/Haar.lean` imports that module. That module's docstring now covers them, and its title is now "Consequences of the uniqueness of Haar measure".

**Reuse**
- `haarProb` is now defined directly as `(haar univ)⁻¹ • haar`. That is already the statement of `haarProb_def`. This removes the private `haarFinite`, `haarFinite_toMeasure` and `haarFinite_ne_zero`, along with the `FiniteMeasure.normalize` detour and the `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure` import. `IsProbabilityMeasure` now comes from Mathlib's `isProbabilityMeasureSMul`.
- Removed declarations that duplicated Mathlib (none had callers outside this file, except the last one):
  - `haar_univ_ne_zero`: same as `NeZero.ne (haar univ)`
  - `haar_univ_lt_top`: same as `measure_lt_top`
  - `haarProb_apply_univ`: same as `measure_univ`
  - the `isMulLeftInvariant_haarProb` instance: already given by `IsHaarMeasure`
  - `eq_haarProb_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure`: a one-line wrapper of `Measure.isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure`. Its only caller, `haarProb_eq_haarAddCircle` in `Compact/Circle.lean`, now uses the Mathlib lemma directly.

**Documentation**
- Removed the roadmap and "Layer 0" paragraph from the module docstring (documentation rubric). The docstring now points to the finite-measure invariance lemmas.

Builds: both edited modules, the direct importers of `MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/Unique.lean`, and all 71 transitive importers of `Compact/Haar.lean` within `TauCeti/` build.

Roadmap: RepresentationTheory

author: injaneity
body:
## Why
pi sessions working in a trycua/cua checkout never see its verify skills, because pi loads skills from packages, `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, and never from `.cursor/skills/`. Shipping a copy in zstack makes them load on every host with the package installed.

## What changed
- `skills/cua/verify-cua-driver` and `skills/cua/verify-cua-spaces`: the Markdown files from trycua/cua `.cursor/skills/` at `53ad9e23e7ecc8a3ff70bcb143e3bbe2909e24aa` (which includes trycua/cua#6898), byte for byte.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`: the frontmatter and name checks also cover `skills/cua/*/SKILL.md`. The copied text gets the same link-only treatment as pstack's verbatim skills.
- README and `docs/PROVENANCE.md` say where the copy came from, why `scripts/` stays in the cua checkout, how its `libs/` links resolve, and how to refresh it.

## Scope
Covers the two skills' text. The scripts are left out: `verify-linux.sh`, `verify-macos.sh` and `spaces-desk.sh` find the repo root four directories above themselves, and the skills already call them from the cua checkout root. trycua/cua stays the source of truth.

## Blast Radius
Hosts pick the skills up on their next launch, once `bin/ensure-package-main` fast-forwards the package. pi's loader recurses into `skills/cua/`. Sessions outside a cua checkout will list two more skills, and those skills match only on cua-driver and Cua Spaces work.

## Verification
- pi's `loadSkillsFromDir` on `skills/` lists `verify-cua-driver` and `verify-cua-spaces` with no diagnostics.
- The workflow's doc-check steps pass, and still fail when a missing skill is named. The unittest suite passes.
- Running the refresh snippet in a temp copy reproduces `skills/cua` with no diff.

author: erickb336
body:
## What this changes

In a shared logbook, any chief may now abandon a task that has no owning chief, with a reason. It needs no claim and no takeover gate, because the abandon gives the task to no chief (owner's decision, 2026-11-08). This lets the chief close the 26 stale tasks that the move brought from the Codex logbooks with one decision, not 26 gates.

- Claude: `sage task <T> set state=abandoned --why "<reason>" --chief C<n>`.
- Codex: `task_set` with `fields` `{"state": "abandoned"}` and `why`. The server passes `--why` to the same core rule; the provider has no copy of it.

## Rules (in core, `packages/sage-core/state.mjs`)

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Task with no owning chief, `state=abandoned` alone, `--why` with text | Passes, from any chief. The task keeps no chief. The decision row `state abandoned` keeps the reason and the chief, for example `stale · abandoned by C1, with no owning chief`. |
| Same, with no `--why`, or an empty or blank one | Refuses: `T1 has no owning chief. Any chief may abandon it, with a reason: add --why "<reason>". Nothing changed.` |
| Any other change of a task with no owning chief, also `state=abandoned` together with another field | Refuses with the claim, as before. |
| A task of another chief | Refuses with the takeover gate, as before. |
| A lead | Refuses, as before: a lead writes only while its chief owns the task. |
| `--why` without `state=abandoned` | Refuses: `--why` is the reason of an abandon. On an owned task, an abandon with `--why` keeps the reason too. |

The Claude hook does not refuse the command before it reaches the state tool. A test now checks that the hook gives a quoted `--why` the plain form's result.

## Tests

- `scripts/chiefs.test.mjs`: `T893 Claude` (a Claude chief abandons a moved Codex task) and `T893 Codex` (a Codex chief abandons a moved Claude task). Each test also checks the refusals for no reason, every other field and another chief's task.
- `scripts/codex-state-mcp.test.mjs`: `T893`, through the Codex server's `task_set`.
- The new tests fail on the base `afb1a925` and pass on this head.

## Docs

- `docs/guide/using-sage.md`: one row in the shared-logbook rules.
- `docs/guide/codex.md`: one line in the logbook tools reference.
- The skill text of `claim` and `task set` in both providers.
- `changes/T893.md`. CHANGELOG.md is not changed.

body:
Three fixes for 1.0.2.

## 1. Monthly Pro as a real subscription
In production, 1.0.1's paywall shows only Lifetime.

The Monthly product in App Store Connect was created as a regular **in-app purchase** with the ID `app.taskwall.pro.month`, not as an auto-renewable subscription. The ID the app asks for, `app.taskwall.pro.monthly`, can't be used for a new subscription: it is already taken by a deleted product, and Apple never lets a deleted product's ID be used again.

- **New ID.** `ProPlan.MONTHLY` now uses **`app.taskwall.pro.sub.monthly`**, as does the StoreKit test file. The README notes why the ID changed.
- **Tests.** The Kotlin test checks the new ID, and that the old one maps to nothing.
- **In App Store Connect:** create the subscription `app.taskwall.pro.sub.monthly` (1 month, $1.99) in the "Wallist Pro" group, attach it to version 1.0.2 with this build, and take `app.taskwall.pro.month` off sale.

## 2. Swap the wallpaper photo
Once a photo was the wallpaper, tapping its swatch did nothing. The only way to change it was Adjust photo › Replace photo, which sits under the Update Lock Screen button.

- **Second tap.** Tapping the photo that's already selected now opens the photo picker, in the Wallpaper sheet and in onboarding.
- **Badge.** The selected photo carries a small badge.
- **VoiceOver.** It hears "Choose another photo".

## 3. Bottom bar stays put while typing a task
With the New task sheet and its keyboard open, Today's Wallpaper, + and Settings bar rode up and sat over the week strip. Today's `GeometryReader` read the keyboard as part of its safe area.

- Today now uses `.ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard)`. The composer sheet still moves with the keyboard.

## Version
`MARKETING_VERSION` 1.0.1 → **1.0.2**. An app's first subscription has to be reviewed together with a new app version, and this build carries it.

author: sgrastar
body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to #791, requested by the parent session. It runs #791's creation operation compare-and-sets on real PostgreSQL in the **AWS Runtime PostgreSQL Tests** CI job. That job picks up this file on its own because the file reads `AUTHRIM_AWS_TEST_DATABASE_URL`.

**Stacked on #791.** Until #791 merges, the diff also shows #791's commit. The only change of its own is `packages/ar-runtime-aws/src/dsql/account-creation-abandon.postgres.test.ts`.

### What it tests (`AccountCreationOperationRepository` through ar-lib-core's `PostgresAdapter`)
The test creates a fresh database and applies every fresh-install core migration. It then checks:
- **A resume's `touch`** moves `updated_at` to now and never later, however often it is resumed.
- **`abandon` gives up an operation only as it was read.** An operation that a resume moved after the read is kept. When it is read again it is given up, and a later resume is refused (`account_creation_operation_blocked`).
- **An operation blocked for another reason is finalised.** This covers the worker's retry budget used up, and a null error code. It is the null-safe compare `COALESCE(last_error_code, '') = ?` from #791 R5.
  - With the earlier `last_error_code IS ?`, PostgreSQL rejects the statement (`syntax error at or near "$5"`), and this test fails. I checked that locally.

### Not covered on PostgreSQL
`insertPreparedUnpublishedAccountRemovals` has no PostgreSQL path to test. The PostgreSQL core has no `account_routing_outbox`, because directory routing runs on Cloudflare only. Its transaction semantics stay covered by the mocked Aurora DSQL test in #791.

## Codex review (gpt-6.1-sol, high, read-only)
| Round | Findings | Fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | 0 (one coverage note) | added the null error code case |

## Test plan
- [x] Local PostgreSQL 17 (`postgres:17` container): 4 passed. Reverting the compare to `IS ?` fails the null-safe case.
- [x] With no database URL, the file is skipped. The CI job sets the URL and fails on any skipped test.

author: guccyon
body:
Closes #1080

## 概要
K-0004 の担保（議決 `D-0037`）を ci_check で入れました。`test_engine.py` は `ENGINE_DIR` を渡したときも CI と同じように、`ENGINE_REF` の版や pytest がなければ飛ばさずに落ちます。CI のひな形 `ci/knowledge-enforcement.yml` は `unittest discover` の出力を見て、`skipped` が 1 件以上あれば落とします。

## 対応内容
- `tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/test_engine.py`: Engine のチェックアウトに `ENGINE_REF` の版がないときと、pytest がないときに落とす条件を `IN_CI` から `REQUIRED`（`ENGINE_DIR` を渡したか `CI=true`）に広げた。
  - Engine のチェックアウトがないときに落とすのは前から `REQUIRED` で決まっていたので、変えていない。
  - 版がないときのメッセージに、手元では `git -C "$ENGINE_DIR" fetch` でその版を取ることを足した。
- `tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/ci/knowledge-enforcement.yml` の `engine-test` のジョブ:
  - 2 つのテストファイルを名指しで走らせるのをやめた。代わりに `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/knowledge-enforcement-check -v` を `shell: bash`・`set -o pipefail` で走らせ、出力を `tee knowledge-enforcement-unittest.log` に残す。
  - そのすぐ後に「飛ばしたテストがないか」の手順を足した。出力の要約の `skipped=` が 1 件以上なら `tests_skipped` で落とし、飛ばしたテストの一覧も出す。走らせたテストの件数（`Ran N tests`、N ≥ 1）が出ていなければ `unittest_not_run` で落とす。
- `tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/test_ci.py`:
  - `problems()` が見る形を足した。discover を `-s tools/knowledge-enforcement-check` で走らせる、`-p`・`-k` で絞らない、`tee` で出力を残す、pipefail を効かせる、すぐ後に `skipped=` を見る手順が bash で 1 つある、の 5 つ。
  - 形から外れた写しの例を 15 とおりから 22 とおりにした。名指しの 2 件を discover の場合に置き換え、絞る・出力を残さない・pipefail なし・件数の手順がない・件数の手順がすぐ後でない・件数の手順に `continue-on-error:` がある、などを足した。
  - `skipped=` を見る手順を本物の bash で走らせるテストを足した。作った出力を渡し、飛ばしたかテストが走っていないときだけ落ちることを確かめる。渡す出力は、`skipped` なし・あり・失敗と一緒・`expected failures` だけ・0 件・`NO TESTS RAN`・出力なし。
- `tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/README.md`: 上の振る舞い・ジョブの形・検査の中身を書き足し、件数を 22 とおりに直した。
- `.factory-config/knowledge/K-0004.yaml`: `enforcement.solutions` に 1 件足した（`kind: ci_check`、`issue: 1080`、`at: 2026-11-08`、`decided_by: committee:D-0037`、`wired: false`、`verified: false`）。
  - 強さは前から `level: deterministic` なので変えていない。今ある記述は消していない。

## 影響範囲・互換性
- 手元で `ENGINE_DIR` を渡したのに、そのチェックアウトに `ENGINE_REF`（`9d3713a`）の版がないと、今後は落ちる。これまではチェックアウトの今の中身で確かめて通っていた（`test_engine_patch.py` は前から落ちる）。
- `ENGINE_DIR` を渡さず `../engine` を使う手元の振る舞いは変わらない。
- ひな形は `.github/workflows/` にまだ写していないので、PR ごとの CI の振る舞いは変わらない。利用者に見える変更がないので `changelog.d` は足していない。

## 動作確認
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/knowledge-enforcement-check -v`: 59 件が通った（skipped=3）。
  - 飛んだ 3 件は、写しがない・pytest がない・`ENGINE_REF` の版がない、で、どれも `ENGINE_DIR` を渡していない手元の場合。
- `ENGINE_DIR=/work/engine` を渡して同じものを走らせた: `test_engine.py` の setUpClass が `ENGINE_REF` の版がないことで飛ばさずに落ちた（`test_engine_patch.py` も落ちた）。
- 一時的なラッパーで `engine_ref()` を `/work/engine` の HEAD に差し替え、`ENGINE_DIR` を渡して `test_engine.py` を走らせた: 8 件のうち 7 件が通った。pytest がないテストは skip ではなく fail になった。
- 上の手元の discover の出力（skipped=3）に、ひな形の「飛ばしたテストがないか」の手順を bash `-eo pipefail` で当てた: `tests_skipped` を出して終了コード 1 になった。
- `yq eval .` でひな形と K-0004.yaml が読めることを確かめた。
- `python3 /work/engine/core-gates/knowledge_check.py --repo . --index` は終了コード 0 で、`INDEX.md` は変わらなかった。`--index` なしの検査もエラー 0 件だった。
- `python3 tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/check.py --repo .`: エラー 0 件。

## 補足
- `ENGINE_REF` の版の Engine と pytest で通るかは確かめていない。手元の Engine にその版がなく、この環境には pytest がない。
- `.github/workflows/` への写しと必須チェックへの登録は建設者の作業なので、行っていない。そのため解決策は `wired: false`・`verified: false` にした。
- `enforcement` のジョブ（`test_check.py`・`test_ci.py` を名指しで走らせる）には `skipped` の検査を足していない。案が指しているのは discover の出力で、この 2 つのテストは `engine-test` の discover でも走る。

## 仮決め
### error_handling e1: ENGINE_DIR を渡したのに ENGINE_REF の版がないとき、今の中身で確かめるか落とすか
- 選んだ: 落とす（CI と同じ扱い）。`ENGINE_DIR` を渡さず `../engine` を使う手元だけ、今の中身で確かめる。pytest がないときも同じ線にした
- 他の案: これまでどおり CI でだけ落とし、`ENGINE_DIR` を渡した手元では今の中身で確かめる
- 根拠: Issue #1080 の「担保の案」、`tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/README.md` の「Engine に移す差分」と「差分が古くなっていないか（`patch_stale`）」
- 解釈: 案の「CI か ENGINE_DIR を渡したときは…ENGINE_REF の版がなくても skip せずに落とす」をそのまま読んだ。`test_engine_patch.py` も `ENGINE_DIR` を渡すと落ちるので、2 つのテストの線がそろう
- 確信度: 0.7
- 影響: `test_engine.py`、README。手元で `ENGINE_DIR` を使うときは、その版を fetch しておく必要がある
- チケットの解釈: はい

### implementation i1: skipped の検査をどこに置き、どう走らせるか
- 選んだ: `engine-test` のテストの手順を `unittest discover` にまとめ、出力をログに残す。すぐ後の別の手順が、その要約の `skipped=` を数える。テストが 0 件のときも落とす
- 他の案: 名指しの 2 本を残してそれぞれの出力を見る／`enforcement` のジョブに discover を足す
- 根拠: Issue #1080 の案（「unittest discover の出力で skipped が 1 件以上あれば落とす手順を足す」）、README の「配線先の照合」（discover も呼び出しに数える）
- 解釈: 案が discover の出力を名指ししている。discover なら `check.py` の照合でも 2 つのテストを呼んでいると数えられる。tee で失敗が隠れないように pipefail を必須にした
- 確信度: 0.75
- 影響: `ci/knowledge-enforcement.yml`、`test_ci.py`。建設者が写すときのジョブの形が変わる

## 知見
- `check.py` の照合は、`unittest discover -s <dir>` を `-p`・`-k` で絞っていても、そのディレクトリのテストを呼んだと数える。そのため絞り込みは `test_ci.py` の `problems()` の側で落としている
- 手元の `/work/engine` には `ENGINE_REF`（`9d3713a`）の版がない。今は `ENGINE_DIR=/work/engine` を渡すと `test_engine.py` と `test_engine_patch.py` が両方落ちる
- この環境には pytest がなく、pip でも入れられない（ネットワークなし）

## 工場の記録
- job: 5702（attempt は dispatcher の記録を参照）
- model: claude-opus-5-5、turns: 13、cost(API 換算): $0.612362
- 権限: P0 は PR 作成まで。マージは人間の判断（manifest.yaml autonomy）

## 続きのジョブの記録

<details><summary>既定ブランチの取り込みと衝突の解消（job 5719、turns 10、$0.318585）</summary>

取り込みの衝突を解消しました。衝突の印は残っておらず、取り込みは中止していません。コミットはしていません。

## 概要
既定ブランチを取り込んだときに 2 つのファイルが衝突したので、両方の変更を残して解消しました。どちらも同じ議決 `D-0037` の別の案の記録で、既定ブランチ側は #1079（test の案）、このブランチ側は #1080（ci_check の案）です。

## 対応内容
- `.factory-config/knowledge/K-0004.yaml`: `enforcement.solutions` の末尾が衝突していました。既定ブランチの解決策（`kind: test`、issue 1079）のあとに、このブランチの解決策（`kind: ci_check`、issue 1080）を並べ、両方に `at`・`decided_by: committee:D-0037`・`wired: false`・`verified: false` を付けました。
- `tools/knowledge-enforcement-check/README.md`: `test_engine.py` を説明する段落が衝突していました。このブランチの文を土台にして、既定ブランチで足された変異体（`MUTANTS`）の説明（議決 `D-0037`、Issue #1079）を「議決 `D-0024`、Issue #1015」の直後に入れました。次の 2 つはこのブランチの書き方のまま残しています。
  - `ENGINE_DIR` を渡したときと CI では、`ENGINE_REF` の版や pytest がなくても飛ばさずに落とす、という記述
  - 「議決 `D-0035`・`D-0037`、Issue #1063・#1080」という表記
- `test_engine.py` は自動で取り込めていたので、手は入れていません。

## 影響範囲・互換性
- 変わったのは知見の記録と README だけです。担保の仕組みのコードはどちらの側の内容も変えていません。
- 既定ブランチから来た `D-0055.yaml` と、このブランチで付け直した `D-0056.yaml` は番号が別なので、そのまま両方残っています。

## 動作確認
- `yq eval . .factory-config/knowledge/K-0004.yaml` で読めることを確かめました。
- 2 つのファイルに衝突の印が残っていないことを確かめました。
- `python3 /work/engine/core-gates/knowledge_check.py --repo . --index` は rc=0 で通りました（knowledge 14 件、議決 56 件、エラー 0 件）。作り直しても `INDEX.md` に差分は出ていません。
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/knowledge-enforcement-check` は `Ran 60 tests`・`OK (skipped=3)` でした。既定ブランチで足された変異体のテストも、この取り込み後のコードで走っています。
  - 飛ばした 3 件は手元の環境によるもので、取り込みとは関係ありません。
    - `.github/workflows/` にまだ写していない（写すのは建設者）
    - pytest がない
    - `/work/engine` に `ENGINE_REF`（`9d3713a`）の版がない

## 知見
- K-0004 の `enforcement.solutions` は議決ごとに項目を末尾に足していくので、同じ議決の別の案を並行して取り込むと必ず末尾で衝突します。両方の項目を並べれば解消できます。

- model: claude-opus-5-5
</details>

## 背景
- K-0004 の担保として、議決 `D-0037` が `ci_check` の案を決めた（Issue #1080）。案の中身は、`test_engine.py` が CI だけでなく `ENGINE_DIR` を渡したときも、Engine のチェックアウトや `ENGINE_REF` の版がなければ飛ばさずに落とすこと。もう 1 つは、CI のひな形が `unittest discover` の出力で `skipped` が 1 件以上あれば落とすこと。
- `ENGINE_REF` の版がないときと pytest がないときに落とす条件は、これまで `IN_CI`（CI だけ）だった。`ENGINE_DIR` を渡した手元では、チェックアウトの今の中身で確かめて通る、または pytest を飛ばす形になっていた。
- `engine-test` のジョブは、`test_engine_patch.py` と `test_engine.py` を名指しで走らせていた。この形では、テストが飛ばされても出力を見る手順がなく、緑になりうる。

## 問題
- `ENGINE_DIR` を渡しても、`ENGINE_REF` の版がなければ今の中身で通り、pytest がなければ飛ばされた。製品の CI が使う版で確かめたことにならないまま、結果が通る。
- CI のジョブには、テストが飛ばされたことを検出する手順がなかった。飛ばす条件を取りこぼすと、テストが走らないまま緑になる。
- tee で出力を残すと、パイプの途中の失敗が隠れる。pipefail を必須にして、`test_ci.py` で形を見る必要がある。

上の「対応内容」は、この 3 点への対応である。読む順は、概要 → 背景 → 問題 → 対応内容になる。

author: ihid
body:
Currently, "required checks" on PRs are hidden from maintainers, and can get out of sync with the reality of a repo. To fix this, we're adding a `.github/required-checks.yml` file, which lists the checks that must pass before a PR can merge into main. 

When this file is changed, the ruleset that manages branch protection automatically gets synced up. The new `Required checks` workflow checks that all the checks listed in `required-checks.yml` exist.

_(Sidenote: I'm increasingly wary of agents that have access to GitHub mistakenly (or potentially nefariously) doing things that could do us damage or cause us to have unexpected or high costs. That's why I'm using CODEOWNERS on a more frequent basis for files that are always worth just getting a second pair of eyes on. It's not a reflection on trust for maintainers 🙂)_

The file adds the following Required Checks:

- `Check / Check exercises`
- `configlet / configlet`
- `i18n / completeness`
- `Validate required checks` (rather recursively, I admit!)

For many repos (including Racket), the exercise tests are named with version (e.g. `Racket 9.2` and `Racket 9.3`). Those names change whenever a version is bumped, which is quite unstable, and then the required checks break. I'm going to fix that separately by adding a check with a more standard name (e.g. "tests"), which can rely on the unstably named tests, and add that to this file. That'll be a separate PR.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"akaza21"} -->
_Requested by **Pragyash** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AueZUKyiAh3ya1hnquwjZE?thread=cmsg_01AueZUKyiAh3ya1hnquwjZEFgP11txnrCkyctzU61wJVD)_

## Outcome

Fixes the intermittent loss of captured diagnostics in unit tests. Under load, `browser_mcp_tests::{browser_startup_warning_is_emitted_once_for_accepted_failure, browser_failure_before_first_prompt_is_reported_once_after_turn_bind}` and some `hard_failure_tests` failed because their captured log was empty.

## Scope

Test code only. New `#[cfg(test)]` module `src-tauri/src/test_diagnostics.rs`; the codex test helpers, `acp/fixture/host/redaction_observer.rs` tests and `browser/passwords/clipboard.rs` tests now capture through it. No production behaviour changes.

## Architecture and invariants

**Root cause.** The old helper installed a global subscriber whose filter was `filter_fn(|_| this thread is capturing)`. In tracing-subscriber 0.3.23, `FilterFn::is_callsite_enabled` (`filter/filter_fn.rs:293-311`) runs that closure once, when the callsite registers, and caches `Interest::always`/`never` process-wide. If a non-capturing test thread reaches a `warn!` first (for example another browser-helper test), that callsite becomes `never` for the whole process and every later capture of it is empty. The old comment claimed the filter kept callsites at `sometimes`; it didn't. The scoped `with_default` subscribers in the clipboard and redaction tests had the standard cross-thread interest race too.

**Fix.**
- One global subscriber, installed once via `OnceLock`; if `set_global_default` fails the test panics instead of falling back to a racy scoped subscriber.
- A per-layer `Filter` that answers `Interest::sometimes` for every callsite and decides each event from the current thread's capture route, so parallel tests never see each other's output.
- `capture_diagnostics` / `capture_matching(admit)`; nested captures panic without disturbing the outer one; each capture keeps at most 1 MiB; thread-local access uses `try_with` so logging during thread teardown can't abort.
- No `with_default`, `set_default` or `set_global_default` remains in test code. Production's `initialize_tracing` is only called from `run()`, which no unit test calls.

## Tests

Proof against the old code: a temporary test that reached a `warn!` callsite on another thread before capturing it on the test thread failed 11 of 11 runs, with the global capture installed each time. It was then kept as a cheap regression test (`callsite_first_reached_on_another_thread_is_still_captured`), alongside `other_threads_do_not_reach_this_capture`.

Stress, same binary, `--test-threads=64`, 4 CPUs:

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `acp::bindings::codex` × 30 | 13 failed | 0 failed |
| `acp::fixture acp::bindings::codex` × 3 | 2 failed | 0 failed |

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     pass
cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings (default features)      pass
cargo clippy --all-targets --features <lint set> -D warnings   pass
cargo test --features <test set> --lib                         3872 passed, 13 failed (container-only: root, ssh, gpg, IPv6, PTY/helper-process/ambient-git under contention; those pass alone)
cargo test ... test_diagnostics acp::bindings::codex redaction clipboard (after review nits)   488 passed
npm run check                                                  pass
```

## Resource impact

| Metric | Base | Change | Delta | Budget |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Per-capture buffer (tests only) | unbounded | ≤1 MiB | bounded | n/a |

## Security, data, and recovery

Not applicable: test-only.

## Known limitations

The redaction observer test now asserts the 64 KiB bound directly instead of relying on a writer that silently dropped excess bytes.

## Review hotspots

`test_diagnostics.rs` (`CapturingThread::callsite_enabled`, `install`).

## Checklist

- [x] Acceptance criteria map to evidence.
- [x] One active writer owned this checkout.
- [x] Tests cover changed behavior.
- [x] Evidence identifies the exact source/artifact and distinguishes self-check from independent verification.
- [x] Failure and recovery behavior were exercised.
- [x] Migration, rollback, and cross-platform impact are covered or marked not applicable with a reason (test-only).
- [x] CSP and Tauri capabilities remain narrow.
- [x] No unbounded queue, list, scan, or transcript was introduced.

Follow-ups to #1977, which has merged. Based on main 649f3a46c.

## For users

- Export plate 3MF stays off, with the collision named, when a slice that struck is followed by a rename. Before, the item turned on, sliced the plate again and then refused. A click on the held back item in the Export menu now does nothing, as in the footer.
- No change in speed. The startup script is 213.5 KB gzip at the head, under its 217 KB budget.

## For integrators

- `app_slice` waits for an auto slice that has started but is still loading the printer profile, instead of giving up after its one second grace. That holds when auto slice cancels one run and starts another.
- A slice the engine refuses comes back from `app_slice` with `status: "error"`, its message and any `code`. A Slice that ends with nothing sliced, or fails before it slices, answers `not_ready`. The tool description and docs/agent-bridge.md now say this.
- `app_state` leaves the last slice's warnings off the plate after a rename or a layer mark change.
- `slicerx_app_ui` 1.1.1 and `slicerx_app_collision_show` 1.0.1 report `collisions.stale` as true after a rename or a layer mark change, matching the plates list and `app_export_gcode` (packages/mcp/changes/fix-manual-layer-height-followups.md).

## Changes

- plate/heimdall.ts: `export3mfBlock` runs the slice's own checks (a strike) when the only other reason is the reslice it does itself. A slice already marked stale reads as it did in #1977.
- workspaces/prepare/object-actions.tsx: Sliced plate as .gcode.3mf runs only when nothing holds it back.
- state/auto-slice.ts: `autoSlicePending()` stays true from the moment auto slice starts a slice until that slice runs or gives up. Each run keeps its own start, so a canceled run never clears a newer one's.
- agent-bridge/page.ts, app-link/ui.ts: the warnings and the collisions readback read `needsSlice`. `sliceSummary` takes the whole app state.
- apps/web/scripts/bundle-size.mjs takes a build folder. A new script test runs it on small builds: under the budget it passes, over it fails, and a lazy chunk does not count. An app test keeps the startup modules reading plates from plate/all-plates.ts.

## Testing

- New tests in resume-stamp.test.ts, resume-waits.test.ts, startup-imports.test.ts, packages/mcp/test/app-ui.test.ts and apps/web/scripts/bundle-size.test.mjs. The behavior tests failed before their fix.
- packages/app (all files), the MCP app tests, app-bridge, ui, the script tests, the MCP change file check, tsc and the bundle budget pass. The e2e journeys for the color change note, the Simple sidebar fit and the Print split button pass.

author: fitchmultz
body:
## Summary

- Removes the fork-only `discover_tools` builtin (`extensions/instruction-groups/`), its `instructionGroupsExtension` export, its docs page and its tests.
- Removes the saved-deferral bookkeeping from `AgentSession`: the `pi:instruction-groups` deferral lists, the run-start retirement and the reload fallback. Transcript restore is upstream's `_restoreToolsFromTranscript` again.
- Removes the fork-only `pi.refreshTools()` extension method and its `preserveSelection` path. Official 1.5.0 has neither, and no maintained extension calls it. The internal runtime `refreshTools` stays.
- Extensions keep optional tools out of the prompt with native `exposure: "deferred"`, and `tool_search` loads them on demand. The browser, macuse, MCP adapter and pstack extensions already use that.

## Old sessions on resume

A scan of 3,124 local journals with `pi:instruction-groups` entries:

- 3,028: the deferred tools were never declared on the branch, so they come back as newly registered tools. This matches the old eager fallback.
- 86: the last deferral list was empty.
- 10: a deferred tool had been declared earlier. It now stays inactive like any other recorded removal; `--tools +name` turns it back on, and `tool_search` loads it when the tool is deferred.

## Managed restarts across tool removals

A restored working session refused every request while any saved tool was unregistered. After an update that removes a tool, such as `discover_tools` here or a tool an extension update drops, the tool never registers, so `pi restart` left the session unable to prompt. A restored session now refuses a run only while saved MCP tools are pending, because those reconnect natively. Other saved tools stay pending without holding requests: a request runs without them, and one an extension registers later, such as a pi-mcp-adapter catalog tool whose server connects after the first request, comes back when it registers. A tool that never registers stays unavailable.

## Verification

- `prompt-cache-prefix.test.ts` now covers the stable cache prefix with a deferred tool loaded through `tool_search`.
- `working-session.test.ts` restores, through the real SDK, a session saved with a direct tool the restored runtime no longer registers and a deferred tool an extension registers only after the first request. The original code refuses the prompt with `Saved tools have not registered: retired`; clearing pending names at the first run instead loses the late tool. The new code runs both requests, declares the late tool once it registers, and still refuses while an MCP tool is pending.
- coding-agent suite: 385 files passed, 7 skipped (`./test.sh -- npm test -w packages/coding-agent`).
- `npm run check` steps: biome, pinned/runtime deps, TS imports, entry graphs, install lock, examples typecheck and browser smoke pass. `tsc --noEmit` reports 9 errors, all in `packages/ai/test/fireworks-models.test.ts` and `packages/ai/test/anthropic-empty-thinking-signature-compat.test.ts`. The gitignored Fireworks catalog regenerated from the live API no longer lists `nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4`. This PR changes no `packages/ai` files.

author: fredj1996
body:
> Stacked on #81. GitHub shows those commits too until they are merged; only the last commit is new here.

## Summary

"Stop sync" only ends the binding, so the album's photos stay in the folder and on the frame. Moving a frame to a new album meant removing them one by one.

```text
<FolderSync> (frontend/src/components/LibraryTab.tsx)
  kept in sync:  Change album | Stop sync | Empty folder
    Change album → [album] Replace folder | Add photos only
  not in sync:   [album] Keep in sync | Add once | Replace folder | Empty folder
```

```text
POST /frames/{id}/folders/empty {folder}
  end the folder's binding              # or the next sync refills it
  remove every photo in the folder + cached image + queued delivery
  LAN frame: delete the files, best-effort

POST /frames/{id}/folders/replace-album {folder, album_id}   # background job
  reconcile the album into the folder   # Immich fails → nothing changed
  swap the binding to this album
  remove the folder's other photos
  queue and deliver the delta           # photos in both stay on the frame
```

"Add photos only" is the existing one-time add: a folder follows one album, because each reconcile replaces the folder's sync rows. Both destructive buttons use the inline two-step `ConfirmButton`. Immich is never touched. The folder name travels in the body because album-style names contain slashes.

## Evidence

- `tests/test_backend_api.py`:
  - `test_empty_folder_removes_its_photos_and_ends_the_binding` — a folder named `2026/09 Italien`: synced and hand-added photos leave, another folder stays, no binding is left, files are deleted on the device.
  - `test_replace_album_leaves_only_the_new_album_in_the_folder` — a photo in both albums stays, the old album's and hand-added photos leave, one binding remains.
  - `test_replace_album_keeps_the_folder_when_immich_fails` — photos and the old binding are unchanged.
  - `test_adding_an_album_to_a_bound_folder_survives_the_next_sync`.

author: koolkdev
body:
Bumpy requests PIT0 interrupts at about 500 Hz, but native Windows timed parking wakes around every 15–16 ms. The timer worker introduced in #941 therefore still synchronizes the PIT too late and collapses elapsed edges.

Use a Windows high-resolution waitable timer for deadlines and an auto-reset event for new requests, cancellation, and shutdown. Retain ordinary Rust parking on other platforms and when the Windows handles cannot be created. This is the first PR in the timer stack. The Windows browser backend is stacked on this branch in #944; macOS and Linux retain their existing parking paths.

The private `clock/driver/wait` module owns the platform wait and retained notification. Its Windows child owns all Win32 handles and unsafe calls. The existing `Clock`, timer handles, worker lifecycle, PIT, and interrupt waker interfaces are unchanged. The shared driver now uses:

```rust
let wait = wait::Wait::new();
let mut context = Context::from_waker(wait.waker());
// Poll requests, cancellation, and expiration, then:
wait.until(timers.iter().map(|timer| timer.deadline).min());
```

An instrumented Bumpy experiment, measured over a 10-second music-menu window on Windows, produced:

| Measurement | Rust parking | High-resolution timer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| IRQ0 deliveries per second | 69.2 | 500.1 |
| Median PIT0 edge interval | 15.746 ms | 1.998 ms |
| Median speaker port-write interval | 77.108 ms | 9.995 ms |

These are observations from one machine, not hard real-time guarantees. No missed PIC edges are replayed.

Validation: six clock lifecycle tests, the retained-notification test, and the PIT busy-guest delivery test passed on native Windows and Linux. Focused Clippy checks passed on both. The six clock tests also passed in Windows Chrome. Formatting and whitespace checks pass; independent review completed. Full suites are left to CI.

A dedicated Windows CI job was prepared locally but is not included: the current GitHub OAuth credential lacks the `workflow` scope required to publish workflow edits.

author: cyyeh
body:
## What

Each CLI's card in Settings gets **Leave out of Harness Relay's runs** at the top of "Skills, MCP servers and memory this CLI loads by itself": four switches for its own **Skills**, **MCP servers**, **Instruction files** and **Memory**.

- Each switch is saved as soon as it changes. The section's title shows how many are off.
- It applies to every run Harness Relay starts of that CLI: members' turns, the lead agent and the group sorter.
- The CLI's own settings files are never changed, so using it in a terminal is not affected. The tool library's items are still provided.
- The list below still shows everything the CLI loads by itself (the probe does not apply the switches). Opening the section no longer starts the CLI: it is asked only when **Ask** is clicked, so the switches can be changed without running its hooks or MCP servers.
- For Codex, **Skills**, **Instruction files** and **Memory** take effect in new chats: Codex records them when a thread starts and replays them on resume. **MCP servers** take effect at the next turn. Codex's card says so.
- When a CLI's skills are off, the briefing no longer tells the agent that its CLI's own skills work as usual.

## How each CLI leaves them out (one run only)

| | Skills | MCP servers | Instruction files | Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `--disable-slash-commands` | `--strict-mcp-config` (the tool library's `--mcp-config` stays) | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1` | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` |
| Codex (thread `config`) | `skills.include_instructions = false` | `enabled = false` for each configured server (from `config/read`), in one `mcp_servers` table that also holds the tool library's servers, plus `features.apps = false` | `project_doc_max_bytes = 0` (the project's `AGENTS.md`; `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is still read) | `features.memories = false` |
| Grok (environment) | `GROK_CLAUDE_/GROK_CURSOR_SKILLS_ENABLED=false`: only what it loads from Claude Code and Cursor | `GROK_CLAUDE_/GROK_CURSOR_MCPS_ENABLED=false`: likewise | no switch (greyed out with a note) | `GROK_MEMORY=0` |

Codex merges that `mcp_servers` table into the user's config, so their other servers stay. A table also reaches names such as `a.b`, which a dotted key cannot, because Codex splits dotted keys at every `.`. If `config/read` fails, the run fails with a translated message saying the servers could not be left out, instead of running them.

`NATIVE_OFF_SUPPORT` (`src/shared/types.ts`) lists what each CLI can leave out, and the server drops the rest. Grok's own skills and MCP servers can only be turned off in `~/.grok/config.toml`, which Harness Relay does not edit.

## Checked against the real CLIs (no model called)

Versions: Claude Code 2.1.319, Codex 0.167.0, Grok 1.0.77.

- **Claude Code:** `initialize` reports 20 → 0 skills/commands with `--disable-slash-commands`. With `--strict-mcp-config`, a project's `.mcp.json` server drops while the `--mcp-config` server stays. The two variables were confirmed in its code only, because observing their effect needs a model call.
- **Codex:** `thread/start` `instructionSources` loses the project's `AGENTS.md` with `project_doc_max_bytes=0`. Disabled MCP servers and `codex_apps` no longer start. With a temporary `CODEX_HOME`, a nested `mcp_servers` override turns off a server named `a.b` while the user's other servers still start, and a library server in the same table starts; `mcp_servers.a.b.enabled` (quoted or not) fails to load. `codex debug prompt-input` with `skills.include_instructions=false` no longer lists any skill. That last check used `-c`; the thread-level overrides above use the same config layers.

author: g-r-ay
body:
Closes #4071

## Review in two minutes

**What changed.** Each Vigil rule's row in the rule listing gains `stage_reason`, the `reason` on its current stage row. That's the same row the listing's `stage`, `stage_from` and `stage_actor` come from, in the same (at, id) order as `GET /rules/{id}/stages`. The console can then tell "new version · back in shadow for its week" apart from Vigil reverting a live rule, and word the row the way the bell does. SIEM rows are unchanged: no `stage_reason`.

**Try it.** `GET /api/detection-rules?rules=<id>` on a rule whose new version went back to shadow: `stage_reason` is `"new version"`. On one Vigil reverted, it is the revert's reason.

---

## Files

- `core/detections/inventory/catalog.py`:
  - `STAGE_ROWS` also selects `reason`.
  - `stage_moves` adds `stage_reason` from the newest row. An empty or null reason reads `""`.
- `tests/unit/test_rule_listing_stage_reason.py` (new): 7 tests, all failing on main.
  - The reason is the latest move's, for a new version, a Vigil revert and a person's revert.
  - A null reason reads empty.
  - Each rule has its own reason.
  - Vigil rows carry it; SIEM rows don't.
  - On Postgres, a row written last but stamped earlier doesn't win: the reason matches `stages.history`'s current row.
- `tests/unit/test_rule_listing_stage_moves.py`: rows are now 5-tuples, and the expected dicts include `stage_reason`.

## Checks

- `VIGIL_TEST_PG_DSN` set to a throwaway DB on a lab Postgres:
  - The new file passes 7 of 7 on this branch and fails 7 of 7 on main.
  - With `test_rule_listing_stage_moves`, `test_rule_listing_fresh_after_revert` and `test_bell_vigil_turned_off`: 24 passed.
- Next: #4032 reads `stage_reason`, so the row says "New version · back in shadow for its week" like the bell.

body:
## Summary

**Filter dropdown sat on top of the chips (Android)**
- **Cause:** a chip's position is measured from below the status bar, but the dropdown's `statusBarTranslucent` Modal starts at the very top of the screen. So the dropdown was drawn one status-bar height (about 44dp) too high and covered the chip row.
- **Fix:** an invisible 1px probe at the Modal's top-left measures where that corner is in the same coordinates as the chip, and the dropdown is shifted by the difference. Unlike a hard-coded status-bar height, this works on any device, whichever way it reports positions. The dropdown stays invisible until it has been placed, so it never flashes in the wrong spot.
- The position calculation moved to `filters/dropdownFrame.ts`. New tests cover the normal case, a 44dp status-bar offset, clamping to the side margins, and a minimum height of 160.

**List | Calendar toggle didn't animate**
- **Cause:** `TransactionsScreen` drew the `SlidingSegmentedControl` in two separate trees, one for each mode. Each switch unmounted the control and mounted a fresh one with its pill already in place, so there was nothing to animate.
- **Fix:** one control now sits in a fixed slot above both views, so it stays mounted and slides with the same spring as the Income / Expense control. A new test checks that switching modes keeps a single mount.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **anil**_

Stacked on anilkay/WindowsUtils#8 (`feature/new-screens`): it touches the same `PcTools` and screens, so it targets that branch. Once #8 is merged, this PR's base should be switched to `main`.

## What

Error handling now follows Railway Oriented Programming with [FluentResults](https://github.com/altmann/FluentResults). Code that can fail in an expected way returns `Result`/`Result<T>` and chains its steps with `Bind`/`Map`, instead of each step having its own `try`/`catch`.

- **PcTools**: every tool is a railway that ends in one `Run`/`RunAsync` exit (`Run(() => RequireLocalFile(path).Bind(...).Map(...))`). The ~27 copies of `try { } catch { return "Error: ..." }` are gone. Shared checks: `RequireDirectory`, `RequireLocalFile`, `RequireHost`, `RequireAlgorithm`. Public tool methods still return `string`, so chat, MCP and the CLI see the same text.
- **UserManagement**: the custom `CreateResult(bool, string?)` is replaced by `Result`. Account creation is one chain: validate → must not exist → `NetUserAdd` → add to Users/Administrators, rolled back if the group step fails.
- **FileHasher** returns `Result<T>`; `DuplicateFinder` and `FileHashControl` check it instead of catching IO exceptions.
- **ChatSettingsStore** (`Load`/`Save`/`Delete`) and **CredentialStore** (`Save`/`Delete`) return `Result`; `ChatControl` no longer wraps them in `try`/`catch`.
- **CLI**: numeric arguments parse to `Result<int>`; output and exit codes are unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md / README**: new "Error handling: Railway Oriented Programming" section. New code follows it: expected failures are results, cancellation is never a failure, absence is a value, messages stay stable, and pure/UI code stays plain. Two new gotchas are noted (async `Bind` lambda ambiguity, the `Result` name clash in `AddUserWizardForm`).

FluentResults (4.0.0) is added to `WindowsUtils.Core`, so every project gets it through Core.

## Behavior

Not meant to change anything a user, the model or a script sees.

- `dotnet build`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- The old and new `wutils` were run on the same 45 commands, including bad paths, UNC paths, locked files, unknown algorithms, wrong hash lengths and bad numeric arguments. Output and exit codes are identical, apart from the clock.

author: imeredith
body:
Typing in a board's search field no longer filters the kanban, list, triage or graph views. Instead, a popover under the field lists the matching tasks so you can open one.

**What changed**
- The search no longer filters the board. `BoardQuery` loses `search`. `taskMatcher` keeps only the filters (type, project, flags; status still picks the columns). The filter bar's search chip and the "N of M tasks" count for a search are gone. A search left in session storage from before this change is ignored.
- **Matching:** a task is found when every word typed appears in its key, title, description, branch or project. The board's done and archived tasks are included.
- **Ranking:** a key typed in full comes first. Then come tasks that aren't done, then done tasks, then archived ones. Within each group, tasks with the words in their key or title come first, then the most recently active.
- **Each result** shows the status icon, key and title, with the matched words highlighted. On the right it shows the project (on boards with several projects) and the status, or "Archived". If the words matched only the description, a line of the description shows where.
- **Limits:** the list stops at 20 results and says how many more there are. With no matches it says "No tasks found".
- **Keyboard:** `/` focuses the search, as before. ↑ and ↓ move through the results and wrap around. Enter opens the selected task, and so does a click (or a tap on a phone). Escape first closes the list, then clears the field, then leaves it. It never closes an open task panel. Clicking outside or blurring the field closes the list.
- **Accessibility:** the field is a combobox with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`, and the results are a listbox of options.
- The search text is now kept in `TaskBoard`, so it survives the controls moving between the header and the row below it when a board is narrow.
- The guide (`docs/guide/concepts.md`) is updated.

**Try it:** open a project's board and press `/`. Type `demo` (or a key such as `DEMO-8`): the board stays as it is and the popover lists the tasks. Move with ↑/↓ and press Enter to open one. Press Escape twice to clear the search.

**Tests**
- Unit tests: `tests/boardQuery.test.mjs` covers matching, ranking, highlighting and the description snippet.
- UI tests: `tests/ui/boardQuery.test.mjs` replaces the old test where the search narrowed the board. It covers the popover, the keyboard, Escape, clicking outside, opening a task by click, the 20-result cap with its "3 more" hint, and opening a task by tap on a phone.
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (web) and the board-related UI test files pass locally.

Goal 0037 — composable domain programs and deterministic simulation, built on the existing `OrElse`/`Replay` state machines.

## What landed
- Source: `DomainProgram.cs` (`DomainProgram`, `Update`, `AsStateMachine`, `OrElse`, `Replay`, parent-aware `Lift`), `ProgramSimulation.cs` (explicit clock, seeded `Random`, `Deliver`/`Reply`/`FailCommand`, ordered transcripts, replay), plus `EmittedCommand` / `SimulationDelivery` / `CommandExecutionFailure`.

The library is larger and slower in every measured row — no win is claimed:

A read-only review found no P1 code defect; its 2 P2 + 7 P3 were fixed: the guide's false state-copy attribution; the goal's mutation clause scoped explicitly to value-immutable inputs (library outputs immune; initial model/recorded messages caller-owned by reference) with an XML caveat and a boundary test; `...At` overloads now validate before advancing the clock and restore it on update exceptions; corrected closure/delegate counts; the comparison now asserts pending/replay counts for both sides; added Lift pre-update-parent and pending-preservation tests; removed dead `FailedInventory`; fixed `performance.md` OrElse wording.

author: charliemarsh-oai
body:
## Summary

A nextest archive can contain a Rust `dylib` and still fail to launch its test. Nextest derives the profile directory from the executable path in Cargo’s JSON. Ohm’s workspace-specific layout put that executable too far below its profile for nextest to find the library.

We now report test executables through a workspace-local `build/<package>/<unit>/out` directory link. This exposes the executable and its siblings at a path nextest understands on fresh and cached builds.

Closes https://github.com/astral-experiments/ohm-cargo/issues/488.

author: blurbery
body: ## Problem Closes #3641 Related issue: N/A Validation tasks: none An account at its household profile limit is still offered profile actions it can't use. The picker shows Add profile, Settings > Profiles opens the New profile editor and only fails with `409 profile_limit_reached` after the form is filled in, and the sidebar shows Switch Profile even when the picker would have nothing else on it. The admin page already gets this right ("1 of 1 allowed"). The cause is that the account's own `GET /api/v2/profiles` never reported the limit, so the web app had no way to know. This PR adds the limit to that response and has the web app hide those actions once the household is full. ## Approach `listProfiles` now returns `max_profiles`, the limit from the account's effective access policy. `CreateProfile` and `ListProfiles` read it through one helper on `ProfileHandler`, so the limit the app shows is the limit a create runs into. The field is additive and optional: - If the limit can't be read, the field is left out and the list still loads. A client then behaves as it does today, and `createProfile` stays the authority. - It's left out on a remote-playback handoff, because that list is filtered to the one bound profile and its length says nothing about room in the household. - Accounts outside every access group, and admins, resolve to the default of 5, so a working server always sends it. It never means "unlimited". - The frozen v1 `GET /profiles` body is unchanged. On the web, a `canAddProfile(count, maxProfiles)` helper drives three places: - The "Who's watching?" picker hides the Add profile tile at the limit, and so does the post-invite "Who's watching?" onboarding page. - Settings > Profiles hides New profile at the limit and says "This account can have 1 profile. An administrator can raise the limit." instead. - The sidebar hides Switch Profile only when there is one profile and no room for another. It keeps showing while the profile list is loading or if it fails to load, an account with several profiles keeps it at its limit, and a profile with a PIN keeps it, since going back to the picker locks that profile without signing out. The silo-apple and silo-android pickers have the same Add profile tile. Follow-ups: Silo-Server/silo-apple#1054 and Silo-Server/silo-android#856. jellycompat has no create-profile flow, so it needs nothing. ## Validation - Go: `internal/apiv2` listProfiles and contract fixture tests, and the `internal/api/handlers` profile tests, pass. The new handler test covers the inherited group limit, an account override, and a failed account read still returning the list. The v2 test covers the field being present with a limit and absent without one. - Contract: `contracts/api/v2/openapi.json` and `web/src/api/v2` regenerated. `verify-apiv2-web-types`, `verify-apiv2-contract` (one non-breaking change: optional response property added), `verify-migration-ledger` and `verify-scenario-catalogs` pass. - Web: type-check is clean, eslint is clean on the changed files, and the 31 test files that use the profile list pass, including the new `canAddProfile` table test. - Not run locally: `make lint-changed` and the full gate. CI runs those. ## Evidence Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/pr-3656/ Before and after captures from one sandbox: before on `main`, after on this branch, for an account limited to 1 profile. They cover the picker, the post-invite page, and Settings > Profiles at desktop and phone width, plus the account menu for a profile with a PIN and one without. What changes in the response, from the v2 router test (same request, profile items trimmed): ```json // Before {"items":[...],"avatar_upload_enabled":true,"max_advisory_age_supported":true,"require_advisory_age_supported":true} // After, account limited to 1 {"items":[...],"avatar_upload_enabled":true,"max_advisory_age_supported":true,"require_advisory_age_supported":true,"max_profiles":1} ``` ## Risks `listProfiles`, and with it v1 `GET /profiles`, now does one account read and, for a grouped account, one access-group read per call. That's the same lookup `createProfile` already does, and the household list isn't on a hot path. body:
## Why
Jason (Ōpeke) reported the phone view is untidy. The side menu was a fixed 220px column that never shrank, so on a phone it took more than half the screen and squeezed the page: headings and cards cut off, booking details wrapping one word per line, a crowded top bar.

## Change (screens 800px wide or narrower only)
- Menu becomes a slide-over drawer opened by a "Menu" button in a bar that stays at the top and shows the current page name. It closes when a page is picked, on the backdrop, on Close, or on Escape.
- Compact top bar: logo, marae name, avatar, Sign Out.
- Smaller page padding.
- Known wide side-by-side layouts are stacked in one column (not the Calendar); summary tiles are two across; rows of buttons, filters and tabs may wrap.
- Board Overview header and the Goals legend wrap.

No change to data, sign-in or the database. Desktop styling unchanged.

## Tested
- Real browser with a simulated signed-in trustee at 390px (phone), 768px (tablet) and 1280px (laptop).
- Drawer opens, closes on page pick and on Escape; the top bar shows the current page.
- All 18 pages fit a phone with no sideways scrolling (tested with no data).
- Checked on a real Samsung phone against the test marae: menu, Board View, Minutes and Calendar. Calendar and summary tiles were fixed after that check.
- Laptop screenshots of Bookings, Finance and Compliance are pixel-identical before and after.
- Build compiles. `ComplianceTracker` "View Document" test fails on main already and is unrelated.

## Not tested
- A live marae. Pages were tested with no data in the automated check, so real data may still need small layout fixes. Forms and pop-ups with fixed-width columns were not checked.
- Browser support for `:has()` (used so button rows can wrap): current Chrome, Safari and Firefox support it. On an old browser those rows just don't wrap, as before.

## Severity
HIGH (dependency advisory)

## Vulnerability
`npm audit` reported a high-severity denial-of-service advisory in `body-parser` (used by `express.json()` on every API route) plus moderate advisories in `qs` and `gaxios`.

## Impact
A crafted request body could tie up the server. All three have non-breaking patched versions.

author: j-reed700
body:
Merge after #371. This branch is built on #371's `ci/fast-prs` (merged in up to 6ac9aa177) and extends its `changes` job, so until #371 merges, the diff here includes #371's commits.

**What it does**

1. **Tests only the crates a pull request changes** (eab203c47).
   - `changes` also outputs the workspace crates the pull request's Rust files belong to, plus every crate that depends on them. `scripts/ci/rust_packages.py` reads `cargo metadata --no-deps`.
   - Only paths under a crate's `src/`, `tests/`, `benches/` or `examples/` map to that crate. The two generated IPC files map to lattice-desktop.
   - Anything else selects the whole workspace: other Rust paths (manifests, `Cargo.lock`, `build.rs`, `resources/`, `scripts/`, `evals/`, `.cargo/`), a push to main, an all-jobs run, or a failure in the job.
   - lattice-desktop is always selected, because the bindings check, the Windows manifest check and `bindings-export` need it.
   - rust-check's test build, nextest run and Ubuntu container exercises use that list. The container steps run only when lattice-learning is selected, since that is where their tests live.
   - The selection's env var is `PACKAGE_ARGS`. rust-cache hashes every `RUST*` and `CARGO*` env var into its restore key, so under a `RUST_` name every narrowed pull request would miss main's cache.
   - A guard test fails when a crate's code names a path under another crate's `src/`, `tests/`, `benches/` or `examples/` without depending on that crate, since a change there would not select it. The guard and the script's 18 unit tests run in the repository barrier.
2. **Lints beside the tests** (eab203c47). fmt and clippy move to a new job, `rust-lint` (Ubuntu and Windows), which runs alongside rust-check with its own main-only cache. macOS keeps clippy inside rust-check, so it takes no extra macOS runner.
3. **Runs the Mac and Windows app jobs on main, not on pull requests** (4e8da546c).
   - macOS rust-check and every desktop-compatibility job except Ubuntu now run on pushes to main only.
   - A pull request that is ready for review keeps the Ubuntu app job, which builds the installer and exercises the installed app. Drafts run no app job, the same way they already ran no macOS jobs.
   - Why: in main's run 42460567737, the Apple Silicon app job took 59 min and macOS rust-check was still running after 75. The Windows app job builds the release installer from cold on every push: 53.8 min with LTO (#367's run) and 43.4 min without it (#371's run 42463698033).
   - The trade-off: a break that shows up only on Windows or macOS now first shows up in main's run, after the merge. To keep the Windows app job on ready pull requests instead, revert this commit's `include` change. A ready run would then wait about 45 min for it.
4. **Runs a draft's Rust tests on Ubuntu only** (1fd49394e).
   - A draft pull request runs rust-check on Ubuntu. Marking it ready runs Windows too.
   - `-reds` branches keep Ubuntu and `-reds-windows` branches keep Windows, since the reds case comes first in the expression.
   - Why: on this branch's warm run, the Windows leg took 33.6 min against Ubuntu's 29.2 over the whole workspace. A narrowed Ubuntu run takes about 18 min (#379).
   - Windows clippy, in rust-lint, still runs on drafts, so a Windows compile error still shows on a draft.
   - The trade-off: a test that fails only on Windows now shows up when the pull request goes ready, the way macOS has since #361.

**Proof runs.** Both are drafts that never merge, built on this branch.

- **learning only, Ubuntu** (#379, run 42465835604, warm cache, full key match): the selection was `-p lattice-desktop -p lattice-learning`.
  - The test build took 7m41s, and nextest ran 6,265 tests in 401 s.
  - The job took 18.2 min. On #367's run 42457207274 the same job took 33.6 min: clippy 6.2 and a 25.3-min test step over the workspace.
  - 2.1 min of the 18.2 went to installing nextest. That was GitHub's release-download 504 outage, which took seven retries.
- **This PR's own run** (a workflow change, so the whole workspace): rust-lint passed on Ubuntu (8.9 min, cold cache) and Windows (15.2 min, cold). The Ubuntu rust-check ran `--workspace` alongside #379, on the same warm cache: the build took 10.8 min, nextest ran 8,091 tests in 14.0 min, and the job took 27.1 min. Against that, narrowing to learning saved 3.1 min of build and 7.3 min of test run.
- **desktop only, Windows** (#378, run 42465832595, cold cache): the selection was `-p lattice-desktop`.
  - The test build took 28m45s from cold.
  - nextest ran 4,445 tests in 555 s (9.2 min). On #367's run the workspace took 18.9 min.
  - Installing nextest took another 9.2 min, again because of the 504 outage.
  - The job took 48.5 min, about 39 without the outage.

- **This PR's own run on a warm cache** (42467863058, full key match, the whole workspace): every job passed.
  - Windows rust-check took 33.6 min: test build 16m42s, and nextest ran 8,104 tests in 895 s.
    - About 3 min of the build recompiled the wasmtime and cranelift crates at #367's opt-level 3, which main's cache predates.
    - The workspace crates took 13.3 min, from lattice-core's start to the end.
  - Ubuntu rust-check took 29.2 min, of which the test step was 25.0.
  - rust-lint ran alongside: Windows 12.4 min, Ubuntu 11.3.

Main's Windows rust-check cache was evicted at about 05:05Z. Main's run 42460567737 saved a new one (1.67 GB) at 09:30Z, so #378 and this branch's first runs built cold.

**Expected effect on a pull request that changes one Rust file**, once #371, #373 and this merge and main's caches are warm:

| Job | Before (#367's runs) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Windows rust-check | 65 min: clippy 14.1, build 31.5, tests 18.9 | 33.6 min warm for the whole workspace (build 16.7, tests 14.9); a desktop-only change ran 9.2 min of tests; drafts don't run it |
| Ubuntu rust-check | 33.6 min | 18.2 min (learning-only demo) |
| desktop compatibility | Windows 57.6 min, Ubuntu 21.7, macOS on ready PRs | Ubuntu only, on ready PRs |
| macOS rust-check | on ready PRs, waiting for a free runner | main only |

The test build barely shrinks with narrowing. Its critical path is core → learning → desktop's lib test, a single 713 s rustc on Windows in #370's timings, and every selection includes all three.

author: thomascrouzet
body:
## Summary

Refs #304, #305, #306.

- Connect revisioned document changes to Source and Code editors with immutable native text snapshots.
- Keep ordinary edits in the native buffer. Capture file identity and materialize text at explicit snapshot boundaries.
- Preserve own-echo undo and selection, reject stale publications without an overwrite, and retain the 400 ms draft save delay and legacy string fallback.
- Keep SourceText in the lazy editor module so CodeMirror state does not enter the boot bundle.

## Verification

- Independent final local CI on `6809a4fd6d7e3075105faa1c394932f1e313384e`: six checks passed.
- Targeted Chromium run: 66 executed cases, no skips or retries; 48 exact source-fidelity comparisons.
- Production boot closure: 208809 gzip bytes against the unchanged 211000 budget. Precache: 410 entries against the unchanged 410 limit.
- Full remote browser and native validation is pending. Reports remain in local evidence storage.

## Remaining limits

The original issues remain open for their complete acceptance criteria. This PR delivers the bounded Source/Code integration, not the complete cross-mode architecture or performance matrix.

- The measured 5 MB burst p95 increased from 54.0 ms to 104.2 ms. This is not strict performance acceptance.
- The conflict negative control reached the conflict alert; its raw process exit was not captured and downstream negative assertions were not reached.
- Native interaction, allocation and stress criteria remain incomplete.
- No budget, sampling rule, workflow or gate was changed.

author: lcos-000
body:
## Summary

Fix RootCoord default-database collection lookup so legacy metadata is used only when the modern default-database key is explicitly absent.

## Root Cause

`loadCollectionFromDb` converted every `Load` error and tombstone into `ErrCollectionNotFound`. `loadCollectionFromDefaultDb` then treated every non-nil error as evidence that the modern key was absent and read the legacy `NonDBID` key.

As a result, a valid legacy collection could be returned after a logical deletion or a storage I/O failure.

## Changes

- Preserve typed storage errors and classify untyped load errors as `ErrIoFailed`.
- Fall back to the legacy `NonDBID` key only for `ErrIoKeyNotFound`.
- Keep tombstones as `ErrCollectionNotFound`.
- Preserve `ErrCollectionNotFound` when both the default and legacy keys are absent.
- Add regression coverage for tombstones, I/O errors, explicit key absence, and both keys being absent.

## Testing

Passed:

- Focused `GetCollectionByID` regression tests with `-tags dynamic,test -gcflags="all=-N -l"`.

## Что

Режим `overlay`: капча не отдельной страницей, а окном поверх текущей. Защита не ослабевает — переход по ссылке отдаёт оболочку сайта, а подзагрузки, `fetch` и API получают капчу как раньше.

```python
KremleFlask(app, overlay=True)   # Flask / FastAPI / Starlette / Litestar
```

```js
KremleWidget.autoGuardOverlay(document)   // виджет
```

```tsx
<KremleOverlay onSolved={() => refetch()} />   // kremle-react
```

author: emreocell
body:
## Problem and result
Task 139 makes learned skills private to the calling bot until an explicit publish operation. Reads and lists resolve bot → shared → bundled; writes use versioned compare-and-swap and unique temporary files. Existing shared installations stay in place.

**Automatic system-prompt suggestions are not yet bot-scoped:** the required caller lives in the explicitly excluded agent-core crate. The resolver API is implemented and tested; the remaining call is documented below.

Base checked immediately before opening: `main` at `a4bfd8678ffe735ac0ed4c0c861b8e9857dc0af8`.

| Deliverable | Change (file:line) | Regression |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three scopes and precedence | `skills/src/index.rs:59,289` adds roots and per-call resolution, preserving legacy shared paths. `Source.scope` marks bot/shared/bundled. | Bot isolation, shared/bundled visibility, same-name shadowing, canonical shared alias priority, legacy constructor compatibility. |
| Context identity | `index.rs:109`, `tools.rs:166` validates bot IDs using workflow-name rules and resolves each call through `ToolContext.bot_id`. | Empty/traversal/unsafe IDs rejected; bot-less read remains shared/bundled and bot-less write is refused. |
| Versioned atomic bot writes | `scoped_store.rs:164`, `index.rs:495` uses an exclusive filesystem lock, expected-version CAS, unique temp file and atomic replacement. | Concurrent writers cannot both win; stale version fails without data loss; initial create races; symlink/device/reparse destinations refused. |
| Explicit publish | `tools.rs:102` declares Write/Fs effect for the existing approval machinery. `scoped_store.rs:278,287` stages a complete bot skill as `<name>@<version>`, locks both roots and rolls back replacement failures. | Publish collision/replace behavior, bundled/shared read-only roots, full skill/provenance preservation, source isolation, shared publication visibility. |
| Migration/wiring | `apps/cli/src/serve.rs:312` supplies `SkillRoots`; existing shared files do not move. `index.rs:299` provides the bot-aware prompt resolver. | Legacy shared and hub-installed skills remain visible with provenance; bot-aware prompt resolver tested. |

## Scope and hub boundary
Changes stay in `crates/skills` and the minimal `serve.rs` import/load function/test fixture. The mechanical `Cargo.lock` update adds `fs4` to skills' dependency list; fs4 already exists in the workspace lockfile. In `hub/mod.rs`, only safe path helper visibility is reused; the scanner, mandatory accept-token flow and installation acceptance logic are unchanged.

## Required follow-up outside the permitted boundary
`crates/agent-core/src/exec.rs::skills_block` still calls the bot-less `prompt_block_suggesting`. Switch it to the implemented `prompt_block_for_bot(Some(&ctx.bot_id.to_string()), context, suggested)` when that paused crate is available. One shared AgentLoop index means constructing a bot-specific index only in build_agent cannot solve this correctly.

Current behavior is explicit: scoped tool operations are active; automatic suggestions still show shared/bundled skills. No agent-core edit was made.

## Tests and checks
**21 new tests: 20 portable and 1 Windows-only.**
- Eight public-API regressions: **0/8** on untouched baseline production, **8/8** here.
- Final skills suite: **55/55 unit + 8/8 integration passed**. A follow-up preserves each backup immediately if publication rollback fails, without relying on a metadata check; its injected regression and final all-target Clippy passed.
- Targeted `cargo clippy -p skills --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Reverse-dependent Clippy (skills, agent-core, evals, daemon-api, remote-api, state-bundle, cli, peer-network): passed.
- Windows `cargo clippy -p skills --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `git diff --check`, `cargo deny check`: passed.
- Full reverse-dependent tests completed: **529 passed, 6 failed, 1 ignored**, plus 2 ignored doctests. Green: agent-core unit145, daemon-api110, evals22, peer-network66, remote-api11, skills63, state-bundle42. Failures are five existing agent CLI-runtime cases and the CLI peer-addressing case, matching the isolated environment failures in D. No code outside this scope was changed to bypass them.
- Native current-head Linux/Windows Actions were inspected; results are recorded below. Baseline main's desktop-windows Linux Clippy failure is fixed separately in #22.

## Windows-sensitive notes
Filesystem locks are portable fs4 locks, not Linux-only advisory code. Atomic replacement uses tempfile's platform implementation; this promises atomic visibility, not power-loss durability. Reparse/device/unsafe-path checks fail closed. Windows-only path tests execute in native CI; cross-target Clippy is not represented as Windows runtime execution.

Do not merge. Open item: the excluded agent-core prompt caller.

## Recorded Actions results
[Current-head CI](https://github.com/emreocell/Praxi-Bot/actions/runs/42475810803): native Windows Build & Test passed completely, including formatting, Clippy and all workspace tests. Linux skills/unit/integration and all other targets passed except the old Cursor/Gemini copied-executable fixtures (fixed in #18); the existing workspace lint failure is fixed in #22. UI, browser integration and license checks passed.

Baseline attribution: the exact existing `cargo test -p agent-core --test cli_runtime --locked -- --nocapture` target was run on clean main `a4bfd86` and independently reproduced the same **2 passed / 5 failed** local outcomes. The separate CLI peer-addressing failure also reproduces on main. Native CI results are recorded separately from these local-runtime limitations.

body:
Removes fleetd's Telegram integration entirely, on the human's ask (D339). Nothing replaces it.

## Removed surfaces

**Hub**
- `hub/telegram` (the bridge loop, pairing, Bot API formatting, approval cards, `/stop`, usage-limit lines) and its tests.
- The `telegram_get`, `telegram_set`, `telegram_test`, `telegram_pair`, `telegram_unpair`, `telegram_pause` and `telegram_remove` tools: their registration, descriptions and contract entries.
- `chat::flow::send_from_telegram`, a forward's `<untrusted source="telegram forward">` wrapping, and the "(on Telegram)" writer tag in what the lead reads.
- The push rule that skipped a phone notification while the person talked on Telegram.
- `Executor::telegram` (the hub → node call) and `intake::attachments::read` (only the bridge used it).
- `navi::store::claim` (pairing made a project its owner's), the checker's forwarded-message source, and the `Telegram` read kind in approval reviews.
- `telegram_bridges` and `telegram_cards` in the project-delete, machine-remove and erase table lists.

**Node**
- `node/telegram` (the long-poller, token store, inbound journal) and its tests; the `telegram` session call and its answer; the `telegram` capability.
- On start, a node deletes `<node home>/telegram/`, the bot tokens and journals an older node kept.

**Contracts**
- `fleetd-contracts::telegram`, the seven tools' input and output types, `SessionCall::Telegram` / `SessionOutput::Telegram`, `CAP_TELEGRAM`, `ChatClient::Telegram` and `ChatMessage.forwardedFrom`. Schemas and the app's generated TypeScript are regenerated.

**Desktop app**
- Settings › Projects › Telegram (`Telegram.tsx`, `telegramModel.ts`, its test and CSS), its settings-search entry, the `telegram:submit` IPC channel with `submitTelegram` in main and preload, the "From Telegram" / "Forwarded from … on Telegram" line over a bubble (`viaOf`), the `fixtures/telegram` fixtures and their QA captures, and `telegram_get` in the settings reads and the `project.settings` effects.

**Phone app**
- The project's Telegram screen and its Info row, its route, `readTelegram` / `telegramAct` with their tests, and the re-exports from the desktop. Comments that named Telegram's app as a design reference now name Messages or chat apps.

**CLI, prompts and docs**
- `fleetd project remove`'s help, `chat_file`'s description and the `assistant.start` prompt (the "From Telegram" section).
- The docs' Projects › Telegram section and every mention in automations, chat, desktop app, glossary, mobile, people, phone notifications and what agents are told. The reference pages are regenerated.

## Stored data
Migration `202611081314_telegram_gone.sql` (sorts after main's newest, `202611081200_attachment_uploads_stored`):
- drops `telegram_bridges` and `telegram_cards`;
- a message written on Telegram keeps its words and loses its `client` and its key name ("Telegram");
- a forwarded message becomes a share-sheet message (`client: share`), so it is still no go-ahead for the checker, with "Forwarded from <name>: " at the start of its text;
- deletes the "Telegram paired with …" and "Telegram unpaired: …" system lines with their `chat.message` events, and the `project.settings` events of an unpair or remove;
- changes the `chat.message` events of the messages that stay the same way their rows change, so the two copies agree.

A test runs it over an older hub's rows and checks every chat message still decodes.

- #1136 (the W467 cuts) landed first too. It had edited the Telegram settings page, its test, the settings-search entry and the `chat_file` text; those are removed here as well.

## Older apps
An app that still calls a `telegram_*` tool gets `not_found` with "Telegram was removed from fleetd." and the fix "Update the fleetd app: newer ones no longer offer it." It doesn't get "No tool …". This is covered in the app-socket test. The old Settings page shows that error, and an older phone's Telegram row does the same.

## What `git grep -i telegram` still finds
- the new migration, its test (`store/tests.rs`) and the node's cleanup of old tokens: the data drop;
- the refusal for older apps (`api/registry.rs`) and its test (`serve/tests.rs`);
- three migrations already on main (`202610311228_telegram`, `202611011200_yolo_lines_gone`, `202611071205_navis_are_projects`). CI refuses edits to landed migrations, so their comments stay as they are.

The release note is this PR's title, which the update notice shows.

## Overlap
- #1129 (security round 2) landed first. Its Telegram parts (pairing that claims a shared project only for an admin, its tests and its docs paragraph) went with the module.
- #1135 (Shortcuts) landed first. Its Telegram parts went too: "via Telegram" in the desktop's and phone's source labels, the Telegram message in the `bubbles-sources` fixture, chat_send's refusal of `client: telegram` (that value no longer decodes) and its test, and "(on Telegram)" in what the lead reads and in the `chat.human` prompt's placeholder text. The desktop's label line now only shows "via Shortcuts" or "via the Share Sheet". A forwarded message the migration turns into a share-sheet one shows "via the Share Sheet".
