body:
## Change

Follow-up to #3397: fixes the review nits from r-3397 and links the new follow-up issue #3425. There is no new mathematics and no statement changes.

- **Citation.** Theorem 8.8 is now cited under `AroraBarak07`, the January 2007 web draft dated 2007-01-08, instead of `AroraBarak09`, the 2009 book. The draft numbering checks out: §8.4 "Public coins and AM", Theorem 8.8 "IP[k] ⊆ AM[k + 2]". The 2009 numbering stays unverified and is no longer attached to the 2009 key.
- **Padded-set size.** The `Emulation.lean` module docstring said the padded set has about `2 ^ (κ + K)` elements. It now says about `2 ^ K`: `2 ^ (κ - b)` messages, each padded in `2 ^ (b + K - κ)` ways. The manual now says the padding prefix length is fixed by both the previous claim and `b`.
- **Duplicate lemma.** Removed the private `geom_two_add_one`, which restated a Mathlib lemma. `le_sum_two_pow` now uses Mathlib's `Nat.geomSum_eq`.
- **Docstrings.**
  - The test docstring says the `IP[2]` emulation pattern has five entries, four moves once adjacent Merlin moves merge.
  - The `amVerifier` docstring states the one-sided bound `2 ^ κ ≤ (3 / 4) ^ T N`.
- **Remaining work.** The ROADMAP direction "Oracle-model `IP[k]`" and the manual's not-covered pointer now link #3425 instead of the closed #2981.

Part of #3425. #3425 records the rest:
- moving the `IPGame` shape lemmas to `IP/Games`;
- moving `hashZero`/`seedEquiv` out of `SetLowerBound`;
- the oracle-model `IP[k]` bridge;

body:
The failing GitHub Actions `build` job was caused by a source-path mismatch: the Pages/Jekyll workflow builds from `./docs`, but the repository served content from the root. This change makes repository layout consistent with the configured Pages source so the build can resolve site assets and render successfully.

- **Root cause addressed**
  - Pages build container resolves source as `/github/workspace/docs`; directory was missing, causing Jekyll/Sass conversion to fail with `No such file or directory`.

- **Repository layout change**
  - Moved the static site entrypoint from repository root to the expected Pages source directory:
    - `index.html` → `docs/index.html`

- **Behavioral impact**
  - No content or runtime logic changes; only source location alignment with workflow expectations.

```diff
- /index.html
+ /docs/index.html
```

author: danyel-claude
body:
<!-- status -->
**Waiting on:** Danyel, since 2026-11-08T18:35:03.522Z
**Ask:** Try one real answer (steps below), then approve and merge
**To test:** 1) Put the board's fine-grained token in this worktree's local secrets: ! printf 'GITHUB_TOKEN=%s\nALLOW_LOCAL=1\n' "$(pbpaste)" > /Users/danyel/code/MISC/pr-board/.claude/worktrees/part-2-answering/.dev.vars 2) Claude starts pnpm dev there 3) Answer one card 4) The card moves to On Claude as answered, and the comment on GitHub is from danyelf
<!-- /status -->

## The problem

The board shows what's waiting on Danyel, but he can't answer from it. Every answer, including "looks good, prep for merge", has to be typed into a Claude session, and nothing tells that session an answer exists.

## What it does

**On the page.** Each card that asks something gets a small form. It works without JavaScript.
- Claude's questions are radio buttons, with the default picked and in bold. Every question also has "file an issue".
- Every PR at "Your look" also asks **How does it look?** (**looks good, prep for merge** | needs changes | file an issue).
- A note box (up to 2000 characters) and **Send answers**.

**Sending.** POST /answer posts one comment from Danyel's own account on the PR or issue. The comment has a machine-readable first line, then readable lines. The Worker never changes whose turn it is: labels and the status section are left for Claude to rewrite. Sending is refused when:
- the request has no Access sign-in, or its Origin isn't the board's own;
- the body is larger than 32 KB, a field is unknown or sent twice, or a choice isn't one of the listed ones;
- the questions changed since the page was drawn (each status carries a short fingerprint);
- the item is closed, already answered, or not Danyel's turn.

**What the board shows after.** An answer newer than the status moves the card to "On Claude", first as "answered, waiting for Claude to pick it up", then as "Claude picked up your answers 3 h ago". If no claim (a 👀 reaction from anyone but Danyel) appears within 10 minutes, the card goes back to the top as **Answered, not picked up**.

**Picking answers up.** `cli/watch-answers.ts <refs>` is started in the background by the session that handed the items over.
- It checks once a minute. When it finds an answer, it claims it with 👀, prints it, and exits, which wakes the session.
- It never exits on a timer or on errors; it backs off from 2 to 5 minutes and keeps going.
- It refuses to run as Danyel's own account, because the board ignores his own 👀.
- It drops items that close.

The `pr-status` skill says what to do with each answer.

**The status as data.** `pr-status set` also writes the status as one JSON line inside the markers. That line holds the fingerprint and the time the status was written. The board uses it only when it matches the visible text exactly. If someone edits the text on GitHub, the text wins, and the card says "status edited by hand; rewrite it with pr-status set".

## Claude's calls, for Danyel to confirm

They're listed in the spec under "Settled for answering". The main ones:
1. The Worker only posts the answer and never touches the label or the status line. This avoids the "label out of sync" problem the spec flagged. It also matters because the label is how answered items are found: the board fetches issues by label, and the Mac service (#10) looks for answers only on items labelled `on danyel`.
2. Answers are timed against when `pr-status` last wrote the status, not against any edit to the description, so adding a screenshot doesn't lose an answer.
3. One token reads and posts: the board's existing `GITHUB_TOKEN`, from Danyel's account. A second token would sit beside it in the same Worker's secrets, so it wouldn't make a leak smaller, and it would be one more secret to renew.

## Before it can be used

Done: Danyel gave the board's token read and write access to **Issues** and **Pull requests** (README step 8). If the token ever can't write, Send says so and nothing is posted.

## Reviews

Three reviewers looked at the branch, none of whom had seen the conversation. They covered code and safety, things said in two places, and the architecture. They found no serious bugs; the architecture verdict was "sound, with changes". The changes are in the last seven commits:
- a status edited by hand is now handled;
- answers are timed by when `pr-status` wrote the status;
- the board and the watcher share one rule for an answer still waiting;
- duplicate and off-turn answers are refused;
- the hand-written SHA-256 became a small hash, since the fingerprint only has to notice changes.

Left for later:
- A single watcher per session that reads a list of items, instead of Claude starting one after each hand-over.
- Splitting the GitHub module into reading and writing.

## Testing

270 tests pass and the type checker is clean. Locally, against live GitHub data:
- the board drew the look question on four cards, with no error lines;
- POST /answer refused a wrong Origin (403) and changed questions (409);
- the watcher ran for real on two PRs without errors.

Not yet checked for real: a successful post, and the 👀 claim on GitHub.

Local dev works again with `pnpm dev`. The script now passes `--infer-origin-from-routes=false`, because the `routes` line had broken it.

author: skyphusion-mackaye
body:
## What

Records a measured b-dosql limitation and makes it reproducible: **admin media upload fails on a WooCommerce-warmed isolate** at the attachment insert, while it succeeds on a non-WooCommerce b-dosql isolate.

- `tests/upload/upload_ceiling.py` -- self-contained (stdlib only, embedded 64x64 PNG). Logs in, uploads through `async-upload.php`, retries past the 503 overload gate, and reports `stored` / `blocked at the write-memory ceiling` / `OOM` with the `x-wasm-mib` reading. Exit 0 stored, 2 ceiling, 1 harness error.
- `docs/results.md` -- one measured row (refines row 168).
- `README.md` -- caveats the "B with WooCommerce -> b-dosql: yes" cell: the storefront and checkout work, admin media upload does not.

## Why

Row 168 established that non-Woo uploads succeed (mib 58) and Woo-warmed ones fail (mib 99), and named the reducibility candidates (EXIF-off, trim sizes). This run shows those candidates do **not** clear the ceiling:

| site | WooCommerce | baseline mib | upload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| imgnw | off | 58 | **stored** (success, flat 58) |
| imgt195 | warmed | 99 | **blocked** at the attachment insert (99 -> 119, no reset) |

Identical for a 400x300 and a 3000x3000 image, so the cost is the WooCommerce per-request working set, not the image. #195's EXIF-off moves the upload past the metadata-read OOM to the insert, but the insert still fails for lack of headroom. This is the same 128-vs-256 wall the code already sends checkout to a Container for (`WooCheckout`), and `serveUpload` has no on-demand size regeneration, so admin media upload needs the Container path like checkout.

Part of #189 (stays open). PR #195 stays held: it is a real memory reduction but its size-trim keep-set cannot be box-verified until an upload completes.

author: denaidark
body:
## Summary

Fixes intermittent 503 errors from GitHub Releases during FRP client download in Actions workflows.

## Changes

### New: `scripts/download-frp.sh`
- Bounded retry: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2s, 4s)
- Timeouts: 10s connect, 120s max download
- SHA256 checksum verification against GitHub Releases API `digest` field
- Cache support: validates cached archives, removes corrupted entries
- Explicit error messages with stage and hostname for debugging

### Updated: `.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml`
- Added `actions/cache@v4` step for persistent cross-run FRP caching
- Cache key: `frp-0.71.1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('**/scripts/download-frp.sh') }}`
- Replaced inline curl with script invocation

### New: Test Suites
- `scripts/test-download-frp.sh`: 10 static assertion tests
- `scripts/test-download-frp-behavioral.sh`: 5 behavioral tests with mocked curl/tar

## Checksum Provenance

SHA256 digests verified against **GitHub Releases API** `digest` field (TLS-authenticated upstream data).

| Platform | Digest |
|----------|--------|
| linux_amd64 | `1d9875210972a5d1a62b2dc4c48df45ab0af05d3ca1b5e494a014428259df803` |
| linux_arm64 | `8edf590b0c396fa42f9c147121a76af83cfc2002b08f5aef0ea1008c43482019` |
| darwin_amd64 | `8acb59b6fb998cc8d209d1373d90bf70fa5ec3efeb4dfbc7bda6ce3abd78cb45` |
| darwin_arm64 | `d15d0324b99e14619c9aa46e37f6db588c06a09be4bc6f7948890b6b61077842` |

## Test Results

**Static Tests (10/10 pass):** Script validation, cache detection, retry/timeout logic, diagnostics

**Behavioral Tests (5/5 pass, mocked):** Transient 503 retry, bounded failure, checksum rejection, corrupt cache recovery, cache hit optimization

## Cache Key Note

Cache key includes `hashFiles` of the download script. Updating the script invalidates stale entries. Does not repair already-corrupt entries on unchanged script; the script validates and removes corrupt files on each run.

author: chihyunpark1
body:
# RE-001: lockwait caller 1site resolver noloader dead duff q50x50

Seventieth packet of the lock-wait-helper-caller frontier (344 survivors; the lu-miss frontier is exhausted 16/16 with #314–#329). FDE 0x639a9c0..0x639ac80 (704 B, 191 strict) has one lock-wait site, resolves its entry through a separate resolver callee (0x6388310) WITHOUT loading the entry through the trivial 8-byte load helper (0x63bfb90 is NOT called) and WITHOUT a fixed inline adjust (the resolver-fixed chain, adjusts +0xb8 through +0x380 over #341–#364, ENDS at #364; #365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376/#377/#378/#379/#380/#381/#382/#383/#384/#385/#386/#387/#388/#389/#390/#391/#392/#393/#394/#395/#396/#397/#398/#399 add no adjust entry), a 3-value exit 0/1/22, and a Duff's-device copy loop that is FULLY DEAD (its dispatch tail and its 8-at-a-time body are never entered). It rejoins at the trylock-SUCCESS block after lock-wait (like #332/#333/#334/#336/#338/#339/#340/#341/#342/#343/#344/#345/#346/#347/#348/#349/#350/#351/#352/#353/#354/#355/#356/#357/#358/#359/#360/#361/#362/#363/#364/#365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376/#377/#378/#379/#380/#381/#382/#383/#384/#385/#386/#387/#388/#389/#390/#391/#392/#393/#394/#395/#396/#397/#398, unlike #330/#331/#335/#337).

Thin packet: README + records.json + MANIFEST + window bytes + disassembly only. No verifier tool, no unit tests, no `make verify`, no `make catalogue`, no full `make test` — every claim is a direct check over the disassembly and bytes, quoted with addresses in the README.

## Window

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FDE | 0x639a9c0..0x639ac80 |
| Bytes | 704 |
| Strict | 191 |
| Lock-wait site | 0x639aaac |
| Rets | 1 (0x639aa67) |
| bsr | 0 |
| shr | 1 (shr $0x3 at 0x639ab17) |
| shl | 0 |
| endbr64 | 1 (entry at 0x639a9c0) |
| Canary | present (2 %fs:0x28 lines; __stack_chk_fail@plt at 0x639ac7b) |
| Jumps | 28 |
| PLT | 3 |
| Prefetch/tzcnt/btc | 0 / 0 / 0 |

## Lock-wait site

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Site | 0x639aaac |
| Setup | lea -0x40(%r15),%rdi at 0x639aaa8 |
| rdi def | {0x639aaa8} (mutex node 0x6712160) |
| Other argument registers | rsi/rdx/rcx/r8/r9/r10/r11/rax = {CALL(0x639a9fb)} (the trylock clobber); rbx = {0x639a9e4} (entry r9 save); rbp = {0x639a9dd} (entry rdi save); r12 = {0x639a9d9} (entry rcx save); r13 = {0x639a9d4} (entry r8 save); r14 = {0x639a9cf} (entry rsi save); r15 = {0x639a9c6} (mutex lea) |
| Predecessors | {0x639aa02} (trylock failed; the nopl at 0x639aabd is padding after the jmp at 0x639aab8, not a real path) |
| After the call | movb $0x1,0x67121c8 at 0x639aab1 (waited flag set); jmp 0x639aa08 (trylock-SUCCESS block; trylock NOT re-run) |
| Flag clear | movb $0x0,0x67121c8 at 0x639aa34 (while lock held, before unlock) |
| Unlock | pthread_mutex_unlock@plt at 0x639aa3e |
| Rejoin | trylock-SUCCESS block at 0x639aa08 |

## Resolver

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Callee | 0x6388310 (#338's next FDE, 0x6388310..0x6388372, 98 B) |
| Call site | 0x639aa74 |
| Input | *(entry rsi + 0x10) (mov 0x10(%r14),%rdi at 0x639aa70) |
| Result | two-step read: qword at +0x50 (mov 0x50(%rax),%rax at 0x639aa79), then qword at +0x50 of that entry (mov 0x50(%rax),%rsi at 0x639aa7d), stored to (%rsp) at 0x639aa81 |
| Loader | NONE — 0x63bfb90 is NOT called |
| Adjust | NONE — no fixed inline adjust (no add $imm,%rdi anywhere; shl 0) |
| Count call | NONE — 0x634eba0 is NOT called; the count logic lives inside the resolver |
| Resolver internals | Per #373's read of the resolver body: TLS check at 0x638831b (init via 0x63ef8e0 if unset); reads count struct 0x6712130; returns table[index] where index is 0 for rbx == 0x1000 or rbx == 0x1001 or rbx == count, else rbx+2 |

## Selector and copy

The copy IS a Duff's-device loop (0x639ab08..0x639ac29), but it is FULLY DEAD. The length is *r8 (`mov 0x0(%r13),%rdx` at 0x639aa8f, r13 = entry r8); if the length is exactly 8, the qword from the stack temp (%rsp) is stored whole to *rcx (`mov %rsi,(%r12)` at 0x639aa99) and the window exits 0 (`xor %ebp,%ebp` at 0x639aa9d). A null dest or null length pointer also exits 0 (`je 0x639aa9d` at 0x639aa88 / 0x639aa8d). Otherwise n = min(len,8) (`mov $0x8,%ecx` at 0x639aac0, `mov %rsp,%r9` at 0x639aac5, `cmp %rcx,%rdx` at 0x639aac8, `cmova %rcx,%rdx` at 0x639aacb); len < 8 goes to the small tail (`jb 0x639ac30` at 0x639aad2), which copies n = len bytes by 4/2/1-byte decomposition (0x639ac30..0x639ac79) and exits 22 with *r8 = n. The 2-byte path sets ebp = len (`mov %edx,%ebp` at 0x639ac6b) as a transient index, but that def is dead — the writeback's `mov $0x16,%ebp` at 0x639ac4b overwrites it on the only path out (jmp 0x639ac47 at 0x639ac79). Len > 8 reaches the n == 8 path: `mov %edx,%eax` at 0x639aad8 sets eax = 8; the first qword is stored to dest+0 (`mov %rsi,(%r12)` at 0x639aada), re-loaded from src+0 (`mov -0x8(%r9,%rax,1),%rsi` at 0x639aae3 — with eax == 8 reads src+0, not src+8), and stored AGAIN to dest+0 (`mov %rsi,-0x8(%r12,%rax,1)` at 0x639aaec), then r12d = (dest - ((dest+8)&~7) + 8) & ~7 = 0 (`lea 0x8(%r12),%rcx` at 0x639aade, `and $~7,%rcx` at 0x639aae8, `sub %rcx,%r12` at 0x639aaf1, `sub %r12,%r9` at 0x639aaf4, `add %edx,%r12d` at 0x639aaf7, `and $~7,%r12d` at 0x639aafa), so `cmp $0x8,%r12d` at 0x639aafe leaves r12d < 8 and the loop-entry jb (`jb 0x639ac47` at 0x639ab02) is ALWAYS taken to the writeback. The dispatch tail (0x639ab08..0x639abc1, `shr $0x3,%edi` at 0x639ab17 + `and $0x7,%edi` at 0x639ab1e, seven je tail entries) and the 8-at-a-time body (0x639abc1..0x639ac29, back-edge `jb 0x639abc1` at 0x639ac27) are never entered — the loop's only CFG entry is the fall-through from 0x639ab02 (no jump in the window targets 0x639ab08; preds[0x639abc1] == {0x639ab2c, fall-through 0x639abbb, 0x639ac27}, all inside the dead region). The writeback stores *r8 = n (`mov %rdx,0x0(%r13)` at 0x639ac47) and exits 22 (`mov $0x16,%ebp` at 0x639ac4b).

## Calls

| Target | Site | PLT |
|---|---|---|
| 0x63f17b0 (pthread_mutex_trylock) | 0x639a9fb | yes |
| 0x6388310 (index resolver) | 0x639aa74 | no |
| 0x63f0b70 (pthread_mutex_unlock) | 0x639aa3e | yes |
| 0x63bf680 (lock-wait helper) | 0x639aaac | no |
| 0x63f0d70 (__stack_chk_fail) | 0x639ac7b | yes |

No lu-miss, bin_table_init, second-handler, resolver (0x6365150), count call, loader call, or #314–#398 window calls. PLT determination is by `@plt` suffix only: the internal `.text` calls (0x6388310, 0x63bf680) are NOT PLT stubs.

## Shape

The single ret at 0x639aa67 returns eax via a single reaching def, `mov %ebp,%eax` at 0x639aa5b; ebp's reaching defs are exactly {0x639aa28 (1 — lock acquired, caller condition failed), 0x639aa9d (0 — success), 0x639ac4b (22 — copy with length writeback)}, so the three exit values are 0 (success), 1 (lock acquired, caller-side condition failed) and 22 (copy of n = min(len,8) bytes with *r8 = n writeback: len > 8 copies only the first qword twice, n = 8; len < 8 copies via the small tail, n = len). The `mov %edx,%ebp` at 0x639ac6b is killed by `mov $0x16,%ebp` at 0x639ac4b on its only path (jmp 0x639ac47 at 0x639ac79 then the writeback). All paths converge on the flag-clear at 0x639aa34 and the canary-check epilogue at 0x639aa43. This is the THIRTY-THIRD frontier window with a FULLY DEAD Duff's-device loop (after #398, the thirty-second; 26 windows with unreachable Duff loops #339–#364, #365 with no loop at all, and #366 with a reachable dispatch tail but a value-dead 8-at-a-time body), and like #365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376/#377/#378/#379/#380/#381/#382/#383/#384/#385/#386/#387/#388/#389/#390/#391/#392/#393/#394/#395/#396/#397/#398 it resolves its entry through a separate resolver callee (0x6388310) WITHOUT loading the entry through a trivial 8-byte load helper (0x63bfb90 is NOT called) and WITHOUT a fixed inline adjust (the resolver-fixed chain, adjusts +0xb8 through +0x380 over #341–#364, ENDS at #364; #365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376

author: ardhankurniawan
body:
### Root cause

For an empty Scenario, TiDB returned HTTP 200 for the scoped Order SELECT with `types` present and `rows` omitted. The strict transport guard rejected the incomplete response and the Orders API returned HTTP 503 `UNAVAILABLE`. A read-only probe reproduced the behavior on TiDB Testing.

### Changes

- Validate the scoped COUNT before fetching Orders. A verified zero returns an empty page. A positive count continues through the existing scoped SELECT and strict response checks.
- Reject invalid COUNT metadata and preserve HTTP 503 for incomplete SELECT responses and provider failures.
- Wait for ResizeObserver registration before asserting resize behavior. Verify cleanup on unmount and Scenario switch.

- Focused tests: 102/102 PASS.

- Coverage: 769/769 PASS.
- ESLint, typecheck, db:check, build, post-build typecheck, and git diff --check: PASS.
- The fixed service returned a valid empty page in a read-only TiDB Testing probe.

Verify the authenticated Orders GET and Map for Scenario 90001 on a Vercel Testing Preview built from the new revision.

## 第三轮：殿堂要建、开局少选

- **殿堂一座座建**：开局只有灵植园和巡山队（丹师多一座丹房）。迎客堂、丹房、外事堂、器阁、执法堂、传功殿要花灵石、满足条件（丹房要先有灵植园，执法堂要弟子满 8 人……），一两季落成；扩建也要时间。工匠有限，同时只能建一处，中品宗门以后两处。地图上空地画成虚线圈，在建的搭脚手架
- **开局只选山门**：出身、传承由天定，第一个开春揭晓；第一年不用点传承
- 开局灵石多一百、造价略降；旧存档的殿堂等级挪一格

## 第二轮：玩法扩充、手机横屏

参考鬼谷八荒、太吾绘卷、了不起的修仙模拟器、一念逍遥、冰汽朋克、王国风云：

- **宗主亲为**：每季闭关、亲传、坐镇、游历、开炉、拜山六选一。闭关能一路修到元婴
- **宗门任务**：新的「任务」页，十种差事，挑一到三人组队，按战力和本事算把握，凶险的可能折人
- **宗门品阶**：草创 → 下品 → 中品 → 上品宗门 → 一方圣地，每阶解锁任务格、召见名额、供奉
- **年度大计**：每年开春三选一，办成有赏，没成掉宗主威望；开春先看去年回顾
- **敌宗也在长**：每年收人、修炼，宗主后几年可能冲上元婴
- **手机横屏**：左边山门和过季，右边事务，顶栏压成一行

## 第一轮：修毛病、补细节

- 奸细藏不住 → 见不得光的事不进季报和经历
- 冲关卡死 → 每年开春再来求，人物卡上能直接下令

author: lakens
body:
Closes #607.

**What happened.** PsyArXiv 6qf9p_v3's OSF project (rwn89) holds an OpenRouter key in the survey flow of its two Study 1 Qualtrics surveys (`.qsf`), as the embedded data field `OpenRouterAPIKey`. The Qualtrics export also wrote that field into every response of the two Study 1 data files. Metacheck did not warn, and copied the key into its saved result (most likely through data_check's copy of the data tables), which GitHub then refused to store.

**What changes**
- `R/keys.R`: finds keys with the rules of the secret scanner betterleaks of high and medium confidence (427 rules; all read by R with `perl = TRUE`), with their filters: minimum entropy, patterns a key must or must not match (such as `.+EXAMPLE$` for AWS), texts, the general placeholders (`${API_KEY}`), and path conditions (a Terraform password only in `.tf` files). Each rule is tried only near its keywords, as in betterleaks. Encoded data (1,000 or more base64 characters, such as an image in a knitted HTML page) is masked. Keys are numbered inside the search and never returned; only their first characters are shown.
- `data_check`: searches every downloaded file the authors wrote (code, settings files such as `.env`, survey definitions, documentation, outputs), including files code_check downloaded and a local folder's hidden files; of a tabular data file, only the column names and first 3 rows of the table as read. A key turns the light red. The report gives each key's files, lines or rows, type and beginning, and says to revoke it (deleting a file does not remove it from GitHub's history or the OSF's earlier versions). New summary column `key_n`, result table `keys`.
- `module_run()`: replaces any key in a module's result by "[key removed]" (report, tables, names), so that no module copies a key into Metacheck's output.
- `data-raw/key_patterns.R` collects the rules into `inst/databases/key_patterns.Rds` (RcppTOML; its reading of literal strings is undone and was checked against Python's tomllib for all 474 rules). betterleaks' MIT notice is in `inst/COPYRIGHTS`, named in DESCRIPTION's `Copyright` field.

**Tested**
- `tests/testthat/test-keys.R` (159 checks): random fake keys of 12 types made while the test runs (so no file holds a key GitHub would refuse), in four forms; placeholders and examples; a key in an R file, a `.qsf` survey and a `.env` file through data_check; a survey key in every row of a data table; a key next to an embedded image; a rule for `.tf` files only; removal from a module's result through `module_run()`.
- On 6qf9p_v3 itself: "We found 1 key in 4 files" (the two surveys, line 1; the two response tables, rows 1-3); no whole key left in data_check's or codebook_check's result.
- On 400 repositories of an earlier corpus run: every find is a key by its form (a database password in deployment instructions; test keys of software copied into two repositories). That run showed two causes of false finds, both fixed: base64 images (4 "Brave Search keys" in one page) and the missing path conditions (8 "Terraform passwords" in Java source).
- Speed: 15 ms per data table; on 18.6 million characters of table text, the keyword search takes 0.3 s.
- The tests of data_check, module_run, codebook_check and the reports pass.

Version 0.4.3.17 (to follow #609 0.4.3.14, #611 0.4.3.15 and #608).

author: sweet-rice
body:
The pipelined Stage 2 design now meets timing at **10 ns (100 MHz core clock)**. The new Vivado target is `top_s2p100`. Software doesn't change: retire traces and frames are identical to the multi-cycle core, and MMIO CYCLES still counts 20 ns ticks, so the game's time base is unchanged.

**Status:**
- The simulator checks and a first board pass are done, both with `main` 7315b19's game (after #70, #72, #74). Results are below.
- The bitstream is ready for game work.
- Live testing of the game on the board continues before this is accepted.

## Bitstream (top_s2p100, main 7315b19 game)

| | |
|---|---|
| Download | **[top_s2p100-pr71-rc1](https://github.com/Sweet-Rice/kennycraft-alpha/releases/tag/top_s2p100-pr71-rc1)** (pre-release): `kc_top_s2p100.bit` plus `kc_top_s2p100.mmi` for `patch_bit.sh` |
| Build | `build_20261108_115553_1f9ddd`, RTL at 63f42c4 (the release tag) |
| SHA-256 | `f667503210fe2ad2483fce2955984056b12c3bbc6225ba9c6354ec911c67cae4` |
| Rebuild | `tools/fpga_mcp.py --project <checkout> --target top_s2p100 build-wait` (run `make top-hex` first) |
| New game images, no rebuild | `fpga/patch_bit.sh <dir with top.bit + kc.mmi> obj_dir/top_hex/kc_chip8_vtrace <out> [program]` (rename the release files to `top.bit` / `kc.mmi`) |

`patch_bit.sh` works as before, with two limits:
- The palette still needs a rebuild.
- The script refuses images that put data in dmem 0x6000–0x7FFF, the per-lane stacks, because that range is distributed RAM on this core. Main's game ends near 0x5F00, close to that limit.

## Timing (core clock `clk0_raw` at 10 ns)

| Build | WNS | Failing endpoints |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline, extreme-hardware-optimizations at 100 MHz | −6.685 ns | ≥3000 |
| All pipeline cuts | −0.093 ns | 8 |
| All cuts + timing-driven directives, `build_20261108_105312_ff7f70` | **+0.100 ns** (hold +0.030) | 0 |
| Same RTL, main 7315b19 game images, `build_20261108_115553_1f9ddd` | **+0.100 ns** (hold +0.030) | 0 |

Every other clock (pixel, MIG/DDR) has positive slack. Utilization is 27,340 LUT / 14,971 FF / 111.5 BRAM36 / 48 DSP. The margin is thin (0.1 ns) and depends on the timing-driven directives.

## Simulator, main 7315b19 merged in (63f42c4)
- `make check`: **200 targets passed**.
- `t_top_frame`, 160×120: the pipelined core's frames are byte-identical to the multi-cycle core's (2 frames, both the 160×120 framebuffer and the 640×480 VGA output).
- Replay: a fixed-timestep build of main's game (`KC_FIXED_DT=1 KC_TAG_PERSIST=1`) with `s2_session.keys` gives retire traces identical to the multi-cycle core over 30 frames.

| Frame (main's game) | Multi-cycle core at 50 MHz | Pipelined core at 100 MHz |
|---|---|---|
| 160×120 | 596,341 cycles = 83.8 fps | 246,623 cycles = **405.5 fps** |
| 320×240 | 2,296,081 cycles = 21.8 fps | 941,471 cycles = **106.2 fps** |

For comparison, the shipped pipelined core (#63) at 50 MHz was 209,190 cycles (239 fps) and 804,185 cycles (62 fps).

## Hardware: Arty A7-100T, `build_20261108_115553_1f9ddd`, 160×120 game
- The board was claimed (`taking-board`) and released (`releasing-board`) on #1.
- UART: `kc: boot`, `kc: ddr3 chunk store ready`, then the chunk tag nonce.
- Error LED (H5) off, both after programming and after the soak (JTAG boundary scan).
- Live video on the capture card, with terrain, HUD and crosshair rendering correctly.
- **59.4 new frames/s while turning**. That's the 60 Hz display cap.
- Live play over the UART: walk, look up and down, break a block, place, turn, strafe and jump all respond. In the captured frames, a broken block disappears.
- 60 s soak: no blank or frozen frames.

## Changes, one commit per cut
- **Build flow:**
  - `CORE_MHZ` on `rtl/top.sv` (default 50) and the `top_s2p100` target;
  - deeper path reports;
  - Vivado limited to 14 threads;
  - timing-driven directives (`kc_timing_opt`) for `top_s2p100`.
- **mmio:** CYCLES advances every second core cycle at 100 MHz.
- **core_pipe:**
  - QRCP over 8 MEM cycles;
  - MEM completion computed a cycle ahead;
  - registered ray-unit strobes;
  - registered EX redirect;
  - registered LSU bus request and read data (`lsu_pipe.sv`);
  - per-lane registered forward selects;
  - a dedicated address adder;
  - the JALR uniformity check moved to MEM;
  - a shorter ALU path;
  - fetch stage F2 (registered imem output);
  - two-cycle MUL;
  - registered slow window accesses.
- **Shared blocks, parameterized so the multi-cycle builds are unchanged:**
  - vtrace: registered axis select, and the world check is off the data muxes;
  - framebuffer: 3-cycle reads on pipelined tops;
  - chunk engine: DDR3 beat buffer on pipelined tops;
  - DDR bridge: CDC bus skew is 10 ns.
- **Tests:**
  - new hazard cases in `t_pipe_stress`;
  - the second result region it needs;
  - updated CPI / QRCP / MMIO / LSU-order expectations.

New pipelined CPI rows are in the README:
- taken mispredict / mask writer: 5 cycles (flush 4);
- load: N+3;
- QRCP: 8;
- MUL: 2.

## Open
- Continued live testing of the game on the board before acceptance.
- 320×240 hasn't been run on the board yet. The 320 images aren't in this bitstream.
- `sx/stallA` and `sx/stallB` are local, unbuilt branches. They would add timing margin if needed.

author: new-usemame
body:
Fixes the held-place reason @sgreadly found on #2804.

A Kobo download row from before CWNG recorded finished downloads has no `completed_at` and no file identity. If its post-download annotation request came back empty, `restore_state` is `empty`, and `completed_kepub_identity` rightly refuses it as proof, so the Kobo keeps its own place. The DEBUG reason had no branch for that row and fell through to "the library KEPUB was written at X, after this Kobo's download at Y", even when X was before Y (book 99 on #2804: written 01:36 UTC, downloaded 10:52 UTC).

Now:

- That row shape says the download is from before CWNG recorded finished downloads and that removing the download on the Kobo and downloading the book again fixes it.
- The last line only says "written after the download" when the times say so.

Only the DEBUG text changes. Which place a Kobo is sent is unchanged.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_2804_held_reason_pre_tracking_download.py` drives the real Kobo `GET /state` route in the share-place span world. The pre-tracking case failed on `main` with the exact misstatement from the report (written 11:18, "after" a download at 20:18) and passes with the fix; the second test keeps the true "written after" case worded as before. The surrounding Kobo place and download-proof suites pass.

author: vimalkryadav
body:
Administrators now have a searchable, downloadable operating guide inside the dashboard and a local MCP bridge for reporting and named administrative actions. The two repository guides contain 36 sections covering onboarding, request inspection, quota/value interpretation, operations, recovery and the complete MCP setup/tool reference. The guide is loaded on demand so its Markdown renderer and content do not enlarge the initial admin page bundle.

The TypeScript stdio bridge uses the official MCP SDK and existing HTTPS admin APIs. It exposes 15 reporting/documentation tools, seven optional administrative actions, two separately enabled sensitive-capture tools, two guide resources and two investigation prompts. Sessions are private, origin-bound, owner-only files; writes revalidate the administrator session and CSRF, validate bounded arguments and never retry automatically. Redirects, arbitrary routes/commands, key issuance and provider inference are excluded. Action hints/confirmation arguments are not presented as proof of human approval. The gateway remains the authorization authority.

Approval/rejection, access revocation and direct member creation/revocation now record the verified actor and bounded metadata transactionally in the existing action log. No credentials or captured bodies are added to those records; existing role policy is preserved. No schema or shared-infrastructure changes.

Validation: Maven verify passed (103 Java tests passed, nine gated integration tests skipped locally; 16 frontend tests passed), 39 Python tests passed, and 14 MCP protocol/transport/tool tests passed. A real SDK stdio client negotiates the protocol and reads guide resources. Playwright/CDP checked all 36 guide sections at 1440/768/390px (108 layout checks), search, deep links and downloads with no JavaScript errors. MCP action mappings are exercised against isolated fixtures; no production member is used as an action test.

Live acceptance completed after release 0ce090c26ddd5f3487b8b231de470ceb3467963f: the guide passed all 108 chapter/viewport checks plus search, deep links and downloads; the other eight admin views passed 24 layout checks. A real stdio MCP client completed ten reporting calls over the production Cloudflare URL with 22 advertised tools, sensitive-content tools disabled and no production admin actions executed. The release is stable and audit-ready, with the edge, tunnel, broker, worker, database and sole-admin roles unchanged.

author: okedeji
body:
## Summary

#137 measured what the operator's 512Mi default covers: some 4,000 workloads. Past that it's OOM-killed, and 100,000 pods behind 10,000 Deployments peaked at 976 MiB. This PR cuts what the operator caches, then sets the default from what it measures.

- **The cache trim** (`controller.TrimPodTemplate`, `cmd/main.go`):
  - **Deployments and StatefulSets that are targets:** their pod template is cut to what the operator reads. That's the labels; each container's name, ports, env, envFrom, requests and restart policy, and whether it has a readiness or startup probe; PVC volumes, the grace period, readiness gates and pod resources.
  - **The template's hash** is kept with it, so deploy detection and the hashes already in status are unchanged.
  - **Size:** a Deployment drops from 13,940 to 9,514 bytes.
  - **Pods:** their requests ride in `Spec.Overhead`, so a cached pod needs no container. That's 2,700 down to 2,235 bytes.
- **Why the trim is safe:** every write to every type was listed.
  - **Not trimmed:** ManagedWorkloads (updated from the cache), the NEG forwarders' Deployments (patched from the cache), and the doorman's EndpointSlices.
  - **Target writes never use the cached copy:** a pause record is a merge patch built from scratch, and a scale is read fresh from the API server.
  - **No reader of a cached pod uses its containers:** the forwarder reads its pods from the API server, and `nodescale.Blockers` is the plugin's.
- **The default:** `resources.limits.memory` goes from 512Mi to **1280Mi**. The request stays at 128Mi.
  - **What it covers:** 10,000 workloads at 794 MiB, or 100,000 pods behind 10,000 Deployments at 954 MiB, each with a fifth to spare.
  - **Held by a test:** `TestOperatorBinary` reads the limit from `values.yaml` and holds both clusters to it.
  - **Matched:** the kustomize install says the same.
- **Shutdown:** a reconcile stopped because the operator is shutting down is no longer logged as an error, sets no `RoutingFailed` condition, and isn't counted in `napwake_reconcile_errors_total`. Every other error is reported as before.
- **Two small fixes:** the docs build's i18n warning is gone, and the e2e skill's one-spec recipe checks the preloaded images.

## Peak resident memory, before and after

| Cluster | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 4,000 workloads | 392 MiB | 361 MiB |
| 10,000 workloads | 875 MiB | 775 MiB |
| 100,000 pods, 10,000 Deployments | 976 MiB | 858 MiB |

## Tests
- **The trim's tests:**
  - `TestTrimPodTemplate_KeepsWhatTheOperatorReads`: each of the 16 kept fields, dropped in turn, fails it.
  - `TestTrimPodTemplate_ReadersAgree`: every reader gives the same answer on the trimmed template as on the whole.
  - `TestTrimTarget`.
- **The shutdown's tests:** `TestRouteDoorman_AStoppedReconcileIsNoFailure` and `TestReconcile_AStoppedReconcileIsNoError`.
- **The gates:**
  - **`go test -race -count=1 ./...`:** ok;
  - **lint:** 0 issues, sizing tag included;
  - **make:** `check-chart`, `test-alerts`, `test-doorman-policy` and `verify-generated` pass;
  - **docs:** the build passes.

## Merging
This carries two commits cherry-picked from #137: the sizing harness, and the preload by digest. Merge #137 first; then `main` is merged into this branch.

author: blockwill-dev
body:
## Why
Security audit OB-09 / PLAT-22: the container ran as root, base images were unpinned (`python:3.11-slim`, `uv:latest`), and the install ignored `uv.lock`.

## What changed
- `python:3.11-slim` (3.11.18) and `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9.18` (same as `mise.toml`) pinned by digest.
- Dependencies installed with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` into `/app/.venv`, so the image gets exactly what `uv.lock` pins. Code and venv stay root-owned.
- The server runs as `app` (uid 10001).
- `plane_mcp/storage.py`: the file token store checks at startup that `TOKEN_STORE_DIR` is writable. Without this, an unwritable mount let the server start but every sign-in failed with a 500.

## Deploy note
Production mounts Azure Files at `/mnt/tokens` with no `mountOptions`. If that mount is not writable by uid 10001, the new revision fails at startup with `TOKEN_STORE_DIR '/mnt/tokens' is not writable`. Safe either way: before deploying, set the `tokens` volume's mount options to `uid=10001,gid=10001,dir_mode=0700,file_mode=0600` (root can still use it, so the current image keeps working).

## Check
- `docker build` OK. Ran the image in HTTP mode as uid 10001 with a writable token dir: OAuth discovery endpoints 200, `/http/mcp` and `/http/api-key/mcp` 401 without valid credentials, client registration 201 and written to the encrypted store.
- Same image with a root-owned 0755 token dir: exits at startup with the clear error above.
- New `tests/test_token_store_dir.py`: an unwritable directory fails at start. `pytest`: 1216 passed, 32 skipped; the only 2 failures are the README count tests fixed by #1.

author: maxjivi05
body:
## Problem

Adding an app from GitHub with a link to one release asset installed a different AppImage. For example, the link `.../Eglantine/releases/download/build-129/eglantine-<commit>-linux-aarch64.AppImage` installed `...-linux-aarch64-pgo.AppImage`.

`UserApps.githubRepo` keeps only `owner/repo` from the link, and `pickAsset` then takes the first ARM64 AppImage of the newest release. Updates repeated that choice, so the app could also switch variants on its own.

## Fix

- **Read the asset:** a `releases/download/<tag>/<file>.AppImage` link now also yields the asset name (`UserApps.githubAsset`).
- **Pick the same variant:** the newest release's asset with that exact name is preferred. Otherwise, the asset with the same variant is chosen. Variant means the name's words with versions and commit hashes ignored, so `-pgo` vs plain or `aarch64` vs `x86_64` stay apart, while a new build's hash or version doesn't matter.
- **Remember it:** the installed asset name is saved with the app (`github-asset`). "Check for updates" then follows the same variant, including apps added from a plain repo link.
- **Unchanged:** with no linked asset, or no matching variant, the existing ARM64-first choice applies.

## Tests

- `LinuxFexTest`:
  - a linked build-129 asset picks its non-PGO twin in a later daily release, whose names have no commit hash;
  - a PGO link keeps PGO;
  - an unrelated link falls back to the default;
  - only release-download `.AppImage` links name an asset, including URL-encoded names.
- **Device:** RedMagic Astra 2, with this PR's CI build (8c5c6b8).
  - Added Eglantine from the non-PGO link `releases/download/build-129/eglantine-a407703f…-linux-aarch64.AppImage`.
  - It installed the same variant from the newest release (`daily-20261107`), and `github-asset` records `eglantine-linux-aarch64.AppImage`, not the `-pgo` build.
  - Eglantine opens and shows its game list. Launching a game stops at the emulator's own missing-keys check (`keys for gen 0x17+ required`), not a DroidDeck problem.

author: jonathanaissu
body:
## The problem

The "Change password" form never contacted the server. It waited 0.8 seconds, saved the new password as plain text in the browser and reported "updated securely". The real password stayed the same, and the current password was never checked.

## What changed

- **New route `POST /api/auth/change-password`:** requires login, verifies the current password, stores the new one as a bcrypt hash, and rejects a new password that is under 8 characters or identical to the current one.
- **Profile page:** calls the new route and shows real error messages.
- **Clean-up:** plain-text passwords stored by the old version are removed from the browser the next time someone visits the site.
- **No silent fallback:** `getUserPasswordHash` and `updateUserPassword` throw if the database fails, rather than falling back to memory like the other database functions, so the app can't report a change that didn't happen.

## Limits

- Changing a password doesn't sign out other devices, because login tokens stay valid for up to 7 days. Moving to Supabase Auth would solve this.
- Not yet run against a real Supabase project; database behaviour is covered with a simulated client.

## How it was tested

- `npm run build` passes with type checking and linting.
- All 91 unit and API tests pass (10 new). All 7 browser tests pass (2 new), including the full form flow: a wrong current password shows an error, then the new password logs in and the old one doesn't.
- Four deliberate regressions (skipping the current-password check, not saving, storing unhashed, swallowing a database error) were each caught by the tests.

author: catati-ops
body:
## Why

Every Catati repo should work one pstack way, and an agent in a fresh `dev` cloud session should be able to install, verify and prove any change. `catati/dev` is becoming the home for the environment, conventions, templates and a shared CLI (#8). This PR groups the environment files in one folder first, so the root stays readable as the rest arrives.

Closes #11

## What changes

- The setup script, the environment variable template and the network allowlist now live together in the `env` folder.
- The variable template takes the standard name `.env.example`.
- The README links and the heading for the template rules point at the new paths.

## Risk

Low. The `dev` environment form holds a pasted copy of the setup script, the variables and the allowlist. The move changes none of them, so no current or new session behaves differently. The next paste after a change comes from the new paths. Old links to the root files, such as links in other repos or in closed issues, stop resolving on `main`.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

## Summary

Three `git mv` renames, each 100% similar, and 8 changed lines in `README.md`. No file content changes apart from the README paths.

## Evidence

The repo root holds only `README.md`, `env/` and git files (`ls -A`):

```
before: .git  README.md  example.env  network-allowlist.txt  setup.sh
after:  .git  README.md  env
```

`rg -n "example\.env|\bsetup\.sh\b|network-allowlist" .` finds only paths under `env/`. Before, it found 8 README lines with root paths, such as `README.md:11:| Setup script | Paste [setup.sh](setup.sh) |`. After, it finds 5 lines, each an `env/` path, such as `./README.md:11:| Setup script | Paste [env/setup.sh](env/setup.sh) |`. The two template lines now read `env/.env.example`, which the pattern does not match. The same search with `--hidden` finds no reference inside the moved files.

`git diff -M --summary origin/main...HEAD` shows renames with no content change:

```
 rename example.env => env/.env.example (100%)
 rename network-allowlist.txt => env/network-allowlist.txt (100%)
 rename setup.sh => env/setup.sh (100%)
```

`git diff -M --stat origin/main...HEAD`:

```
 README.md                                          | 16 ++++++++--------
 example.env => env/.env.example                    |  0
 network-allowlist.txt => env/network-allowlist.txt |  0
 setup.sh => env/setup.sh                           |  0
 4 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)
```

`shellcheck env/setup.sh` (shellcheck 0.11.0) exits 0.

## Guards

None

## Merge Danger

- Door: two-way. A revert puts the three files back at the root.
- Blast Radius: the README and anyone who links to the root file paths. Cloud sessions are not affected.

</details>

author: sonaszjojka
body:
## Summary
Arrows now show when and where they attach, and an existing arrow can be re-attached. Before, ADR 0048 bound an end only while the arrow was drawn, nothing on screen showed it, and a selected arrow had only box handles, so its ends could not be dragged.

- A single selected arrow has a round handle on each end instead of a box. Dragging an end snaps it onto the outline of the shape under it and attaches it, or frees it over empty space. One drag is one undo step.
- The shape an end would attach to is outlined (along its own outline) while an arrow is drawn, while an end is dragged and while the Arrow tool hovers over a shape.
- Moving or resizing the shape keeps the arrow attached (existing `followBindings`).
- ADR 0052 (partly supersedes the "cannot be re-attached yet" sentence of ADR 0048). No document, storage or server change.
- Lines keep the box frame; bending and binding to lines are roadmap 4.6 and 4.7.

## Done when
- [x] Failing scenario reproduced first: the editor tests were written before the code and failed (re-attach, highlight); written up in #135.
- [x] Target highlighted while an end is near it, end snaps to the outline: `editor.test.ts`, `render.test.ts`, browser check light and dark.
- [x] Dragging an existing end onto a shape attaches it, dragging away detaches it: `editor.test.ts`, `e2e/tests/editing.spec.ts` (both modes).
- [x] Moving or resizing the shape keeps the arrow attached: `editor.test.ts` and e2e (move and resize steps).

## Review
- Plan review (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, medium): 2 findings, 2 accepted (stale preview state after keyboard actions; style bar needs the selection frame).
- Code review round 1 (medium): 1 bug, 1 rule. Bug: Shift-click on an end handle did not toggle the selection (fixed in 5b8b15d, unit test). Rule: no e2e for resizing the target (a39324d). 0 disagreements, 0 cleanups.
- Code review round 2 (medium, fix commits only): clean.
- Retest (Codex, medium): pass. Highlight, attach, detach, move, resize and Shift-click verified in light and dark; full e2e green in both modes and three browsers. Not checked: the #135 reproduction comment, posted separately.

## How to test
1. `cd web && npm run dev`, draw an ellipse and a free arrow, select the arrow.
2. Drag an end onto the ellipse: it snaps to the outline and the ellipse is outlined while you drag. Drag it away: it detaches.
3. Move or resize the ellipse: the arrow end follows.
4. `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` in `web/`; `npm test` in `e2e/`.

Closes #135

author: micahwhitephd
tannevaled
body:
M2 W4d: static locals and `main(argc, argv)` in `wasmgen`, plus a W4a defect the census exposed.

## What

- **Static locals.** Each one gets its own segment and a local symbol named `fn.name`, as clang names them. The symbol exists before the initialiser runs, so `static int *p = &p;` works.
- **`int main(int argc, char *argv[])`.** It is defined as `__main_argc_argv`, without a `main` symbol, which is what clang emits (checked with `llvm-objdump -t`) and the name BasicCABI.md specifies. wasi-libc's `__main_void` calls it. Other parameter lists are refused.

## Defect found by the census

`staticInit` wrote through a pointer into `m.o.Segments`. A string literal in the initialiser appends a segment, which can move the slice, so the relocation went to the old array. The static `{"foo" + 1}` of `pr53084.c` read 0.

The same pattern was in `object()`, for an initialised definition that follows a tentative one. Control: reverting that site gives 0 instead of 97. `initSegment` now initialises a copy and writes it back by index.

## Verification

- New `TestAgainstClang` programs: static locals (scalars, an address of a static, an array, a struct), `main(argc, argv)` (also called recursively), and both segment cases.
- Control: not running a static local's initialiser fails the two static-local programs.
- gcc torture census: **1049 same as clang, 0 different**, 2 known differences (1005 after W4c). The floor is raised to 1049.

The strings now come from the language the app is showing, and pending reminders are reworded when you change the language. *Tests:* the language reminders are written in matches what a `MaterialApp` shows for the same phone settings (chosen language, phone language, or a phone language the app doesn't have). Both now open the meeting itself, as the Meetings tab does, and the dashboard reloads when you come back. *Tests:* routed widget tests for a meeting without a deal and one with a deal. Merging adds server-independent GitHub monitoring. The deployed website stays unchanged because automatic Vercel Git deployments are disabled. CI must pass before merge.

- **Search:** `search_source`, `search_query_daily`, `search_page_daily`
- **Content:** `content_page`, `content_version`, `content_publish`, `content_redirect`
- **Claims:** `claims_version`
- **Reports:** `marketing_report`, `marketing_report_action`
- **Forum:** `forum_thread`, `forum_reply`

Every table has:
- a `tenant_id`, with RLS on and forced, and the `tenant_isolation` policy;
- a `pack:marketing` table comment;
- grants for `cs_runtime`, written by hand: only the verbs each table needs;
- foreign keys to the same client's rows, made of the row id plus `tenant_id`.

Version and history rows are only ever inserted. Triggers enforce this, and let only the named status columns change.

## Checks

- `packs/marketing/src/schema.test.ts` checks every table: the Drizzle schema matches the database, RLS and the policy, comments, exact grants, triggers, and that `cs_worker` cannot read or write another client's rows.
- `packages/db` `migrations.test.ts` and `purgeClient` pass.

## QA impact

none: this adds tables only; there is no screen or route yet.

body:
## Problem

The provider model cards and endpoint editor fall back to `chat · Assumed` when imported model metadata has no confirmed endpoint declaration. For known OpenAI models this hides documented Responses support even when the router already uses that protocol.

## Change

Resolve display metadata from an explicit, provider-scoped list of documented OpenAI model capabilities before using the assumed fallback:

- GPT-6, GPT-5.6 and other explicitly documented chat models show both `chat` and `responses`.
- The documented Pro entries show only `responses`.
- Operator overrides and confirmed/inferred endpoint declarations retain precedence.
- Unknown IDs, unlisted snapshots and other providers retain their existing behavior; there is no broad GPT-prefix heuristic.
- The badges and the editor's initial checkbox selection use the same resolved values.

The inferred label distinguishes model-ID-derived display metadata from a provider declaration or operator override. This is deliberately display-only: no persisted capability records, dispatch rules, endpoint gates or credentials change. Opening the editor does not save an override.

## Official references

Capabilities were checked against the individual model pages on 2026-11-08:

- [GPT-6 Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna)
- [GPT-5.6 Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna)
- [GPT-6.1 Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol)
- [GPT-5.5 Pro](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.5-pro)
- [GPT-5.4 Pro](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-pro)

## Validation

- Before the fix: six new regression cases failed.
- After the fix: 14 endpoint-editor UI tests passed.
- Ten existing endpoint-evidence, endpoint-guard and override tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck:core` passed.
- The isolated backport to the existing deployment fork passed the same checks.
- Commit hooks passed. No full-repository-suite claim is made.

Only the shared display resolver, endpoint editor and its regression tests are changed. Fork deployment configuration is excluded.

## Isolated deployment verification

The fix was backported to the existing deployment fork and built through GitHub Actions. The deployed application is healthy with zero restarts; authenticated provider, combo and key reads return HTTP 200 with unchanged counts. The public provider-page JavaScript bundle contains both the dual-endpoint and Responses-only display logic. The pre-existing deployment-specific login correction was preserved; other containers were not restarted. A consistent database backup passed integrity and foreign-key checks.

The live browser interaction was not completed because the operator was using the browser. Editor behavior is covered by the automated UI tests above. Separate fork-only workflow cleanup is not included in this PR.

author: palmoni5
body:
## מה

בניות Windows לשחרור (x64 ו-ARM64) אורזות `flutter_windows.dll` שבנינו מ-Flutter 3.47.7 עם תיקוני נגישות, במקום ה-DLL הרשמי.

- פעולה מורכבת חדשה: `.github/actions/patched-flutter-engine/action.yml` (קלט `arch`: `x64` / `arm64`).
- נקראת ב-`build_windows` וב-`build_windows_arm64` שב-`build-and-announce.yml`, מיד אחרי התקנת Flutter. שום workflow אחר לא בונה Windows לשחרור (`flutter_tests.yml` בונה debug, `tool/perf_probe` בונה profile כברירת מחדל (release אופציונלי, לא לפרסום) — אלה נשארים עם המנוע הרשמי).
- אחרי `flutter build windows` כל אחד משני ה-jobs משווה את `build\windows\<arch>\runner\Release\flutter_windows.dll` ל-`PATCHED_FLUTTER_DLL_SHA256` (הפעולה כותבת אותו ל-`GITHUB_ENV`) ונכשל אם ה-DLL שנארז אינו המתוקן.
- `build_windows` שומר את ה-SDK ב-cache במפתח נפרד (`cache-key: 'flutter-:os:-:channel:-:version:-:arch:-:hash:-patched-engine'`), כך שמפתח ברירת המחדל של flutter-action לא מקבל את ה-DLL המתוקן.
- `AGENTS.md`: פריימים של `flutter_windows.dll` בגרסאות ש-`build-and-announce.yml` מפרסם מפוענחים עם ה-PDB שלנו, שנבחר לפי ה-GUID בשורת `Module PDB:` של הרשומה.

## למה

- **flutter/flutter#196183** (תיקון מוצע ל-upstream מהענף palmoni5/flutter:a11y-visible-ranges-perf) — `ITextProvider::GetVisibleRanges` ריבועי במספר השורות של צומת טקסט. כל לקוח UI Automation (קורא מסך, Narrator, כלי נגישות) תוקע את חוט הפלטפורמה לשניות על ספרים ארוכים. באוצריא, על שלושה מסכי ספר: מ-145–892ms לסבב (עד 164ms לקריאה) ל-16–110ms (עד 7ms לקריאה).
- **flutter/flutter#175041** (PR ל-upstream: flutter/flutter#195448) — עדכון סמנטיקה עם מעבר אב מקונן נדחה, ואחריו כל עדכון נכשל והנגישות מתה; בשחרור גם מחיקה מחוץ לתחום וקריאה דרך מצביע תלוי.

המנוע: ענף `otzaria-3.47.7` ב-https://github.com/palmoni5/flutter, שחרור `otzaria-3.47.7-a11y.1`. אותם ארגומנטי GN כמו המנוע הרשמי, מעל מנוע `deb287481e3ce9468f3434937ced4240a70539ca`. ה-headers, הייצואים וה-`gen_snapshot.exe` זהים לרשמיים ולא מוחלפים.

## איך זה עובד

1. מוודא ש-`flutter --version --machine` מדווח `engineRevision` = `deb287481e…`. בשדרוג Flutter השלב נכשל במפורש במקום לארוז DLL שלא תואם ל-snapshot.
2. `flutter precache --windows` — מוריד את ארטיפקטי Windows **לפני** ההחלפה. ב-ARM64 ה-SDK משוכפל מ-git ואין בו עדיין `windows-arm64-release`; בלי זה `flutter build windows` היה מחלץ את הארטיפקטים הרשמיים מעל הקבצים שלנו.
3. מוריד את הזיפ מהשחרור עם `curl --retry 5 --retry-all-errors`, משווה SHA-256 לערך המוצמד ונכשל באי-התאמה.
4. מעתיק את ארבעת הקבצים (`flutter_windows.dll`, `.pdb`, `.lib`, `.exp`) ל-`$FLUTTER_ROOT/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/windows-<arch>-release/`. כל הארבעה מוחלפים כי `UnpackWindows` מעתיק את כולם ל-`windows/flutter/ephemeral`, וה-runner מקושר מול `flutter_windows.dll.lib` (`windows/flutter/CMakeLists.txt`).
5. מריץ `flutter precache --windows` שוב, בודק שה-hash של ה-DLL לא השתנה, וכותב אותו ל-`GITHUB_ENV` לבדיקת התוצר אחרי הבנייה.

**למה flutter לא יוריד מחדש:** ב-`flutter_tools` (`cache.dart`, `CachedArtifact.isUpToDate` / `EngineCachedArtifact.isUpToDateInner`) הארטיפקט נחשב עדכני כשקובץ ה-stamp (`bin/cache/windows-sdk.stamp`) שווה למהדורת המנוע והתיקיות קיימות. אין בדיקת תוכן או hash של הקבצים, ולכן אחרי `precache` ההחלפה נשמרת עד `--force` או שינוי מהדורה.

## Hashes מוצמדים

| קובץ | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `flutter_windows-windows-x64-release.zip` | `cc04e8c75d7b8740b3b2705e87a9f9d6839366518ad1eb842e33c6efd2048818` |
| `flutter_windows-windows-arm64-release.zip` | `ed7d43bbc77af371cb44303d9484503417761c2ba36480982bc467552c888eab` |
| `windows-x64-release/flutter_windows.dll` | `e89c7edfa794498944cd2c3b442a17569e98ce2624b11e16f71b364520791e67` |
| `windows-arm64-release/flutter_windows.dll` | `a92ce0d8d9159d209955b38968530f298f516a1faa4c3b4c5008ff8465f040cf` |

PDB (מאומת מרשומת ה-RSDS בתוך ה-DLL): x64 `{9A3F8E48-5EA7-4A0A-8316-21352F723250}` age 1, arm64 `{7324F4D1-92B4-455F-BA47-E65B47E2E69B}` age 1. ה-PDB נמצא בזיפ של השחרור ב-palmoni5/flutter. לא מעלים אותו לשחרורי אוצריא (~250MB לארכיטקטורה).

## חפיפות עם PR-ים פתוחים

נבדק עם `git merge-tree --write-tree` מול ראש כל PR:

- #3403 (`build-and-announce.yml`, טיוטה) — מתמזג נקי. הוא עוקף את flutter/flutter#175041 בצד ה-runner (`accessibility_request_filter`). המנוע הזה מתקן את #175041 בבניות שחרור; בניות debug/profile עדיין משתמשות במנוע הרשמי, אז העקיפה עדיין נחוצה שם.
- #4519 (`build-and-announce.yml`, טיוטה) — מתמזג נקי.
- #4500 (`build-and-announce.yml`) — מתמזג נקי.
- #4269 (`AGENTS.md`) — מתמזג נקי.
- #4525 (`AGENTS.md`, איחוד של #4269) — מתמזג נקי.

## איך נבדק

- YAML של הפעולה ושל ה-workflow נטען ב-PyYAML. השלבים בשני ה-jobs מסודרים: התקנת Flutter, ואחריה החלפת המנוע.
- הסקריפט של השלב חולץ מה-YAML והורץ מקומית (Windows PowerShell 5.1) מול הזיפים המקומיים (`file://`). `flutter` הוחלף בפונקציה מדומה (פלט `--version --machine` עם באנר לפניו, `precache` ריק):
  - x64 ו-arm64: ארבעת הקבצים הועתקו, וה-hashes שלהם תואמים ל-`SHA256SUMS.txt`. `flutter_windows.h` הרשמי נשאר.
  - hash שגוי: נכשל עם `SHA-256 mismatch`.
  - מהדורת מנוע אחרת: נכשל לפני ההורדה.
  - URL חסר: נכשל.
  - בדיקת התוצר (חולצה מה-YAML של שני ה-jobs): עוברת כש-`flutter_windows.dll` בתיקיית הבנייה הוא המתוקן, ונכשלת כשמניחים שם את ה-DLL הרשמי.
- **בדיקת Release אמיתית ב-CI — x64 עברה:** [ריצה 42484608174](https://github.com/Otzaria/otzaria/actions/runs/42484608174/job/128743628011) התקינה Flutter 3.47.7 ו־engine `deb287481e3ce9468f3434937ced4240a70539ca`, הפעילה את אותה composite action כנגד SDK אמיתי, ביצעה `flutter precache --windows`, בנתה אפליקציית Flutter Windows מינימלית ב־`--release` והוכיחה ש־`flutter_windows.dll` שנארז מכיל SHA-256 `e89c7edfa794498944cd2c3b442a17569e98ce2624b11e16f71b364520791e67`. כל השלבים עברו. הבדיקה אינה בונה את האפליקציה המלאה ואינה מכסה בניית ARM64 אמיתית או שחזור תקיעת נגישות אצל משתמש. ה־Windows CI הרגיל של האפליקציה עדיין עלול להיכשל בגלל הורדות PDFium/SQLite שאינן קשורות לשלב ההחלפה.

## לשים לב

- השחרור [`otzaria-3.47.7-a11y.1`](https://github.com/palmoni5/flutter/releases/tag/otzaria-3.47.7-a11y.1) כבר פורסם; מחיקתו תכשיל כל בניית Windows בהורדה.
- **ה-cache של flutter-action:** `build_windows` משתמש במפתח cache נפרד עם הסיומת `-patched-engine`. ה-SDK עם ה-DLL המתוקן נשמר רק תחת המפתח הזה, ומפתח ברירת המחדל (שמשמש את `warm_flutter_cache.yml`, `flutter_tests.yml` וכו') לא מושפע. ב-ARM64 אין cache (ה-SDK משוכפל מ-git בכל ריצה).

## TODO

לחזור למנוע הרשמי כששני התיקונים (flutter/flutter#196183 ו-#195448) יגיעו ל-Flutter יציב: למחוק את `.github/actions/patched-flutter-engine`, את שתי הקריאות אליו, את בדיקות ה-hash אחרי `flutter build windows`, את שורת `cache-key` עם הסיומת `-patched-engine` ואת הפסקה ב-`AGENTS.md`. כל שדרוג Flutter לפני כן דורש לבנות מחדש את המנוע (השלב נכשל במפורש עד שזה נעשה).

Fixes #4518
Fixes #4547

author: jjavar1
body:
Fixes code issue #160

The bug was still present at 5bbd281. `UpdateCharacterInventoryRequest.Handle` (src/OWSCharacterPersistence/Requests/Characters/UpdateCharacterInventoryRequest.cs:56) passed a null `Inventory` straight to the Postgres `CharactersRepository.UpdateCharacterInventory`. That method locked the row, deleted every bag item, inserted from `updateCharacterInventory ?? Enumerable.Empty`, committed and returned Success=true.

The fix:
- `CharactersRepository.UpdateCharacterInventory` now checks for a null bag first and returns `InventoryFail("bad_request")` (Success=false, ReasonCode "bad_request") before it opens a connection. This is the same rule the combined `UpdateCharacterData` path already uses. An empty list still counts as a real empty bag and saves.
- `InsertInventoryItems` no longer has the `?? Enumerable.Empty` fallback. Both of its callers now refuse null first, so a null that slipped through would throw inside the transaction and roll back instead of quietly saving an empty bag.

I put the guard in the repository rather than in the request's Handle, as the proposal suggested, for three reasons: the DELETE lives there, it matches where `UpdateCharacterData` guards, and it covers every caller of the repository method. The request file is unchanged; the endpoint now returns the repository's bad_request response.

Two DB tests went into `UpdateCharacterDataTests.cs` next to `MissingInventoryKeepsBag`. Both go through the real `UpdateCharacterInventoryRequest.Handle` against Postgres:
- `StandaloneSaveWithMissingInventoryKeepsBag`: sends Inventory=null and expects Success=false, ReasonCode bad_request, the OldShield row still there and EconomyRevision unchanged.
- `StandaloneSaveWithEmptyInventoryEmptiesBag`: sends Inventory=[] and expects Success=true with an empty bag.

Committed as 68153c4 on this branch. Not pushed, no PR.

**How it was tested:** I started a throwaway postgres:14 container on 127.0.0.1:15499 (user postgres, password postgres, same as the CI service) and removed it afterwards. I didn't use the existing Postgres on localhost:5432; I don't have its credentials and it isn't the CI throwaway. OWS_TEST_POSTGRES pointed at the container and CI=true was set.

- Before the fix: StandaloneSaveWithMissingInventoryKeepsBag failed (Assert.False: Success came back true and the bag was wiped). StandaloneSaveWithEmptyInventoryEmptiesBag passed.
- After the fix, the CI steps from .github/workflows/ci.yml, run from src/:
  - `dotnet restore OWS.sln`
  - `dotnet build OWS.sln --configuration Release --no-restore`: 0 errors, 104 warnings, all already there before this change.
  - `dotnet test OWS.sln --configuration Release --no-build`: 460 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped. The skipped ones are the Valkey session-cache tests, which need a Valkey server that neither CI's workflow nor this run provides.
- UpdateCharacterDataTests and InventoryOwnerTokenTests together: 23/23 passed.

I didn't run the CI vulnerable-packages job; this change adds no packages.

**Not sure of:** - I didn't touch the MSSQL `UpdateCharacterInventory` (src/OWSData/Repositories/Implementations/MSSQL/CharactersRepository.cs:619). Per AGENTS.md it's dead code, the interface didn't change, and it still compiles.
- The failure is reported in the response body as Success=false with ReasonCode "bad_request" and HTTP 200, the same way the other inventory failures are reported. It's not an HTTP 400. The request-level `revision_required` check still runs before the null check when RequireExpectedRevision is on, so a request missing both fields reports revision_required. It's refused either way.

## Review
Built by Claude. Reviewed by Codex: approve in round 1.

- [#​16186](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16186) [`f1d81a2`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f1d81a20c8e535ec7cb870143283f4a683fec70d) Thanks [@​leostera](https://redirect.github.com/leostera)! - Support local Artifacts across Wrangler, Vite, and Workers Vitest

  Set `remote: false` on an Artifacts binding to opt into the Miniflare simulator and persistent local repositories during development. Omitted `remote` continues to use the deployed resource, with a warning that changes affect real repositories; `remote: true` explicitly selects it. When remote bindings are disabled (`wrangler dev --local`, or Vite's `remoteBindings: false`), Artifacts bindings use the local simulator. Workers Vitest uses the local simulator when `remote` is omitted, so tests do not change real repositories by accident; set `remote: true` to test against the deployed resource. Local development does not require Cloudflare credentials, but does require Git 2.32 or newer on the host.

  In Miniflare's own options, Artifacts bindings route like every other binding: only `dev.remote: true` with a remote proxy connection uses the deployed resource. Wrangler and Vite resolve the deployed-by-default rule, and Workers Vitest its local default, before passing options to Miniflare.

The bundles now include `brace-expansion` 2.1.7 (from 2.0.1) and 5.0.12 (from 5.0.5). Normal glob patterns expand as before; only the pathological patterns targeted by the advisories are handled differently.

- [#​16700](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16700) [`dc35efb`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dc35efbd3cdfe67b3ef972c75b8faae65dfed195) Thanks [@​cjol](https://redirect.github.com/cjol)! - Bump bundled `fast-xml-parser` from 4.4.1 to 4.5.5 to pick up security fixes

  Miniflare bundles `fast-xml-parser` into its local R2 S3 API, and Wrangler bundles it through the AWS SDK used by `wrangler pipelines`. Version 4.4.1 is affected by several published advisories, and 4.5.5 includes their fixes. XML handling does not change.

- [#​16700](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16700) [`dc35efb`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dc35efbd3cdfe67b3ef972c75b8faae65dfed195) Thanks [@​cjol](https://redirect.github.com/cjol)! - Bump bundled `minimatch` from 5.1.6 to 5.1.9 to pick up security fixes

  These packages bundle `minimatch`, and 5.1.6 is affected by published ReDoS advisories. Version 5.1.9 includes the fixes. 5.1.8 is skipped because it broke recursive `**` matching, which D1's `migrations_pattern` relies on.

- [#​16700](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16700) [`dc35efb`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dc35efbd3cdfe67b3ef972c75b8faae65dfed195) Thanks [@​cjol](https://redirect.github.com/cjol)! - Bump bundled `shell-quote` from 1.10.0 to 1.11.0 to pick up a security fix

  `shell-quote` is bundled into Wrangler, which uses it to parse and quote shell commands such as custom build and Pages dev commands. Version 1.10.0 is affected by a published advisory, and 1.11.0 includes the fix. Command parsing does not change.

- [#​16700](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16700) [`dc35efb`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dc35efbd3cdfe67b3ef972c75b8faae65dfed195) Thanks [@​cjol](https://redirect.github.com/cjol)! - Bump bundled `yaml` from 2.8.1 to 2.9.0 to pick up a security fix

## Change

This candidate replaces per-byte UTF-8 iterator equality and hashing in `ExactText` with a length-checked contiguous byte comparison and bulk byte hashing. It preserves exact-byte equality, including embedded NULs and canonically equivalent Unicode encoded with different bytes, along with equal-hash dictionary-key behavior.

Candidate commit: `a447398287a97222401ee58844514a503182d70f`.

## Verification

- The unchanged canonical `Scripts/verify.sh` wrapper ran the focused `ExactTextTests` suite on an isolated iOS 27.0 simulator: 2 passed, 0 failed.
- `git diff HEAD^ --check` passed.

## Performance status

This change targets the large `ExactText` equality and hashing CPU buckets seen in prior traces. No matched candidate timing run has been performed, so this PR makes no claim of lower main-thread CPU or lock wait. Keep it open and unmerged until the Product Owner's matched timing gate is satisfied. Record host load and booted simulator counts at the start and end of future timing runs.

author: adityakk9031
body:
### Summary
In `graphify/affected.py`, `affected_nodes(graph, seed)` seeds the reverse walk with the root's member nodes using one-hop outward `out_edges(seed)` where `relation in ("method", "contains")`.

While a 1-hop outward check seeds methods when `seed` is a class (`class --method--> method`), when `seed` is a file node (e.g. running `graphify affected path/to/file.py`), the file node's 1-hop outward edges only reach classes and top-level functions (`file --contains--> Class`). The methods of those classes sit two hops away (`file --contains--> Class --method--> Method`). Because the traversal only checked 1 hop from `seed`, class methods were never added to the seed queue.

Callers of class methods bind to method nodes rather than the file node, so querying `graphify affected <filepath>` returned an empty list (`[]`) for any callers that bind directly to methods inside that file's classes.

### Fix
Use a BFS queue (`member_queue`) to recursively traverse all outward `method` and `contains` relations starting from `seed`, seeding all nested members (including class methods inside a file) at depth 0. Added regression test in `tests/test_affected_member_seed.py`.

author: kapji
body:
The Revolut dividend-tax steps and the Trading 212 share-distribution note told readers to write a separate RAW file and pass it with `--raw-file`. Since #1278 cgt-calc refuses a second `--raw-file`, so a reader who already passes a RAW file, for a split or a spouse transfer for example, followed the guide into that refusal. Nothing was miscalculated; the run stopped.

## The fix

The guides now give the instruction #1363 gave in the Schwab gift sections and the RAW guide: add the rows to the RAW file you already pass, or start one if you do not use one yet.

- `revolut.md`, dividends and withholding tax: step 2 says to add the two rows to the RAW file already passed with `--raw-file`, or start one, and not to write a separate file for them. Step 3 passes the export and that RAW file. The example name is now `raw_data.csv`, as in the RAW guide, since the file may hold other rows.
- `revolut.md`, the check after step 3: it said the `Unknown` balance the RAW file adds is zero. That holds only while the file has just these rows, and a shared RAW file with cash rows has a balance of its own. It now says the two rows add nothing to that balance.
- `trading212.md`, share distributions: the distribution goes in the RAW file you pass with `--raw-file`, or a new one, instead of "a separate file".
- `schwab.md`, gifts in a complete export: the spouse bullet no longer says "through a small RAW file". The paragraph below it already says, for both bullets, to copy the line into your RAW file or start one.

The CSV rows, the tax explanation and the calculation are unchanged. No code changes.

body:
Builder overhaul W1: the Studio shell (docs/builder-ux.md). A level now opens straight into an in-world Studio on its map, replacing the layout editor, its menus and HUD, and the level page.

**What's in it**

- The dock (`Core/UI/ModDock.cs`, a new UI-kit piece) holds a top bar, a tool column, a palette, a right panel and a status line, with 24 px gutters.
  - Top bar: menu, level and pack name, unsaved dot, undo/redo, Snap, View, Problems badge, Play.
  - Palette: Slots, Scenery, Spawns, and Library (an `IAssetBrowser`; the default is `HostSceneryBrowser`).
  - Right panel: Inspector (multi-select, "—" for mixed values, one undo step per change), Outliner (filter chips, text filter, groups) and Level tab.
- Tools: Select (click, Shift add, Ctrl/Cmd toggle; a marquee from empty ground; dragging the selection moves it all as one undo step), Lasso, Paint select, Move (grab; X/Z lock an axis), Rotate, Place, Erase. W3's Link (K) and W4's Terrain (T) plug in through `Studio.AddTool`.
- Camera:
  - WASD pan, Q/E turn, wheel zoom.
  - Middle-drag pans. Right-drag pans past 6 px, and a shorter right click cancels the current action or opens the context menu.
  - F frames the selection, Home frames the whole level, and an optional edge pan is in Studio settings.
- Keys (context `BuilderStudio`, rebindable):
  - Delete: Backspace and Del.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y.
  - Cmd/Ctrl + D (duplicate), C/V (copy, paste), A (select all), G (group), Shift+G (ungroup), S (save).
  - H and Alt+H hide and show, X toggles x-ray, `,` and `.` turn, 1-9 recall recent kinds, Tab toggles the palette, F5 and Shift+F5 play.
- Input ownership: `Keybinds.ClaimExclusive` (in `Core/Keybinds.cs`) keeps every other mod key inert while the dock is on top, so Backspace no longer reaches UndoUpgrade ("Nothing to undo today").
- Groups are saved in `LevelDef.groups`. Labels are coloured by kind, never overlap and follow the zoom. Hover cards on objects. The game's HUD fades out while editing.
- Play mode: panels registered with `Studio.AddPanel(..., StudioMode.Play)` (W2's sandbox) get a passive dock that doesn't freeze the king. F5 out and back keeps the camera, selection and undo history.
- Removed: `LayoutEditor.cs`, `LayoutMenus.cs`, `LayoutHud.cs`, the level page, both first-use hints and the `layout-*` keys. `builder-level` forwards its editing subcommands to the new `builder-studio` dev command.

**Files outside W1's own (minimal or additive)**

- `Level/LevelOverlay.cs`: one line; the edit-load claim is now `StudioShell.ClaimSession` (W3's file).
- `Model/LevelDef.cs`: `groups` and `GroupDef`, additive.
- `Studio/Play/StudioPlayManager.cs`: `PlayKeys.Label` calls `StudioKeys.Label` because the old `Level.Keys` is gone (W2's file).
- UI kit: `ModPage.FieldIndent`, and an optional indent on `ModField`, so fields fit narrow panels (default unchanged).
- `KeybindsManager.ControlsScreen.cs`: `keybinds press` accepts chords such as `LeftCommand+Z`.
- `StudioApi.cs` additions since #80: `PointerOverUI`, `EditPack`, `AddPlaceHook`, `ItemPlaced` and `StudioServices.PropResolver`.

**Verified** on a pool instance (Nordfels) with `builder-studio` dev commands, scripted pointer gestures and screenshots:

- Marquee selected 21 objects. Backspace removed 14 of them, skipping the castle and the locked add-ons.
- Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z undo and redo. Cmd+D duplicates and grabs the copy, and Cmd+G groups.
- Moving 14 objects was one undo step ("Move 14 objects").
- Paint select works. The Inspector shows "—" for mixed costs, and a cost change on 3 slots was one undo step.
- Right-drag panned the camera, and a right click opened the context menu. Esc opened the Studio menu, and Leave returned to the pack screen.
- F5 to play showed the sandbox panel, and F5 back restored the editor.
- No PalaceMod errors in the log. 5 new unit tests in `tests/PalaceMod.Tests/StudioTests.cs`; all 141 pass.

author: davidshoval
body:
## Summary
The download page kept showing 1.4.0 well after 1.5.0 was published. `api.motionql.com/downloads/latest` returned 1.4.0 with `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`, so the stale answer came from the backend itself. GitHub's own API says v1.5.0. The backend calls the GitHub API without a token (no `GITHUB_TOKEN` on Render). That call has been failing, from GitHub's current incident with timeouts for unauthenticated users and the 60/hour limit shared per IP. On any failure, `latestRelease` served its last cached answer, with no end date.

When the API fails, the release is now read from its public release files, which don't go through the API:
- `releases/latest/download/latest.yml`, `latest-mac.yml` and `latest-linux.yml` give the version, the release date and most sizes.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` names every installer and its checksum.
- A HEAD request sizes the installers the yml files leave out (the deb and the Windows portable).

The old cached answer is served only when both sources fail, and a warning is logged either way.

## Testing
- New `test/downloads.test.ts`: the API answers 1.4.0, then fails 11 minutes later. The result is 1.5.0 from the release files, with sizes, checksums and the date, not the cached 1.4.0. Also covers the yml size parser.
- Live run against github.com with the API forced to fail: it returns 1.5.0 with all 8 installers and real sizes.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` are clean. I couldn't run the Mongo-backed suites here because the MongoDB test binary can't be downloaded in this environment. The existing API-path test is unchanged.

author: jmin12663
body:
### 변경 사항

화면에 그대로 보이는 오류 문구(`detail`)의 형식과 단위를 맞추고, 고치는 방법이 보이게 다듬었습니다.

- 크기 단위를 `KB`·`MB`로 통일했습니다(`2MiB` → `2MB`). 한도 값은 그대로입니다(2MB = 2,097,152바이트).
- 파일·값은 따옴표로 감싸 문장 안에 넣습니다. 예: `없는 태그예요: dp` → `'dp' 태그가 없어요`
- `slug` 같은 개발 용어를 뺐습니다(`CONCEPT_TAG_EXISTS`).
- 예제 실행에도 쓰이는 `SOURCE_TOO_LONG` 문구에서 "제출"을 뺐습니다.
- 재설정에도 쓰이는 `SAME_PASSWORD` 문구에서 "현재 비밀번호"를 뺐습니다.

| code | 전 | 후 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SOURCE_TOO_LONG`(제출·예제 실행) | 코드는 64KB까지 제출할 수 있어요 | 코드가 64KB를 넘어요. 64KB 이하로 줄여 주세요 |
| `SOURCE_TOO_LONG`(정답 코드) | 정답 코드는 64KB까지 넣을 수 있어요 | Python 정답 코드가 64KB를 넘어요 |
| `TEST_CASE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 3번째 케이스의 입력이 2MiB를 넘어요 | 3번째 케이스의 입력이 2MB를 넘어요 |
| `TEST_CASE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 케이스를 모두 합쳐 10MiB를 넘어요 | 모든 케이스의 합이 10MB를 넘어요 |
| `TEST_CASE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`(ZIP) | hidden/3.in이 2MiB를 넘어요 | 'hidden/3.in' 파일이 2MB를 넘어요 |
| `ZIP_INVALID` | 규칙에 맞지 않는 파일이 있어요: x. sample/ 또는… | 'x' 파일 이름이 규칙에 맞지 않아요. sample/ 또는… |
| `ZIP_INVALID` | 번호가 같은 파일이 있어요: a, b | 'a', 'b' 파일의 번호가 같아요. 하나만 남겨 주세요 |
| `ZIP_INVALID` | 짝이 없는 파일이 있어요: x | 'x' 파일의 짝이 없어요. N.in과 N.out을 함께 넣어 주세요 |
| `ZIP_INVALID` | UTF-8이 아닌 파일이 있어요: x | 'x' 파일이 UTF-8이 아니에요. UTF-8로 저장해 다시 올려 주세요 |
| `TAG_NOT_FOUND` | 없는 태그예요: dp | 'dp' 태그가 없어요 |
| `CONCEPT_TAG_EXISTS` | 이미 있는 태그 이름이나 slug예요 | 같은 이름이나 같은 영문 이름의 태그가 이미 있어요. 다른 이름을 입력해 주세요 |
| `SAME_PASSWORD` | 현재 비밀번호와 달라야 해요 | 지금 쓰는 비밀번호와 같아요. 다른 비밀번호를 입력해 주세요 |
| `PASSWORD_MISMATCH` | 비밀번호가 일치하지 않아요 | 비밀번호 확인이 일치하지 않아요. 같은 비밀번호를 입력해 주세요 |
| `CODE_MISMATCH` | 인증번호가 맞지 않아요 | 인증번호가 맞지 않아요. 메일로 받은 인증번호를 다시 확인해 주세요 |
| `MAIL_FAILED` | …1분 뒤 다시 시도해 주세요 | …1분 후 다시 시도해 주세요 |
| `JUDGE_UNAVAILABLE` | 지금은 검증할 수 없어요 | 현재 채점할 수 없어요. 잠시 후 다시 시도해 주세요 |

### `code` 없는 오류

화면이 미리 막는 오류라 `code`가 없습니다. `detail`이 Spring 기본 영어 문구(`Maximum upload size exceeded` 등)거나 비어 있습니다.
화면은 `code`가 없으면 `detail`을 쓰지 않고 상태별 문구를 보여 주므로, 사용자에게는 보이지 않습니다. 그래서 코드는 그대로 두고,
openapi `ProblemDetail`에 "`code`가 없으면 `detail`은 개발용이라 화면에 보여 주지 않는다"를 적었습니다.

### 명세

- `contracts/openapi.yaml`: 테스트케이스 크기 단위 `MiB` → `MB`, `ProblemDetail` 설명
- `docs/feature-spec.md`: COM-08·MY-03의 `SAME_PASSWORD` 문구
- `web/src/api/schema.d.ts`: 다시 생성

### 테스트

임시 테스트로 ZIP 오류 문구가 위 표대로 나오는 것을 확인했고, 테스트 파일은 커밋하지 않았습니다. 기존 테스트도 모두 통과했습니다.

### 웹

화면이 직접 적은 문구와 목업의 오류 문구는 별도 이슈로 서버와 맞출 예정입니다.
그 전까지는 화면에서 먼저 막히는 경우 옛 문구가 보일 수 있습니다.

- 관리자 테스트케이스 화면(`testCasesSchema.ts`, `TestCasesTab.tsx`): `2MiB`·`1MiB`·`10MiB` → `MB`
- 마이페이지 비밀번호 변경(`AccountSettings.tsx`): `현재 비밀번호와 달라야 해요`, `비밀번호가 일치하지 않아요`
- 가입(`SignupPage.tsx`), 재설정(`PasswordResetPage.tsx`): `비밀번호가 일치하지 않아요`
- 목업(`mocks/handlers.ts`)의 오류 문구
