author: fmflurry
body:
## Content

Three fixes so one session can ship several goals at once and clean each one up afterwards.

1. **Per-goal decision logs.** Each goal logs to `<main>/.claude/state/decisions/<slug>.tsv` (`<slug>` is the goal registry slug). With no goal bound, the log stays at `.claude/state/decisions.tsv`.
   - `agent-harness goal decisions-path` prints the right path for the current checkout.
   - `ship-init` creates the log with the show-your-work header and makes sure `.claude/state/` is excluded from git.
   - `cleanup`, which teardown runs, moves a merged goal's log to `decisions/archive/<slug>.tsv`. An escalated or blocked goal keeps its log where it is.
   - The autonomy hooks (`autonomy-context.sh`, `autonomy-ask-guard.sh`) name the per-goal path. In OpenCode, `ASK_DENIED` points at the command.
2. **Guards read the checkout the command runs in.** Before this, they read the session's working directory.
   - `pr-visual-report.sh` follows a leading `cd <dir> &&`, and maps `gh pr create --head <branch>` to the branch's registered goal worktree. It uses that checkout for the provenance and memory checks, and reads a relative `--body-file` from the cd target.
   - `autonomy-git-guard.sh` uses the goal of the checkout a `git push` or `gh pr create` runs in (`cd`, `git -C`, or `--head`), so that goal's own reviews gate it. There is no push fast path while any goal exists.
   - The rule that `ship-init` and teardown must run alone is unchanged.
3. **Teardown with Orca not running.** Master (0.4.38) already skips the Orca state for goals created `via: git`. The installed `~/.claude` copy is older, which is why the error still shows up. This PR adds a regression test with a fake orca that prints `runtime_unavailable` and exits 1. Neither `ship-merge` nor `cleanup` calls Orca.

Cursor plugin bumped to 0.4.39.

## QA tests

- `scripts/agent-harness/test/run.sh` (run without the session-injected `core.hooksPath`): 2354 passed, 75 failed. The same 75 checks fail on unchanged `origin/master`; they depend on the environment (GraphQL-down stubs, Chrome, the stop gate). None of the new checks fail.
- New checks:
  - `decisions-path` from the main checkout and from two goal worktrees;
  - `ship-init` creates the log with its header, and the logs stay separate and leave the main checkout clean;
  - teardown archives the log (git and orca), and an escalated goal keeps its log;
  - the hook messages name the per-goal path;
  - `cd`, `git -C` and `--head` resolution in the provenance and review guards;
  - teardown via git with orca `runtime_unavailable`.
- `npm test`: 273 passed, 4 failed. The 4 depend on the environment (a browser is on PATH, the kpi vendor test) and also fail on master. `npm run typecheck:strict` passes. `node scripts/cursor-plugin/check.mjs` passes. shellcheck reports no new warnings.

## Locked decisions

- The log lives in the main checkout's state dir, next to `goals/`, so it never dirties a worktree and survives teardown.
- Archiving happens in `cleanup`, so teardown and `ship-merge` share one code path. An archive name that is already taken gets a timestamp suffix.
- `gh pr create --head <branch>` is allowed under the review gate only when the branch maps to a registered goal worktree that has it checked out.
- Fail closed (security review round, d9eb64c): the guards switch to a target checkout's goal only when that goal is gated; otherwise the session's goal still gates. `--head owner:branch` and `--repo` must name origin. `.git/agent-harness/` is protected from shell writes. pr-visual-report denies any `cd` it cannot follow (`cd -`, `-P`, `~`, `$`, missing path, after `||`/`|`/`&`, `pushd`/`popd`/`builtin`).
- Allow-list (4524f57): pr-visual-report follows a `cd` only as `[VAR=] cd <dir> && gh ...` at the start of the line. Any other `cd` form, and any `gh pr create/new/edit` it does not reach in command position (`sh -c`, `env -C`, `xargs`, `exec`, `if/then`, brace groups, multi-line), denies.
- CDPATH (f1500d9): the followed `cd` target must be absolute or start with `./` or `../`; a `CDPATH=` prefix or a bare relative target denies.

## Non-blocking follow-ups

- `worktree-rm` (unregistered worktrees) still stops when the Orca state is unreadable.
- Reinstall `~/.claude` after merge: the installed teardown predates 0.4.38.

## Visual report

- [x] Skip Reason: harness shell scripts and hook messages only; nothing to render

author: leomo42
body:
Part of #700. Decided with the PROMOP owner in https://github.com/healthkey-ai/exact/issues/700#issuecomment-6715317334 (option A).

## Why

`PhrTokenProvider` keyed every portal identity as `phr:<user_id>`. For a PROMOP-issued family token, `user_id` is PROMOP's integer `Identity` pk. After a restore from a dump, PROMOP hands the same pk to a different person, who would then sign in as an existing exact `Identity` and inherit its saved filters and state. PROMOP's `sub` (`urn:local:<uuid4>`) is never reused, and PROMOP itself keys family tokens on it.

## What

`accounts/providers/phr.py`: the subject now follows the issuer, through one `_subject` helper that both the JWKS and the introspection paths use.

| issuer | `Identity.sub` |
|---|---|
| `healthkey-phr` (legacy phr) | `phr:<user_id>`, unchanged, so existing identities keep matching |
| anything else (PROMOP family auth) | the token's `sub` as issued; no `user_id` fallback |

A non-legacy token is **rejected** if its `sub` is absent, not a string, blank, or longer than the 255-char `Identity.sub` column. The last case would otherwise be a 500 on insert. On introspection, only an absent or null `sub` in the response falls back to the payload; a malformed one is a rejection.

The rule is derived from the issuer, not from a setting. Flipping it for an issuer that already has identities would re-provision every one of them, so a deploy should not be able to do that. The assumption this rests on is now in the docstring: PROMOP runs with its documented `FAMILY_AUTH_ISSUER` (its origin), not `healthkey-phr`.

No PROMOP-issued identities exist in exact yet, so there is nothing to migrate. The same rule applies to soc and labs (soc#325, hk-labs#59).

Also: `docs/setup.md` (`PHR_ISSUER` row), `.env.example`, and a comment in `accounts/models.py`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_phr_auth.py`: new `TestPromopSubject` and `TestPromopSubjectViaIntrospection`. They cover the subject as issued, `user_id` never used as the key, blank / non-string / oversized `sub` rejected, the reused-pk case, the legacy rule unchanged, and the two paths agreeing.
- `tests/test_partner_auth_chain.py`: the issuer-switch test now uses a PROMOP `sub`. Added an end-to-end test: two people with the same `user_id` get two Identities.
- Locally: `pytest tests/test_phr_auth.py tests/test_partner_auth_chain.py tests/test_identity_model.py`, 126 passed. With the provider reverted to `origin/dev`, 13 of the new tests fail.

## Review before push

Reviewed by `codex review` (no findings) and by a fresh-context review (no P1). Its P3s are fixed in the second commit: the empty-vs-blank fallthrough, the length cap, and stale comments.

## Deploy

Render staging switches to `dev` in healthkey-ai/phr#81. Find Trials is enabled separately, in healthkey-ai/phr#82, after this is deployed and sign-in is verified.

author: mikelward
body:
## Scope
This brings tide for Linux's keymap presets (mikelward/tide#389) to tide for Chrome, as a guide. Chrome has no API for an extension to set its own command keys, so a preset changes only the keys checklist's suggested column. You then enter the keys at `chrome://extensions/shortcuts`.

- A **Start from** choice in the keys checklist: tide (the spec's keys), dwm, i3, sway, xmonad or bspwm. It's saved per device in `chrome.storage.local` (`keysPreset`).
- `src/keymaps.mjs` is tide's `shell/lib/keymaps.mjs`, byte-identical below a 3-line header. `src/presets.js` translates it:
  - Super becomes Search, and each conf binding name maps to the tide for Chrome command that does the same.
  - Names with no command here are dropped: terminal, close, quit, fullscreen, focus and move left and right, resize mode, and home or back.
- A preset key Chrome can't bind keeps the spec's key, with a note saying why. That covers Return, `\`, `=`, `` ` ``, `;` and brackets, plus the Search+arrows chromeOS keeps. For example, dwm's and xmonad's swap with the master stays Search+Shift+M, and bspwm's workspace steps stay Search+PageUp/PageDown.
- When a preset takes a command's spec key, that command shows "Your choice". For example, dwm's Search+M monocle takes Meet's key.
- A command counts as done when Chrome has bound the suggested key, as before.
- SPEC gets a new §7.4 and an updated §13. The README is updated, and TODO's decisions log the calls I made.

## Rationale
The keys checklist is already where you're shown which key to give each command, and Chrome doesn't let tide for Chrome set them. A preset that changes the suggestions is as much as Chrome allows.

## Test plan
- `make lint` and `make test` pass (389 tests). The new `src/presets_test.js` (12 tests) covers:
  - the Search mapping and keys that can't be bound
  - dropped names and clashes
  - no duplicate suggestions in any preset
  - the checklist under dwm
  - saving and loading the choice
- `make smoke` passes (30 tests). It picks dwm on the options page, checks the Key column, and switches back.
- Not tried on a Chromebook.
- dwm's and xmonad's grow, and i3's focus previous, are suggested Search+L. chromeOS uses that for lock unless you remove it in the Shortcuts app, and the checklist doesn't warn about it yet. This is logged in TODO.

## Privacy, reliability, cost
- Privacy: none. The choice stays on the device.
- Reliability: an unknown stored preset falls back to tide's keys, with a warning.
- Cost: none.

body:
Recipe API facts, wave 2, group B, part 2: the non-DeepSeek recipes on creator vLLM fork images (part 1 is #2473, the DeepSeek family). 5 of the 10 recipes are documented here; the other 5 are left out and listed below. The change is documents plus two Model display modality edits. No recipe or contract file changes.

## How the engine was established
The method is the same as #2473:
1. Stream the image layers that install `vllm/` (registry API, no container run) and apply them in order.
2. Take the version from the installed `vllm/_version.py` and the image labels.
3. Diff the installed `vllm/*.py` against the public vLLM tree at that commit.
4. Read the facts from the installed files.

| Image | Installed vLLM | Verified against | Differs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ghcr.io/r0b0tlab/glm53-flash-nvfp4-sm121@b9edc8e0` | `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` (label `ai.vllm.build.commit=385dce36`) | upstream `385dce36` | **0** files |
| `ghcr.io/r0b0tlab/sm121-vllm-nvfp4@0f4ede25` | `0.25.1+r0b0tlab.w4a4.1` (labels `VLLM_COMMIT=752a3a50`, `VLLM_TAG=v0.25.1`) | upstream `752a3a50` | 1: `model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py` (W4A4 quant), off the API path |
| `ghcr.io/r0b0tlab/vllm-v0250-cu130-sm121@2d144faf` | `0.25.0` (label `upstream.revision=702f4814`) | upstream `702f4814` (v0.25.0) | **0** of the 1966 tree files. The image's adapter patches only `modelopt.py` (`patch_modelopt_w4a16_native_w4a4.py`) |
| `ghcr.io/tonyd2wild/vllm-m3-chthonic@cdeae56d` | `0.11.2.dev279+chthonic…` (label `local-inference.vllm.commit=5e839488`) | upstream `5e839488` | **0** files |

## Evidence per fact
Paths are relative to the installed `vllm/`.

**Common to all five**
- **Endpoints.** All four routes are registered unconditionally in `entrypoints/generate/api_router.py` (lines 24-46).
- **`reasoning_effort` and request kwargs.**
  - `reasoning_effort` is passed into the template, and when no `enable_thinking` is set it also sets `enable_thinking = effort != "none"` (`entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`: `385dce36:588,597`, `752a3a50:519,528`, `702f4814:519,528`, `5e839488:482,491`).
  - Request kwargs override `--default-chat-template-kwargs` (`renderers/params.py`, `defaults | overrides`).
- **Output tokens.** `max_output_tokens` is `{"setting":"context_tokens"}` (`--max-model-len` is bound) and `max_input_tokens` is `null`. `default_output_tokens` is `{"remaining":"context"}`: `get_max_tokens` (`entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:169/170`) uses only `max_new_tokens`, and none of these Models' `generation_config.json` sets it (fetched at the pinned revision and sha-checked).
- **Templates.** All are the Model's own `chat_template.jinja` at the pinned revision, since no recipe here passes `--chat-template`. Each renders a system turn.
- **Other facts.** `structured_output` and `streaming` are true; audio, pdf and audio output are false.
- **Tools, qwen3_coder / qwen3_xml / glm47.** `["auto","required","named"]` with `parallel_calls: true`:
  - The parser has a structural tag model, `qwen_3_coder` (`Qwen3EngineToolParser`) or `glm_4_7` (`Glm47MoeModelToolParser`, `tool_parsers/glm47_moe_tool_parser.py:10-11`), both xgrammar builtins.
  - Strict tool calling is on by default (`envs.py`).
  - Required and named are constrained by the structural tag in `parser/abstract_parser.py` `_apply_structural_tag` (`385dce36:560`, `752a3a50/702f4814:514`).
  - The xgrammar build inside the image is not read, the same accepted gap as before.

**Per recipe**

| Recipe | Inputs | Reasoning | Tools | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| glm-5-3-flash-nvidia-nvfp4-dflash2-vllm-dual (`385dce36`) | text, image, video | `always-on`; effort `top_level` `reasoning_effort` `[low, high, max]`, default **max** | glm47: full | Template `1d007386:2-3`: `low` and `high` are kept and any other value becomes `max`. The generation prompt always opens `<think>`, and the `deepseek_r1` parser handles the opened block. `--default-chat-template-kwargs {"reasoning_effort":"max"}`, which a request overrides. `Glm5NextProcessingInfo(Glm4vProcessingInfo)` serves `{"image": None, "video": 1}` (`model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py:968-969`, `models/glm5next/nvidia/multimodal.py:614`), with no limit set. `processor_config.json` has a `video_processor`, the template emits image and video blocks, and the checkpoint has vision tensors. The `speculation`/`autotune` options change no API fact. |
| qwen3-6-27b-nvfp4-r0b0tlab-vllm-single (`752a3a50`) | text | `switch` `enable_thinking`, default on, effort null | qwen3_xml: full | `--language-model-only` makes every modality limit 0. Template `0893e160`: opens `<think>` unless `enable_thinking is false`. The `qwen3` parser defaults to on (`parser/qwen3.py:217`). The `mtp-depth` options change only speculation. |
| xyz-aquila-mini-nvfp4-r0b0tlab-vllm-single (`702f4814`) | text | same | qwen3_xml: full | `--language-model-only`. Template `39f7345d`, byte-identical to the Qwen3.6 35B one. The `qwen3` parser defaults to on (`:217`). |
| qwen3-6-35b-a3b-nvfp4-r0b0tlab-vllm-single (`702f4814`) | base: text. `modality=multimodal`: text, image, video | same | qwen3_xml: full | The `modality` option defaults to `text` (`--language-model-only`); its `multimodal` choice carries its own block (`option_choices`). `Qwen3_5MoeProcessingInfo(Qwen3VLProcessingInfo)` serves image and video, the template renders `<\|video_pad\|>`, and the checkpoint has vision tensors. |
| minimax-m3-nvfp4-tonyd2wild-vllm-triple (`5e839488`) | text, image, video | `switch` `thinking_mode`, on `"enabled"`, off `"disabled"`, default **`model`**, effort null | minimax_m3: `[]` | See the MiniMax M3 notes below the table. |

**MiniMax M3 evidence**
- **Reasoning.**
  - Template `e7c7b65d`: `thinking_mode` is `enabled` (opens `<mm:think>`), `disabled` (closes it), or `adaptive`/unset (no prefix, so the checkpoint decides). That is the contract's `default: "model"`.

body:
## Roadmap item

**I-03 Trustworthy Deck Feedback (Now)** → *Keep warning calculations deterministic and independent from AI output.*

Bracket warnings (`scoreBracket`) named each banned, off-identity or Game Changer card once **per deck row**. A deck that holds the same card in two printings showed `2 Game Changer(s): Sol Ring, Sol Ring` and `Banned cards in deck: Griselbrand, Mana Crypt, Mana Crypt`. `validateDeck` already deduplicated these names, so the two warning surfaces disagreed.

## Change

- `src/lib/deck/validation.ts`: moved the existing order policy out of `sortedUniqueCardNames` into a new `sortedUniqueNames(names)` helper (deduplicate, then sort case-insensitively with a case-sensitive tiebreak). `sortedUniqueCardNames` now delegates to it.
- `src/lib/deck/bracket.ts`: `warningCardNames` now uses `sortedUniqueNames`, so bracket and validation warnings share one ordering and deduplication rule.
- The Game Changer **count** is unchanged and still counts copies. Only the list of names is deduplicated.

No migration, no external service, no product decision.

## TDD

**Red** (`npx vitest run src/lib/deck/bracket.test.ts -t "names a card once"`):

```
FAIL  scoreBracket > names a card once when the deck holds several printings of it
- "Banned cards in deck: Griselbrand, Mana Crypt",
- "Color identity violations: Lightning Bolt",
- "2 Game Changer(s): Sol Ring",
+ "Banned cards in deck: Griselbrand, Mana Crypt, Mana Crypt",
+ "Color identity violations: Lightning Bolt, Lightning Bolt",
+ "2 Game Changer(s): Sol Ring, Sol Ring",
```

**Super Green:** reused the existing deduplication and ordering policy instead of adding a second comparator. **Refactor:** `sortedUniqueCardNames` became a thin adapter over `sortedUniqueNames`. Its existing tests still pass.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `pnpm lint`: no warnings or errors
- `pnpm test`: 344 files, 3510 tests passed
- Pre-push Docker Playwright: 74 passed and 8 passed. The first attempt failed on `e2e/i18n-routing.spec.ts:52` ("locale prefix is preserved after navigation"). That failure is unrelated: an `isVisible()` guard races the onboarding dialog. The second attempt failed because `playwright-report` was owned by root, which I fixed with `chown`. The third attempt passed with no retry flag and without `SKIP_E2E`. The flaky i18n test deserves its own fix: call `suppressOnboarding` and drop the `isVisible()` guard.
- Sonar: no `.env.sonar` in this worktree, so it is left to CI.

Roadmap, changelog and progress docs are untouched (they go in the `chore/docs` PR).

author: demircaliskan2009-pixel
body:
## Summary

This PR builds the human-approved S1 sizing doctrine as deterministic, replayable, fail-closed paper construction under one contract: `S1_APPROVED_SIZING_CHAIN_CONSTRUCTION_V1`.

It admits no entry. Every S1 entry is still refused, and an entry that passed every decision-time check would still be refused at its fill.

## Approved doctrine it builds

The source is PRDV4 `6f5ad917` and the approved companion `docs/crypto_core/s1_approved_doctrine_adoption_v1.md` (`d351b4fb`), both adopted by #433.

- **D9 / ALLOCATION_ENVELOPE_V1** (companion §4.1–§4.6, items 2.1–2.2):
  - eligibility counts only proven readings;
  - top five, ties broken by the higher EHS, then the UTF-8 edge id;
  - the share vector, with BOOST evaluated under every value of an unknown condition;
  - for 3 ≤ n ≤ 5, the exact KKT breakpoint projection; for n ≤ 2, a clip that leaves the residual unallocated;
  - ENVELOPE_FIT at the decision and at the fill.
- **A9′** (§4.7, item 2.3, FCD-07): SCALE-1 replaces only its meta-layer term with ENVELOPE_FIT and keeps every other term.
- **D15 / CTR_SOURCE_QUALIFICATION_V1** (§5, items 3.1–3.2): the CTR consumer and the strict 2% depth cap at 5 bps, checked at the decision and at the fill.

## Changed files

**New source files:**
- `src/crypto_core/validation/governed_paper_allocation_envelope.py`: allocation and ENVELOPE_FIT (pure, exact).
- `src/crypto_core/validation/governed_paper_ctr_qualification.py`: qualification, revocation and capture records; the production and test-only tables; the CTR reading; the visible depth on authenticated depth-50 tips.
- `src/crypto_core/validation/governed_paper_sizing_chain.py`: decision-time readings, fill-time bounds and the sizing evidence.

**Changed source files:**
- `historical_execution_economics.py`: schedule v5 (exact-rational exposure envelopes and depth caps) and one fill hook. It returns nothing for every older schedule.
- `governed_paper_entry_safety.py`: rule set v8 (ENVELOPE-FIT, SCALE-1 under A9′, CTR-DEPTH) and the sizing evidence.
- `governed_admitted_variant_paper_execution.py`: seal v9 and evidence v9, plus the CTR-source lineage rules and capture rewrite/backfill checks.
- `governed_paper_kill_switch.py`: the derivation also returns its re-run's exact values (in memory only), so ENVELOPE_FIT compares against the exact NAV of the same single engine re-run.
- `governed_paper_regime_state.py`: two thin public wrappers over its existing authenticated depth-50 parsing.

**Docs:** `docs/crypto_core/paper_trading_phase_map.md` §12 gains the construction status.

**Tests:**
- new: `tests/crypto_core/validation/test_governed_paper_allocation_envelope.py`;
- new: `tests/crypto_core/validation/test_governed_paper_ctr_qualification.py`;
- new: `tests/crypto_core/validation/test_governed_paper_sizing_chain.py`.

## Versioned opt-in lineage

- A lineage opts in from day 0 by passing a sizing context in its protection inputs (only on an integrated v8 lineage). It can never switch in either direction.
- Seal v9 binds:
  - the sizing evidence digest;
  - the CTR source, which is either one qualification for the whole lineage or none;
  - its revocations, append-only and each effective inside the day that adds it;
  - its capture, complete through each seal.
- The lineage evidence refuses a capture that rewrites a record or backfills one received before the day.
- Without a sizing context, every seal and evidence is exactly the accepted v8 artifact.
- No v2–v8 payload, and no schedule v2–v4 payload, carries a new field.

## Known unproven methodology (fail-closed)

- **Allocation:** no EHS or Sharpe_30d method exists (FCD-13), and no activation proof (X-H1) or PRDV4 edge-state machine. So every candidate is UNKNOWN at every UTC-midnight rebalance and every allocation is BLOCKED. Without an edge-state record, no rebalance is proven to still apply after its own instant.
- **Incubation:** INCUBATION_MEMBER and COLD_START_EXCEPTED are not represented (item 1.7, A_max, T_max and W_INC are pending).
- **SCALE-1:** the Kelly fit (items 5.1–5.2), §1.24 calibration (HD-07), crowding, capacity, the regime dimensions, margin and DTL have no reading, so SCALE-1 never passes.
- **CTR:** no source is qualified (X-M1-C). The production table admits none, and this PR creates no qualification.
- **Venue:** no venue fact exists (D1), so a qualification's venue is bound to its capture, never to a venue fact.

## Effect on admission

- ENVELOPE-FIT fails on usage above 40% of NAV; otherwise it is BLOCKED.
- SCALE-1 keeps every rule set v7 FAIL with its reason and is otherwise BLOCKED.
- CTR-DEPTH fails at or above 2% of the exact visible depth; otherwise it is BLOCKED.
- The first refusal is unchanged (NT-D01 on the accepted worlds).
- Schedule v5 proves no envelope and no depth cap, so the engine would refuse every entry fill. One test forces the decision gate open (permissive, test-only) and shows the engine refusing every entry fill on the integrated path.

## Validation (local self-checks; not an independent audit)

- **Full suite** through `scripts/crypto_core/run_full_tests_logged.ps1`, on the committed head `53eec8e9`:
  - `PYTEST_EXIT=0` and `WRAPPER_EXIT=0`;
  - 21,440 passed, 37 skipped, 0 failed, 0 errors;
  - 21,477 tests in total, up from main's 21,364: the difference is exactly the 113 new tests.
- **New suites:**
  - allocation and ENVELOPE_FIT: 58 passed;
  - CTR qualification: 31 passed;
  - integration (schedule v5, rule set v8, seal and evidence v9): 24 passed.
- **Neighboring suites:** a targeted run of the economics, protective-lifecycle, entry-safety, kill-switch, regime and system-safety suites passed 799 tests.
- **Ruff** check and format check over the CI scope are clean (1,371 files).
- `git diff --check` and `git show --check` are clean.
- **Legacy pins:** rule sets v1–v7 and world G's v8 lineage seals, entry evidence and lineage evidence equal accepted main `5f88effa`.

## Gates

- A protected T4 `CLASS_C_CROSS_CONTRACT` audit by GPT-6.1 Sol (Ultra) on the exact head is required and pending.
- Independent review is pending.
- Merge is not authorized. It needs a separate human authorization that names this PR, its exact head and the standard-merge command.

author: davidbasilefilho
body:
## What and why

The Pi provider, device access and worktree settings agreed for HolyAgent were documented but never written, so a fresh install ran with Pi's own defaults. Setup now writes them and doctor reports them.

- **Write only what differs.** Setup deep-merges `toolSettings` into the Pi settings file of the chosen scope and writes a key only where it is unset and differs from the package default, so nothing the owner chose is overwritten and no default is restated.
- **Scopes.** At project scope a key the global settings already set is skipped, so a project file does not shadow a global choice. Project and local settings that are symlinks are refused, so setup cannot write through a link to a file outside the project.
- **Undo.** `--remove` takes back only the keys the setup record says it wrote.
- **Doctor.** When Pi is in use, adds a hint line for each Pi settings file that lacks keys setup writes.

## How it was checked

- `mise run build` leaves the tree clean and `mise run verify` exits 0 on the last code change (2334 tests); the head adds one documentation line.
- `packages/runtime/tests/setup-pi-settings.test.ts` covers the merge, defaults, global precedence, symlink refusal, undo and doctor output.
- Code, security and documentation reviews, with each finding repaired and re-reviewed.

## What remains

- A swap of a settings file for a symlink between the check and the write is not guarded against.

author: khuongln-1346
body:
## Summary

Five small hardening changes, one commit each so any one can be reverted alone (the push change has a second commit for its PWA wording).

- **Container password (`entrypoint.sh`).** With no `TERMOTE_PASS` and a home where the generated password cannot be saved (a read-only root), the entrypoint printed the password to the container log, which anyone with `docker logs` can read. It now stops with an error naming the two ways out (set `TERMOTE_PASS`, or a writable `$HOME/.config`). `termote container up` always passes `TERMOTE_PASS`, so this only reaches `docker run` by hand.
- **Push for password sign-ins.** A subscription made by a browser signed in with the password named no session, so `termote signins revoke` (or revoking it in Settings) left that browser receiving notifications until the password changed. It now carries the session id and goes when the session ends (revoked, signed out, 24 h expiry, pushed out) and at start, since sessions live in memory. The push store checks the session under its own lock when it adds one, so a subscribe racing the end is refused (401 `signed_out`). A subscription made with Basic auth, or stored before this, keeps the current behaviour. The PWA re-confirms its subscription on load, so signing in again turns push back on. The website's Settings page (EN, VI) says so. The PWA has an English and Vietnamese sentence for the new `signed_out` code.
- **Machine answer bodies.** An ssh pipe has no read deadline, so a machine that sent its headers and then stalled the body held one of its 16 connections for as long as the client waited. Each read of a body now gets 2 min and the whole body 30 min, the same bounds as a download from this server; past either, the request ends, which closes the connection and its ssh. A WebSocket stream (101) is not bounded by either.
- **`docker-tags` job.** It only runs `imagetools`, but `setup-buildx-action`'s default `docker-container` driver pulled `moby/buildkit` by tag while the job held the GHCR and Docker Hub tokens. It now uses the `docker` driver, which starts no container.
- **Docs.** The rate-limit entry now says the shared `proxied` cap (30/min) lets anyone reaching the tunnel lock password sign-in through it until the minute passes, and that Cloudflare Access stops this (accepted trade-off).

`docs/security-invariants.md` carries each change in the same commit; `docs/system-architecture.md` covers the container password.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] CI/CD or build configuration
- [x] Documentation update

## Test plan

- [x] `make test-entrypoints` (28 pass). The static check refuses any non-comment line that echoes `$TERMOTE_PASS`. A new runtime case (`--read-only`) runs where CI builds the image. Old and new `entrypoint.sh` were also run in an alpine + bash + openssl container with `--read-only`: the old one printed the password, the new one exits 1 with the error.
- [x] `TestPushSubscriptionEndsWithItsSession` (revoke, sign-out, restart; a Basic-auth subscription stays) and `TestPushStoreRefusesEndedSession`.
- [x] `TestMachineProxyBoundsBodyRead`: a fake bridge sends a header, part of a body, then stalls. All of 18 concurrent requests end and every connection closes. Against the old proxy the 16 slots stay taken and the last requests never get headers. `TestMachineProxySlowBody`: a body trickled slower than the idle wait is still read in full, and one past the total is cut. `TestMachineProxyStreamAndRevoke` now runs with both waits at 50/100 ms and checks the stream's connection survives (removing the 101 exemption breaks the upgrade). All with `-race`.
- [x] `docker-tags` driver: with buildx v0.36.1 (the job's version) and the `docker` driver, `imagetools create` copied a multi-arch index to a second local registry under two tags, kept its digest, and started no BuildKit container. Not run in the real workflow yet; the next release exercises it.
- [x] `go vet` for linux, windows and darwin; `gofmt`; dprint. `go test ./...`: everything passes except `TestTmuxPaneLayoutInRealServer`, `TestTmuxSnapshotParsesPaneFields` and `TestTmuxAgentSessionArgv`, which fail on a clean `main` on this machine too.

author: sc0210
body:
## How this was found
I audited the dashboard in a real browser (demo mode, Docker dev stack) at four sizes (390 / 768 / 1280 / 1920) in light and dark, with axe for accessibility. I then signed in as a **brand-new user with no data** on desktop, phone and Compact. Before this PR the audit found no errors and no overflow, but it did find the following.

## Charts
- **Repeated y-axis labels.** The Investment Portfolio chart read "2M, 2M, 2M, 2M, 1.9M, 1.9M…" because one fixed decimal can't tell close ticks apart. A new `compactAxisFormatter` picks the fewest decimals (1–3) that keep every tick distinct, giving "2.05M, 2.03M, 2M, 1.98M…". It's used by both the portfolio chart and the net-worth chart. `formatCurrency` gains an optional `compactDigits` (default 1, so other callers are unchanged).
- **Clipped date.** The last x-axis date was cut off ("Nov ("). The chart's right margin is wider now.
- **Empty account, net-worth axis.** It read "NT$1, NT$1, NT$0". `niceAxis` now gives an all-zero series a single `NT$0` baseline.
- **Empty account, Allocation donut.** It drew three equal coloured thirds, implying a split that doesn't exist. It's now one grey ring that follows the theme.

## Zero is not a gain
- **Phone and Compact.** "▲ NT$0 +0.0%" in green, "+NT$0" cash flow and "▲ NT$0" portfolio gain were all shown as gains. A shared `direction()` helper now treats 0 as flat: grey, no arrow, no sign.
- **Empty cash-flow bar.** With nothing in or out it drew a full green bar. It's now an empty track.
- **Savings rate with no income.** "0.0% savings rate" now reads "No income this period" on the strip and "—" in the Cash Flow card; a rate of nothing isn't 0%. The net no longer prints "+NT$0".

## New users on every layout
- **Getting-started steps everywhere.** They only existed on the full desktop view, so a new user on a phone or in Compact saw just zeros. They're now a `GetStarted` component, a row of cards on desktop and a stacked list on phone and Compact.
- **`isNewUser` in the shared model.** It means no assets, no debt, no activity this month and no goals, and it waits for goals to finish loading so the card can't flash.
- **Step 1's text** now says "Your salary, or what's in the bank today as a starting balance". Without that, a new user's Life Wallet starts at 0.

## Accessibility and dark mode (axe now passes at every size, light and dark)
- **Donut and screen readers.** Each donut slice was exposed as an image with no text. The legend beside it already lists every figure, so the donut is now hidden from screen readers and taken out of the tab order.
- **Dark-mode contrast.** "Debt Balance" was 3.99:1, the Portfolio legend % 3.46:1, and the period chip 4.05:1. Each moves to a lighter shade in dark mode.
- **Phone carousel.** The swipeable "Today's highlights" row scrolled but couldn't be reached by keyboard. It's now a focusable, labelled region.
- **Truncated wallet tile.** On a phone, "Emergency Fund" was cut to "Emergenc…". The label now wraps.

## Consistency
- **Same metric, same name.** The dashboard called the Portfolio page's "Annual return" figure "CAGR". It now uses the Portfolio page's label and caption ("Annual return · Time-weighted, per year").
- **Translated debt labels.** The allocation tooltip's debt slice was hard-coded as "負債" and "of assets". Both are translated now.

## Verification
- **Jest:** 2,487 passed. New tests cover `compactAxisFormatter`, the all-zero axis, `direction()`, `GetStarted` (both layouts), and `isNewUser`: true only with nothing recorded, false in demo, false while goals are loading. Existing card-test mocks pass the new pure helper through.
- **Checks:** type-check and `type-check:tests` clean; lint 0 errors, warnings back at baseline.
- **Browser:** axe reports no serious or critical issues at any size, light or dark. Before-and-after screenshots confirm each fix on the demo dashboard and for a new user on desktop, phone and Compact.

Review note dismissed: the empty donut can't show a "1.0%" tooltip. The tooltip already returns nothing for a slice without a name (`WalletNetWorthCard.tsx`, `if (!entry.name) return null`).

author: belhaouazakaria
body:
## Root cause
The existing live `growth-daily-observe` timer executes a single account-identity sync, **not Pinterest analytics**. The local intelligence loop is offline-only. This leaves Telegram report analytics stale/unavailable indefinitely.

## Scope
- Opt-in-only `04:20 UTC` isolated one-account Pinterest analytics timer, **installed disabled**. Refreshes seven prior complete UTC dates (never current incomplete day) using the existing official account analytics handler; optional top-Pin summary GET only when provider quota permits.
- Single exact job per UTC day, no retries, 180s expiring Growth lease, watchdog, and pre-/post-condition verification.
- Shared global Pinterest API request budgets of four requests/hour, sixteen/day plus provider headers. No artificial data or invented clicks.
- Strict `ANALYTICS` rollout scope, blocked without `onlyJobId` and private scoped job flag; no broad generic worker execution.
- Read-only official Pinterest API traffic (GET); no Pin creation, no paid AI, no Attribution, no Telegram outbound.
- Root-owned disabled installer + throttled failure alert; unit tests, runtime assertions, documentation.

## Still separate work
Fresh account metrics may be PROCESSING; this is not a fix for all historical Pin-level gaps or attribution consent. Do not activate without coordinated review and owner production go-live.

## CI
Require full lint/typecheck/tests/build and isolated tests before merge. No deployment/production settings changes from this PR.

author: raspbeguy
body:
3.4.1 publishes the v4 announcement, in the "Upcoming in v4" block of the spec and in `docs/deprecations.md`. A review of the 3.x commits compared it with what `origin/v4` does and found it wrong in several places. This makes it match the branch, before 3.4.1 is cut.

What changes in the announcement:

- **The opening sentence.** It said that this major accepts both forms of every item. Only `ip6prefix` is accepted in both forms. The `/uapi/...` paths, `?family=v6` and the other items exist only in v4, so a client that moved early got a 404 or v4 leases.
- **#307.** v4 also changes the write: a `wireless/interfaces` write that sends no `mode` stores none (`toUci` on v4), where 3.x stores `ap`, so wifi-scripts sets up no interface for it and the write answers 2xx. The announcement said only that the read changes.
- **#308.** A write that only disables a section with a stored error is refused too, as in LuCI's form.
- **#319.** The `path` label of the metrics follows the new paths, which a dashboard keyed on the old label has to follow.
- **#320.** The `dhcp:leases6` scope goes with its endpoint: a token that holds only that scope gets 403 on `?family=v6`. A v6 entry is addressed by its `ip`.
- **#321 is withdrawn.** libuci names an anonymous section at each load from its ordinal in the package and a hash of its type, so its name moves to another section when an earlier one is deleted. Without `adopt`, a client that stores such a name can write or delete another section with a 2xx. v4 reverts the removal (a PR on `v4` follows), so the announcement no longer lists it.
- **#322.** v4 makes `runtime` required on every resource. It does not document every runtime block: 4 of 45 resources document theirs, and the others keep an opaque object.

The #366 entry of `[Unreleased]` now names the carve-out it uses: the 200 it replaces left a peer committed and the interface down, and the 500 for an interface that another stored peer already keeps down is tracked in #370.

Two defects of v4 itself are left to PRs on `v4`, not to this text: the response type of `network/routes.table` and `network/rules.lookup` widened to a string, and the `family` parameter that the v4 spec does not declare.

**Does this change the wire surface?** Not in 3.x: the text of the spec description and of the deprecations log changes. It changes what 3.x announces for v4, which is why it lands before 3.4.1.

**Was it verified against a real device, or only by CI?** The v4 behaviors were read in the code of `origin/v4` (`src/resources/wireless.interfaces.uc` `toUci`, `src/lib/scope.uc`, `src/main.uc`, `src/lib/handler.uc`) during the review. CI checks that the two lists keep the same count.

**Was LuCI checked?** Yes. For #307, both paths that create a wireless interface in LuCI write `mode`: `ap` for a new network (`luci-mod-network` `view/network/wireless.js:2521`) and `sta` or `adhoc` to join one (`:2371`). For #308, `form.js:2134-2139` refuses to save the map while a field that the form shows holds an invalid value, so a change of `disabled` alone is refused too. A stored value that the form does not show is not checked by LuCI, which v4 is stricter about.

Make authored objectives eligible from verified story-context facts and explicit choices. Selected objectives use existing completion, chapter-transition and carryover rules. Eligibility is rechecked on submission; retries, stale timestamps, changed receipt payloads and paused-story choices are guarded. Context changes remove ineligible unselected options without erasing selected responsibilities.

Validation: 58 local unittest tests passed, including 10 new responsive-objective tests; 14 existing function tests passed directly. Changed Python files passed Python 3.7 grammar checks. No in-game runtime validation.

The example career/support/university/promotion rules are illustrative content, not finalized objective design. Context is supplied by trusted adapters; this does not add gameplay detection, targeted-Sim binding, active-objective cancellation, focus pause semantics or ending effects. The two-option limit applies to response previews; full reveal sequencing for legacy fixed chapter plans remains separate. Rules are consumed once per story, and unchosen candidates never block chapter progression.

Stacked on #10. See docs/technical/Responsive-Objectives.md for integration and limits.

author: anslwy
body:
## Why

An agent cannot currently find out what the user sent to its Telegram DM while it was asleep, mid-turn, or when a reply failed to send. The Telegram Bot API has no "fetch past messages" call for bots (`getUpdates` only returns what has not been confirmed yet), so the only honest source is what Kurisu itself saw.

## What changed

**Store at the channel boundary** (`store.rs`, `telegram/history.rs`, `telegram/bridge.rs`)
- New `telegram_messages` table (owner DM only): `seq`, `chat_id`, `direction` (`user`/`agent`), Telegram `message_id`, `update_id`, `text`, `attachment` JSON `{kind,name,mime}`, `answered`/`answered_at`, `at`.
- Inbound messages are written in `handle_update` **before any work**, so a message that arrived while a turn was running, while Kurisu was down (it is replayed from `pending_updates`), or whose reply never went out is still there afterwards. A partial unique index on `update_id` for user rows makes replayed updates idempotent.
- Voice: the row exists immediately (marker `voice`, caption as text) and the speech-to-text transcript is appended when it arrives. Photos/documents/videos get their marker; an empty body gets `{kind:other}`.
- Outbound text is recorded at the single send choke point (`send_text_with`), chunk by chunk; chunks of one reply join into one row (`TG_REPLY_JOIN_S`). Recording is not "answering".
- `answered` is set only when agent text is actually relayed for that update (or a slash command sends its own reply). Queue acks and notices do not count, which is exactly the "it arrived but nobody answered" case.
- Rows are pruned per chat (`TG_KEEP = 5000`), the table grows only for the owner's DM.

**Tool** (`mcp.rs`, `server.rs`)
- `telegram_history` is built in, so every session has it: `chat` (optional; only the owner's DM — `dm`/`me`/the configured id — anything else is refused), `limit` (default 20, max 200), `before` (seq paging), `search` (case-insensitive substring in text or attachment name), `unanswered` (only user messages never replied to).
- Returns `order: "oldest first"`, `total`, `has_more`, `first_seq`/`last_seq` and per message: `seq`, `at`, `direction`, `text`, `message_id`, `attachment`, `answered`/`answered_at`.
- The op reads the config from disk, so it works even when the channel is stopped.
- Description states the limits plainly: Bot API cannot fetch past messages; nothing from before the feature, nothing from groups or channels, no other chat.

## Tests

- `store::tests::telegram_rows_keep_order_answer_flags_and_transcripts` — idempotent replay, join of streamed chunks, transcript fill, answered once, LIKE wildcards literal, paging, unanswered, chat isolation.
- `telegram::bridge::tests::telegram_history_records_updates_and_pages_searches_and_stays_owner_only` — a fake Bot API channel feeds a text update, an attachment with caption and a queued message, asserts the tool returns them with direction/attachment/answered, paging via `before`, search, `unanswered`, and that a group message is not recorded and another chat id is refused.
- Full suite locally: `cargo test -p kurisu` — 111 passed (one pre-existing stack-overflow test needs `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`, also overflows on the base commit; unix-socket-path tests need a short `TMPDIR`, environmental).
- Runtime smoke with a fake Bot API and isolated `KURISU_HOME` (ports not 8791/8798, live instance untouched): messages sent before a restart, a file with caption, and one queued while the server was down all came back through the MCP tool, the late one flagged unanswered; paging, search, `unanswered`, and owner-only refusal verified.

body: ## Summary Public, unauthenticated legal pages and a Creem prompt-moderation gate for image generation. This branch does not include Creem billing, checkout, or webhooks, does not change Lemon Squeezy, and does not set a production Live key. - `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/acceptable-use`, and `/contact` are public. `/aup` redirects to `/acceptable-use` (301). - The marketing footer links to those pages and shows `liyan215500115@gmail.com`. Contact uses the same address. - Terms and Acceptable Use prohibit NSFW, explicit, sexually suggestive, and harmful image generation, and state that deepfake / face-swap abuse is not allowed. The operator is described as an individual seller in mainland China, not a company. - `POST /api/generate` and `POST /api/generate/batch` screen user-controlled prompt text with `POST /v1/moderation/prompt` before any model call. ## How moderation is gated - `CREEM_MODERATION` defaults to **enforce** (including when unset). `off` skips screening and is for local development only. - Host: `creem_test_…` → `https://test-api.creem.io`. Other `creem_…` keys → `https://api.creem.io`. `CREEM_TEST_MODE=true|false` overrides the prefix. - Only user-typed text is sent. Static style-picker prompts, scene templates, platform suffixes, and catalog templates are stripped and are not screened. A request with no user text is not sent to Creem. - `deny` and `flag` return HTTP 400 `prompt_rejected` and do not call the model. - Timeout, network error, non-200, unknown decision, or a missing `CREEM_API_KEY` while enforce is on returns HTTP 503 and does not call the model. - Tests: 24 new cases. `allow` reaches the model; `deny`, `flag`, and timeout do not. Three existing Lemon quota tests still fail because `checkGenerationQuota` has an admin bypass. That billing code was not changed. ## Preview smoke (test key only) Do not put these values on Production. Do not use a Live `creem_` key. Do not change `LEMONSQUEEZY_*`. 1. Deploy this branch to a Vercel Preview. 2. Preview env only: - `CREEM_API_KEY` = a `creem_test_…` key - `CREEM_MODERATION=enforce` (or leave it unset) - `CREEM_TEST_MODE=true` if you want to force the sandbox host; a `creem_test_` key already selects `https://test-api.creem.io` 3. Logged out, open `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/acceptable-use`, `/contact`. Each page should be the policy, not the login screen. `/aup` should redirect to `/acceptable-use`. The homepage footer should link to all four pages and show `liyan215500115@gmail.com`. 4. Terms and Acceptable Use should contain NSFW, explicit, sexually suggestive, harmful, deepfake, and face-swap. 5. Sign in and generate from a normal product prompt. The image should succeed, and the moderation call should hit `https://test-api.creem.io/v1/moderation/prompt` before the model. 6. Submit a prompt Creem denies or flags. Expect HTTP 400 `prompt_rejected` and no image. 7. Break the key or block the moderation host. Expect HTTP 503 and no image. Restore the test key afterward. ## Production Live moderation Not verified. A Live key is still unavailable. Sandbox calls do not count as production moderation. After a Live `creem_` key exists, repeat steps 5–7 against `https://api.creem.io` with `CREEM_TEST_MODE` unset or `false`. Leave this PR open for the project manager to merge and deploy.

body:
## 改动范围

本 PR 收尾 11 个已确认的 P1，涉及五个插件，初始修复提交为 `0661c68`，回归用例与 Clearbit 补齐提交为 `4e2864d`，评审修正提交为 `7a57150`。

- Design `0.1.6`，`emil-design-eng`、`improve-animations` 和 `review-animations` 按 Motion 版本判断 transform shorthand 的硬件加速能力。
- Growth `0.1.7`，修正 `analytics` 的观察窗、GA4 事件与 GTM 金额读取，`churn-prevention` 的 NPS 和 Paddle Billing 事件判定，`growth-experiments` 的样本量与统计解释，`pricing` 的价格感知调查结论，以及 `search-visibility` 的 hreflang 和 canonical 规则。
- Product `0.2.5`，`ui-ux-pro-max` 增加 RTL 查询支持，修正版本识别与嵌入式 Python 模块加载。
- Sales `0.1.3`，`prospecting` 修正 LinkedIn 私信的合规表述和 Clearbit 的可用性说明。

## 验证结果

- UI UX 单元测试 159 项通过。数据校验通过，覆盖 12 份领域数据、22 份技术栈数据和 `ui-reasoning.csv`。
- RTL 命令行冒烟测试通过。隔离模式下运行 `search.py`，确认 `--rtl=full` 返回符合条件的结果。
- 维护测试 3 项通过。变更范围、JSON、Markdown 本地链接和 `git diff --check` 通过。
- 40 个技能文件的本地 SHA-256 和固定上游版本的 SHA-256 与同步台账一致。五个插件的 Claude Code、Codex manifest 及 Claude Marketplace 版本一致。
- GitHub CLI 的依赖参数已在本机核对。GitLab 的 `glab mr list --output json` 已对照官方文档，本机未安装 `glab`，因此未做 GitLab CLI 实测。 [GitLab CLI 文档](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/mr/list/)

## 补齐的上游回归与实跑结果

从 `coreyhaines31/marketingskills@96798cf` 同步了六道相关用例，保留上游题面、期望和断言。每道题以独立的 Codex CLI 会话运行一次，使用 `gpt-6.1-sol`（low），仅提供本地技能正文、相关参考文件和题面。模型作答时未提供答案或评分标准。以下为对照上游断言人工判分的结果。

| 上游用例 | 断言结果 | 实跑观察 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analytics #7 · GA4 自动事件 | 5/6 | 事件名、过滤条件、各事件计数正确，也用 DebugView 校验。未覆盖搜索参数及 YouTube JS API 等增强衡量配置。 |
| Analytics #8 · GTM 金额 | 5/5 | 用数值数据层或标准化 `data-price`，覆盖 US/EU 显示格式、真实零值和无效值。 |
| Churn Prevention #7 · Paddle | 5/6 | 三个 Billing 事件及保留访问权限的判断正确。未引用 Paddle 文档或区分 Classic 通知。 |

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A sub-agent completion that cannot be delivered within 20 minutes no longer kills a parent that is still busy in its own long turn.

When a finished sub-agent's result waits longer than `_ON_DONE_TIMEOUT` (1200 s) to reach its parent, the delivery is given up and the parent session is reset. A cron job, channel or webhook run whose own turn keeps working for more than 20 minutes after a child finishes is killed mid-turn by that reset: the gateway logs `completion injection timed out ... after 1200s`, then `runtime kill pid=<parent> ... reason=provider shutdown`, and the run ends with an error.

## Why it matters

Any unattended run that starts a short child and then keeps working (a long build, a code change and a push) loses its live turn 20 minutes after the child ends, and each later child's delivery kills the replacement process the same way. The reset was meant to clear a stuck injection prompt; a busy parent is not one.

## Not a goal

- Moving the busy-parent wait outside the 1200 s cap, or queueing a completion for the parent's next turn (#17898).
- Stopping the re-delivery of results that `spawn_sub_agents` already returned inline (#17684, #23434).
- Changing the cron and channel routes' own `INJECTION_TIMEOUT` resets, which act only on an attempt that holds the parent's session itself.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

A parent that is busy in its own turn now keeps running when a completion's delivery times out; a delivery that is itself stuck still gets the parent's session reset.

The timeout arm in `subagent_manager/terminal.py` reset the parent unconditionally. The cron and channel routes wait for the parent's session lease inside the 1200 s cap, so a long, healthy turn reached the same arm as a stuck injection. At that moment the two differ in who holds the lease: the timeout cancels the route first, and the route's `finally` cancels its own prompt and releases any lease it held before the arm runs. A turn still holding the lease is then the parent's own turn, or a channel member's lifetime lease. A permit that release handed to another queued delivery names no holder until that delivery runs.

The arm now asks `sessions.turn_holder(parent_key)`. No holder: the session is reset as before, so a stuck provider is cleared and a queued delivery validates onto a fresh one. A holder: the parent is left running and the arm logs that. Either way the delivery is still reported failed through `notify_injection_failed`. The `_ON_DONE_TIMEOUT` row and the Two-Level Timeout section of `docs/system-specs/modules/subagent.md`, and the outer-cap row of `docs/architecture/resource-protection.md`, state the rule.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the reset is declined only while a turn holds the parent's session; every timeout with no holder resets exactly as before.

Removes nothing: no path, record, key or function is taken away; one reset now waits for no turn to be holding the session.

## Tests

- `test/test_subagent_injection_timeout_reset.py` drives the real `SessionManager` lease under the real terminal report, with only the provider process mocked.
  - `test_a_parent_busy_with_its_own_turn_is_left_running[turn-lease|lifecycle-lease]` runs the real cron route and locks in that the parent's session, provider and turn survive the timeout.
  - `test_a_stuck_injection_is_reset_while_a_sibling_waits_for_the_parent` locks in that a delivery stuck holding the lease is still reset when its release hands the permit to a queued sibling, and that the sibling gets a fresh provider. It passes on `main` too, which resets unconditionally: it guards the reset this change keeps.
  - `test_a_stuck_injection_prompt_is_still_reset` runs the same through the real cron route with no sibling.
- `test/test_subagent.py::TestOnDoneTimeout::test_injection_timeout_resets_parent_session`: with no turn holding the parent, the arm still resets it.
- Determinism: 20 repeats at `-n0` (80 passed); 10 repeats at `-n 4 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=2` beside `test_subagent_injection_live_turn.py`, `test_subagent_injection_session_reload.py` and `TestOnDoneTimeout`, one of which lost every test at setup when a concurrent session on the shared temp root removed its pytest base directory and passed again with a private `TMPDIR`; one shuffled order (seed 25715, the same 14 tests). All green.

Proof: PROVEN test/test_subagent_injection_timeout_reset.py::test_a_parent_busy_with_its_own_turn_is_left_running[turn-lease], test/test_subagent_injection_timeout_reset.py::test_a_parent_busy_with_its_own_turn_is_left_running[lifecycle-lease] (head d949bdf8dd40)

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage sufficient: the tests drive the real session lease, cron route and terminal report, and only the kiro-cli process is mocked.

## Screenshots / video

N/A — no frontend change.

## Related Issues

Closes #22157

Builds on #26275 by @rnoack1.

## Sibling sweep

Swept: git grep -nE "sessions\.reset\(" -- src/kiro_crew/subagent_manager src/kiro_crew/slack/gateway_runtime/subagent_injection.py src/kiro_crew/slack/gateway_runtime/runtime_charge.py
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/gateway_runtime/subagent_injection.py:1207 -- not affected -- every parent reset in this file runs under the route's own claim (the channel attempt timeout at 1207, the cron route's new-session reset at 1340 and its injection timeout at 1392) or already passes skip_if_busy=True (the idle cleanup at 1503)
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/gateway_runtime/runtime_charge.py:293 -- not affected -- the prompt-busy and process-death resets in `_inject_with_retry` (293, 329, 368) run under the delivery's own claim
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/subagent_manager/terminal.py:1051 -- not affected -- resets the child run's own session during a reap, never the parent's
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/subagent_manager/run_lifecycle.py:176 -- not affected -- resets the child run's own session at its teardown, never the parent's

## Pattern harvest

Not generalizable: the defect is one timeout arm resetting a session after its caller had already given up the lease; every other parent reset either runs under the route's own claim or already passes skip_if_busy.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: zeecm
body:
## Why
People tell a designer standing rules: "no bed facing the door", "keep the corridor clear", "the TV not on the window wall". Until now the designer treated these as one-off remarks it could forget the next time it proposed something. Slice 3a turns them into **house rules**. Every proposal and every accept is checked against them, and the designer is told about them.

## What it does
- **Core: the rule object.**
  - A rule has a subject, a relation, a target and an optional distance in metres. The relations are `notIn`, `in`, `faces`, `notFaces`, `within`, `atLeast`, `against` and `keepClear`.
  - Rules compile to hard checks (`R|rule|piece`), the same kind of check that already blocks a bad layout.
  - `vetRule` turns down rules the app can't measure, or that the plan makes impossible, and says why.
  - `measureRoute` measures walkway rules.
- **Talk.**
  - When the designer hears a standing wish, it offers it as a rule: "Make this a rule". The offer is priced like a Send, at about US$0.03.
  - A Decision can be moved to Your rules.
  - Rules go into the designer's prompt.
- **Web: Your rules.**
  - A list where you can rename, edit numbers, delete (Undo writes "You brought a rule back…"), and Show on plan with the route band.
  - Each proposal card lists the rules with their verdict. A card worked out before your rules changed reads "Not checked against your rules yet".
  - A plan that already breaks a rule says so, naming the piece.
- **Records v3**, the foundation for slice 3 (3b's `owns` key uses it too). Question keys and enums are read tolerantly, and `restore()` brings back records that were set aside. No schema bump, no API change.
- **Phone.** Show on plan lowers the sheet, using #58's `coversPlan`, and switches a 3D-only phone to Plan.

## Reviews
- **Tech lead: mergeable.** Fixed along the way:
  - the plan-status cost;
  - rule moves;
  - tolerant records;
  - the `owns` key, now part of records v3 rather than added without a version bump.
- **QA:** acceptance criteria pass at 1280, 390 and 844 touch. Fixed findings B1–B5:
  - Show on plan on a phone;
  - the undo line;
  - Esc while renaming cancels only the rename;
  - wording and number limits;
  - stale verdicts on folded cards.

## Tests
- Core 976 + 3, web 279, render 41, edge 18. Typecheck and lint are clean.
- e2e: `designer.spec` and `frames.spec` pass (51), including a phone house-rules test and the priced "Make this a rule → Moved to Your rules." path.

author: jeonghun917
body:
Found while walking the setup steps from the README with the published 0.26.2 on a fresh repository.

**The bug.** Right after `npx readfirst init --agent --ci`, the next two steps failed:
- `prompt`: "map.json has problems: 2 file(s) in no group: .github/workflows/readfirst.yml, AGENTS.md"
- `check`: "new top-level folder .github/ is in no group"

init wrote the map first and AGENTS.md and the workflow after it, so the files it had just made were in no group. `readfirst fix` repaired it, but nothing told the user to run it.

**The fix.**
- init writes the agent notes, agent configs and the workflow first, then lists the files again and drafts the map from them. The output keeps its order.
- `setup` and `hook --install` may add files to a repository that already has a map (`.claude/settings.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/mcp.json`). They do not write the map (rule `only-init-and-fix-write`). When the map no longer places every file after them, they now say to run `npx readfirst fix` or let the Action's auto-fix do it.

**Checks.**
- Two new tests in test/readfirst.test.mjs; both fail on main and pass here.
- `npm test`: 129 pass. `readfirst verify`: all checks passed.

Checked as well, and working as described: `audit` and `scan` with no map, `read` (risks, broke before, checks), `check`, `verify`, the MCP server (6 tools), and `hook --gate` (the first edit is refused with the notes, the retry passes).

body:
## Summary

R1 (product code, tests, docs; no governance, workflow, `landing_review.py` or dependency paths). Owner request 2026-11-08: build a competitive radar on Nerelan itself instead of relying on manual research.

- `reverse_agent/platform_v1/radar.py`: a host background job, **off unless `REVERSE_AGENT_RADAR` names a config**. Every `interval_hours` (default weekly) it collects, with **no model calls**:
  - watched projects' releases and star growth, via `gh api -X GET` with the Owner's existing login (no token read or exported);
  - new related GitHub repositories (search by query, created within `lookback_days`, `min_stars`);
  - Hacker News stories via the public Algolia API (no credentials, no redirects, 2 MiB cap).
- Only items not seen before are reported; the first run is a baseline. A failing source is recorded; if every source fails the run is retried at the next poll.
- New findings become **one PLANNED triage Goal per run** (idempotent). The radar never approves or launches it: model work happens only after the Owner admits it into an Owner window (#1401), and it ends in a Draft PR to `docs/architecture/COMPETITIVE_LANDSCAPE.md`. The objective is capped at 12k chars so it fits the Owner window prompt with other Goals.
- Source text is quoted in the report and fenced as untrusted data in the objective, which tells the executor never to follow instructions in it.
- `trusted_host.py`: starts/stops the radar next to the research loop.
- `docs/radar.md`: operation; `docs/architecture/COMPETITIVE_LANDSCAPE.md`: seeded from the Owner's 2026-11-08 analysis, repo names and stars verified via GitHub the same day, with "revisit when" per project and the first radar preview (untriaged).
- CLI: `python -m reverse_agent.platform_v1.radar status|preview --config radar.json` (`preview` collects once and prints, saving nothing).

## Verification

- `tests/platform_v1/test_radar.py`: 16 passed, all sources faked (baseline, only-new items -> one PLANNED goal with no launched tasks, interval, all-sources-failed retry, goal-creation retry, untrusted text fenced, objective size cap, `gh api -X GET` only, config validation, off by default).
- With `test_owner_window`, `test_trusted_host`, `test_trusted_host_lifecycle`, `test_goal_service`: 265 passed, 3 skipped.
- Live `preview` against GitHub and HN (read-only): 40 recent releases across 9 watched repos, 5 new related repositories, 3 HN stories; output recorded in the landscape doc.
- `git diff --check` clean.

## Not verified

- Not run inside a real host over a full week; the triage Goal has not been admitted into a real Owner window or executed.
- Triage quality depends on the executor model; its PR still needs independent review.

author: tnk-git-hub
body:
## Task
## Goal
Add an endpoint to post a review for a product: `POST /products/:id/reviews` (backend only).

Interface (keep these names exactly):
- DTO class `CreateReviewDto` in `backend/src/products/dto/create-review.dto.ts`.
- Service method `ProductsService.addReview(productId: number, dto: CreateReviewDto)`.
- Controller: `@Post(':id/reviews')` with `ParseIntPipe` on `:id`, returns status 201.

Body: `{ rating, reviewerName, reviewerEmail, comment? }`
- `rating`: integer from 1 to 5.
- `reviewerName`: string, non-empty after trimming whitespace, at most 100 characters.
- `reviewerEmail`: a valid email address.
- `comment`: optional string, at most 1000 characters.
- `date` is set by the server (current time). A `date` sent by the client is ignored
  (the global `ValidationPipe` already uses `whitelist: true`).

Behavior:
- Returns the created review `{ id, rating, comment, date, reviewerName, reviewerEmail }`
  (no `product` field). `comment` is `null` when not sent.
- Invalid body → 400. Non-integer `:id` → 400. Product not found → 404 and nothing is written
  (no review row, no product update, no cache change).
- In one transaction: insert the review, then set `products.rating` to the average of ALL reviews
  of that product (including the new one), rounded to 2 decimals.
  Examples: existing 5,4 + new 4 → 4.33; existing 5,5 + new 4 → 4.67; no existing + new 3 → 3.
  Seeded ratings get overwritten by the real average — this is expected.
- After the transaction commits: delete the product's detail cache key AND invalidate the list
  caches (bump the list version), because lists can be sorted by rating. Same pattern as `update`.
- Afterwards `GET /products/:id` shows the new review last (reviews are ordered by id ASC),
  the new `rating`, and `reviewCount` increased by 1 (`reviewCount` is a virtual column, no manual update).

## Behaviors to test
- `CreateReviewDto` validation (class-validator): `rating` 0, 6, 2.5 and missing are rejected; 1 and 5 pass.

## 1. Hành vi quan sát được

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `POST /products/5/reviews` với body hợp lệ | **201**, trả `{ id, rating, comment, date, reviewerName, reviewerEmail }`. Không có `product`. `comment` là `null` nếu không gửi. |
| Body sai (rating ngoài 1–5 hoặc không nguyên, tên rỗng hoặc toàn khoảng trắng hoặc dài hơn 100 ký tự, email sai, comment dài hơn 1000 ký tự, thiếu trường bắt buộc) | **400** từ `ValidationPipe` |
| `:id` không phải số nguyên (ví dụ `abc`, `1.5`) | **400** từ `ParseIntPipe` |
| Product không tồn tại | **404** (`NotFoundException`). Không ghi review, không update product, không đụng cache. |

- `products.rating` bằng trung bình của **tất cả** review (kể cả review mới), làm tròn 2 chữ số thập phân.

## 2. File cần sửa/tạo

### Tạo: `backend/src/products/dto/create-review.dto.ts`
Class `CreateReviewDto`:
- `rating`: `@IsInt() @Min(1) @Max(5)`. Thiếu hoặc 2.5 thì bị từ chối.
- `reviewerName`: `@IsString() @Matches(/\S/) @MaxLength(100)`.
  - Dùng `@Matches(/\S/)` thay cho `@Transform(trim)` + `@IsNotEmpty`. Nhờ vậy `"   "` bị từ chối kể cả khi test gọi `validate()` trực tiếp mà không qua `plainToInstance`.
  - Tôi không trim giá trị lưu, vì spec chỉ yêu cầu kiểm tra "không rỗng sau khi trim".
- `reviewerEmail`: `@IsEmail()`.
- `comment?`: `@IsOptional() @IsString() @MaxLength(1000)`.
- Không có trường `date`.

Thêm `import { Review } from './review.entity'` và `import { CreateReviewDto } from './dto/create-review.dto'`. Thêm hàm `addReview(productId: number, dto: CreateReviewDto)`:

1. Trong `this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => …)`:
   - `manager.findOneBy(Product, { id: productId })`. Nếu không có thì `throw new NotFoundException(...)`, giống `update`. Dùng hàm này vì fake test hiện đã hỗ trợ.
   - `manager.create(Review, { rating, comment: dto.comment ?? null, reviewerName, reviewerEmail, date: new Date(), product: { id: productId } })`, rồi `manager.save(review)`.
   - Đọc rating của mọi review của product, **sau** khi insert, nên đã gồm review mới: `manager.find(Review, { where: { product: { id: productId } }, select: { rating: true } })`.
   - Tính `avg = Math.round((sum * 100) / count) / 100`. Làm tròn bằng số nguyên để tránh lỗi float. Ví dụ: (5+4+4)/3 → 4.33, (5+5+4)/3 → 4.67, một review 3 → 3.

2. **Sau khi commit** (giống `update`): `await this.cache.del(detailKey(productId))` rồi `await this.invalidateLists()`.

- Không bọc `try/catch` với `handleUniqueError`, vì không có ràng buộc unique nào liên quan.

author: klimpaskov
body:
Fixes #168

## What changed
- `prefetch_verified_files` now downloads the pinned commit once from `https://codeload.github.com/klimPaskov/Agentic-HOI4-Modding/tar.gz/<commit>` when 24 or more declared blobs are uncached. The archive streams to a partial file (resumed with a Range request when the server allows it, bounded retries on 429/5xx/resets, capped at 1 GiB compressed / 4 GiB declared).
- Extraction never uses an archive path on disk. Each entry is looked up by its exact manifest path, accepted only if it is a regular file with the declared size and SHA-256, and stored in the existing hash-addressed blob cache. Links, special files, undeclared paths and mismatches are skipped.
- Anything the archive did not supply, and the whole install if the archive fails, is fetched by the existing per-file route. The developer local-source mode and the web edition are unchanged. `codeload.github.com` is approved only for `/<fixed owner>/<fixed repo>/tar.gz/<40-hex commit>` with no query; redirects stay refused.
- `git archive` can differ from Git blobs (export-ignore/export-subst/eol), so the archive is never evidence, only a faster byte source checked against manifest hashes.

## Measurement (Windows, live, kit revision c191d109, 1,766 unique files, debug build, cold cache)
| | requests | time |
|---|---|---|
| per-file (before) | 1,766 | 64.1 s |
| one archive (after) | 1 | 25.9 s |
All 1,766 blobs came from the archive; 0 fell back. Reproduce: `cargo test live_archive_vs_single_files -- --ignored --nocapture`.

## Tests
New unit tests: hash/size/link/traversal/unlisted entries, shared hash, truncated archive, approved-URL matrix, and an interrupted download resuming via Range against a local server. `cargo test -p hoi4-mod-setup --lib source::` 56 passed; fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean.

Docs: `docs/04`, source-manifest skill, CHANGELOG. No schema, credential or transaction change. Offline acceptance and component markers are untouched (local source and cache semantics unchanged); the CI candidate-acceptance run exercises the live path.

body:
Closes #843.

Every imperative entry in `CLAUDE.md` is now adjudicated and indexed in `docs/agents/rules.toml`, with a `<!-- rule:<id> -->` anchor at the end of the entry line.

## Count

The ticket counted 47 bullets. Two changes since then: #842 added the registry pointer line (+1), and the launch-foreground / wait-for-page bullets shared one source line, so splitting them for anchors adds another (+1). 49 entries adjudicated; one of them (the review base SHA) moved its body to `docs/agents/code-review.md`, leaving 48 registered against `CLAUDE.md`.

50 registry rows in total: 17 `enforced`, 10 `code`, 23 `manual`. The two `docs/agents` rows are the surviving bodies of the merged duplicates, so the rules stay indexed after the merge.

## Changes by category

- **Deleted**: none. No entry was `dead`; every one still has a failure mode.
- **Downgraded**: three claims of enforcement that the review found too strong, now `manual` with the partial guard named in `why` — the regression command (CI runs the same command but nothing compares the two), the clean-copy baseline (the test only forbids floating revisions), and the two-interpreter CI split (nothing compares the versions to the workflow).
- **Checks added**: none. The one candidate from #840 (`CHANGELOG` touched whenever `tool/`, `gui/`, `recipes/` change) is a CI job, not this batch.

author: victorantos
body:
## Why
The language code doubles as the date locale, so the `/en/` pages of a bilingual site print US dates ("July 5, 2026"). British and Irish sites had to set `site.language` to `en-GB` to avoid it, which a bilingual site can't do: the code is also its URL prefix and file suffix.

## What
- `site.locales` (optional): maps a site language to a BCP 47 locale used only for dates, e.g. `"locales": { "en": "en-GB" }` keeps `/en/` URLs and `.en.md` files but prints "5 July 2026".
- `dateLocale(site, lang)` in `lib/util.js` (isomorphic); used by the build for `dateFormatted` and by `api-form` for deadlines.
- Validation with teaching errors: keys must be site languages, values must be real locales (`Intl.getCanonicalLocales`).
- Docs: CLAUDE.md, cms-spec §5.4, plain-site skill.
- Version 1.21.0, engine.json regenerated.

## Checks
- `node --test tests/`: 139 pass, 0 fail (3 new tests: helper, validation, build with `en-GB` and `fr-CH`).
- `node build.js` builds; goldens unchanged, since output is identical when `site.locales` is unset.

author: jamesflames
body:
Closes #3412. Refs #1995.

## Defect
On Start → Advanced, submitting an otherwise valid anonymous code with a missing required house/friend name displayed an engine-owned `names_needed` alert, but left keyboard focus on the Sign/Start button. The alert was described only by the code textarea rather than the fields the reader needed to correct.

## Fix
- Keep core as the only name validator; use the structured `names_needed` categories to focus the house or first suitable friend input after refusal.
- Associate the refusal with the affected editable fields using `aria-describedby`; mark a missing house as invalid. Preserve the intentionally optional founder name.
- Keep the structured refusal in a shallow ref so Vue preserves the identity checked by the deferred focus action.
- Do not move focus after successful import or after the reader changed the input before the deferred focus action.
- Add real-Chromium acceptance tests in **Original** and **Plain English** with two sequential refusals, correctable house/friend focus, preserved previous autosave, and canonical founding equality after retry.

## Verification
- Windows, Node 22.23.4: `npm run land -- --no-issue-check` reached `preflight-green` on `95d7f9b4` after rebasing onto main: typecheck, content validation, and all 8,344 fast tests across 264 files passed.
- All 153 Start component tests passed.
- All 16 share-code Playwright tests passed on the rebased head, including the previously failing missing-name focus cases in both prose modes. Used installed Chrome through `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`; the pinned Chromium download timed out.
- Claim #3412 was taken over at the owner's request; `agents check` reported no overlapping paths.

author: yama
body:
## 概要

管理画面の「更新 + 」の選択（保存後の行き先）が、管理ユーザー・Web ユーザー・プロフィール・文書で効かない、または保存のあとで引き継がれなかったのを直した。画面が送る値と、保存処理・戻った画面が読む値が食い違っていた。

Closes #1285

## 変更内容

- 管理ユーザーの新規作成で「次の作成」「この画面」が効くようになった。「この画面」では、作ったユーザーの編集画面へ移る（これまではどれを選んでも一覧へ戻っていた）
- 文書・管理ユーザー・要素で「この画面」を選んで保存すると、1 回目の保存から、開いていたタブのまま戻る
  - 設定「アクティブなタブを記憶する」に従う。「いいえ」なら 1 枚目、「はい (Stay mode)」なら「この画面」のときだけ、「はい (Full)」ならいつも覚える
- 管理ユーザー・Web ユーザーで入力エラーにより差し戻されたとき、選んでいた「保存後」が残る
- プロフィールの「更新 + 」の選択欄を外した（選択を見ておらず、保存後はいつもトップへ戻っていた。戻り先は変わらない）
- 管理ユーザーの画面を全体の読み込みで開いたとき、タブを記憶するかの指定が無視されていたのを直した（「続けて新規」で開いた画面が前のタブから始まっていた）
- 管理画面のタブの部品（`tabpane.js`）は、タブを切り替えたらいつも記録し、開いたときに復元するかを引数で決める形にした。復元しない画面を開いたときは、その画面の記録を消す

## 確認手順

Docker の検証環境（PHP 8.4 / MariaDB 11）で main と比べ、Playwright でシェルの画面遷移と全体の読み込みの両方を確かめた。

- 管理ユーザーの新規作成: 3 つの選択とパスワードの通知方法（画面に表示・メール）で、戻り先が上のとおり。main ではどれも一覧
- 「この画面」のタブ: 文書・チャンク・管理ユーザーで、入口と保存の 4 通りすべて 1 回目の保存から残る。別の文書で選んだタブは紛れ込まない。設定 0・1・2 で上のとおり
- 差し戻し: 管理ユーザー（新規・編集、メール不正・パスワード不一致）と Web ユーザー（新規・編集、メール不正・ユーザー名重複）で、選択と入力値が残る
- 回帰: 文書・管理ユーザー・Web ユーザーの通常の戻り先は main と同じ。タブを復元する画面（バックアップ・ログ・アクセス権限）と復元しない画面（システム情報・文書の情報・ダッシュボード）の動きは main と同じ。管理ユーザーの画面の写真の選択・削除の確認・パスワード欄の出し分けが動く
- JS のエラー・PHP の警告は 0 件。PHP の変更は `php:7.4-cli` の `php -l` を通過

body:
## What

Exclude redirect-only HTTPRoute backends from ordinary Service forwarding exposure.

A ClusterIP Service referenced only by `rules[].backendRefs[].filters[type=RequestRedirect]` previously received an HTTPRoute exposure path, although the Gateway responds with a redirect rather than forwarding to that Service. The same configuration across namespaces could also create unnecessary exposure uncertainty.

Fixes #4676

## Why

The Gateway API supports RequestRedirect on HTTPBackendRef at the Extended support level ([upstream definition](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/blob/main/apis/v1/httproute_types.go#L935-L943)). The adapter added every ordinary backend reference to the exposure model unconditionally.

Recognize a configured RequestRedirect filter and omit that HTTP backend's ordinary forwarding reference. Continue collecting independent mirrors and other forwarding paths. Require both the filter discriminator and a present configuration; incomplete filters retain the existing conservative handling. GRPCRoute processing is unchanged.

## How Tested

The same-namespace and cross-namespace regressions fail against the original implementation and pass with the fix.

Added coverage for:

- Redirect-only backends and cross-namespace uncertainty.
- Other forwarding backends and rules targeting the same Service.
- Rule-level request mirrors and direct NodePort exposure.
- URL rewrites, header modifiers, incomplete filter configurations, and GRPCRoute controls.
- The actual `analyze_service_exposure` response, with a normal forwarding control.

Validation before committing:

- `go test -race -p 2 ./core/pkg/exposure -count=1` — passed.
- `go test -p 2 ./cmd/mcpserver -run 'TestAnalyze(Service|Vulnerability)Exposure' -count=1` — passed.
- `go test -p 2 ./core/pkg/attackpath -run TestCollectInputs -count=1` — passed.
- `golangci-lint run --concurrency=2 --timeout=10m --new-from-rev=origin/master ./core/pkg/exposure/... ./cmd/mcpserver/...` (v2.15.0) — 0 issues.
- Formatter diff and whitespace checks — clean.

The full repository suite and a live Gateway-controller deployment were not run.

- Store pending Spotify URLs, owning Telegram user IDs, metadata snapshots, creation times, and absolute expiry timestamps.

body:
# O que mudou?

Cria um workflow reutilizável (`workflow_call`) que analisa os workflows do GitHub Actions nos PRs: o actionlint (com shellcheck) verifica sintaxe, expressões e scripts, e o zizmor faz a auditoria de segurança. Aplica o workflow primeiro no APAE-INFRA e corrige os findings dos workflows existentes antes da adesão dos demais repositórios.

## Tarefas Relacionadas

* Issue: #72
* Relacionada: #20

## Mudanças Realizadas

* `workflow-lint-reusable.yml` com os inputs `run-actionlint`, `run-zizmor` e `zizmor-min-severity` (padrão `medium`)
* actionlint 1.7.12, shellcheck 0.11.0 e zizmor 1.31.1 baixados dos releases oficiais e verificados por SHA-256, sem actions de terceiros
* `permissions: {}` no topo e permissões mínimas por job
* findings como anotações no PR e SARIF do zizmor publicado na aba Security (categoria `zizmor`); o envio é pulado em PRs de forks
* caller `workflow-lint.yml` no APAE-INFRA (PR e push em `dev`/`main`)
* correções nos workflows existentes:
  * `unpinned-uses`: checkout, markdownlint-cli2, attest e login-action fixados por SHA
  * `artipacked`: `persist-credentials: false` em 5 checkouts sem `git push`
  * `template-injection`: expressões movidas para `env` no SCA e no terraform-validate
  * `ref-version-mismatch`: comentário de versão do `setup-python` no SAST corrigido para `# v5.4.0` (SHA inalterado)
  * shellcheck: correções no SCA e no flyway-validate
* exceções de falsos positivos em `.github/actionlint.yaml` (`job.workflow_repository`/`job.workflow_sha`, ainda não reconhecidos pelo actionlint) e em `.github/zizmor.yml` (`github-env` no `setup-kustomize`)
* documentação em `docs/workflows/reusable-workflow-lint.md`

## Evidências

Execução neste PR:

* **Bloqueio funcionando:** na primeira execução, a auditoria online `ref-version-mismatch` encontrou 1 finding `medium` em `sast-semgrep.yml:62`, exibido como anotação no PR, e o job `zizmor` falhou. Após a correção (`e0acce9`), o job passou.
* **Aba Security:** o SARIF foi processado pelo Code scanning (check `zizmor` concluído); os findings `low` (`self-repository`) aparecem como comentários do `github-advanced-security` sem bloquear o PR.
* **Status final:** `Workflow Lint / actionlint` e `Workflow Lint / zizmor` passando, junto com os demais checks.

Pendente após o merge: validar a adesão em um repositório de aplicação (sugestão: `APAE-atendimento`).
