- 원격 브랜치·디렉토리 모드는 정리 없음 (안내만)
- 커서 이동·글자 입력·esc 는 묻던 것을 취소. 정리를 묻는 중 alt-l 은 벨

## 피커가 속한 창 (4단계 pane 전환 대비)

피커가 정리할 창 안의 modal 패널이면 창을 닫는 순간 피커도 죽는다. modal pane 은 `move-pane`/`join-pane` 불가(3.8 "pane is modal"). 그래서 **그 창의 다른 패널만 닫고 `@worktree` 를 지운다**. 푸터에 "this window closes when you leave the picker". 피커가 끝나면 마지막 패널이 사라지며 창이 닫힌다. **세션의 마지막 창**이면 세션 디렉토리에 창을 먼저 열어 세션을 지킨다.

## 그 밖

- 백업 이름: `refs/archive/<날짜>/<브랜치>`, 같은 날 같은 이름이면 `-2`, `-3` (결정 1). `WorktreeRemove` 훅도 같은 함수
- 옛 `pause`·`confirm`·`delete_branch`·`remove_target`·`--remove` 삭제
- **고친 버그**: 목록 마커와 미리보기가 같은 patch-id 집합을 동시에 계산할 때, 먼저 끝난 쪽의 `find -delete` 가 다른 쪽 임시 파일을 지워 `mv` 가 실패하고(`set -e`) **목록이 통째로 비었다**(원격 없는 저장소에서 재현). 임시 파일을 정리 대상에서 빼고 `mv` 실패도 넘긴다(집합 없으면 조상 관계로만 판정)
- `claude-code.md` 정리 단계 문장

## 시험 (tmux 3.8, fzf 0.74.5, 격리 서버 + 임시 원격·저장소·XDG)

- [x] 거절: 메인 체크아웃, 원격 브랜치, locked, dirty(변경 수)

pull 하고 `chezmoi apply`. 바인딩 그대로라 tmux 재로드 불필요.

author: adolanium
body:
Hermes Desktop reads a package's name from a `name:` line at the start of a line in `plugin.yaml` (`detectPluginComponents` in `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-plugin-install.ts`). `scripts/build_catalog.py` wrote `catalog/plugin.yaml` as JSON, which has no such line. A Desktop catalog install therefore fell back to the folder name and put the desktop half in `desktop-plugins/catalog`. The agent side parses the YAML and uses the package name, so the two halves disagreed. Every plugin packaged this way also collided in the same `desktop-plugins/catalog` folder, so installing a second one failed with `Desktop plugin 'catalog' already exists`. Adolanium/hermes-office#1 reported it, and Adolanium/hermes-office#2 fixed it there.

The build now writes block YAML with JSON scalars (`name: "..."`), still without a YAML library. It also refuses to write a manifest whose name Desktop wouldn't read, so the existing `build_catalog.py --check` CI step guards this. The manifest's fields and values are unchanged.

Tests:

- Desktop's name pattern finds no name in the manifest on the default branch and reads the package name from the regenerated one.
- `build_catalog.py --check`, the catalog policy tests (where the repo has them), `py_compile` and `node --check` pass.
- `hermes plugins validate` passes on the regenerated `catalog/` tree.

`plugin.js` is unchanged, so I didn't rerun the feature test suites. I didn't run a catalog install in Hermes Desktop.

author: oliverhenrichs
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"OliverHenrichs"} -->
_Requested by **Oliver** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FZoQU3XPvco5kDB7fFEbWc?thread=cmsg_01FZoQU3XPvco5kDB7fFEbWcFn5Pa1eMDEehDvnQcBQfjU)_

## What changes for the user

Anonymizing a 10 s Full HD couple clip on the Play alpha failed with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate a 16779280 byte allocation ... growth limit 268435456`. That size is exactly `EdgeTamTracker.decodeOne`'s decoder input (`IE + H0 + H1 + 512` floats plus the array header), allocated fresh on every decode while the Java heap was at its 256 MB cap. With this change, the render should finish instead.

- **Reused graph inputs.** `EdgeTamTracker` now keeps its memcond, decode and memorize inputs as reused fields instead of allocating them on every call. `assemble` writes the memory bank straight into the memcond input, and the encoder's output is read by offset instead of being copied into three arrays. That is about 110 MB less garbage per tracked couple frame, much of it in 16 MB pieces. The fields are lazy, so the tap outline (`DancerOutline`) doesn't pay for the tracking inputs.
- **Pruned corrections.** Re-anchoring corrections are now dropped once they expire (`CORRECTION_TTL`). Before, they were kept for the whole clip at 256 KB each, though `assemble` had stopped reading them.
- **`android:largeHeap`.** The module's manifest now sets it, so the app's manifest picks it up through the merge. This raises the heap cap to the device's large-heap value (512 MB on a Pixel). It is a ceiling, not a reservation.

The math is unchanged: the same values reach the same graphs.

**Needs a native rebuild.** DPM (Dev) and a new Play build both need it, because of the manifest and the Kotlin changes.

## How it was tested

- `npm run docs:check` passes.
- **Not compiled or run here:** the cloud container has no Android SDK, and the laptop wasn't reachable. Please build and test it on the Pixel: re-render the same 10 s Full HD couple clip, and if possible a clip near 30 s.

## Docs

- [x] Behaviour changed: nothing a user could notice changed, except that the render no longer fails
- [ ] A choice with real alternatives was made: a record is added in `docs/decisions/`
- [ ] A plan in `docs/plans/` is done: folded into the spec and the plan file deleted
- [x] New rules or traps for the code are in the nearest `AGENTS.md` (`modules/AGENTS.md`: keep large per-frame buffers as reused fields)
- [ ] New user-facing strings are in all nine `locales/*.json`

author: serathius
body:
Unblock https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143833 OptimisticGetFromCache is change that is meant to improve scalability by potentially sacrificing the latency, but breaks the current `TestDRA/all/ShareResourceClaimSequentially` test by adding 100ms to serial loop executing 4000 times.

Additional 100ms latency is caused by fact that global etcd RV increased but there was no pod event that would inform us so we need to pull from etcd new RV which is done at 100ms period.

This doesn’t matter in for Get method with 1s SLO, and it only appears if there are 0 updates to pod resource. Only cluster that has would care about 100ms latency, would be a high scale high churn cluster that would already be doing a lot of writes to pods, in that case there would not be 100ms delay.

body:
`toLocaleString()` without an explicit locale follows the **host** default, so the same build renders the same count differently:

```
// measured on this host: Intl.NumberFormat().resolvedOptions().locale = "pl-PL"
(1500).toLocaleString()        -> "1500"     // pl-PL groups only from five digits
(1500).toLocaleString("en-US") -> "1,500"
```

`AgentContextUsage` (trigger label, input/output/cached tokens, compact fallback) and `AgentPullRequestBar` (additions/deletions) use the bare call, so the product copy - and its own tests - disagree with the rendered numbers on any non-en-US machine:

```
AssertionError: expected '<button aria-label="Context window: 1…'
  to contain 'aria-label="Context window: 1,500 of 2,000 tokens used (75%)"'
Received: "<button aria-label="Context window: 1500 of 2000 tokens used (75%)" ..."
```

### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A - no matching issue found (`repo:cline/cline is:pr is:open COUNT_LOCALE` → 0 results).

Related PR: #15603 (same class, CLI status bar only). This PR covers the shared `@cline/ui` package, which `#15603` does not touch.

### Description

The repository already pins `en-US` where a number is part of the product's copy - `apps/cli/src/utils/output.ts`, `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/history/HistoryPreview.tsx`, `sdk/packages/shared/src/parse/time.ts` - so this change follows the existing convention:

-   both components get a local `const COUNT_LOCALE = "en-US";`
-   every `toLocaleString()` call passes it: **5** sites in `agent-context-usage.tsx` (trigger label, input, output, cached tokens, compact fallback) and **2** in `agent-pull-request-bar.tsx` (`+additions`, `−deletions`)
-   a new test in `agent-pull-request-bar.test.tsx` covers the second component - the existing fixture only has 5 additions / 2 deletions, which never reach a grouping separator

No exported API changes.

### Test Procedure

Windows 11, Node 24.14.1, bun 1.4.2, `@cline/ui` package:

| step | measurement |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run test` (whole package) **with** this change | **36 files / 372 tests passed**, rc=0 |
| targeted (`agent-context-usage` + `agent-pull-request-bar`) **with** this change | **2 files / 19 tests passed**, rc=0 |
| the two components restored to `main` (new test left in place) | **4 failed**, `Test Files 2 failed \| 34 passed`, rc=1 - 3 assertions in `agent-context-usage`, 1 in `agent-pull-request-bar` |
| `biome check` on all three touched files | rc=0 |
| `git apply --check` of the patch on clean `main` (`94eecbbe1`) | rc=0 |

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Screenshots

N/A - the numbers keep the same markup; only digit grouping becomes stable. Screenshot from the failing run above shows `1500 of 2000` (without) vs `1,500 of 2,000` (with).

author: dillardblom
body:
Release 1.1.0.

- A schedule per location (off, once a day, or every N hours), and locations backed up one after the other instead of at the same time. On the update each existing location keeps the current daily time.
- Administrators are told about a location without a schedule.
- Pin a restore point so the retention policy leaves it alone, and keep a note on it.
- Restore without the recovery kit: the key comes from the location, opened with one of the passphrases.
- A backup key that was never used (no location, no backup) can be replaced by the key of existing backups, with the old kit or with a passphrase. A key that was used is never replaced.
- Heavy background jobs of other apps (Memories, Recognize, Preview Generator, full text search, antivirus scan) pause while a backup runs, at most 6 hours in a row; can be switched off.
- All folders get their original modification time back on a restore.
- Files are read in pieces of 4 MiB instead of 8 KiB (measured on a spinning disk: 5.2 to 26.8 MiB/s for reading).
- A name a snapshot cannot hold gets a notification of its own.
- The list of backups stays within the page: long text wraps instead of scrolling.
- New screenshots.

Tested: unit tests, psalm, recovery scenarios (12, including the key replacement), the update from 1.0.3 on a server that was backing up (SQLite and PostgreSQL), Nextcloud 32, 34 and 35 with SQLite, MariaDB and PostgreSQL, three small disaster recovery simulations (plain, stopped and resumed, full disk), the admin page in a browser. Reviewed locally before this PR.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Pin restore points to protect them from pruning, and add or edit notes displayed with snapshots.
  * Set daily or hourly schedules and time zones per backup location, and pause selected background jobs during backups.
  * Recover using a location passphrase when a recovery kit is unavailable, and repair missing location configuration when possible.
* **Improvements**
  * Restore folder modification times from backups made with version 1.1.0 or later.
  * See queued backup runs and warnings about items omitted due to unsupported names.
  * Locations back up sequentially, with reminders when schedules are turned off.

author: chinmaymk
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"chinmaymk"} -->
_Requested by **Chinmay** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0176mKABrycX377npXK9kW2i?thread=cmsg_0176mKABrycX377npXK9kW2iV3jcMWQCUZQ4sxTkDUf4Cp)_

## Problem
1. `fn nested[T](value: T) Result[T?, String]: return ok(value)` passes `ms check` but fails at build with `alt.new: field 0 has type int but opt<int> is expected` (#2978).
2. `SortedMap.keys()` and `values()` fold chunks with `out = out.concat(chunk)`: quadratic in chunk count (#3033).
3. A temporary resource passed to a call whose later default argument can `try` is never closed (#3005).
4. A generic helper that returns `ok(x)` for a temporary resource argument duplicates its ownership (#2981).
5. `add(var values[key], replace_key(var key))` is accepted, then fails MIR verification: the later argument replaces the key the first one selected with (#2843).
6. `missing.ok_or(cause)` with a named resource keeps `cause` and also puts it in the Result, so it closes twice (#2903).
7. `let get = value.get` on a resource Optional hands out the same resource on every call, so it closes once per call plus once for the owner (#2911).
8. `String.get(i)` and `slice` walk from the start, so an index loop over long non-ASCII text is quadratic (#2916).
9. A Release build of one 20k to 100k line function takes tens of seconds in LLVM: 1500 simple loops in `main` took 10.8 s, 3000 took 41 s (#2929).
10. `missing.get(cause)` with a named resource default returns it as an owned result while the caller still owns it, so it closes twice when the Optional is absent (#3086).

## Proposed change
1. `wrapped_borrow` (`ms-check/src/ownership/walk/returns.rs`) declines a payload the checker marked as wrapped into an optional.
2. `stdlib/collections/sorted.ms`: a private `joined` helper halves the chunk range and concatenates the halves.
3. `try_default_call` / `build_default_thunk` (`ms-lower/src/closure.rs`) keep the temporary registered in the caller and show the thunk an `opt.view`; thunk holders are registered as temps so an early `try` return drops them.
4. `call_callable` (`ms-lower/src/call.rs`): when a borrowed-return call yields a `Result` whose single case wraps a temporary argument, build the owned variant and transfer the temporary's cleanup to it.
5. `held()` (`ms-check/src/ownership/walk/calls.rs`) also holds the non-Copy keys that select an element of a held place for the whole call, so the existing overlap check rejects a later operand that replaces the key. `values[key.clone()]` or a Copy key still compiles.
6. and 10. A retained native argument with no `clone` that the call wraps in its result or may hand back (`ok_or(cause)`, `get(default)`) now moves instead of borrowing. Naming it again later is the usual use-after-move error; a temporary or last use still works. Generic parameters are left to the instantiation. `get-default-closes-unused.ms` is updated: a named default now moves into `get`.
7. `wrapper_passthrough` lists Optional `get` and `get_or_else`, so a bound method value of a resource payload is rejected by the existing "keeps its receiver for repeated calls" rule. Direct calls are unchanged.
8. `@std/text.ms` gains `TextCursor` and `cursor(text)`: pure Manuscript over `Bytes` and `decode_utf8_range`, with `read`, `peek`, `offset`, `seek`, `since` and `is_done`. No runtime change.
9. `ms-clif/src/llvm_ir.rs`: functions over 25k IR lines are compiled `optsize`, which stops loop unrolling and inlining from growing the body, and the `optnone` cliff moves from 100k to 60k lines.

The streaming tar question is settled without a behavior change: `tar_entries` already agrees with `unpack` (stops at the first zero block, accepts a last member with short padding, `EBADMSG` on truncation), and a tar has no trailer to verify, so it is documented and tested rather than made zlib-strict.

Fixes #2978
Fixes #3033
Fixes #3005
Fixes #2981
Fixes #2843
Fixes #2903
Fixes #2911
Fixes #2916
Fixes #2929
Fixes #3086

## Alternatives considered
1. Wrapping in lowering fixed the MIR error but left the result typed as a borrowed variant; the checker records the wrong fact, so it is fixed there.
2. A scalar append loop regresses small maps about 5x; a size threshold hides the tradeoff; a list-extend primitive needs separate design.
3. Cloning the resource for the thunk would double-close it; the one-owner model forbids it.
4. Cloning the result's payload would copy the resource; moving the temporary into the variant keeps one owner.
5. Retaining a snapshot of the key needs new lowering state and an implicit copy; the checker rule needs neither and matches how other overlapping operands are rejected.
6. Cloning `cause` into the Result is impossible (resources have no `clone`); moving every native argument breaks read-only calls, so only arguments the call wraps or may return move. For `get(default)`, making the result a borrow of the default would keep the named default usable, but it needs a new borrowed-result fact for natives; the one-owner rule already says a value handed to a call that may return it moves.
7. Making indirect call results borrowed would break genuine owning functions.
8. A scalar-offset index in the string header grows every string and needs a runtime layout change; an address-keyed cache is ruled out in the wiki.
9. A custom LLVM pass pipeline per function is not expressible (only `optnone` and size attributes are per-function); IndVarSimplify stays superlinear, so the lower cliff bounds the worst case. Outlining statement runs in MIR is a larger change.

## Testing
- New e2e: `accept/generic-result-optional-payload.ms`, `stdlib/sorted_map_lists.ms`, `accept/fallible-default-closes-temporary.ms`, `accept/generic-result-wraps-temporary-resource.ms`, `accept/optional-resource-argument-moves.ms` (ok_or and get, closes once each), `stdlib/text-cursor.ms`; extended `stdlib/archive-stream.ms` and `accept/get-default-closes-unused.ms`. Debug and Release on Cranelift pass.
- New checker fixtures under `crates/ms-check/tests/ownership/`: reject `var_argument_replaces_selecting_key`, `native_argument_moves_resource`, `bound_optional_get_resource`; accept `var_argument_selecting_key_copy`. `cargo test -p ms-check -p ms-lower` and `-p ms-clif --lib llvm_ir` pass; `cargo fmt --check` and clippy are clean; `make repo-check` and `make docs-check` pass. All `accept` and `stdlib` e2e files pass locally on Cranelift.
- Perf, this container, Release: SortedMap issue repro (100k entries, 30 rounds) 0.89 s to 0.026 s; the 100k-scalar non-ASCII scan with a cursor 4 ms (was 7.9 s after the first fix, 23 s before); `ms build` of 1500 loops in `main` 10.8 s to 5.0 s, 2000 loops 17 s to 8.8 s, 3000 loops 41 s to 1.7 s (now `optnone`). The largest function in `bench/perf/` programs is about 21k IR lines (below 25k) except one archived rollback input (56k). Not compared against the dated `bench/perf/` baseline.
- Not run locally: Windows, macOS, the full conformance corpus.

author: raananw
body:
This PR implements step 1 of `docs/INCREMENTAL.md` (#18): an element whose style can't have changed since the last snapshot now reuses its declarations, instead of having all ~380 computed properties read and diffed again.

## What changed

- **The cache** (`StyleCache` in `src/snapshot/serializer.ts`). For each element and pseudo-element it keeps the values that differ from its UA default and the declarations derived from them. A reused element re-reads, and re-diffs, only these properties: sizes, margins, padding, insets, `transform` and origins, grid tracks, `line-height`, and the properties element geometry overrides (`position`, `z-index`, `clip-path`, `translate`/`rotate`/`scale`). A change in the element's UA default, such as becoming `:disabled` or a different `appearance`, re-reads it.
- **What re-reads an element in full** (`freshStyles` and `markStyle` in `src/host/canvas-state.ts`):
  - a DOM change on it or an ancestor, or on a preceding sibling when the page's CSS uses `+`/`~`;
  - a child-list change on its parent;
  - a state pseudo-class or `:has()` selector matching it differently. `src/snapshot/selectors.ts` generalises the `:hover` analysis from #7 and replaces `hover.ts`;
  - a running animation, plus its start and end events.
- **What re-reads everything:** stylesheet changes (except the polyfill's own sheet), viewport changes, fonts loading, an ancestor outside the canvas changing, and a query container changing size.
- **A fix independent of the cache:** an attribute change on an element that contains a canvas, such as a theme class on a wrapper, now takes new snapshots of it. Before, such a change wasn't drawn until something inside the canvas changed.
- **`install({ incremental: false })`** turns reuse off. The test fixture's `?full` uses it.
- **Each snapshot's user timing carries `{ read, reused }`**, and `pnpm bench` reports it as `read/reuse`.
- **Docs:** `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` explains the behaviour, what can still be drawn stale, and the off switch. `docs/INCREMENTAL.md` has an "As implemented" section.

## Where it departs from the design, and why

- **Container queries.** The design said "container queries → re-read everything". Both Underglass demos have `@container` rules somewhere, so reuse was 0 on both. Now only a query container that changed size re-reads everything; each snapshot records the size of the containers in and above the drawable.
- **The polyfill's own stylesheet** holds element geometry, which changes as elements are drawn. Counting it in the stylesheet check made every snapshot after a draw re-read everything. It's left out, and the properties geometry overrides are always re-read instead.
- **Animation end events.** Once a transition ends, `getAnimations()` no longer lists it, so its end state was drawn from the last mid-transition value (a test caught it). Start and end events now mark their target.
- **Declarations are cached, not only values.** With values alone, diffing all properties per element was still most of the cost.

## Results

`pnpm bench` on Windows, against 0.3.0. Chromium is the median of 3 runs; Firefox and WebKit are 1 run each.

| Workload | Engine | Snapshot time, 0.3.0 → now | Longest | Latency median, 0.3.0 → now | Read / reused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| form-typing | chromium | 1460 → 514 ms | 58 → 33 ms | 99 → 44 ms | 0 / 161 |
| list-update | chromium | 3164 → 730 ms | 338 → 101 ms | 344 → 156 ms | 1 / 2000 |
| grid-hover | chromium | 4248 → 1299 ms | 72 → 37 ms | 96 → 58 ms | 2 / 299 |
| theme-switch | chromium | 326 → 384 ms | 66 → 82 ms | 75 → 84 ms | 301 / 0 |
| large-transition | chromium | 682 → 341 ms | 88 → 44 ms | 114 → 63 ms | 1 / 502 |
| underglass-compare-hover | chromium | 444 → 327 ms | 22 → 24 ms | - → - ms | 22 / 35 |
| underglass-strata-clicks | chromium | 2359 → 1751 ms | 246 → 85 ms | 242 → 69 ms | 2 / 529 |
| form-typing | firefox | 1818 → 619 ms | 150 → 31 ms | 97 → 59 ms | 0 / 161 |
| list-update | firefox | 4006 → 900 ms | 465 → 115 ms | 432 → 154 ms | 1 / 2000 |
| grid-hover | firefox | 5496 → 1767 ms | 83 → 44 ms | 84 → 35 ms | 2 / 299 |
| theme-switch | firefox | 411 → 417 ms | 82 → 92 ms | 97 → 96 ms | 301 / 0 |
| large-transition | firefox | 600 → 325 ms | 135 → 38 ms | 117 → 33 ms | 1 / 502 |
| form-typing | webkit | 645 → 402 ms | 36 → 29 ms | 48 → 46 ms | 0 / 161 |
| list-update | webkit | 3025 → 721 ms | 327 → 93 ms | 405 → 188 ms | 1 / 2000 |
| grid-hover | webkit | 6595 → 1992 ms | 97 → 47 ms | 101 → 46 ms | 2 / 299 |
| theme-switch | webkit | 373 → 404 ms | 91 → 86 ms | 121 → 135 ms | 301 / 0 |
| large-transition | webkit | 547 → 280 ms | 105 → 34 ms | 117 → 54 ms | 1 / 502 |

The theme switch, which really does change everything, costs about 15% more for the bookkeeping. In Strata, each snapshot is now about 3× cheaper, so the polyfill follows the button transitions with more snapshots (33 against 10), and total time falls less than per-snapshot time. Long tasks remain on Strata (about 100 ms each): what's left is copying the elements, building the SVG text, and the decode. That's the next thing to profile.

## Tests

- **New `tests/browser/incremental.spec.ts`:** 12 scenarios, each run with reuse on and off; both must draw the same.
  - The scenarios: a class change, a sibling combinator, a child-list change under a structural selector, `:checked` and `:has()` without a DOM change, `:focus-within`, a class on a wrapper outside the canvas, an added stylesheet, a custom property on the layer root, a container query flipped by a text change, a transition's end state, and a text change that moves its neighbour.
  - **Results:** 144 of 144 pass in chromium, firefox and webkit, with `--repeat-each=2`.
- **The tests catch broken rules.** I disabled each rule temporarily and checked which tests fail:
  - Disabling the selector-match and container-size checks fails exactly the 4 scenarios that depend on them, with reuse on.
  - Disabling the DOM-change rules fails exactly the 6 that depend on them. The wrapper scenario also fails with reuse off, confirming that bug predates this PR.
- **Unit tests:** `tests/unit/selectors.test.ts` replaces the hover tests, adding sibling detection, the rules key and changed matches. `pnpm test` passes 49 of 49.
- **Other checks:**
  - `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` are clean.
  - `pnpm size`: 22.69 KB main, up from 20.96 KB; I raised the budget to 23 KB, within the 25 KB cap. Worker 3.69 KB.
  - Full `playwright test` on Windows across chromium, webkit, firefox, native and canary: 326 passed, and the 16 failures are exactly the known Windows ones.

## Not in this PR

body:
## Summary

Adds feedback package v2 (`pkg:feedback.evidence-finding/v2`). Recurrence now counts distinct operations, on the time the outcome was observed, within one scope. The v1 fixtures are frozen, so namespaces certified on v1 keep resolving v1.

- The observation record gains three fields:
  - `operation_id`: the plan or deployment, stable across attempts;
  - `observed_at_ms`: the producer's observation time;
  - `scope`: the environment and tenant.
  The observation Action requires all three, and `operation_id` and `scope` must not be blank.
- The investigator:
  - counts distinct `operation_id`s, so retries of one operation never qualify;
  - windows on `observed_at_ms`, clamped to ingest time, so a drained backlog is not recurrence;
  - clusters by (signature, scope), so two environments are two problems;
  - skips observations without an operation or scope.
- The analysis bucket and the GitHub marker include scope.
- ADR 0095 and `docs/capability-packages.md` describe v2.

Fixes #2061
Fixes #2063

### Breaking

- Producers must emit `operation_id`, `observed_at_ms` and a non-blank `scope` against the v2 package.
- The investigator ignores observations without them.
- The GitHub marker now hashes (namespace, signature, scope). No issue was ever published under the old marker, since no runner has been deployed.

### Upgrade

Install the v2 package in a namespace and move its producer to v2. Namespaces left on v1 keep their v1 types.

## Tests

- `cargo test --test feedback_adapters`, which adds:
  - retries of one operation staying internal;
  - a drained backlog not being recurrence;
  - one signature in two scopes being two problems;
  - a blank scope never being investigated.
- A digest test keeps the shipped v1 fixtures frozen.
- `cargo fmt-check`, `cargo clippy-all` and `cargo test-all` pass at the top of the stack.

author: sergeberwert
body:
Closes #25, the last feature milestone of 0.2.

## What was done

- **Drag source.** `platform::DragSource` takes the window as `winit` describes it (`WindowRef`: the raw window and display handles eframe's `Frame` gives out, plus the scale) and is polled while the desktop runs the drag. macOS begins an `NSDraggingSession` from the content view with the files as `NSURL` items and the first file's icon under the cursor; Windows runs `DoDragDrop` with an `IDataObject` serving `CF_HDROP`; Linux joins `winit`'s own `wl_display` through the raw display handle, binds its own seat and pointer to see the press serial, and starts a `wl_data_source` offering `text/uri-list`, or, on X11, an XDND version 5 source on a connection of Rick's own that follows the pointer every frame and serves the selection.
- **Drop position.** The new `DropTarget` trait supplies the cursor position the backend leaves out (`GetCursorPos` against the window, `NSEvent.mouseLocation` converted into the view, `XQueryPointer`, the Wayland data device's motion), so a drop from outside lands on the folder row under it. On Wayland, where `winit` 0.30 has no drop target at all, Rick's own `wl_data_device` receives the files, read by a blocking thread of the runtime that wakes the UI.
- **UI.** The handover happens one frame after the cursor leaves, so the ghost is off the screen when the desktop takes over; egui's pointer state and dragged widget are reset when the native drag ends, since the backend never sees the release. Without a position the drop lands in the focused pane's folder, which the UI now does explicitly instead of using the stale pointer.
- **Benchmarks.** A five-run bench on the three runners ([42488206033](https://github.com/Open-Breach/rick/actions/runs/42488206033)) re-measured everything; `BENCHMARKS.md` is rewritten from it with the 0.2 tables filled, and `bench.rs` follows. macOS: listing first batch 400 ms → 50 ms, complete 3 s → 1.6 s, PDF first frame 1.2 s → 200 ms, fixture 40 → 35 s, startup 150 → 25 ms, session start 15 → 12 ms; Windows: search first 150 → 100 ms; plugin-load and archive-zip-first provisional targets 100 → 50 ms. Two had to loosen because the runner fell short: macOS cancel 50 → 80 ms, Windows fixture 30 → 45 s. `3d-first` landed on `dev` after the run and waits for the next one.
- `dev` was merged into the branch (ext-ssh, permissions, localisation, the installer); the new questions are 185 to 188. Four pedantic clippy findings of the merged permissions code on the macOS and Windows targets, which tier 1 never sees, are fixed in their own commit so tier 2 stays green.

## What was assumed

QUESTIONS.md 185 to 188: `winit` 0.30 receives no drops on Wayland (question 62 assumed otherwise), so the platform receives them there; positions and handovers are for the root window only, since eframe hands out its handles alone, and secondary windows fall back; no drag image on Wayland and X11; the pointer reset after a native drag; the four macOS benchmarks are the listing pair, `pdf-first` and `tree-first`, retargeted by the 0.1 rule (median × 1.5, never below Linux, the spec's number where that is met), with the two that fell short following the runner.

## Which acceptance test proves it

`crates/tests/tests/dnd.rs`: `leaving_the_window_hands_the_drag_to_the_platform` (the fake records the items' URIs when the cursor leaves, one frame after, and the drag runs on the platform until it ends), `an_external_drop_with_a_position_lands_on_the_row_under_it`, `an_external_drop_without_a_position_lands_in_the_focused_pane`, `files_the_platform_receives_itself_drop_like_the_backends`, `without_a_backend_window_the_drag_stays_inside`. The platform crate's unit tests cover the URI list and the fake; two display-gated smoke tests exercise the real X11 and Wayland connections (run under Xvfb and a headless Weston). `bench::tests::benchmarks_md_matches_the_targets` ties `BENCHMARKS.md` to `bench.rs`. Clippy passes for the platform crate cross-checked against `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; fmt, clippy, doc, the workspace tests, cargo deny and the string check pass on the merged tree.

## What was deliberately left out

The manual checklist with a screen recording per OS could not be done in the cloud session, so the macOS and Windows code is compile-checked and reviewed but not yet run against Finder or Explorer; no drag image on Wayland and X11; secondary windows keep 0.1's fallback.

author: copoka
body:
### What

Real-time collaboration for DeckCraft presentations: one authoritative session per document,
ordered operations with de-duplication, per-user undo, presence, reconnect, viewer roles and a
server-side `.pptx` commit. The whole feature is behind a flag and is off by default.

### Why

The cabinet needs a browser-capable editor without a server-side OnlyOffice; today DeckCraft is a
single-user editor. Two or more people must be able to edit one deck at the same time without
losing each other's text, and the result must still open as a valid `.pptx`.

### How

- **Model**: authoritative server, one `Hub` per document. The server applies each operation to the
  engine and broadcasts the confirmed command, so every replica runs the same command in the same
  order. No OT/CRDT dependency: operations carry final values, and the few relative edits
  (`text.insert`, `text.delete`) are rebased against the journal tail on the server.
- **Protocol**: WebSocket, JSON envelope `hello/welcome/op/applied/rejected/presence/resync/
  snapshot/commit-result/error/ping`. The token travels in the first frame, never in the URL. The
  actor and role come from the JWT. One server `version` orders everything, `opId` de-duplicates a
  10 000-entry window, structural operations are exclusive at the head, tombstones refuse late
  operations.
- **Identity**: session keys (`slideKey`, `shapeKey`) are derived identically on both sides from
  `fileId` plus the same document walk; new object ids are deterministic on every replica.
- **Storage**: optional `COLLAB_STORE_DIR` keeps a native base plus an append-only journal, flushed
  before apply, with a snapshot every 200 operations and replay through the same `apply` path.
  Without it the server is memory-only.
- **Media**: pictures, audio and video do not travel in operations.
  `PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/media/{sha256}` stores content-addressed bytes (signature allowlist:
  images ≤ 8 MiB with 512 objects / 64 MiB; audio and video ≤ 32 MiB with 32 objects / 192 MiB per
  session) and the operation carries only the digest; every replica fetches it. The desktop HTTP
  client follows the link scheme: `ws://` is plain, `wss://` uses `rustls` with the platform roots.
- **Client**: `CollabDoc` normalises commands to absolute operations and applies the confirmed
  commands; unanswered operations return to the front of the queue on a disconnect and are resent
  with the same `opId`. `WsTransport` reconnects with the same handshake.
- **UI**: flag `DECKCRAFT_COLLAB=1` (web `?collab=1`) shows the status indicator, participants,
  remote selections/carets, commit warnings and the viewer lock. With the flag off nothing changes.
- **Roles and limits**: a viewer's operation is refused by the server and by the engine's read-only
  gate. Message size, operations/second and participants are bounded.
- **Commit**: the server builds the `.pptx` from the authoritative document and returns
  `sha256`, inline bytes and `warnings[]`; a stale `expectedVersion` is a `409` and never
  overwrites an externally changed file.

### Flag and compatibility

- Off by default: no transport, no command normalisation, `Session::is_read_only()` is `false`.
- File format untouched: the writer is the existing `crates/pptx` writer; the native base is the
  existing `.deckcraft` format.
- Existing commands, CLI and MCP are unchanged; a collab room introduces no new required
  configuration for single-user runs.

### Tests

```bash
cargo test -p deckcraft-collab-proto
cargo test -p deckcraft-collab
cargo test -p deckcraft-collab-server
cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui collab::
cargo test -p deckcraft-engine
cargo clippy -p deckcraft-collab -p deckcraft-collab-proto \
  -p deckcraft-collab-server -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
cargo xtask layers
```

Covered scenarios:

- two editors converge on shapes, text, slides, groups and order; concurrent text inserts in one
  paragraph keep both texts (server-side rebase);
- duplicate `opId` is applied once; a late operation on a deleted object is refused by the
  tombstone; structural operations do not interleave;
- per-actor undo/redo with `undo-conflict` when someone else touched the object; fill, outline and
  `format.*` steps restore the exact model value they replaced, a group's fill/line restores every
  changed member, and slide insert/delete/duplicate restore the whole slide;
- reconnect: unanswered operations are resent with the same `opId`; `resync` replays the tail;
- viewer: server refusal and engine refusal;
- security: invalid/expired token, wrong app/file/session, rate and size limits;
- restart: a room reopens from the base and journal with the same version and document;
- media: rejected uploads (viewer, wrong digest, no token), one object for repeated bytes, a
  picture applied from a reference, and a journal replay that loads the object before the
  operation;
- flag off: single-user behaviour and the engine test suite are unchanged.

### Limits (deliberately out of this PR)

- The v1 command set is collaborative (`shape.move/setBounds`, `text.set/insert/delete`,
  `shape.insert`, `insert.picture/video/audio`, `shape.fill`, `shape.line`, 17 `format.*`
  commands over an explicit shape, `edit.delete`, `slide.new/delete/move/duplicate`,
  `arrange.group/ungroup/reorder`). Other mutating commands are refused in a shared session
  instead of silently diverging; the list is in `docs/collab/production.md`.
- Media covers pictures, audio and video; fonts and 3D models are still refused by the channel.
- The browser build has no `web-sys` link yet; the UI is honest about the offline state.
- The cabinet callback that turns `commit-result` into a new file version is a host-bridge
  contract and is not wired (same external blocker as WordCraft).
- Edits become visible on `applied`, not on the keystroke; optimistic preview is a later slice.
- Structural undo of shape insert/delete and group/ungroup is out of v1; merge operations,
  fill/outline/`format.*` value steps, a group's fill/line (one image per changed member) and
  slide insert/delete/duplicate (whole-slide image) are covered.
- A client that missed a compacted journal tail cannot rebuild; a chunked base `snapshot` is the
  next step. Restart persistence is covered by the journal.

## Review guide

The stack is intentionally one commit per slice; review in this order:

| Branch | Slice |
|---|---|
| `collab/rfc` | RFC and ADRs 0001–0010 |
| `collab/pr1` | wire types, adapter, `apply_remote` |
| `collab/pr2` | per-user undo/redo |
| `collab/pr3` | `DocSession`: versions, dedup, snapshots, commit |
| `collab/pr4` | `ClientSession`: queue, dedup, resync, viewer |
| `collab/pr5` | commit/409, presence, two-client e2e |
| `collab/pr6` | UI behind a flag, presence, viewer gate |
| `collab/pr7` | `CollabDoc` glue, in-memory `Hub` |
| `collab/pr8` | WebSocket server, desktop link, UI wiring, undo requests, persistence |
| `collab/pr9` | text insert/delete with rebase, shape insert, engine command queue |
| `collab/pr10` | media channel: pictures by `sha256`, upload/fetch, persistence |

Only the final branch is meant to be pushed as `feature/realtime-collaboration`; the intermediate
branches exist for review.

## Checklist mapping

- [x] RFC/design doc — `docs/collab/rfc.md`; operator view — `docs/collab/production.md`.
- [x] Sync server — `apps/deckcraft-collab-server`.

author: alvarocumora
body:
## Resumen

Implementa la arquitectura de 3 zonas dockeadas propuesta por Alvy para resolver el problema de "Widget Overload": en pantallas angostas (~1002px), los 6 widgets flotantes absolutos del visor sumaban ~1056px de ancho (panel de capas 320px + Sentinel-2 240px + leyenda de muestras 232px + otros), tapando ~75% del mapa.

- **Izquierda**: `SceneLayerPanel` pasa de overlay absoluto a columna flex real (dockeada), conservando las carpetas Leapfrog, filtro P1/P2/P3 y leyenda espectral ya existentes.
- **Centro**: lienzo 3D limpio; cabecera y toolbar quedan acotados a esta columna (ya no invaden las laterales). Se agrega un botón de pantalla completa real (Fullscreen API).
- **Derecha**: nuevo `SceneInspectorPanel` — unifica los controles de Sentinel-2 L2A y de ley de muestras (antes 2 cajas flotantes separadas) en un solo panel contextual que no ocupa espacio si no hay nada que mostrar.
- `MiningEvidenceInspector` ("Evidencia") se reubica de `ProjectSceneFrame` a la columna central de `GeoScene3D`, porque con el nuevo dock izquierdo a ancho completo habría quedado tapado en su posición original (`bottom-3 left-3`).
- Altura del visor: de fija (`620px`) a responsiva (`min(78vh, 900px)`, mínimo `520px`) en `ProjectSceneFrame`.

## No tocado intencionalmente
- Animación de transición al colapsar los paneles (hoy es mount/unmount instantáneo, no un slide suave). Se puede agregar en un follow-up si Alvy lo quiere.
- `SceneCopilot` (el bubble flotante de chat): sigue sin montarse en producción (`showCopilot={false}` en el único call site), no requirió cambios.

## Verificación
- `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=4096" npx tsc --noEmit` — sin errores.
- `npx eslint` sobre los archivos tocados — sin errores.
- `npx vitest run` — suite completa: 886 tests pasados, 0 fallos.
- Sin credenciales de Supabase en este sandbox: no se verificó visualmente en navegador contra datos reales.

author: buiducnhat
body:
## What

**Deep research is a mode**, like Claude Research or Gemini Deep Research, replacing the `deep-research` skill.

- A **Research** switch in the message box (Quick / Standard / Deep) and `/research [depth] <question>` in the app; `/research` in Telegram and Zalo.
- The agent frames the question, shows a **plan card** to confirm (depth, and items × fields for comparisons), researches in rounds of parallel `delegate_task` helpers (up to **8 at Deep**), records the sources it cites, rates each key claim, critiques its own draft (a **four-role red team** at Deep with one loop-back round), and saves `research/<slug>-<date>.md` plus a self-contained `.html` report **without an approval** (new files only, inside `research/`, symlink-safe, size-capped).
- A **banner** shows phase, pages read and sources cited; opening it lists the sources and, on the phone, the report. The report opens in the Files panel.
- Telegram sends the plan as buttons and the report as `.md`/`.html` files; Zalo sends text and the saved path.

**Visual output**: mermaid diagrams are drawn by **Pele** (replacing mermaid; the renderer build shrank from ~13 MB to ~8 MB), SVG as data images, and HTML artifacts run after a **Run** press in a sandboxed frame with no network (Chart.js allowed); the Files panel previews `.html`.

**Prompt**: reply in the user's language; treat text from MCP tools and files as data; cite `[n]` with a Sources list; name saved files; confirm before deleting, sending to others, or bulk changes.

**Quit fix**: quitting (including from the tray) stops a daemon an app started, even one reused from an earlier crash; a login-service or terminal daemon keeps running.

## Verification

- `vp check` clean; **998 tests pass** (new: research session tests, research lib tests, artifact protocol + save-artifact tests, daemon quit tests, channel tests).
- Smoke in the built app with a scripted model: `/research` → plan card → Start → banner "Report ready" → report opens in the Files panel. Crash → reuse → quit: the daemon is shut down.

## Changesets

`visual-output-deep-research` (minor: desktop, web, daemon, shared, agent-core) and `quit-stops-app-daemon` (patch: desktop, daemon, shared).

> [!NOTE]
> Fourth of six stacked pull-requests bringing the Cartesian2D work of v10.2.0 to `pyTooling.Cartesian3D`. This one mirrors the arranging part of #694.

# New Features

* `pyTooling.Cartesian3D`:
  * `Element3D.MoveTo(parent, keepPosition=True)`: moves an element into another group; by default it keeps the absolute position, so its local coordinates change. `AddChild`'s `AlreadyOwnedError` suggests it.
  * `Element3D.AlignTo(reference, alignment)`: moves an element, so an edge or the center of its absolute bounding box aligns with another element's.
  * New enum `Alignment3D`: the members of `Alignment2D` (`MinX` ... `MaxY`) plus `MinZ`, `CenterZ`, `MaxZ`. A separate enum with the 3D suffix (as decided for #696); an `Alignment2D` is rejected with `TypeError`.
* `pyTooling.Cartesian3D.Groups`: `Group3D.DistributeX`, `DistributeY`, `DistributeZ` move the children along that axis to equal gaps, at a given gap after the first child or evenly between the first and the last one.


# Documentation

* `doc/DataStructures/Cartesian.rst`: moving, aligning and distributing 3D elements.
* `doc/News.rst`: the 3D groups line mentions arranging.


# Unit Tests

* `tests/unit/Cartesian/Cartesian3D.py`, `Groups3D.py`: `MoveTo` with and without keeping the position, `AlignTo` for every `Alignment3D` member, distributing along each axis (gap and evenly), every error with its full message.

body:
Ports the movement from #725 to current `main` (which now has #723's render pacing and #724's rooms). The player is still Kenney's `character-female-b`; the Quaternius character from #725 is not included. Supersedes #725.

## What changed
**Movement** (`native/crates/office/src/sim.rs`, `walk.rs`). These are #725's changes, applied unchanged.
- **Acceleration and braking.** The keys steer a velocity: it takes about 0.3 s to get up to speed, letting go stops you within about a step, and changing direction is quicker still, so a square turn becomes a short curve.
- **Smooth facing.** You turn towards where the keys point, easing in at the end of the turn.
- **Shift to run.** Hold Shift to run at 6 m/s instead of walking at 3 m/s. A click-to-walk also runs while Shift is held. The app tracks Shift through `on_modifiers_changed` and each key event's modifiers, and forgets it when the window loses focus.
- **Camera look-ahead.** Following you, the camera aims 0.3 s ahead of where you're going, eased.
- **Wall sliding.** You keep the part of your velocity that runs along a wall, and `slide` now takes you right up to the wall instead of stopping a step short. If you're placed inside an obstacle, you can walk out of it.
- With reduced motion, everything still happens at once.

**The figure** (`native/crates/office/src/player.rs`)
- Still Kenney's character. Nothing from #725's character came over: no Quaternius asset or License, no head or build scaling, no hoodie recolour, no material names in `glb::SkinnedPart`, no `from_glb`/`find_clip`, and no `player` example.
- **Stride measured from Kenney's legs.** Kenney's figure has no foot bones, so `stride_of` takes the floor point under each leg's hip and carries it through the clip. Each cycle's length is how far the feet swing apart front to back. Measured: 1.62 m walking and 1.90 m running, against 1.64 m and 1.90 m from the old leg-length constants, which are still the fallback if the legs aren't found. The walk and run play at the speed you move, so the feet stay roughly planted.
- **Run cycle.** Kenney's figure has a `sprint` clip and uses it. A figure with no `sprint` or `run` clip runs on its walk clip, sped up, with the same stride.
- **Start and stop lean.** The figure leans forward as it sets off and back as it stops, on top of the existing lean into turns.

**Help.** The help card has a new row, **Shift: Hold to run**, and both keyboard hints mention Shift. The strings are in en-US and pt-BR.

## Checked
- `cargo test --release -p agentbox-office`: 66 pass, including #725's tests for acceleration, turning, Shift and slide, and a new check that Kenney's measured strides are close to the leg-length figures and that the run's stride is longer.
- Ran both builds in the app on the agent's desktop against `fake-daemon` with lavapipe (software rendering, so the frame rate is low): walking, turning while walking, running with Shift and reversing. The recordings are in Media as `office-movement-before` and `office-movement-after`.

## Not done
- Software rendering only; on a GPU the motion is smoother.

author: yutamago
body:
The open Phase 9 items: per-field data edits, `[Inject]`, and private data for a mod's new workers. Laying out unchanged workers in place is not in it; `docs/plan.md` says why.

## Per-field data edits

A mod sets single values in a C# static constructor, where C# itself sets static fields before anything uses them:

```csharp
partial class M209
{
    public static int Turns = 5;                 // a new variable with an initial value
    static M209()
    {
        MonsterStats.Hp = 4321;                  // the monster file's stat record (section 2 and its copy, 6)
        MonsterRewards.Gil = 999;                // its rewards (section 4)
        V7 = 2; Table[3] = 7;                    // shared/event variables, elements of tables
        Data.At<ushort>(DataArea.Other, 0x20) = 7;   // bytes no variable covers
    }
}
partial class Boy { static Boy() { Steps = 12; } }   // an event worker's private data
```

- The battle reads stats and rewards from the monster's own file (ffx-decomp `docs/formats/monster.md`: `Mon_AttachData`, `MsSetRamChr`). All 361 monsters have identical stats in sections 2 and 6, and the linker writes both.
- Each assignment becomes a `data` edit (package format 3) with a hash of its area's vanilla bytes. The linker writes the bytes in place before any layout, so nothing moves. Two mods setting the same bytes are a conflict (the later one wins); edits to different fields combine.
- In battle the game clears a worker's private data at set-up, so a monster's worker can't take initial values there; this is a compile error.
- ATL4001 flags a static constructor that does more than set initial values.

## `[Inject]`

```csharp
[Inject(nameof(OnTurn), After = nameof(Btl.UseCommand), Occurrence = 3)]
void Exhausted() { Btl.SetActorProperty(ActorProperty.Hp, 1); }
```

- Anchor model: the statement of the decompiled source that holds the n-th call of that name, as written there. A label was rejected because few statements have one; a statement index was rejected because it is unreadable and shifts when the decompiler folds code. The compiler resolves the anchor against the vanilla source at each build (a source map of the compiled vanilla code). The package holds the statement's code range under the method's hash, so a changed method is a hash mismatch and a changed source is a build error. Neither can put the code in the wrong place.
- The linker weaves injects into the copy of the method it already makes for postfixes. Jumps from inside the statement stay inside it: a loop's back edge doesn't repeat the code before the loop, and its exit runs the code after it once. Jumps from outside run the code before it. Injects from several mods at one point run in load order. A replacement of the method drops them, reported as a conflict.
- ATL4002 checks the anchor in the IDE.
- Limit: labels are 16-bit, so blitzball's 1.6 MB method (worker 36, 53,203 labels) can't be copied. The linker reports it as an error.

## Private data for new workers

`[Worker(PrivateLength = …)]`, `[PrivateData]` and a static constructor on a mod's new worker. The linker gives the worker a private block of its own.

## Numbers

- Data edits, corpus: 1,614 scripts took 5,424 edits (shared, other and event data; on all 361 monsters also HP and gil). Exactly those bytes change, and the file size stays the same.
- Inject, corpus: injects before and after a statement in 67,851 methods of 1,598 scripts. Each result parses, lays itself out again byte for byte, and keeps its data areas, its other workers' code and the file's later sections. Each patched method is its vanilla code, instruction for instruction, with the injects at their points. The 5 copies of blitzball's oversized method were skipped. Files grew by 57 KB on average, because every worker's first six methods were copied.
- `atel link` of the examples onto `m209.bin`: ToughLarva leaves the file at 55,280 bytes (vanilla size, edits in place); LarvaInject makes it 56,688.

## Examples

`examples/ToughLarva` (data edits) and `examples/LarvaInject` (`[Inject]`); the SDK test builds both and compares their packages with `atel compile-mod`'s.

Tests: full suite green locally (593 passed, 1 skipped; corpus and SDK tests with FFX_GAME_DIR). Not checked in game yet.

author: aevnsvi
body:
## What was wrong

The "Collection versions" tab of an ansible repository listed `content/ansible/collection_versions/` with a `repository` parameter and a `keywords` filter. That endpoint does not know either, and Pulp answers an unknown filter with `400 Invalid Filter`, so the tab showed an error instead of its rows. It also read each row as `{ collection_version, repository }`, a shape the plain content endpoint does not return: it returns flat rows (`pulp_href`, `namespace`, `name`, `version`, `description`, ...).

The "Add collection" dialog read the same nested shape and threw a `TypeError` into the error boundary as soon as the server held one collection version.

## What changes

- The tab lists the collection versions of the repository's latest version with `repository_version`, and sends only parameters the endpoint accepts (paging, `namespace`, `name`). The sort key of the list is no longer forwarded: the columns are not sortable.
- Rows are rendered from the flat fields. The collection is plain text.
- The Remove action reads the flat row and takes the repository from the tab state. Opening and closing its dialog no longer drops the repository from that state, which made "Add collection" fail afterwards.
- The Add dialog lists the server's collection versions as flat rows, keys the selection on the content href, and no longer shows a repository column or filters by repository name (flat rows carry no repository). Adding content that is already in the repository is a no-op in Pulp.
- The ansible repository page has no "Collections" tab any more, and the collections of its versions tab are no longer links into the collection placeholder.

## Tests

- `tab-collection-versions.test.tsx`: the request carries `repository_version` and nothing the endpoint rejects, a flat row shows as `ns.col v1.0.0` with its description and without a link, the namespace filter is sent as `namespace`, removal sends `modify/` with the content href, and Add collection still opens after a removal dialog was cancelled.
- `ansible-repository-collection-version-add.test.tsx`: the dialog renders flat rows without a repository column and without throwing, asks only for paging parameters, adds through `modify/` with `add_content_units`, and unselects a row clicked twice.

All tests fail on the previous code and pass now. The full local gate (unit tests, type check, lint, prettier, ls-lint, public content guard, production build) is green.

author: ygdrasil-io
body:
## Scope

The glyph chain draws the HUD in framebuffer pixels with fixed anchors (font 18 px, base 24/60, line height 30). That is only correct at density 1: the web Retina canvas, Android Vulkan surfaces and iOS Metal drawables are 2–3.5× denser, so off desktop the HUD rendered at a third to a half of its intended on-screen size, hugging the top-left corner. The web host had also drifted to its own smaller anchors (14/30/26).

While demoing on all platforms, the iOS app turned out to be unbuildable in the first place (orphan iosMain source set + a Kotlin/Native supertype-mixing violation in the controller) — fixed in the second commit.

## Changes

- `GlyphOverlay`: new `scale` parameter (default 1); font size and every anchor (24/60, line height 30) multiply with it.
- `WebMain`: drops the inline HUD plumbing for the shared `GlyphOverlay` scaled by `devicePixelRatio`, rebuilt when browser zoom changes the ratio; anchors unified with desktop.
- `CornellActivity`: passes `resources.displayMetrics.density`.
- `CornellViewController`: passes `UIScreen.mainScreen.nativeScale`; restructured because Kotlin/Native forbids mixing Objective-C and Kotlin supertypes on one class.
- `build.gradle.kts`: iosMain created and attached over mobileMain (explicit dependsOn edges had left it orphaned, so the Xcode app could not find `CornellViewControllerKt`).
- Tests: JVM pins the 2× anchor math, the unchanged 1× desktop reference, and the 512×192 atlas placing every status glyph at xxxhdpi (4×); iOS simulator test walks the whole glyph chain at 3× density.

## Validation

- [x] Tests run: `./gradlew jvmTest iosSimulatorArm64Test` → 10/10 pass
- [x] Compile: `compileKotlinWasmJs`, `:androidApp:compileDebugKotlin`, `compileKotlinIosArm64`, `compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` → all green
- [x] Manual check: desktop window (live), web at http://localhost:8080 (WebGPU, controls), Android emulator 420dpi — HUD ink verified at 63/157 px (predicted 63/123 + bearing), iOS simulator @3x — HUD verified rendering at the expected 3× size (36 px caps ≈ 39 predicted; sits one safe-area inset lower than the screen top, which is host-view layout, not the scale factor)

## Notes

- The desktop JVM host keeps scale 1; if it ever reads the GLFW content scale on Retina Macs, the same parameter is the hook.
- On emulators the first HUD build (CPU rasterization of the status glyphs) can take several seconds to appear after launch.
- The 512×192 R8 atlas holds the full two-line status at 4× (verified by test); a longer status text at xxxhdpi would be the first case to watch.

author: accuser
body:
Closes #255 (models-first approach).

## What

Runs a nightly CodeQL scan over the TypeScript that `bynk compile --target workers` **emits**. It comes with models of the Workers runtime, plus canaries that prove those models still fire.

- **`.github/codeql/bynk-emitted/`** is a QL pack.
  - `BynkEmitted.qll` models two things:
    - the Worker entry's `request` parameter, as a remote source and a redirect source;
    - a `Response`'s `Location` header, as a URL-redirect sink.
  - `queries/` re-runs `js/request-forgery` and `js/server-side-unvalidated-url-redirection` with those models imported, as `bynk/emitted-request-forgery` and `bynk/emitted-url-redirection`.
- **`canaries/`** holds four deliberately vulnerable projects:
  - SSRF through a body field, and through an `Option`;
  - open redirect through `?next=`, and through a `Result`.

  `expected.tsv` names the query that must flag each one.
- **`scripts/codeql-emitted.sh`**:
  - compiles `examples/*` plus the canaries, builds the database, and runs the default suite plus the pack;
  - exits 1 if any canary isn't flagged by its expected query **inside its own emitted tree**;
  - writes a SARIF with canary results stripped, for upload.
- **`.github/workflows/codeql-emitted.yml`** runs on `schedule` (08:20 UTC) and `workflow_dispatch` only.
  - It installs the CLI with `codeql-action/setup-codeql`, not `init`, so a failing job can't upload under `codeql.yml`'s JS category.
  - It uploads as category `emitted-ts`. When a canary isn't flagged it uploads nothing, so blind models can't mark real alerts fixed.
  - On a scheduled failure it opens or comments on a tracking issue.
- **ADR**: the `design/pending/codeql-emitted-ts.md` increment (patch).

**Out of band.** No `pull_request`, `merge_group` or `push` trigger. It is not in `ci-green` and not called from any release job. `ci.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `release.yml` and `release-bootstrap.yml` are untouched. `rust-cache` is restore-only, so nightly entries don't evict PR caches.

## Phase 1 result (local, CodeQL 2.27.4)

| canary | query | flagged |
|---|---|---|
| `ssrf-body` | `bynk/emitted-request-forgery` | yes |
| `ssrf-option` | `bynk/emitted-request-forgery` | yes |
| `redirect-query` | `bynk/emitted-url-redirection` | yes |
| `redirect-result` | `bynk/emitted-url-redirection` | yes |

- **False-positive load on the 13 real examples: 0 findings.**
- That zero is real: the source model matched all 13 Worker entries.
- The failure path is tested: an unmatched expectation exits 1. That test caught a real bug, where a `| tee` subshell had swallowed the failure; it's fixed.
- A full run takes about 2 minutes locally. Expect 10 to 15 minutes on a hosted runner, with a cold debug build of `bynk`.

## Findings worth knowing

- **The experiment's SSRF example didn't test sources.** `webhook-relay`'s target comes from `Secrets`. The real gap was that the stock models find no sources in a module Worker. The `fetch` sink was already there.
- **Not needed:** a `Fetch.send` sink (default call resolution follows `compose.ts` → `deps.Fetch` → global `fetch`), and `Result`/`Option` flow summaries (default taint follows the `{ tag, value }` codecs).
- **QL, not models-as-data.** A data-extension row names code by npm package, or by a `file:` path that another file imports. The emitted runtime is reached only through relative imports, and the Worker entry is imported by nothing.
- **No KV model.** CodeQL doesn't follow taint across storage. The only KV-to-sink flow is `link-shortener`'s stored redirect, which is that example's purpose.
- **Coverage is narrow.** Only the two wrapped queries see user input. The other stock taint queries stay blind (the README says so). Covering another class means wrapping its query and adding a canary.

## Not verified

A `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow can't be triggered before it's on `main`. So the `setup-codeql` output, the SARIF upload and the report job haven't run in CI. After merge, run:

```
gh workflow run codeql-emitted.yml --repo bynk-lang/bynk
```

Then check that the run passes and that the Security tab shows an `emitted-ts` configuration with 0 alerts.

author: ivarvong
body:
A pan or zoom re-render misses the layout cache on every frame (set_xlim changes the spec). Each miss used to walk the spec with `sameSpec` up to the change, then deep-copy the whole spec (data arrays included) with `snapshot` to store a key that the next frame would miss again. The browser re-render bench put `sameSpec` + `snapshot` at 13–28 % of mpl's warm SVG time.

`resnapshot(prev, live)` (core/snapshot.ts) compares and snapshots in one walk and shares structure. Every subtree that still matches keeps prev's node, so a miss copies only the changed spine (the axis limits), and a hit returns `prev` itself (`Object.is`, so NaN leaves still hit). The key is still content-based, as strict as JSON equality. In-place mutation of a caller's zero-copy Float64Array still invalidates, including after misses that shared that array's snapshot. New tests in test/layout-cache.test.ts cover that, a pan returning to an earlier view, and the snapshot semantics (key order, array length, non-plain objects by JSON, typed array kind and bytes).

### Gate
`npm test` (compare 348/348 pixel-exact), test:size, test:browser, test:workers, test:interactive: green.

### Browser re-render bench (headless Chrome 156, 5 charts × 240 panned frames × 3 loads; harness in the lab note)
Base 4e0add6 vs this branch 3846f96, run twice in opposite orders. p50 ms is the median over 3 loads:

| chart | lib-only SVG (hot) p50 | full SVG frame p50 | lib-only raster (hot) p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| counts | 0.32 → 0.25 (−22 %, −23 %) | 0.81 → 0.73 (−9 %, −11 %) | 1.52 → 1.42 (−7 %, −8 %) |
| latency | 0.28 → 0.23 (−16 %, −16 %) | 1.12 → 1.07 (−4 %, −4 %) | 1.19 → 1.18 (−2 %, 0 %) |
| quickstart | 0.23 → 0.21 (−11 %, −9 %) | 0.56 → 0.53 (−7 %, −5 %) | 1.65 → 1.62 (−2 %, −2 %) |
| scatter_cbar | 6.45 → 5.98 (−7 %, −7 %) | 18.5 → 17.8 (−4 %, −4 %) | 8.35 → 7.88 (−6 %, −4 %) |

author: alexis-marcel
body:
## Summary
Step 1b of #244 (#243 step 2). The Home Assistant voice becomes a channel both ways, on its own connection and its own token. Stacked on #245.

- **Out**: eriphe-core no longer calls Home Assistant to speak, and never with the HA tool's token. The Eriphe integration holds the voice token, keeps `GET /v1/voice/announce?wait=50` open, and says each sentence itself (`assist_satellite.announce`, or `tts.speak` on a media player).
- **In**: the voice guarantees only that someone is in the room. A sentence said to it taints its turn (`voix`): the brain reads and answers freely, but a write goes on a card. A card is never answered aloud. The voice says « Je te l'ai mis à confirmer sur ton téléphone. », and a notice in the code's words goes to the phone. This closes #243's open question.

## Changes
- `core/voice_out.go` (new): the announcement queue (10 at most, dropped after 1 min), the long poll, `voiceSpot` (the voice line only while the integration has listened within 2 min) and `announce`, which now only queues.
- `core/channels.go`: each outbound channel has `reach` (one routed target). `route_send.go`'s `reach` dispatches by the channel of the line, so the voice is no longer a special case there. `viaChannel` and `isUser` tell a message's channel from its `via`.
- `core/voice.go`: a voice sentence is tainted. The spoken card question is replaced by `voiceCardConfirm` and a phone notice (`voiceCardNote`).
- `core/convo_cards.go`: `resolveByText` takes a yes or no only from a channel that guarantees it is the user.
- `core/ha_presence.go`, `core/ha_client.go`: the old `announce` and `haCall` are gone. Presence still uses `haLink` until #244 step 4.
- `ha/`: `EripheClient.async_announcements`, `service_call` (only `assist_satellite.*` and `media_player.*`, nothing else whatever the core sends), and a background loop with retries (5 s growing to 5 min; once an hour for an older core).
- The brain prompt (French), `core/README.md`, `ha/README.md`, and the card hint (fr and en).

## Tests
- `cd core && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: all pass. New: `voice_out_test.go` (token, long poll, at once and once, expiry, cap, the listening gate), `TestVoiceCardConfirm` (a spoken « oui » does not decide; the notice has no card text), `TestViaChannel`, a taint check in `TestVoiceReply`, and `TestHAVoice` (queued, no call to HA).
- `python3 -m pytest ha/tests`: 21 passed (client, malformed items left out, 401 and 404, `service_call` refuses `light.*`, `lock.*` and the like).
- `pytest ha/tests_ha` on Home Assistant 2026.10.4 (Python 3.14): 8 passed, including `test_speaks_on_the_speakers`. CI does not run these; they ran locally.

## Notes
- **Deployment**: speakers stay silent until the Eriphe integration is updated in Home Assistant. Until then the router skips the voice line, because the integration is not listening.
- **Behaviour change**: a « oui » said aloud no longer approves a card, and any write asked aloud goes on a card.

Part of #243.

author: adolanium
body:
Hermes Desktop reads a package's name from a `name:` line at the start of a line in `plugin.yaml` (`detectPluginComponents` in `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-plugin-install.ts`). `scripts/build_catalog.py` wrote `catalog/plugin.yaml` as JSON, which has no such line. A Desktop catalog install therefore fell back to the folder name and put the desktop half in `desktop-plugins/catalog`. The agent side parses the YAML and uses the package name, so the two halves disagreed. Every plugin packaged this way also collided in the same `desktop-plugins/catalog` folder, so installing a second one failed with `Desktop plugin 'catalog' already exists`. Adolanium/hermes-office#1 reported it, and Adolanium/hermes-office#2 fixed it there.

The build now writes block YAML with JSON scalars (`name: "..."`), still without a YAML library. It also refuses to write a manifest whose name Desktop wouldn't read, so the existing `build_catalog.py --check` CI step guards this. The manifest's fields and values are unchanged.

Tests:

- Desktop's name pattern finds no name in the manifest on the default branch and reads the package name from the regenerated one.
- `build_catalog.py --check`, the catalog policy tests (where the repo has them), `py_compile` and `node --check` pass.
- `hermes plugins validate` passes on the regenerated `catalog/` tree.

`plugin.js` is unchanged, so I didn't rerun the feature test suites. I didn't run a catalog install in Hermes Desktop.

author: alarion239
body:
Re-applies #1305 on integration 5195c444 (a revert of the revert), plus a product fix for the in-frame GPU allocations that made steps_glide_cost_cmd red (Gate 42480334207, n=9).

**Cause.** The idle job (svRingNext) made the outer ring's sizes, and built their polar meshes, only for the two glides next to the plane the thread is at. A scrub crosses every glide. A polar ring size not made when the scrub reached its glide was made in the frame (svRingFor), and its mesh, skip flags and carry textures were created there (svRingGPU<svPolarGPU, svSkipSet, carryPrep). Whether a frame takes the carried-mesh path (which needs the ring) or the inverse pass (svExactGlide, which does not) depends on whether the inverse program has linked, which is timing; so the defect showed only on some runs. It is not LRU eviction: a suite log shows two polar meshes built, both by the idle job, never more than one resident.

**Fix.** svRingNext goes on to the other glides of the chain after the two next to the thread, while svPolarRes has room, so no mesh made for a far glide drops one next to the thread. The zero-allocation assertions are unchanged.

**Red first.** New check in steps_glide_cost_cmd (hook `__cmwSvRingMade`): with the idle job ended, the ring sizes of every glide are made. On this head without the fix: FAIL `{"made":21,"left":21,"glides":2}`. With the fix: the whole suite passes (260 s).

**mask_carry restored.** The revert brings back test/steps_glide_mask_carry_cmd.js, its ci/suite_views.js entry and its ci/browser_shards.js views-2 entry.

**Not covered.** Two CPU burners trip a ring slice-budget timing check in the ring section (unrelated assertion; not chased).

author: ivansentient
body:
## Summary

Paste an Instagram link (or slide screenshots), pick one of our pages, and Engine rebuilds the post as an editable 3:4 carousel in that page's template, language and voice. A team of agents does the work, each with its own role card, and a person approves the plan and picks the hook at a checkpoint (or autopilot does it).

## What's in it

- **Recreate post** (`lib/engine/agents/`): an editor-in-chief reads the original slide by slide. Research runs in parallel (facts with sources, the chart's real data, viral reactions from X, photos). A story editor plans the slides and the headline model writes hook options. Then a copywriter, a chart maker and an art director work in parallel, and the designer builds the deck. A fact critic and a design critic check it and send must-fix issues back, at most twice.
- **Post file**: one saved record per run, with stage outputs, timing, models and token use. Runs pause at the checkpoint and resume after a restart.
- **Charts** recreate the original's series, span and markers from FRED and the S&P 500 monthly history since 1871, aligned to the text margin.
- **Supporting charts**: the data agent can also draw up to two short charts from the same real data for reader questions a chart answers better than words (for example, openings since 2019 with the March 2022 peak and ChatGPT's launch), so question slides about numbers don't end up with an empty photo slot.
- **Slide renderer**: `renderSlides` renders pages headlessly exactly as Export does, for the design critic and previews. It uses `ENGINE_CHROMIUM_PATH`, else Playwright's Chromium, else an installed Google Chrome.
- **Reaction pages**: one, two or three real posts from X per page, drawn like phone screenshots of the X app:
  - the profile photo, with the right check mark per account;
  - the post word for word with X's own line breaks;
  - the post's photo, or a video's poster frame with X's play button and its length (0:45), or "GIF";
  - rounded corners, a thin grey border and padding inside the card;
  - no source line, because the cards show whose posts they are.
- **Posts from X by link**: paste links to posts on X when you start a run, or add one at the checkpoint. Engine reads them from X's public embed data (no Apify plan needed), puts them on the reaction slides first, and nothing reruns. Agents do the same through `engine_recreate_add_posts`.
- **Headline model client** for hook options and real picks. Picks are saved only for human choices, never in autopilot. Credit, source and link lines the model sometimes sends back are dropped, and the copywriter tops the options back up to five.
- **Layout and export**: smart layout for every template (not just @chatgptricks), and Export no longer doubles blank lines between paragraphs.
- **Fetching safety**: one public-address check shared by everything Engine fetches.
- **The ChatGPTricks style guide's rules** in the agents' role cards.
- Also on this branch: the developer handoff doc and the design-system files from 0c5489f.

#35 (slide content that fills the page) targets this branch.

## Before merging (merging deploys to production)

- [ ] Chromium on Render, so the design critic can render slides in production. Without it, `renderSlides` returns null and the critic falls back to geometry checks.
- [ ] Render env vars: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `HEADLINE_API_KEY` (optional), `APIFY_TOKEN`.
- [ ] Post files need cloud storage in production (Supabase `gf_client_state`). They're refused without it.
- [ ] X search needs a paid Apify plan. On the free plan, reaction search returns nothing, and Engine says so plainly. Posts added by link work either way.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and eslint are clean
- [x] `npm run test:template-editor`: 828 tests, 825 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped
- [x] The last four commits each pass tsc, eslint and the tests on their own
- [x] Rendered Reaction slides (William Baude's post with a photo; one, two and three cards) checked against X's app
- [x] Video and GIF cards rendered with sample posts
- [x] Checkpoint "Add a post from X" tried in the browser on a copy of a paused run
- [x] One full autopilot run locally (AI vs Jobs, @chatgptricks, 3 posts from X added by link): 10 slides in about 8 minutes, one critic fix round, then 0 must-fix
- [x] Supporting charts drawn offline from real FRED data on that run's question slides (the role-card change itself hasn't run with the model yet)

body:
The long-command intent assumes its main bundle is an extension exactly two directories below a-Shell. If the extension sits at a different depth, that lookup selects a directory without the app's metadata.

Find the nearest enclosing `.app`, including the main bundle itself, and include the starting bundle path in the lookup error. Command execution and the shared-container error stay unchanged.

`sh tests/long-commands-errors.sh` passes nine host checks through the production `perform()` entry point, using Foundation bundles and substitutes for platform scheduling and command execution. The fixtures cover flat `Extensions` and `PlugIns`, a wrapped iOS app, the app as main bundle, `Contents` layouts, and lookup failures. The expanded harness fails against the previous source. These checks do not identify the Discord reporter's runtime layout.

The build before this change gave the same results there: in that layout the extension sits in the app's `Extensions/` directory, two levels below the app, so the old lookup was already correct and the Simulator does not reproduce the failure. I did not run it on a physical device.
