body:
## The card

Two screens already on the PC hold unspent evidence:

- **pc-tailor-field** (`work/x5f`) fought every robot on eight levers but kept ONE lever a robot. A robot whose second-best lever also beat master there has never had that lever tried on top of the one it now carries.
- **pc-race-power** (`work/rpf`) fought every robot on race power at 2 seeds and kept the 5-point winners. The robots where rp led by 1-5 points were never fought again. That is the evidence shape pc-tailor-near turned into 28 holding picks (+0.03 APS, #706).

`pc-tailor-stack` gives both a second look in one build, ln:

- **Stack set**: every robot the table tailors (read from `ShieldTableData` at prep by the new `x5_card.py carried`, so it follows the table), on its best lever of another family that beat c by 1+ point on the x5f screen. Families: one bullet-power rule among x5, fp, rp; one stop-and-go variant among sg, sw; gs, hj, fl, mm alone; neither gs nor fl on a shield-mode robot (`--shielded panel-shield-listed-321.txt`).
- **Race set**: every other robot not among pc-race-power's 19 picks and not on a power lever, where rp beat c by 1+ point on the rpf screen.

c and ln fight them at 4 new seeds from 10400. Every fifth robot of each set is that set's pilot: a set drops when ln's mean gain over c there is under 0.3 points, and the card stops when both drop. Picks at a 2-point margin on the new seeds alone, mapped back to each robot's lever; xr confirmed against c and aa at 4 fresh seeds from 10500; gate +0.03 APS with the 95% low end above 0; results PR on `claude/pc-tailor-stack-results`.

Size: ~100-150 stacking robots plus ~300-500 race-power leaners x 2 arms x 4 seeds, about 3,500-5,000 battles (6-8 h), plus the confirm (1-2 h).

## Why it should win

- Per-opponent tailoring with no new mechanism: every lever ships and has held its own confirm; the only question is which robots get a second one. The levers work different parts (power, gun aims, stop-and-go, heat timing, flattener, mimic aims), so a second lever's gain has no reason to cancel the first's. Whether it adds is what the card measures, against c carrying the first lever.
- Race power's screen read like heat-jit's did (+0.14 ± 0.16 APS over the field at 2 seeds): a mass of small gains the 5-point margin could not keep. Here its leaners get the same 4 new seeds and 2-point pick that worked for the other levers.
- No winner's curse: lean on the old seeds, pick on new ones, confirm on fresh ones before anything ships.
- Risk: a robot keeps a lever only at a 2-point margin with the low end above 0; each set has its own pilot bar, so a dead set costs a fifth of its battles.

## Changes

- `hadur-bench/plans/pc-tailor-stack.queue`: the card (prep, pilot, screen, pick, prep2, confirm, gate, pr; every bench step with the standard stop rules; nothing ships from the card).
- `hadur-bench/tools/x5_card.py`: `rp` joins the levers (rplist / RACE_POWER); `carried` reads the table's per-robot levers; `lean` takes `--carry`, `--only-carried`, `--shielded`, `--req`.
- `TailorStackPlanTest`: the card and the helper's rules are complete before they reach the PC.
- `docs/requirements.md`: BENCH-214 (T7) and its rationale note.

Tests: hadur-core traceability (427 of 427 covered) and hadur-bench plan tests green; the plan parses in `benchqueue.py` and every step passes `bash -n`.

Nothing here changes the robot. Leigh starts the card from master when the PC is free.

author: grizzlyone95
body:
When the single-player 98/TRO toggle is set to TRO, the main-menu banner plays `odyssey.ogv` instead of `bzone.ogv`. The video is The Red Odyssey's `anims\odyssey.avi`, converted to Theora 556x72 at 15 fps, the same format as `bzone.ogv`. The mode is also kept across launches.

**How it works:** one DWORD patch and two call-site patches, all GOG-only.
- **DWORD patch (`TRO Banner Movie Name`):** the banner builder's `push "bzone.ogv"` (0x0078DEBC) now points at a shim buffer.
- **Call-site patches (`TRO Banner Mode Refresh 1/2, 2/2`):** these wrap both calls to the SP mode refresh, which is the only writer of the TRO flag 0x009455DC. The 1/2 pattern is extended back over the preceding thunk, because the old pattern matched three identical thunks and failed closed. It now matches only 0x007BEE2A.
- **Fail-closed:** each call-site patch checks that its call still reaches the resolved refresh, and otherwise leaves the call stock. A resolve miss also leaves everything stock.

**Persistence:**
- **Saving:** the mode is saved to `openshim.ini` `[General] LastSinglePlayerMode` (`TRO`/`98`).
- **Restoring:** after patching, a saved `TRO` seeds three things:
  - the TRO flag;
  - the shell music track (`TroMenuMovie::ShellMusicTrack`, 0x008E772C → 0x1B);
  - the banner name.

  The engine then re-applies TRO when the SP view is built (FUN_007bf440 line 348).
- **When it is active:** save and restore run only when both refresh sites are hooked, so a restored TRO can always be toggled off.

**TRO DLC gate:**
- **Engine behaviour:** stock creates the 98/TRO toggle only when the TRO DLC is owned (FUN_007bf440 lines 173-175: `FUN_007537a0(FUN_007647a0(1), 1)`). The new resolves `TroMenuMovie::DlcManager`/`DlcOwned` call that same test.
- **Gate at restore:** a restore is skipped when the DLC is known not to be owned. The DLC manager is created after patching (FUN_00764f50 from FUN_00618c10), so at restore time ownership is usually unknown, and the restore goes ahead.
- **Gate in the SP view:** the wrapper checks again before the stock refresh. If the TRO flag is set and ownership is not confirmed, it drops to 98 without calling the stock refresh, because without the DLC that refresh would read a toggle that was never built. The saved preference is kept. The ownership functions are resolved whatever the saved mode is, and the SP-view check runs only when they resolved. Without them no TRO restore happens, so a set flag can only come from the toggle, which exists only when the DLC is owned.

**Shipping:** `odyssey.ogv` goes out through `custom_widgets` (deploy/install/uninstall lists). `ui_tiles_consistency_tests` now ignores `$uiTiles` entries that are not `.png`.

**Live results** (GOG 2.2.301, TRO DLC owned, five launches):

| Launch | Steps | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Toggle SP to TRO | `LastSinglePlayerMode = TRO` written; main menu shows the ODYSSEY banner |
| 3 | Start with saved TRO | First menu builds `odyssey.ogv`; SP opens in TRO (Dogs of War / Red Storm, TRO intro); toggle back writes `98`; clean exit |
| 4 (final build) | Same as launch 3 | Same result; the SP-view DLC check passed (no fallback); toggling to 98 rebuilt the menu with `bzone.ogv`; clean exit |
| 5 (final build) | Start with saved `98`; in SP toggle 98 → TRO → 98 | Menu shows `bzone.ogv`; ini goes TRO, then `98`; campaigns switch both ways (Stars and Stripes ↔ Dogs of War); no fallback; clean exit |

**Limits:**
- **Restore ordering:** patching runs alongside the game thread. If the menu is already built before the restore runs, the first menu stays 98 and the shim logs a warning. Ordering is UNVERIFIED, but it did not occur in launches 3 and 4.
- **No-DLC install with a stale `TRO` ini:** the first main menu can show the ODYSSEY banner until SP is opened, which drops back to 98. This is cosmetic only, because only SP-view code reads the flag.
- **No-DLC path is untested live:** on the drop-back, the stock 98 branch's `FUN_007d3e80(0,0x1d,0)` is not called; its effect is UNVERIFIED. It was not tested on a no-DLC install.
- **TRO intro:** it plays once per launch, on the first SP entry (stock first-toggle behaviour).
- **Tests:** 185/186 local tests pass. The one failure is `steam_tunnel_runtime_test`, because port 127.0.0.2:1337 was already in use on this machine; it is unrelated to this PR.
- **Steam delivery:** Steam/Workshop-updater delivery of the new `.ogv` is unverified.
- **Asset licensing:** this commits a TRO-derived video asset to the public repo.

body:
## What it adds
- A **We'll build it for you** section on the home page (`#build`), linked from the menu, the hero and the closing call to action, with info@moonpuck.com in the footer.
- Its form fields:
  - **Email** is the only required field.
  - Name, organisation, "your site now" and a message are optional.
  - A hidden honeypot field catches robots, and the Turnstile widget sits above Send.
- `docs-site/worker.js`: the docs site's Worker now runs `POST /api/contact` (`run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]`). Everything else is still the static files.
  - It checks the Turnstile token with siteverify, then emails `CONTACT_TO` through Email Routing (the `CONTACT` send_email binding), with the visitor as Reply-To.
  - Without JavaScript the form posts and the page comes back with the outcome. With JavaScript the form is sent in place.
- The page's code sample now says `npm run core:update`.

## Set up before merging (merging deploys moonpuck.com)
1. **Turnstile:** add a widget for moonpuck.com.
   - Put its site key in the docs site's Workers Builds variables as `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, since it's read at build time.
   - Set its secret with `cd docs-site && npx wrangler secret put TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`.
2. **Email Routing on moonpuck.com:** `CONTACT_TO` (info@moonpuck.com in `wrangler.jsonc`) must be an address Email Routing will deliver to.
   - If Cloudflare refuses it because only verified destination addresses can be sent to, change `CONTACT_TO` to the verified destination.
   - The mail is sent from `CONTACT_FROM`, form@moonpuck.com.

Until these are set, the form answers "not working just now, please email info@moonpuck.com" and refuses rather than sends.

## Tested
- I ran the Worker locally with `wrangler dev`:
  - An invalid email is refused, a missing or invalid Turnstile token is refused, and the honeypot is quietly dropped.
  - Without JavaScript the form redirects back to the page with the outcome.
  - With the check skipped, both test emails came out right (headers, Reply-To, UTF-8 name and organisation, and an email-only message).
- The real siteverify call couldn't be tried: challenges.cloudflare.com is blocked from the build sandbox.
- `astro build` passes. I took screenshots on desktop and phone.

author: posio07
body:
## Qué cambia
Un módulo nuevo del núcleo v2, `core-v2/dolor.js`, sin conectar a la app (el corte lo conecta). Pasa a funciones puras lo que depende de lo que se registra durante la sesión:
- **A5, back-off válido.** Un back-off pesa 90 % o menos del top set de esa sesión. Si pesa igual o más, se guarda como serie de trabajo y la app lo avisa.
- **A6, dolor por zona** (lumbar, hombro, rodilla; escala 0 a 10). Con dolor sobre 5 la zona queda marcada y se limpia con dos sesiones distintas seguidas sin pasarse. Con 2 sesiones con dolor en 28 días, la app recomienda consultar a un profesional. Con la zona marcada, los ejercicios que exigen mucho a esa zona no llevan top set ni suben de carga, y la app propone cambiarlos por una variante más suave del mismo patrón. **Siempre pide confirmación: nunca cambia nada sola.**
- **A4, tope de hombro.** Solo con la bandera de hombro activa: máximo 2 ejercicios que exijan mucho al hombro por sesión (aviso).

Es el mismo comportamiento del motor actual (`applyPainReading`, `painProfessionalAdvice`) con **una diferencia**: la marca es por zona y no por patrón de movimiento. Eso es **DEC-034 (Propuesto)**. Mientras no lo aceptes, dos reglas del registro y el estado `implementada` de otras tres dependen de él; si lo rechazas, se revierten (el módulo no está conectado, así que no afecta a nadie hoy).

Registro: 2 reglas nuevas, E4 (`DOLOR_SESIONES_LIMPIAS_DESMARCAR`, antes un 2 escrito en el código del motor, y `MAX_HOMBRO_ALTO_POR_SESION`); el 90 % de A5 sale de la reducción que ya existe (`BACKOFF_REDUCCION_PORCENTAJE`, DEC-002). Privacidad (DEC-009): el módulo no guarda ni exporta dolor.

Documentos nuevos: `docs/decisions/DEC-034.md`, `docs/backlog/B-051.md` y sus filas en los índices. No toqué B-039 (para no chocar con los PR en paralelo).

## Plan generado
No cambia (no se toca el reparto, el catálogo ni la app): sin tabla de antes y después, sin `CACHE_VERSION`.

## Pruebas
- 14 tests nuevos (`core-v2-dolor.test.js`); 284 en total pasan.
- Mutaciones, todas detectadas: umbral con `>=`, desmarcar con 1 sesión, la misma sesión contando dos veces, ventana de 28 días exclusiva, tomar como "demanda alta" cualquier nivel, proponer una variante que ya está en la sesión, proponer una de demanda igual de alta, A4 sin bandera, propuesta sin confirmación, no corregir el back-off, A5 con `<` en vez de `<=`. Dos de esas se me habían escapado en la primera versión y agregué el test que las atrapa.
- Fidelidad: comparé la lógica con `applyPainReading` y `painProfessionalAdvice` (ventana de 28 días inclusive, dolor igual al umbral no marca, etc.).

## Revisor
Aprobado con observaciones, sin bloqueos. Resuelta: la nota de `DOLOR_SESIONES_MINIMAS` decía "patrón" y ahora "zona". Las otras dos son lo que cuento arriba (dependencia de DEC-034).

## Decisiones que necesitan al usuario
**DEC-034** (nivel 3): ¿la marca de dolor pasa de patrón a zona? Recomendado: sí. Alternativas en el DEC: seguir por patrón (A4 tendría que adivinar "dolor de hombro" desde los patrones), o no portar A6 por ahora. Lo aceptas con un comentario en este PR.

author: macmayo1993
body:
This adds a **Twist table** to the Data page (under *Cut it* on a wide screen) for the current shape. It lists every twist that closes up and what cutting the color lines gives at each one.

## The rule
A tube with **n** painted pieces (faces, arms, teeth, or the round tube's two halves) closes every 1/gcd(sym, n) of a turn. That is thirds for a triangle, quarters for a square, fifths for a pentagon, halves for the round tube and whole turns for the egg and heart. Write the twist as **p/q in lowest terms**. Then:

- each strip takes **q laps** and winds **p times** around the tube;
- there are **n / q strips**, so strips × laps = n;
- each strip is the **(q, p) torus knot**;
- any two strips are linked **p × q** times;
- turning the other way gives the mirror images, with negative windings and linking numbers.

Flat strips follow the half-turn lane swap. Odd half turns join the lanes in pairs, and the middle lane of an odd strip becomes a Möbius band. Even half turns keep every lane.

## What the page shows
- **The rule for the shape.** The round tube, egg/heart and flat strips each get their own wording.
- **The current twist, worked out.** For example: "⅔ turn = 2/3, so 3 laps, winding 2 times, 6 ÷ 3 = 2 strips, each a trefoil, each pair with linking number 6." A negative twist keeps its sign: "−⅔ turn = −2/3, … winding −2 times (the other way), … each a left-handed trefoil, the mirror image of its row, each pair with linking number −6." Twists that don't close are noted.
- **The table.** One row per closing twist, from one step up to whole turns, at least six rows. Columns are strips, laps, windings, knot and linking. The current row is marked and tapping a turn applies it. The table fits a 360 px Pixel without sideways scrolling.

## Code
- `KnotMath.twistTable()` builds each row from `describe()`, which reads the strips, laps and linking numbers off the braid. So the table doesn't depend on the formula it illustrates. The worked example's linking number also comes from the braid.
- The page code in `index.html`, its styles in `index.html` and `game.css`, and the explanation in the README and the page's "Reading the numbers" note.

## Testing
- New `test/twist-table.test.cjs` (2161 checks, added to CI). For all 20 cross-sections in the app, it checks the rule above against `describe()`, checks that no twist between the rows closes, and checks the flat-strip lane rule.
- `app-smoke.cjs`, all five variants: rows, rule, worked example, non-closing twists and the row buttons. It also checks negative twists: the hexagon at −⅔, the square at −¾ (T(3,−4)) and the round tube at −1.

author: mjharkin
body:
fetch_activity_GPS() returned [] from three places inside its per-activity loop, so a
single skip or failure discarded the detail for every activity after it in that batch:

an activity already in PARSED_ACTIVITY_ID_LIST (garmin_fetch.py:1035)
a TCX request timeout (garmin_fetch.py:1221)
any other TCX exception (garmin_fetch.py:1224)
The first one is not an error path: PARSED_ACTIVITY_ID_LIST is module-level and appended as
activities are processed, so on every re-sync within a long-running container the earlier
activities of that date are "already processed" by definition. With two activities on a day,
a third appearing later is never fetched — the loop hits an already-parsed activity before it
and returns, and every subsequent sync repeats the same order, so it stays missing until the
container restarts. The timeout and exception paths do the same to the rest of any batch whose
download fails.

-            return []
+            continue # must not abandon the remaining activities in this batch

Three lines, no change other than the batch surviving.

Two other `return []` sites are deliberately left alone: `get_daily_stats` (:284) and
`get_vo2_max` (:1468) are per-date rather than inside a loop, where an empty list is the
correct answer.

**Note for reviewers:** the first run after updating may import more than usual — activities
that previously aborted a batch are now processed. That is a one-off backfill of FIT files
that were being silently dropped, not a steady-state cost.

No schema, field, tag or type changes; InfluxDB needs nothing.

Verified behaviourally against a multi-activity date with one already-processed activity in
the batch: the remaining activities produce their `ActivityGPS`, `ActivityLap` and
`ActivitySession` rows in the same run.

author: frcjules
body:
Fixes #33

**Problem**
In CardsNX Quick Settings, turning Bluetooth off also turned Airplane mode on, and the Airplane row no longer matched the rest of the system.

**Cause**
`setBluetooth()` (`projects/cards/src/Library.cpp`) calls `btmsysDisableRadio()` on firmware 13+ so the radio goes off at once. That call seems to be what flips the system's Airplane state, while CardsNX reads Airplane from nifm.

**Fix**
- When turning Bluetooth off, read nifm's Airplane state first (new `readAirplaneMode()`, nifm only).
- If it was off and the read worked, put it back to off after `btmsysDisableRadio()`. If it was already on, or the read failed, nothing is touched.
- `flipBluetooth()` refreshes the Airplane row afterwards.
- One `[bt] off: ...` line goes to `perf.log` (only if that file already exists), so a regression is visible.
- The Wii U look only sets the setsys flag, so it is not affected.

**Tested on a Switch (FW 20.2.0, AMS)**
- Airplane off, Wi-Fi on, Bluetooth off from Quick Settings: Airplane stayed off, Wi-Fi stayed connected, also after reopening Quick Settings. Log: `airplane before=0 restore=1 after=0`.
- Bluetooth back on: the row shows on. HOME starts, Sphaira opens and closes, no crash report from the menu or daemon.
- Not tested: Airplane already on, and a real controller reconnecting.

## What and why

The owner's decision of 2026-11-08: a buyer no longer prints a gift card themselves. If they want it on paper, the store prints it and delivers it, and the buyer pays the store's own fee for that on top of the card's value. The print options (A6, A4 with cut marks, fold and glue) are for the store's staff only.

## Behaviour

- **Settings (Gift cards → Settings):** a new card, "We print and deliver cards", with an on/off switch and the store's fee for printing and delivery (0 to 1000 in the store's currency; 0 = free).
- **Shop page:** when the store prints, the buyer chooses **Digital** or **We print and deliver it · + fee**. Choosing printed asks for the delivery address and a phone number at the address. The buy button shows the total (value + fee).
- **Payment:** the card charge and the BenefitPay transfer check ask for the total. **The card is issued at its value only.** The fee is saved on the purchase at the price of the day.
- **Buyer's page:** the buyer can only save the card's picture. The page says where the printed card is going, then that it is on its way, then that it was delivered.
- **Order sheet (admin):** a paid printed order asks staff to **Print the card**, opening on the design the buyer chose. Staff then press **Printed**, then **Delivered**; each press records who and when. The sheet shows the address, the phone with a WhatsApp link, the card value, the fee and what was paid.
- An older purchase where the buyer ticked "I will print it too" prints nothing and asks the store for nothing.

- The fee is the store's income for a service, never money held on a card. `rpc_reporting_gift_cards` gives each period's `print_fees` and `print_count`, counted on the day the purchase was paid. The monthly statement and the month pack show them as their own line, outside the cards' balance and outside sales.

## The fee counts in sales (third commit, migration `20261126100000`)

The owner's decision of 2026-11-09.

- The margins check compares the products with sales less these services.

author: ibjunior
body:
## Problem

`run_sql` ran agent-written SQL as the app's own database user, inside a READ ONLY transaction. That blocked writes but not reads, so `SELECT auth_tokens, env, headers FROM mcp_server` worked. That table holds plaintext MCP OAuth tokens, stdio env vars and HTTP headers. The checkpoint tables (every conversation), `config` and `thread` were readable too. MCP tools auto-approve, so text injected into an MCP tool result could get the agent to read those secrets and send them out through another tool, with no approval card along the way.

## Fix

Postgres now decides what `run_sql` can read; there is no table filter in code.

- **Migration `0006_analytics_readonly_role.sql`** (hand-written, idempotent): creates a `cameron_analytics` role (NOLOGIN) with USAGE on `public` and SELECT on `transaction` and `category` only, then grants the app user membership in it.
- **`runReadOnlyQuery`** runs `SET LOCAL ROLE cameron_analytics` inside the existing transaction. READ ONLY, `statement_timeout`, the rollback and the row cap are unchanged.
- **Closing the `set_config` escape.** `SET ROLE` changes only the current role, and `set_config('role', 'none', true)` is `SET ROLE` as a function call, which the guard's `SET` keyword check misses. Paired with `query_to_xml('select … from mcp_server', …)`, a single SELECT read `mcp_server` on the dev database. The migration therefore revokes `EXECUTE` on `set_config` from `PUBLIC` and grants it back to the app user. It ends with a check that raises if the role can still call `set_config` or read `mcp_server`, because a `REVOKE` run by a non-owner only warns. **Migrations must run as a superuser**; all three compose stacks already do.
- **Agent-facing error:** a permission denial (`42501`) comes back as `{ error: "That table isn't available to run_sql…", availableTables, detail }`. Other DB errors keep the existing `Query failed:` shape. The tool description is unchanged.

## Tests

- `pnpm test` (459) and `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- New unit tests cover the denial mapping and confirm that other errors aren't treated as denials.
- A drift test reads `drizzle/*.sql` and checks that the role's grants match the tables `describe_finance_schema` documents, with nothing beyond `SELECT` and no whole-schema grants.
- Live on the dev DB (`mydb_dev`, 5544), through the real `runSql`:
  - A finance aggregate gives the same result as before.
  - `mcp_server`, `checkpoints`, `config`, `thread`, the `drizzle` schema and the `set_config` escape are all refused.
  - Re-running the migration SQL succeeds.
- The eval sandbox (5545) migrates cleanly and has the expected grants.
- Production was not touched. Its `migrate` image copies `drizzle/` and runs as the superuser, so it picks this up on the next `--profile full up`.

## Docs

The `run_sql`, raw-SQL boundary and `config` bullets in `AGENTS.md`, plus a "What `run_sql` can read" subsection in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

author: istvanhlc230
body:
## Scope and root cause
AIDO agents previously spent repeated 45/60/90-second turns polling expensive external acceptance. Tests also lacked a central conflict-aware parallel execution workflow. This PR contains both the existing supervised external runner and a **resource-aware parallel scheduler**, with no changes to SMC or other target projects.

## Implementation
- `external_check_runner.py`: one foreground supervised command, hard wall-time budget, bounded output, unique run ID/PID, sparse progress and result JSON; timeouts are BLOCKED with uncertain effects. Fix `_bounded_process` output tracking using `fstat` instead of the parent file cursor.
- `parallel_test_scheduler.py`: validated JSON plan; dependency DAG with cycle rejection; default max 3 workers and CPU-count-based admission heuristic; per-job and global wall timeouts; read/write/exclusive resource collision detection; explicit `isolated: true` required to run jobs without resource declarations; unknown resource use serialized; fail-fast blocks **new** jobs while allowing already running checks to finish; one atomic project-level scheduler lock; per-job progress files and one aggregate result. No agent polling.
- Regressions: `test_external_check_runner.py` and `test_parallel_test_scheduler.py` cover actual parallel overlap, conflict serialization, dependencies, failure propagation, single-owner locking, wall timeout, output limit and summary preservation.
- Install packaging and source-policy tests updated. Controller, Codex and Antigravity instructions and README updated with usage and limits.

## Verification status
- Local isolated prototype of scheduler: **7 focused behavioral tests PASS** (not revision-pinned evidence for PR head).
- **NotRun on current PR revision:** Windows full targeted tests and L3 framework regression; native agent/provider integration. Keep this PR DRAFT until revision-specific tests and required release gates pass.

## Required local commands
`python -B -m unittest framework.scripts.test_parallel_test_scheduler framework.scripts.test_external_check_runner framework.scripts.test_installer_source_policy -q`
`python -B framework/scripts/verify_framework.py --codex-hooks`
At final release: `python -B -m pytest framework/scripts -q` and `python -B framework/scripts/verify_framework.py`.

## Limitations
Resource annotations are trusted caller declarations, not automatic operating-system isolation. CPU percentage is a **worker admission heuristic**, not a live CPU cap. Scheduler allows a single instance per repository, but cannot prevent manually launched external processes from colliding. Windows descendant termination on timeout is best-effort; affected checks must be reconciled. This is local execution orchestration, never independent L3 release authority.

author: l7aromeo
body:
## What changed

The eight Windows archives in `skia-binaries-0.156.0-3f566dd7198c` hold no library: `bindings.rs`, `icudtl.dat`, `key.txt` and `tag.txt`, where the macOS archive holds `libskia.a`, `libskia-bindings.a` and six more. A download would fail on the first library skia-bindings unpacks. `skia-pack` read the libraries from the build's `output`, matching only `rustc-link-lib=static=<name>`, and on Windows skia-bindings prints them without `static=` (cargo.rs `add_static_link_lib`). The archive's libraries now come from the features, as skia-bindings' `binaries_config.rs` lists them. The build's `output` has to link them the way skia-bindings prints them: one run of consecutive lines in that order (`commit_to_cargo`), `static=` before each name except on Windows. A build whose output has no such run is refused: it links none of them, leaves one out, puts one the features do not build inside the run, or uses the other platform's form. The lines around the run are what the target links from the system, and none is packed. On musl that is expat, which fontconfig's pkg-config probe prints before the run and `link_libraries` prints again after it.

The packed line in a cell's log now lists each file the archive holds, with its size. Nothing in the run showed the empty archives: cargo hides the build script's output, and the archive's name and upload line were the same either way.

Part of #649.

## Release impact

**Reaches**

- [ ] npm package
- [ ] Rust crate
- [x] Neither: tests, CI or the repository only

Nothing in the crate reads the archives yet. After this merges, the eight Windows assets are deleted from the release and re-uploaded by a publish dispatch. The other fourteen are held, so their cells build nothing.

The eight musl archives already published stay. They were packed by the code before this PR, which took every `static=` name whose file was in `out/skia`, so they may hold Skia's own `libexpat.a` beside the built libraries. That file is never read: skia-bindings' download copies only `built_libraries`, `additional_files` and `bindings.rs` out of an archive (`copy_libs_and_additional_files`), and links expat from the consumer's own pkg-config probe, as a source build does.

**Breaking**

- [ ] Yes: working code gets a different outcome -- a value it passed is now refused or ignored,
      a value it reads back changes, or a signature or type changes
- [x] No. A pixel correction is not breaking: it goes under Fixed.

**Changelog**

- [ ] A fragment, `changelog.d/npm/<n>.md` and/or `changelog.d/crate/<n>.md` with `<n>` this PR's
      number, for each channel it reaches: one line an entry, in the terms of someone using it and
      linking the issue or this PR; a Breaking entry adds one line saying what to change
- [x] None: it reaches neither channel

## Checks

- [x] `just prepush` passes -- `just ci` but the suites and the build, which PR CI runs; the
      recipe is the authority on what that covers
- [x] New behaviour is tested, and a fix's test fails without the fix
- [ ] Every new `unwrap`/`expect` under `src/` carries a `// SAFETY:` comment
- [x] The docs and comments the change affects are updated in it, including those outside the diff
- [ ] Output that differs from Chrome is in `docs/browser-differences.md`, and explained where it
      diverges
- [ ] A new workaround for a dependency carries an `UPSTREAM:` marker
- [ ] A new platform target went into `lib/targets.json` only
- [ ] A new bundled dependency is in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`
- [x] No plans, notes or other process files are committed

`just prepush` passed on the head commit, every Skia step linking a cached set. The change is `scripts/skia-pack.mjs` and `docs/internals/packaging.md`.

The self-test's Windows fixture now writes the form skia-bindings prints there, with `user32` and `opengl32` beside the built names, and the old parser fails it. The refusal cases used to expect an empty listing, so an archive packed by mistake also failed them, on the listing compare. They now expect the listing an acceptance would make. Ten mutants each fail a case: matching only `static=`, counting every bare name, dropping either direction of the comparison, adding `skresources` twice under skottie, ignoring the patch check, leaving out `icudtl.dat`, reporting no sizes, leaving `tag.txt` and `key.txt` out of the report, and printing no file lines. 34 cases.

The third commit adds a case from this PR's first run, whose eight musl cells refused their own builds with "the build links expat, skparagraph, …, skia-bindings, expat". It holds expat before and after the run with `libexpat.a` in `out/skia`, and it packs without expat. It fails under the second commit's rule with that message. Further cases refuse a library inside the run that the features do not build, on Linux and Windows, a Linux run without `static=` and a Windows run with it. Three mutants each fail a case: matching names without their form, accepting the names anywhere rather than consecutively, and requiring every `static=` line to be skia-bindings'. One case is not caught: a library that a later skia-bindings prepends to the run, since a system library can sit there too. 37 cases.

No Windows build ran locally. This PR's own `skia-binaries.yml` run builds and packs all 22 archives and uploads none. On its first run, 42517456551, every Windows cell listed eight `.lib` files under the packed line. x86_64 base, for example, listed `skia.lib` at 25946406 bytes and `skia-bindings.lib` at 3078930. The glibc and macOS cells packed as before. On the third commit's run, 42523403791, all 22 cells packed. The musl cells listed the eight `.a` libraries without expat: x86_64 base gave `libskia.a` 28486208 bytes and `libskia-bindings.a` 699416.

author: jmformenti
body:
## Summary

Implements **decision 11**. Its doc commit from #11 is included here: merge #11 first, or close it and merge this one.

- **Chaining:** `fix-review` and `e2e` are jobs of the review's own `pull_request` run, started with `needs: review` on the new `next-stage` output of `review.yml`. A failed e2e returns `next-stage=fix-review` to a new `fix-e2e` job. Every stage shows in the PR's checks.
- **State:** a deterministic step sets the verdict labels with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so a label can never start a stage twice, and no comment ever asks to relabel by hand. The routing is in `scripts/route-review.sh`, which is pure and tested offline. The reviewer and the e2e tester lose `gh pr edit`: they only read and comment.
- **People still drive the flow:** a person who adds `pass`, `warning` or `fail` starts that stage alone, in a run of its own.
- **New guards and behaviours:**
  - A review, e2e run or fix-review that finds the PR moved on sets no label and starts nothing.
  - A `pass` on a red CI becomes `fail` + `needs-human-review`, with no fix, because that report asks for no change.
  - A CI failure unrelated to the diff is reported with `needs_human` in the structured result.
  - A re-run of e2e puts `pass` back first.
- **Fix (existed before):** after a failed e2e, fix-review applies the e2e report. It used to read only the latest review report, which said `pass`, so it had nothing to fix. The trust flow is documented in `security.md`.

## Breaking change

Callers need `needs: review` and the new `if:` on `fix-review` and `e2e`, plus the `fix-e2e` job. With an old caller the flow stops after every review. **The new caller also works with v1.3.x**, so the three consumers can be migrated before `v1` moves. See `docs/migration.md` → *To v1.4.0*.

## Testing

- `tests/run.sh`: all pass. New cases cover the routing, the single-call labelling, the caller structure, the moved-on guard, and the report fix-e2e reads.
- `shellcheck` and `actionlint` were not available locally; `self-check.yml` runs them.
- **Real cycles on `patufet-sandbox`**, with its caller on `@feat/needs-chaining` and `claude-sonnet-5-5`:
  - **PR #22** (a bug in the code): review `fail` → **fix-review in the same run** fixed and pushed → review `pass` → **e2e in the same run** `pass` → "ready for merge".
  - **PR #23** (correct code, failing e2e requirement): review `pass` → e2e `fail` (page title) → **fix-e2e in the same run** applied the e2e report and pushed → review `pass` → e2e `pass` → "ready for merge".
  - In both, every label event came from `github-actions[bot]`, none from Claude. There were no warning comments and no manual steps.
- **Not exercised live** (covered offline): a label added by a person, the moved-on guard, and a `pass` on a red CI.

## After merging

1. Migrate the three consumers' `patufet.yml` (compatible with the current `v1`).
2. Release v1.4.0 marked **Breaking** and move `v1`.
3. Point the sandbox caller back to `@v1`.

A step-by-step bridge from the 260 X3D 4.0 node types to the Babylon bodies' reader, with a program that drives it. All new files are under `x3d.webgpu/bridge/`; nothing in the older reader, body or builder files changes. See `bridge/README.md`; every batch has its own `BATCH-NN.md` with a per-node table (fixture, XSD, ours, X_ITE, gaps) and `receipts/` holds the raw results.

- `NODES.json` / `NODES.md`: the 260 concrete nodes of X3DUOM 4.0 with component, level, rank and status. Baseline from `tools/census.js` over six reader parts at b21734e: 75 of the 260 were already read.
- `tools/driver.py`: `init`, `next`, `scaffold` (field table generated from the UOM), `check`, `batch --close`, `report`.
- `tools/run-tests.js`: one test spec per node, run in our reader and in X_ITE 16.6.0 as the oracle. Event nodes run headless through the SAI; sensors, geometry, lines, points, textures, video, backgrounds and fog run in scene mode (real Babylon body, synthetic mouse and key input, the same input replayed in X_ITE; a `px` op reads the composited pixel in both engines).
- `tools/smoke.js` and the batch gate: a ROUTE chain through the bridged nodes, loaded into the real Babylon 9.32.0 WebGPU body.
- `src/kit.js`, `src/body-br.js`, `src/nodes/*.js`: the registry (with preparse and postparse hooks), pointer drag layer, key input, Anchor click, geometry composer, line and point stand-ins, texture combine and transforms, hatch overlays, two-pass materials, video, background stack and sky, local fog, PROTO expansion, and one file per node.

## Batches (reader now knows 135 of 260)
| batch | nodes |
|---|---|
| 1 | BooleanToggle, BooleanTrigger, IntegerTrigger, TimeTrigger, PositionInterpolator2D |
| 2 | NormalInterpolator, SplinePositionInterpolator, SplinePositionInterpolator2D, SplineScalarInterpolator, SquadOrientationInterpolator |
| 3 | MetadataBoolean, MetadataFloat, ScalarChaser, ScalarDamper, PositionChaser |
| 4 | PositionDamper, OrientationChaser, OrientationDamper, ColorChaser, ColorDamper |
| 5 | PositionChaser2D, PositionDamper2D, CoordinateChaser, CoordinateDamper, TexCoordChaser2D |
| 6 | TexCoordDamper2D, PlaneSensor, SphereSensor, CylinderSensor, VisibilitySensor |
| 7 | TransformSensor, KeySensor, StringSensor, LoadSensor, Anchor |
| 8 | TriangleFanSet, QuadSet, IndexedQuadSet, IndexedTriangleFanSet, IndexedTriangleStripSet |
| 9 | LineSet, TriangleSet2D, Arc2D, ArcClose2D, Circle2D |
| 10 | Polyline2D, Polypoint2D, StaticGroup, TextureCoordinateGenerator, MultiTexture |
| 11 | MultiTextureTransform, FillProperties, TwoSidedMaterial, MovieTexture, Script |
| 12 | TextureBackground, LocalFog, EaseInEaseOut, ProtoInstance, AcousticProperties |

Every node: fixture validates against x3d-4.0.xsd (xmllint, schema from x3d_mcp), test spec passes in our reader, and passes in X_ITE 16.6.0 except ColorDamper and VisibilitySensor size 0 0 0 (see below). Regression gate: pass, 13 frames in the Babylon body, no page errors, the follower nodes emit value events in it. All 61 fixtures were re-run after batch 12 (the kit gained hooks). Rig: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, SwiftShader, headless, correctness only. No real-GPU timing exists and none is claimed.

## Batch 12
- **TextureBackground**: Background and TextureBackground share one bind stack (first one bound at load; set_bind moves a node to the top; unbinding re-binds the one below; isBound and bindTime on every change), matched to X_ITE step by step (87 steps ours, 86 X_ITE). The stock Background gains isBound and bindTime. Drawn as a vertex-coloured sky and ground sphere plus six textured faces, orientations from X_ITE's cube table; sky colours, ground colours, the gradient, three faces and the four-colour top face are compared by pixel against X_ITE.
- **LocalFog**: fogs the geometry of its own group only (checked on two boxes, one inside and one outside the group; enabled, colour, range and fog type changed live). Babylon's fog is scene wide, so each mesh gets `applyFog` by scope and loads its scope's values just before drawing.
- **EaseInEaseOut**: closed-form parabola, line, parabola map; 50 steps identical in both engines.
- **ProtoInstance**: the stock reader had no PROTO support at all. ProtoDeclare and ProtoInstance (IS, fieldValue, nested instances, SFNode fields) are expanded before parsing; the instance's node answers to the PROTO's field names through the SAI. 21 steps ours, 19 X_ITE, all agree.
- **AcousticProperties**: fields held, `BR.acoustics(appearance)` hands them to a sound port; out-of-range values agree with X_ITE (not clamped).
- **CollisionSensor deferred (status blocked)**: it needs CollisionCollection, CollidableShape, RigidBody and a contact solver (ranks 227 to 239); built alone it could never fire. It will be built with them as a physics group. AcousticProperties took its place. Scaffold kept in `_deferred/`.
- **CylinderSensor test change**: re-running everything, CylinderSensor differed from X_ITE (1.47 vs 1.20 rad) on this batch and on the batch 6 commit alike: the 30 px test drag ended at the cylinder's edge, where the angle jumps by half a radian between two pointer samples. The drag is now 15 px (0.492 vs 0.485); the sensor code is unchanged.

## Security note: Script
The Script node runs ECMAScript that comes with the scene, with the page's rights. It is **off** unless the page sets `R.bridge.allowScripts = true` (a regression fixture, `_script-off`, checks that it stays inert by default). Only the test pages turn it on.

## Findings and gaps
- X_ITE 16.6.0 ColorDamper never goes inactive when the colour path crosses the hue seam. Ours stops; recorded as `xiteDisagrees` in its spec.
- X_ITE 16.6.0 keeps a VisibilitySensor with size 0 0 0 active; the 4.0 text says it never fires. Ours follows the text; recorded as `xiteDisagrees`.
- X_ITE's bindTime starts at -1, not 0, for a bindable that was never bound.
- The body's default neutral tone map turns white into 239 and desaturates a pure colour by about 15%, so pixel probes against X_ITE use tolerances of 25 to 45; the sky and cube faces bypass it (shown as authored).
- LocalFog: EXPONENTIAL and EXPONENTIAL2 use Babylon's EXP and EXP2 scaled to 1/e at half the range (softer at the end than X3D's exp(-d/(range-d))); all LocalFogs of a world share the fog law of the first active one; the range is not scaled by the parent's scale.
- TextureBackground: only ImageTexture faces; transparency lowers alpha but what shows through is the body's clear colour.
- ProtoInstance: ExternProtoDeclare is not loaded; an SFNode field connected through IS twice is copied; IS inside a nested ProtoInstance connects values only; getNodeTypeName on an instance returns its first inner node's type.
- The official x3d-4.0.xsd cannot express TransformSensor.targetObject (containerField is limited to children, proxy, rootNode, shape, skin). Its fixture leaves it out and the test sets it through the SAI.
- QuadSet and IndexedQuadSet belong to CADGeometry, which the Immersive profile does not include; their fixtures declare the component, otherwise X_ITE draws nothing.
- A shape with FillProperties filled=false and hatched=false is not drawn but still answers the pointer in X_ITE; ours does the same.
- Geometry and 2D fills are compared with X_ITE by where the pointer is over the shape (hit and miss probes) and triangle counts, not by pixels. Lines and points cannot be picked, so they are compared by segment or point count, read from X_ITE's private `getVertices()`. WebGPU draws every point one pixel.
- Generated texture coordinates, the MultiTexture combine and its per-stage transforms, TwoSidedMaterial sides and hatch overlays are checked in our body only; the camera-space texgen modes use the i

author: destacey
body:
## Summary

Since #1237, work items take their statuses from the status workflow engine. But the Azure DevOps sync still wrote Work's old status tables (`WorkStatuses`, `Workflows`, `WorkflowSchemes`, `WorkProcessSchemes`), which nothing read except the sync itself. This PR:

- removes that write path and drops the four tables;
- keeps a synced process in the engine alone: its work types, record types, workflows, scheme and workspace assignments;
- reads a process's work types from its managed scheme.

It also closes the leftovers recorded on #1238: renamed-state history, descriptions on upgrade, collision errors, the first-sync assignment, and the `work-item-status-workflows` flag.

Closes #1238

## Changes

**API and MCP (breaking)**
- `WorkProcesses_GetSchemes` (`GetWorkProcessSchemesQueryHandler`) now reads the process's managed scheme in the engine.
  - `isActive` is gone. It came from `WorkProcessScheme`, and nothing in the engine carries it.
  - `id` is now the work type's entry in the scheme.
  - A type whose source offers no state has no workflow and is not listed.
  - `workflow` is null only when the workflow its entry names can't be read.
- The endpoint description, which is also the MCP tool text, `specification.json`, `wayd-api.ts` and `WaydApiClient.g.cs` are updated.

**Sync** (`SyncExternalWorkProcessWorkflowsCommandHandler`, `AzureDevOpsInitManager`, `AzureDevOpsWorkItemSource`)
- **Removed:** `SyncExternalWorkStatusesCommand`, `SyncExternalWorkTypesCommand`, `Create/UpdateExternalWorkflowCommand`, `ExternalWorkflowBuilder`, `GetExternalWorkProcessWorkflowsQuery`, `IExternalWorkStatus` and its Azure DevOps mapping.
- **Process row only:** `Create/UpdateExternalWorkProcessCommand` keep just the `WorkProcess` row (name, description, created active).
- **Work types:** the engine sync now creates a work type Wayd doesn't have yet, at the Other level. Names are compared ignoring case, and deleted types count, because the name index is unique across them. `SyncExternalWorkProcessWorkflowsCommandValidator` validates the source's types again.
- **Item sync:** matches a work type's name ignoring case. Work keeps one type for every spelling, and history already matched without regard to case.
- **Failed process syncs:** a process whose sync fails is forgotten for the run (`AzureDevOpsWorkProcessSyncTracker.Forget`), so the next workspace on it syncs it again. Before, the run skipped it and that workspace synced its items against no work types, then cleared its full-sync mark.
- **Processes ahead of items:** a connection's first workspace in a run syncs every set-up project's active process before any items (`SyncOtherSetUpProcesses`), paused projects included. Without that, a history rebuild on a first sync after an upgrade could resolve revisions read in another workspace before that workspace's process reached the engine, and lose their work type.
- **Setup assignment:** `InitWorkspaceIntegration` assigns a new workspace its scheme right after creating it. A failure is logged, and the first sync assigns it again before any item.

**Status workflows**
- **Former names:** `WorkflowStatus.FormerNames` records the names a source renamed a status from. `WorkTypeStatuses` matches current names first, then former ones, within the type's workflow. Azure DevOps revisions report states by name, and the history sync rebuilds an item from all its revisions, so history written before a rename now keeps its status.
- **Descriptions:** `StatusWorkflow.DescribeStatus` and `WorkflowStatusDescriptionChangedEvent` (1.0) rewrite a status's description on any non-system, non-archived workflow, managed ones included. Only the sync calls it for now.
- **Collisions:** the four `SyncManaged*` commands, and the work-type insert, report a save that fails on a unique key (SQL Server 2601/2627) as a collision with another sync (`ManagedSyncCollision`). Any other save failure reports an error.

**Database**
- **Migration `Remove-Work-Status-Tables`:**
  - adds `StatusWorkflows.WorkflowStatuses.FormerNames` (JSON, default `[]`);
  - copies each non-deleted, non-blank `WorkStatus` description (trimmed, cut to 512 characters) into `Work.LegacyWorkStatusDescriptions`;
  - drops the four tables.
- **Why the descriptions table:** on an upgrade from v0.237.0 the engine holds no work item statuses when migrations run. So the descriptions are kept by name, and the sync gives each to a status of that name that has none, through the workflow so the change is recorded.
- **`EventCoverageTests`:** the set-based-write guard now covers child tables, including dependents reached through an aggregate's navigations. It flagged three shipped migrations, now allow-listed with their reasons. One of them, #914's operating-model backfill, wrote no Activity log entry; it is left as is.

**Settings and client**
- The `work-item-status-workflows` flag is retired. Status Workflows always lists work item workflows, and the seeder archives the stored flag.
- The process page's work type grid drops its Active column.

**Docs and skills**
- `work-configuration.mdx`, `status-workflows.mdx`, `settings/index.mdx`, `feature-flags.mdx`, `mcp-server.mdx` (the Work row) and the glossary.
- `llms-full.txt` and `skills/wayd-work/SKILL.md`.
- `contributing/architecture.mdx`: where a synced process lives, former names, the legacy description table, and the retry.

## Testing

Tests ran one at a time through a memory- and CPU-capped runner. The machine crashed twice when two runs overlapped.

- **.NET:**
  - `dotnet-test-projects.sh unit`: 13,509 passed, 0 failed (the Azure DevOps live tests skip without credentials).
  - `dotnet-test-projects.sh integration`: 1,026 of 1,026.
  - `Wayd.ArchitectureTests`: 161 of 161.
- **Client:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (7,885) and `npm run test:docs` (1,930). Evals: `npm test` (14).
- **New tests:**
  - **End to end, Testcontainers** (`Wayd.Work.IntegrationTests/.../SyncExternalWorkProcessWorkflowsCommandHandlerTests`): a process synced twice through the real engine commands, with items and history:
    - a state renamed at the source keeps its status for items and for history written under the old name;
    - a removed state is retired and still resolves;
    - a new work type gets a record type, a workflow and a scheme entry;
    - a new status takes its legacy description and the Activity log records it.
  - **Migration:** keeps descriptions trimmed and cut, skips deleted and blank ones, and existing statuses read `FormerNames` as empty.
  - **History:** a revision read by a since-deleted workspace still resolves.
  - **Collisions:** `ManagedSyncCollision` recognises a real SQL Server duplicate.
  - **Unit:** former names (recorded, case-only ignored, a taken-back name forgotten; resolution order), `DescribeStatus`, work-type creation and validation, the description copy, process work types from the scheme, collisions vs other save failures, retrying a failed process, syncing other processes ahead, assignment at setup, and the slimmed process commands.
- **Mutation gate:** 47 mutations across the changed behaviours, all killed.
- **Two review rounds,** two reviewers each, with all findings fixed.
- **Live run on a copy of production (wayd-prod), migrated by Aspire:**
  - **After the migration:** the four tables are gone. All 28,571 items and 185,565 history periods are identical to a snapshot taken before migrating.
  - **Full sync:** succeeded (2 workspaces, 28,573 items, 0 errors). No existing period changed; 15 were added.
  - **Differential sync:** succeeded (5 items).
  - **Afterwards:** every item matches its engine status, its expected workflow, and Azure DevOps' latest revision. Unresolved periods are unchanged (1,136), 2,885 periods keep the retired "Resolved", and no item has two open periods.
  - **Pages:** the work process page lists its 7 types with workflows. Status Workflows lists work item workflows with no flag. The retired flag is

Lane `01M6YBCH38H6JGX41PQRHJEXW3`.

Advisory proposal for the commerce role's first lane: how model compute musterd runs is priced — the resident seat on musterd-held keys (nearest), and the musterd harness and LLM nick plans (2026-11-08).

- Per token at the provider's list price plus a **published markup**; range to test 15–25%, 20% first. Arithmetic in §3: pass-through at 0% loses ~4–5% after card fees and the ~1% unpriced share.

- No price for the LLM until a cost per MTok is measured.
- BYOK stays outside budgets; unpriced calls are musterd's cost.
- §6: ADR 461 §5's price rule reads two ways against the wake ledger (~$2.30/agent-hour blend vs ~$43 on a resumed Opus worker); nick picks the reading before a page cites it.

author: mocktar2021
body:
Owners can set per-visit estimated work minutes in Dispatch and configure weekly work budgets for themselves and active crew under Team → Working hours. Blank means unknown; zero is a day off. Dispatch compares known planned work for scheduled and completed visits against the current weekday budget, shows missing estimates and overload warnings, and never claims a complete fit when estimates or budgets are missing.

Work totals exclude travel/breaks and are separate from actual visit time, historical shift records and payroll. No automatic estimates, route optimization or recurring-series edits.

A separate protected planning revision fences atomic estimate/assignment/date changes while preserving crew acknowledgements and visits. The old date/assignment API preserves estimates and rejects stale edits. Weekly settings are private, owner-scoped and versioned. Includes EN/ES mobile editor, guide/screenshots and tests.

Validation: 74 application test files; lint/TypeScript; full PG17 schema replay and real concurrent estimate/completion/availability checks; actual-component EN/ES availability, Dispatch, crew and guide browser suites. Hosted QA rollback tests passed for totals, unknown/off distinction, CAS, completed protection and notice/ack preservation. QA migration applied with unchanged notice/outbox counts and zero persisted settings. App QA deployment and production rollout pending. No physical-device or authenticated hosted-owner-browser acceptance claimed.

author: edios
body:
## Co i dlaczego
Intro z logo klatkowało, pokazywało się przy każdym wczytaniu i z opóźnieniem.

- **Bez opóźnienia:** overlay to statyczny HTML w `index.html` (`#boot-intro`), malowany od pierwszej klatki. Decyzję „grać czy nie" podejmuje `public/intro-boot.js` synchronicznie z `localStorage` (zewnętrzny plik, bo CSP zabrania inline script). Nie czeka na Ustawienia ani fonty; napis to tekst HTML (bez `getComputedTextLength`), fonty z preload.
- **Płynność:** animacja w czystym CSS (`transform`/`opacity`, `animation-delay`, `will-change`), zero pętli rAF i `setAttribute`. Całość 1,5 s (1,25 s + 0,25 s zanik). Overlay sam znika (`forwards`), nawet bez JS. Tap/klawisz pomija, reduced motion = statyczne logo ok. 0,6 s, e2e/webdriver/Effects off = brak.
- **Częstotliwość:** pierwsza wizyta, potem najwyżej raz na 7 dni (`hypercycling.intro.last`, w try/catch, bez storage = pokaż). Ustawienia → Trening: „Pokaż intro" Zawsze / Raz w tygodniu / Nigdy (PL+EN). Wybór jest w `localStorage`, nie w schemacie Ustawień, bo boot go czyta przed paintem; „Effects: off" jest tam lustrzanie zapisywany.
- Per-tick stany startowe w `intro-boot.css` są generowane z `tickVarsCss()` (test pilnuje zgodności); ticki SVG wstrzykuje plugin Vite z jednej geometrii logo.

## Pomiar (headed Edge, 1280x720, pierwsza wizyta, 3 przebiegi, build pages)
| | przed | po |
|---|---|---|
| intro widoczne po | 584–935 ms | 77–130 ms |
| klatki rAF >25 ms w oknie 3 s | 40–60 | 32–42 (z `will-change`: 25–39) |

Uwaga: sonda rAF mierzy wątek główny, a w tle startuje cała aplikacja (długie zadania 200–500 ms), więc zostają „dropped frames" niezależne od intro; ścieżki SVG mogą nie być w pełni kompozytowane. Faktyczna płynność wymaga oceny na telefonie właściciela.

## Testy
- `npm run check` zielony (typecheck, lint, vitest z pokryciem).
- e2e: projekt `pages` 143 passed / 4 skipped (Edge). Projekt `local` nie uruchomiony: w tym worktree nie zbudował się `better-sqlite3`.
- Testy: polityka częstotliwości, zgodność `intro-boot.js` z `introMode` na tych samych przypadkach, storage niedostępny, pomijanie, CSS.

Bez auto-merge, czeka na recenzję.

**Why:** a version tag or branch can point to a different commit at any time. That is how the March 2026 `trivy-action` supply-chain attack worked ([GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23)). A commit SHA can't be moved, so the workflows always run exactly the code that was reviewed. That matters here because several workflows push images to Docker Hub, publish the chart and create releases. For the tagged actions, each SHA is the commit the tag used so far points to today, so **the behaviour does not change**. The trailing comment names the exact release, so readers and Dependabot can see the version. I checked exposure: `trivy.yml` had no runs between 2026-03-18 and 2026-03-21. - **`upload-artifact@master` (`dependency-check.yml` 2×, `publish-documentation.yaml` 1×):** the action's `master` branch is a 2020 v2 commit (the default branch is now `main`), and v1–v3 were retired on 2025-01-30, so these uploads fail. I moved them to v4.6.2, like the other uploads in this repository. The artifact names in `dependency-check.yml` are unique and `publish-documentation.yaml` uploads one unnamed artifact, so v4's unique-name rule is met. - **KICS (`kics.yml`, 2 steps):** the scans used the `master` branch. I pinned the latest release, v2.1.20; every input used (`path`, `fail_on`, `disable_secrets`, `enable_comments`, `exclude_paths`, `exclude_queries`, `exclude_severities`) is supported there. - **SonarCloud (`sonar-scan-frontend.yml`):** `SonarSource/sonarcloud-github-action` is archived; its successor is `SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action`. I switched to its latest release, v8.4.1, which takes the same `projectBaseDir` and `args` inputs and the same `SONAR_TOKEN`. This workflow is currently disabled by GitHub for inactivity, so the change only takes effect when it is re-enabled. - **`setup-chrome@latest`, `auto-request-changes-action@v3`:** `latest` and `v3` are branch names that today match releases v2.2.0 and v3.0.1; I pinned those commits. - **`sig-infra` quality checks:** `sig-infra` has no release tags yet, so I pinned today's `main` HEAD. Dependabot can't update this pin; once eclipse-tractusx/sig-infra#583 is merged it can be bumped. body:
> 🤖 Opened by NikitaMGrimm's AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5), not by NikitaMGrimm personally.

## What and why

Off Linux's virtual screen, the vanilla client of `tools/test_wire_stream_parity.py` takes the pointer of the person at the computer, and their mouse and keys move its player (#12797). Now only the script plays it:

- `VanillaTickScript` has SDL drop the keyboard, mouse and text events, gives back a pointer the join took (`SDL_SetWindowRelativeMouseMode(.., false)`) and lets go of held keys (`KeyMapping.releaseAll`).
- Its grab is the `mouseGrabbed` flag and nothing more (`FlagMouse`). Vanilla's `MouseHandler.releaseMouse` warps the pointer to the window's middle on every screen the script opens (inventory, chest), focused or not.
- `Window.focused` starts true and only SDL's focus events change it, so the join's `grabMouse` warped the pointer even in a window that opened in the background. As soon as the window exists, it learns its real focus from SDL (`SDL_GetWindowFlags`, the private `Window.onFocus`).
- `Window.onResize` grabs and warps the pointer again while the flag is set, so SDL drops the window's resize events too. Its pixel-size events still come, so the frame still follows a resize.
- The harness opens the window with `SDL_WINDOW_ACTIVATE_WHEN_SHOWN=0`, so it doesn't take the focus.

On Linux's virtual screen nothing changes: no one is there, and the script's own input never went through SDL's events.

The Horizon half of the issue is #12836.

Part of #12797

## Kind

- [ ] parity: Horizon now does what vanilla 26.3 does
- [ ] bug: a crash or a breakage
- [ ] perf: faster, or less memory
- [ ] feature: something new for players (listed under New in the release notes)
- [ ] extra: Horizon-only, off by default
- [x] tooling: tools, CI, tests, harnesses
- [ ] docs

## Vanilla reference

26.3 (SDL3 through LWJGL 3.4.3): `MouseHandler.grabMouse` checks `Minecraft.isWindowActive()` (`Window.isFocused`); `MouseHandler.releaseMouse` warps without a focus check; `Window.handleEvent` sends `SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_RESIZED` to `onResize`, which grabs again while `isMouseGrabbed()`, and `SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_PIXEL_SIZE_CHANGED` to `onFramebufferResize`; `InputConstants.grabMouse` is `SDL_WarpMouseInWindow` plus `SDL_SetWindowRelativeMouseMode`. The script's grab flag is still read where vanilla reads it (`Minecraft.continueAttack`, `MouseHandler.onButton`).

## Other projects' code

none

## Self-check

**pr_ready** (`tools/pr_ready.py --quick` on vivus, against origin/main at 5f7cadfff, 4 min 25 s)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | ✅ 2 files, +95 −5 |
| Cargo.lock | ✅ unchanged |
| Public tree | ✅ |
| Python tests | ❌ 756 run, FAILED (failures=2, errors=3, skipped=3) (4 min 19 s) |
| rustfmt | ➖ no Rust change |
| clippy | ➖ no Rust change |
| tests | ➖ no crate touched |
| doc tests | ➖ no crate touched |
| content root tests | ➖ content root untouched |
| tokens.css up to date | ➖ theme untouched |
| launcher rustfmt | ➖ launcher untouched |
| launcher clippy | ➖ launcher untouched |
| launcher tests | ➖ launcher untouched |
| Parity | ➖ not run (--quick): CI's parity job picks the affected harnesses |
| Label | `skip-release` |

The Python failures are the ones on main (`tests/test_optional_release_assets.py` on Windows, `tests/test_nightly_set.py` since 99bd96551). The vanilla client runs only on Linux's virtual screen and macOS, so the wire-stream harness is CI's.

End to end on Windows 11, with the vanilla client and this script:
- A script played a person with `SendInput` (keys and mouse, only into the window while it was in front). Before, they moved the player 8.8 blocks and turned it (2.1°, 12.9°), and the join clipped and hid the pointer. After, the player moved 0.0 blocks and turned 0°, the pointer stayed free, and the script's own walk still moved it, with the window opened in front or behind.
- No simulated input: a real person used the computer through the run, and the window was resized mid-run and back. The walk finished exactly (facing and height unchanged, no sideways drift), and sampled every 10 ms, the pointer was never clipped and never landed on the window's middle.

author: ainergiz
body:
## Change

PET/CT opens in one axial pane with PET uptake over the matching CT. Layout offers the 2×2 reporting screen (CT, PET, fusion, MIP) and a follow-up screen when a compatible prior is loaded. Layouts the reader explicitly kept still take precedence. [#14](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/pull/14) preserves this default and adds a shortcut beside Fusion.

Beta 2 hashed the complete CT study during listing and then reread it to parse headers. The engine now reuses the first 8 KiB. On supported Linux filesystems a short read lease rules out existing writers before the engine trusts a settled file’s identity and change times. On APFS it reads a private copy-on-write snapshot and also checks the original around each read. An existing writable memory mapping cannot silently change returned pixels. Recently written files, tmpfs, other unsupported filesystems and failed fast-path admission use block hashes. Tests cover replacement and writes through a mapping that leave the timestamp unchanged.

Axial MPR Auto Window samples the displayed pixels. MR thumbnails share the frame cache. Ordinary pictures reuse validated headers, avoid redundant previews, and check their pixel limit before requesting a sandbox decode. The file picker can prepare the decoder while open and closes it when unused. A MIP can be paged while the acquired PET frame is visible; the selected turn survives arrival of the full volume. Undoing a requested layout restores the prior slice, window, zoom, fusion and MPR workspace.

Linux and macOS each ran seven paired desktop trials and ten warm and five cold engine pairs against beta 2. The extra Linux opening-speed check used twenty warm and ten cold pairs against the PR base. All fixtures are synthetic.

## Hosted results

| Median, beta 2 → candidate | Linux | macOS |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cold CT listing (ms) | 1,022 → 108 | 509 → 177 |
| Cold complete CT open (ms) | 3,065 → 2,411 | 2,319 → 2,336 |
| Axial MPR Auto Window (ms) | 1,074 → 41 | 725 → 75 |
| MR frame requests for eight series | 15 → 8 | 15 → 8 |
| First drawn PET/CT fusion (ms) | 374 → 316 | 286 → 235 |
| PNG after file selection (ms) | 330 → 212 | 340 → 213 |
| 100-frame MP4 (decimal MB) | 6.48 → 3.32 | 5.09 → 3.26 |

The 501 MiB CT listing read 1,000.9 → 7.8 MiB on both hosts. File opens went from 3,001 to 1,001 on Linux and 2,002 on APFS, where the count includes private snapshots. Three Auto Window commands produced the same center and width; they read zero additional study bytes on the candidate.
The harness also flushes the cache after listing to measure volume reads separately. The worst checked video frame was 38.1 dB on Linux and 40.7 dB on macOS.
Cold whole-open verdicts were faster on Linux and same on macOS under the paired timing gate.

[Paired Linux and macOS results](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957069) · [Independent Linux opening-speed check](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957047) · [Packaged viewer, browser and native verification](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957090). The desktop artifact includes screenshots of the fused and reporting layouts.


Mac MR first-draw times varied across runners. The [first attempt on the final commit](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957069/attempts/1) flagged 269 → 376 ms over seven pairs. An [independent integrated run](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42531561600) reported 281 → 246 ms. The [fresh Mac repeat at the same threshold](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957069/attempts/2) passed (314 → 239 ms; no consistent MR timing difference on that runner). #14 separately avoids creating an APFS clone for each small DICOM slice.

## Imaging correctness

- Pixels and window/level: on the synthetic axial CT the three Auto Window requests produce the same center and width as beta 2. The PET image is an overlay on its matched CT. During MIP loading, a real acquired frame is displayed until reconstruction is possible.
- Geometry and measurements: no change to registration, quantitative PET values or ROI calculations. Desktop checks exercise linked paging, a MIP lesion click and synthetic PET values. Layout undo restores slice, zoom, window and fusion.
- Decoding and export: oversized ordinary pictures are rejected before requesting pixels. Original DICOM export and patient/source identity tests still run. The MP4 test decodes all 100 frames and checks dimensions, timing, file size and sample image quality.

## State and timing

Choosing files can prepare the decoder early. A cancelled picker or a non-picture selection retires the unused decoder; an active decode is allowed to finish. Failed decoding is reported for that job, and closing the viewer closes the decoder pool. Import capabilities and pixel replies remain scoped to the engine generation. A changed source is rejected or served from its verified snapshot, and private snapshots are removed when released. The extra cache flush takes place only in the benchmark, between listing and full-volume decode in a separate trial.

## Accessibility and interface

PET/CT opens fused without a key press. The Layout toolbar button and its named English and Turkish options are reachable by keyboard; Enter/Space activates a focused button, and Escape dismisses the picker. The [Verify artifact](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957090) includes English screenshots of 1×1, 2×2 and Undo. No separate Turkish screenshot or screen recording was captured. The change follows the design guideline to use the existing Layout control and pane notice.

## Verification and review

- Candidate `b5843b8`; baseline `v0.1.0-beta.2`. CI runs `pnpm test`, `cargo test --release --locked --manifest-path native/Cargo.toml`, and `node tools/check-arrangements.cjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/petct-study" "$EVIDENCE/arrangements"` on synthetic data. The [comparison workflow](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532957069) records the exact two-build commands; the desktop comparison is `node tools/check-beta-performance.cjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/beta-desktop" 7`.
- [Hosted Windows engine, packaging and software-rendering checks](https://github.com/veacom-viewer/veacom/actions/runs/42532952444). Performance was measured on Linux and macOS. No separate Tesla T4 VM test was run.
- [x] Synthetic studies only. No patient data or service credentials in the evidence.
- [x] Reviewed the contribution policy; the repository labels its CLA a draft.
- [ ] Separate Claude review: the local reviewer is not authenticated. CodeRabbit reviewed the PR. Fixes cover picture bounds and cancellation, source integrity on APFS and Linux, the benchmark gate description, layout Undo and MIP paging. The important source contracts are documented in docs/imaging-security.md; the bot’s comment-coverage percentage is advisory.
- CI status and raw evidence are linked above. Signing, publication and release telemetry are outside this PR.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --><!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * PET/CT studies now open in a single fused pane. Choose the four-pane reading layout or PET follow-up layout from the Layout menu.
  * A previously saved PET follow-up layout opens automatically when it matches the loaded studies.
* **Improvements**
  * Image imports and previews have been updated. Reconstructed views can use image data to determine display windowing.

author: onelove999
body:
## Что ломалось

1. У подписки кончился трафик → статус `limited`, открывается грейс (`GRACE_ACCESS_MODE`, Telegram-only оверлей).
2. Пользователь делает **мгновенную смену тарифа** на тариф с бо́льшим лимитом (например, 150 → 300 ГБ при расходе 150 ГБ) и доплачивает разницу.
3. `traffic_limit_gb` поднимается, но статус остаётся `limited`.
4. `update_remnawave_user` при открытом грейсе и статусе `expired`/`limited` обновляет только карточку аккаунта (`Routine Remnawave update masks grace-owned fields`) — сквады тарифа в панель не уходят.

Итог: пользователь оплатил, в боте и в панели видит «150 из 300 ГБ», но остаётся на Telegram-only сквадах до конца грейса.

Другие пути так не ломаются: докупка трафика вызывает `reactivate_subscription`, продление/покупка и смена тарифа с выбором периода идут через `extend_subscription`, переход на суточный тариф ставит `active` явно. Мгновенная смена — единственный путь, который статус не трогает.

## Исправление

`lift_traffic_limit_after_switch` в `app/services/tariff_switch_policy.py` (там уже лежат общие правила смены тарифа для всех флоу). Снимает `limited` → `active`, если:
- новый лимит безлимитный или больше израсходованного;
- `end_date` в будущем.

Не трогает `disabled` (ставит администратор или другая политика), `expired` (её путь — покупка) и режимы учёта трафика `managed`/`migrating` (статус квоты там ведёт учёт трафика).

Вызывается перед коммитом во всех трёх флоу мгновенной смены: бот (`confirm_instant_switch`), кабинет (`switch_tariff`), Mini App (`switch_tariff_endpoint`). Дальше `update_remnawave_user` видит `active` и штатно применяет тариф, как при обычной оплате во время грейса.

`reactivate_subscription` намеренно не использован: он поднимает и `disabled`, а смена тарифа не должна снимать отключение администратором.

## Тесты

`tests/test_instant_switch_lifts_traffic_limit.py`: функция на всех ветках (есть запас / безлимит / новый лимит всё ещё исчерпан / disabled / истёкшая / naive `end_date` / managed и migrating) и проверка, что все три флоу её вызывают.

Воспроизведено на живой инсталляции (v5.2.0): после мгновенной смены тарифа в логе `Routine Remnawave update masks grace-owned fields`, подписка `limited` при расходе 150 из 300 ГБ, грейс-сессия `active`.

body:
## Change

Phase A step 0 of the [naming split plan](https://github.com/Ameyanagi/ReShiki/blob/main/docs/plans/naming-split.md): a byte-exact gate for moving the naming engines.

`tests/fixtures/s2n/worker_snapshot.jsonl` freezes 4,933 naming-worker requests and their exact response bytes. They come from the 1,650 distinct SMILES in the full bakeoff, openclatura and rules corpora, plus three SMILES and one name from the unit tests that populate otherwise-empty response fields (neutral-parent verification, unknown-configuration units, atropisomer axes):

| Request                                          | Count |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----: |
| Generate, IUPAC                                  | 1,653 |
| Generate, Boughton                               |     1 |
| Verify (generated, alternative and parent names) | 1,658 |
| Parse (strict)                                   | 1,621 |

`naming::s2n_harness::worker_snapshot::s2n_worker_snapshot` replays each request through `worker::respond` with the app's own request builders and compares the response strings byte for byte. It also checks that the frozen requests still match the corpora, their order and the current protocol, and that every optional response field stays populated somewhere in the fixture. On failure it prints the difference count and the first ten expected/actual responses. `RESHIKI_UPDATE_S2N_SNAPSHOT=1` regenerates the fixture; the harness guide explains when that is legitimate. Each later step that only renames or re-versions a crate must show a diff limited to version metadata.

Test code, fixture and docs only. Naming behaviour and production code are unchanged.

## Validation

- Replay passes on macOS arm64, Arch Linux x64 (65 s) and Ubuntu arm64 (57 s) with identical bytes (rerun after the review fixes). Windows x64 is covered by CI's `windows-2022` Rust test job.
- Two independent regenerations produced byte-identical fixtures (no nondeterminism).
- A deliberate whitespace change to 11 frozen responses failed with 11 differences and ten detailed reports.
- `cargo clippy --locked --lib --tests -p reshiki -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `bun scripts/check_docs_tree.mjs` and `bun fmt --check` on the docs pass.

## Visual evidence

Nonvisual change: a test fixture and its replay test; no drawing, UI or exported output changes.

## Release-note material

None (test infrastructure).
