- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ameyanagi/ReShiki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). I have the right to submit this contribution and agree to offer my original contributions under both MIT and Apache-2.0, so recipients may choose either license (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`).
- [x] Any third-party material is identified below with its source and license, and its required notices are preserved; otherwise, no third-party material is added.

Third-party sources, if any: the snapshot inputs come from the existing s2n corpora, whose provenance (openclatura 0.4.3, MIT; PubChem names) is already recorded in `licenses/openclatura/NOTICE` and the s2n fixtures; no new third-party material.

author: krzemienski
body:
## Why
The owner's goal is zero known production defects on https://awesome.video, with every fix proven on the live site. Owner approved this design on 2026-11-08: "yes to all three, use the column". A real visitor must not get a 5xx because our own route-resolution gate is full.

## Symptom
86 page-document 5xx in 7 days, all classed `human`, none for any bot class (`traffic_hourly`). Two bursts: 2026-11-07 22:16Z (~291 shed log lines) and 2026-11-08 07:21Z (86 distinct routes in seconds). Route-meta cache hit rate 31%; pool sampled idle (active 0 / waiting 0). `human` only means "UA matched no bot regex" (`server/ops/operationalTelemetry.ts:225-232`), and the burst shape is a scraper, but a person caught in it got the same 503.

## Root cause
`acquireUncachedResolveSlot` (`server/og-middleware.ts` ~:588-609 after this change) rejects at once when 5 cold resolutions run and 32 wait. The handler's catch (~:2589-2625) answered every HTML client with the shell at status 503, including real browser navigations. Nothing in `client/src` reads the document status, so the visitor saw a working page but it counted as a page 5xx.

## Change
- **E** New `isBrowserNavigation(req)`: `Accept` includes `text/html` AND `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`. On a bounded dependency failure such a request gets the SPA shell with 200, `Cache-Control: no-store` (already stamped on every buffered document) and `noindex` (generic meta, no prerender, so it must not be indexed). Other HTML clients (bots, scripts) keep shell + 503 + `Retry-After: 1`. Non-HTML clients keep JSON 503.
- **Shed stays counted** (diff beyond og-middleware, because the code forced it): `server/index.ts` logs the "shed" line when `res.locals.shed` is set, not only at status >= 400, and adds the client class (`clientClass(ua, x-audit-run)`, class only, never the UA) and a reason (`route-gate`, `cache-cap`, `aborted`, `dependency`). `server/lib/logger.ts` `logHttpRequest` carries `class` and `reason` on shed lines. A degraded navigation sets `shed` for any bounded failure, including database-unavailable, so an outage cannot look healthy.
- `.agents/memory/og-middleware-outage-shell.md` updated to the new response shape.

## Burst walk-through (300 cold crawler requests in 5 s + 5 navigations)
Assumption: ~100 ms mean cold hold, so the gate drains ~50/s; arrivals are ~60/s.
1. First ~37 requests fill 5 active + 32 waiting; the rest are rejected at once with the gate message. There is no retry for that message, so a shed request never holds a waiter slot again.
2. A crawler rejected gets shell + 503 + `Retry-After: 1`; shed line `class=bot-* reason=route-gate`.
3. A navigation rejected gets 200, `no-store`, `noindex`, generic meta immediately; shed line `class=human reason=route-gate`. Its SPA fetches its own data through `/api/*`, which never uses the gate.
4. Shed counter stays non-zero; page 5xx for navigations goes to 0.
Not run locally: no prod-like burst was generated from this worktree. The walk-through is from the code; real proof is the rows below.

## Gates
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0
- `npx eslint server/og-middleware.ts server/index.ts server/lib/logger.ts`: 376 problems before and after (pre-existing type-strictness noise, none added)
- `npm run build` (bash, pipefail, tmux): `EXIT=0`, log `e2e-evidence/20261108T1819Z/f336-build-r2.log` (includes `lint:guards`)

## Rejected alternatives
- **A retry the gate message (dropped in review round 1):** see F1/F2 below.
- **B bigger queue (e.g. 32 to 128):** moves the failure point, adds latency FIFO behind scrapers, retains more promises (the thing F027 was built to avoid). No gate counters exist to size it.
- **C class lanes:** headless-Chrome scrapers send the same Sec-Fetch headers, so no header separates them from people. Wait until the new shed lines carry class data, then decide.
- **D longer route-meta TTL:** only reduces how often the gate fills, does nothing after a deploy or any write (whole-cache clear), and needs `public-cache-freshness` first. Pool guide favours caching, so revisit if shed lines show the cache is the limit. Citation: `audit/20261108T1819Z/research/docs.md` (pg-pool: waiter not served in `connectionTimeoutMillis` gets "timeout exceeded when trying to connect"; "make queries faster, or cache") and `research/how-336.md`.

## Prod re-verify rows (after merge and deploy)
| # | Check | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `curl -s -D- -o/dev/null -H 'Accept: text/html' -H 'Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate' https://awesome.video/` | 200 as before (unaffected path) |
| 2 | Same, plus a deliberately cold distinct route while a 40-way cold crawler walk runs | navigations 200; if shed: 200, `cache-control: no-store`, `<meta name="robots" content="noindex…">` |
| 3 | Crawler UA, no Sec-Fetch-Mode, same burst | shed ones answer 503 + `Retry-After: 1` |
| 4 | Instance logs after the burst | `shed` lines with `class=` and `reason=route-gate` |
| 5 | `/api/admin/traffic?days=1` page 5xx by class | `human` 5xx stays 0 across the burst |
| 6 | Normal browser visit to a category and a resource (chrome-devtools) | full page, correct title, no noindex |

## Review round 1
- **F1/F2 (retry A):** removed the "uncached route resolution capacity is temporarily full" clause from `isRetryableSaturationFailure` and restored its comment (function now identical to origin/main). The retry ran for every client including the no-Accept resilience probe and crawlers, added 1.25-2.0 s, let each shed request occupy a waiter slot up to 3 times, and delayed real visitors up to 2 s before the shell. E alone gives navigations the shell immediately.
- **F5 (ladder comment):** "Only crawler-facing prerender pays this latency" in `resolveRouteWithSaturationRetry` is accurate again after the revert, so it is unchanged.
- **F3 (outage visibility):** during a real DB outage a navigation is now answered 200 and logged as a WARN `shed` line with `reason=dependency` and `class=<class>`. `recordDocumentRequest` counts it as 2xx for that class, so the 5xx dashboards no longer show outages for navigations; the shed lines are the signal to watch.
- **F4:** kept as is (E, `isBrowserNavigation`, `shedReason`, index.ts and logger.ts shed logging unchanged).
- Gates re-run on 325a3316: tsc exit 0; eslint 376 problems before and after; build `EXIT=0`.

Fixes #336

author: dskilton
body:
## Summary

Refactors the existing Feedback Loop prototype without changing its teacher-led educational workflow or exposing actual learner data.

- **State Machine:** `FeedbackStateMachine.decide` is the sole policy for legal tutor/learner transitions, including required learner progress evidence and exclusive tutor closure. Pure domain logic with parametrised tests.
- **Observer:** typed `FeedbackChanged` notifications with a publisher and two subscribers: structured append-only domain events + readable timeline, and aggregate report projection. Both run **inside the write transaction** so changes commit or roll back together.
- **CQRS-style read model:** materialised `mvp_report_counters` updated by the projection observer. `/api/reports` reads counters only, retaining its response shape while avoiding full feedback table scans on every QA request. One-off rebuild/backfill handles existing synthetic demo DBs.
- Detailed design rationale, Mermaid component/flow diagram, SOLID connections, tradeoffs and release gates in `mvp/docs/design-patterns.md`.
- New tests for transition matrix, permitted/forbidden roles, tutor approvals, event/reports consistency, transactional rollback and read-model backfill.

## Important boundaries
- **Not full event sourcing or asynchronous event delivery.** Event notifications are synchronous, transactional and local to the FastAPI app.
- Prototype only; Entra ID, Teams and evidence work remain on prior draft PR #12 and require separate College IT/DPO review.
- This PR targets **the feature branch from PR #12**, which itself targets the first MVP branch in PR #9. Do not independently merge out of order.
- No AI-generated teacher feedback; student attachments and pastoral records are absent from aggregate reports.

author: imnotjarvis
body:
A design pass using the rules of the [unslop](https://github.com/heydamir/unslop) skill as a reference. By its own scale the app was already designed; its gradients, glows, emoji icons and all-caps labels went in earlier passes. So this pass keeps the palette, the type and the layout and fixes what the audit found. You approved the before/after screenshots in light, dark and minimal colors.

## Corners

There's still one radius, the corner radius setting (`AppCornerRadius`), and every shape reads it.

- A block set 8 dp inside another one now takes the radius less the gap, never under 4 dp (`nestedShape`), so the corners stay concentric. That covers a switch's selected half (loan type, one time / multiple times) and the Add income / Add expense buttons in the account and category cards. Before, they took the full radius of the block around them.
- `NivyButton` takes a `shape`.

## Labels, grey and amounts

- **Labels over amounts** are in regular weight and the secondary grey, so the amount leads. Before, they were ExtraBold black. That covers Home's income and expense cards, the two-amount rows of Accounts and the account and category cards, and the income and expense cards of Reports and the account and category pages.
- **The light theme's secondary grey** is #6B6A70, 5.1:1 on the page and 4.6:1 on cards. #939199 was 3.0:1 and 2.7:1, under the 4.5:1 text needs. It's used for captions, hints, empty states and unselected options. The dark theme's grey and minimal colors' are unchanged.
- **Amounts** put the currency code after the number everywhere. Headline numbers used to put it first ("BGN 1,314.58"), next to "-10.00 BGN" in the same screen. `BalanceRow` loses its `currencyUpfront` option, which only ever got `false` passed. The income and expense cards show "BGN", not "Bulgarian Lev".

## Copy

- **Sentence case** for 28 labels ("Add tags", "Associated account", "Create a main transaction", "Category budget", "Mark as interest"…). Three groups keep their case:
  - the CSV column names, which match the file's real headers;
  - the default category names ("Food & Drinks"), which are the user's content;
  - date and month formats ("Date/Day", "Jan, Feb…").
- **No emoji or exclamation marks:**
  - the three reminders (🏁 💸 💳);
  - the deletion warnings ("Warning!", "Final warning!");
  - the CSV import warning ("!!!⚠️ … !!!");
  - "Not intended for backup use";
  - the pie chart hint.
- **The planned payments empty text** says "Tap "Add payment"" instead of showing a ⚡.
- **No final period** on one-sentence captions, hints and empty states (11 strings). Dialog sentences keep theirs.
- **The note hint** is "Details", not "Enter any details here".

## Spacing and edges

- **The 4 dp grid:**
  - button and chip text paddings of 10 dp become 12 dp, so they're 48 dp tall, the components' default;
  - tag pills and compact rows use 8 dp;
  - icon gaps of 6 dp become 8 dp.
- **Off-grid values that stay,** because they center or align something exactly:
  - 6 dp paddings that center an icon in its circle;
  - the 22 dp nudges that align an account's icon with its amount;
  - the 14 dp touch padding in Home's menu;
  - chart strokes;
  - the + button's raise.
- **Page text at 24 dp:** Home's balance was at 20 dp, and Reports' title and balance at 32 dp.
- **Home's menu button** was placed as if it were 40 dp wide; it's 48 dp, so it sat 16 dp from the edge. It's now 24 dp from the edge, like the other screens' header buttons, and the month pill keeps its 12 dp gap.
- **Budgets:** amounts end 24 dp from the right, mirroring the names that start 24 dp from the left. That covers the budget rows and the savings goal.
- **The shared top bar** (Reports, Trends, Settings, onboarding) puts its back or close button 24 dp from the edge, like the buttons on the other side.
- **Dialogs** have one 24 dp edge for their title, labels, fields, color label and option rows. These were at 32 dp, with the controls under them at 24 dp.

`docs/conventions.md` gains a "Layout and copy" section with these rules.

## Tests

- **`ColorModeTest`:** the test that pinned the light theme's grey to #939199 now checks the rule instead: 4.5:1 on the light theme's page and cards, in default and minimal colors. The dark theme keeps #939199. Against main's palette the light-theme test fails, at 2.98:1.
- **All modules compile** without warnings. All 719 unit tests pass, and detekt, `assertModuleGraph` and the offline guard pass.
- **Screenshots** were re-recorded locally for every screenshot test, and 83 of 89 change. Local renders match CI's: the ones this PR doesn't touch came out byte-identical to main's goldens. The test job checks them against its own renders.
- **No unit or device test** relies on the changed texts or the old currency position.
- **Not covered by screenshot tests:** the home-screen widget's paddings and Home's menu panel animation, which starts from the moved button. Worth a look on a phone.

author: leynos
body:
## Summary

`compiletest_rs` 0.11.2 accepts extra compiler flags only as the single
`Config::target_rustcflags` string, and `runtest.rs::split_maybe_args` splits
that string on literal spaces. Quoting is not interpreted because no shell is
involved. `select_ui_test_flags` already preserved `--extern` and non-native
`-L` values, but `run_tests` destroyed their boundaries when it joined the
flags into one string, so an `--extern` or `-L dependency=` value under a
directory such as `dylint testing ...` reached rustc as several arguments.

This change adds a private `argfile` module to the vendored `dylint_testing`
crate. It rewrites only the arguments containing a literal space: each is
written verbatim, plus one trailing line feed, to `<n>.rsp` in a space-free
temporary directory created in the working directory, and replaced at its
original position by `@<directory>/<n>.rsp`. rustc expands a response file into
one argument per line, so the boundary survives the split. Unspaced arguments
are joined exactly as before, whitespace-only arguments stay inline so
`compiletest` still drops them, and the `-L native=` filter is untouched.
Encoding fails rather than silently changing meaning when a transported
argument contains a line feed, ends with a carriage return, or starts with `@`.
The `TempDir` owner lives until `compiletest` has run rustc.

The regression
`example::spaced_paths::compiles_example_from_spaced_dependency_paths` builds a
disposable Cargo workspace under spaced paths (`spaced dep`, `spaced
transitive`, `target dir`) and drives it through the real example-test path. It
failed at the rustc boundary before this change and now proves both dependency
artefacts are produced. The fixture build clears inherited `RUSTFLAGS`, because
`make test` compiles this crate with `-Z force-unstable-if-unmarked` and the
example, built by `compiletest` as a separate crate, would otherwise fail to
load its dependencies at `E0658`.

The vendored README and the Developer's Guide document the transport, its
restrictions, and the removal criteria.

Closes #531

## Validation

- `make check-fmt` — pass
- `make lint` — pass
- `make test` — pass (nextest 2303 passed, 6 skipped; vendored suite 29 passed)
- `cargo nextest run -p rstest_helper_should_be_fixture --features dylint-driver --test ui --profile ci` — pass (32/32)
- `make markdownlint` — pass
- `make spelling` — pass
- `coderabbit review --agent` — completed with no findings after the fix

## References

- Lody session: https://lody.ai/leynos/sessions/1f61b2ea-e45d-491f-8255-451cb39d5b92
- Supersedes the spaced-path limitation recorded in PR #528:
  https://github.com/leynos/whitaker/pull/528

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Preserve compiler argument boundaries for dependency paths containing spaces when running examples through compiletest.

New Features:
- Preserve dependency paths containing spaces when passing compiler flags through compiletest by transporting them as response-file arguments.
- Add regression coverage that compiles an example from dependency paths containing spaces.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix compilation failures caused by spaced --extern and dependency search paths being split into multiple rustc arguments.

Enhancements:
- Reject response-file arguments that cannot be transported without changing their meaning and document the transport behavior and restrictions.

Documentation:
- Document spaced-path handling, response-file restrictions, regression coverage, and required test setup.

Tests:
- Add an end-to-end vendored testing regression covering spaced direct and transitive dependency paths.

author: mistakeknot
body:
Fixes mk-bxfvc and mk-htpmr (Clavain 0.7 milestone, epic mk-47vtm).

**Merge order: merge mistakeknot/intercore#48 first, then this PR.** That PR makes `ic`'s `Acquire` create `owner.json` exclusively; this PR's bash fallback relies on that to exclude a Go holder.

## Problem
uutils mkdir 0.8.0 (uutils/coreutils#13970) can return success for a directory that already exists. Two locks relied on mkdir failing, so two callers could both hold them:
- `hooks/lib-intercore.sh` `intercore_lock` bash fallback (shares the directory + `owner.json` layout with `ic`)
- `scripts/collect-zaka.sh` per-session collector mutex

## Change
- **mk-bxfvc**: the fallback keeps the `<base>/<name>/<scope>/owner.json` layout `ic lock list/clean` reads, but ownership is decided by exclusive-creating `owner.json` (noclobber = `open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)`, a shell builtin independent of coreutils). A caller whose mkdir "succeeded" but lost the claim retries and never removes a held lock; an empty leftover directory from a failed claim is cleaned with `rmdir`. `INTERCORE_LOCK_FALLBACK_DIR` (default `/tmp/intercore/locks`) overrides the fallback base so tests stay out of the shared namespace.
- **mk-bxfvc lifecycle (review round 1)**: each acquire writes a `token` field into `owner.json` (`ic` ignores unknown fields). `intercore_unlock` removes the lock only when `owner.json` names this caller (same pid and, when this shell recorded one, the same token). `intercore_lock_clean` removes an aged lock only when its owner pid is gone, as `ic lock clean` does; it claims the owner record with an atomic rename first and removes the directory with `rmdir`, which refuses once a successor has written its own `owner.json`.
- **mk-htpmr**: the mutex is now an exclusive file create at the same `.collect.lock` path. A directory left by an older collector still blocks the new one; the new file blocks an old one. Stale locks still fail closed.

## Tests (`tests/shell/lock_exclusivity.bats`)
A `mkdir` shim on PATH reports success for any directory that already exists (worst case of the bug). Overlap is measured from O_APPEND enter/leave records plus a read-modify-write counter.

Before (origin/main code, same tests): 4 of 6 fail.
- intercore_lock stress, 6 workers x 15: 62 overlaps, 45 lost updates (real mkdir control: 0/0)
- held lock refused by second caller: fails
- collect-zaka held lock (file or dir) blocks collector: fails
- collect-zaka, 6 concurrent collectors: 3 overlaps, up to 4 inside at once

After: 6 of 6 pass, 0 overlaps and 0 lost updates in both stresses (5 repeat runs green); 1 collector completes, 5 are refused. Also green: `test_lib_sprint.bats`, `test_seam_integration.bats`, `tests/routing/zaka-collect-test.sh`, structural `test_shell_suite_safety.py` and `test_shared_state_authority.py`.

## Round 2 (review round 1 fixes)
Tests added to `lock_exclusivity.bats` (now 11): cleanup leaves an aged lock whose owner is alive and it still excludes; cleanup removes a dead owner's lock and an aged empty directory; cleanup, re-acquire, then a delayed unlock leaves the new holder's lock; same pid with another token is not removed; a lock held by another process is not removed by unlock. Against the previous commit 4 of these 5 fail (the dead-owner test passes there because the old cleanup removed everything). With the fix 11 of 11 pass (3 repeat runs), plus `test_lib_sprint.bats` and `test_seam_integration.bats` (61 tests), `tests/routing/zaka-collect-test.sh` and the two structural tests.

## Mixed Go/bash acquisition
Fixed in mistakeknot/intercore#48 (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL` for `owner.json`, `EEXIST` treated as contention, Go tests). A manual check with an `ic` built from that branch: a bash-held lock is listed by `ic lock list` and refused by `ic lock acquire`; after unlock `ic` acquires it and the bash fallback is refused. No automated test here covers the cross-tool interleaving, because the Go side lives in the other repo.

## Round 3 (review round 2 fixes)
Three races reproduced in review of round 2; each now has an interleaving test that fails at bf86dd52 and passes at the new head (all 5 new tests fail there; `lock_exclusivity.bats` is now 16 tests).

1. **Incomplete record.** `owner.json` is no longer created and then filled. The record is written whole to a unique `.pending.*` file in the lock directory and claimed with plain `ln` (link(2), never `-f`), which fails if `owner.json` exists. A reader or cleaner therefore never sees a partial record. A cleaner never removes an empty or unparsable record: it is left with a stderr note, however old. (Consequence: a lock whose record is corrupt stays stranded until someone removes it by hand; two holders is the worse outcome.)
2. **Competing cleaners.** Cleanup is kept, and serialized per lock. A cleaner publishes a `cleaner.json` claim the same way (link of a complete record), then re-reads `owner.json` under the claim and removes it only if it is byte-identical to the record it judged dead, then releases the claim. A cleaner that finds another claim backs off. (Superseded in round 4: an abandoned claim is now taken over.) The directory is now only a container: finding it already present is not contention, and publishing `owner.json` decides the lock.
3. **PID-only unlock.** `intercore_unlock` removes the lock only when pid and acquire token both match. A shell with no token recorded for that lock refuses with a message on stderr and returns 0 without touching it. Effect on releases delegated to ic: the token check covers only the bash fallback. When ic exists the release is delegated and ic keeps its own `pid:host` owner check, which does not use the token.

### Round 3 results
- `lock_exclusivity.bats`: 16 of 16, three runs in a row. Stress: overlaps=0, lost_updates=0. Collectors: completed=1 refused=5 overlaps=0.
- Same file against bf86dd52's `lib-intercore.sh`: the 5 new tests (10 to 14) fail.
- `test_lib_sprint.bats` + `test_seam_integration.bats`: 61 ok. `tests/routing/zaka-collect-test.sh`: PASS. Structural tests: 24 passed, 25 subtests.


## Round 4 (cleaner protocol aligned with intercore#48)
A cleaner that died while holding the claim left `cleaner.json` behind and wedged the lock for every later cleaner and unlock. Now matches the protocol in mistakeknot/intercore#48 (head f8f5ffd), which must merge first.

- **Claim format.** `cleaner.json` = `{pid,host,created,token}`, published exclusively with link(2); the host is `uname -n` (Go's `os.Hostname`). A client removes a claim only if its bytes are still its own.
- **Takeover.** A claim is abandoned when older than 30s, or when its host is empty or this host and its pid is dead; an unparsable claim is judged by mtime. An abandoned claim is taken over by removing exactly the bytes judged abandoned (rename aside, compare, delete or put back).
- **Revalidate before delete.** Under the claim the cleaner re-reads `owner.json` and removes it only if byte-identical to the record it judged dead.
- **Unlock** takes the same claim (up to ~2s), re-checks pid and token, and leaves the lock in place with a message if the claim stays held.
- **Ownerless directories** follow ic: a dead or >30s `.pending.*` is dropped, a live one means hands off, a claim-only directory is reclaimed only if its claim is abandoned. A pid-less or unparsable `owner.json` is still left alone.
- Fixed the comment that claimed nothing else removes the dead record.

### Round 4 results
- `lock_exclusivity.bats`: 26 of 26. Stress: overlaps=0, lost_updates=0; collectors completed=1 refused=5 overlaps=0.
- The same file against the previous head 2598f0ee's `lib-intercore.sh`: 8 of the new or changed tests fail (dead cleaner's claim, claim older than the bound, unparsable claim, claim format, own-claim-only removal, claim-only directory, unlock waiting on a live claim, unlock taking over a dead claim).
- `goal_audit.bats`, `test_lib_sprint.bats`, `test_seam_integration.bats`: 70 of 70.
- New `tests/shell/lock_cross_client.bats`

author: baartch
body:
## Summary

The memory extractor now uses provider-enforced **structured outputs** (OpenRouter-style json_schema response_format, strict mode) instead of lenient fence-stripping JSON parsing, and extraction is **refused — with no fallback —** for any model that does not report structured_outputs in its /models supported_parameters.

## Motivation

llmExtract previously stripped markdown fences and leniently parsed the model reply; whenever the model wrapped JSON in prose or fences, the parse failed and the extraction was silently dropped. Structured outputs make the extraction contract enforceable at the API level; the eligibility rule makes the failure mode visible instead of silent.

## Behavior rules (per the design doc)

- Eligibility = /models reports structured_outputs for the **effective** extractor model (configured extractor model, else the chat model under the existing fallback).
- Known-unsupported, unreported support, fetch failure, and model-absent-from-list all mean **ineligible** — no exceptions, no fallback.
- The fence-stripping/lenient-parse path is deleted; fenced JSON is now rejected as "invalid json".
- validateExtractionPayload stays as defense-in-depth (confidence range, action/category enums, update-requires-target_id, importance 1-10).
- response_format is set only by the extractor; ordinary chat completions are unchanged.
- OpenRouter-only require_parameters routing pref is sent only with response_format and only on openrouter.ai endpoints.
- Ineligible effective model → one-line footer warning ("Extractor model lacks structured outputs — extraction paused."), extraction paused until an eligible model is picked (picker lists only eligible models; /model extractor refuses ineligible IDs).

## Key changes

- internal/provider: ModelInfo.SupportsStructuredOutputs parse; CompletionRequest.ResponseFormat + wire types; buildChatCompletionsPayload extraction; isOpenRouterEndpoint.
- internal/memory: extractionSchema() (strict JSON schema generated from the existing response structs); WithStructuredOutputsEligible gate (zero LLM calls when ineligible); strict parse.
- internal/chat: Session.extractorEligible (default false) under adapterMu, applied in extractAsync.
- internal/commands: ExecContext.ListModels hook; /model extractor refuses ineligible/absent models with clear errors.
- internal/app: resolveExtractorEligibility; applySessionModelMetadata sets + returns eligibility; TUI msg wiring incl. fetch-failure paths; chat + web paths both covered.
- internal/tui: filtered extractor picker, footer warning, eligibility msg handler.
- docs/superpowers/: design doc + implementation plan.

## Testing

- Full make fmt lint test green; new unit/integration tests across provider, memory, commands, app, chat, TUI, and web flows pin every rule above (wire-level response_format + provider-prefs gating, fenced-JSON rejection, eligibility defaults/fallback-follows-chat-model, fetch-failure truthfulness, importance range, picker filtering, footer warning).
- Design + plan were implemented task-by-task with a per-task review gate plus a final whole-branch review; all findings addressed.

## Authorship disclosure

Authored by an AI agent (GLM-5.3 via OpenCode, subagent-driven workflow with independent review subagents), directed by the repository owner. Design doc: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-extractor-structured-outputs-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-extractor-structured-outputs-plan.md (both in this PR).

author: diolektor
body:
## Summary

`oxphp_http_request()` reads the query string and cookies with its own parser, and `query()`, `cookie()`, `cookies()` and `header()` answered differently from the `$_GET`, `$_COOKIE` and `$_SERVER` they mirror. The stub also promised bracket parsing that does not exist. This makes the answers agree for plain names and documents where they still differ.

## Changes

- **Repeated query names.** `query('a')` returns the last value, the one `query()` and `$_GET` hold. The lookup takes the last match instead of deduplicating during parsing, because PHP counts every occurrence against `max_input_vars` and a deduplicated list would stop at a different pair.
- **Query pairs with no name.** `?=x` is no longer listed under an empty name. It still uses up one slot of the limit, as it does in PHP.
- **Empty headers.** `header('X-Foo', 'fallback')` returns `''` for a header sent empty. It returned the default while `hasHeader()` said the header was there and `headers()` listed it.
- **Cookie splitting.** The `Cookie` header is split in the steps PHP takes for `$_COOKIE`: a pair with no name is ignored, a name with no `=` is a cookie with an empty value, and a value keeps its trailing whitespace.
- **Repeated cookies.** `cookies()` keeps the first of two cookies with one name, as `cookie()` does and as `$_COOKIE` does for a name without brackets.
- **The limit follows `max_input_vars`.** `query()` had a fixed 1000 and `cookies()` had no limit. The value is read once after `php_module_startup()`, through `PG()`, because `zend_ini_long()` would take `5K` for 5 where the engine applies 5120.
- **Bracket notation.** The stub no longer promises it. Names stay flat, so `?a[]=1` is a parameter named `a[]`, and `$_GET` is where arrays live.

## Worth checking in review

- This changes visible behaviour: code that read the first value of a repeated parameter, or relied on `$default` for an empty header, gets a different answer. All of it is in the changelog.
- With `SUPERGLOBALS_ENABLED=false` PHP does not build `$_GET`, so nothing warns when `query()` reaches the limit. The docs say so.
- `max_input_vars` is `PHP_INI_SYSTEM|PHP_INI_PERDIR`. One read at startup is enough because this SAPI activates no per-directory sections.
- Parity deliberately stops at names. Names come back as the client sent them, while PHP rewrites a space, a dot and `[` to `_`, so `Cookie: a.b=1; a_b=2` gives `$_COOKIE['a_b'] === '1'` and `cookie('a_b') === '2'`. Left as is here.
- For `a[x]=1; a[x]=2`, `$_COOKIE['a']['x']` holds the last value because PHP keeps the first only at the top level of the array, and `cookies()['a[x]']` holds the first.
- Query pairs are split only on `&`, where PHP uses `arg_separator.input`.

## Testing

Run on PHP 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 on this tree, with the same counts on both:

| Profile | Passed |
|---|---|
| `default` | 329/329 |
| `worker` | 110/110 |
| `superglobals_off` | 6/6 |
| `inputvars` (new) | 1/1 |

- `cargo fmt`, `clippy` (including `--features php` for 8.4 and 8.5) and `cargo test` pass, with 1518 tests without plugin features and 2280 with them.
- `scripts/test-php-feature.sh` passed on PHP 8.4 (2275 passed, 4 ignored) before the rebase onto current `main`. It was not rerun locally after that; the CI job runs it on this tree.
- Each condition in the two parsers was reverted on its own and turned a unit test red. Each SAPI-level change has an assertion that failed on a build without the fix.
- The PHP behaviour this relies on was read in the 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 release sources.

author: dinoderek
body:
## Objective

A session that waits after a denied permission now stalls as the **Permission** hard stop, not "outside a hard stop". This works in `engine run` and in server mode. The executor skill now treats such a denial as that stop, and runs merges as a standalone command.

Closes #164. Closes #161.

## Gates

| Lane | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `./dev test` (every required lane) | PASS | `Overall: PASS` with format, vet, lint, unit, coverage, file-length, imports, versions and docs-check all passing (local, at the head commit) |

- New or changed tests:
  - `internal/run/denial_test.go`: Decide unit tests. A denial just before, at the lead's edge of, or after the wait gives the Permission-stop text with tool, input and reason. No denial, or one older than `DenialLead`, gives the plain stall. Also covers the planner stall and the `deniedInput` quoting and truncation, and a fake-boundary run whose host status reports a denial (one comment per wait).
  - `internal/controlrun/denial_test.go`: fake-boundary test. Server mode reads the denial from the host status and posts the Permission stop once.
  - `internal/hostops/permissions_test.go`: `LastDenial` (no log, a denial last, auto-review last, unreadable log). `ReadStatus` attaches the denial only to a waiting window, and a denial survives the status reply's JSON round trip.
- Not run, with reason: none

## Rulings

Ruling (risk: med): A denial counts for a wait when it is the newest `permissions.jsonl` entry and was logged no earlier than `DenialLead` (10 min) before `waiting-since`, or at any point after it. This replaces the literal rule "newer than the wait start".
Why: the denial always comes before the wait. `waiting-since` is when the coordinator first sees the wait (`engine run` passes every 5 min), so "newer than the wait start" would never match.
If wrong: a session that worked around a denial and then waited on something else within 10 min gets a Permission-stop comment. That comment still shows the real denial. Undoing it means changing one constant in `internal/run/view.go`.

Ruling (risk: low): The host `status` op gains an optional `denial` field on waiting windows, `hostops.Denial` with `omitempty`. `run.Session` carries it.
Why: this is the host status path the run already reads, so `engine run` and the control server get the denial the same way. Older remote binaries send no field, which gives the plain stall.
If wrong: one additive JSON field to remove.

Ruling (risk: low): The optional PermissionDenied hook context was not added.
Why: the hook's deny message already points at the Permission hard stop in rulings.md, and the skill wording now makes the rule explicit.
If wrong: a follow-up adds it.

Ruling (risk: low): The operator's rulings, recorded:
- The merge guard and hook do not refuse compound merge commands (explicitly skipped).
- The durable merge fix, where the coordinator performs merges in server mode (#166 track B), is built in another session and is not duplicated here.
- #161's other asks are declined because #166 track B supersedes them: setup checking for a merge allow rule or `autoMode.allow` entry, and setting `skillOverrides` for the auto-mode-setup modal.
Decided by: operator

## Review

- Fresh reviewer: Claude Code subagent; first round `Verdict: APPROVED` with four optional findings. Findings 1, 3 and 4 were fixed in 8078e7a. Re-review of 8078e7a: `Verdict: APPROVED`. After merging main (#186, #187, #188, #189, #191, #192, #193, #197) and trimming `docs/coordinator.md` back under budget: `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on a distorted parenthetical, which was fixed. `Verdict: APPROVED` at eeb72d2.
- Declined findings: shortening `DenialLead` below 10 minutes. `engine run` passes every 5 minutes, and a session writes its wrap-up after a denial, so a shorter lead misses real cases. A mislabel costs little because the comment shows the real denial.
- Review hard: `internal/run/view.go` (`denied`, the timing rule), `internal/run/decide.go` (`waitText`, `deniedInput`), `internal/hostops/status.go` (the denial is read only for waiting windows).

## Deviations

None.

The window existed but only behind the Play button of an item's own page, so pressing a poster never showed it. This applies the rule at the card-activation seam instead of per screen.

## What now opens the window

- Film poster on a Home shelf or the Home grid.
- Film tile in a Library grid or shelf.

The press pushes the item page as before, and the page spends the arm on its landing: the same `preplay_available` predicate the hero's Play already used decides. Nothing in the path emits `ContentReq::Play`, and the window is presented over the page, so BACK closes it and the page stays.

- Hero Play, Continue Watching rows, Library in-progress tiles: they carry a resume point and mean play; a window would delay a promise they already made.

author: oyviba
body:
Agents could only print text that spor reads after the fact. This adds a `surface` tool to spor's MCP server so an agent can put something in the task's right panel while it works: a link (a preview or dashboard), a file it made, or a short note.

## What changed

**Core (`src/mcp.rs`, `src/agent.rs`)**
- `surface(kind, title, value)` takes `kind` as `link`, `file` or `note`.
  - `link` must be an `https://` URL, matching what `open_url` accepts in the desktop app.
  - `file` must be a relative path that exists in the task's folder, with no absolute paths or `..`.
  - `note` is capped at 400 characters, and titles at 80.
- Each call appends a `spor_surface` line to the run's log, the same way `report_progress` does.
- `Runs::surfaced()` reads those lines across all runs and skips undone runs. Surfacing the same kind and value again keeps its position and takes the newer title.
- The tool is added to `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`, so it needs no permission prompt.

**Desktop**
- `TaskDetail` carries a new `surfaced` list (`agents.rs`, `types.ts`).
- A new `SurfacedItems.tsx` renders the list in the Inspector, under the work card.
  - A link opens in the browser.
  - A file copies its absolute path.
  - A note shows as text.
- `mock.ts` has sample data on `dark-mode-dashboard`.

**Docs:** `docs/agents.md` mentions the new tool.

## For review
- **Permissions:** `surface` is pre-approved and writes to the run's log. It doesn't touch git or anything outside the log. Please check the validation in `surface()`, since the agent supplies both the URL and the path. Links must be https and files must stay inside the task's folder.
- **Files only copy a path.** I didn't find an existing way to jump to a file in Changes, so that is left for a follow-up.
- **Merge overlap:** `Inspector.tsx` is also being changed by another in-flight task on the right panel. My edit there is one import and one line.

## Testing
- `cargo test` passes on the core crate. It includes a new `surface_puts_items_in_the_panel` test covering ordering, dedupe and the rejected inputs, and the tool-list test now includes `surface`.
- **Not verified:** the desktop UI. `tsc` and `cargo check` in `desktop/` already fail on `main`, so I couldn't build or run it. I filtered the errors for the new code and none mention it.

<!-- fm:description -->
# FN-38: Publish report images to PR body and panel

**In one sentence**
Images a report names (`![what](x.png)`, saved in `reports/ID/`) now show in the GitHub PR body (via an `fm-evidence` branch the loop pushes) and in the panel.

**Why**
FN-37 made the report the PR description, but screenshots in it had nowhere to live without polluting the task branch.

**What changes**
- GitHub: the loop pushes the images to `ID/` on the orphan `fm-evidence` branch (git plumbing, never forced, checkout and task branch untouched) and links `…/blob/fm-evidence/ID/x.png?raw=true`; nothing is pushed if unchanged.
- Panel: `GET /evidence?p=&id=&name=` serves only bare image names in `reports/ID/` (else 404); the task view draws them.
- Guard: `git push … fm-evidence` is action `push-evidence` for agents; new pure module `fm/evidence.py`; brief says to use bare file names.

**Look here first**
- `fm/providers/github.py:155` `evidence`: the tree merge that keeps other tasks' images; the one push fm makes.
- Merged foreman-next (task-branch pushes by the loop): the provider docstring names both pushes; `make check` 182 tests.
- Off the plan: no `pr["evidence"]` hash memory; the provider compares blobs with `fm-evidence`'s tree, so it is stateless. The panel param is `p=` (the panel's convention), not `project=`. A failed image push writes the body unlinked and leaves `described` unset so it retries.

**Proof**
| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| PR body links the image; origin has `ID/x.png` equal to the file | `test_github_pushes_evidence_and_links` |
| task branch and checkout untouched | `test_evidence_leaves_task_branch_and_checkout` |
| unchanged pushes nothing the second time | `test_evidence_twice_pushes_once` (also `test_changed_image_is_pushed_again`, `test_second_task_keeps_first`) |
| missing image left as written | `test_missing_image_is_left_alone` (also no images, big image, push failure) |
| panel serves only files in `reports/ID`; escapes 404 | `test_panel_serves_evidence`, `test_panel_evidence_refuses_paths` |
| push-evidence guard action | `test_guard_push_evidence`, `test_push` |
| panel draws the image (UI) | before: `reports/FN-38/before-description.png` (raw markdown text); after: `reports/FN-38/after-description.png` (image drawn) |
| make check green | `make check: all passed` (182 tests) |

**Risk**
Private-repo images show only to signed-in viewers (`?raw=true`). Panel image rendering is shown in the screenshots below.

**Not done**

author: ermo75
body:
Fixes #16

## What does this change?

SMB saves can report success while leaving old lock contents in place. This makes the stored heartbeat timestamp become stale and can let exclusive maintenance proceed despite refresh attempts. The fix publishes a flushed temporary file with replace-enabled rename and stops lock acquisition on unreadable holders.

- Pins github.com/cloudsoda/go-smb2 at v0.0.0-20261105190815-95be04a983b8, whose Rename uses ReplaceIfExists=1. The previous client exposes no replace-enabled rename API. Connection setup is adapted to DialConn; the share URL and credential options are unchanged.
- Publishes the flushed temporary file by atomic replacement and reports rename errors. It never removes the destination first and no longer reports success just because a destination exists.
- Treats only backend.ErrNotFound as a concurrently removed repository lock. Windows may transiently deny sharing while a rename handle is open; other lock read errors must stop acquisition rather than hide a live lock.
- Adds real-SMB integration tests for overwrites of different lengths, empty data, independent sessions, failed replacement preserving the target and removing temporary files, concurrent complete reads, stale-to-current heartbeat writes, and the real five-minute refresh timer.
- Adds portable tests for unreadable and concurrently removed repository locks.
- Regenerates third-party notices (BSD and MIT dependencies) and updates the storage guide in all 14 languages. No new UI text keys or repository format changes.


Targets `develop`. Commit 22d27b823e62c57d55f0b568a09902ff6463049d contains the F04 fix, tests, dependencies, licenses and 14 translated storage guides (22 files). Separate commit fe3324f4f0034024c8090878aa3731424b1be09d enables existing CI for PRs targeting `develop`, identical to the one-line CI change in #13 and #15. No vTPM or CLI restore implementation changes are included.

## How was it tested?

The original two SMB regressions fail before the fix and pass after it. The real heartbeat updates the stored timestamp after five minutes, excludes exclusive maintenance while active, and permits it after unlock. Failed replacements are reported, not silently ignored. Concurrent reads may return explicit Windows sharing errors; successful reads saw complete old or new contents, never missing or partial files. Portable lock-read regressions fail with the original lock.go and pass with the fix. Scoped backend/repository/e2e/Hyper-V tests, scoped vet, Windows build, Linux cross-build, license check and i18n check pass.

The real-server tests are opt-in. Set `BACKUPZIT_TEST_SMB_URL` to a disposable `smb://user@server/share/test-root`, supply `BACKUPZIT_TEST_SMB_PASSWORD` securely in the test process environment, and set `BACKUPZIT_TEST_SMB_DOMAIN` if needed. Then run:

```sh
go test -count=1 -timeout 3m ./internal/backend ./internal/repo -run '^(TestSMBSave|TestSMBLockRefreshPersists|TestLockUnreadableHolder|TestLockHolderRemovedDuringRead)'
```

Set `BACKUPZIT_TEST_SMB_LONG=1` and use `-timeout 7m` to run `TestSMBLockHeartbeat` with the real five-minute interval. Tests create and clean unique subdirectories below the supplied disposable root. Without a server, SMB cases skip; portable lock-read cases still run. The successful five-minute run took approximately 308 seconds on the Windows SMB fixture.

Other scoped checks run locally:

```sh
go test -count=1 -timeout 6m ./internal/backend ./internal/repo ./internal/checker ./internal/diskimg ./internal/e2e ./internal/hyperv
go vet ./internal/backend ./internal/repo
go build ./cmd/...
go run ./tools/licenses
go run ./tools/i18n missing sr
git diff --check
```

Windows build and Linux cross-build passed. The checker package has no tests. `go run ./tools/licenses` passed and the generated third-party notices are included. The i18n check reported `0 missing`.

## Limits and review points

Windows SMB over loopback only; no NAS/Samba/WAN, >30-minute workload, real concurrent destructive prune, full suite, race detector or Linux runtime validation. Replacing the SMB client requires broader server compatibility qualification. Existing compression vulnerability findings remain outside scope; this patch is not a general security clean-up. Persistent heartbeat write failures are not redesigned here.

- [ ] `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass — full-suite CI still required; scoped checks passed locally.
- [x] New console texts are translated and the user guide is updated where behaviour changes — no new UI text keys; all 14 storage guides updated.

body:
Every "the database admits N photos; the page shows none" alert from the
logged-out live check (6 of 309 post-deploy runs, 0 of 603 scheduled runs,
2026-10-26..11-08) came from a run that started within seconds of a
production deploy. The failing screenshot (run 42506713439, 2026-11-08 09:52
PT) is the middleware's text-only shell: React never mounted. That run
straddled two frontend deploys (index-Cc7tnit2 -> index-jpV_43tr, alias
switch 09:52:38 PT).

Cause: an old entry bundle name on nuke.ag is answered by the SPA fallback
with index.html (200 text/html, 3025 B; measured for 4 old hashes), so a page
whose HTML came from the previous deployment fails its module script and
never boots. The existing chunk reload in main.tsx cannot help: it lives in
the bundle that failed to load.

Fix: a 12-line inline guard in index.html reloads once (at most once a
minute per tab) when an /assets/ module script fails to load.

Check: LIVE_SKEW=1 answers the first entry-bundle request with the app
shell, as Vercel does across a deploy; a public page that makes no data
request now fails ("the app did not start") instead of silently skipping
the photo check; a self-reload is reported as a warning.

Before (live, LIVE_SKEW=1): 12 failures; 4/4 vehicle pages no photos after
30 s. With the guard injected into the live pages under the same skew: 4/4
show photos in 3.5-8.7 s. Unskewed live check: ok both before and after.

## What was wrong

Benchmark sample `uhtr2-16058` (lean-quality-indicators `unnecessary-hypotheses`): `NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt` took the section variable `[NumberField K]` although it is a statement about a Galois extension `L/K` with `[NumberField L]`. A subfield of a number field is a number field: `K` has characteristic zero because `algebraMap K L` is injective into a characteristic-zero field, and it is finite over `ℚ` because it embeds `ℚ`-linearly into the finite-dimensional `ℚ`-space `L`.

## Evidence

The theorem now says `omit [NumberField K] in` and its proof first rebuilds `NumberField K` (`RingHom.charZero`, `Module.Finite.of_injective`) and then continues unchanged. `TauCeti.NumberTheory.NumberField.Frobenius` builds with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and so do 11 of the 15 modules that mention the theorem. No junk values.

Local `omit` plus four proof lines. The signature gains generality only; every call site (about 25) already has `NumberField K` in scope, so none changes.

Meridian Crown (Terra), Redline Claim (Rustia), Indigo Reach (Neptunia) and Kite Saddle (Wyattmattoe) become always-on first-person combat zones built around Claude of Duty's core loop. Shadowreach, Actuality and WaveMall Prime return from `spawnWorldEntities` before a city is built, so they never reach the new code.

## What's in it

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `world/warzone.js` | Cover dressing (sandbags, jersey barriers, crates, burnt hulks, containers) registered as real colliders on `city.structures`. Armored alien raiders on `aliens.js` rigs with an advance / take-cover / burst-fire state machine and a shooter-token cap. Hitscan ballistics against wall boxes, the town deck and head/body hit volumes. Tracers, sparks, dust, ichor, bullet holes, smoke over wrecks. Waves, regenerating armor, death and redeploy at the pad, ammo drops, pad resupply. |
| `world/warzone-weapon.js` | Procedural carbine and gloved hands in a separate view scene drawn over the finished frame, so the rifle can't clip into walls or terrain. ADS with red dot, recoil climb and partial recovery, spread bloom, sway, bob, sprint pose, reload animation, wall retract. |
| `world/warzone-hud.js` | DOM HUD: crosshair, hitmarkers, ammo, armor bar and vignette, damage-direction arcs, wave banner, KIA card. |

| `world/city.js` | `makeStructure` gains a 3D `rayHit`. |
| `src/walk.js` | Spawns and tears down the warzone with the city. Forces first person on foot in a warzone, applies recoil, ADS FOV, ADS look slowdown and combat move speed. Redeploys at the pad. `walkPostRender` hook. |
| `src/input.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/walkLazy.js`, `src/controls.js` | LMB fire, RMB aim, R reload (screen recording is gated off in warzones only). Combat key hints in the on-foot panel. |

author: sehtej-coderabbit
body:
## Summary

Moves the CodeRabbit configuration from `.coderabbit.yaml` to `.coderabbit.config.ts` so that it can depend on the pull request author, and uses that to stop CodeRabbit from blocking core contributors' pull requests.

For a pull request whose author is a member of the SPACE core-contributor GitHub team (`CORE_CONTRIBUTOR_TEAMS` in the file), `reviews.auto_approvals.enabled` is `false`: CodeRabbit still reviews and comments, but it neither submits a "changes requested" review nor approves automatically, so a person decides. For every other author the value stays `true`, as it is today: CodeRabbit requests changes on actionable findings and approves once they are resolved. `auto_approvals.enabled` is the only switch CodeRabbit has for the request-changes review (the older `request_changes_workflow` key is an alias of it), and the team overrides under `auto_approvals.overrides` only withhold approval, so the team check has to happen in the configuration itself, which a YAML file cannot do. When CodeRabbit cannot resolve the author's teams, or when there is no pull request (an issue event or a chat command), the author is treated as not a core contributor and the workflow stays on; a request-changes review posted during such a lapse stays until a maintainer dismisses it.

Every other setting, string, and comment is carried over unchanged. The YAML `|` blocks are written with a small `text` template tag that reproduces their exact value, and the `&test_instructions` anchor becomes a shared constant. CodeRabbit evaluates the file itself, so nothing is added to any `package.json`; the `@coderabbitai/config` import only supplies types.

`ci/scripts/lib/rust-isolated-crates.sh` lists the configuration file among the root files the isolated-crates lint knows it never reads; the entry follows the rename, so a change to the file keeps linting only the affected crates instead of every crate.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` (strict) on `.coderabbit.config.ts` with `@coderabbitai/config@1.2.0` installed passes. The SDK's strict schema type rejects unknown keys and invalid enum values.
- The factory was evaluated with Node under eleven synthetic contexts: author in the core team (three spellings and team combinations), author in another team only, author in a team with a similar slug, resolved with no teams, lookups reporting `unavailable`, `unsupported`, and `stale`, no pull request, and a local CLI invocation. In every case the result deep-equals the object `js-yaml` parses from the deleted `.coderabbit.yaml` (132 keys, byte-for-byte string equality), except `reviews.auto_approvals.enabled`, which is `false` only for the core-team cases. Every result also validates against `https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json`.
- `coderabbit review --uncommitted` ran on this change (the CLI evaluates the TypeScript configuration too).
- Not validated: the team slug. `CORE_CONTRIBUTOR_TEAMS` names `perplexityai/space`, which the author cannot see from outside the organization; a maintainer should confirm it and that the team is visible to the CodeRabbit GitHub App. Also not validated: the live team lookup. `@coderabbitai configuration` on this pull request shows the resolved values, and its author is not on the team, so it shows `auto_approvals.enabled: true`; a core contributor's pull request after merge shows `false`.

## Severity and risk

Severity: does not apply.

Risk: pull requests from core contributors no longer receive CodeRabbit's approval either, since the same switch controls both; branch rules that counted on that approval need a person instead. Request-changes reviews CodeRabbit already submitted on open pull requests stay until dismissed. If the team slug is wrong or the team is not visible to the CodeRabbit GitHub App, every author is treated as a non-member and behavior is unchanged from today. If CodeRabbit fails to evaluate the file, it reports the error on the pull request and reviews fall back to the web settings until fixed. Roll back by reverting this commit; `.coderabbit.yaml` takes precedence over the TypeScript file as soon as it exists again.

AI assistance: Claude Code drafted the TypeScript file from the YAML, the validation harness, and this description.

author: maxghenis
body:
Under [8 CCR 1403-1 section 3.124](https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=12658&fileName=8%20CCR%201403-1#page=79), a Colorado county charges each household one monthly parent fee, which it sets from gross countable income, household size and the number of children in care. Main charges that fee once for each eligible child and weights each charge by the child's hours of care a day, so a child with no recorded hours adds nothing. Populace US 2024 records no hours, so on main no Colorado family pays a fee.

With this PR, the model applies the section 3.124 fee formula:

- 1% of gross countable income plus 14% of income above the federal poverty guideline (3.124(P)(1) and (2)), with the guideline Colorado sets each October 1 under 3.111(H)(2) and (3);
- $15 for each child in care after the first when income exceeds the guideline (3.124(P)(3));
- the fee in whole dollars, with the model dropping the cents after each step as the parent fee tool from the Colorado Department of Early Childhood (CDEC) does (3.124(A));
- 55% of the fee when every child in care receives part-time care (3.124(U) and (W));
- 20% off when a provider for any child in care rates in the top three quality levels (3.124(H));
- no fee without income (3.124(I)(7));
- the marginal rates of 3.124(Q), with no $15 add-on, from August 1, 2028.

## Schedules

The model picks the 3.130(C) care unit from hours a day: 0.55 through 5 hours, 1 through 12, 1.55 through 17 and 2 through 24. When a family reports only weekly hours, the model spreads them over the child's days of care in a week. It takes the larger of days a week and attending days a month x 12 / 52, or five weekdays without either. It counts days of care a month as the larger of days a week x 52 / 12 and attending days a month.

The model counts a child as in part-time care below 13 units a month, or at up to 5 hours a day for a child in school aged 6 or older (3.124(W)). A child of that age with only an after-school expense and no recorded hours or days also counts as in part-time care, since that care fills part of a school day. Without recorded hours the model reads a full-time day, and without recorded days a five-day week (21.67 days), so a household with no schedule otherwise pays the full-time fee.

The model counts an eligible child as in care when the child has recorded hours or days of care, or child care or after-school expenses.

## Impact

We ran this code and main (`040fe5686c`) on Populace US 2024, and we estimate that Colorado's child care subsidies for 2026 fall by $66.8 million, from $270.7 million to $203.9 million. Populace records one child care bill for each SPM unit, with no schedule or provider rating, so every household in the run pays the full-time fee with no quality discount. The model splits each bill across the unit's children, so every eligible child in a paying family counts as in care. Each child after the first adds $15 when income exceeds the guideline.

The subsidy falls for all 19 Colorado records that receive one, and 11 of them reach zero. We estimate that SPM units receiving a subsidy fall from about 31,400 to about 18,800. Three records make up 91% of that starting weight.

We estimate that families claim $6.1 million more in federal child and dependent care credits and receive $0.8 million more in SNAP, since the credit and SNAP's dependent care deduction both rise with what families pay for care themselves. We also estimate that household net income falls by $59.9 million and that the national SPM poverty rate holds at 14.52%. No other state changes.

## Readings

PolicyEngine reads 3.124(P)(2) to charge 1% of all gross countable income plus 14% of income above the guideline, as CDEC's [Above 100% FPG Parent Fee Tool](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HtPiC2qxclzWfBa7LRo2Uohrg-RCBkyZ/view) computes it. CDEC's [At 100% FPG tool](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EEc3z8Iwu_KRTlBtd2NssDDEx_FITqVq/view) computes 1% of the guideline instead for incomes above it. For example, a family of 3 with $40,000 a year and 2 children in full-time care owes $192 under that formula on the January 2026 guideline and $204 under the Above 100% formula. `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` records the difference as `us-co:ccap-parent-fee-income-share`.

The model also reads:

- "all children in a household" in 3.124(U) as the children in care, as CDEC's tool asks for the number of children requesting care.
- the 3.124(Q) table, which skips from 100% to 101% FPL, from 130% to 131% and from 160% to 161%, to start each rate on the first dollar above 100%, 130% and 160% of the guideline.
- a child in school aged 6 or older as in grades 1 to 12 under 3.124(W), since the model has no grade input.
- gross countable income below zero as no income.
- each new guideline and fee table as reaching every household on its first day. Counties update a fee at the next redetermination (3.124(R) and (T)), and the model has no redetermination dates. For example, a family of 3 with $60,000 a year and 2 children in full-time care owes $454 in September 2026 and $446 in October 2026.
- monthly income and the guideline in cents, as 3.111(H) lists the guideline. For example, a family of 3 with $23,999.64 a year owes $19 in January 2026, since 1% of $1,999.97 comes to $19.9997. CDEC's tools keep annual amounts unrounded, so the fee can differ by $1. For example, a family of 2 with $21,340 a year in January 2026 owes $19 here and $20 under the tool's formula.

## Tests

- YAML cases for each variable. The fee cases match the formula in CDEC's Above 100% FPG tool where they overlap. For example, the formula gives a family of 3 with $40,000 a year and 2 children in full-time care $204 on the January 2026 guideline and $196 on the October 2026 guideline, which CDEC's published tool uses.
- `test_co_ccap_parent_fee_properties.py` checks four invariants with Hypothesis, on generated households:
  1. The fee never falls below zero and always comes to whole dollars.
  2. Through July 2028, at a given income and household size, each child in full-time care after the first adds $15 at a provider below quality level 3 when income exceeds the guideline, and nothing when it doesn't.
  3. At a provider below quality level 3, the fee falls to 55% of the full-time fee, without cents, when every child in care receives part-time care, and stays at the full-time fee when any child in care receives full-time care.
  4. A provider in the top three quality levels for any child in care cuts the fee by 20%, without cents. A lower rating, or a rating for a child outside care, changes nothing.

  A differential test compares the model with a reference written from the rule in exact decimal arithmetic, in January and October 2026 and in July and August 2028, on incomes in whole dollars and in cents. The reference uses the model's schedule defaults and, for 2028, its projected guideline.
- The new Python file adds about 29 seconds to the 28-minute Rest Python shard 4 on Linux CI, whose log reports no peak memory. On a loaded Mac it took 43 seconds and peaked at 1.5 GB, against 23 seconds and 1.2 GB to import the model and build one simulation. It checks generated households across income cents and schedules, which fixed YAML cases can't enumerate.

## Overlap with #10723

#10723 adds the same 3.130(C) units (`rates/care_unit.yaml`) and day count (`co_ccap_care_days_per_month`) for the rate cap, and caps the fee at the reimbursement rate under 3.124(L). Once both merge, we keep `rates/care_unit.yaml` and delete `parent_fee/part_time/full_time_equivalent_units.yaml`. `co_ccap_full_time_equivalent_units` then reads `co_ccap_care_unit` x `co_ccap_care_days_per_month`, `co_ccap_care_unit` reads `co_ccap_care_hours_per_day`, and `co_ccap_child_in_part_time_care` tests `co_ccap_care_unit` below 1. Both PRs edit `court_supervision.yaml` case 5: with #10723's $837.42 reimbursement and this PR's $128 fee, the subsidy comes to $709.42.

author: perber
body:
Part of the SEO series for #1292, follow-up to #1789 (split for size). Bounds what one `RenderHTML` call may cost before the crawler-body contributor exposes it to anonymous requests.

Any client can claim to be a crawler. Without limits a 14 KB GFM table allocated over a gigabyte (n² cells) and a 256 KB paragraph of `[a](` took 98 s.

## What's in it
- `internal/render/limits.go`: a linear pre-pass with goldmark's block parser alone, then budgets per page and per inline container (table cells, delimiter runs incl. backticks, container size, emphasis, blocks, nesting, link definitions, a page-wide `<` budget for x/net/html's text merging, 4 MB output). Past a limit `RenderHTML` returns `ErrTooComplex`.
- `balanceHTML` fails closed: the parsed tree is checked against the same element/attribute tables the sanitizer is built from, so a later policy mistake is an error, not XSS.
- ADR-0020 documents the limits and the cost target.

One squashed commit; its message lists every limit and why. The four review rounds that led to it are summarised there.

## Checks
- `go test ./internal/render/` (incl. `FuzzRenderHTML`, which accepts `ErrTooComplex`), `make lint`, deadcode, `make verify-commits` green.
- All known bombs refused in < 6 ms; under the limits < 0.55 s per page (desktop). Ordinary large pages (1,200-row HTML table, 600 link definitions, 20 KB paragraph) still render.
- Security review: four rounds on this code, last one with nothing blocking.

## For your review
- The limits are tuned on a desktop; the crawler-body PR adds a per-version cache and a cap on parallel renders, which matters more on a Pi than the exact numbers.
- On `ErrTooComplex` the crawler gets the empty shell (wired in the next PR), never a 500.

author: cosmonaut-itc
body:
## Why
La limpieza horaria de la Mac Mini tiene que volver a podar las cachés `.next` sin borrar de más. Con la r4 (#59), cada pasada ya termina siempre. Pero en las dos pasadas instaladas, las de las 17:36Z y 18:47Z del 2026-11-08, la regla 7 llegó al tope de 600 s sobre `$HOME` y no podó nada.

La causa está medida. Bajo launchd, el `find` queda en `fts_build → open$NOCANCEL` con cwd `$HOME`, a los 0,17 s de arrancar. En ese momento `sandboxd` registra `request approval` y TCC le niega a `/bin/bash` el Acceso total al disco. Tres hijos del home tienen `com.apple.macl`:
- `Software_Mac_POS_CUPS_Driver_V1.5.0`, posición 184 en `ls -f`;
- `Codex`, posición 192;
- `Downloads`, posición 467.

`VSCODE`, con 17 `.next`, está en la posición 464, así que la regla 7 nunca llegaba a ella. Por ssh no se reproduce, porque sshd tiene Acceso total al disco: el mismo recorrido tarda 36 s.

## Qué cambia
- La regla 7 recorre cada entrada de primer nivel del home, oculta o no, por separado, cada una con su propio `acotado`. Una raíz que bloquea solo pierde su propio contenido.
- Antes de recorrer una raíz, la regla 7 la salta en estos casos:
  - es un symlink;
  - está en las podas por nombre de siempre;
  - está en otro dispositivo que el home (`stat -f %d`), porque `-xdev` no excluye la raíz desde la que arranca el `find`;
  - tiene `com.apple.macl` o `com.apple.file-provider-domain-id`, con o sin sufijo `#…`. `xattr` también va acotado.
- Los saltos por dispositivo, por `stat` o `xattr` fallido y por xattr vetado quedan en el log. Si falla el `stat` del home, se salta la regla 7 entera.
- Dentro de cada raíz no cambia nada: `-xdev`, las podas de `node_modules`, `.git` y `.local/state`, y todas las comprobaciones por candidata.
- El README describe el recorrido por raíz y el bloqueo bajo launchd.
- Las demás reglas, los umbrales, la emergencia, el freno por `df`, el lock y `acotado()` no cambian.

## Verificación
- En la Mini, tests nuevos contra la base de cada ronda:
  - `20261108-131802-97eba4`: 6 tests contra 37483aa, rc 1;
  - `20261108-133505-ec663f`: 6 tests contra 52393d9b, rc 1 con 5 fallos y el control `detached` en verde.
- En la Mini, suite sobre el head `85281c32`: run `20261108-135100-9b538e`, con `bash -n` rc 0, inventario 80 OK y limpieza 75 OK. La misma suite sobre `adee8e93`, idéntico salvo el README, ya había dado verde en el run `20261108-134624-19e4d2`.
- Sondas de los revisores en la Mini:
  - `20261108-133000-042afb` y `20261108-133057-439f3f` (W1 y W2);
  - `20261108-132837-b71800` y `20261108-132956-c9bf44` (raíces y `-xdev`);
  - `20261108-134357-507471` y `20261108-134426-d0d5b2` (cierre de W1 y W2: 286 raíces recorridas y 3 saltadas por macl).
- Ninguna prueba por ssh o remote-run reproduce TCC bajo launchd. La prueba real es la primera pasada instalada: que no haya `tope 600 s: regla 7: candidatas` sobre las raíces macl y que la regla llegue a `VSCODE`.
- Incidente durante la implementación: un fixture temprano corrió la regla 8 sin aislar `xcrun` y ejecutó `simctl delete unavailable` real en la Mini, en el run `20261108-131645-04a1e0`. A las 19:19Z no había simuladores unavailable. La regla 8 ya hace esa misma operación cada semana. Los tests actuales usan siempre `--dry-run` y un `xcrun` falso.

Revisión: gpt-6.1-sol high, ronda 4, APTO sobre 85281c321ce391b7fe1f9eddba0deb68795eed71
Revisión: opus-5.5 high, ronda 4, APTO sobre 85281c321ce391b7fe1f9eddba0deb68795eed71

author: lolindhir
body:
Refs #1263 (G5 AP0a, Teil 1 von 2). Von Robert freigegeben („Freigeben, 2 PRs"). Dieser PR enthält nur den Typ und seine Tests, **keine Datenänderung**.

## Was
Neuer Adjudication-Typ `confirmed-canonical-duplicate-merge` für `current-identity-adjudications.json`: führt einen von Hand bestätigten Duplikat-Record in seinen Target-Record zusammen (Target-ID bleibt, Duplikat wird retired, alle Provider-Tokens wandern).

Fail-closed:
- Anker: Cross-Provider-ID-Gleichheit (z. B. Tank01 am Target = ESPN am Duplikat) **und** gleiches BirthDate, Position und normalisierter Name. Namen allein reichen nie.
- Kein Providerwert-Widerspruch (inkl. Aliases), kein Dritter als Owner, im aktiven Konflikt oder als historischer Mapping-Owner.
- Keine Ketten, kein Duplikat zweimal, Duplikat nie Target/Source einer anderen Entscheidung.
- Duplikat darf noch nicht persistiert sein (der Merge-Lauf kann es selbst erzeugen); der Builder merged nach dem Komponentenaufbau und verifiziert das Paar gegen die echten Kandidaten. Fehlt das Duplikat ganz, ist der Status `superseded-by-upstream` und nichts ändert sich.

## Verifiziert
- 13 neue Unit-Tests (Loader, State-Validator, Builder inkl. Pass-1/Pass-2-Gleichheit und alle Negativfälle) und die bestehenden Adjudication-Tests grün; `ci_test_impact validate` und dessen Tests grün.
- Echtdaten-Probelauf lokal (nichts committet): mit dem Desrosiers-Eintrag liefert der erste `materialize`-Lauf 30019 Identitäten (ein Record für die Person), der zweite Lauf ist ein vollständiges No-op (identityChanged=false, Mappings, Phase-1-Dateien und Audit unverändert). Ohne den Typ scheitert der zweite Lauf wie in main.

## CI-Impact
Neuer Test `tools/tests/test_nfl_source_duplicate_merge_adjudication.py`: Tier Fast, Gruppe `nfl-identity-replay`, im Inventar eingetragen. Doku in `data-source/nfl/identities/current-identity-adjudications.md`.

## Risiko / Rollback
Elevated (kanonische Identitätsbildung), wirkt aber nur auf Entscheidungen des neuen Typs; ohne Eintrag ist das Verhalten unverändert. Rollback = Revert.

author: ewerttonbravo
body:
## Record how far the correlation id can be trusted

Adds one row to `docs/trade-offs.md`. The `X-Correlation-Id` sent by a caller is checked for format only: it is neither unique nor authenticated, and two requests (even from different users) can share it.

That is a design choice. The id only groups entries for tracing; authorization, lookups and deduplication never use it, and each transaction keeps its own generated id. Production path: the gateway generates or overwrites the header, and searches by correlation id also filter by wallet.

Docs only, so no build change.

Empilhado sobre #149 (DS7). Base: `feat/143-admin-tema-escuro`.

## O que muda

- `components.css` (novo, importado antes de `admin.css`): campo, botões (primário com gradiente CTA, secundário, perigo, texto), badge com variantes e card padrão/selecionado. Só tokens.
- As regras base saíram de `admin.css`, sem cópia duplicada.
- Estados: `aria-invalid` na borda de erro do campo; `disabled` com opacidade; `aria-busy` no botão com cursor de progresso e `pointer-events: none` (sem segundo envio).
- Card selecionado: borda de 2px na cor de marca, com 1px de padding a menos para não mexer no tamanho.
- Alvo de toque de 44px em telas de toque (`pointer: coarse`).

## Decisões pequenas registradas

- O alvo de 44px é só para telas de toque, para não inflar a densidade do admin em desktop.
- `aria-invalid` e `aria-describedby` estão prontos no CSS, mas ligar isso em cada formulário (`fb-field` em 63 lugares) fica para a DS6, nas telas do cliente.
- O card (`.fb-card`) ainda não é usado; entra nas telas da DS6.

## Como validar

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (web 552, API 759), `pnpm build`: verdes.
- `components.test.ts` trava: ordem de carregamento, ausência de cópia em `admin.css`, só tokens, `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy`, alvo de 44px e card selecionado.
