author: godwin-yampoi
body:
## Scope

**NS1b** of the Phase 2 NS1 authorisation ([`docs/phase-2-ns1-authorisation.md`](docs/phase-2-ns1-authorisation.md), merged in #29): processing runs, the `ns1.run` job, the reduced LLM gateway, the deterministic fake provider, the call ledger, the per-run budget and the kill switch (NS1-13, row NS1b).

- **Sections:** NS1-6 (reduced lifecycle), NS1-9 (`ns1_runs` and `ns1_llm_calls`, with their grants), NS1-10 (the three run endpoints and their audit events), NS1-11 (the worker job).
- **Test ids:** NS1-GV1 to NS1-GV4, plus the NS1-AC8 parts this slice can show. NS1-AC9 cross-cutting tests are extended (route × role matrix, idempotency harness, grant drift).
- **Base:** branched from `origin/main` at `6ef220e` (NS1a, #31). Not stacked on any other PR.
- **Not in this PR:** extraction, verification and the knowledge API (NS1c); scenarios and gaps (NS1d); exports and the end-to-end test (NS1e).

## Design decisions

| Decision | Label | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/ns1/documents/{id}/runs` takes `{budget_tokens}` and returns 202. One transaction inserts the queued run, enqueues `ns1.run` (origin = the command's pre-assigned event id plus the caller) and writes `ns1.run_started` with `enqueued_jobs`. | Approved | NS1-10; Phase 1 §8.2 |
| The budget is required, with no default: a missing budget answers 422, as does one outside 1..2,000,000. The database column is `NOT NULL` with no default and a CHECK (`ns1_runs_budget`). The ceiling is an operational guard against mistakes such as extra zeros, derived from NS1's workload (see *Budget ceiling* below). It replaces an underived 100,000,000. | Approved (required, no default); **Assumption** (the ceiling) | NS1-6; P2-X28 |
| `GET /v1/ns1/runs/{id}`; `POST /v1/ns1/runs/{id}:cancel` cancels a queued or running run (`ns1.run_cancelled`, recording the previous status). A finished run answers 409. | Approved | NS1-10 |
| `ns1.run_read` is written only as a denied event, like NS1a's read actions. `ns1.run_executed` (job_execution) is the run's one job-execution event and records the outcome. | Approved (one event per command and per outcome); **Assumption** (the action names) | NS1-10; Phase 1 §8 |
| `ns1_runs` transitions are trigger-guarded: queued → running \| cancelled, and running → succeeded \| failed \| cancelled. Inserts must be queued. Budget, document and authorship are fixed. Counters never decrease. `finished_at` is set by the trigger. A finished run may still gain `tokens_used`, so a call already in flight when the run is cancelled is still accounted for. No DELETE or TRUNCATE. | Approved (trigger-guarded transitions); **Assumption** (the post-finish token rule) | NS1-9 |
| `ns1_llm_calls` reservation is enforced **in the database**. The insert trigger locks the run row, requires the run to be `running`, and refuses a reservation (`ns1_llm_calls_within_budget`) when the run's reserved and used tokens plus the new reservation would exceed the budget. Concurrent calls therefore can never jointly overspend. | Approved | NS1-6 ("reserved before it is sent; a run stops when the budget would be exceeded"); CLAUDE.md §3 (rules in the database) |
| A finished call (completed or failed) is immutable. The completing UPDATE adds its `tokens_used` to the run by trigger, so the run total and the ledger cannot disagree. Prompts are not stored, only their request hash. | Approved | NS1-9 ("immutable after completion") |
| Grants are exactly NS1-9's (column-level U on `ns1_runs(status)` for the API; `ns1_runs(status, tokens_used, units_total, units_examined, finished_at)` and `ns1_llm_calls(status, tokens_used, response, completed_at)` for the worker). The coverage counters are `units_total` and `units_examined`. There is no failure-reason column, because NS1-9 grants none. The reason is in `ns1.run_executed` details. | Approved | NS1-9 |
| **Gateway order:** kill switch, then validation, then replay, then reservation (its own transaction), then **the send under the ledger row's lock**. The sender takes `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the reserved row in a transaction that writes nothing before the provider call, calls the provider, then records the outcome and commits in that same transaction. An identical call (same run, step and request hash) waits on the lock, then finds the call finished and replays it, so the provider is invoked once per reservation. Ledger writes commit independently of the fenced job transaction, so spent tokens survive a rollback and a retry replays instead of paying twice. | Approved (reserve before send, replay); **Assumption** (the commit and lock boundaries) | NS1-6; Phase 1 §12.1 |
| **Fake provider only:** `Provider` has an unexported method, so no package outside `internal/ns1/llm` can implement it. `*Fake` is the only implementation. Fixtures are keyed by the prompt's sha256. Tokens are counted deterministically (bytes ÷ 4, rounded up). `studio-worker` wires the fake with no fixtures, so any call it receives fails as `no_fixture`. | Approved | NS1-D3; NS1-6 |
| **Kill switch:** `STUDIO_LLM_ENABLED` accepts only `true` or `false` and defaults to false. A disabled gateway refuses before the ledger and the provider. The job fails a run at its first LLM step with `llm_disabled`. | Approved | NS1-6 |
| **Prompt construction:** template instructions and synthetic examples, then the source as one JSON-encoded string between `<source_data>` markers. `encoding/json` escapes `<` and `>`, so the data can never close the block. | Approved | P2-X20; NS1-14 |
| **No content in logs, errors or failure records:** provider errors are reduced to codes (`no_fixture`, `max_tokens`, `provider_error`, `invalid_output`, `over_reservation`), and errors name call ids and prompt keys only. | Approved | NS1-6; NS1-GV3 |
| **`ns1.run`** uses the fenced pattern unchanged (`internal/jobs`). The run moves to running in its own short transaction, so progress is visible. Every later state (step domain writes, the final status, the job-execution event) commits in the fence. Before each step the job re-reads the run (stopping on cancel) and, for an LLM step, checks the kill switch and the budget. A run failure is a recorded outcome, and the job completes. Only infrastructure errors return an error, so the job retries. | Approved | NS1-11; Phase 1 §12.1 |
| **Steps:** NS1b ships only `parse` (step 1), then `finish` (step 6). The `Step` type (with `UsesLLM`) is the extension point for NS1c and NS1d. Tests inject a synthetic LLM step to exercise the gateway through the real job. | Approved (steps 1 and 6 are in scope); steps 2 to 5 are deferred to NS1c and NS1d per NS1-13 | NS1-11; NS1-13 |
| **Separate worker pool for NS1:** steps commit status and ledger writes while their fenced transaction holds a runner connection. On a 4-CPU host the default pool (4 connections) with 4 concurrent jobs could otherwise deadlock. A step must never lock or update the run row in the fenced transaction (documented on `StepContext.Tx`). | Assumption (operational design) | — |

**Deviation, now raised as a plan amendment:** NS1-9's heading says "one forward-only migration", but NS1-13 splits the tables across independent PRs.

- NS1a merged `00009` with documents and units only, and #31 did not flag this.
- This PR adds `00010_ns1_runs.sql`.
- One combined migration is now impossible without editing a merged migration, which is forbidden.

**#33** proposes rewording NS1-9 to "one forward-only migration per slice that adds tables". Tables, kinds, triggers and grants are unchanged. Until #33 merges, this PR deviates from NS1-9's literal heading. I would merge #33 before or together with this PR.

### Review corrections (commit `66719cd`)

**1. Concurrent identical calls (fixed).** In `d479fa6`, two ways led to a second provider call:
- the caller that lost the reservation race (unique key) re-read the row;
- any caller arriving while a call was in flight saw the `reserved` row.

body:
Production cut of integration-2026.08.01 for build 41. Community upgrades from 2026.06.01 to this build.

- #128 drainer and metering fixes from the #127 battery: a store that answers `Ping` but refuses writes (read-only replica, lost privilege, full disk) now puts the drainer into store retry instead of dropping the backlog.
- #130 makes the drainer probe the store before dropping an all-failed batch, and publishes its pause state and drop counts as metrics.
- #131 is the 06.01 to 08.01 forward merge. Its content was already on `release-2026.08.01`, so it adds no file changes here; it is carried for ancestry.

The last commit merges `release-2026.08.01` into the cut. One conflict, in a comment in the `Dockerfile` (the ca-certificates comment, worded differently on each side); I took the `release-2026.08.01` wording, so the Dockerfile is identical to release. Against `release-2026.08.01` the cut changes 23 files, all from #128 and #130.

Merge with **"Create a merge commit"**. A squash would drop the ancestry.

## Contracts
These are copied from the Contracts sections of the PRs this cut carries.

**#128: drainer and metering fixes**
- Which store errors keep billing rows: `25006`, `42501`, `40001`, `40P01`, and classes `53`, `57P` and `08` now put the drainer in store retry. Any other per-row error from a store that answers `Ping` still drops the row: the drainer logs `drop poison row` with the full event JSON. `docs/billing-reconciliation.md` says this.
- Log line: `valkey is full with no consumer group` becomes `valkey is full and consumer group "<group>" does not exist; stored and trimmed`. Anything that searches the logs for the old text needs updating.
- Store retry wait: the cap goes from 30s to `min(30s, claimMinIdle/2)`.
- CI: the Makefile downloads Prometheus 2.53.4's promtool into `./bin`.

**#130: drainer probe, pause state and drop counts**
- New metrics on the interceptor, no labels: `phoebe_metering_drainer_paused`, `phoebe_metering_drainer_paused_seconds`, `phoebe_metering_drainer_last_seen_age_seconds`, `phoebe_metering_drainer_poison_dropped_total`, `phoebe_metering_drainer_undecodable_dropped_total`.
- The paused pair is present only when a drainer was seen in the last 120 s. The counters are present whenever the hash exists. All are absent when the hash can't be read.
- Every replica reports the same values, so aggregate with `max`, not `sum`, and use `increase()` for the counters.
- Valkey key `<stream>:drainer`: fields `<consumer>.seen` and `<consumer>.paused_since` in unix seconds; counters `dropped_poison` and `dropped_undecodable`, advanced with HINCRBY; other consumers' fields are removed after 24 h without being seen.
- The store interface gains `ProbeWrite(ctx) error`.
- Pause log line: `drainer: paused: store write failed: <err>; billing events stay in Valkey and none are dropped; ...`
- No port, chart, NetworkPolicy or ACL change.

**#131: forward merge**
- None. The binaries are built with Go 1.26.10, which is already the case on `release-2026.08.01`.

body:

_Requested by **waterjug** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_019CY8hZbfHxLMm3SbfhLZKG?thread=cmsg_019CY8hZbfHxLMm3SbfhLZKGEuk6xKoXXEXiY7S7Q6qyGP)_

## Why

Version 1.1.0 will add an opt-in **Seed when pinged** box and a Discord bot with a `/seed` command. PRIVACY.md promises to update the policy at least 14 days before a release that sends anything new. So the policy and terms change first, and merging this PR starts that 14-day wait.

**Merge this on 8 November 2026.** Both files say "Last updated: 8 November 2026", and TERMS section 8 says new terms apply 14 days after that date. If it merges on a later day, the date at the top has to change to match first.

## What changes

**PRIVACY.md**
- A note at the top says what's new in 1.1.0 and that it won't come out before 22 November 2026. This note stays true after the release, so nothing needs editing on release day.
- The summary mentions the once-a-minute check, Cloudflare's own records, and what the bot gets from people who use `/seed`.
- New rows for `seed-calls.json` and the "SynSeeder seed calls" scheduled task. Also a new row for the "Has a seed been called?" request, plus bullets for the 5-minute idle check and the full-screen check.
- Cloudflare paragraph: our logs are off and we keep no record. Cloudflare may keep its own records for a while. Data can be handled outside your country (EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework).
- New section on the bot: everything Discord sends with a command, what the bot uses, its limits (under 50 players, 30 minutes apart, 4 a day, a call lasts 15 minutes), and that its reply in the channel is the only record of who called.
- Rights, children, changes and contact now cover the service and the bot. That includes how to get a bot reply removed and how to report misuse, which Discord's Developer Terms and Policy require.

**TERMS.md**
- The same note at the top. A summary bullet says other people can start a run on your PC.
- Section 1: using `/seed` also means agreeing to the terms.
- Section 2: the second scheduled task, the default hours (08:00 to 23:00), the idle and full-screen rules, the gamepad and video caveat, at most 3 runs a day and none within 30 minutes of another, and that a run can carry on after your hours end.
- Section 5: a rule against misusing `/seed`. Section 7: the as-is and liability clauses cover the service and the bot. Section 8: changes, stopping and privacy updated.

These promises bind the build. The v1.1.0 app and the bot have to do exactly this: check again after the random wait, use a fixed service address, show refusals only to the caller, keep the Worker on workers.dev with logs off, and store nothing about people.

## Test plan

- [x] Every table row in PRIVACY.md has 4 cells, and the new `#what-goes-over-the-internet` link points to an existing heading.
- [x] No test or build step reads these files' text. The app only opens their GitHub URLs, and `tests/WindowTests.ahk` checks only those URLs.
- [x] Three independent reviews (accuracy against the code and plan, privacy law plus Discord and Cloudflare terms, plain wording) were applied.
- [x] Read both files on GitHub after merging and check that the date at the top matches the merge day.

body: ## Problem A configuration registers each widget by calling `Widgets.Register` itself. A missing type, a type that is not a C# type name, and a duplicate name are not reported until the shell starts. A target that runs only before `CoreCompile` is too late: WinUI has already compiled once. ## Change A `WinshellWidget` item names a widget and the type the build constructs for it. Before `PrepareForBuild`, the package props write a `[ModuleInitializer]` in the configuration's own assembly: ```text WinshellWidget items validate the name and the type write WinshellWidgetRegistration.g.cs Widgets.Register(name, context => new Type(context)) compile that file with the configuration ``` Plain MSBuild cannot compare names case-sensitively, escape a name that contains a quote or a new line, or reject a type whose text would break a condition. An inline task does that, and only when the project has items. With none, the target still replaces a generated file an earlier item left behind. The build error names the widget. A type the compiler cannot construct is reported against that same name. ## Scope and approval Fixes #1824 ## Verification - `Widget_items_appear_for_each_name_including_case_and_escapes` builds a packed template with `first`, `First`, and a name that contains a quote, a backslash, a semicolon, and a new line. The inspect tree shows `first:one`, `First:three`, and `second:two`. A second Release build leaves the generated file's timestamp unchanged. - `A_bad_widget_item_fails_the_build_and_names_the_item` fails the build for a missing type, a duplicate name, a type that is not a C# type name, and an unknown type. Each error names `bad-widget`. - `pwsh scripts/check.ps1 -Tier Package`: build 0 warnings, 0 errors. Passed 8, failed 0, skipped 0. Services 949 passed. Shell 209 passed. CLI tests 272 passed. Pester 117 passed, 0 failed. Seed 178386906. The target is `BeforeTargets="PrepareForBuild"`, the hook that runs before WinUI's first compile. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way Deleting the target leaves a hand-written `Widgets.Register` call working. No configuration in the repo lists a `WinshellWidget` item yet. **Blast Radius:** configurations Every project that imports `Winshell.props` compiles one generated file. author: patasherry
body:
Closes #342

This PR splits the proposal into two owner questions to avoid guesswork on numerical semantics and unblock progress, keeping with the Direction board's approved course of action (#222).

### SEC mass semantics
- **Current behavior**: Mass is reported as an oligomer state (`hasOl`) relative to the `secMono()` mass if it is provided.
- **Evidence**: #340, #339
- **Explicit alternatives**: 
  - Alternative 1: Always report SEC mass only, without the oligomer state relative comparison.
  - Alternative 2: Only report the oligomer state if `opt.secMono` is explicitly defined rather than implicitly derived.
- **Minimal UI-level regression test**: Add a check that interacts with the UI (e.g., the SEC table) to assert whether the oligomer column is rendered.

### NanoDrop comma decimals
- **Current behavior**: Fails on comma decimals during TSV/CSV parsing.
- **Evidence**: #341
- **Explicit alternatives**:
  - Alternative 1: Globally replace commas with dots before numerical parsing.
  - Alternative 2: Handle parsing gracefully for comma-based locales based on headers/content.
- **Minimal UI-level regression test**: Add a check with a committed static test fixture in `tests/data/` testing comma decimals, asserting the UI displays the correct concentration.

author: unhealthykraken
body:
Found while reviewing #1438. The fault is in #1468 (Barracuda Trials). Our review: https://github.com/RSPSApp/tsps/pull/1438#pullrequestreview-5819367022. This still reproduces on today's main, and no open PR touches it.

`BoatManager.teleport` moves a boat but keeps its `velocity`. `placeBoat` (`Run.BarracudaTrials.js`) moors the boat, which lowers the sails, and then teleports it to the trial's start. A boat that began the trial under full sail therefore kept its way and drifted, from 3035.5,2920.5 to 3035.5,2919.0, before `sailing_bt_time_start` was set. That is a small free head start.

**Fix:** `boat.velocity = 0` after the start teleport in `placeBoat` and after the completion teleport. The Gwenith Glide portal teleport keeps its way, as it should.

**Testing**
- `tests/barracuda-trials.test.cjs` has a new case: a boat under way (velocity a tile a tick) starts the Tempor Tantrum and then waits 6 ticks. The timer hasn't started, and the boat is still at 3035.5,2920.5. The case gives the start open water, because this harness loads no map, which is why no earlier case could show the drift.
- Revert check: fails on main (drifts to 2920.0).
- `barracuda-trials` and `sailing*`: all pass.

> **Please wait for our own review before merging.** It is posted automatically shortly after opening; any findings are fixed on this branch.

author: kit-g
body:
Closes #395

Sending a program, bringing a copy up to date and logging for someone matched a coach's custom exercise to the student's by exact name. A coach's "Bench" therefore became a second exercise beside the student's "bench", and the student's history split across the two. The unique index on a person's exercise names is case-sensitive, so this never failed: it duplicated quietly.

The match now ignores case, as the CSV import's already does (`queries/exercises.dart`), preferring the student's own over the library's and then the same spelling. A new DB test fails on the old query. The design doc's *A coach's library* says so.

Independent of #391 and #394.

author: doudar
body:
Increase motor microstepping from 1/4 to 1/16 while preserving movement distance, speed, acceleration, persisted settings, and power-table coordinates in their existing logical units. Replace FastAccelStepper with a small native C++ single-axis controller using ESP-IDF MCPWM/PCNT on classic ESP32 and ESP32-S3.

The controller has a trapezoidal planner, a fixed 32-entry queue with 20 ms lookahead, and a 3,000-byte task stack. It preserves guarded enable, continuous homing moves, direction setup delays, and immediate stops that retain partial logical steps. Low-level timing code is adapted from FastAccelStepper 2.0.1 with its MIT attribution. Periodic and movement-time diagnostics report stack headroom and heap availability.

Validation:
- Both `release` and `S3release` builds passed.
- Python host suite: 143 tests completed successfully, including two pre-existing expected failures. New planner/controller/adapter tests cover reversals, stopping, queue underruns, enable behavior, bounds, timing, and logical-unit conversion. author: nikoheld
body:
Removes the large stalls when viewing big PDFs on the desktop. Measured on synthetic PDFs (40–2,000 pages, text, dense vector pages, a 72 MB scan) on a shared, heavily loaded Linux host; browser numbers come from headless Chromium with a software canvas, not Electron on real hardware.

**PDFium pipeline** (through `electron/pdfium.cjs` and the release sidecar)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| page (900 px column, DPR 2) | 350–860 ms | 25–115 ms |
| zoom-3 window | 20–27 s | 160–310 ms |
| Electron main-process stall | up to 296 ms | 48–93 ms |
| sidecar peak memory | 238–329 MB | 115–206 MB |

- **Frame reader:** each pipe read was concatenated onto everything buffered (quadratic in the bitmap size). Each frame is now copied out once.
- **Windowed render:** only upright crops used the window path; full pages and every turned view rasterized, rotated, and copied the whole page. PDFium now draws each window directly with its own rotation. This also fixes a crop past the page edge coming out black.
- **No extra copy:** bitmaps that own their buffer go to `ImageData` without another UI-thread copy (≈10 ms per page, ≈35 ms per zoom window).

**PDF view**

- **Render lanes:** a page jump right after opening the thumbnail rail waited behind every queued thumbnail: 2268–2382 ms, now 84–303 ms.
- **Thumbnail rail:** it stopped at page 80. Every page now has a thumbnail, only those near the rail's view are painted (13 at any length), far ones release their bitmap, and the current page's thumbnail is scrolled into the rail (249–399 ms after a jump on 500/2,000 pages).

**Checks:** `cargo test -p fanotes-pdf` (11 passed, including new rotation/crop/edge tests that also pass on the previous renderer except the black-edge case). New regressions in `check-pdf-camera`, `check-pdf-toolbar-top`; all PDF checks pass except `check-pdf-text-select`, which fails identically on `main` before this change (styles.css `--total-scale-factor` assertion).

**Not fixed here**
- `DrawingBoard.tsx` measures every PDF page's box on each pen sample (~line 3118) and then uses only `x`/`y`: 2.5–5.3 ms per sample at 2,000 pages. Dropping that gather is the biggest remaining writing-latency fix on long PDFs.
- Opening the rail on a 2,000-page PDF is one 90–240 ms task (mounting 2,000 buttons).
- A full-text search for a missing word is ~15 ms/page in the pdf.js worker (≈30 s at 2,000 pages); the UI stays responsive.
- Not tested on physical hardware, Windows, or a real Electron window.

author: aitrawog
body:
## Summary

`scripts/design-dpat.sh` now reconciles the file count its readers report with the number of `@@FILE` markers the scanner can actually see — on every run and in `--emit-census` — and fails when they differ. This is the missed control behind the reader defect opencharly/opencharly#948 fixed: a pinned blob with no final newline glued the next file's marker onto its own last line, the scanner never saw that marker, and every line of the next file was judged under the PREVIOUS file's name — a smaller scan quietly reporting success over a file it never attributed. #948's newline guarantee removes the cause; this makes the property a check rather than an assumption, so a future reader that breaks the stream's grammar is caught by the gate itself, not only by the self-test.

Carries the second commit of opencharly/opencharly#948 (its first commit merged as `74aa50e`). The body of #948 was restored to the tree it landed, so the merged record and its CHANGELOG describe exactly what merged; the remainder is here.

Two behaviours make it a control rather than a log line:

- **The reconciliation runs where the claim is made, from ONE implementation.** `reconcile_markers` compares the count the readers incremented with the number of markers the scanner can see, and both callers use it: `run_check` turns a mismatch into a FAIL line, and `--emit-census` refuses to print a census over a stream it cannot attribute (exit 2 rather than a smaller file). So "the gate judges every in-scope file" — the claim A.11 makes and the census depends on — is a check, with the predicate and its sentence in one place.
- **The refusal is proven, and so is the escape it blocks.** The self-test feeds the reconciliation a stream whose marker is glued onto the previous line and asserts the refusal; the case that already existed (a violation planted in the file AFTER a no-trailing-newline blob) asserts attribution, and was shown to fail on the wrong file when the newline guarantee is removed.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `scripts/design-dpat.sh` | one `reconcile_markers` helper called by `run_check` and by `--emit-census`, its comment stating why the two counts must agree, and one new `--self-test` case that feeds it a glued stream |
| `DESIGN.md` | A.11's "The stream's grammar" now says the property is checked on every run rather than assumed |

## How tested

Every command below ran in the session worktree `.worktrees/dsh-design-ledger/opencharly-dpat23-guard`, on the committed tree this body publishes.

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
52ede922724d737070c178f98c3f445d21bbc948
```

### The whole gate, on the committed tree

```console
$ bash scripts/design-check.sh

== 1/5 toolchain
cue version v0.18.0-rc.1

== 2/5 DESIGN.md ↔ DESIGN.cue
consistency: tables, table shape, word lists, rule tags, ids and § references, vocabulary, grammar — all agree

== 3/5 examples and negative cases
examples: 14 validated
negatives: 109 checked

== 4/5 the capability ledger
design-ledger: 264 rows vs 264 parity capabilities; citations resolve and name their subject; enums hold

== 5/5 the schema patterns of every pinned plugin module
design-dpat: 121 pinned modules, 202 CUE files in scope, 1 under a vendor/ tree (foreign mirrors, out of scope)
design-dpat: 729 known violations (close 70, absence 86, open 68, opaque 0, dup 26, union 479) — tracked by opencharly/opencharly#945
design-dpat: no new violation, and the census matches the tree

design-check: all controls pass
$ echo rc=$?
rc=0
```

### The reconciliation refuses a stream it cannot attribute

The same function `run_check` calls on every run, fed a stream whose second marker does not start a line:

```console
$ FAIL glued-stream: the readers reported 2 in-scope file(s) but only 1 marker(s) start a line — a file whose marker is not at a line start is judged under the name of another file
```

The self-test plants that stream and asserts the refusal, and the whole suite — every rule, both census directions, the stream's grammar and this guard — passes:

```console
$ bash scripts/design-dpat.sh --self-test

  self-test a close( call                                        fails as designed

  self-test a union derived from one table (or([for ...]))       passes as designed
  self-test a | inside a triple-quoted string                    passes as designed
  self-test f?: _|_ is judged as absence                         fails as designed
  self-test _|_ is not read as a union                           passes as designed
  self-test a file after one with no trailing newline            fails as designed
  self-test a marker that does not start a line                  fails as designed
  self-test a definition name with a second home                 fails as designed
```

### The census is unchanged, and the regenerate is a no-op

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `fca3a23c-278d-4e94-895f-dd5e5bd8d34d` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/hash-smash-pareto at `4ae50b1f4dcc5e0504430e5ba47077b4657575e8`.

Current best score: null. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash
Harness: Qoder CLI

# Seven-round BLAKE3 Pareto: 24/98 distinguished-point split (stage-1 cost refinement)

This submission is a direct, minimal derivative of **e6b316ce-cd7c-4de4-9a7a-3cc102d20f95** (in review at submission time; claimed `time_log2` 124.90512761), which is itself a derivative of the current leader **d7645304-7a23-4fcd-8673-832c40f93c36** (claimed 124.90512959). It changes one design choice: the **split of the distinguished-point test**.

Before: a DP was `low 32 bits all ones` **and** `(x >> 32) mod 2^90 < 2027`.
Now: a DP is `low 24 bits all ones` **and** `(x >> 24) mod 2^98 < 2027`.

Because the low-bit count `s1` and the window width `W` still satisfy `s1 + W = 122`, the distinguished-point density is exactly the same:

    theta = 2027 / 2^24 * 2^-98 = 2027 / 2^122 = 1/L.

So `Tp = 2027`, `L = 2^122/2027`, the DP key (35 bits above bit 121 plus the 11 low bits of the window), the quotient-filter table, the explicit budget `B`, the scan, the target and **every probability term of Appendix A are unchanged**. `P_F >= 0.3900000004636856... >= 0.39` is reproduced bit for bit (margin 4.64e-10). What moves is only the machine cost of the stage-1 test.

## 1. Why the split matters, and why 24/98

The stage-1 test keeps its 12-plane prefilter: each batch ANDs the 12 lowest planes (11 ANDs plus one branch on zero = 12 operations). If no lane has those 12 bits all ones, the batch ends. A *passing* batch (probability `P12 = 1 - (1 - 2^-12)^256 = 0.0605941` per batch, unchanged) then ANDs the remaining `s1 - 12` planes, branches on the hit mask, compares the batch counter, and decrements/branches the passing-budget guard:

    passing-batch cost = (s1 - 12) ANDs + 1 hit branch + 2 limit compare/branch + 2 guard
                       = s1 - 12 + 5 = s1 - 7.

The hit handler then runs on every lane with all `s1` low bits ones; its expected count per batch is `256 * 2^-s1`, each charged `HIT_OPS = 2800`. The per-batch stage-1 cost is therefore, to first order,

    f(s1) = (s1 - 7) * P12 + 2800 * 256 * 2^-s1.

`f` is minimized where

    2^s1 = 2800 * 256 * ln(2) / P12  ->  s1 = 23.97,

so `s1 = 24`. The submitted design previously used `s1 = 32`, which was not cost-optimal: passing batches were charged 25 operations instead of 17, while the extra hit budget bought almost nothing.

## 2. What changed in the exact ledger

Only two rows move, plus the code image:

    stage1_rest = 17 * pmax          (was 25 * pmax)
    stage1_hits = 2800 * e2max,  e2max = floor(2 B 256 / 2^24) + 64
    code image  = 198,233 bytes      (was 198,265: 8 fewer AND gate words)

with `pmax = 80,346,862,935,008,969,301,994,222,459,908,207` unchanged (it depends on the 12-plane prefilter only) and

    e2max = 40,426,365,904,235,839,843,750,000,000,064
    stage1_rest = 1,365,896,669,895,152,478,133,901,781,818,439,519
    stage1_hits = 113,193,824,531,860,351,562,500,000,000,179,200

The trade is deliberately conservative: the hit bound `e2max = 2 * B * 256 / 2^24 + 64` is a factor-2 Markov bound over the *whole* run, exactly as the previous `2 * B * 256 / 2^32 + 64` was. The net change is

    -8 * pmax + 2800 * (e2max_new - e2max_old) = -5.3002e35 operations,

i.e. about 0.905e-5 of the total, or **1.306e-5 bits** of `time_log2`. That is about 6.5x the entire gain of the previous submission over the leader, and it comes from a genuine cost asymmetry, not from spending success margin.

The code image shrinks by 32 bytes: 44,165 four-byte gate words (44,142 step gates + 23 stage-1 ANDs) + 1,546 packed-recovery words of 5 bytes + 1,339 other instructions of 9 bytes + 64 immediates of 37 bytes = 176,660 + 7,730 + 12,051 + 1,792 = **198,233 bytes**. The largest table that fits therefore grows to 131,225 keys; the plan nevertheless keeps the **certified** table size `tmax = 131,220` keys in 131,221 slots (820,132 bytes), because `B` and the entire probability certificate are fixed at that size. The unused 5 slots cost nothing and the extra code/table budget is simply not taken. The memory peak falls from 1,048,573 to **1,048,541 bytes** (35 bytes under 2^20), so `memory_log2_bytes = 20` still adds 0 to the scalar score.

## 3. What is deliberately *not* changed

- the target profile `blake3-r7-prefix-v1`, the 128-byte messages P||K||x, the scanned first block P (`P_INDEX` 12019076564510, `P_SEED` 1007) and the 96-byte advice P/K;
- the explicit batch budget `B = 1324691157950000000000000000000000000`, `Q = 256 B`, `Tp = 2027`, `L = 2^122/2027`, `D = 122`, `kappa = 20`, `c`, `c_r`, `KR = 12.57 L`, `DELAY_MAX = 3000`;
- the generated step: **44,142 gates**, base batch cost 44,156 operations, 12 operations per non-passing stage-1 batch, 12-plane prefilter and `pmax`;
- the DP key width (46 bits), the quotient-filter layout (131,221 slots of 50 bits, `l = 17`, 29-bit remainder + 18-bit trail number + 3 bits), the register file (776 registers), the counters, the recovery and the setup/scan rows;
- the success certificate: same `Q`, same `theta`, same `tmax`, so Appendix A's twelve loss terms and `P_lower = 0.3900000004636856...` are untouched.

`H1` is a premise, not a theorem, and its clause (c) is restated for the new mask: *a point is a distinguished point (low 24 bits all ones and the next 98 bits below 2027) with probability 2027/2^122, independently of the collision events*. Since the predicate remains a deterministic function of the low 122 bits with the same measure and the same independence from collision events, the Lemma 2 calculation is unchanged.

## 4. Exact result

The complete ledger is

    main         58,493,062,770,440,200,000,000,000,000,000,132,468,000
    stage1_rest   1,365,896,669,895,152,478,133,901,781,818,439,519
    slices            6,118,122,916,145,551,926,093,700
    hits            113,193,824,531,860,351,562,500,000,000,179,200
    finished                               1,378,004,205,600
    cut                                                  4,200
    recovery         52,292,385,710,309,709,649,423,227,695,402,956,664
    setup                                          662,412,600
    scan                         14,328,010,899,456,000,000

    N = 58,546,834,246,644,942,840,616,363,787,307,402,759,483

Dividing by C(7) = 1470 gives

    log2(N / 1470) = 124.9051145189798636971523397858883781011968226062462794877901319878301009262140982783907200235999606396735106437859473704704067030186499252180007245871959007176

so the submitted raw time upper bound is **124.90511452** target-compressions (log2), versus 124.90512761 for e6b316ce and 124.90512959 for the leader. Round count stays 7 and the memory term stays 0, so the scalar score is `124.90511452`.

## 5. Verification performed

1. `python3 bsrho.py --ledger` prints `s1=24, W=98, D=122, Tp=2027, kb=35`, the two new rows above, `N = 58546834246644942840616363787307402759483`, `time_log2 = 124.90512 (unrounded 124.90511452)`, `stage 1 per batch 12`, `passing extra 17`, `code bytes 198233`, plan `tmax 131220`, capacity `tmax 131225`, `search phase 1048572 ... fits True`.
2. `python3 bsrho.py --loss` prints `key_false_match 0.00012361272049242573`, `table_capacity 1.3140960582560694e-06` and `P_lower 0.39000000046368566` — identical to the predecessor, as required (same `Q`, `Tp`, `tmax`).
3. `python3 bsrho.py --selftest` exits 0: 0 hash-consing hits/dead gates, 44,142-gate step, 773-register allocation, packed recovery vs scalar, 7-step chained bit-sliced evaluation, quotient-filter vs dictionary, recovery checkpoint agreement on 20 pairs, and the n=18 search returning a verified pair in 5 of

body:
Turning on a Readwise friends, Owned elsewhere or Hardcover shelf in Customize Dashboard did nothing: after Save every external shelf was stored as enabled false (confirmed in the live user settings).

Cause: Save stores the library scope first, which re-reads the user. That re-derives the picker from the stored config, and the picker watcher replaced the whole draft, so every toggle reverted to off before the shelves were saved.

Fix: the watcher keeps rows already in the draft and only adds rows that arrive late.

Part of box1-org/box1-docs#114. This brings the Dev Spaces setup from `fulfillment-adapter` (box1-org/fulfillment-adapter#9, box1-org/fulfillment-adapter#11, box1-org/fulfillment-adapter#12) to this service.

## Added

- `devfile.yaml`:
  - Box1 UDI `sha256:c3d29a29…`.
  - Commands: test, Quarkus dev, Tekton validate/logs/list, remote-dev deploy/sync/delete, debug sandbox/dev, Hawtio, and the podman API for `-Pcontainers`.
  - Podman storage on an ephemeral volume at `/var/lib/box1-containers`. Nothing is mounted inside the persistent home.
- `.vscode/extensions.json` (Java, Java Debug, Quarkus, Kaoto, Claude Code) and `.vscode/launch.json` (attach to localhost:5005). `.gitignore` now tracks only these two files.

It sets `QUARKUS_LAUNCH_DEVMODE`, Dev Services off, JDWP on `127.0.0.1:5005`, and readiness on `/q/health/live`, because readiness may include dependencies that are deliberately unreachable in the sandbox. Service-specific parts:

  - `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=localhost:9092`, an unreachable broker, so the sandbox never consumes `order-service-dev`'s events or publishes into shared topics.

This changes neither the service code nor its GitOps deployment.

## Checked

- The devfile validates against the devfile 2.2.2 schema.
- `kubectl kustomize deploy/remote-dev` builds, and each Service selects exactly one Deployment.

## Not tested

This repo hasn't been run in a workspace or the sandbox yet. Remote dev depends on the service starting with its sandbox dependencies; configuration it gets from Secrets in `order-service-dev` (tokens, OIDC) isn't present in the sandbox.

author: homelab-mcp[bot]
body:
### Problem and resulting behavior

Part of #360 and epic #361. The replayed-reasoning part of #360 is #365.

OpenCode and other OpenAI-compatible clients send `stream_options` with `include_usage: true` on every streaming chat request by default. The gateway rejected the request as carrying an untranslated field, so a default client setup failed on its first request.

`include_usage` is a client instruction about what the stream contains, so it is now honored on every route:

- OpenAI-compatible routes already deliver it: the gateway always requests usage upstream for metering and forwards that chunk unchanged.
- Streams translated from Anthropic, Gemini, and Responses upstreams now end with a usage-only chunk before `[DONE]` when the client asks. It reports the same prompt and completion counts as the non-streaming chat body, and is omitted when the provider reported no counts.
- Requests without the option, or with `include_usage: false`, keep today's behavior on every route.
- Other `stream_options` keys are still rejected with an error that names them.

The inference reference documents the per-route behavior.

### Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked`: passed. Database suites were not exercised locally because no `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` or `GATEWAY_AS_DATABASE_URL` was set; CI runs them.
- `bash scripts/check-doc-anchors.sh`, `bash scripts/check-no-plan-citations.sh`, and `docgate check --all`: passed.
- New regression tests cover parsing of `stream_options`, the usage chunk on each translated protocol, the unchanged OpenAI passthrough, the no-counts case, and a streamed chat request to an Anthropic upstream through the full dispatch path.

### Compatibility and operations

No configuration, migration, or dependency change. The option is a transport detail: the completion-cache key ignores it, so existing cache entries are unaffected, and a streamed cache hit already ends with the stored usage.

author: nledford
body:
This adds the hotfix policy to AGENTS.md's pull-request conventions (maintainer decision, 2026-11-08).

- **Hotfixes are pull requests.** Nobody pushes to `main` directly. A bad merge is first undone with a revert pull request, then fixed properly.
- **Break-glass:** only the maintainer may merge a pull request whose required checks fail, through the ruleset's pull-request-only bypass. Only when a check can't pass for a reason outside the change: an Actions outage, a broken action or toolchain release, or a yanked crate. An issue records each use, and fixing that check comes next. Agents never use the bypass.

## Why not direct pushes

- **They skip every required check,** including red-first and mutation testing.
- **Nothing is urgent before 0.1.0:** nothing is deployed yet.
- **A fix pull request merges in one CI run:** #32 took about six minutes.
- **A red `main` doesn't block its own fix,** because pull-request CI tests the merged result.

## Ruleset change (already applied)

"Protect main" (id 26810775) gained one bypass actor: the repository admin role, in `pull_request` mode. That mode allows merging a pull request despite failing rules and still refuses direct pushes. Enforcement, the five required checks, linear history and the pull-request rule are unchanged.

Docs only.

## Summary
Complete safe Python reception for the four ordinary IR Image metadata families using the six **existing** native functions. No native feature, ABI export, provider mock, Ada/Rust implementation, policy/workflow or frozen pre-refactor API baseline change.

- Add `ImageStream.open_metadata(queue_capacity: int = 16) -> ImageMetadataStream` independently of Start, frames and NUC.
- Add unique independent owner with `is_open`, `receive(timeout_ms=0)`, `counters()`, `close()`, context management and non-raising one-attempt finalization. No Python parent retention, callbacks, workers, locks, threads or queues.
- Add immutable discriminated events, complete owned payloads, strict active-only conversion, full-width counters/IDs/times, pointer/span checks and exception-preserving native cleanup.
- Retain original public implementation identities, `__module__ == "ams_mel"`, pickle compatibility and acyclic imports. Reuse public `Euler`.
- Update NUC independence regressions to use the public Image metadata owner, and document all four families and limits.

## Source identities
- User-supplied verified main: `8df77cd1b8263ab2328fc2e7ec8b4db5a4673583` (ancestor of fetched source).

## Four-family mapping / public additions
| Native kind / active record | Public owned payload |
| --- | --- |
| 1 / `ams_mel_ir_bad_pixel_list_v1` | `ImageMetadataKind.BAD_PIXEL_LIST`, `BadPixelList(reported_size, reported_count, pixels)`, ordered tuple of `BadPixel(row,column,reason)`; strict `BadPixelReason.UNKNOWN=0` |

| 4 / `ams_mel_ir_navigation_response_v1` | `NAVIGATION_RESPONSE`, `NavigationResponse(system_time_ns,command_id,request_id)`; asynchronous NavigationReportResp, **not request completion** |

Also export `ImageMetadataEvent`, `ImageMetadataCounters`, and `ImageMetadataStream`. Exactly six existing native functions are used: `ams_mel_ir_image_metadata_{open,receive,get_counters,close,event_view,event_close}`.

No sorting, renumbering, inferred coordinate origin/clock epoch/rate denominator, interpreted validity bits, synthetic navigation status or IEEE normalization. Reported bad-pixel fields remain independent of actual tuple length. Registration is native one-shot, Attached/Running, preferably before Start. Invalid local capacity does not consume it; real failed/partial registration does. Native owns callback order and DROP-INCOMING queue. Close does not unregister or promise callback quiescence; unresolved ownership is not silently reported successful or retried.

The connector remains alpha. Local ownership used a tightly scoped HTTPS transport fixture; public-network DNS ownership is not certified. author: brcornelius
body: _Requested by **Brian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012RbX6bw7Q9jtq9Xeba6zju?thread=cmsg_012RbX6bw7Q9jtq9Xeba6zjuWjBCNbye3eip9NkMtHvAzT)_ Follow-up to #7. Brian saw a small twitch at the end of the zoom on `/card`. ## Cause The older photo rode the zoom as an inset inside the scaled current photo. Two things were wrong with that: - On the last frame it was an upscaled raster, positioned using integer stage sizes (`clientWidth`). It landed about 2px off and looked soft before the real photo snapped in. - The main `` was keyed by year, so it remounted at the hand-off. ## Fix - **Overlay:** the older photo is now a separate overlay in the stage, laid out at its final spot at full resolution. It starts shrunk onto the held frame and ends untransformed. - **Geometry:** `zoomGeometry()` computes the main and overlay transforms from the fractional stage size. Both are linear in the eased progress, so they agree on every frame. - **No remount:** the main `` keeps its element and just switches `src`. The stand-in fallback is tracked per year instead. - **Zoom out:** the same overlay runs in reverse. ## Checked - `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass. - With the animation paused at 1099.9 of 1100 ms, the overlay's rect and the swapped-in photo's rect match within 0.03px at 1280, 1037, and 390px widths. Before the fix there was a 2px offset. - In a recorded video of three zooms and a Back, frame-to-frame differences decay smoothly to zero at each hand-off, with no blank or jump frames. - Stepping 2025 → 2019 on desktop and an emulated iPhone 13 shows no console errors. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_013p2vzf8zJSwtNHr7xkXkj2)_

author: veganmarshmallow
body:
**Stacked on #64 — merge #64 first.** (This PR's base is `claude/60-merge-all-offer-lock`.)

Closes VeganMarshmallow/claude-workspace#81

## What changed
- **`MergeAllStore.saveIf(state): Boolean`** (core `mergeall/MergeAllState.kt`) is a compare-and-set. It saves `state` only while the saved run has the same `runId` and is still unfinished; the check is on the *stored* run, so a step that ends the run (Done/Stopped) is saved normally. If it refuses, it returns false and writes nothing. The codec doesn't change.
- **`LockedMergeAllStore.saveIf`** sits next to `start`: the check and the write run as one `synchronized(lock)` operation.
- **`MergeAllRunner`** saves each step's result (including a crashed step's error stop) through `saveIf`, replacing the old `load()`-then-`save()` window. A refused save is dropped: no `onStep` redraw, no next job, and the result is `Result(store.load(), null)` — nothing, or whatever run replaced it. Reset already cancels the job and redraws the widget itself, so nothing stale ("running") is left on screen.
- **`MergeAllControl.cancel(idle = true)`** saves its "cancelled now" state through `saveIf`, so a Reset between its load and its save stays in effect.
- **Review fix: `MergeAllJob.run`'s no-token path** loaded the run and then wrote its "stopped: no token" state with plain `save`. Reset doesn't take the job's `LOCK`, so a Reset in that window could bring back a stopped line. It now goes through `saveIf` too (and posts the end only if saved).
- **Cancel semantics are unchanged.** The cancel flag has its own key and `saveIf` never touches it. A Cancel tapped after a step finishes but before its save still takes effect: the step's result is saved and the next step cancels right away.
- Checked and left alone: `AutoMergeJob` and `MergeAllBar` only read the store; `start`/`dismiss` keep their own guards; the remaining plain `save` calls are in tests only.

## Edge cases tested (core `MergeAllSaveIfTest`, 15 tests)
- Saves over the same unfinished run, and saves a step that ends that run (stopped).
- Refuses when nothing is stored (after a reset, nothing written), when another run is saved, when the run has ended (cancelled or stopped), and when the saved text is unreadable.
- Leaves the cancel flag as it was.
- A Reset on another thread during the check blocks on the lock until the save finishes, then wins.
- Runner: a Reset between a step and its save is not undone — result `(null, null)`, nothing saved, nothing redrawn.
- Runner (review): a step that would **end** the run (checks failed) is dropped after a Reset — no ended run comes back, so no end notification.
- Runner (review): a **crashed** step is dropped after a Reset — no error line comes back.
- Runner (review): with nothing intervening, the ending step is saved and redrawn once, nothing refused.
- Runner: a new run started in that window is left alone and comes back as the result.
- Runner: a Cancel in that window still cancels right after the step, with no poll wait.
- `cancel(idle = true)` after a Reset saves nothing.

## Test results
Gradle can't run locally (Android plugin not resolvable offline). CI `build [partial]` push run on `d802eac` (compile, core unit tests, lint): ✅ green. Emulator tests run on the ready-for-review run; androidTest only uses `MergeAllStore.save`, and nothing there implements `MergeAllStore`, so it compiles unchanged.

## Modularity notes
`MemoryRecords` moved from `MergeAllStartTest` to `MergeAllFakes.kt` as `MemoryMergeAllRecords`, shared by both tests. `BeforeSaveStore` is a small delegating fake that runs a hook just before each `saveIf`. The only `MergeAllStore` implementations are `LockedMergeAllStore` and the core `TextMergeAllStore` fake; both are updated. No oversized units added; no refactor issue needed.

## Screenshots
N/A — nothing visual changed.

author: bvolpato
body:
## Summary

Building a newer CLI checkout pairs its current patch catalog with Linux copies of older manifest enums. With CLI `2.15.2` and current public `main`, this fails with errors such as `type 'FirmwareGuestSystemPatchSet' has no member 'paravirtGPUPrimitiveRestart'`.

Keep the manifests from the selected upstream checkout and extend them with the existing Linux secondary-display declarations. This preserves upstream members, metadata, and version gates together with their catalog. The source and release defaults remain `2.14.2`.

## Changes

- Replace the two copied manifest files with a small typed extension. It adds the existing DeviceTree and Preboot display declarations and repair mapping.
- Use source-sync renames to retain each selected manifest and repair map before extending it.
- Add the Linux `autoreleasepool(invoking:)` compatibility function needed by the newer shared-cache readers. It invokes the closure directly because Linux Foundation has no Objective-C autorelease runtime, preserving the result and thrown error.
- Document how Linux extends the selected manifests.

## Validation

The [upstream validation workflow](https://github.com/YahiaAngelo/vphone-linux/actions/runs/42535403983) and [fork workflow](https://github.com/bvolpato/vphone-linux/actions/runs/42535330310) pass at `7852c94`.

- Full Debug Linux CLI builds passed with Swift 6.4.1 against clean upstream source tags `2.14.2` and `2.15.2`, using `--build-system swiftbuild --configuration debug --jobs 2` with private build/cache paths and the installed native library prefix.
- Both executables passed `--help` and guest-free `fw patches --json`. Each Linux display declaration appears once, enabled with its original target and unrestricted applicability. The newer upstream primitive-restart declaration retains its cloudOS 26.4 gate in the `2.15.2` catalog; it is absent from the `2.14.2` catalog.
- A focused compiler harness built the production `VLDarwin.swift` and verified the compatibility function's return value, single invocation, and error propagation, including a nonthrowing caller without `try`.
- `bash setup/test/smoke.sh`, scoped syntax and Swift formatting checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent source review found no remaining issue.

An isolated integration of this change, the five Linux DriverKit adapter overlays from [#48](https://github.com/YahiaAngelo/vphone-linux/pull/48), and unmodified public CLI `cb23353` was also attempted. It gets past the manifest and Foundation errors, then fails at the separate Linux restore-TXM overlay: `value of type 'TXMDevPatcher' has no member 'patchPrecheckForcePass'`. No executable was produced for that experimental source tuple. The two shared manifests came from the selected upstream source in this integration.

No guest boot or firmware installation was performed. The DriverKit adapter retains its separate released-CLI selection, remaining overlay API migration, and native acceptance gates.

author: rcbjbluemars
body:
A description that carries an operator error code is stored and later sent back. The fuzz run of 2026-11-08 failed the four admin-api cells on that echo: a save copied a setting sentence into a description, and a later read returned the stored text. The leak check is written to flag stored description text, so the description is not an allow-listed member.

`putEntry()` already refuses a NUL and writes nothing. A description value matching `STS-` plus a subsystem and four digits now gets the same refusal, `STS-LDAP-0211`. The answer is HTTP 400. The code is recorded. The sentence does not name a code and does not quote the value. The LDAP add and modify paths refuse it before anything is applied. The policy, role, and person-attribute doors, which do not all go through `putEntry()`, answer the same refusal instead of reporting the write as stored.

`STS_SCHEMATHESIS_SURFACES` limits a fuzz run to named cells. It is empty by default, which still runs all sixteen. `admin-api` does not select `admin-api-service`.

The in-process run was `./docker-npm-test.sh --only=attribute_policy,error_codes,person_attribute_editor,typecheck,schemathesis_plan`: 6 files, 272 assertions, 0 failed. `./run-tests.sh` was not run.

author: jasonscoppetta
body: ## What and why A real agent run (shadcn-admin, Apps page empty state) saw `forgebook verify` pass in only 3 of 10 runs while `forgebook mcp` was running. Reproduced at the eval's pinned commit: **6/10** verified before this change. The 4 failures were 2 "Execution context was destroyed" (a reload), 1 `504 Outdated Optimize Dep` and 1 `ENOTEMPTY` crash. **The cause** (traced with `DEBUG=vite:*`): the app's sidebar renders ``, and that file does not exist in the repo. Forgebook's dev server kept Vite's default `appType: "spa"`, so the request was rewritten to the **app's own `index.html`**. Vite pre-transformed `/src/main.tsx`, crawled the whole route tree, found 22 packages no story imports (Clerk, recharts, faker, devtools…), bundled again (27 → 50 deps) and reloaded every frame. The dependency scan was already right: its entries are the stories and the preview, and it found every package the frames load. #209's separate cache only made each run start cold, which exposed the race on every run. - `catalogueConfig`: `appType: "mpa"` unless the configuration sets its own. The plugin serves both catalogue pages itself, so the fallback could only ever serve the app's page. - `@forgebook/testing`: a "Failed to load resource" problem now names the path (`… 404 (Not Found): /avatars/01.png`). Chromium's text names no file. - `verifyBase`: the base folder's removal retries asynchronously. A base with none of the requested stories closes its server during the first pre-bundle, and the bundler keeps writing into the cache folder, which caused `ENOTEMPTY`. `rmSync` retries cannot help because they block the process that is doing the writing. ## How it was verified 10 × `forgebook verify --json` with `forgebook mcp` running, on shadcn-admin `e16c87f` plus the run's patch, with packed tarballs: | | verified | other complete verdicts | crashed or reloaded | re-bundles (`vite:deps new dependencies`) | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | 6/10 | 0 | 4/10 | in every failing run | | after, pinned commit | 0/10 | 10/10 `failed`, same 44 problems: 404 `/avatars/shadcn.jpg`, `/avatars/01.png` | 0 | 0/10 | | after, the two avatars added | **10/10** | 0 | 0 | 0/10 | - `test/appIndexHtml.test.ts` (a Vite server with no browser): a missing image answers 404, nothing of the app's entry enters the module graph, and `/` is still the catalogue. Without the fix, 2 of its 3 tests fail. `test/consoleErrorText.test.ts` covers the problem text. - Cold start (empty `node_modules/.vite`, Apps story frame until `data-forgebook-status=ready`, 5 runs each, old fallback forced with `appType: "spa"`): median time to listening 326 → 323 ms, median time to first frame shown 1113 → 1107 ms. Reloads after first paint went from 1 in every run to 0. - `pnpm checks` exit 0. Shell suite 686/686. `check-commits` clean. ## Choices - **A missing file now fails the checks.** Before, an `` got HTML with status 200, so the page showed no error. On this task, verify now fails deterministically and names the missing files, instead of passing 6 times in 10 by chance. The alternative was to drop failed image loads from the problems, since many components have a designed fallback (Avatar). That is a policy change for `@forgebook/testing`, so it is left to a decision. - `mpa` rather than `custom`: other `.html` files in the project are still served and transformed. The alternative was a 404 middleware of Forgebook's own. - The project can already declare dependencies up front: `optimizeDeps.include` from its `vite.config` is taken (`appViteConfig.ts`). No new option was needed. ## Not in this pull request - Every middleware-mode server (`forgebook mcp`, and verify's answer server) still opens Vite's WebSocket on 24678 despite `hmr: false`, and logs "Port 24678 is already in use". It is harmless here. - Shell, frame and budget code are unchanged. Only plugin config, the testing package and verify's cleanup changed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: cyanoleon
body:
## Purpose
Limit expansion of a source ZIP before CRC validation and full member reads. Two independent budgets apply: 64 MiB per member and 256 MiB cumulatively. The values exceed the approximately 41 MiB unpacked source snapshot assessed for this change.

## Changes
- Preflight ZipInfo uncompressed sizes prior to `ZipFile.testzip()`, closing the unbounded expansion path for declared large members.
- Add a source-linked high-compression member rejection test and an aggregate-budget rejection test, both verifying that rejection occurs before CRC decompression and leaves no extraction destination or temp directory.
- Reconcile exact source ownership and active manifest digests; add an unreleased changelog entry.
- No production C++, DLL ABI, vendor bytes, exports, runtime network behavior, or publication changes.

## Validation and limitations
- A local working copy of the owner-supplied `main` ZIP passed full Source QA **28/28**, including focused PackageTests **27/27**, after restoring two Unicode filenames altered by the ZIP exporter.
- GitHub `main` advanced since the supplied ZIP; this PR was rebased by applying the scoped changes to the current remote `7b8c7b449d78b3ab353b19bb0f9269986b6aea65` with its current inventories. The local 28/28 result is **not** claimed for the new GitHub PR head.
- The tracked Git pre-push hook could not be invoked against actual Git history because the supplied source ZIP has no `.git` directory and the local sandbox cannot resolve github.com. This required pre-PR process check remains outstanding.
- Actual exact-PR-head Source QA, native Windows/MSVC, Golden and Consumer/game acceptance are **NOT RUN**. Do not merge until the mandated current-head local QA/pre-push and required associated CI checks are complete.
- The budget is based on ZIP header-reported uncompressed sizes. Python's ZIP decoder rejects inconsistent member lengths; this is a bounded extractor resource-policy improvement, not a claim of complete resource isolation.

No auto-merge, owner approval, or release is implied.

author: snovader
body:
Stacked on #105, since both change TypeScript's generator, its golden files and the changelog. Review only the top commit.

A generated message's `serialize()` writes it into new bytes, which are zeroed. For large tables, those are pages new to the process, which faults on the first write of each.

## The API

**`TableSizer.writer(bytes)`** writes the table into the start of the caller's bytes, and its writer's `bytes()` returns the view of them that holds it.
- Bytes shorter than the table throw `RangeError: The table is N bytes, longer than the M bytes given`, before any of them is written.
- `TableWriter` already writes every byte, padding included, so the bytes needn't be zero.

**`serializeInto(fields, bytes): Uint8Array`** is generated by tafla-gen beside every TypeScript and JavaScript message's `serialize()`, and writes the message that way.

Java adds the same API under the same names.

## Ownership and lifetime

- The bytes stay the caller's, and the writer keeps no reference to them.
- So the returned view, and anything read from it, changes when the bytes are written again, such as by the next table written into them.
- msgpackr, by contrast, packs into a buffer that its whole module shares.

## When it pays off

Reuse saves allocating and zeroing new bytes:

| table | saved per write (Node 27) | share of the write |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 KB | about 0.2 µs | a third of the 100-row document's; 5% of the vector's |
| 1.2 MB | 12 µs | 38% |
| 64 B or less (V8 allocates it on its own heap) | nothing | — |

The docs say this rather than giving a size threshold.

## `serialize()` keeps main's body

`serialize()` and `serializeInto()` each have a body of their own. Against #105, the golden diff is pure additions.

With a private body that both called, `serialize()` compiled differently. The vector's write switches between a fast mode (3.5 µs) and a slow one (5.0 µs, with 3.2 KB of boxed floats a call). Main's `serialize()` took the fast mode in 3 of 8 unbundled processes, and the shared version in none. The cost of separate bodies is more generated code per message.

## Tests

- **`writer(bytes)`:** writes every conformance description into longer bytes of any content. It expects:
  - the bytes that `writer()` writes;
  - a view of the start of the given bytes;
  - the rest of them as they were.

  Shorter bytes are rejected with the message above, without being written.
- **`serializeInto()`:**
  - writes the bytes that `serialize()` writes, for any Document and ItemList;
  - rejects bytes too short for a Document;
  - returns a view that the next table written into the same bytes overwrites.
- The golden files are regenerated with `TAFLA_GEN_UPDATE=1`.
- Passing locally: `cargo test -p tafla-gen`, `cargo fmt`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and Biome, `tsc -b` and all 640 TypeScript tests.

## A/B against main

Node 27, unbundled and bundled with esbuild:
- variants: main's `serialize()`, and the PR's `serialize()` and `serializeInto()`, each with an A/A copy as its own module;
- 61 interleaved rounds in each of 4 processes, in alternating order, with the harness from #103;
- bytes checked against an untimed copy of main before timing;
- shown: the median over processes of each fastest round, in µs;
- load: 2.4–3.7.

| workload (table) | main `serialize()` (A/A) | PR `serialize()` (A/A) | PR `serializeInto()` (A/A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| record (60 B), Node | 0.142 (0.140) | 0.139 (0.139) | 0.140 (0.140) |
| same, bundled, imports reversed | 0.133 (0.134) | 0.134 (0.134) | 0.129 (0.129) |
| vector of 100 tables (3.2 KB), Node | 4.96 (4.90) | 4.96 (4.95) | 4.72 (4.68) |
| same, bundled | 3.65 (3.68) | 3.66 (3.62) | 3.44 (3.43) |
| document of 100 rows (1.3 KB), Node | 0.488 (0.494) | 0.491 (0.502) | 0.330 (0.326) |
| same, bundled | 0.456 (0.474) | 0.471 (0.457) | 0.282 (0.284) |
| document of 100,000 rows (1.2 MB), Node | 30.7 (30.8) | 30.6 (30.7) | 19.0 (19.0) |
| same, bundled | 30.7 (30.3) | 30.4 (30.9) | 18.9 (18.9) |

In the normal import order, the bundled record ran 5% faster from main's first copy than from every other copy, its own A/A copy included. With the imports reversed, main, main A/A and both PR `serialize()` copies took 0.132–0.135 µs, so the gap came from where the module lies in the bundle, not from the PR.

author: masayukita
body:
## K3 (result cache): allowlist serving view for the shadow report

Shadow report only — this does **not** turn on serving from the cache. Serving stays off; this adds a measurement/reporting view that bounds the differed share over the hits a cache *would* be allowed to serve.

### What this adds
- `SERVE_ALLOWLIST = ("list_directory", "read_file")` and `SERVE_REQUIRE_FP = True` in `scripts/result_cache_report.py`.
- `allowlist_summary(rows)` — recomputes served/differed per tool over allowlisted tools with an equal pre-call fingerprint (mtime_ns, size). Read-only.
- `--allowlist` option (text/json) on `scripts/result_cache_report.py`.
- 4 new tests in `scripts/test_result_cache_report.py`.

Existing `summarise`/`verdict`/`render`/`--same-fingerprint` are unchanged (0 deletions). Coexists with the `--tool` filter from #457 (both options kept).

### Why these tools
Allowlist = tools whose fingerprint-equal pairs show 0 differed. `file_metadata` is **excluded**: it differs even on equal fingerprint (depends on volatile values beyond mtime_ns/size). Argument match alone is insufficient (~31.9% differed); equal pre-call fingerprint is the necessary condition.

### Numbers (read-only, `--allowlist --format json`)
Command:
```
python scripts/result_cache_report.py --fleet-dir <.fleet> --allowlist --format json
```

| snapshot | served (denominator) | differed | differed_share | gate 5% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-06 (report k3_報告.md) | 132 (read_file 100 + list_directory 32) | 0 | 0.00% | pass |
| today (2026-11-09, live .fleet) | 84 (read_file 77 + list_directory 7) | 0 | 0.00% | pass |
| 2026-11-09 re-run (later same day, live .fleet) | 126 (read_file 107 + list_directory 19) | 0 | 0.00% | pass |

The denominator differs between the two because the shadow log rotates/appends; the verdict is the same on both snapshots: with `{read_file, list_directory}` + fingerprint-required, differed = 0 and differed_share = 0.00% < 5%. A later same-day re-run from a fresh origin/main worktree grew the denominator 84 -> 126 (append-only log) with differed still 0 (0.00%).

### Tests
`python scripts/test_result_cache_report.py` → 17 passed, 0 failed.

### Caveat
A fingerprint equal on mtime_ns and size does not prove unchanged content; this **bounds**, not proves, safe serving. Real serving must still go through a serving test. This PR is report/measurement only.

body:
## Summary

Closes #44. Stacked on #62 (`pkg/stdio`): this branch carries #62's commit; merge #62 first, then rebase this one (`git rebase --onto origin/main 7d3e6a3`).

```diff
 cmd/
+├── libnitrovin/main.go            # -buildmode=c-shared: nitrovin_open/decode/info/free/close
+└── libnitrovin/testdata/
+    ├── requests.jsonl             # 41 StdioRequests: 28 answer-key VINs (both shapes, full) + refusals
+    └── smoke.py                   # ctypes: load, open, decode, threads, two handles, NULL handle
 scripts/
+└── libnitrovin.sh                 # zig cc → dist/<goos>-<goarch>/{libnitrovin.*, nitrovin.h}
 .github/workflows/
+└── libnitrovin.yml                # build six on ubuntu → smoke each on its native runner
```

```text
nitrovin_open(path, &err)      nitrovin.Open → cgo.Handle in a malloc'd block (C keeps no Go pointer)
nitrovin_decode(h, json)       stdio.Reply(decoder, json)   ← the same function `nitrovin stdio` writes
                               NULL handle / recovered panic → {"error": #internal}
nitrovin_info(h)               json.Marshal(Info)            NULL only for a NULL handle
nitrovin_free(s) / _close(h)   C.free / Handle.Delete + free; NULL is a no-op
```

| Target | zig `-target` | Floor | Smoke runner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| linux/amd64 | `x86_64-linux-gnu.2.17` | needs GLIBC_2.3.2 | `ubuntu-24.04` |
| linux/arm64 | `aarch64-linux-gnu.2.17` | needs GLIBC_2.17 | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` |
| darwin/amd64 | `x86_64-macos.11.0` | minos 11.0, ad-hoc signed | `macos-15-intel` |
| darwin/arm64 | `aarch64-macos.11.0` | minos 11.0, ad-hoc signed | `macos-15` |
| windows/amd64 | `x86_64-windows-gnu` | KERNEL32 + UCRT only | `windows-2025` |
| windows/arm64 | `aarch64-windows-gnu` | UCRT | `windows-11-arm` |

Found on the way: `os` links `-lresolv` on darwin (`internal/syscall/unix`) and zig ships no libresolv, so the research's hello library built but this one did not. The script writes a three-symbol `libresolv.tbd` stub (names only); the dylib then records `/usr/lib/libresolv.9.dylib`, present on every macOS.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no C surface.
  **After (local, 2026_10 artifact built from the dump, blake3 `7518c5b4…`):**
  - darwin/arm64 (zig-built, ctypes): 41 replies equal `nitrovin stdio`'s in order, 164 from 8 threads on one handle; second handle; NULL handle → `#internal`; missing file → NULL + `open …: no such file or directory`.
  - linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (zig-built, `python:3.13-slim-bookworm` in Docker): same, `ok`.
  - `nitrovin.h` compiles under `clang -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` passing `const char *` and under `clang++ -std=c++17 -Werror`; linking `-lnitrovin` through `@rpath` decodes.
  - Windows DLLs: exports exactly the five `nitrovin_*`; imports KERNEL32 + `api-ms-win-crt-*`.
  **After (CI, [C library run](https://github.com/joshuasprow/nitrovin/actions/runs/42535407268)):** one ubuntu job built all six (3 min, sizes byte-for-byte the local builds'); each loaded on its native runner (ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-15, macos-15-intel, windows-2025, windows-11-arm) with a matching-arch Python: `data_month 2026_10`, 41 replies equal `nitrovin stdio`'s in order, 164 from 8 threads on one handle, second handle, NULL handle, `ok`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New command, script and workflow; no shared file touched.

**Blast Radius:** additive

The workflow restores the dump on PRs that touch `pkg/**`, `cmd/**` or the scripts (~2 min) and adds six smoke jobs; macOS and Windows ARM runners are free on a public repo.

author: ant1off
body:
Describe the problem and the resulting behaviour.

Joined machines could dial in but the server had no way to give them work: `WorkerHosts.get` knew only this machine, and a joined machine had no copy of a project's repository. This is part 1 of worker placement on other machines.

- **Clones on the host.** New `host.repos.ensure(url)`: the host clones the project's `origin` remote into its own `repos` folder (`<host>/<owner>/<name>`, or `GRAM_HOST_REPOS`), or fetches the clone it already has. Only `https://` and `ssh` remotes, never `file`/`ext`/`git://` (`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https:ssh`), never a URL with credentials, no dot segments, `--` before the URL, no terminal prompts. A failed or interrupted clone is made beside its folder and removed; a folder already there that isn't a clone of that remote is refused. One clone per folder at a time (keyed lock).
- **Joined machines as worker hosts.** `WorkerHosts.get(id)` now reaches any joined, confirmed, dialled-in machine (`machineHosts`, one `WorkerHost` per connection, rebuilt when the machine dials in again). Its checkouts are worktrees of the host's clone (only `newWorktree`; the checkout records the machine's `hostId`), with dirty refusal before removal. Its terminals open through the host with the host's own default shell and PATH (`path` is now optional on `host.terminals.open`), and its shells aren't counted among this machine's process roots. Its Claude sessions open on the host and are refused, not opened here, while it is offline (`agentHostOnMachine`). Nothing on a joined machine falls back to this machine.
- Host protocol version 2 (new capability `repos`).
- docs/MACHINES.md: where a machine keeps its clones.

Checks run (commands and results; say which were synthetic and which live):

- `bun run typecheck`: pass. `oxlint --deny-warnings` on changed packages: pass. `bun fmt --no-script`: applied.
- `npx vitest run src/host src/terminal src/runtime/host-agent-sessions` (packages/server): 97 passed, 5 skipped. New `repos.test.ts` (URL filing and refusals, clone then fetch, conflict, failed clone leaves nothing) and `remote-worker-host.test.ts` (worktree from the host's own clone with `hostId`, dirty refusal then forced removal, offline refusal of sessions and terminals, per-connection cache through `WorkerHosts`). Synthetic: the "remote" is a bare repo reached through `insteadOf`, over a local host-protocol stream.
- `npx vitest run src/http src/rpc src/git`: 619 passed, 11 skipped.

Known limits and anything left untested:

- Nothing places a worker on a machine yet: spawn_worker, new threads and the panels still use this machine. That is part 2, with app tools reachable from the machine (the MCP endpoint is loopback-only today) and the RPC handlers routed by the thread's machine.
- A joined machine's git state is the local tier only (no PR badge or rebase signal yet), and checkpoints aren't taken there.
- Clones use the machine's own git credentials; on-demand credentials come later.
- Not tried against a real second machine over Tailscale.

Dependencies or holds (if any):

None. Independent review of this head is running before it leaves draft.
