author: binary1215
body:
Stacked on #42 (`codex/stage3c-registry-6`). This is the seventh and last stage 3-C PR. It moves every remaining CLI command into the operation registry and deletes the CLI dispatch branches.

After this PR, both `scripts/mcp-server.mjs` and `scripts/lode.mjs` dispatch only through `scripts/lib/operation-registry.mjs`.

## Commits

1. **cdb3b6e – Recorder nits from the #42 review, plus a recording gap fixed before the move.**
   - **`caller` stand-in:** MCP dispatch now gets a frozen `caller` stand-in, recorded in the 6 `conversation_list`/`send` inputs.
   - **Recording gap:** the recorder's CLI command scan only read `if (command === …)` branches. It now also reads `if (["a", "b"].includes(command))` branches, so `project-document-prepare`/`-publish` and `work-document-prepare`/`-configure`/`-publish` are recorded before they move. CLI recordings go from 385 to 400.
   - **Cross-check:** the fixture is byte-identical when recorded on the pre-registry commit `4e8159c`, as before with the recorder's registry lines removed.
   - **`call()` guard:** `callRegistered`'s `call()` now refuses explicitly when a handle-only entry has no implementation. No caller does this today.
2. **c2e01fd – All remaining CLI commands.**

## How the CLI branches moved

The 61 remaining `runRoutedCommand` branches were converted mechanically. Each became a registry `cli.handle(context)` whose body is the branch body verbatim:
- `lode.mjs` library imports used by the body become lazy imports at the top of the handle, for example `const { compileContext } = await import("./context-compiler.mjs")`. The registry is a dispatch module, so these calls are recorded under the same names.
- `lode.mjs` helpers (`inputJson`, `optionalInputJson`, `readJsonFile`, `evidenceNeedsInput`, `requireRuntimeSurface`, `usage`, `packageMetadata`, `pluginRoot`) and dispatch values (`command`, `surface`, `projectSessionRoute`, the Host adapters, `signal`, `onProcess`, `onExportScope`) are passed in through the call context.
- Commands with more than one name use `cli.aliases`: `status`/`doctor`, `init`/`resume`, `help`/`--help`/`-h`, `--version`/`version`, and the two document prepare/publish groups.

The converter checks that the whole branch region was made of branches; nothing else was dropped.

**Where the 61 went:**
- **16 became the `cli` side of their MCP entry:**
  - `status`/`doctor` → `project_status`;
  - `graph-query` → `project_graph`;
  - `session-create` and `session-list`;
  - `init`/`resume` → `project_initialize_or_resume`;
  - `project-native-history`, `project-export`, `project-bundle-inspect`, `project-import`;
  - `worker-integrate`, `worker-integration-status`;
  - `runtime-invocation-result`, `session-work-record`, `session-continue`;
  - `project-document-status`, `work-document-status`.
- **45 became CLI-only entries named `cli:<command>`,** with no tool or MCP side:
  - help and version;
  - `graph-explorer`, `runtime-invocation-authorize`/`-execute`/`-apply-run-result`, `worker-execute`;
  - `onboarding-start`/`-candidates`/`-review-read`, `source-scope-set`/`-status`, the `feature-mapping` reads;
  - the `change-set`/`change-impact` record/read operations, `observation-file-ingest`, `head-continuity`;
  - `world-index`, `storage-gc`, `world-status`, the `world-refresh` family, `world-graph-remote-database-initialize`/`-activate`, the `world-docs` capture/review/apply/policy commands;
  - `checkpoint`, the document prepare/publish groups, `lineage-plan`/`-next-plan`/`-contract`, `run-finish`, `run-review`, `context-compile`.

**Registry changes:** the catalog takes only entries with a `tool`, MCP lookup only entries with an `mcp` side, and CLI lookup covers commands and their aliases.

**`runCommand`:** in `lode.mjs` it keeps its Session-routing pre-steps unchanged (the `--session` handling, the `session-list`/`status`/`doctor` location projection, the bundle-command checks, the `init`/`resume` route). Then it calls `runRoutedCommand`, which now only looks the command up or throws the same `Unknown command: <name>` error.

**Registry totals:** 188 entries, of which 143 have an MCP side, 172 a CLI side, and 45 are CLI-only.

**Lines:**
- `lode.mjs`: 923 → 515 here. Over stage 3-C it went 1,439 → 515.
- `mcp-server.mjs`: 5,985 → 601 over stage 3-C.
- Registry: 4,977 → 5,958.

## Verification

- **Dispatch recordings:** unchanged after the move. The fixture now covers 320 MCP inputs and 400 CLI argument lists.
- **Byte-identical surface:** `tools/list`, the catalog, both `toolsForSurface` lists and every `discoverTools` page match before and after.
- **CLI output byte-identical to the previous commit:** `help`, `help-all`, `--version`, `managed-maintenance help`, a `status` error on a missing root, and the unknown-command error.
- **Full suite:**
  - Base: #42 at `633f321`, 2708 tests, 221 failing. One of those is the label-count test, which #42 fixed in `fed6070` after that run.
  - Branch `c2e01fd`: 2708 tests, 220 failing.
  - `compare-test-baseline 3c6.tap 3c7.tap`: **new failures: 0**. Fixed: 1, the label-count test, already fixed in #42.
  - Then the branch merged `origin/codex/stage3c-registry-6` (beta.97). The recordings, core helpers, hooks, adoption labels, MCP contract and display-label tests pass after the merge.
- **Checks:**
  - `prettier --check`: clean.
  - `verify:docs`: 51/51.
  - `generate-claude-hooks --check`: current.
  - `verify-documented-flow`: verified.
  - `verify-claude-marketplace`, `verify-codex-marketplace`, `verify-newcomer-readme`: exit 0.

## Test expectations changed

None.

## Not done

**`usage()` is not derived from the registry.** The help text is a hand-ordered list grouped by workflow, with explanatory lines between groups, and registry order is the MCP catalog order. Producing the same bytes from the registry would mean moving every help line and comment into the entries, plus a separate ordering table. That relocates text without removing any duplication, so I left `usage()` in `lode.mjs`. The help output is unchanged (checked above).

## MCP/CLI differences: additions from the CLI move

These extend the consolidated list in #42. Each surface still keeps its own mapping.

- **`status`/`doctor`:** the CLI can pre-empt `project_status` with the location projection in `runCommand`. MCP's `dispatchSessionRequest` does the same; the two use the same library call.
- **`session-create`:** the CLI calls `createLodeSession` and MCP calls `createHeadSession`. They are one function: `session-routing.mjs` exports it under both names.
- **`session-list`:** `runCommand` always answers it before `runRoutedCommand`, with `--session`, `--max-sessions`, `--after-session` and `--conversation-candidates`. The registry `cli` handle (root only) is the previously unreachable branch, kept verbatim.
- **Bundle commands:**
  - `project-bundle-inspect` takes the bundle as the positional root, and also accepts a standalone handoff file.
  - `project-import` returns `nextRead: { command: "conversation-enter" }`, where MCP returns `{ tool: "lode_conversation_enter" }`.
- **`session-continue`:** the CLI never attaches a coordination workspace Host; MCP does when one is configured.
- **`init`/`resume`:** the CLI reads `--runtime` (comma list), `--profile`, `--copied-project`, `--instruction-integration`, `--write-root-instructions` and `--input` (onboarding JSON). MCP maps the same fields from snake_case and composes the plugin installation context.

## CHANGELOG bullets (for the version this merges under)

- Every CLI command now dispatches through the operation registry. `scripts/lode.mjs` no longer has per-command branches; CLI-only commands are registry entries without an MCP tool. No behavior change.

P1-2 from the outside-audit plan ("What to build" 1): starting from visibility, a reader opens its prompts, one prompt's executions, then the raw answer with its engine, time and citations. **Stacked on #375** (P1-1 evidence queries, `feat/evidence-queries`); it gets rebased with the stack.

- **In the URL:** `?drawer=visibility` (the prompts) or `?drawer=prompt:ID` (its executions), plus `&execution=ID` on top (the answer); `epage`/`esort`/`edir` page and sort the executions table on the server. Every drawer can be shared, reopened, and restored on reload. The page's filters are kept (`parseDrawer` / `withDrawer`).
- **Drawers** (`EvidenceDrawer`):
  - From the right at 90% width, and 85% for the one stacked on top; full screen on phones. The page behind is dimmed.
  - A title bar and a Close button.
  - Esc closes only the top drawer. Focus moves in, is trapped (Tab / Shift+Tab), and returns to what opened it.
  - `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal` and a label. Rendered on `document.body`, with everything else **inert** (`useInertOutside`, the same hook as #376).
- **Visibility → prompts** (`PromptsBody`): "named in n of d answers", then each prompt with its own counts. These add up to the headline (P1-1).
- **A prompt → executions** (`ExecutionsBody`): a sortable table (date, engine, named) with server-side paging. Columns: date, engine, named with position, brands named, and the answer excerpt. Each row opens the answer on top.
- **The answer** (`ResponseBody`):
  - a **"Discovery signal"** label, plus whether you were named and at what position
  - the prompt as asked, the engine, the time, the location and the brands named
  - the answer as **plain text**, with every named brand highlighted by **splitting it into spans** (`highlight`, `<mark>`, never innerHTML, per the review). Markup in an answer shows as text.
  - the citations, in order, with title and domain
  - a quarantined prompt's answer is labelled as being in no metric

Experiment E1. Adds `tests/bench/cpi_breakdown.py`, which charges every cycle that retires nothing to exactly one cause (load-use, mul-use, csr-use, mul/div busy, mispredict, trap/mret/fence.i, I-cache, D-cache, straddle, other). author: andresosa21
body:
## Qué hace

Implementa la **Semana viva** (fila 6 del cronograma: escenarios de la demo final, orden de desbloqueo y actualización real del progreso al completar tareas).

- **Cada tarea completada es un paso** del camino de Pandoro. Los pasos se guardan como eventos en `users/{uid}/completions` (solo id de la tarea e instante, ningún texto del usuario) y sobreviven aunque la tarea se borre.
- **Pandoro camina por el sendero en Progreso** al entrar, con saltitos, balanceo, aplastón y huellitas. Avanza con rendimientos decrecientes (nunca pasa del 80 % del tramo), no retrocede y recuerda dónde se le vio por última vez, también entre sesiones.
- **El lugar nuevo se decide al cerrar la semana** (lunes a domingo, hora local): se abre si la semana tuvo al menos un paso y no quedó ninguna tarea pendiente con fecha hasta el domingo. Cada semana da un lugar una sola vez y lo ganado no se revierte.
- **Aviso de cierre** (`WeekClosureScreen`, modal sobre la app): aparece solo, sin recargar. Muestra «Semana completada» con el lugar nuevo y «Ver mi mundo», o «Tu semana» si no se completó, y el bloque plegado «Para la próxima semana». «Pasar todo» y cerrar sin elegir hacen lo mismo y no tocan ninguna tarea. «Ajustar una por una» permite mover la fecha o marcar «Ya no aplica». Cada domingo ya se muestra si la semana quedó completa; si no, espera al lunes.
- **Fecha de entrega con calendario** en «+ Nueva tarea» (nueva tarea nace con fecha de hoy), sin escribirla a mano.
- Se retira la racha de días (ningún contador se reinicia por inactividad) y los umbrales por total de tareas (25/40/58/80/105). Los textos de progreso pasan a «tareas completadas» / «semanas completadas».
- En «Ahora», las pendientes con fecha pasada van primero, sin etiqueta de culpa.

La lógica de dominio es pura (la fecha entra como parámetro) y está en `src/services/progress/`.

## Decisiones que necesito que el equipo confirme

Están registradas en `docs/CONTEXTO.md` como pendientes:

1. «Semana completa sin porcentaje»: ≥1 paso y ninguna pendiente con fecha hasta el domingo. **Las tareas sin fecha o con fecha futura no cuentan**, así que una semana solo de tareas sin fecha se gana con una sola tarea.
2. Se retira la racha de días.
3. Una tarea de una semana ya cerrada no se puede desmarcar (queda en silencio).
4. Con un lugar por semana, la demo del 16/11 solo mostrará el segundo mundo; falta decidir si se agrega un modo para simular semanas.
5. Toca archivos de otras tareas (6 Diseño, 15 Persistencia, 21 Priorización, 23 Integración): `worldData.ts`, `demoState.ts`, `TasksProvider.tsx`, `mapping.ts`. Conviene revisar que no pise ramas ajenas.

## Cómo probarlo

- `npm install`, `npm run typecheck` y `npm test` (105 pruebas, incluyen límites de semana, cambio de año, zona horaria y los criterios de aceptación de la especificación).
- Antes de aprobar, correr `npm run check:firestore`: se agregaron la colección `completions` y campos nuevos en `progress/world`, y el script no los cubre todavía.
- Flujo manual: Ajustes → Reiniciar demo, generar el plan en Hablar, completar tareas y abrir Progreso; para ver el cierre, cambiar la fecha del computador a un domingo con todo hecho o al lunes siguiente.

## Limitaciones conocidas

- Verificado con pruebas automáticas; **las animaciones y el modal de cierre no se han revisado en un dispositivo ni en otros navegadores**.
- `TaskCelebration.tsx` y `DEMO_CELEBRATION_TITLES` quedaron sin uso.
- La sección «Qué es real y qué está simulado» de `AGENTS.md` sigue desactualizada.
- El mensaje del commit no sigue gitmoji; si se prefiere, se corrige con squash al fusionar.

body:
## What

- `.github/CODEOWNERS`: a copy of `shared/.github/CODEOWNERS` (`* @semnil`), so a pull request here, Dependabot's included, asks the owner for a review, as it does in the public extensions.
- `test/codeowners.test.cjs`: holds the copy to the shared file byte for byte, and to a line that names an owner for every path.
- `README.md` / `README.ja.md` / `CLAUDE.md`: what the copy is and what holds it to the shared file.

## Why

`gh repo list semnil` lists 22 public repositories that are neither forks nor archived. 21 of them have `.github/CODEOWNERS` reading `* @semnil` on their default branch, with 0 entries in `codeowners/errors`. This repository, created on 2026-10-30, is the 22nd: `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS` and `docs/CODEOWNERS` return 404 here.

Dependabot has opened 211 pull requests in semnil's repositories since 2026-10-22. 203 of them are in the 21 public repositories above; 191 of those 203 have a `review_requested` event for semnil. The other 12 (analyze-loudness#93–97, analyze-spectrum#96–101, urx-lcd-sim#120) were opened on 2026-10-22 before CODEOWNERS reached those repositories. #53, the one Dependabot pull request here, has no `review_requested` event, and it was auto-merged.

The shared file reaches the extensions through the `public` group; nothing copies it into this repository's own `.github/`, where GitHub reads it.

## Checks run

- `node --test test/*.test.cjs test/*.test.mjs` on 43b42f9: 254 tests, 254 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.
- Mutants of the new test on 43b42f9, with both files restored after each: 4 cases, 4 fail as they should: the copy removed (as on `main`), the copy naming another owner, both files emptied, both files' line commented out. The restored tree passes.

author: toufikze77
body:
**Sandbox only, read only.** Production stays refused in code. Nothing was applied, deployed or sent to HMRC. Production was only read: table names, function md5s and the audit event rule. Full details are in `docs/hmrc-p8/README.md`.

## What was verified, and what was skipped
Verified on 8 Nov 2026 against HMRC's published VAT (MTD) API 1.0 definition (`hmrc/vat-api`, `resources/public/api/conf/1.0/application.yaml`). For each endpoint the README lists the path, version, scope, query, response fields, error codes with HTTP status, and sandbox scenarios.

- **Built:**
  - view VAT return;
  - liabilities;
  - payments;
  - penalties.
- **Verified but not built:**
  - financial details (follow-up);
  - customer information (not requested).
- **Not verified:** HMRC's Test Fraud Prevention Headers page and the VAT end-to-end guide. developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk is blocked from this session.

## New scope
**None.** All four reads use `read:vat`, which we already request.

## What's in it
**Four Edge Functions:** `hmrc-vat-return-view`, `hmrc-vat-liabilities`, `hmrc-vat-payments` and `hmrc-vat-penalties`. They follow the `hmrc-vat-obligations` pattern (shared code in `_shared/hmrc/vatReads.ts`):
- **What they send:** GET only, with the same fraud headers, a 20 s timeout and no retries. The only repeat is the shared one-off token refresh on a 401, as for obligations.
- **Audit:** one row before each call (`<kind>_call`) and one after (`<kind>_result`), codes only.
- **Limits and storage:** 10 reads an hour per company for each kind. Nothing that HMRC returns is stored.
- **Return view:** compares the nine boxes with our stored `hmrc_vat_submissions` copy and returns `{ matches, differences }`.
- **Config:** each has `verify_jwt = true`, and each is in the demo guard's refuse list.

**Screens on the VAT Returns page:**
- **Check what HMRC holds** and **Receipt**, for each accepted submission. The receipt comes from our stored row with no HMRC call, and prints to PDF with browser print CSS.
- **What you owe and what HMRC received**, in GBP, with a note that it is sandbox test data.
- **Penalties**, with "This is what HMRC shows. Check your HMRC account for the final position."
- Every new button has loading and error states, and a "This isn't available yet." state.

**Deadline reminders:** an in-app banner for returns due within 14, 7 or 1 days, or overdue. It uses only the obligations already read on the page, so there is no extra HMRC call.

**Pre-submit checks:**
- **Block** only what HMRC itself rejects:
  - box 3 ≠ box 1 + box 2;
  - box 5 ≠ |box 3 − box 4|;
  - a negative box 5.
- **Warn** when a box changed by more than 50% since the last accepted return.
- The wording says "This is a check, not tax advice."

**Shared change:** `api.ts` now allows `%XX` in a path, so a period key with `#` is sent as `%23`.

## SQL needed: yes (written and tested, NOT applied)
`docs/hmrc-p8/proposal.sql` is additive and uses `SET search_path = ''`. It doesn't touch any immutability trigger. It does two things:
- adds eight audit event names;
- adds `hmrc_take_read_slot`, which only the service role can call.

It refuses if production has drifted from what was read on 8 Nov 2026. The rollback refuses while P8 audit rows exist, unless it is forced.

Local suite: `PG_RUN_USER=postgres bash docs/hmrc-p8/run-test.sh` gives **37 PASS, 0 FAIL**.

## Rollout (owner): SQL, then functions, then front end
1. After review, apply `docs/hmrc-p8/proposal.sql`.
2. Deploy the functions:
```powershell
cd C:\b2bnest-deploy
git pull
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-return-view --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-liabilities --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-payments --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-penalties --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-obligations --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
npx.cmd supabase functions deploy hmrc-vat-submit --project-ref gvftvswyrevummbvyhxa --use-api
```
   - JWT verification stays on. Never use `--no-verify-jwt`.
   - No new secret is needed.
   - `hmrc-vat-obligations` and `hmrc-vat-submit` are redeployed only because of the small shared `api.ts` change.
3. Publish the front end. Until steps 1 and 2 are done, the new buttons say "This isn't available yet."

The sandbox test steps for the owner (view return for 18A1, liabilities, payments, penalties, receipt, reminder banner) are in README §2.

## Still not done
- The sandbox run of the new reads. That happens after rollout.
- Email reminders. There is no existing safe pattern, and it would need a new scheduled job or stored due dates. Both are owner decisions.
- Financial details and customer information.
- HMRC's fraud-header page and the end-to-end guide are not verified.
- No accountant review, no independent penetration test, no HMRC approval. None of these is claimed.

## Docs
- New: `docs/hmrc-p8/README.md`.
- Updated:
  - `production-request-pack.md`: endpoints, scopes, scenarios, audit actions;
  - `error-handling.md`: the verified P8 codes, with date and URL;
  - `privacy-wording.md`: data is read live and nothing new is stored;
  - the demo README.

## Checks
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`: exit 0.
- `npx eslint .`: 509 problems (baseline 510).
- `npx vitest run`: 184 files and 1726 tests passed, with no "Unhandled". 24 of the tests are new.
- Deno (`supabase/functions/`): 504 passed, 0 failed. 17 of the tests are new.
- `npm run build`: exit 0.

author: alexander-turner
body:
On a Kubernetes node, each pod's Envoy, verdict service, audit sink and monitor now run as the unprivileged `glovebox-node-stack` account with no capability. Before, they ran as root and parsed guest bytes. This is row B5 of AlexanderMattTurner/agent-glovebox#10076. It stacks on AlexanderMattTurner/agent-glovebox#10139. The netd relay still runs as root inside the egress daemon; a stacked PR moves it. Planning doctrine now refuses a per-platform code path: `explore-plan` and `code-style.md` require laptop, Lima and node to share ONE code path.

## What & why

On the node, Envoy and the verdict service ran as uid 0, so a parser bug reached by guest bytes ran with root's power over every pod.

This PR changes three things:
- Systemd template units `gb-kata-node-stack@`, `-authz@` and `-envoy@` start each pod's stack as the `glovebox-node-stack` account, through one `gb-kata-proxy exec envoy|authz` verb that the laptop also runs.
- Root follows no link the account writes: it checks the owner before each socket dial and each read, and writes inside a held directory fd.
- A live check fails while any pod-stack process holds uid 0 or a capability.

```text
Probe run 42563429793 at 2a567013a4 (this PR's head c5ce232bfa plus the probe workflow):
  green: Kata --node install on Ubuntu 22.04 (systemd 249)
  green: Kata --node install on Ubuntu 24.04
    both include the cell pods check: no stack process runs as root
  rerun: Kata Cloud Hypervisor boot posture (cell posture); it died in provisioning on HTTP 504 before any check ran
Earlier probe run 42555310029 at e96254edfd was red on both node legs:
  every pod's stack unit exited: upstream-ca.pem is missing.
  The operator's CA sat in a 0700 directory the stack account cannot read.
  c5ce232bfa stages root's copy of the CA for the account.
```

The doctrine commit answers the user: "why werent you combining codepaths anyway? update .claude to be VERY STRICT about this".

## Decisions made

- Systemd template units start each pod's stack, not a root broker. A broker would be a root parser of `systemd-run` arguments that the account writes.
- All pods share one account on this PR, so one pod's stack can reach another pod's. A later stacked PR gives each pod its own minted account. It reuses the minting that already gives each pod's VMM an account; `DynamicUser=` is not taken, because it allocates the uid only at start, after root must hand over the directories.
- A node that still has root-owned pod directories from before this change refuses those pods and names the directory to remove.

## Review focus

Read `kata_layout.node_stack_unit_text`, `bin/lib/kata/node-stack.bash` and `bin/lib/kata/node/node_stack_host.py` first. The least-sure part is the list of root reads of account-written paths: the proxy, lookup, refusal and route sockets, the routes file, the CA, the policy write, unit liveness, the key log, the verdict store and the witness markers. A path root reads that this list misses would let the account point root at a file it chose. The live check's egress-unit exemption still passes the egress daemon's main pid, because the netd relay runs in it.

body:
Refs #327

## What

A plugin skill, `/che-ical-mcp:quota`, for use-it-or-lose-it quotas (an allowance that resets on a fixed cycle and is lost if unused). No Swift change.

- **Declarations**: `~/.claude/.ical/quotas.yaml`, read from that one place (no walk-up; a quota belongs to an account). `find-ical-config.sh --quotas` applies the `config.yaml` trust check: 0 trusted, 1 absent, 3 present but not trusted (never read, never overwritten). Closed key list; labels only, no credentials. This replaces the decision record's `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` proposal: the plugins reference says that directory is per plugin id and is deleted on uninstall (design.md).
- **Dates**: `plugin/bin/quota-dates.sh` (bash + BSD `date`) prints each period's reset, due (reset minus lead) and alarm offset, and whether one recurrence rule reproduces every local due and alarm over 104 weeks / 24 months. Day 29–31 use the month-end clamp (decision record row 5).
- **Reminder**: title `Use up <name> (<account>, <when>)`; the due stays at the real deadline, also at night; `notify_at` becomes a relative alarm at the latest local HH:MM before the due, plus one at the due (`[n, 0]` or `[0]`); date-only resets get no alarm. Notes end in `quota-module: <id>`; text below it is the user's. Rule mode = one recurring reminder; per-period mode (no single rule fits) = one one-off per period for 90 days.
- **Operations** (closed list): declare, update (in place; an overdue reminder keeps its due), retire (deletes open reminders only after a yes to that quota in that run; `delete_reminder` not pre-approved), list, sync.
- **Spec**: `openspec/changes/add-quota-reminders` (validate and analyze clean).

**Needs the binary that ships #333 and #354** (both under `[Unreleased]`). With v1.23.0 the alarm and an in-place rule change are not written; the skill's read-back reports it. `plugin.json` is unchanged (tied to the binary version).

The list was deleted; `list_calendars` piped through `grep -c '#327'` returned 0 at 07:24:03 and at 07:25:22.

author: raktim-mondol
body:
## Why
A free-form review asks the model what it notices, so it notices something different every time. This adds the opposite: fixed, versioned criteria that give the same verdict on the same text.

## What
**Engine** (tier `TR`, rubric 1.4.0)
- A criterion is one versioned yes/no question about one paragraph, asked about a **defect** (so there are words to quote). Defaults ship per profile (`core`, `empirical`, `grant`); projects add or reword in `rubric/*.yaml`.
- A "yes" counts only if its quote is found in the paragraph (case/whitespace normalised, >= 8 chars per piece). One corrected retry, then `unverifiable`: never a finding.
- Verdicts are cached on (prompt version, criterion hash, paragraph hash, model). Unchanged text is never asked twice; an edit re-judges that paragraph only. Errors and unparseable replies are not remembered.
- A (criterion, paragraph) pair that got **no verdict** (no model, error, over `--judge-limit`) is **carried** in the ledger, never closed.
- Everything reports at **info** until the author admits it: `ah rubric admit` runs the model over their hand labels and needs Cohen's kappa >= 0.6, precision >= 0.8, 20 labels with 5 of each kind. An admission is **void if the question or the model changes**, and a carried finding then falls back to info. `rubric/**` is a protected path so an agent cannot admit its own check.
- Ledger causes: `evidence-changed` for a first verdict on unchanged text, `rubric-changed` for a criterion edit, never `UNEXPLAINED`.
- CLI: `ah audit|check --rubric|--judge|--judge-limit`, `ah rubric list|run|sheet|admit`. `--judge` has its own backend switch, so it does not also send every cited claim to the T3 verifier.

**Plugin**: tool `ah_rubric` (list, run, sheet), `rubric`/`judge`/`judge_limit` on `ah_audit`, `rubric` on `ah_check`, `ah_author action=rubric-admit` (DSH asks the human to confirm). `BUNDLE_REV` dsh7 -> dsh8.

## Not done / limits
- **Not validated with a hosted model.** That would spend the user's DeepSeek credits, which has not been authorised. The first real pass is something to run deliberately.
- The `pi` backend cannot set temperature 0 (the `http` backend does); the cache is what makes it repeatable.
- One paragraph at a time: a defect spanning paragraphs is invisible. The shipped criteria are starting points, not validated instruments.
- The remaining phase-3 work (deterministic format rules) is untouched by this PR.

## Verification
- [x] 25 new engine tests with a faked model (57 total). 6 deliberate breakages (quote not checked, model missing from the cache key, unjudged pairs not carried, admission ignoring the model, admission ignoring the question, unadmitted criterion reporting at its own level) each fail a test.
- [x] argv tests; the **installed** engine ships the bundled criteria (non-editable venv)
- [x] `npm test` 102/102 files, `npm run test:ah-engine`
- [x] On a copy of `paper/rsi-local` through the plugin with a **stub** model (keyword matcher with verbatim quotes): 157 paragraphs x 4 criteria = 629 pairs judged in 4.6 s; the repeat made 0 calls in 0.5 s, `ledger new 0`, and `ah_audit rubric=true` (no model) replayed the same 28 findings

body:
## What this adds

A focused attempt records exact countercontrols to the proposed free four-cut ramp obstruction through sixteen rotations. body:
## What
Adds a build-time list of the spoken languages a build hears: `EXPO_PUBLIC_SPOKEN_LANGUAGES` (D-125 item 2). It is section 4.1 of the speech proposal on spoken languages for build 12, which the coordinator accepted on 8 Nov: build 12 ships English only.

- `testflight`, `preview` and `production` write `"EXPO_PUBLIC_SPOKEN_LANGUAGES": "en"` next to `EXPO_PUBLIC_ENGLISH_ONLY=on`, so build 12 behaves exactly as today.
- `development` and `e2e` leave both unset, which means every language, also as today. **This is a deliberate exception to "en in every profile":** writing `en` there would change today's development behaviour, and the per-language gate needs a development build that hears the language for its 30 SE 3 device runs (experiments/README.md section 7.2).
- **Backward compatible:** `EXPO_PUBLIC_ENGLISH_ONLY` stays and still wins: with it on, the build hears English alone whatever the list says, so the list can only narrow what the switch allows. `capabilities.englishOnly` and its pins are unchanged.

## How
- `src/lib/capabilities.ts`: `parseLanguageList` and `spokenLanguagesListed()`. The variable is read once, written out in full so Expo inlines it, and remote config has no key for it. A test-only setter follows the existing pattern. `capabilities` itself is unchanged.
- `src/lib/language/heard-languages.ts` (new, pure): `heardLanguages(englishOnly, listed)`. English is always heard, the other languages follow catalog order, and unknown codes are ignored, so a typo narrows the build and never widens it. The result is stable and frozen, so screens can memo on it.
- Readers: the picker, Settings > Spoken language (Also spoken), first run's language row and the queue's language hold now read `heardLanguagesForBuild()`. The pure functions still accept the old boolean, so existing tests are unchanged.
- Preflights: `preflight-production` gets a new `spoken-languages` check, and `preflight-testflight` checks both alpha profiles. Each FAILs a profile whose list is not `en`.
- `#498` claims test (`packages/content/test/claims-capabilities.test.ts`), extended per language and never loosened. A named language counts as a true claim only if the production build hears that language: Spanish, Hindi, Chinese/Mandarin, French, Arabic and Portuguese map to their codes, and every other name is false in every build. Counts and "any language" claims follow the same rule as before. The production profile line now pins `heard: ['en']`.

## Tests
- New: `apps/mobile/test/heard-languages.test.ts` (14 tests). It covers parsing, the English-only switch winning, unknown codes, stable results, and that the readers treat English plus Spanish as two languages with five on hold.
- Extended: `capabilities.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `preflight-production.test.ts` (three new failing fixtures), `language-picker-english-only.test.ts` (the source pins and the list of files that read the switch, with a wider pattern), `onboarding-language-row.test.ts`, and the claims test (two new tests).
- Run in this worktree, from `origin/develop` 107508e1:
  - `@scribe/mobile`: 4,154 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are in `licences.test.ts` (`npm ls` disagrees with the lockfile walk). That comes from the shared node_modules in this sandbox; the same test fails the same way in an untouched worktree, and this PR changes no dependency.

  - Not run: on a device, `npm run test:db`, `npm run test:functions`.

## Review notes
- `apps/mobile/eas.json` and `capabilities.ts` are founder-path files (D-107), and `eas.json` is frozen until after the Mon 9 Nov go/no-go (D-124 item 1). **Do not merge before Tue 10 Nov.**

author: pete-builds
body:
## What it fixes

Invited devices are meant to be stream only: they reach a file only inside one of their own open playback sessions for it (`streamOnly` in `server/internal/api/invites.go`). Video files and extras check this. The music track routes never did, so an invited device could fetch a whole track with `GET /api/v1/music/tracks/{id}/file` and no session. #154 copied the same gap into `/api/v1/audiobooks/files/{id}/file`. **The music half predates #154.** `TestNoTokenRouteServesAWholeFile` missed it because its walker compared answers only against `media_versions` and `item_extras` files, and its device had no music library.

## What changed

- **Server:** the track and book file routes, both `/file` (direct) and `/stream` (converted), call `streamOnly`. For an invited device the session must be its own, still open, and a listen to that exact track or book file. The household's own accounts and profiles are unchanged. `/stream` follows the rule video's converted routes follow: those only exist under a session, so an invited device needs its listen there too. `playback.ForFile` loads a session with whatever it plays (version, extra, track or book file). `ForStream` and the converted video routes are untouched.
- **Tests:** the whole-file walk now grants the invited device a Music and an Audiobooks library (each with files), counts `music_tracks` and `audiobook_files` as whole files, and checks that a track or book file plays inside its own listen (direct and converted) but not inside another file's listen, an ended listen, or none. The access walk now probes audio files inside the principal's own listen, and also by the bare URL for household devices, as it already did for versions.
- **Web:** on an invited device (`/me` kind `token`) the player opens the listen first and then loads the file with `session=`. It does not preload the next track there, so tracks meet with a short gap on invited devices only. Seeking a converted stream keeps the session. The smoke test gains a step that plays an album and a book as an invited device and checks that a bare track URL answers 403 `stream_only`.
- **TV:** a `ResolvingDataSource` (`ListenSessions`) opens the listen when Media3 first asks for a file, adds `session=`, and the player's listen reuses it. Media3 loads the next file early for gapless play, so this keeps gapless. Listens opened ahead and never played are closed on stop or on a new queue. This only happens when `/me` says `token`; accounts behave as before.

## Controls

The walker on the code before the fix (test extended, server unchanged):

```
--- FAIL: TestNoTokenRouteServesAWholeFile (1.04s)
    invites_test.go:781: routes serving an invited device a whole file: [GET /api/v1/music/tracks/{track_id}/file HEAD /api/v1/music/tracks/{track_id}/file GET /api/v1/audiobooks/files/{file_id}/file HEAD /api/v1/audiobooks/files/{file_id}/file]
FAIL
```

After:

```
--- PASS: TestNoTokenRouteServesAWholeFile (0.68s)
ok  	github.com/pete-builds/vcrx-media-server/server/internal/api	0.940s
```

The web smoke step with the old `player.js` (no session on the URL):

```
invited listening: the album did not play on the invited device (t=-1)
invited listening: the track was asked for outside its listen:
invited listening: the book did not play on the invited device (t=-1)
```

With the fix: `album played to 0.6 s and the book to 0.6 s, each in its listen; a bare track URL: 403 stream_only`.

## Gates run locally (all passed)

`go vet`, golangci-lint v2.12.2 (0 issues), `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go mod tidy` with no diff, `web/check-js.sh`, `deploy/deploy_test.sh`, `scripts/check-private.sh`, web smoke against two dev servers, and the TV `docker buildx ... --target check` (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, lint 0 errors, `ListenSessionsTest` 3 passed).

## What is left

- The TV change is tested by unit tests and the build only. It has not been played on a real TV as an invited device.
- Repeat one on an invited TV: the listen is closed and reopened at each loop. If Media3 re-reads the file under the old session at that moment, one read could be refused. Not seen, not tested.

Base is `feat/audiobooks` (#154); retarget to `main` once that lands.

body:
## Why

Follows PR #232, which has merged. This branch is rebased onto `main`. Anthony asked that the guard also cover `Agent` helpers ("Yes, add that"): an `Agent` call keeps Sonnet only when it is one of the routine kinds AGENTS.md lists, or a pstack role that `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md` puts on Sonnet. Any other non-Opus pick runs on Opus. Rewriting to Opus is better than blocking, because the work keeps going.

PR #232's verifier (PASS+NOTES) also found a gap. The app's `set_session_model` tool could downgrade a session after a model-free `start_session` passed the guard. #232 had already passed, so the fix goes here instead of being pushed to #232.

## What changed

- `.claude/hooks/verifier-model.mjs`: a new `helper` kind covers an `Agent` call that isn't a verifier, trail review or audit and sets a non-Opus `model`.
  - It keeps Sonnet only when the description starts with a routine prefix: Research, Inventory, Docs pass, Docs-only, Lint fix, Format or Formatting fix.
  - It also keeps Sonnet when the description starts with a pstack Sonnet role: How explorer, How explainer, Why investigator(s), Reflect, Hillclimb or Arena cross-judge.
  - Anything else, including Haiku, Fable or Sonnet under another description, is rewritten to `opus`. The reason names the allowed prefixes.
  - A call with no model, or with Opus, is untouched. Helpers skip the GitHub read.
- **How pstack roles are recognized:** pstack's `how`, `why`, `reflect`, `arena` and `hillclimb` instructions set `model` and `subagent_type: generalPurpose`, but they give no description. So the only signal the hook can use is a description that starts with the role name, and AGENTS.md now tells agents to name them that way. A role helper named some other way falls back to Opus. In all JustGO transcripts there are only 6 non-Opus `Agent` calls, and none is a pstack role, so nothing in use today depends on a different name.
- `.claude/hooks/session-model-guard.mjs`: it now also denies every `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_model` call. The `settings.json` matcher covers both tools. The deny reason no longer says the parent is Opus. The code comment marks the Sonnet-parent cause as unconfirmed.
- `AGENTS.md`: the routine-helper bullet now lists exactly the enforced kinds: research, inventories, docs-only passes, and lint and formatting fixes. "Small review notes" is gone, so those now run on Opus. A new bullet names the prefixes and the pstack role names. The session bullet covers `set_session_model`, and says to start a session with a `preset` only when Anthony names it. The "same hook" wording now names `verifier-model.mjs`, because #232's new bullet came between them. The verifier-model rules row is extended, and so is the session-guard row. Prettier reflowed the rules table's column widths. It is still a table.

## Scope

- Tooling and docs only. Not a sensitive path.
- `preset` is still not blocked by the hook, because a preset is Anthony's saved choice. A written rule covers it.

## Verification

- Tests came first. The new `verifier-model-hook` cases failed on the rewrite cases (2 of 17), then passed (17/17). The new `set_session_model` case failed against #232's guard (7/8), then passed (8/8). `node --test scripts/quality/*.test.mjs`: 338 pass, 0 fail. `npm run lint`: 0 errors (the 167 warnings were already there). Changed-file Prettier and eslint are clean. `doc-links`: 4 pass.
- **Verified (fresh headless Claude Code 2.1.317 in this branch's worktree, with stub `ccd_session` and `ccd_session_mgmt` MCP servers that record every call):**
  - `set_session_model` to Sonnet was denied, with "session-model-guard: agents never change a session's model …".
  - `start_session` with a model set was denied. Neither call reached its stub.
  - `Agent` "Merge verified PRs" with `model: sonnet` ran with `resolvedModel: claude-opus-5-5`.
  - `Agent` "Inventory hook files" with `model: sonnet` kept `resolvedModel: claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- **Inconclusive:** the app's own in-process session tools. Project hooks load when a session starts, and this session can't start a fresh app session.

author: sev7nfold
body:
**Phase 4 of the build plan: FOLD Score.** Every film now has a soundtrack composed from its own edit, with a hit on every cut.

## How it works
- **Cues from the timeline** (`src/audio/fold-score.mjs`): cuts and their transitions (paper swooshes on The Fold, whooshes that follow the wipe, a riser into a push), word and type-window letter landings, light sweeps, the opening beam, the logo drawing and its glint, product reveals, and the end card.
- **Tempo from the edit:** the bpm in the mood's range whose beat grid sits closest to the cuts.
- **The score:** a pad that changes chord on each cut and resolves on the end card; a groove (kick, hats, bass, arpeggio) between the opening and the end card; sound design on every cue; a room reverb. It's deterministic: the same timeline and mood give the same samples.
- **Moods:** Premium calm (84–96 bpm, D minor), Energetic (118–128, A minor), Editorial (104–114, E minor), Warm (78–90, F major). Auto picks one from the storyboard's words; No music renders silent.
- **Mastering in JavaScript:** loudness measured with ITU-R BS.1770 and brought to −14 LUFS under a −2 dBFS look-ahead limiter, so FFmpeg only encodes AAC. FFmpeg's own `loudnorm` upsampled to 192 kHz and took FFmpeg from 145 to 263 MB, too close to the free plan's 512 MB; with JS mastering it stays at 155 MB.

## Studio
- A **Music** picker beside "Render and run QA" (Auto, the four moods, No music), remembered per production.
- The render card shows the score, for example "Music: FOLD Score, Energetic, 120 bpm, A minor".
- QA lists **Loudness**, **Peaks** and **Sync** (10 checks in all).

## QA
Production QA now requires: audio present, audio duration within one frame, loudness within 1.5 LU of −14, true peak at most −0.5 dBFS, and at least 90% of cuts, type-window letters and the end card with an onset within one frame, measured from the samples.

## Prompts
The storyboard prompt says sound is automatic: describe the mood rather than specific music. Voiceover, dialogue and licensed songs are still not promised.

## Verification
- `npm test`: **206 passing**, 0 failing. New tests cover cue extraction, tempo alignment, mood keywords, all four moods (deterministic, every major hit within a frame), BS.1770 loudness (a −20 dBFS tone reads −20 LUFS), mastering to −14 LUFS under the ceiling, and the WAV format.
- **Mix measured per mood:** stereo correlation 0.52 to 0.78; the low end and presence rebalanced after the first pass (Energetic's sub-bass down from 55% to 38%, Premium's from 31% to 15%).
- **Full CLI renders** of a 10-second product film, Premium calm and Energetic: production QA and creative QA pass; −14.1 and −14.2 LUFS with peaks at −2.0 and −1.9 dBFS in the final MP4; 25 s on one core; 280 MB peak.
- **Browser:** the Music picker sends the choice; the render card shows the score; all 10 QA checks pass; the MP4 has an AAC track. No console errors.

## Next
Lyria via OpenRouter as an optional AI music bed under FOLD Score's hits.

Adds `.github/workflows/release-publish.yml` — a **workflow_dispatch-only** job that creates a GitHub Release for an existing tag from the executables an earlier `windows-release` run already built and hashed.

**Why in CI:** GitHub's artifact/release CDNs are unreachable from the development sandbox, but a runner downloads the artifact normally. Publishing from CI means the release assets are the **exact bytes** from run `42534211521` — not a rebuild, not the CI zip, not hand-copied hashes.

**Permissions:** `contents: write`, scoped to this workflow only. `windows-release.yml` keeps its read-only permissions and `--publish never`.

## Web-first S4 — Shared invite QR presentation and manual QA provenance

- Four artistic QR artwork labels localized for IT, EN, ES, FR and PT.
- Artwork headings use readable dark ink even in dark-mode pastel backgrounds; labels wrap at large text.

author: kaileido
body:
## Problem

An error-miss claim carries the executor's own error stream as evidence. A verifier hashes that payload and compares it with the hashes in the executor's signed Finish, so a line kept or dropped differently turns an accepted claim into a rejected one. Each gateway had its own copy of this rule: devshardctl's line filter, envelope test, `[DONE]` check and payload marshal sat in `cmd/devshardctl/redundancy.go`, and the new gateway's sat in `cmd/gateway/engine/miss_proof.go`. The two copies were identical, but nothing stopped them from drifting apart.

## Change

- New package `devshard/gatewayprotocol/streamevidence`. `DataLines` returns the evidence lines of a read: `data: ` lines with a trailing `\r` trimmed, without the `devshard_receipt` and `devshard_meta` envelopes. `IsDoneLine` is the `[DONE]` test. `Payload` is the JSON of `completionapi.SerializedStreamedResponse` over those lines. The envelope keys, the terminator and the line framing are in `vocabulary.go`.
- A golden in `streamevidence/testdata`: the terminal-error fixture `newlineless_final_error.sse`, copied from `cmd/gateway/filters/testdata/sse/`, with the payload bytes that both gateways' previous code produced from it. Both produced the same bytes.
- devshardctl's `raceWriter` retention and `errorMissArtifacts`, and the new gateway's `errorStreamRetainer`, now call the package. The four duplicated helpers are deleted. The two devshardctl tests that called `ssePayloadDataLines` now call `streamevidence.DataLines`.
- The envelope test stays unexported. No call site uses it outside `DataLines`.
- Guard row for the package (`common/completionapi` and the standard library). Updated the tree README, `devshard/docs/gateway-protocol-library.md` §3.5, and the shared-rules lines in `cmd/gateway/CONTRIBUTING.md` and `cmd/gateway/docs/rules.md`. Added one line in `cmd/gateway/docs/race.md`.
- Stacked on the timeout claim PR.

## Unchanged

- The lines kept and the payload bytes, in both gateways. The package runs the same expressions as the code it replaces, and the golden pins the bytes.
- The per-chunk retention path makes the same allocations as before: 2 allocs/op for a content chunk, 3 for an envelope plus error chunk and 3 for a meta plus `[DONE]` chunk, in both devshardctl and the new gateway, measured with `-benchmem` before and after.
- Each gateway keeps its own retainer and bound: devshardctl reads 1 MiB from `GATEWAY_ERROR_STREAM_MAX_ATTEMPT_BYTES` and charges its participant classify budget per line; the new gateway uses a fixed 64 KiB. Release and ownership of retained lines, claim eligibility and the Finish source are also unchanged.
- Hosts do not link the tree: `go list -deps ./cmd/devshardd ./cmd/devshard-host | grep gatewayprotocol` prints nothing.

author: tyler-v
body:
## What

Fixes from the audit of the marketing rebuild (PRs #118 to #124):

- **Screenshots.**
  - The workflow picture on /product and /product/automate-anything is now the product designer job's, with automations the capture adds: a thank-you email, stage emails, a reminder when Screening runs late, and a task when someone reaches Interview. It no longer shows "queue for rejection review" beside "a check never rejects anyone".
  - The two verification-panel pictures are deleted, and so is their capture. They named the kind of network, shared details and the ruleset version, which the site never says, and the repository is public. No page used them.
- **The never-guessing number.** Monster's 2024 poll: 59% of US workers rarely hear back after applying, and 33% never do. I read it on Monster's page in a browser, so pain-points.md now marks it Verified.
- **The trial length.** The site says "Start your free 14-day trial". The length and plan live in a new `packages/plans/trial.json`, which the marketing site reads and billing uses as its default (`TrialDefaults`), so the two cannot disagree.
- **Copy.**
  - The Workable and Ashby prices now say what their pricing pages say about the billing term.
  - A missing space in "higher plan.See how we compare" is fixed.
  - Three lines in the "Why no fraud score" post change: one said how a check works, one framed AI help as a quantity, and one implied an ID check exists.
  - The law pages state the law's duties instead of our plans: the planned ID verification is gone, and the bias-audit line now says whose duty it is.
- **Smaller fixes.**
  - The starting price uses the catalogue's currency instead of always "$".
  - The status chips under "What you see" stack instead of wrapping unevenly.
  - The GoHire research is corrected, and the open items are added to `docs/status.md`.
- **Flaky test.** `SettingsTests.An_area_menu_lists_only_its_own_pages...` expected the menu from before the billing query answered. It now expects the final menu, with Billing. Recorded in the flake history.

## Why

The audit's two reviewers, one against the briefs and one against the copy and verification rules, found these. The owner chose three of the defaults:
- the trial length belongs in the catalogue;
- the Monster figure gets confirmed and shown;
- the law pages state duties, not plans.

## Decisions

- **Both verification pictures removed, not only the flagged one.** docs/process/testing.md already said the clear one showed the network kind and ruleset version too.
- **The showcase job keeps a Rejected stage in its stage list.** Every pipeline has one. What a buyer could misread was an automation that queues rejection.
- **`TrialDefaults` reads the embedded file.** A host that overrides `ScreenHire:Billing:Trial:Days` must change the file too, or the site states a different trial. billing.md says so.

## Tests

- `pnpm verify:fast`.
- Vitest for @screenhire/marketing: 168 tests, with updated pricing and shell tests.
- Unit: `*Billing*`, `DocsBundleTests`, `PersonalInfoTests` (231).
- End-to-end: `SettingsTests` and `MarketingTests` (67).
- Recaptured with `UPDATE_MARKETING_SCREENSHOTS=1`. I opened each changed image: no rejection wording, no check details, each under 600 KB.

author: jenslynkc87
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Jenslynkc87"} -->
_Requested by **Jens** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KrVLJAdnENunEpMh4RRUJm?thread=cmsg_01KrVLJAdnENunEpMh4RRUJmVxDNWeRSSyHTBb3E9wueGr)_

## What changes

Replaces the "Chart results" window with views built around the questions student studies ask, on honest scales.

- **Distribution** shows every point of the rating scale, so a 1–7 study that only used 3–7 still shows 1 and 2 as zero. Stats: median, average, most common, range. The scale comes from the prompt (strict output syntax or a plain "1–7" / "−3 to +3"), otherwise from the data; students can edit it (min, max, low-to-high or neutral-middle colors, end labels).
- **Over time** places each text at its year and exact score (dots move sideways only when they share a year and score), with an optional smoothed trend line. "Share per period" shows 100% columns with automatic round period lengths and a warning when periods are thin. Large corpora default to shares, since dots would pile up.
- **Compare groups** reads groups from filenames (…F/…M, B-/G-) or a subject field, or lets students type and rename them. 100% bars plus group averages with 95% ranges.
- **Run agreement** (Model knowledge only) lists subjects whose runs disagree first.
- **Ranked list** with search replaces the ranked figure.
- Free-text answer fields are listed, not charted.

Whole-flow items 1, 3, 4, and 5 from the review:

1. Results that mix prompts, models, or reasoning effort are flagged and default to the latest settings. Chunks combine per document and runs per subject, with a "Count" switch to count each separately.
3. Years are read from filenames or a Year field automatically; "Review years" is optional, not a required step.
4. Downloaded figures (PNG/SVG) have a title, legend, and an automatic, editable caption (field, n, scale, models, effort, dates, notes) with "Copy caption".
5. The window is wider (up to 1080px) and full screen on phones.

Groups and reviewed years are saved with the study and exported to Excel ("Group" column). Model knowledge items can now hold years and groups too.

Item 2 (declaring field types in the prompt step) is deliberately not included.

## Removed

`lib/results-figure.ts`, `components/results-figure.tsx`, `components/chart-year-review.tsx`, and the old layout helpers in `lib/results-chart.ts` (the year and number parsers stay).

## Testing

- `npm run build && npm test`: 37/37 test files pass. The three chart test files are rewritten for the new modules and keep the robustness checks (completed-only filtering, INSUFFICIENT_KNOWLEDGE, escaping, no NaN/Infinity with extreme values, filename year cases, large sets). `startup-bundle` still confirms the chart stays out of the initial bundle.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. `npm run lint` fails before and after this change (missing `next` parser for eslint-config-next).
- Checked in Chromium at desktop and phone sizes with the inaugural corpus (60 texts), an obituary F/M set, Model knowledge runs, a 3,000-text corpus, mixed settings, and a −3 to +3 scale.
